Alchemy System

Alchemy System

Alchemy System

Gathering

  1. Use Downtime to Gather Herbs, max usage 3x a day (uses 8 hours in a session). Note: You can no longer sacrifice adventuring time to harvest extra herbs.

  2. Choose one environment [Cave, Forest, Desert, Grasslands, Swamp] + Rarity [Common, Uncommon, Rare, Very Rare]

  3. Roll Nature/Medicine/Arcana + Herbalism/Poisoner/Brewer/Alchemist Tool Prof Bonus (If proficient) --> DC scales depending on rarity of ingredient. Once check is completed, post in transcript using template found in pins of transcript . Craftmaster will roll for the herb gathered randomly depending on location chosen and DC rarity met.

DCs for Enchantment Ingredients:
Rarity DC
Common DC 10
Uncommon DC 13
Rare DC 17
Very Rare DC 20
Targeted Gathering

  1. You can target herbs based on which potion you wish to make! If you are targeting a herb for a specific potion, use the Targeted gathering Template pinned in transcript

  2. If the herb you are searching for isn't in the environment you chose, you get nothing. If it is, a Craftmaster will roll the herb normally, and you only get the herb if the dice comply.

The DCs for targeted gathering are as followed:
Rarity DC
Common DC 13
Uncommon DC 17
Rare DC 20
Very Rare DC 23
Bonuses:
  1. You can only target one herb per day until you have gathered 3 of that herb, at which point you may target for two herbs per day due to your familiarity.
  2. You cannot use help actions in herb gathering. Self-Buffs are allowed for now.
  3. Nat20 Rule: If you roll nat20 on the check (RAW Nat20 without modifiers and bonuses) you get 1 Extra Herb.
  4. Over10 Rule: If your total roll is 10 over the applicable DC you get 1 Extra Herb. Example, if your total roll for a rare is 31, you get 2 Herbs instead of 1.
  5. Nat20 and Over10 rules can both apply, to a max of 3 Herbs per roll.

Potion Brewing

Potions are brewed using herbs, each herb is used for a specific potion, the potion is hinted at in the description.

Time, base Cost, Herb Requirement to brew:

Rarity Time (Days) Cost Herb Requirement
Common 2.5 25 gp 1 Herb
Uncommon 5 100 gp 1 Herb
Rare 12.5 1,000 gp 2 Herbs
Very Rare 25 10,000 gp 3 Herbs

Monster Part Substitution

You can substitute 1 Herb for a monster part, however uncommon and higher potions need at least 1 Herb.

Potion Rarity Monster CR Loot DC
Common CR 1-3 DC 13
Uncommon CR 4-8 DC 17
Rare CR 9-13 DC 21
Very Rare CR 14-18 DC 24
Legendary CR 19+ DC 26

Bulk Brewing

  • Bulk Brewing has a discount on overall cost now. For every 10 potions you make at a time, you get a 5% discount on cost, cap for the discount is 20%.
  • Bulk Brewing also requires less herbs. For every 10 potions you brew, you only need 7x the amount of herbs for one potion of the same rarity. Example: 10 common potions of healing - 7 enchantment herbs needed.

Time Reduction

  • You get a 50% time reduction if you use double the amount of enchantment herbs for the potion.
  • Sacrificing Potions:
  1.   You can sacrifice one potion per brew.
  2.   Lowers base time by half the time it takes to brew a potion of that rarity.

Animal Taming Rules

Animal Taming Rules

Animal Taming Rules

Overview

  • A PC may attempt to tame animals over an extended period of time.

Taming Check

Check: Wisdom (Animal Handling)

Tame DC: 15 + (2 * CR) (minimum 11)

Time: 1 full day of calm interaction (one day of downtime)

Initial Tame

Before training begins, the creature must first be made non-hostile through patience, calmness, or courage.

Roll Result
Natural 20 Start at 25% Bond Progress
Success Creature becomes non-hostile and open to training
Fail by 5 or less You fail to train the creature, you may retry after 1 day
Fail by 5 or more You fail to train the creature, you may retry after 3 days
Natural 1 The creature flees or attacks, you may retry after 1 week

Long-Term Bond Training

Each day requires 8 hours of focused interaction. You can train only one creature at a time. Each success adds your roll to a cumulative total.

Roll Result
Natural 20 Add roll plus 10% of total progress threshold
Success You Progress your bond with the creature
Fail by 5 or less Your bond with the creature does not progress
Fail by 5 or more The creature refuses training, you may retry after 3 days
Natural 1 The creature flees or attacks, you may retry after 1 week

Progress cannot fall below your current bond stage unless broken by neglect or narrative reason.

Bond Progression

Bond Stage Progress Threshold
Non-Hostile Success on Initial Tame
Sociable 10 + (10 * CR)
Basic Commands
Stay. Come. Stop. 15 + (15 * CR)
Complex Commands
Dodge. Attack X creature. Hide. 20 + (20 * CR)
Mounted / Complex Tasks
Scout X area. Return to X location. Find X person. 25 + (25 * CR)

Example: A CR 3 beast needs 80 total progress to reach Complex Commands.

Once a stage is reached, it remains permanent unless broken through RP.

Food and Shelter

Proper care sustains trust.

Food

Creature Size Daily Cost
Tiny 10gp
Small 30gp
Medium 50gp
Large 100gp
Huge 150gp
Gargantuan 200gp

Unique Diets: Costs may be altered at DM Discretion

Shelter: Will be determined by DM

Luxury Care: Double Daily Cost

Care Factors

  • One day without care: Lose 10% Progress
  • Two days without care: Creature may flee and reset to 0%
  • Luxury Care: After 3 days of Luxury Care you gain advantage on the next training roll

Class and Subclasses Modifiers

Class/Sub-class Benefit
Ranger (Any) Advantage on Initial Tame for beasts with CR level beasts with CR ≤ half proficiency bonus
Ranger (Beast Master) Advantage on Initial Tame for equal to or less than half your ranger
Ranger (Drakewarden) Advantage on Initial Tame for draconic creatures or wyrmlings with CR equal to or less than half your level
Druid (Any) +2 to one Animal Handling check per long rest; reduce daily food cost by 25%
Druid (Circle of the Shepherd) Add 1d4 once per day to a training check.
Barbarian (Totem Warrior) Advantage when taming beasts matching your Totem Spirit
* Only one class bonus applies at a time.

Tamable Creatures

  • Beasts & Monstrosities comprised of Beasts (ex: Griffon, Hippogriff)
  • Subject to DM discretion. A number of monsters that may technically fit the criteria may not be tamable for lore reasons, or may otherwise be inaccessible due to where they may be located.
  • Young Griffin (CR 0, ¼, 1)
  • Griffon (CR 2)
  • Owlbear (CR 3)
  • Amphisbaena (CR ½)
  • Peryton (CR 2)
  • Kamadan (CR 4)
  • Death Dog (CR 1)
  • Shadow Mastiff (CR 2)
  • Giant Strider (CR 1)
  • Skyjek Roc (CR 2)
  • Two-Headed Owlbear (CR 3)
  • Hippogriff (CR 1)
  • Giant Ice Toad (CR 3)
  • Two-Headed Cerberus (CR 2)
  • Snowy Owlbear (CR 3)

Limitations

  • It must be reasonable for the creature to be tamed, per DM discretion.
  • It must make sense within the context of TWR lore, per DM discretion.
  • The creatures you can potentially tame are limited by the CR. In order to have the skill necessary to safely handle a creature, you must be capable of hitting the initial tame DC through just a straight animal handling roll without additional modifiers from items, spells, abilities, etc.

Maximum Tamable CR = (5 + Your Base Animal Handling Modifier) / 2

  • Creatures with legendary or mythic abilities can not be tamed.
  • Creatures with an INT of 1 can not be tamed.
  • Creatures with an INT of 4+ can not be tamed.
  • The initial tame, and subsequent checks, must be RPed for and submitted in transcript.
  • For CR 1+ The initial tame must occur in a mini-quest or RPed targeted hunt run by DM. A DM can not run their own quest if they are attempting to tame a creature.
  • For any creatures intended as a mount, the initial tame must occur in a mini-quest or RPed targeted hunt run by DM. A DM can not run their own quest if they are attempting to tame a creature.
  • Purchasable domesticated mounts are an exception, and can be purchased as normal.
  • No more than 1 creature can be tamed per day.
  • Exceptions may exist for things such as domesticated animals, per discretion of the DM.
  • Only creatures at least one size larger than a PC are mountable.
Owl-Bear Taming Example Steps
  • Go on a mini quest hosted by a DM.
  • RP to find and convince the Owl-Bear that you are both not food and non hostile.
  • CR3 creature, so DC 30 animal handling check for an adult Owl-Bear.
  • Upon success, it will be non hostile but still aggressive.
  • Cumulative DC of 300. The daily RPed animal handling checks would be added together.
  • With an average roll of 10, with the +10 modifier required to initially tame the creature, it would take 15 days in real life of daily checks and RP to tame the creature.
  • At 75 points, it would become sociable
  • At 150 points, it would accept simple commands
  • At 225 points, it would accept complex commands and barding
  • At 300 points, it would accept complex tasks and be mountable

To be updated

Use of Tamed Creatures In Combat

The creature acts on its own initiative. You control it as you would a summon RAW from spells such as Conjure Animals.

Mounted Combat for Tamed Creatures

  • Because of the inherent danger of things such as meteor swarms, when you are mounted the creature shares your HP.
  • If you fall to zero HP, your mount falls to 1 HP, you are dismounted if on land, and if it is a flying creature it begins to crashland at 60ft/round.
  • For the purposes of movement, the mount replaces your move speed(s).
  • HP when dismounting: When you dismount, if your HP is lower than the mount's HP, the mount will adopt the same current HP as you.
  • If you choose to have the mount attack, take any action, or otherwise treat it as a separate creature, ignore points 1~4 and it will be treated as a normal mount RAW.
Mounted Combatant Feat interaction

Under this system you can use either RAW and risk damage to the mount or the alternative rules in the Animal Taming doc. If you're using the alternative rules only point 1 of the feat pertaining to advantaged against creatures is applicable, the other two are nullified.

Sale and Transfer of Animals

  • The recipient must be capable of hitting the initial tame DC to be capable of controlling the creature in any way.
  • By default, the bond level resets to zero. If you are proficient in Animal Handling, it resets to 25%. If you have expertise in Animal Handling, it resets to 50%

Tame Death

If your tamed creature dies and is revived it will regress one cumulative level. If your tame is regressed past 0 the taming process with restart requiring a new initial tame roll.

Barding

Barding

Barding

Barding is equipment made for creatures not Medium size. Barding can be either mundane or magical.

The base cost of creating the item will be increased by the following modifier for each size above and below Medium:

Size Cost Modifier
Diminutive x 64
Tiny x 16
Small x 4
Large x 4
Huge x 16
Gargantuan x 64

Core / Character

Character Creation

Character Creation

The rules for Character Creation are below. For how to manage characters as they level up, see the Character Progression page.

2014 vs 2024

2014 characters follow the rules in this document as written. 2024 characters, or mixing the two, follow an additional set of rules: Allowed 2024 Rules Content

Character Creation

  1. Unless otherwise stated, rules regarding characters are RAW (rule as written).
    • Approved/Disapproved Modules can be found here: Approved and Disapproved Modules
  2. Characters can start at level 1-3 (player choice)
  3. Items, Experience, Abilities, etc do not carry over from other games/servers/campaigns.
  4. Backgrounds which grant feats are disallowed.
  5. You may choose Fixed or Rolled HP for your character, but must continue with that method for the lifetime of your PC. If rolling, ping a @Dungeonmaster to record your rolls.
  6. Character level advancement is via XP, not Milestone.
  7. All character stats are Point Buy or Standard Array.
  8. Character sheets must be kept up to date. If there is ever a question as to what level you are supposed to be, what items you have, how much gold you have, then we need to be able to refer to your sheet and check it against what we have on record in #records, #story-log or #transaction-log.
  9. You may have no more than 8 player characters to begin with. Once a character reaches T3, you may submit a request for additional PC slots.

Starting Equipment

  1. New PCs begin with standard starting equipment per the PHB.
  2. Starting gold is not allowed.
  3. PCs may select a single Uncommon magic item to start with, if they submit a written backstory that includes receiving it.
    1. This item must be available from the Favor Tables. This can be access in discord with <!loot uncommon wondrous s>, <!loot uncommon armaments s> or any +1 weapon or shield.
    2. The base value of the item may not exceed a gold value of 400gp (i.e. no Mithral Plate, firearms, except a pistol or arquebus, etc.)
  4. PCs who visit Elysium and complete an Entry Survey in character will receive 400gp in additional gold from the player-provided Adventurer's Fund. (LINK NEEDED)
Character Sheet Generators

Dndbeyond is recommended for easy character creation, but you may use another system if you wish. (Avrae supports Dndbeyond, Dicecloud, and Gsheet)

For DNDBeyond users, you may join one of the donated campaigns for access to sourcebooks.

Disclosures

  1. DMs have the right to refuse characters a spot in their quests, including those using UA/Homebrew supplements otherwise permitted by the server

Steps to Submitting a New Character

  1. Submit a link to your character sheet using the Character Submission template pinned in #transcript for Staff review and approval. Once approved, it will be posted by a Staff Member to #active-pc-sheet-links at which time your character can officially be played on the server.
  2. While not required, it is highly recommended you set up a "tupperbot" for your character. This allows you to speak "in character" easier when participating in role-play. Refer to Discord Commands for more information on the tools we use.
  3. While not required, if you desire you may introduce your character in #pc-introductions and include an image and short description of them.

Changing your Starting Choices

Sometimes your original concept for a build doesn't exactly work out. We get it. While you are in T1, you can make any changes you wish to your character to bring it in line with what will be most fun for you to play. Once you have made changes, post a summary to #transcript for review and records keeping. Once your PC is in T2, your choices are locked in without following Retraining Rules where they apply.

Regardless of any other changes your PC's name must not change.

Character Progression

Character Progression

Character Progression

Gaining Experience

Once your character has been approved, any successful gameplay logged in #story-log or #records will provide you with XP to add to your sheet. Characters level up following the normal XP Tables defined in the Dungeonmaster’s Guide.

PC Tiers and Levels

Gameplay is generally restricted to “Tiers” as defined in the Dungeonmaster’s Guide.

Tier Level Range
Tier 1 1-4
Tier 2 5-10
Tier 3 11-16
Tier 4 17-20
Post-20 “21-26”
Paragon Special

Item Rarity and PC Level Restrictions

The item restrictions below determine whether your PC is able to use/attune to a magic item:

Tier Level Range Rarity
Tier 1 1-4 Uncommon
Tier 2 5-10 Rare
Tier 3 11-16 Very Rare
Tier 4 17-20 Legendary

Soft Level Cap

You have the option to apply a level cap to any of your PCs. If you choose to do this, any experience you would have gained while capped cannot be applied at a later time/date. You must state your intention to cap a character in #transcript. If you wish to uncap the character, you must announce your intention to do so the same way. Either instance will be posted to #records for record keeping.

Character Retirement

Sometimes the arc of a character results in their retirement from the life of an adventurer. Other times you may simply wish to no longer play that character. It is possible to turn that character into an NPC via ‘retirement’. See Character Retirement for a full understanding of how to retire a PC.

Core / Character

Character Retirement

Character Retirement

Character Retirement

Sometimes the arc of a character results in their retirement from the life of an adventurer. Other times you may simply wish to no longer play that character. It is possible to turn that character into an NPC via ‘retirement’. Simply make a post in the #transcript channel stating your intention to retire the character as an NPC. To unretire a PC NPC, they start at level 1-3 and need to start as if they are new PC.

Defining What A Retired PC Can Do in Regards for Their Downtime Activities

Retired PCs Can:

  • Craft
  • Perform Services (Including spellcasting.)
  • Run Businesses, Organizations, and other passive income/influence.

Retired PCs Cannot

  • Train
  • Obtain Vehicle or Tool Profs
  • Obtain Languages
  • Other Item Production (Such as using class features for item production)

Converting an NPC to a PC

To unretire a PC NPC, they start at level 1-3 and need to start as if they are a new PC.

Unretirement

  • Unretiring requires a PC slot available.
  • Unretiring characters are limited to level 20 (post20’s revert back to level 20).
  • Retired PC sheet link must be in ⁠npc-listings to keep any form of wealth or level. If the sheet isn’t there, then the PC must be created as any new PC would be

Unretiring an ex PC

Unretire at previous level with old items and gold, provided the following:

  • 2d4 * PC level days of retraining (via downtime)
  • PC can still be used to roleplay/adventure while retraining
  • Cooldown of 1 month to unretire another PC
  • Make a report and post in ⁠transcript (staff approving will roll the 2d4)
  • Report should consist of player name, character name, and character level

Otherwise, the PC will

Methods to Speed Up Unretirement

RP related to returning to adventuring, retraining, or something of the sort. Submit a rp xp request, but state you want it to speed up retraining instead. Staff approving the request decides how many days to remove, to a max of 10.

Money Pit
Tier Daily Cost Maximum # of Days
T1 - -
T2 1,000 gp 3 Days
T3 10,000 gp 5 Days
T4 20,000 gp 5 Days
Core / Character

Companion PCs

Companion PCs

What this Document Contains:

  • Companion Leveling System
  • Converting your Companions to Player Characters
  • Boon of Ascension

Companion Leveling System

Presenting the Companion Leveling System, allowing creatures special to your characters to gain a spotlight of their own, matching the power-scaling of the character themselves. Below details the system and how your companions can gain levels, and which are eligible for use in this system.

Eligible Companions

All subclass companions are eligible for this system. This includes, but is not limited to:

  • Beast Master’s Animal Companion
  • The Extraplanar’s Planar Tether
  • Purple Dragon Knight’s Amethyst Dragon
  • Battle Smith’s Steel Defender

Other creatures can be eligible, but must be either permanently available to you, or otherwise not tied to a duration. Examples of this include:

  • Creatures Tamed by your character
  • Artificer’s Homunculus Servant
  • Spirits Summoned by Find Familiar, Find Steed, or similar magic

Hirelings are not eligible for this system.

Starting the Leveling Process

To start the leveling process for a character’s companion, the character must first take the [Boon of Ascension] detailed later in this document. This boon may be taken multiple times, but only once for each 20 class levels a character has.

When the character takes the boon, they may select a single companion that they control and is eligible for this system, and grant that creature a single level in a class of their choosing. The creature then may gain experience through RP as if they were a paragon PC, with the ability to level up all the way to P26. A companion under this system has the following restrictions:

  • The companion must fill an empty PC slot. You cannot add a creature to this system if you do not have an available slot.
  • The companion does not gain a Boon, Blessing, or Feat at P26, but must still meet the requisite xp to enter a new paragon cycle in order to do so.
  • The companion counts as a controlled entity for the purposes of Hunts, Trials, Raids, etc. A DM can rule otherwise for the purpose of quests.
  • The companion may not reach a level higher than the original character.

In return, the companion gains the following benefits:

  • If the companions actions are normally determined by the original character’s actions, bonus actions, or other similar requirements, they no longer need to do so in order to act.
  • The companion rolls its own initiative in combat.
  • The companion retains any benefits that it had as part of the original character’s class features

Converting Your Companions to Playable Characters

This section contains guidelines for converting your companions into player characters.

Hit Points

When your companion becomes a player character through this system, it retains its previous hit point maximum. It then gains hit points equal to the [Hit Points at 1st Level] hit points of the class it gains, and [Hit Points at Higher Levels] as it gains levels.

Proficiencies

Your companion also retains any skill or saving throw proficiencies it had, as well as any bonuses to them that your class features provided.

In addition, your companion gains the skill, saving throw, tool, weapon, and armor proficiencies that would normally be given with their selected class.

Armor and Other Equipment: More bestial creatures can still make use of barding, of which they are always considered proficient. In order to use weapons, a creature must have a reasonable capacity to use it. If a creature is a size other than medium, any weapons and armor it uses must be properly sized for its use, following the same price conversions as barding.

Submission

You may create a character sheet for your companion on any of the available platforms that allow you to do so. Some may be better suited than others for this. When your sheet is completed, you may submit it as normal to #transcript for approval. Please provide the original character’s name, and specify that the sheet is for a companion when you do so.

Example: docs.google.com/spreadsheets/therestoftheurl Companion Sheet of Syn. Original Character: Bim

Boon of Ascension

Below are the details of the Boon of Ascension

Boon of Ascension - Boon - Repeatable

Prerequisites: Having at least one companion eligible for ascension

One eligible companion of your choice gains a level in a single class of your choosing. The companion then may level as normal as through the Paragon System.

Core / Character

Death and Retrieval

Death and Retrieval

Death and Retrieval

If you are being revived by a member of your own party during the course of any content, revival is successful with no penalty aside from the typical cost of casting and any damage to your body or belongings.

If you died but your party succeeded, you may skip the below retrieval steps provided that the party members state your corpse was recovered.

Body Retrieval: Hunts

Characters wishing to return to the scene of a failed hunt to recover their fallen allies or missing friends may do so by engaging the creature that killed them, by targeting them in a hunt. Once the enemy has been defeated, make a body retrieval (Investigation) check.

Body Retrieval: Trials

To retrieve lost bodies in Trials of Tempus, a new party must first spawn into the trial per all the usual rules at the same level of the bodies. The players must then fight through the temple to secure the room containing the corpses before recovery is possible. Once the room is secured, make a body retrieval (Investigation) check.

Body Retrieval: Mapped Hunts

Characters wishing to return to the scene of a failed hunt to recover their fallen allies or missing friends may do so by engaging in a random deadly hunt using the applicable alias of the same tier as the dead party. Once the enemy has been defeated, make a body retrieval (Investigation) check.

Body Retrieval: Delves

  1. The Party is banished to a special retrieval zone that acts like a hunting ground
  2. Any Tier party, excluding Paragon, can attempt to retrieve them, but there needs to be In character motivation or reason to look for the party. #leaveanote
  3. The Party will do a random hunt at deadly difficulty for the Party, upon conclusion of the hunt. A single Investigation check per dead body can be made to retrieve the dead party members.
    1. If the party fails the check, they must do another random hunt to repeat the attempt

Body Retrieval: Other

If you die as a part of a quest or roleplay session run by a @Dungeonmaster, who will provide you details about the location and condition of your body, as well as any necessary information regarding retrieval.

Body Retrieval Checks

Only PCs within the same tier as the dead character may participate in body retrieval. Once the enemy has been defeated, make a body retrieval (Investigation) check:

Tier Investigation DC
T1 10
T2 15
T3 20
T4 25
Post-20 30

Leaving a Note

If your PC is going on a dangerous mission, read below!

Leave a Note Before You Go:

• Tag: @YourName | PC Name

• What part of the map are you’re exploring (coords or pin)

• How long do you expect to be gone • When others should start searching

• How you want to be revived if you die

• If you don’t list revival plans, retrieval parties decide your fate

• Unknown/isolated PCs may not be retrieved at all

•Leaving a note does not guarantee that the party will perform the task as wished as this extends outside of the player's control

Pre Retrievals MUST be roleplayed and require staff approval. It is not necessary to roleplay dungeons/hunts/raids

Further Options: Fate’s Offer – Return from the Dead Quest Hosted by: @ todo (Entity: Fate) If your PC dies and can’t be retrieved, this quest gives a final chance to return. High risk. If you fail, your PC is likely lost forever. Open and always available.

Elysium Corpse Collection Agency

The first time a PC dies within a trial or hunt in tier 1, their body is automatically collected and brought to a nearby clinic, where they are revived via raise dead or resurrection (in cases of disintegration). Note that this only occurs once per pc, and thus will not be available after prestige, or retirement.

For tracking reasons, when this is done, add Collection Agency in a separate line within the hunt or trial transcript, with the collected character's name printed again after it in the case of multiple characters.

Core / Character

Followers and Attunement

Followers and Attunement

Summoned and PC controlled entities, can attune to magic items, but they share the attunement slot of the PC. Examples of Entities: Simulacrum, Familiars, Beast companions, steel defender, undead, planar bound summons, etc.

When a controlled entity uses a PC's attunement slot to attune to an item. Only one item of the same name can be attuned by either PC or Controlled entity. ex: A Wizard and their Simulacrum can't both be attuned to Illusionist Bracers.

Core / Character

Leaving the Server

Leaving the Server

Leaving TWR

Sometimes, you feel the need to take a break from the server or leave. That's okay! However, if you DO plan on leaving, you should retire your PCs so that the sheets are not lost.

When a player leaves, their sheets will be moved to the Inactive PC Links thread.

If you wish to bring back an Inactive PC, just post in #transcript with a link to their inactive sheet and a staff member will move it for you.

Core / Character

Player-Run NPCs

Player-Run NPCs

Player-ran NPCs

A player may run an NPC with the following caveats. Breaking any requires the permission of a @Dungeonmaster or @Loremaster.

1: The NPC must act according to its character, or alignment.

2: The NPC cannot be a high-standing or of great importance individual.

3: The NPC must be given adequate reason to physically exist in this plane.

4: The NPC cannot grant PC's mechanical benefits of any sort. Items, Crafting, Gifts, all of the like. Only acceptable as shopkeep or storefronts selling items.

----

Rule 1 dictates that monsters must act relevant to lore. To break such action, or to play an outlier, requires permission.

Rule 2 dictates that NPC roleplayed must be of low bearing. Shopkeep, Bartenders, Apprentices and the generic like. A player cannot run any characters which could influence a greater plot that they are not actively running.

Rule 3 dictates that no creature may exist without bearing. A mind flayer would not exist in a town as a vampire lord would not be sleeping in a forest.

Rule 4 dictates that NPC may not grant mechanical benefits. Pure and simple, save shopkeeps selling mundane items at reasonable (per market discretion) prices.

Core / Character

Post-20 Rewards

Post-20 Rewards

Post 20 Rewards

A Player Character is considered to be Post20 if they have reached 385,000xp, and receive rewards at the following thresholds:

XP Threshold Reward
385,000 ASI +1
415,000 AS1 +1
445,000 Boon/Feat/Blessing
475,000 AS1 +1
505,000 AS1 +1
535,000 Boon/Feat/Blessing

Post-20 Rules

  • Boon/Blessing/Feat choices are permanent.
  • Your PC's first Boon/Blessing may be chosen from the list of Boons or Blessings once the slot has been unlocked (use the !boon or !blessing command in discord)
    • For PCs who earned Boons via a quest before this change, you may choose the next Boon slot that you unlock through the Post-20 or Paragon systems
  • Feats can be selected once unlocked.
  • Feats can be retrained into quested Boons/Blessings if desired
  • Boon and Blessing choices are permanent
  • Blessings/Charms can be removed by the granting Deity at DM discretion.
  • Blessings are not limited to a fixed list, and can be shaped and created to better fit a circumstance, at the DM’s discretion. This would require a majority vote to proceed.
  • Post 20 Boons and Blessings can be obtained using the Wish spell, but the Wish must be worded appropriately. This only applies to the second Boon slot of a PC's first 20 levels. PCs cannot use Wish to gain boons or blessings for any paragon cycle boon slots.
  • A comprehensive list of blessing and boons can be viewed on discord using !boon or !blessing
  • Please post your Post 20 rewards in #transcript as you receive them
  • A PC that gets Post20 rewards is still considered a level 20 character for all intents and purposes
Core / Character

The Cursed Role

The Cursed Role

The @Cursed Role

  1. If a player leaves during a quest, trial, or other event without the permission of the DM or person running it, they will be cursed, and put into the @Cursed role for two weeks.
  2. During this time, all characters belonging to the player receive only half XP and gold rewards, and cannot be resurrected if killed (except via Revivify spell).
  3. The @cursed role may also be given for other offenses at the discretion of the DM, Moderator, and Admin teams.

Approved 5.5e (Dungeons & Dragons 5th Edition (2024)) Sourcebooks will only permit use of the below types of features. Please note that 5.5e Backgrounds are never approved. The types of content which will be approved are:

  • Species
  • Classes
  • Subclasses
  • Feats
  • Spells
  • Items

  1. DMs have the right to refuse characters a spot in their quests, including those using UA/Homebrew supplements otherwise permitted by the server

Steps to Submitting a New Character

  1. Submit a link to your character sheet using the Character Submission template pinned in #transcript for Staff review and approval. Once approved, it will be posted by a Staff Member to #active-pc-sheet-links at which time your character can officially be played on the server.
  2. While not required, it is highly recommended you set up a "tupperbot" for your character. This allows you to speak "in character" easier when participating in role-play. Refer to Discord Commands for more information on the tools we use.
  3. While not required, if you desire you may introduce your character in #pc-introductions and include an image and short description of them.

Changing your Starting Choices

Sometimes your original concept for a build doesn't exactly work out. We get it. While you are in T1, you can make any changes you wish to your character to bring it in line with what will be most fun for you to play. Once you have made changes, post a summary to #transcript for review and records keeping. Once your PC is in T2, your choices are locked in without following Retraining Rules where they apply.

Regardless of any other changes your PC's name must not change.

Soft Level Cap

You have the option to apply a level cap to any of your PCs. If you choose to do this, any experience you would have gained while capped cannot be applied at a later time/date. You must state your intention to cap a character in #transcript. If you wish to uncap the character, you must announce your intention to do so the same way. Either instance will be posted to #records for record keeping.

Character Retirement

Sometimes the arc of a character results in their retirement from the life of an adventurer. Other times you may simply wish to no longer play that character. It is possible to turn that character into an NPC via ‘retirement’. See Character Retirement for a full understanding of how to retire a PC.

Character Retirement

Character Retirement

Character Retirement

Sometimes the arc of a character results in their retirement from the life of an adventurer. Other times you may simply wish to no longer play that character. It is possible to turn that character into an NPC via ‘retirement’. Simply make a post in the #transcript channel stating your intention to retire the character as an NPC. To unretire a PC NPC, they start at level 1-3 and need to start as if they are new PC.

Defining What A Retired PC Can Do in Regards for Their Downtime Activities

Retired PCs Can:

  • Craft
  • Perform Services (Including spellcasting.)
  • Run Businesses, Organizations, and other passive income/influence.

Retired PCs Cannot

  • Train
  • Obtain Vehicle or Tool Profs
  • Obtain Languages
  • Other Item Production (Such as using class features for item production)

Converting an NPC to a PC

To unretire a PC NPC, they start at level 1-3 and need to start as if they are a new PC.

Unretirement

  • Unretiring requires a PC slot available.
  • Unretiring characters are limited to level 20 (post20’s revert back to level 20).
  • Retired PC sheet link must be in ⁠npc-listings to keep any form of wealth or level. If the sheet isn’t there, then the PC must be created as any new PC would be

Unretiring an ex PC

Unretire at previous level with old items and gold, provided the following:

  • 2d4 * PC level days of retraining (via downtime)
  • PC can still be used to roleplay/adventure while retraining
  • Cooldown of 1 month to unretire another PC
  • Make a report and post in ⁠transcript (staff approving will roll the 2d4)
  • Report should consist of player name, character name, and character level

Otherwise, the PC will

Methods to Speed Up Unretirement

RP related to returning to adventuring, retraining, or something of the sort. Submit a rp xp request, but state you want it to speed up retraining instead. Staff approving the request decides how many days to remove, to a max of 10.

Code of Conduct

Code of Conduct

Code of Conduct

TWR is a server based on mutual respect. Rude, disruptive, and generally toxic behavior will be subject to moderator review. Below are some explanations of behavior which is not acceptable, but this is by no means an exhaustive list:

  1. Abuse/harassment/bullying/threats of mental or physical harm against one or more people.
  2. Insults directed against any player or staff on the server.
  3. Repeated insensitive or inappropriate jokes. Be respectful of subjects such as race, religion, politics, etc.
  4. Use of any type of slur.
  5. Threats of self harm Self harm is a serious matter and should not be joked about or taken lightly.
  6. Follow Discord TOS found here https://discord.com/terms
  7. No spamming, raiding, or anything that disturbs the peace.
    1. While mods and admins are here to help you, abuse of moderator or staff pings may result in a warning.
    2. Voice chats: Don’t play any alarmingly loud sounds or scream into the mic.
  8. Please keep channel content appropriate to the channel being used
    1. Keep memes and shitposting to #the-c-o-r-n-e-r where possible. #general can be a fun place, but please don’t flood the channel with memes.
    2. Swearing is banned in #the-peoples-court
    3. Roleplay in RP channels, Out of Character talk in OOC etc
  9. Art Advertising or solicitation of any kind is not allowed.

If you are ever made to feel uncomfortable by content on the server, or by someone’s behavior, please report it to anyone with the @Moderator or @Admin role. We want everyone to feel comfortable and safe here.

Core

Companion PCs

Companion PCs

What this Document Contains:

  • Companion Leveling System
  • Converting your Companions to Player Characters
  • Boon of Ascension

Companion Leveling System

Presenting the Companion Leveling System, allowing creatures special to your characters to gain a spotlight of their own, matching the power-scaling of the character themselves. Below details the system and how your companions can gain levels, and which are eligible for use in this system.

Eligible Companions

All subclass companions are eligible for this system. This includes, but is not limited to:

  • Beast Master’s Animal Companion
  • The Extraplanar’s Planar Tether
  • Purple Dragon Knight’s Amethyst Dragon
  • Battle Smith’s Steel Defender

Other creatures can be eligible, but must be either permanently available to you, or otherwise not tied to a duration. Examples of this include:

  • Creatures Tamed by your character
  • Artificer’s Homunculus Servant
  • Spirits Summoned by Find Familiar, Find Steed, or similar magic

Hirelings are not eligible for this system.

Starting the Leveling Process

To start the leveling process for a character’s companion, the character must first take the [Boon of Ascension] detailed later in this document. This boon may be taken multiple times, but only once for each 20 class levels a character has.

When the character takes the boon, they may select a single companion that they control and is eligible for this system, and grant that creature a single level in a class of their choosing. The creature then may gain experience through RP as if they were a paragon PC, with the ability to level up all the way to P26. A companion under this system has the following restrictions:

  • The companion must fill an empty PC slot. You cannot add a creature to this system if you do not have an available slot.
  • The companion does not gain a Boon, Blessing, or Feat at P26, but must still meet the requisite xp to enter a new paragon cycle in order to do so.
  • The companion counts as a controlled entity for the purposes of Hunts, Trials, Raids, etc. A DM can rule otherwise for the purpose of quests.
  • The companion may not reach a level higher than the original character.

In return, the companion gains the following benefits:

  • If the companions actions are normally determined by the original character’s actions, bonus actions, or other similar requirements, they no longer need to do so in order to act.
  • The companion rolls its own initiative in combat.
  • The companion retains any benefits that it had as part of the original character’s class features

Converting Your Companions to Playable Characters

This section contains guidelines for converting your companions into player characters.

Hit Points

When your companion becomes a player character through this system, it retains its previous hit point maximum. It then gains hit points equal to the [Hit Points at 1st Level] hit points of the class it gains, and [Hit Points at Higher Levels] as it gains levels.

Proficiencies

Your companion also retains any skill or saving throw proficiencies it had, as well as any bonuses to them that your class features provided.

In addition, your companion gains the skill, saving throw, tool, weapon, and armor proficiencies that would normally be given with their selected class.

Armor and Other Equipment: More bestial creatures can still make use of barding, of which they are always considered proficient. In order to use weapons, a creature must have a reasonable capacity to use it. If a creature is a size other than medium, any weapons and armor it uses must be properly sized for its use, following the same price conversions as barding.

Submission

You may create a character sheet for your companion on any of the available platforms that allow you to do so. Some may be better suited than others for this. When your sheet is completed, you may submit it as normal to #transcript for approval. Please provide the original character’s name, and specify that the sheet is for a companion when you do so.

Example: docs.google.com/spreadsheets/therestoftheurl Companion Sheet of Syn. Original Character: Bim

Boon of Ascension

Below are the details of the Boon of Ascension

Boon of Ascension - Boon - Repeatable

Prerequisites: Having at least one companion eligible for ascension

One eligible companion of your choice gains a level in a single class of your choosing. The companion then may level as normal as through the Paragon System.

Core

Daily Life on TWR

Daily Life on TWR

The Passage of Time

Time passes at the same rate within the world of TWR that it passes in our world. For easy reference, there is a channel in the server that lists the time on Elysium. This is an optional time you can use for coordination and envinronmental change, but you may act out your character’s life within each day as it meets your schedule.

Daily Reset

For the purposes of downtime and daily activities, your PC’s day begins when you wake up in the morning and ends when you go to bed. For fringe cases, daily resets should occur roughly every 24 hours.

Daily Resources

Each day, characters have the following resources:

Hunting Tags - 5
Trial Tags - 2
Downtime Hours - 8
Long Rest - 1 *
Short Rest - 8 *

Long and Short Rests

Aside from rests which occur in Trials or Quests, players are limited to 1 Long Rest and 8 Short Rests per day. These can be taken at the player’s discretion by using the !sr or !lr command in discord.

Quest Locks & Restrictions

During the course of a quest, characters may be restricted by the DM from pursuing hunts, trials, downtime options and rests as usual. While your PC is attending a quest, work with your DM to determine what parts of their daily routine can be continued.

Repetitive Actions

Some spells or projects require daily activity to fully realize. In cases like this, players should post in #transcript describing the action, how long they will repeat it, and outlining all the materials required (which must be procured ahead of time). Staff will then review the post, notify you of any issues or extra requirements, and when the time has passed your actions will become official.

Downtime

Each PC may utilize 8 hours per day of downtime to further their character’s goals and story. Downtime options can be pursued as outlined by RAW in books such as the PHB, DMG, and XGtE. Some examples include crafting magical items, performing research, gambling, or working a mundane job. Additional downtime options may be defined in other TWR supplements.

This server uses the “Optional Rule” for sleep deprivation located in Xanathar’s Guide to Everything if you wish to work through the night.

Core

Death and Retrieval

Death and Retrieval

Death and Retrieval

If you are being revived by a member of your own party during the course of any content, revival is successful with no penalty aside from the typical cost of casting and any damage to your body or belongings.

If you died but your party succeeded, you may skip the below retrieval steps provided that the party members state your corpse was recovered.

Body Retrieval: Hunts

Characters wishing to return to the scene of a failed hunt to recover their fallen allies or missing friends may do so by engaging the creature that killed them, by targeting them in a hunt. Once the enemy has been defeated, make a body retrieval (Investigation) check.

Body Retrieval: Trials

To retrieve lost bodies in Trials of Tempus, a new party must first spawn into the trial per all the usual rules at the same level of the bodies. The players must then fight through the temple to secure the room containing the corpses before recovery is possible. Once the room is secured, make a body retrieval (Investigation) check.

Body Retrieval: Mapped Hunts

Characters wishing to return to the scene of a failed hunt to recover their fallen allies or missing friends may do so by engaging in a random deadly hunt using the applicable alias of the same tier as the dead party. Once the enemy has been defeated, make a body retrieval (Investigation) check.

Body Retrieval: Delves

  1. The Party is banished to a special retrieval zone that acts like a hunting ground
  2. Any Tier party, excluding Paragon, can attempt to retrieve them, but there needs to be In character motivation or reason to look for the party. #leaveanote
  3. The Party will do a random hunt at deadly difficulty for the Party, upon conclusion of the hunt. A single Investigation check per dead body can be made to retrieve the dead party members.
    1. If the party fails the check, they must do another random hunt to repeat the attempt

Body Retrieval: Other

If you die as a part of a quest or roleplay session run by a @Dungeonmaster, who will provide you details about the location and condition of your body, as well as any necessary information regarding retrieval.

Body Retrieval Checks

Only PCs within the same tier as the dead character may participate in body retrieval. Once the enemy has been defeated, make a body retrieval (Investigation) check:

Tier Investigation DC
T1 10
T2 15
T3 20
T4 25
Post-20 30

Leaving a Note

If your PC is going on a dangerous mission, read below!

Leave a Note Before You Go:

• Tag: @YourName | PC Name

• What part of the map are you’re exploring (coords or pin)

• How long do you expect to be gone • When others should start searching

• How you want to be revived if you die

• If you don’t list revival plans, retrieval parties decide your fate

• Unknown/isolated PCs may not be retrieved at all

•Leaving a note does not guarantee that the party will perform the task as wished as this extends outside of the player's control

Pre Retrievals MUST be roleplayed and require staff approval. It is not necessary to roleplay dungeons/hunts/raids

Further Options: Fate’s Offer – Return from the Dead Quest Hosted by: @ todo (Entity: Fate) If your PC dies and can’t be retrieved, this quest gives a final chance to return. High risk. If you fail, your PC is likely lost forever. Open and always available.

Elysium Corpse Collection Agency

The first time a PC dies within a trial or hunt in tier 1, their body is automatically collected and brought to a nearby clinic, where they are revived via raise dead or resurrection (in cases of disintegration). Note that this only occurs once per pc, and thus will not be available after prestige, or retirement.

For tracking reasons, when this is done, add Collection Agency in a separate line within the hunt or trial transcript, with the collected character's name printed again after it in the case of multiple characters.

Disciplinary Info

Disciplinary Info

  1. Violation of any of the rules will generally result in a verbal warning.
  2. A second violation of the same rule will result in a strike. A strike typically lasts for 2 months from the date of issue.
  3. Players with three active strikes will be banned from TWR for a 3 month period
  4. Any other disciplinary action up to and including a permanent ban may be dispensed by the mods following a majority vote.

Bans issued for any reason are, of course, subject to an optional appeal by the offending player, if they should choose to do so. Contact a @Moderator or @Admin if you wish to appeal a ban issued to you or to another member of the server.

Core / Economics

Agriculture System

Agriculture System

Agriculture System

How to Start Your Farm

  1. Choose what crops and land you will be using: Select a crop from the list available in the document below. Each crop has a maximum amount that can be planted per acre, a cost per pound, and a base yield stat which determines the multiplier of how much crops you gain at the end of a growing period. The minimum amount of land you must have to use the agriculture system is one acre, and each crop takes 90 days to plant and/or harvest. To use the agriculture system, you must select an amount of acres of land that you own to become farmland.
  2. Determine the Statistics of your Land: Ping Craftmaster in ⁠#crafting-ooc stating where geographically you are planting. You will be told the statistics of the land, including Disease Resistance, Pest Resistance, Ground quality, and weather. Multiply these together with the yield- this is your overall amount of crops gained. These statistics can be increased for the next growing period using roleplay and money investments submitted to the Craftmaster team.
  3. Find Workers: A hireling of any CR is required to work your land. Each hireling can work on 3 acres for the entire 90 days of a growing period. You must pay the deployed rate for the hireling for each day of the growing period. The amount of time and gold it takes to originally till an acre of land to be ready for crops is negligible. Any supplies and resources used in the growing process are included in the hireling’s pay.
  4. Submit a filled in Template to ⁠#crafting-submissions.

Alchemy System

Alchemy System

Alchemy System

Gathering

  1. Use Downtime to Gather Herbs, max usage 3x a day (uses 8 hours in a session). Note: You can no longer sacrifice adventuring time to harvest extra herbs.

  2. Choose one environment [Cave, Forest, Desert, Grasslands, Swamp] + Rarity [Common, Uncommon, Rare, Very Rare]

  3. Roll Nature/Medicine/Arcana + Herbalism/Poisoner/Brewer/Alchemist Tool Prof Bonus (If proficient) --> DC scales depending on rarity of ingredient. Once check is completed, post in transcript using template found in pins of transcript . Craftmaster will roll for the herb gathered randomly depending on location chosen and DC rarity met.

DCs for Enchantment Ingredients:
Rarity DC
Common DC 10
Uncommon DC 13
Rare DC 17
Very Rare DC 20
Targeted Gathering

  1. You can target herbs based on which potion you wish to make! If you are targeting a herb for a specific potion, use the Targeted gathering Template pinned in transcript

  2. If the herb you are searching for isn't in the environment you chose, you get nothing. If it is, a Craftmaster will roll the herb normally, and you only get the herb if the dice comply.

The DCs for targeted gathering are as followed:
Rarity DC
Common DC 13
Uncommon DC 17
Rare DC 20
Very Rare DC 23
Bonuses:
  1. You can only target one herb per day until you have gathered 3 of that herb, at which point you may target for two herbs per day due to your familiarity.
  2. You cannot use help actions in herb gathering. Self-Buffs are allowed for now.
  3. Nat20 Rule: If you roll nat20 on the check (RAW Nat20 without modifiers and bonuses) you get 1 Extra Herb.
  4. Over10 Rule: If your total roll is 10 over the applicable DC you get 1 Extra Herb. Example, if your total roll for a rare is 31, you get 2 Herbs instead of 1.
  5. Nat20 and Over10 rules can both apply, to a max of 3 Herbs per roll.

Potion Brewing

Potions are brewed using herbs, each herb is used for a specific potion, the potion is hinted at in the description.

Time, base Cost, Herb Requirement to brew:

Rarity Time (Days) Cost Herb Requirement
Common 2.5 25 gp 1 Herb
Uncommon 5 100 gp 1 Herb
Rare 12.5 1,000 gp 2 Herbs
Very Rare 25 10,000 gp 3 Herbs

Monster Part Substitution

You can substitute 1 Herb for a monster part, however uncommon and higher potions need at least 1 Herb.

Potion Rarity Monster CR Loot DC
Common CR 1-3 DC 13
Uncommon CR 4-8 DC 17
Rare CR 9-13 DC 21
Very Rare CR 14-18 DC 24
Legendary CR 19+ DC 26

Bulk Brewing

  • Bulk Brewing has a discount on overall cost now. For every 10 potions you make at a time, you get a 5% discount on cost, cap for the discount is 20%.
  • Bulk Brewing also requires less herbs. For every 10 potions you brew, you only need 7x the amount of herbs for one potion of the same rarity. Example: 10 common potions of healing - 7 enchantment herbs needed.

Time Reduction

  • You get a 50% time reduction if you use double the amount of enchantment herbs for the potion.
  • Sacrificing Potions:
  1.   You can sacrifice one potion per brew.
  2.   Lowers base time by half the time it takes to brew a potion of that rarity.

Construction Rules

Construction Rules

Building Rules

Walls and floors are all considered to be 1 feet thick, a 1 foot by 1 foot by 1 foot cube of material is considered to be 1 unit.

How to Build a Structure

Determine the floor plan of your building. For example, you wish to build a 20 by 20 shack made of stone brick, the walls are say 8 feet high and for ease of calculation the roof is flat, there are no extra internal walls and is just open.

If the floor is 2 feet thick, it will be 20 long x 20 wide x 2 thick = 800 units The ceiling is normal (1 feet thick) and is 400 units Walls are 8 feet high and 20 long x 8 high x 1 wide, and you have 4 of them, therefore they equate to 640 units The building is a total of 1840 units, and can now be priced and the time can be found accordingly.

Base Construction Time

Base Time: Units/100/number of workers = # workweeks it takes to construct.

Workers

Decide the wages you want to advertise to determine how many NPCs will work. A Craftmaster will roll only 1 time and that number is final.

Cost (Per NPC/Day) Roll for Workers
5 gp 1d20 NPC Workers
10 gp 1d15 + 5 NPC Workers
15 GP 1d10 + 10 NPC Workers
20 GP 1d5 + 15 NPC Workers

Note: You can do Craftmaster-approved roleplay to increase worker count, but what you roll is limited to what you can achieve without roleplay.

Notes:

  • On Elysium, the limit is 20 workers
  • Limit is based off population, depending on where you want to build. Contact craftmasters for a different limit.
  • You must decide on the wage before rolling for results
  • If you have some kind of other material you plan on using, ping a @craftmaster

Construction Material Costs

Material Selected Cost (per Unit)
Stone Brick 5 gp
Low-End Wood 4 gp
Mid-Range Wood 8 gp
High-End Wood 12 gp
Glass 10 gp

Note: Materials not listed above can be taken on a case-by-case basis. Please ping Craftmaster for approval and costs of those materials.

Core / Economics

Crafting an Item

Crafting an Item

Crafting Items

Crafter Information

  • Unnamed NPCs can only work on mundane items, and building projects. These types of crafters require a Named NPC or PC to lead the project. Unnamed NPCs working on mundane equipment are required to be paid at least 25 gp a day.
  • Named NPCs originate one of two ways; either through roleplay ran by a Dungeonmaster and approved by a Craftmaster, or when a PC retires. These types of crafters can lead their own projects, and can increase their magical crafting capabilities through means separate of both PCs and Unnamed NPCs.
  • PCs are characters that are actively being controlled by a player. These types of crafters can lead their own projects, make their own decisions (unless given up by the player to a guild), and are limited in what they can craft based on rarity which is determined based on the level of the character.

Magic Item Proficiency Requirements: A character needs to be proficient with the tools needed to craft an item and have access to the appropriate equipment. Everyone who collaborates needs to have the appropriate tool proficiency. You need to make any judgment calls regarding whether a character has the correct equipment. The following provides some examples.

  • Herbalism Kit: Antitoxin, Potion of Healing
  • Leatherworker's Tool: leather Armor, Boots
  • Smith's Tools: Armor, Weapons
  • Weaver's Tools: Cloaks, Robes
  • Tinker's Tools; Wondrous Items

Note: The above are just examples. If you can justify the use of a tool in a craft/project, it would be acceptable for that craft/project.

Magical Crafting Subsection

Any player characters (active or retired) involved with the crafting needs to meet a level requirement to craft items of certain rarities:

  • Level 1-4: Uncommon and Below
  • Level 5-10: Rare
  • Level 11-16: Very Rare
  • level 17 and up: Legendary

Named NPC: To allow for Named NPC crafters to upgrade the rarities they can craft. A specific amount of crafts of a certain rarity must be made (listed below) as well as a Wisdom check (made by PC) following the final craft (DCs also listed below).

  • Common -> Uncommon: 20 Common crafts with DC 15 Wisdom Check
  • Uncommon -> Rare : 40 Uncommon crafts with DC 18 Wisdom Check
  • Rare -> Very Rare: 60 Rare crafts with DC 20 Wisdom Check
  • Very Rare -> Legendary: 80 Very Rare crafts with DC 22 Wisdom Check

Crafting Time Calculation

When calculating time reduction, the order in which a player should calculate is as follows:

  1. Magic Item Sacrifice
  2. Magic Item Adept (MIA)
  3. Master Scrivener (MS)
  4. Workers
  5. Craft Roleplay Reduction

Magic Item Sacrificing

  • You can sacrifice one item per craft.
  • Lowers base time by half the time it takes to craft an item of the rarity of the item sacrificed.
  • Sacrificing an item that would make the craft instant instead results in the craft taking 1 day.

Magic Item Adept

  • An artificer only class feature that reduces both time and cost of crafting common and uncommon items.

Master Scrivener

  • A wizard only class feature that reduces both time and cost of scribing scrolls.

Workers

  • To a max of five; the more people working on a project, the quicker it gets done. To calculate this reduction method, you divide the base time by the amount of workers you have on the project.
  • Players who have not received the @player role cannot assist with a craft as a worker

Craft Roleplay Reduction

  • Add the initial roleplay in the crafting submission.
  • Additional roleplay regarding the craft, brew, or construction can be submitted in the crafting submissions channel.
  • No XP or favor can be given out in the same request as time reduction.
  • The Craftmaster approving the log, and any subsequent RP submissions that may follow, will determine how long it reduces by, to a max of three days per submission. No reduction can take the completion time below 1 day.
  • Reductions are capped at a 25% total reduction to the original crafting time.
  • Each roleplay request can reduce the log by more than three days, but this requires two or more Craftmaster approval.

Crafting Report Template

@you (PC Name) would like to craft x

The process includes (The crafting process. Be creative!)

(Summary of all PCs and Third Parties involved)

Total time taken: Base Time - (Item Sacrifice) / (Magic Item Adept) / (Workers) - (Roleplay Request)

Total cost: Base Cost + Wages for Workers

Materials:

  • (List of all materials used in crafting)

Mundane Crafting Summary

  • Crafting Cost = Listed Value / 4
  • Crafting Time = Listed Value / 50 Days

Magical Crafting Summary

Rarity | Time | Crafting Cost | Materials

  • Common | 5 days | 50gp | 1x CR 1-3
  • Uncommon | 10 Days | 200gp | 1x CR 4-8
  • Rare | 25 Days | 2k gp | 2x CR 9-13
  • Very Rare | 50 days | 20k gp | 3x CR 14 -18
  • Legendary | 100 days | 100k gp| 3x CR19+, of which two of the three materials for legendary crafting needs to be resulting from a quest.

Consumables take half the time and cost needed, and require 1 less monster material to craft, down to a minimum of 1 material.

Crafting material Harvesting

A player can harvest crafting materials from hunts.

A player can use survival, nature or investigation to harvest material. The DC of the check is based on CR as seen below:

  • CR 1-3: DC 13
  • CR 4-8: DC 17
  • CR 9-13: DC 21
  • CR 14-18: DC 24
  • CR 19+: DC 26

Homebrew Upgrading Rules

You can add a + enchantment onto an existing magic item. This upgrade will boost the crafted item's rarity a tier up, starting at the higher rarity item. The item's rarity can't exceed legendary, and the + enchantment can't exceed +3.

  • Example 1: Adding +1 to a Dragon Slayer Sword will make it Very Rare and +2
  • Example 2: Adding +1 to a Serpent Scale Armor will make it a Very Rare and +1

This upgrading process is limited to weapons and armors only.

Re-forging

You can re-forge the type of item you have according to the class and enchantment of the item.

  • The class of item refers to the grouping allowed by the enchantment, found in parenthesis after the item type in its description. Whether that be simple/martial, melee/ranged, any, any kind of sword, etc.
  • The enchantment of the item refers to the magical ability of the item.

You can only re-forge an item to another item of the same class and enchantment. For example, a Dragon Slayer Longsword couldn't be re-forged into a Flame Tongue Greatsword, but it could be re-forged into a Dragon Slayer Rapier.

Re-forge Cost: Half of the cost it takes to craft an item of that rarity.

Re-forge Time: Half of the time it takes to craft an item of that rarity.

  • Re-forging is only applicable with weapons and armor.
  • Magic Item Adept feature works with re-forging.

Crafting Updates

Base costs: Magic items will cost more if the base item is worth 100 gp or more will cost more accordingly

Example: Double bladed scimitar (100 gp): +1 DBS is 500 gp Plate armor (1500 gp): +1 Plate armor is 5500 gp

(these are the minimum prices)

Acheron artifacts will be considered quested leg mats and leg mats to contribute to the formation of gravity drives.

Transforming an Acheron artifact to a quested leg mat will alert enemies and players within Acheron.

Economics

Economics

Economics

Minimum Trade Value

To ensure a fair and predictable economy on TWR, trades and purchases are limited by a minimum value, which can only be exceeded through Roleplay with @dungeonmaster or @craftmaster approval.

Minimum Selling Price Limits for Trading Magical Items to Other PCs: Base Price + Rarity Mods as below. If an item does not have a base price, then just use the rarity mods below. this applies if the base price is above 400gp.

Rarity Minimum Trade Value
Common 100 gp
Uncommon 400 gp
Rare 4,000 gp
Very Rare 40,000 gp
Legendary 200,000 gp

* Consumable items can be traded for (rarity)/2 gp

For example plate being 1500 gp

the magic item variants will be 1500 gp + x amount of gold

Selling Magic Items

Players can now sell magic items to NPCs for gold, or offer it to a deity of their choice for favor.

Selling to NPCs gives the character gold equal to half the minimum price of that item. Offering it up to a deity of their choice gives the character favor equal to a quarter of what it costs to roll a random item of that category.

Selling Mundane Items

There are three item types: Scrap, Old, and New.

  • Scrap sells at 10% of sale value. Unusable
  • Old sells at 50%. Used & Starter Gear
  • New sells at 100%. Recently Forged

Repairing takes 1/8 of the item cost in material, and value/100 days. For example, 15 days for plate, around 200 gp to repair.

If Mending is used, scrap items are repaired into functional old items. Halving time on repair, unless additional replacement material is required.

Monster Parts

Crafting materials are only interchangeable for money. Monster Parts may not be traded for magic items

Gifting Rules

Characters may not gift each other money or items at will. Characters within the same party may loan each other items during the course of a quest, trial, or other content, but must retrieve their belongings at the end. If your character would like to gift an item, you must first roleplay a justification for the gift, then submit the below report to #transcript for review.

Taxes

For the sale of objects

  • Any object valued under 200gp will not be taxed.
  • Any object valued between 200gp and under 20,000gp will be taxed at 5%.
  • Any object valued at 20,000 GP and above will be taxed at 20% tax.
  • This applies per item, meaning bulk purchases are taxed based on the value of each individual object.
  • Taxes only apply when transactions occur in civilized areas

Tax Evasion Guidelines

To evade taxes of any amount, you need to roleplay the transaction at a location that would prevent the enforcement of tax.

Requirements below:

  • Administratively, the roleplay must be linked into the ⁠transaction-log.
  • Title the transaction as “Tax Evasion” for ease of search.

Failure to do so may summon an angry pink god(dess) and void the transaction or enforce the tax and other demerits.

Core / Economics

Full & Part Time Jobs

Full & Part Time Jobs

Part Time & Full Time Jobs

You can now find gainful employment within the city of Waterdeep (and abroad). This can be done in two ways, a weekly job or daily job.

Daily Jobs

Daily Jobs uses an alias in discord and can only be done once a day per PC, this also takes your downtime. To do the job, use the alias: !job skill Then link the result in #transaction-log with a short deception of what you did in character and the amount earned

Weekly Jobs

Part time jobs, such as casual work at a smithy or a bard playing for a tavern, will take up all of your downtime (meaning no crafting or learning skills) but still let you quest, hunt, and trial.

Full time jobs pay more but in addition to no downtime you will no longer have time to trail, quest, or freely adventure.

Q: How do you find employment/work?

A: Provide a brief description of the job you’re looking to do, such as a part time job at an apothecary, then roll 2d20 and add your proficiency bonus if applicable (In this case it would be alchemy or herbalism). (2d20 + applicable mod) * 14 * Tier = gp/wk using all downtime. x2 for full time, but no hunts/trials as a result Part Time tier averages T1 = 294 T2 = 588 T3 = 882 T4 = 1,176

Hireling Update 2

Team involved: @Loremaster

Hello lurkers!

This update is an addendum to the previously released Hireling spreadsheet for NPC pricing. Utilizing this, you will have guidelines with which you may hire NPCs over time, up to a predetermined maximum amount, for whatever individual, group, or organizational needs you have. If there is confusion on how this works, please use the attached spreadsheet, or ask a @Loremaster.

Contracting NPC Requirements:

Maximum CR that can be hired as a single unit is capped at CR 20

Total CR across all hired units is capped at CR = 30

Hiring occurs weekly, using a point deduction system (Hire Points)

Points accrue at a rate of 1/week from the time interest is expressed, and equate to the Total CR that can be used to hire units

Point deductions are based against the CR being hired.

Example: Player currently has total of 5 Hire Points. The player can Hire any combination of humanoid creatures less than or equal to the total CR of 5.

Spreadsheet for CR to Hire Points breakdown can be seen here: https://docs.google.com/file/d/1Qv2-Cna8BUpkpW0geMdIO68BIL-coSrd/edit?usp=docslist\_api&filetype=msexcel

Please submit these hire requests to transcript and ping a @Loremaster for approval.

Attunement and Magic Items for Hirelings Hirelings can equip and attune to magic items provided to them by their employer based upon their CR, as shown below:

  • CR 1/8 - CR 1/2: Common (no attunement)

  • CR 1 - CR 4: Uncommon (attunement up to 1 item)

  • CR 5 - 10: Rare (attunement up to 2 items)

  • CR 11 - 16: Very Rare (attunement up to 3 items)

  • CR 17+: Legendary (attunement up to 3 items)

If the hirelings statblock has an armor or weapon listed, they are treated as proficient with all weapons or armor of that same type (e.g. leather - light armor, Shortsword - martial weapons). If you have questions or concerns, please me know, and I will be working with existing groups/organizations to get you switched over to this new framework

From #Patch-Notes

Much discussion and collaboration has gone into the merger of Hireling system with the previously used Organizations system. They will now be brought under one framework, with some added rules for how groups and organizations will work under this system, how hirelings can be equipped with items from their employers, and some promising prospects for future updates.

Individual & Group Hirelings

The ability for individuals and established groups to hire NPCs to augment their personal or collaborative efforts will be broken into one of two categories, with slightly different considerations for each. Hirelings can be reskinned to represent any humanoid race or alignment, and can speak common by default.

Contracting Requirements (Individual)

Hiring updates occur once per week, using a point deduction system (Hire Points)

Points accrue at a rate of 1/week, requiring an approved post from a Loremaster These points are logged via ⁠transcript and the total equates to the Total CR that can be used to hire units for that update.

Point deductions are based on the CR being hired. CR 0 units count as CR 1/8 for this, there is a graph that breaks down these numbers in more detail.

Individuals contracting NPCs will use the 'Deployed Monthly' rate, as opposed the normal Daily/Monthly rate. These expenses are logged via ⁠transaction-log after the update is approved by a Loremaster. These expenses occur at the 1st of every month.

Maximum CR that can be hired as a single unit is capped at CR 20

Total CR that can be hired is capped at CR 20

The screenshot below shows a week-by-week breakdown of how hire points can be spent on the corresponding CR.

Contracting Requirements (Group/Organizational)

Hiring updates occur once per week, using a point deduction system (Hire Points)

Points accrue based upon the modifiers calculated for your group, from 1-10, requiring an approved post from a Loremaster. These points are logged via ⁠transcript and the total equates to the Total CR that can be used to hire units for that update.

Publicity (popularity, reputation, goodwill)

Accessibility (access, reach)

Logistics (training, supplies, budget)

Opportunity (job security, importance, need)

Temp buffs (quests/significant events)

Groups/Organizations consisting of multiple PCs behave as a single ‘entity’ for the sake of point accumulation and spending. Updates will be logged with a single PC representing the group.

Point deductions are based on the CR being hired. CR 0 units count as CR 1/8 for this, there is a graph that breaks down these numbers in more detail.

Groups/Organizations contracting NPCs will use the normal 'Monthly' rate. These expenses are logged via ⁠transaction-log after the update is approved by a Loremaster. These expenses occur at the 1st of every month.

Maximum CR that can be hired as a single unit is capped at CR 20

NPCs & Workers

NPC Crafting Update

A) Unnamed NPCs can still be hired to make mundane crafts, with minimum/no RP. Unlimited NPCs per mundane craft, although a PC still needs to lead it. You have our blessing, changes will be implemented if this is abused.

B) Named NPC Crafters require RP to be created. What ‘skill level’ this NPC starts with varies from case-to-case depending on the RP being done. Follow the chart below for upgrading rules.

NPC Upgrading

To allow for Named NPC crafters to upgrade the rarities they can craft. A specific amount of crafts of a certain rarity must be made (listed below) as well as a Wisdom check (made by PC) following the final craft (DCs also listed below).

NPC Crafter Upgrade Requirements
New Tier Minimum # of Crafts Wisdom DC
Uncommon 20 Common DC 15
Rare 40 Uncommon DC18
Very Rare 60 Rare DC20
Legendary 80 Very Rare DC22

Notes:

  • Mundane Crafters will never be able to upgrade to common or higher.
  • Link the check in the final craft (whether the check passes or not).
  • Failing the check sends you back to 50% progress.
  • Worker Limit is still 5

Retired PC Crafter Limit

Players are limited to three retired PC crafters at any one point. All retired PCs may do other allowed forms of downtime, but only three can craft at any one time.

Reason: To prevent people from overpopulating their personal supply of crafters by making and retiring PCs over and over again.

Crafter Rule Change

If a player leaves the server, their characters can not be used to craft. If a character is retired and their sheet is not posted in ⁠retired-listings, they can not be used to craft. This change also removes the 3 month mandatory check-in between Guild Owner and Employee, because the assumption is the employee can leave the guild whenever they see fit.

Note: If a craft has already been initiated, and the player or players involved in the craft leave the server, the craft will be completed on schedule.

Worker Rights

When you are using a PC to craft (everyone aside from the 'starter'), you MUST pay them each a minimum of 25 GP per day of crafting. This includes your own PCs, if applicable.

Retraining Rules

Retraining Rules

Retraining Rules

Class Retraining

By spending 10 workweeks of downtime, a character can choose to replace one of their levels in one class with a level in another class. This time is reduced by a number of workweeks equal to the character’s ability modifier in the key ability of the new class. If their new class has more than one key ability, the characters lowest ability modifier should be used for this calculation. The character must have a minimum of 13 in the key abilities of both their current class and their new class They must have an instructor of at least 1 level higher (or be level 20) than your new level in the new class and must spend 50gp per week for the instructor and relevant supplies.

Fighting Style Retraining

(For Fighters, Rangers, Paladins, Blood Hunters, and College of Swords Bards only) By spending a week of downtime, you can choose one of the (insert class name here) fighting style you know and replace it with another fighting style from the (insert class name here) class.

Feat / ASI Retraining

By spending a week of downtime, you can choose to replace one Feat or ASI you qualify for with another Feat or ASI you qualify for. Post20 ASIs can be retrained only to ASIs, and Post20 Feats can be retrained only to Boons or Feats.

Spell Retraining

(For sorcerers, warlocks, bards and rangers only) By spending a week of downtime,you can choose one of the (insert class name here) spells you know and replace it with another spell from the (insert class name here) spell list, which also must be of a level for which you have spell slots.

Mystic Arcanum Retraining

Warlocks can spend 1 week of downtime to retrain one of their mystic arcanum spells for another spell that is applicable for that version of the mystic arcanum classfeat.

RP Reduction

When you undergo retraining, you can submit an RP-XP request for roleplay related to the retraining and receive a reduction in the overall time spent retraining. Each RP-XP request is worth a 5% reduction, up to a maximum of 25%.

Retroactive Downtime

Retroactive Downtime

We get it, you can’t always plan your character’s lives in real time. That’s why we’ve designed Retroactive Downtime, which lets you apply unused downtime at a reduced wait to cover gaps in gameplay and incetivize coming back to TWR!

Starting from the last date your PC used their downtime, you can now file a report to use 1/3 of the total days (rounded down) on a single goal or downtime activity with staff approval.

How does it work?

Players wishing to file for retroactive downtime must complete the report on the right and submit it to #transcript. Staff will determine the appropriate daily value for your character and resources and return the report with any important notes.

Custom Retroactive Downtime

We are also introducing a few new forms of “retroactive” downtime you can add to the report:

General Adventuring: XP Bonus

Characters who spend their time hunting, traveling, or otherwise generally adventuring receive bonus XP:
