Core / Economics

Settlement Endeavors

Settlement Endeavors

Settlement Endeavors allow characters to attract residents, workers, specialists, and families through roleplay and investment in a growing settlement.

Sponsor

A Sponsor is an individual who begins a Settlement Endeavor.

There may be multiple Sponsors for the same Settlement.

The sponsor need not personally appear. Narrating recruiters or employees, creating housing or employment, negotiating with communities, or hosting an event may qualify.

Investment:

Each resident requires at least 25 sq. ft. of residential interior space. Empty land does not count, occupied space cannot be reused, and multiple floors count separately.

Examples: 100 sq. ft. houses 4 residents; 400 houses 16; 900 houses 36; and 2,500 houses 100.

Workshops, farms, shops, and public facilities provide employment or opportunity but only count as housing if residential space is included.

The Endeavor must link its approved Charter Request or identify unused space in an existing approved structure.

Recruitment Limit:

An individual may recruit up to 5 residents per month.

An established agency, organization, or player settlement may recruit 5 residents per participating player, to a maximum of 50 residents per month.

Only distinct players who meaningfully contribute to that month’s Endeavor count toward its limit.

The agency submits one combined monthly Endeavor through a single representative. Each character may participate in only one Settlement Endeavor per month.

Unused recruitment does not carry over. A major quest or event may receive a one-time Craftmaster and Loremaster-approved exception.

The requested population cannot exceed the settlement’s unused housing capacity.

Approval and Gain:

Craftmasters confirm construction, housing, and available support. Loremasters approve the residents’ origins, culture, faction connections, and effect on the setting.

Recruiting an established community, faction, or large migration requires approval before roleplay begins.

Staff records the final residents and approved specialists gained. A successful Endeavor may gain any number from 1 up to its recruitment limit. An unsuccessful Endeavor gains 0.

Distribution:

Note where the residents will live, what work or opportunities are available, and how they will fit into the settlement. Requested specialists or communities should be listed here.

Monthly Upkeep:

A settlement must pay 50 gp per resident each month for food and basic necessities. This includes food, clean water, medicine, clothing, fuel, sanitation, and common household supplies.

Examples: 5 residents cost 250 gp; 15 cost 750; 30 cost 1,500; 50 cost 2,500; and 100 cost 5,000.

Upkeep may be paid with coin or an equal value of appropriate food and supplies. Any number of players, Ventures, or organizations may contribute. Residents maintained through another system, such as paid hirelings, are not counted again.

Paying upkeep grants no ownership or control over residents and creates no exclusive supplier rights.

If upkeep is missed, the settlement cannot begin another Endeavor. After two consecutive missed months, 1 resident leaves for every 10 unsupported residents, minimum 1.

Hiring:

Settlement residents are independent NPCs and cannot be commanded by a sponsor.

Anyone recruited for personal service, military use, or direct control must use the appropriate hireling or follower rules.

Residents do not automatically become soldiers, controlled NPCs, or sources of passive income.

Spell Copying Rules

How to copy a spell on TWR

  • Locate a source in-character to copy the desired spell from
  • Post the above template to #transcript, including all of the relevant information
  • Once the post is moved to #records, you may add the spell to your spellbook and deduct the money from your sheet

Other Useful Tips

  • Check the "Your Spellbook" section of the PHB for information on creating a backup or replacing a spellbook
  • Check the Retroactive Downtime rules if you forget or get busy!
  • Don't forget, copying takes time! You haven't finished coyping until the post moves to #records

** 📚 Spell Copying 📚 **

*PC Name:* [Name] (@discordtag)

*Spell Source:* Name the player or NPC providing the spell

*Spells Copied:* List any spells learned here

*Reductions:* List any Subclass reductions or other buffs here

*Gold Spent:* List the final cost for all copied spells here

*Time Taken:* List the amount of downtime spent copying (round to the next day) here

Core / Economics

Training Downtime

Training Downtime

Training Downtime

Characters can perform activities to train and practice in their free time, those who do not wish to hunt can spend time training themselves as well, this could be tinkering and experimenting for Artificers, praying and studying for Clerics, scribing and practicing spells for Wizards, sparring for fighters, and stealthing around for rogues, all forms of training are applicable and make no mechanical difference

Characters can choose to spend 5 Hunting Tags or expend 8 hours of downtime in training which awards experience points to reflect the development of skills. Players who choose to roleplay the lessons will be awarded with additional RPXP as per usual

Tier | XP Per Day (not RPXP) 1 | 100 xp 2 | 250 xp 3 | 500 xp 4 | 1,000 xp Post-20 | 2,000 xp

Core / Economics

Ventures

Ventures

Business empires and peddler wagons. Player characters can now obtain money, experience, and more by roleplaying their business ventures. The owner of a venture, need not be personally involved. Narration of employees and the setting or providing venues for an event qualifies for gain.

Investment:

The value of things committed to make coin. Capital is the stuff that are not consumed in the venture. General examples: land, property, and facilities.

Gain:

Scaling from 0 to 200% of the investment. Graded by pinks and bookworms.

Because we do not capture depreciation here, more weight will be given to expended coin than capital, which can be reused. Do not be surprised if your million gold cargo ship does not get you 1.5 million in returns.

Distribution:

Player notes the percentage of gain given to people involved.

If you wish for particular items, materials, or other gains that are not coin, do it here and mark to whom it should go to.

Pinks/bookworms will revise this section which tells the player(s) what was earned. Including RPXP.

Artillerist Artificer Subclass Addition

- They are now granted proficiency with firearms if they do not already have it.

- Eldritch Cannons, when tiny, can now be integrated into a firearm. They now move with you if integrated, but otherwise function RAW.

- The Arcane Firearm feature can now be used on firearms as well, instead of just a wand, staff, or rod.

Infusion Master (18th level Artificer) - Optional Class Feature

Starting at 18th level, you can apply infusions and magical tinkering on magic items, however bonuses to attack rolls, damage, and armor class cannot exceed +3

Spell Storing Addition

At 11th level, you can now store a spell in an object. Whenever you finish a long rest, you can touch one simple or martial weapon or one item that you can use as a spellcasting focus, and you store a spell in it, choosing a 1st- or 2nd-level spell from the artificer spell list that requires 1 action to cast (you needn't have it prepared). You may upcast a 1st level spell to use a 2nd level slot, if previous conditions are applicable. (edited)

Artificer: Alchemist Balance Update

Experimental Elixir

Drinking an Elixir: As a Bonus Action, a creature can drink the elixir or administer it to another creature within 5 feet of itself.

You can create additional experimental elixirs by expending a spell slot of 1st level or higher (to a maximum of 5th level) for each one. When you do so, you use your action to create the elixir in an empty flask you touch, and you choose the elixir's effect from the Experimental Elixir table.

Experimental Elixir

d6    Effect

1    Healing. The drinker regains a number of hit points equal to 2d4 + your Intelligence Modifier (+2d4 hit points restored for every spell slot level above 1st)

2    Swiftness. The drinker's walking speed increases by 10 feet for 1 hour. (+10 feet walking speed for every two spell slot levels above 1st)

3    Resilience. The drinker gains a +1 bonus to AC for 10 minutes. (+1 bonus to AC for every two spell slot levels above 1st)

4    Boldness. The drinker can roll a d4 and add the number rolled to every attack roll and saving throw they make for the next minute.

5    Flight. The drinker gains a flying speed of 10 feet for 10 minutes. (+10 feet flying speed for every two spell slot levels above 1st)

6    Transformation. The drinker's body is transformed as if by the Alter Self spell. The drinker determines the transformation caused by the spell, the effects of which last for 10 minutes.

Restorative Reagents

Whenever a creature drinks an experimental elixir you created, the creature gains temporary hit points equal to your Intelligence modifier plus your Artificer level

Armorer Artificer Option. Dreadnought

Dreadnought: you design your armor to become a towering juggernaut in battle it has the following features:
Armor Flail: an iron ball on a chain appears on one of your armor's gauntlets and has the following traits:
Weapon damage: 1d10+ability modifier used for the attack roll (bludgeoning)
Weapon Category: Simple melee
Properties: Reach

Giant Stature: As a bonus action you transform and enlarge your armor for one minute. For the duration your reach increases by 5 ft, and if you are smaller then large you become large, along with anything your wearing. If there isnt enough room for you to increase your size, your size doesnt change. You can use this Bonus Action a number of times equal to your intelligence modifier (minimum of once). You regain all uses when you finish a Long Rest.

Wrecking ball: If you hit a creature that is atleast one size smaller then you with the flail, you can push that creature up to 10 ft straight away from yourself or pull the creature up to 10 ft toward yourself.

Level 15 Perfected Armor: Your arcane armor gains additional benefits based on its model as detailed below:

Dreadnought: The damage for your flail increases to be 2d6 bludgeoning. In addition when you use your Giant Stature, you can increase your size to large or huge, your choice. you also gain a fly speed equal to your speed.

Clone (Errata)

:::warning [LEGACY GATE DISCLAIMER]
This errata applies to a standard 2014 spell/feature that does not have a corresponding page in the TWR Wiki.
It is preserved here for completeness.
:::

Clone Limitations

All PCs can have one active clone without fear of reprisal.

To unlock the second clone slot, there must be a significant entreaty to Kelemvor, or alternative god of death, or a significant effort to control the manipulation of the soul.

To unlock the third clone slot temporarily, the same process as above is applied but with greater scrutiny. A higher bar to achieve.

Mechanics Note:

Those that have more than one clone right now can pick one from what they have. The rest go inert and are permanently inactive.

Monetary Note:

Materials costing gold that were used in the casting/storage of clones are refunded. Log the refund in ⁠transaction-log and provide proof of the expense. If you casted the Clone spell via Wish, you only get a refund of the storage item used.

Flame Blade (Errata)

:::warning [LEGACY GATE DISCLAIMER]
This errata applies to a standard 2014 spell/feature that does not have a corresponding page in the TWR Wiki.
It is preserved here for completeness.
:::

2nd-level evocation (Druid, Sorcerer, Wizard)

Casting Time: 1 bonus action

Range: Self

Components: V, S, M (leaf of sumac)

Duration: Concentration, up to 10 minutes

Description

You evoke a fiery blade in your free hand. The blade is similar in size and shape to a scimitar, lasts for the duration, and counts as a simple melee weapon with which you are proficient. It deals 3d6 fire damage on a hit and has the finesse and light properties. If you let go of the blade, it disappears, but you can evoke the blade again as a bonus action.

The flaming blade sheds bright light in a 10-foot radius and dim light for an additional 10 feet.

At Higher Levels

When you cast this spell using a 3rd- or 4th-level spell slot, the damage increases to 4d6. When you cast it using a 5th- or 6th-level spell slot, the damage increases to 5d6. When you cast it using a spell slot of 7th level or higher, the damage increases to 6d6.

(Changes: It now conjures a real weapon like Shadow Blade does and scales at higher levels the same as Shadow Blade. This makes it usable for Eldritch Knights and Channelers.)

Perfect Self - Optional Feature (Replaces Original Perfect self)

Starting at 20th level, when you roll for initiative and have 0-3 ki, your ki is reset to 4. In addition, your Dexterity and Wisdom scores increase by 4. Your max for these abilities is also increased by 4, up to a max of 30.

Plant Growth Errata (Errata)

:::warning [LEGACY GATE DISCLAIMER]
This errata applies to a standard 2014 spell/feature that does not have a corresponding page in the TWR Wiki.
It is preserved here for completeness.
:::

Casting this on a normal seedling or any plant past this state of growth will have a chance to magically grow it, cutting off 50% of its current growth time, applicable until its fully aged. Having a 25% chance to fail, yielding nothing on a failed roll. Ex. Tree has 25 years to grow, rolling a 26 or higher on a d100 causes the tree to only need to grow for 12.5 more years.

This spell channels vitality into plants within a specific area. There are two possible uses for the spell, granting either immediate or long-term benefits.

If you cast this spell using 1 action, choose a point within range. All normal plants in a 100-foot radius centered on that point become thick and overgrown with a year's worth of growth. A creature moving through the area must spend 4 feet of movement for every 1 foot it moves.

Any harvestable plant in this area produces a poor quality harvest for the next [month]. Additional casts in this manner will regrow damaged areas to maintain the rough terrain, but grants no additional agricultural benefits beyond what was granted in the first cast until the cooldown period has elapsed.

You can exclude one or more areas of any size within the spell's area from being affected.

If you cast this spell over 8 hours, you enrich the land. All plants in a half-mile radius centered on a point within range become enriched for 1 year. The plants yield twice the normal amount of food when harvested then return to their normal production levels.

When the land is enriched this way, casting Plant Growth in a attempt to enrich the soil again within one year and six months after the initial casting will grant no additional agricultural benefits.

Specific Triggers (Errata)

:::warning [LEGACY GATE DISCLAIMER]
This errata applies to a standard 2014 spell/feature that does not have a corresponding page in the TWR Wiki.
It is preserved here for completeness.
:::

Triggers and activation conditions must have a known/detectable effect, for instance a readied action for when a creature comes through the door, contingency cant be set to activate with a thought, glyph of warding doesn't work if its "when a neutral good creature steps on it" because alignment can't be perceived immediately

Some exceptions: You can ready an action to attack if the target thinks something, if you have detect thoughts or a way to hear their thinks

Note: this applies to anything that has an effect based on a condition or requirement

Core / Errata_orphans

Spellwrought Tattoos (Errata)

:::warning [LEGACY GATE DISCLAIMER]
This errata applies to a standard 2014 spell/feature that does not have a corresponding page in the TWR Wiki.
It is preserved here for completeness.
:::

Spellwrought Tattoos whose spells requires a material component with a cost require those materials to be provided at the time of crafting and are consumed if the spell consumes them, eg. Raise dead's 300 gp diamond

Equipping one tattoo takes a minute. Using it remains the casting time of the spell.

Every character has 5 'points' worth of tattoo space to work with on their body:

  • Rare - 3 points
  • Uncommon - 2 points
  • Common - 1 point

This can also be interpreted as the size of each tattoo, but the point system is a clear cut way to define it and prevent abuse such as playing as a race that has an additional set of limbs. Additionally, familiars and other magical summons that are smaller than Medium are no longer eligible for Spellwrought Tattoos.

Core / Errata_orphans

Storm Boomerang (Errata)

:::warning [LEGACY GATE DISCLAIMER]
This errata applies to a standard 2014 spell/feature that does not have a corresponding page in the TWR Wiki.
It is preserved here for completeness.
:::

This boomerang is a ranged weapon carved from griffon bone and etched with the symbol of elemental air. When thrown, it has a range of 60/120 feet, and any creature that is proficient with the javelin is also proficient with this weapon. On a hit, the boomerang deals 1d4 bludgeoning damage and 3d4 thunder damage, and the target must succeed on a DC 10 Constitution saving throw or be stunned until the end of its next turn. On a miss, the boomerang returns to the thrower's hand.

Once the boomerang deals thunder damage to a target, the weapon loses its ability to deal thunder damage and its ability to stun a target. These properties return after a long rest.

:::warning [LEGACY GATE DISCLAIMER]
This errata applies to a standard 2014 spell/feature that does not have a corresponding page in the TWR Wiki.
It is preserved here for completeness.

A Character can only benefit from a single item source of +X Attack and Damage bonus to their Unarmed Attacks.

A character can use multiple items with +X bonuses, but their +X Bonus will be equal to the highest single bonus from their equipped items.

Before Errata:

Someone with Dragonscale Knuckles, +3 Wraps of Unarmed Prowess, Insignia of Claws, Eldritch Claw Tattoo, will have the Following Benefits:

  • +6 Bonus to Attack
  • +6 Bonus to Damage
  • +1d6[dragontype] to Damage
  • + Ability to activate tattoo for extra force damage and reach

After Errata:

The same items will now give:

  • +3 Bonus to Attack
  • +3 Bonus to Damage
  • +1d6[dragontype] to Damage
  • + Ability to activate tattoo for extra force damage and reach

Construct healing

If the mending spell is cast on you, you can spend a Hit Die, roll it, and regain a number of hit points equal to the roll plus your Constitution modifier (minimum of 1 hit point). In addition, your creator designed you to benefit from several spells that preserve life but that normally don't affect Constructs: cure wounds, healing word, mass cure wounds, mass healing word, and spare the dying.

Weapon Mastery (Errata)

:::warning [LEGACY GATE DISCLAIMER]
This errata applies to a standard 2014 spell/feature that does not have a corresponding page in the TWR Wiki.
It is preserved here for completeness.
:::

Add the weapon mastery properties and class features from the 2024 PHB

Cleave

If you hit a creature with a melee attack roll using this weapon, you can make a melee attack roll with the weapon against a second creature within 5 feet of the first that is also within your reach. On a hit, the second creature takes the weapon’s damage, but don’t add your ability modifier to that damage unless that modifier is negative. You can make this extra attack only once per turn.

Graze

If your attack roll with this weapon misses a creature, you can deal damage to that creature equal to the ability modifier you used to make the attack roll. This damage is the same type dealt by the weapon, and the damage can be increased only by increasing the ability modifier.

Nick

When you make the extra attack from two-weapon fighting, you can make it as part of the Attack action instead of as a Bonus Action. You can make this extra attack only once per turn.

Push

If you hit a creature with this weapon, you can push the creature up to 10 feet straight away from yourself if it is Large or smaller.

Sap

If you hit a creature with this weapon, that creature has Disadvantage on its next attack roll before the start of your next turn.

Slow

If you hit a creature with this weapon and deal damage to it, you can reduce its Speed by 10 feet until the start of your next turn. If the creature is hit more than once by weapons that have this property, the Speed reduction doesn’t exceed 10 feet.

Topple

If you hit a creature with this weapon, you can force the creature to make a Constitution saving throw (DC 8 plus the ability modifier used to make the attack roll and your Proficiency Bonus). On a failed save, the creature has the Prone condition.

Vex

If you hit a creature with this weapon and deal damage to the creature, you have Advantage on your next attack roll against that creature before the end of your next turn.

Added to Fighter:

Weapon Mastery - 1st Level

Your training with weapons allows you to use the mastery properties of three kinds of Simple or Martial weapons of your choice. Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can practice weapon drills and change one of those weapon choices.

When you reach certain Fighter levels, you gain the ability to use the mastery properties of more kinds of weapons, gaining one additional selection at 4th, 10th, and 16th level.

Tactical Master - 9th Level

When you attack with a weapon whose mastery property you can use, you can replace that property with the Push, Sap, or Slow property for that attack.

Added to Rogue:

Weapon Mastery

Your training with weapons allows you to use the mastery properties of two kinds of weapons of your choice with which you have proficiency, such as Daggers and Shortbows.

Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can change the kinds of weapons you chose. For example, you could switch to using the mastery properties of Scimitars and Shortswords.

Added to Barbarian:

Weapon Mastery

Your training with weapons allows you to use the mastery properties of two kinds of Simple or Martial Melee weapons of your choice. Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can practice weapon drills and change one of those weapon choices.

When you reach certain Barbarian levels, you gain the ability to use the mastery properties of more kinds of weapons, gaining one additional selection at 4th and 10th level.

Added to Paladin:

Weapon Mastery

Your training with weapons allows you to use the mastery properties of two kinds of weapons of your choice with which you have proficiency, such as Longswords and Javelins.

Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can change the kinds of weapons you chose. For example, you could switch to using the mastery properties of Halberds and Flails.

Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can change the kinds of weapons you chose. For example, you could switch to using the mastery properties of Scimitars and Longswords.

Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can change the kinds of weapons you chose. For example, you could switch to using the mastery properties of Pistols and Quarterstaffs.

Wish (Errata)

:::warning [LEGACY GATE DISCLAIMER]
This errata applies to a standard 2014 spell/feature that does not have a corresponding page in the TWR Wiki.
It is preserved here for completeness.
:::

  1. Wish cannot be used to give more than one damage resistance to more than a single creature.

  2. Any effects other than what is clearly stated in the text of the Wish spell needs DM approval prior to casting wish

  3. When using Wish for anything other than casting a 8th level or lower spell, the DM or DM trainee role needs to be pinged, and their presence acknowledged before rolling the d100.

  4. Wish is a 9th level spell, regardless of what you use it for. If you use it to replicate a spell of 8th level or lower, it still counts as having cast a 9th level spell. (for the purposes of counterspell/dispel magic, spell storing items, etc.)

  5. Wish has a range of self, and its effect cannot be twinned as a result of that

Core

Followers and Attunement

Followers and Attunement

Summoned and PC controlled entities, can attune to magic items, but they share the attunement slot of the PC. Examples of Entities: Simulacrum, Familiars, Beast companions, steel defender, undead, planar bound summons, etc.

When a controlled entity uses a PC's attunement slot to attune to an item. Only one item of the same name can be attuned by either PC or Controlled entity. ex: A Wizard and their Simulacrum can't both be attuned to Illusionist Bracers.

Core

Full & Part Time Jobs

Full & Part Time Jobs

Part Time & Full Time Jobs

You can now find gainful employment within the city of Waterdeep (and abroad). This can be done in two ways, a weekly job or daily job.

Daily Jobs

Daily Jobs uses an alias in discord and can only be done once a day per PC, this also takes your downtime. To do the job, use the alias: !job skill Then link the result in #transaction-log with a short deception of what you did in character and the amount earned

Weekly Jobs

Part time jobs, such as casual work at a smithy or a bard playing for a tavern, will take up all of your downtime (meaning no crafting or learning skills) but still let you quest, hunt, and trial.

Full time jobs pay more but in addition to no downtime you will no longer have time to trail, quest, or freely adventure.

Q: How do you find employment/work?

A: Provide a brief description of the job you’re looking to do, such as a part time job at an apothecary, then roll 2d20 and add your proficiency bonus if applicable (In this case it would be alchemy or herbalism). (2d20 + applicable mod) * 14 * Tier = gp/wk using all downtime. x2 for full time, but no hunts/trials as a result Part Time tier averages T1 = 294 T2 = 588 T3 = 882 T4 = 1,176

Weekly Job Report

@ Player PC & Tier: Lanscan Tallfast, T2 Job: Bard at a the The Silken Slyph Tavern & Inn Roll: 22 Link to the roll: https://discord.com/channels/817263494818693170/817269893514395658/928341274916962386 Wages: Start Date: MM/DD/YYYY End Date: MM/DD/YYYY

Core / Gameplay

Alchemy System

Alchemy System

Alchemy System

Gathering

  1. Use Downtime to Gather Herbs, max usage 3x a day (uses 8 hours in a session). Note: You can no longer sacrifice adventuring time to harvest extra herbs.

  2. Choose one environment [Cave, Forest, Desert, Grasslands, Swamp] + Rarity [Common, Uncommon, Rare, Very Rare]

  3. Roll Nature/Medicine/Arcana + Herbalism/Poisoner/Brewer/Alchemist Tool Prof Bonus (If proficient) --> DC scales depending on rarity of ingredient. Once check is completed, post in transcript using template found in pins of transcript . Craftmaster will roll for the herb gathered randomly depending on location chosen and DC rarity met.

DCs for Enchantment Ingredients:
Rarity DC
Common DC 10
Uncommon DC 13
Rare DC 17
Very Rare DC 20
Targeted Gathering

  1. You can target herbs based on which potion you wish to make! If you are targeting a herb for a specific potion, use the Targeted gathering Template pinned in transcript

  2. If the herb you are searching for isn't in the environment you chose, you get nothing. If it is, a Craftmaster will roll the herb normally, and you only get the herb if the dice comply.

The DCs for targeted gathering are as followed:
Rarity DC
Common DC 13
Uncommon DC 17
Rare DC 20
Very Rare DC 23
Bonuses:
  1. You can only target one herb per day until you have gathered 3 of that herb, at which point you may target for two herbs per day due to your familiarity.
  2. You cannot use help actions in herb gathering. Self-Buffs are allowed for now.
  3. Nat20 Rule: If you roll nat20 on the check (RAW Nat20 without modifiers and bonuses) you get 1 Extra Herb.
  4. Over10 Rule: If your total roll is 10 over the applicable DC you get 1 Extra Herb. Example, if your total roll for a rare is 31, you get 2 Herbs instead of 1.
  5. Nat20 and Over10 rules can both apply, to a max of 3 Herbs per roll.

Potion Brewing

Potions are brewed using herbs, each herb is used for a specific potion, the potion is hinted at in the description.

Time, base Cost, Herb Requirement to brew:

Rarity Time (Days) Cost Herb Requirement
Common 2.5 25 gp 1 Herb
Uncommon 5 100 gp 1 Herb
Rare 12.5 1,000 gp 2 Herbs
Very Rare 25 10,000 gp 3 Herbs

Monster Part Substitution

You can substitute 1 Herb for a monster part, however uncommon and higher potions need at least 1 Herb.

Potion Rarity Monster CR Loot DC
Common CR 1-3 DC 13
Uncommon CR 4-8 DC 17
Rare CR 9-13 DC 21
Very Rare CR 14-18 DC 24
Legendary CR 19+ DC 26

Bulk Brewing

  • Bulk Brewing has a discount on overall cost now. For every 10 potions you make at a time, you get a 5% discount on cost, cap for the discount is 20%.
  • Bulk Brewing also requires less herbs. For every 10 potions you brew, you only need 7x the amount of herbs for one potion of the same rarity. Example: 10 common potions of healing - 7 enchantment herbs needed.

Time Reduction

  • You get a 50% time reduction if you use double the amount of enchantment herbs for the potion.
  • Sacrificing Potions:
  1.   You can sacrifice one potion per brew.
  2.   Lowers base time by half the time it takes to brew a potion of that rarity.

Allowed 2024 Rules Content

Allowed 2024 Rules Content

General Rules

General:

  • 2024 character creation content, subclasses, classes, feats, items can be submitted via the Homebrew channel

Classes:

  • Any approved 2024 Class can be played with a 2014 subclass, unless otherwise stated in the wiki.
  • You can choose a 2024 Subclass on a 2014 Class, unless otherwise stated in the wiki.
  • 19th Level Epic Boon feats are replaced with ASI or a Feat
  • Once you chose the 2024 version of a Class you can't multiclass into it's 2014 version or choose the 2014 version in Paragon leveling, and vice versa
  • 2024 Classes can start with their starting gold instead of equipment

Feats:

  • If you take a 2024 feat, you can't take its 2014 version as a feat, and vice versa

Barding

Barding

Barding

Barding is equipment made for creatures not Medium size. Barding can be either mundane or magical.

The base cost of creating the item will be increased by the following modifier for each size above and below Medium:

Size Cost Modifier
Diminutive x 64
Tiny x 16
Small x 4
Large x 4
Huge x 16
Gargantuan x 64
Core / Gameplay

Code of Conduct

Code of Conduct

Code of Conduct

TWR is a server based on mutual respect. Rude, disruptive, and generally toxic behavior will be subject to moderator review. Below are some explanations of behavior which is not acceptable, but this is by no means an exhaustive list:

  1. Abuse/harassment/bullying/threats of mental or physical harm against one or more people.
  2. Insults directed against any player or staff on the server.
  3. Repeated insensitive or inappropriate jokes. Be respectful of subjects such as race, religion, politics, etc.
  4. Use of any type of slur.
  5. Threats of self harm Self harm is a serious matter and should not be joked about or taken lightly.
  6. Follow Discord TOS found here https://discord.com/terms
  7. No spamming, raiding, or anything that disturbs the peace.
    1. While mods and admins are here to help you, abuse of moderator or staff pings may result in a warning.
    2. Voice chats: Don’t play any alarmingly loud sounds or scream into the mic.
  8. Please keep channel content appropriate to the channel being used
    1. Keep memes and shitposting to #the-c-o-r-n-e-r where possible. #general can be a fun place, but please don’t flood the channel with memes.
    2. Swearing is banned in #the-peoples-court
    3. Roleplay in RP channels, Out of Character talk in OOC etc
  9. Art Advertising or solicitation of any kind is not allowed.

If you are ever made to feel uncomfortable by content on the server, or by someone’s behavior, please report it to anyone with the @Moderator or @Admin role. We want everyone to feel comfortable and safe here.

Core / Gameplay

Daily Life on TWR

Daily Life on TWR

The Passage of Time

Time passes at the same rate within the world of TWR that it passes in our world. For easy reference, there is a channel in the server that lists the time on Elysium. This is an optional time you can use for coordination and envinronmental change, but you may act out your character’s life within each day as it meets your schedule.

Daily Reset

For the purposes of downtime and daily activities, your PC’s day begins when you wake up in the morning and ends when you go to bed. For fringe cases, daily resets should occur roughly every 24 hours.

Daily Resources

Each day, characters have the following resources:

Hunting Tags - 5
Trial Tags - 2
Downtime Hours - 8
Long Rest - 1 *
Short Rest - 8 *

Long and Short Rests

Aside from rests which occur in Trials or Quests, players are limited to 1 Long Rest and 8 Short Rests per day. These can be taken at the player’s discretion by using the !sr or !lr command in discord.

Quest Locks & Restrictions

During the course of a quest, characters may be restricted by the DM from pursuing hunts, trials, downtime options and rests as usual. While your PC is attending a quest, work with your DM to determine what parts of their daily routine can be continued.

Repetitive Actions

Some spells or projects require daily activity to fully realize. In cases like this, players should post in #transcript describing the action, how long they will repeat it, and outlining all the materials required (which must be procured ahead of time). Staff will then review the post, notify you of any issues or extra requirements, and when the time has passed your actions will become official.

Downtime

Each PC may utilize 8 hours per day of downtime to further their character’s goals and story. Downtime options can be pursued as outlined by RAW in books such as the PHB, DMG, and XGtE. Some examples include crafting magical items, performing research, gambling, or working a mundane job. Additional downtime options may be defined in other TWR supplements.

This server uses the “Optional Rule” for sleep deprivation located in Xanathar’s Guide to Everything if you wish to work through the night.

Core / Gameplay

Disciplinary Info

Disciplinary Info

Disciplinary Info

  1. Violation of any of the rules will generally result in a verbal warning.
  2. A second violation of the same rule will result in a strike. A strike typically lasts for 2 months from the date of issue.
  3. Players with three active strikes will be banned from TWR for a 3 month period
  4. Any other disciplinary action up to and including a permanent ban may be dispensed by the mods following a majority vote.
    1. Some examples of what might bypass the process include, but are not limited to:
      1. Art Advertising (specifically public posting or DMing other server members)
      2. Trolling and Raids (coming to the server with the sole intent of causing trouble)
      3. Extreme cases of rule #1 violations (slurs, excessively vulgar/targeted language, harassment, etc.)
      4. Illegal Activities
      5. Repeated disregard of staff instructions regarding rules or server norms. (Especially if such disregard comes in the form of blatantly disrespectful or hostile behavior in violation of of our Code of Conduct)

If you are ever made to feel uncomfortable by content on the server, or by someone’s behavior, please report it to anyone with the @Moderator or @Admin role. We want everyone to feel comfortable and safe here.

Bans issued for any reason are, of course, subject to an optional appeal by the offending player, if they should choose to do so. Contact a @Moderator or @Admin if you wish to appeal a ban issued to you or to another member of the server.

Core / Gameplay

Downtime Buffs

Downtime Buffs

Downtime Buffs

When performing any downtime activities, any bonuses to skill checks made must last for the full eight hours of downtime to be applicable to the final skill check.

(Cases that specifically state otherwise overrules this, i.e. herb gathering)

Core / Gameplay

Full & Part Time Jobs

Full & Part Time Jobs

Part Time & Full Time Jobs

You can now find gainful employment within the city of Waterdeep (and abroad). This can be done in two ways, a weekly job or daily job.

Daily Jobs

Daily Jobs uses an alias in discord and can only be done once a day per PC, this also takes your downtime. To do the job, use the alias: !job skill Then link the result in #transaction-log with a short deception of what you did in character and the amount earned

Weekly Jobs

Part time jobs, such as casual work at a smithy or a bard playing for a tavern, will take up all of your downtime (meaning no crafting or learning skills) but still let you quest, hunt, and trial.

Full time jobs pay more but in addition to no downtime you will no longer have time to trail, quest, or freely adventure.

Q: How do you find employment/work?

A: Provide a brief description of the job you’re looking to do, such as a part time job at an apothecary, then roll 2d20 and add your proficiency bonus if applicable (In this case it would be alchemy or herbalism). (2d20 + applicable mod) * 14 * Tier = gp/wk using all downtime. x2 for full time, but no hunts/trials as a result Part Time tier averages T1 = 294 T2 = 588 T3 = 882 T4 = 1,176

Core / Gameplay

Gameplay Rules

Gameplay Rules

Gameplay Rules

  1. Rules and mechanics are RAW by default. Any exceptions to this rule will be documented in the Homebrew section or Errata section.
  2. DM rulings are final. You don’t have to agree with it, but you must abide by it.
    1. If you have an issue with a DM’s ruling you may bring it up to the DM directly after the game/quest, not mid-session.
    2. If you speak with the DM and still disagree with the ruling, you may bring it up in #the-peoples-court for further discussion.
  3. Within player-led content (quests, trials, whatever), the DM of the session is king.
  4. All staff and players are expected to respect each others’ time by remaining present and attentive during gameplay.
  5. Do not leave a quest, trial, hunt, or other event without permission from the DM or person running it, or you will be cursed.
  6. If your DM or the person running your content leaves unexpectedly, contact a @Moderator or @Dungeonmaster for guidance
  7. Do NOT cheat. Modifying your loot or experience past their actual values is strictly prohibited.
    1. If you are controlling an enemy in a Trial or Hunt, playing the enemy poorly on purpose is cheating.
    2. If you are uncertain about anything, ping the DM/DM trainee that posted the record or post your question/concern to #questions.
  8. You may not play as or with a character on the server until it has been posted by a DM, DM Trainee, or Admin in #active-pc-sheet-links.
  9. RP and Gameplay should not include erotic or overly sexual themes. A fade to black is generally acceptable.
  10. Monsters in hunts and trials should use their pre-2024 statblocks. MotM statblocks take priority over legacy statblocks. Quest statblocks are on DM-discretion.
Tracking PC Activity in Discord

All changes to your PC’s character sheet, canonical events, rewards, downtime results, etc. must be recorded in one of the following four channels:

#transcript: Players can submit any player-run RP, gametype or event, downtime activity, or other official changes to #transcript for review. Once the post has been moved to #records by staff, it will become official TWR Canon.

#transaction-log: Players submit any financial transactions with other players or NPCs (including mundane item purchases) in this channel for review.

#records: Staff will post final reports from #transcript or related to their own content in Records, where it becomes official and rewards are applied to the player.

#story-log: Contains the results of quests, large scale plotlines, and other

Character Interaction Consent

All character interactions are based on the consent of the players controlling them. That means that if someone refuses to interact with someone’s character for any reason, they may do so. This rule is to protect players from unwanted interaction, not to shield players from consequences.

Hireling Update 2

Team involved: @Loremaster

Hello lurkers!

This update is an addendum to the previously released Hireling spreadsheet for NPC pricing. Utilizing this, you will have guidelines with which you may hire NPCs over time, up to a predetermined maximum amount, for whatever individual, group, or organizational needs you have. If there is confusion on how this works, please use the attached spreadsheet, or ask a @Loremaster.

Contracting NPC Requirements:

Maximum CR that can be hired as a single unit is capped at CR 20

Total CR across all hired units is capped at CR = 30

Hiring occurs weekly, using a point deduction system (Hire Points)

Points accrue at a rate of 1/week from the time interest is expressed, and equate to the Total CR that can be used to hire units

Point deductions are based against the CR being hired.

Example: Player currently has total of 5 Hire Points. The player can Hire any combination of humanoid creatures less than or equal to the total CR of 5.

Spreadsheet for CR to Hire Points breakdown can be seen here: https://docs.google.com/file/d/1Qv2-Cna8BUpkpW0geMdIO68BIL-coSrd/edit?usp=docslist\_api&filetype=msexcel

Please submit these hire requests to transcript and ping a @Loremaster for approval.

Attunement and Magic Items for Hirelings Hirelings can equip and attune to magic items provided to them by their employer based upon their CR, as shown below:

  • CR 1/8 - CR 1/2: Common (no attunement)

  • CR 1 - CR 4: Uncommon (attunement up to 1 item)

  • CR 5 - 10: Rare (attunement up to 2 items)

  • CR 11 - 16: Very Rare (attunement up to 3 items)

  • CR 17+: Legendary (attunement up to 3 items)

If the hirelings statblock has an armor or weapon listed, they are treated as proficient with all weapons or armor of that same type (e.g. leather - light armor, Shortsword - martial weapons). If you have questions or concerns, please me know, and I will be working with existing groups/organizations to get you switched over to this new framework

From #Patch-Notes

Much discussion and collaboration has gone into the merger of Hireling system with the previously used Organizations system. They will now be brought under one framework, with some added rules for how groups and organizations will work under this system, how hirelings can be equipped with items from their employers, and some promising prospects for future updates.

Individual & Group Hirelings

The ability for individuals and established groups to hire NPCs to augment their personal or collaborative efforts will be broken into one of two categories, with slightly different considerations for each. Hirelings can be reskinned to represent any humanoid race or alignment, and can speak common by default.

Contracting Requirements (Individual)

Hiring updates occur once per week, using a point deduction system (Hire Points)

Points accrue at a rate of 1/week, requiring an approved post from a Loremaster These points are logged via ⁠transcript and the total equates to the Total CR that can be used to hire units for that update.

Point deductions are based on the CR being hired. CR 0 units count as CR 1/8 for this, there is a graph that breaks down these numbers in more detail.

Individuals contracting NPCs will use the 'Deployed Monthly' rate, as opposed the normal Daily/Monthly rate. These expenses are logged via ⁠transaction-log after the update is approved by a Loremaster. These expenses occur at the 1st of every month.

Maximum CR that can be hired as a single unit is capped at CR 20

Total CR that can be hired is capped at CR 20

The screenshot below shows a week-by-week breakdown of how hire points can be spent on the corresponding CR.

Contracting Requirements (Group/Organizational)

Hiring updates occur once per week, using a point deduction system (Hire Points)

Points accrue based upon the modifiers calculated for your group, from 1-10, requiring an approved post from a Loremaster. These points are logged via ⁠transcript and the total equates to the Total CR that can be used to hire units for that update.

Publicity (popularity, reputation, goodwill)

Accessibility (access, reach)

Logistics (training, supplies, budget)

Opportunity (job security, importance, need)

Temp buffs (quests/significant events)

Groups/Organizations consisting of multiple PCs behave as a single ‘entity’ for the sake of point accumulation and spending. Updates will be logged with a single PC representing the group.

Point deductions are based on the CR being hired. CR 0 units count as CR 1/8 for this, there is a graph that breaks down these numbers in more detail.

Groups/Organizations contracting NPCs will use the normal 'Monthly' rate. These expenses are logged via ⁠transaction-log after the update is approved by a Loremaster. These expenses occur at the 1st of every month.

Maximum CR that can be hired as a single unit is capped at CR 20

Retraining Rules

Retraining Rules

Retraining Rules

Class Retraining

By spending 10 workweeks of downtime, a character can choose to replace one of their levels in one class with a level in another class. This time is reduced by a number of workweeks equal to the character’s ability modifier in the key ability of the new class. If their new class has more than one key ability, the characters lowest ability modifier should be used for this calculation. The character must have a minimum of 13 in the key abilities of both their current class and their new class They must have an instructor of at least 1 level higher (or be level 20) than your new level in the new class and must spend 50gp per week for the instructor and relevant supplies.

Fighting Style Retraining

(For Fighters, Rangers, Paladins, Blood Hunters, and College of Swords Bards only) By spending a week of downtime, you can choose one of the (insert class name here) fighting style you know and replace it with another fighting style from the (insert class name here) class.

Feat / ASI Retraining

By spending a week of downtime, you can choose to replace one Feat or ASI you qualify for with another Feat or ASI you qualify for. Post20 ASIs can be retrained only to ASIs, and Post20 Feats can be retrained only to Boons or Feats.

Spell Retraining

(For sorcerers, warlocks, bards and rangers only) By spending a week of downtime,you can choose one of the (insert class name here) spells you know and replace it with another spell from the (insert class name here) spell list, which also must be of a level for which you have spell slots.

Mystic Arcanum Retraining

Warlocks can spend 1 week of downtime to retrain one of their mystic arcanum spells for another spell that is applicable for that version of the mystic arcanum classfeat.

RP Reduction

When you undergo retraining, you can submit an RP-XP request for roleplay related to the retraining and receive a reduction in the overall time spent retraining. Each RP-XP request is worth a 5% reduction, up to a maximum of 25%.

Retroactive Downtime

Retroactive Downtime

We get it, you can’t always plan your character’s lives in real time. That’s why we’ve designed Retroactive Downtime, which lets you apply unused downtime at a reduced wait to cover gaps in gameplay and incetivize coming back to TWR!

Starting from the last date your PC used their downtime, you can now file a report to use 1/3 of the total days (rounded down) on a single goal or downtime activity with staff approval.

How does it work?

Players wishing to file for retroactive downtime must complete the report on the right and submit it to #transcript. Staff will determine the appropriate daily value for your character and resources and return the report with any important notes.

Custom Retroactive Downtime

We are also introducing a few new forms of “retroactive” downtime you can add to the report:

General Adventuring: XP Bonus

Characters who spend their time hunting, traveling, or otherwise generally adventuring receive bonus XP:

Service to a Deity: Favor Bonus

Characters who spend time in service of a deity will be rewarded for their faith with favor:

Tier Bonus Favor Cap (Per Day)
1 1 Favor

The Career Path: Gold Bonus

Through smart investments, performance bonuses, side hustles and promotions, business ownership, etc., you receive bonus Gold:

Core / Gameplay

Soulbound Item

Soulbound Item

Soulbound Items

In the ancient epochs, when the world was young and the weave of magic was still being shaped, the gods and primordial forces sought to leave their mark upon the mortal realm. They imbued certain objects with Runes of their essence, creating artifacts that resonated with the very souls of those who wielded them. These are the Soulbound Items.

A Soulbound Item is more than just a tool; it is a companion, a reflection of the bond between the bearer and the object. To attune to such an item is to forge a pact, intertwining one's fate with the artifact's power. As the wielder grows in strength and experience, so too does the Soulbound Item, awakening latent abilities and evolving in response to the challenges faced together.

However, this bond is not without its trials. The path to unlocking a Soulbound Item's full potential is fraught with challenges, requiring the bearer to prove their worth and commitment. Only through perseverance, valor, and a deep connection can the true power of the Soulbound Item be realized.

Soulbound Item Mechanics

  1. A Player Character can only ever be attuned to one Soulbound Item
  2. The Item is a relic

Progressing the Soulbound Item

  1. Each Soulbound Item has its progression on the relevant Item Progression table
  2. At certain levels the weapon gains one of 4 types of features, Base, Ability, Unique and Runes. Each feature will have options to choose from.
  3. For Ability and Unique features, The player can decide whether to take a Novice Rank option or to promote an previously chosen option to the next rank
  4. Runes provide minor benefits, where some Runes you need more than 1 before unlocking its benefits
  5. When you choose an option as part of a feature you cannot choose that option again, other to promote it, unless it's stated otherwise.
  6. Ability and Unique feature ranks are constrained limited by the strength of its owner. To unlock an Expert feature the owner must be level 11 or higher, to unlock a Master feature they must be level 17 or higher
  7. The Weapon can at no point be at a higher level than it's owner

Item Leveling

  1. While the item is attuned to a character, any experience that the player gains while attuned to the item is split 50/50 between the player and their soulbound item
    1. The XP will be scaled to the item's level via an alias.
    2. This includes XP from random hunts, dungeons, raids and quests.
    3. It is the players choice if up to 50% of RPXP goes to the weapon
    4. Example:
      1. If a level 8 Player gets 5000XP for Killing a Monster in a hunt and the item is also level 8, the Player and the Item each gets 2500XP
      2. If the weapon was at level 5, Player would get 2500XP which is 18% of XP Required to level to level 9. Thus the Item will get 18% of the exp required to go from level 5 to level 6, which is 1350 XP.
    5. When a player caps their level, the Item will still get 50% of the Exp that the player would have received
    6. This seems like complicated math, but there will be an alias to take care of all that
  2. Paragons:
    1. 50% of the experience gained from non-hunt combat participation can still go towards the weapon, this will be scaled for the Weapons level
    2. Paragon's Soulbound Items receive 50% of the Experience they would have gotten from combat. This includes Non-targetted hunts, Delves, Trials and Raids

Obtaining a Soulbound Item

  1. The secret of creating a soulbound item has been unlocked, but as the magic is tied to the wielder and not the crafting they can only be crafted at its common stage.
  2. In lieu of choosing an uncommon item tied to the backstory of a submitted character, a player can choose a Soulbound* item, with the item starting at the same level of the Character, however this should be covered in the backstory
  3. Soulbound Items can be traded, but they will start at level 1 for a new PC and progress will be reset. For all intents and purposes when being traded, they use common item selling values.

Retraining Item Levels

  1. By spending 1 workweek of downtime a Level feature can be retrained to a different option for that level.
  2. Only a single level can be retrained at a a time
    • If you are Master of item Feature A, and want to retrain the weapon into a Journeyman of Path B and Path A, you will spend 1 workweek to go to Expert Path A and Novice Path B and then another workweek to reach Journeyman Path A and Journeyman Path B

Reset

  1. A soulbound weapon can be reset at anytime. This does mean that that it restarts at level 1, and any progress or experience it gained will be lost.

Homebrewing

  1. Players are Encouraged to Homebrew their own Unique Features and Runes via Homebrew System & Index, this will expand the options for other players as well

Future Updates

  1. As this is a new system, it may receive some balancing updates, either with nerf, buffs or sideways adjustments. Participation in this system acknowledges that your Item may change.

The page will first look at the Base and Ability Features, then it will list the Runes, First general and then the different type Runes. Lastly we will look at the available Unique features for each type of item.

Base and Ability Features

Soulbound Weapons

"To draw steel that bleeds with your soul is to accept its hunger. A soulbound weapon is not a weapon forged in a smith’s fire but in the crucible of oath and intent. The weapon listens to its wielder’s will, whispering back in sparks of battle-born instinct. As its bearer grows, the weapon awakens, reshaping itself to mirror the paths chosen. In time, the warrior and the weapon are no longer two, but one sharpened edge against fate itself."

Base:

Each weapon starts with the following Base Stats, when you unlock a Ability feature, you can choose one of the below options to promote to a higher rank.

Base Attack: Attacks made with this weapon is considered to be magical

Path Die: D4, this applies anytime a Path option references Path Damage Die

Weapon DC: 8 + Wielder Proficiency Bonus, whenever a Path feature requires a saving throw or allows the casting of a spell, it will use the Weapon DC has it's DC

Charges: 2, Some Path option may Require the use of Charges. Charges reset to full at dawn.

Ability Features

Rank Base Attack Path Die Weapon DC Charges
Novice +1 Attack Bonus d6 Base + 2 Base + 2
Journeyman +1 Attack and Damage Bonus d8 Base + 3 Base + 3
Expert +2 Attack and Damage Bonus d10 Base + 4 Base + 4
Master +3 Attack and Damage Bonus d12 Base + Wielders Choice of Ability Modifier, set when choosing Wielders Choice of Ability Modifier, set when choosing

Soulbound Armor and Soulbound Shields

To carry a soulbound ward is to carry more than protection — it is a covenant between bearer and bulwark. These wards are not merely hammered plates or shaped wood; they are vessels of resolve, tempered by sacrifice and sealed with spirit. At first they guard as any armor or shield might, but as the bond deepens, the ward awakens — answering the bearer’s instincts, hardening in defiance, softening in stealth, or shining in defense of others. In time, the warrior is no longer clad in armor, but in a living testament of their soul’s endurance.

Base:

Each armor or shield starts with the following Base Stats, when you unlock a Ability feature, you can choose one of the below options to promote to a higher rank

  • Base AC Bonus: determined by the armor type (light, medium, heavy) or shield.

  • Ward Die: d4,

  • Armor DC: Used for any feature that requires a saving throw or reactive effect. Starts at 8 + Wielder proficiency bonus.

  • Charges: 2 (for active Ward abilities).Charges reset to full at dawn.

Physical and Mental Features

Shield: +1 AC

Soulbound Foci

To wield a conduit is to place your soul in the current of the unseen. A staff, gem, or relic can be bound not by chains, but by resonance—its lattice aligned with the bearer’s essence. At first, it channels spells as any focus would, but soon the conduit hums with hidden voices, amplifying thought, bending the weave, answering only to the one who claimed it. By journey’s end, mage and conduit are indistinguishable: the caster’s will flows as lightning, and the relic itself becomes the echo of their soul.

A Soulbound focus can be any focus as determined by the Spellcasting feature of class. However the Owner can only attune to it if the item is an acceptable focus. This does include instruments and tools as well.

If the player character can use a weapon as a spellcasting focus, they can choose whether to use it as a soulbound focus or weapon. However once the choice is made the item will be locked into either beign a soulbound or soulbound weapon. For example if a player decided to make their weapon a soulbound focus, the progression is locked into conduit and focus abilities.

Base:

Each Focus starts with the following Base Stats, when you unlock a Ability feature, you can choose one of the below options to promote to a higher rank.

Base Focus: 0. Spell Save DC granted by class items do not stack with this focus. The Spell Save DC and spell attack bonus only applies if using the focus to cast.

Conduit Die: d4, this applies anytime a Conduit option references Conduit Die

Focus DC: 8 + Wielder Proficiency Bonus, whenever a Conduit feature requires a saving throw or allows the casting of a spell, it will use the Focus DC as it's DC

Charges: 2, Some Path option may require the use of Charges. Charges reset to full at dawn.

Rank Base Focus Conduit Die focus DC Charges
Novice +1 Spell Attack d6 Base + 2 Base + 2
Journeyman +2 Spell and +1 Spell Save DC d8 Basic + 3 Basic + 3
Expert +3 Spell and +2 Spell Save DC d10 Base + 4 Base + 4

Runes

As the Soulbound Item grows in power, etchings, runes or engraving may appear on it, this will either directly confer benefits, or in combination with other runes provide additional benefits.

Universal Runes:

These Runes can be used on weapon, armor, shields and foci:

  • Reclamation Rune - You can return the item to your hand (or your body in the case of armor) as an action.
  • Quick Reclamation Rune - You can return the item to your hand (or your body in the case of armor) as a bonus action, requires Reclamation Rune
  • Glamour Rune - You can freely change the appearance of the item as an action.
  • Compass Rune - While holding or wearing the item, you can determine the direction of true north, or the direction to a creature of which you speak its name.
  • Echo Rune - You can cast the message cantrip while the item is on your person.
  • Skill Runes - Once the item has accumulated two skill Runes, you gain proficiency in one skill of your choice while attuned to the item. An item can take skill Runes more than two times, and grant a new skill for every two of them it has accumulated.
  • Shifting Rune - Once the item has two shifting Runes, over the course of a long rest, you can move the properties of the item to another of the same category, in your possession, making the new item your soulbound item. For example, you can move the properties of a soulbound dagger onto a mundane spear, receiving a soulbound spear.
  • Shining Rune - The item sheds bright light out 10 feet, and dim light another 10 feet. This Rune can be taken a second time, doubling the radius of the light.
  • Specialization Rune - Once an item has accumulated four specialization Runes, the item gains one level of any path, ward, or conduit.
  • Intricate Rune - Once an item has accumulated four intricate Runes, the item gains one point to spend on any base feature.
  • Mnemonic Rune (2x) – The item can “store” one memory you designate. At 2 Mnemonic Runes, you can replay it vividly.
  • Expertise Runes - Once the item has accumulated two skill Runes, and two expertise Runes, you can add double your proficiency to the skill Rune skill, instead of normal proficiency.
  • Awakening Rune - When you have two Awaking Runes, your weapon gains sentience. See link for detail information Awakening Rune

Weapon Runes:

These Runes can only be taken on weapons:

  • Twin Rune - As a bonus action, you may split your weapon into two identical light versions for two-weapon fighting. They recombine as a bonus action, only works with weapons with the light property. Each of these weapons function as your Soulbound weapon, but still only requires one attunement slot.
  • Master Reclamation Rune - Immediately after hitting or missing, the weapon flies back to your hand, this requires a Quick Reclamation Rune, Thrown Property and a Level 12+ Soulbound weapon
  • Identical Rune - This rune bypasses the light requirement of the twin rune, allowing you split one handed and versatile weapons with the twin rune, that don't have the light property
  • Hunter’s Rune - While attuned, you can spend 1 minute studying a creature’s tracks or remnants to learn the direction it traveled within the past 24 hours.
  • Sanguine Rune - Once per short rest, when you reduce a creature to 0 HP, you get THP equal to your Path Die.
  • Dueling Spirit Runes - With 2 Deuling Spirit Runes, while fighting with the weapon in one hand and no other weapon or shield in the other, you gain +1 AC. With 4 invested, increase it to +2 AC.

Armor/Shield Runes:

These Runes can only be taken on Armor or Shields:

  • Defiant Rune – When you have 2 Defiant Runes, Once per long rest, when reduced to 0 HP while wearing the ward, you drop to 1 HP instead.
  • Aegis Rune – When you have 2 Aegis Runes and you succeed on a saving throw against a spell, you can use your reaction to grant advantage to one ally within 10 feet against the same effect.
  • Mirrorplate Rune – As a reaction once per short rest, impose disadvantage on an attack against you.
  • Beacon Runes – When you have 2 Beacon Runes, allies within 5 feet gain +1 on saving throws against being frightened. At 4 Runes, the aura extends to 10 feet and grants advantage instead.
  • Masterwork Rune - If you have 3 Masterwork Runes, you can upgrade your armor to highest tier armor of its type, any light armor, becomes studded leather, medium armor becomes half-plate and heavy armor becomes plate.

Focus Runes:

These Runes can only be taken on a focus:

  • Sigil Rune – While holding the conduit, you can inscribe temporary glowing runes that last 1 hour. You may leave one “mark” at a time that sheds dim light in 5 feet.
  • Spellkeeper Rune – You may store a cantrip in the conduit each long rest. You can cast it once as if you knew it, you can take this Rune again. If you have more than 1 you can store a spell you know during a long rest. The maximum level of spell you can store is equal to the number of Spellkeeper Runes minus 1. Regardless of how many Runes you have, you can only store 1 spell, and you can cast the spell without expending a spell slot.
  • Scryer’s Rune – Once per long rest, you can use the conduit as a divining rod, giving you advantage on a single Wisdom (Perception) or (Survival) check.
  • Resonance Runes – (Requires 2+) When you cast a spell, faint motes of energy linger. Allies within 5 feet gain +1 to their next attack roll. At 4 resonance Runes, the bonus is +1d4 instead.

Staff Disciplinary Process

Staff Disciplinary Process

Staff Disciplinary Process

This is the general process through which our staff process any complaints or necessary review of a player's actions.

Moderators - Warnings and Strikes

  1. In the event that a Warning or strike is needed, the person first calling for a vote will create the poll in the Moderator Votes thread with a Moderator role ping, a brief description and a link to the comment.  A 24 hour period will be given for moderators to discuss or vote.  At the end of the 24 hours, or a majority is reached whichever comes first, the Moderator creating the poll will issue the action to the player and post in #The-Strike-Zone.

Bans

  1. In the event a player incurs a 3rd strike, the moderator issuing the strike will instead issue the ban message from the template, ban the player, and make the record in the strike zone.
  2. If it is for a major event, or other concern, any moderator may open a discussion and call for a vote.  Once the vote is open with the ping, the issue is decided as soon as there is a majority vote or super majority vote either direction.
    1. The three strike process may be bypassed if especially toxic or repeated inappropriate behavior is present, to the discretion of a supermajority of the Mods.
    2. A supermajority is 70% of available persons voting in favor of a particular position.
  3. A majority vote is required for Moderators to escalate such a case to Admins for final vote approval to ban or not.
  4. IF a Supermajority for Ban is reached by Moderators then the moderator starting the vote will ban the player, record the reason in Strike Zone, and ping admins with a summary so they’re aware.

Training Downtime

Training Downtime

Training Downtime

Characters can perform activities to train and practice in their free time, those who do not wish to hunt can spend time training themselves as well, this could be tinkering and experimenting for Artificers, praying and studying for Clerics, scribing and practicing spells for Wizards, sparring for fighters, and stealthing around for rogues, all forms of training are applicable and make no mechanical difference

Characters can choose to spend 5 Hunting Tags or expend 8 hours of downtime in training which awards experience points to reflect the development of skills. Players who choose to roleplay the lessons will be awarded with additional RPXP as per usual
