TWR DM

TWR DM's Guide

TWR DM's Guide

What is this Guide?

This page is a guide to getting started running Quests on TWR, a discord-based Westmarches campaign. Quests can be run by any player, with certain exceptions where the player may need to seek approval from staff for lore/balance reasons. As noted in our Code of Conduct, while running a quest or other content, the player acts as the DM and is considered such during play.

Preparing to DM

Being a DM on TWR is easy and fun. Most of the adventures can be prepared in a short period of time, and you don’t have to create an entire setting and form a campaign or spend a ton of time plotting out a large overarching plot. Most Quests on TWR are run as “one-shots,” though more advanced DMs may choose to run quests in a series to tell a more intricate story.

What you Need to Run a Game

In order to run a game as a DM on TWR, you’ll need the following:

Players

The #quest-board channel is the perfect place to seek out players, if you do not have a full group in mind already. For traditional adventures a group of 4-6 players is recommended, but there is no specific number of players required to participate in a quest. Just be sure to balance any potential combat or roleplay encounters around the number of participants to ensure everyone gets to play.

A Plot

Balance the three pillars of gameplay (Roleplay, Adventuring, Combat) to your liking and create a plot for your quest. It is best to keep plots simple at first until you’ve got some practice running Quests. Consider what type of story you want to tell, what type of rewards might fit with the quest, Prepare any puzzles, difficult choices, or monster statblocks for combat ahead of time so that you can spend gameplay time interacting with the players and building the story. Remember, CR values translate to what an average difficulty is for a group of 4 well balanced adventurers. Though combat should be challenging, it should still be possible to win (unless your story dictates that the party loses!).

A Format

Some DMs prefer to run quests in a dedicated session for a more traditional experience, planning a start and end time. Others prefer a play-by-post (PBP) format, which can span multiple days or weeks and provide a more relaxed pace. Each option has benefits and detriments, so it's important to specify which one in your #quest-board post to attract the right players.

Other Tools

Avrae

For combat, spellcasting, and other mechanical functions it is highly recommended that you use Avrae which will automate the majority of tracking and run combat. You can also upload maps to use for tactical placement during combat.

Tupperbot

You will want to set up at least a "Narrator Tupper" to describe scenes, effects and other miscellaneous actions during play. You may also consider creating specific Tuppers for your NPCs to improve immersion and create a more aesthetically pleasing experience.

Group Composition

There’s no general rule that requires members of a group be of the same level. In quests that revolve around combat, we recommend restricting them by Tier as defined in the Player’s Handbook and Rules Compendium. For quests that are more roleplay-centric, this is less necessary, but bear in mind that some high level PCs may have spells and abilities that far outshine the rest of the group.

Facilitator of Fun

You have the most important role. You guide the narrative and provide the players with an immersive and enjoyable quest. While guiding the players, it is also your responsibility to make everyone feel welcomed, creating a fun and fair environment. Here are some things to keep in mind:

You are Empowered

Make decisions about how the group interacts with the quest; adjust or improvise your plan as needed. You have the ability to create NPCs, locations, challenges and scenarios with broad authority within your quest. Interacting with official D&D NPCs, Factions, Deities and other key lore entities may require approval from Staff; we encourage DMs who are concerned that their content may not accurately reflect the setting reach out to an official Dungeonmaster or Loremaster for guidance. See the "When to Seek Staff Approval" section below for a better understanding of when to reach out. Be aware that, in the instance of particularly challenging deviations from the setting Staff may have to retcon the contents of your quests to maintain fairness and server continuity.

Challenge your Players

Gauge the experience level of your players, as well as what they enjoy in a game and attempt to deliver what they’re after; everyone should be able to shine. You can adjust an encounter’s difficulty by adding or removing thematically appropriate monsters but can’t create new monsters or modify them in such a way that modifies their challenge rating (aside from changing their hit points within the range afforded by their hit dice). Be careful of going too far, however. The intent is to have a collaborative and challenging story-telling experience; it’s not to do everything you can to kill your players’ characters. Similarly, destroying equipment generally shouldn’t happen unless an encounter specifically directs you to. In fact, unless they have conditions detailing their destruction (such as an ioun stone), permanent magic items can’t be destroyed.

Dealing with Disruptive Players

If a player is acting in a disruptive manner during a play session, attempt to address the issue as soon as it becomes clear that someone (including you) might be uncomfortable. Take the player aside and explain why the behavior might be causing others to feel uncomfortable. If the problem persists, contact a Moderator or Admin for help with resolution.

Disruptive Magic Items, Spells or Class Features

There are several magic items, spells, class features and homebrew submissions within the rules of TWR that might become disruptive to the overall enjoyment of others at the table. If use of any personal equipment, features etc. through play leads to an uncomfortable play experience, take the player aside and explain the issue. You may wish to discuss temporarily removing the item or ability from the character and providing them an alternative replacement instead. You may choose to review a character’s sheet prior to play to help identify any potential issues, You should not mandate removal of magic items or gear solely on your preferences, but rather on their impact to the story and enjoyment of the players/DM as a group.

Safety Tools

Safety tools help ensure players aren’t pushed beyond their comfort levels. These tools let your players know you want them to have a positive experience. Some common safety tools are provided below, each with a summary of how they work. An article about one such safety kit is provided to help with further information. Ensure that you discuss these tools with your players before the game:

  • Code of Conduct: TWR has a code of conduct that outlines rules for play across the server. It defines desired and prohibited behaviors and possible consequences. Familiarize yourself with the Code of Conduct before running a quest to help understand what is acceptable and what is not.
  • Pregame, Postgame, and Out of Character Discussions: Use time before the game to explain content warnings and set boundaries. This helps you understand the players' various goals and comfort levels. Be sure to discuss the possibility of lethal combat, if applicable, as many players prefer to avoid risking the safety of their long-running PCs. During play, most DMs prefer to have an Out of Character (OOC) thread for combat and ongoing discussion of the story. After the quest, decompress and discuss what worked and what didn't with the players.
  • Be Welcoming: Welcome and encourage respectful and open conversations about issues as they arise. Show that you’re listening by avoiding defensive responses.
  • Direct Communication: Allow direct messaging between the players and yourself as the DM. Generally, do not share information sent to you in private with the rest of the group without permission.

Keep the Game Moving

If the game gets bogged down, provide hints and clues to your players facing puzzles or engaging in combat and roleplay interactions that get frustrating. This gives players “little victories” for making good choices based on clues. Don't be afraid to skip someone's turn or allow them the ability to act retroactively in the future if one player is unavailable and disrupting the flow of play.

Running the Game

As the DM, you are charged with not only guiding the story, but also fairly adjudicating the game’s rules and rewarding your players’ characters for their accomplishments.

The Rules of the Game

TWR generally uses Dungeons & Dragons 5th Edition (2014) with some added Homebrew Rules. You can issue rulings to your table when the rules of the game are ambiguous or vague, but you must otherwise adhere to the rules as they are provided in the core rulebooks and can’t change them or make up your own. You must always use the most current incarnation of a rule. Oftentimes, if a rule is in dispute, you can go to the #questions channel or ping a Dungeonmaster for assistance; generally, we follow Sage Advice for clarification from the game developers and, in some cases, Homebrew or #town-hall posts will include rules clarifications. Don't be afraid to ask for help, or issue a temporary ruling while you wait to maintain the flow of play. Otherwise, the rules as written in the rulebooks always take precedence.

Quest Locks

Depending on the content of your quest, you have the ability to "Quest Lock" PCs who are participating. Locked PCs cannot gain experience from or participate in Hunts, Trials, or any form of activity outside of your quest. They are also unable to benefit from downtime while engaged in your quest. Whether or not to lock a PC is up to you, as is whether or not their possible progression applies within your quest. Keep in mind travel, in-character duration, and mechanical balance when deciding whether or not to lock the PCs, and be sure to communicate a quest lock during your original post or pregrame discussion.

Death, Disease and Curses

Adventuring is a risky job, and bad things often happen to adventurers. Diseases, poisons, and other similar effects persist until they’re removed, and death within a quest applies to a PC outside of the quest as well. However, thanks to the proliferation of healing and revival services from players in our setting, they are often simple to overcome. If you wish to enact permanent effects, be sure to communicate that possibility to the players during your original post or pregame discussion.

Character Rewards

You award the players rewards for their accomplishments in the form of experience, gold, and magic items for their characters, which must be detailed in your #story-log post recording the quest.

Experience

Players should receive experience for participating in combat and for engaging in good roleplay. DMs should follow the usual guidelines for granting Experience, and are encouraged to request approval for more than the general amount in quests which are long-running or highly impactful.

Magic Items

Player generally expect to receive a Magic Item as a reward for their participation in your quest. It is often most exciting to include these items as possible rewards within the quest which they can then use or keep, but sometimes it is most appropriate to provide the items as a form of payment at the end. Regardless of the source, the below table outlines what rarity of items can be rewarded per PC without Staff Approval, provided that the items are available on the loot list:

Tier Rarity
Tier 1 Uncommon
Tier 2 Rare
Tier 3 Very Rare
T4 and Above Legendary
Misc. Treasure

You may wish to award the players with gold or valuable treasures which they may keep or sell as an additional reward from the questgiver or discovery during play. The below table outlines what the maximum amount of additional treasure which can be rewarded per PC without Staff Approval. If no Magic Items are awarded, you may increase this amount by the item's trade value:

Tier Amount Item Trade Value
Tier 1 200 gp 400 gp
Tier 2 2,000 gp 4,000 gp
Tier 3 20,000gp 40,000gp
Tier 4+ 100,000 gp 200,000 gp

Cosmetic Rewards

DMs may provide cosmetic rewards such as eye color changes, floating halos, or other thematically appropriate character options as they see fit, provided that they do not allow for any mechanical benefits.

When to seek Staff Approval

As mentioned throughout the above document, there are a number of times when it is appropriate to seek approval from Staff to assist with running your quest or to ensure that your quest is in-line with the general lore and balance expectations of our server. The following list outlines the most common reasons you may need to request Staff oversight:

  • Running named NPCs, Deities or important factions from the Forgotten Realms setting
  • Providing players with information relevant to ongoing Questlines or content provided by members of staff
  • Running content inside of an area of the Forgotten Realms which a staff member is currently focused on
  • Attempting to exceed the XP, Item or Gold reward limits for long-running quests or exemplary gameplay
  • Rewarding magic items which do not appear on the existing loot lists
  • Rewarding high-level awards such as Super Legendary items, Artifacts or Boons
  • Rewarding items which provide a permanent stat boost
  • Providing other custom rewards such as automatons, legendary crafting materials, custom items, or anything that may impact future gameplay on TWR
  • Including homebrewed monsters or equipment within your quest (if included, such additions cannot leave your quest without majority Dungeonmaster approval)

DM Rewards

Running a quest takes time and effort that we feel should be rewarded. Rewards for running a quest come in two main ways:

Omni-XP

Omni-XP is awarded to the DM based on the average amount of XP delivered to their players. Omni-XP is restricted by tier and only applies to non-Paragon PCs.

Paragon Tokens

Paragon Tokens can be taken in lieu of Omni-XP and can be applied to future roleplay to increase the amount of RP-XP rewarded to one of your Paragon PCs.

Please note that you MAY choose instead to have one of your PCs participate in the request and receive the same rewards as the players, instead of choosing one of the above rewards. If you do so, Staff must approve the rewards whether they fall within the otherwise stated limits or not.

Core

Gameplay Rules

Gameplay Rules

Gameplay Rules

  1. Rules and mechanics are RAW by default. Any exceptions to this rule will be documented in the Homebrew section or Errata section.
  2. DM rulings are final. You don’t have to agree with it, but you must abide by it.
    1. If you have an issue with a DM’s ruling you may bring it up to the DM directly after the game/quest, not mid-session.
    2. If you speak with the DM and still disagree with the ruling, you may bring it up in #the-peoples-court for further discussion.
  3. Within player-led content (quests, trials, whatever), the DM of the session is king.
  4. All staff and players are expected to respect each others’ time by remaining present and attentive during gameplay.
  5. Do not leave a quest, trial, hunt, or other event without permission from the DM or person running it, or you will be cursed.
  6. If your DM or the person running your content leaves unexpectedly, contact a @Moderator or @Dungeonmaster for guidance
  7. Do NOT cheat. Modifying your loot or experience past their actual values is strictly prohibited.
    1. If you are controlling an enemy in a Trial or Hunt, playing the enemy poorly on purpose is cheating.
    2. If you are uncertain about anything, ping the DM/DM trainee that posted the record or post your question/concern to #questions.
  8. You may not play as or with a character on the server until it has been posted by a DM, DM Trainee, or Admin in #active-pc-sheet-links.
  9. RP and Gameplay should not include erotic or overly sexual themes. A fade to black is generally acceptable.
  10. Monsters in hunts and trials should use their pre-2024 statblocks. MotM statblocks take priority over legacy statblocks. Quest statblocks are on DM-discretion.
Tracking PC Activity in Discord

All changes to your PC’s character sheet, canonical events, rewards, downtime results, etc. must be recorded in one of the following four channels:

#transcript: Players can submit any player-run RP, gametype or event, downtime activity, or other official changes to #transcript for review. Once the post has been moved to #records by staff, it will become official TWR Canon.

#transaction-log: Players submit any financial transactions with other players or NPCs (including mundane item purchases) in this channel for review.

#records: Staff will post final reports from #transcript or related to their own content in Records, where it becomes official and rewards are applied to the player.

#story-log: Contains the results of quests, large scale plotlines, and other

Character Interaction Consent

All character interactions are based on the consent of the players controlling them. That means that if someone refuses to interact with someone’s character for any reason, they may do so. This rule is to protect players from unwanted interaction, not to shield players from consequences.

Hireling Update 2

Team involved: @Loremaster

Hello lurkers!

This update is an addendum to the previously released Hireling spreadsheet for NPC pricing. Utilizing this, you will have guidelines with which you may hire NPCs over time, up to a predetermined maximum amount, for whatever individual, group, or organizational needs you have. If there is confusion on how this works, please use the attached spreadsheet, or ask a @Loremaster.

Contracting NPC Requirements:

Maximum CR that can be hired as a single unit is capped at CR 20

Total CR across all hired units is capped at CR = 30

Hiring occurs weekly, using a point deduction system (Hire Points)

Points accrue at a rate of 1/week from the time interest is expressed, and equate to the Total CR that can be used to hire units

Point deductions are based against the CR being hired.

Example: Player currently has total of 5 Hire Points. The player can Hire any combination of humanoid creatures less than or equal to the total CR of 5.

Spreadsheet for CR to Hire Points breakdown can be seen here: https://docs.google.com/file/d/1Qv2-Cna8BUpkpW0geMdIO68BIL-coSrd/edit?usp=docslist\_api&filetype=msexcel

Please submit these hire requests to transcript and ping a @Loremaster for approval.

Attunement and Magic Items for Hirelings Hirelings can equip and attune to magic items provided to them by their employer based upon their CR, as shown below:

  • CR 1/8 - CR 1/2: Common (no attunement)

  • CR 1 - CR 4: Uncommon (attunement up to 1 item)

  • CR 5 - 10: Rare (attunement up to 2 items)

  • CR 11 - 16: Very Rare (attunement up to 3 items)

  • CR 17+: Legendary (attunement up to 3 items)

If the hirelings statblock has an armor or weapon listed, they are treated as proficient with all weapons or armor of that same type (e.g. leather - light armor, Shortsword - martial weapons). If you have questions or concerns, please me know, and I will be working with existing groups/organizations to get you switched over to this new framework

From #Patch-Notes

Much discussion and collaboration has gone into the merger of Hireling system with the previously used Organizations system. They will now be brought under one framework, with some added rules for how groups and organizations will work under this system, how hirelings can be equipped with items from their employers, and some promising prospects for future updates.

Individual & Group Hirelings

The ability for individuals and established groups to hire NPCs to augment their personal or collaborative efforts will be broken into one of two categories, with slightly different considerations for each. Hirelings can be reskinned to represent any humanoid race or alignment, and can speak common by default.

Contracting Requirements (Individual)

Hiring updates occur once per week, using a point deduction system (Hire Points)

Points accrue at a rate of 1/week, requiring an approved post from a Loremaster These points are logged via ⁠transcript and the total equates to the Total CR that can be used to hire units for that update.

Point deductions are based on the CR being hired. CR 0 units count as CR 1/8 for this, there is a graph that breaks down these numbers in more detail.

Individuals contracting NPCs will use the 'Deployed Monthly' rate, as opposed the normal Daily/Monthly rate. These expenses are logged via ⁠transaction-log after the update is approved by a Loremaster. These expenses occur at the 1st of every month.

Maximum CR that can be hired as a single unit is capped at CR 20

Total CR that can be hired is capped at CR 20

The screenshot below shows a week-by-week breakdown of how hire points can be spent on the corresponding CR.

Contracting Requirements (Group/Organizational)

Hiring updates occur once per week, using a point deduction system (Hire Points)

Points accrue based upon the modifiers calculated for your group, from 1-10, requiring an approved post from a Loremaster. These points are logged via ⁠transcript and the total equates to the Total CR that can be used to hire units for that update.

Publicity (popularity, reputation, goodwill)

Accessibility (access, reach)

Logistics (training, supplies, budget)

Opportunity (job security, importance, need)

Temp buffs (quests/significant events)

Groups/Organizations consisting of multiple PCs behave as a single ‘entity’ for the sake of point accumulation and spending. Updates will be logged with a single PC representing the group.

Point deductions are based on the CR being hired. CR 0 units count as CR 1/8 for this, there is a graph that breaks down these numbers in more detail.

Groups/Organizations contracting NPCs will use the normal 'Monthly' rate. These expenses are logged via ⁠transaction-log after the update is approved by a Loremaster. These expenses occur at the 1st of every month.

Maximum CR that can be hired as a single unit is capped at CR 20

Optional Rule: Banking RP XP

Optional Rule: Banking RP XP

Optional Rule - Banking RP XP

Characters who submit RP XP in normal gameplay (Levels 1–26) may choose to not apply the XP immediately, instead banking it to be claimed later during Paragon progression. When you reach that same level in Paragon, you can claim your banked XP using our automated tracking alias.

How to Bank & Claim XP

Step 1: Nominate to Bank Your XP

When reporting your RP XP in transcripts, explicitly state that you are banking the XP next to your character's name Example:

Characters Involved: @Player name Name McNameson L6 (Banking)

Step 2: Record it with the Alias

Once your RP XP is approved, save the XP to your character using the !bankxp alias

  • Note: The transcript link is required to successfully log the XP.

!bankxp <level> <xp amount> <records link>

Example:

!bankxp 6 3000

Step 3: Changing Sheets

If you switch character sheets, as many folks do when transitioning to Paragron, your banked XP does not carry over automatically as it is tied to your character's local variables. You can easily transfer your bank to a new sheet using the alias as it uses your user variables:

!char <old char>
!bankxp export
!char <new char>
!bankxp import

Step 4: Claim Your Banked XP in Paragon

Once you reach that same level in Paragon, you can withdraw your banked XP by linking your RP XP Record in Transcript. The bot will automatically wipe the bank for that level and generate your claim transcript template.

!bank use <level>

Template:

**Banked XP**
[name] has reached [paragon level] and claims their banked xp from [level]

Amount banked: [xp recorded]
Records: [link to record]

Example:

!bankxp use 6

Bot output:

**Banked XP**
Name McNameson has reached A1 L6 and claims their banked xp from L6

Amount banked: 3000xp
Records: [link to record]

Checking Your Banked XP

At any time, you can view your entire 26-level bank sheet. This displays a table of all your logged XP, featuring a Link status column showing how many links you have for that level

!bankxp

Core

Paragon Systems

Paragon Systems

Prestige of the Gods

Prestige of the Gods

A character who has reached level 20 and achieved the 6 post-20 milestones may choose to undergo a divine transformation in which the gods revert their mind and body to the state of a neophyte adventurer. Starting again at level 1-3, a ‘prestiged’ adventurer may begin again - choosing any new class, feats, or even remodeling their own personal attributes. They retain all knowledge, wealth, and any items they had prior to this.

Upon choosing to undergo the transformation, the adventurer may choose a cosmetic effect to be bestowed upon them. This effect must be proposed by the player, and approved by a DM in the request to prestige the character (in #transcript). Examples of such an effect could include: Flittering sparkles that follow the character, an ethereal halo above their head, or a glowing/changing tattoo.

Paragon Systems: Gestalt and Ascendant

Gestalts are now considered a Paragon system, with the addition of Ascendants, which operate in a similar way - granting class levels past 20 - without having to reset.

A character’s Paragon stage represents the number of times they have completed a full class level system (finished p20), starting at a value of 1. This number is used to determine experience gain, and for communicating your character’s progress, as seen in “How are Levels Counted”. Such systems and changes can and will be subject to change and active monitoring.

How Levels are Counted

Levels are counted through the following format A#L#, where A represents your paragon stage, and L represents your remaining levels. For example, a P26 wizard with 10 additional levels from this system would be an A1L10. This can be similarly done with tiers.

This is similarly done with gestalt, in which the format is G#L#, where G represents your Paragon stage, and L represents your current level, up to 26. This can be similarly done with tiers.

Ascendant Paragon

Characters can now progress past level 20, continuing to gain character levels, being known as Ascendants rather than Gestalts. The character’s XP counter would reset to zero, though they would keep their character levels, proficiency bonus, and P20 rewards. Such Ascendants would proceed to level another class, starting from T1, and gaining an appropriate amount of XP, with the ability to do so again upon completing P20.

Build Rules

  • To qualify a PC must be fully leveled, meaning level 20 with all post 20 levels completed.

  • Ascendant PCs cannot gain experience from hunts, trials, DM-XP, Transcript-XP, etc. They can only gain experience from RP-XP or Quests.

  • In quests that involve combat, while you will receive XP for the RP, you will receive no XP for the creatures killed.

  • Ascendant hit dice are restricted to the two highest hit dice per level (as opposed to getting all hit dice per level).

  • Rather than gaining the save proficiencies of all classes, Ascendants choose one strong save and one weak save from the options given to them by their classes:

    • Strong Saves: Dex, Con, Wis
    • Weak Saves: Str, Int, Cha

  • Any changes to the locked classes or subclasses are allowed and follow the normal retraining rules.

  • Due to the documentation required for this system, character sheets must be handled in G-Sheets.

  • ASIs stack, but do not stack past the normal cap of 20 unless otherwise specified. Stats may not exceed 30 for any reason.

  • You can not take the same feat multiple times unless otherwise specified. Feats that scale based on level are calculated based on your class levels.

  • Ascendant PC's, May only hunt, trial or delve with PC's who are also Ascendant

  • Spell save DCs and spellcasting follow multi classing rules. Spell Save DCs and Spell Attack Bonuses calculate based on the class providing the spell.

  • Class features that references class levels are self contained for the applicable class and paragon cycle

Stacking

Class Features, Spell Slots, Proficiencies and Stat Changes generally stack unless otherwise specified.

Exceptions

The following features do NOT stack when creating a Ascendant PC:

  • Proficiency Bonus
  • Extra Attack
  • Unarmored Defense
  • Duplicated Paladin Auras
  • Movement speed increases from duplicate sources.
  • Bladesong, and other features with limited uses such as rage, do not get doubled buffs but do get a increased number of uses.

Prestige Classes

The Ascendant Paragon system also includes Prestige Classes, classes that have specific requirements for their use and play, but are generally stronger than the normal classes. Further information can be found at the Prestige Classes page.

Gestalt Paragon

This is a variant to the typical prestige system, and while it may grant great boons it also has great restrictions as well. When you Gestalt Paragon, you must post in #transcript including both the new and original sheets for reference.

Gestalt Overview

  • Upon gestalt prestige you can select a class to level alongside your current one.
  • The starting proficiencies, skills, and other benefits are granted to the character.
  • When you level up, both classes level simultaneously, and you gain the benefits from both.
  • Put simply, you have build A which was gestalted, getting added to build B. This is similar to if you had two separate characters who were merged into one.
  • ASIs granted through level ups can be reassigned.
  • This process can be repeated, allowing for a singular character to slowly grow in power over the years as they grow more involved in the world at large.

Cumulative Level

  • Cumulative Level is the total number of levels from all your classes combined.
  • Cumulative Level is used to calculate what trials, hunts, and quests you can be involved in.

Current Level

  • Current Level is the current base level of the character and calculated as it would be normally, as though you were leveling a normal character.
  • The Current Level is what is used to calculate proficiency bonus, character progression, and RP experience gains. Things that scale based on level use your Current Level.

Gestalt Reversion

  • At any time a character can revert a gestalt prestige. This will reset the character to a level 1 class of their choice akin to a normal prestige, provide zero cosmetic and stat benefits, and allow the character to once again gain experience from trials, hunts, etc.
  • The character will then be locked out of the gestalt prestige system for 6 months.
  • This can be done at any time and at any level.

Build Rules

  • All Gestalt PCs begin at level 1

  • Class levels do not mix between Gestalt Prestiges. Each prestige is treated as a unique PC build.

  • To qualify a PC must be fully leveled, meaning level 20 with all post 20 levels completed.

  • Gestalt PCs cannot gain experience from hunts, trials, DM-XP, Transcript-XP, etc. They can only gain experience from RP-XP or Quests.

  • In quests that involve combat, while you will receive XP for the RP, you will receive no XP for the creatures killed.

  • Gestalt PCs may not change their race, background, Racial ASIs, class or subclass choice, or anything else regarding the basis of the character which was set during their initial creation.

  • On level up, the initial class chosen will follow the same build path (for example Fighter Champion) and multi class level split (if applicable) that the character had PRIOR to that prestige.

  • Gestalt hit dice are restricted to the two highest hit dice per level (as opposed to gestalts getting all hit dice per level).

  • Rather than gaining the save proficiencies of all classes, Gestalts choose one strong save and one weak save from the options given to them by their classes:

    • Strong Saves: Dex, Con, Wis
    • Weak Saves: Str, Int, Cha

  • Gestalt PC's may choose to redistribute their ASI's and redo their first class in any way that is within the rules.

  • Due to the documentation required for this system, character sheets must be handled in G-Sheets.

  • ASIs stack, but do not stack past the normal cap of 20 unless otherwise specified. Stats may not exceed 30 for any reason.

  • You can not take the same feat multiple times unless otherwise specified. Feats that scale based on level are calculated based on your Current Level not your Total Level.

  • Gestalt PCs may attune to any item they own, however, Gestalt PCs may not use items which exceed their “Current Level” during hunts or trials with non-Gestalt PCs.

  • Gestalt PCs may choose to join hunts above their Current Level, but not if non-Gestalt PCs are present. This does not affect Body Retrieval Hunts. If a gestalt hunting party is a mix of tiers, they can not recover a body.

  • Spell save DCs and spellcasting follow multi classing rules. Spell Save DCs and Spell Attack Bonuses calculate based on the class providing the spell.

Stacking

Class Features, Spell Slots, Proficiencies and Stat Changes generally stack unless otherwise specified.

Exceptions

The following features do NOT stack when creating a Gestalt PC:

  • Proficiency Bonus
  • Extra Attack
  • Unarmored Defense
  • Duplicated Paladin Auras
  • Movement speed increases from duplicate sources.
  • Bladesong, and other features with limited uses such as rage, do not get doubled buffs but do get a increased number of uses.

Paragon Wish Patch:

tl;dr - Introducing a very arduous method to regain wish through a whole gestalt prestige and questline using a Post20 Blessing/Boon Slot.

Requirements

  1. Paragon into a spellcasting class that also learns wish
  2. Complete self RP and DM-led quests (at least 4) throughout your prestige that meet the following guidelines
    1. Integrate with an existing group of worshipers for a particular deity
    2. Receive character references from leadership within the church/group
    3. Reach a level that would otherwise grant you wish from your prestige class
    4. Travel to the chosen deity’s home plane and petition their aid directly with offerings and references prepared
    5. Donate at least 2 items to the god directly, sacrificing them to prove your devotion. One item must be of legendary power and the second must be of great personal importance to your PC.
    6. Perform a quest for that god directly, run by a Dungeon master and approved by at least 2 more DMs or LMs

Regaining Wish

Once all of the requirements have been met and your PC is eligible for a Post20 Boon/Blessing Slot, the God will decide whether or not to grant you the Blessing of Forgiveness:

Blessing of Forgiveness - This blessing removes one existing instance of permanent loss of wish. Once a creature has received this blessing, they can no longer receive it from the same deity.

Note: It may not be possible to convince any other gods to grant this blessing or you may attract significant attention from your previous god if so. It would require unfathomable time and effort to regain wish a second time.

Gestalt and Ascension Interaction:

Gestalt or Ascension can be chosen when a character finishes p20 or completes a paragon cycle (finishes p20 on another class system). In doing so, a character may choose to Gestalt as a way to prestige and change through their class choices, though would still level according to their paragon cycle number.

For example, a P3L0 (has finished this cycle but has not started a new one) may choose to Gestalt, and become a G4L1, where they may again choose to move back into ascension after leveling to p20.

Core

Player-Run NPCs

Player-Run NPCs

Player-ran NPCs

A player may run an NPC with the following caveats. Breaking any requires the permission of a @Dungeonmaster or @Loremaster.

1: The NPC must act according to its character, or alignment.

2: The NPC cannot be a high-standing or of great importance individual.

3: The NPC must be given adequate reason to physically exist in this plane.

4: The NPC cannot grant PC's mechanical benefits of any sort. Items, Crafting, Gifts, all of the like. Only acceptable as shopkeep or storefronts selling items.

----

Rule 1 dictates that monsters must act relevant to lore. To break such action, or to play an outlier, requires permission.

Rule 2 dictates that NPC roleplayed must be of low bearing. Shopkeep, Bartenders, Apprentices and the generic like. A player cannot run any characters which could influence a greater plot that they are not actively running.

Rule 3 dictates that no creature may exist without bearing. A mind flayer would not exist in a town as a vampire lord would not be sleeping in a forest.

Rule 4 dictates that NPC may not grant mechanical benefits. Pure and simple, save shopkeeps selling mundane items at reasonable (per market discretion) prices.

Core

Post-20 Rewards

Post-20 Rewards

Post 20 Rewards

A Player Character is considered to be Post20 if they have reached 385,000xp, and receive rewards at the following thresholds:

XP Threshold Reward
385,000 ASI +1
415,000 AS1 +1
445,000 Boon/Feat/Blessing
475,000 AS1 +1
505,000 AS1 +1
535,000 Boon/Feat/Blessing

Post-20 Rules

  • Boon/Blessing/Feat choices are permanent.
  • Your PC's first Boon/Blessing may be chosen from the list of Boons or Blessings once the slot has been unlocked (use the !boon or !blessing command in discord)
    • For PCs who earned Boons via a quest before this change, you may choose the next Boon slot that you unlock through the Post-20 or Paragon systems
  • Feats can be selected once unlocked.
  • Feats can be retrained into quested Boons/Blessings if desired
  • Boon and Blessing choices are permanent
  • Blessings/Charms can be removed by the granting Deity at DM discretion.
  • Blessings are not limited to a fixed list, and can be shaped and created to better fit a circumstance, at the DM’s discretion. This would require a majority vote to proceed.
  • Post 20 Boons and Blessings can be obtained using the Wish spell, but the Wish must be worded appropriately. This only applies to the second Boon slot of a PC's first 20 levels. PCs cannot use Wish to gain boons or blessings for any paragon cycle boon slots.
  • A comprehensive list of blessing and boons can be viewed on discord using !boon or !blessing
  • Please post your Post 20 rewards in #transcript as you receive them
  • A PC that gets Post20 rewards is still considered a level 20 character for all intents and purposes
Core

Prestige Systems

Prestige Systems

Prestige of the Gods

Prestige of the Gods

A character who has reached level 20 and achieved the 6 post-20 milestones may choose to undergo a divine transformation in which the gods revert their mind and body to the state of a neophyte adventurer. Starting again at level 1-3, a ‘prestiged’ adventurer may begin again - choosing any new class, feats, or even remodeling their own personal attributes. They retain all knowledge, wealth, and any items they had prior to this.

Upon choosing to undergo the transformation, the adventurer may choose a cosmetic effect to be bestowed upon them. This effect must be proposed by the player, and approved by a DM in the request to prestige the character (in #transcript). Examples of such an effect could include: Flittering sparkles that follow the character, an ethereal halo above their head, or a glowing/changing tattoo.

Paragon Systems: Gestalt and Ascendant

Gestalts are now considered a Paragon system, with the addition of Ascendants, which operate in a similar way - granting class levels past 20 - without having to reset.

A character’s Paragon stage represents the number of times they have completed a full class level system (finished p20), starting at a value of 1. This number is used to determine experience gain, and for communicating your character’s progress, as seen in “How are Levels Counted”. Such systems and changes can and will be subject to change and active monitoring.

Ascendant

Characters can now progress past level 20, continuing to gain character levels, being known as Ascendants rather than Gestalts. The character’s XP counter would reset to zero, though they would keep their character levels, proficiency bonus, and P20 rewards. Such Ascendants would proceed to level another class, starting from T1, and gaining an appropriate amount of XP, with the ability to do so again upon completing P20.

How can you Swap

For Gestalts currently in place, they may choose to revert to P20 and take 20 levels in each class system they have already finished leveling. They would take levels equal to their level before the shift in the class levels they had taken. For example, an A2 Level 13 whose base classes are 20 Fighter and 20 Wizard, and is currently leveling Artificer, would revert to 20 Fighter, 20 Wizard, and 13 Artificer, along with P20 rewards.

How Levels are Counted

Levels are counted through the following format A#L#, where A represents your paragon stage, and L represents your remaining levels. For example, a P26 wizard with 10 additional levels from this system would be an A1L10. This can be similarly done with tiers.

This is similarly done with gestalt, in which the format is G#L#, where G represents your Paragon stage, and L represents your current level, up to 26. This can be similarly done with tiers.

After Ascension:

When a pre-existing character begins their first ascension cycle (starting to level a new class system) or converts from gestalt, they can choose to adjust their base ability scores through point buy and may choose to swap current feats, asi, and p20 asi at no penalty. This must be submitted through transcript

Gestalt and Ascension Interaction:

Gestalt or Ascension can be chosen when a character finishes p20 or completes a paragon cycle (finishes p20 on another class system). In doing so, a character may choose to Gestalt as a way to prestige and change through their class choices, though would still level according to their paragon cycle number.

For example, a P3L0 (has finished this cycle but has not started a new one) may choose to Gestalt, and become a G4L1, where they may again choose to move back into ascension after leveling to p20.

Changes to Gestalt System:

Gestalt would remain with the ability to adjust stats upon reset, as stated previously. In addition, they would no longer be required to level their base class as they would normally, and may choose to level a different class instead.

Retroactive Adjustments:

For those who choose to stay in gestalt, characters may receive retroactive rewards. Firstly, a character may adjust base stats and character levels, submitting a new sheet to transcript along with the old (make a copy and do changes from there) to be used as a reference. Additionally, players may reclaim downtime for changing class levels for characters or training characters, since the gestalt system was first introduced. Players must submit the time they would receive to transcript, with relevant links, where they would then be able to use that time in the future. Players may complete this same process for the gold cost.

Note:

All character changes must be done through the transcript. It is recommended that you make a copy of your old gsheet when adjusting things.

PART 6 | GESTALT PRESTIGE

Gestalt Prestige System

This is a variant to the typical prestige system, and while it may grant great boons it also has great restrictions as well. When you Gestalt Prestige, you must post in #transcript including both the new and original sheets for reference. Once approved, the new sheet will be posted in #3-gestalt-pc-links

Please note this system is still in playtesting and is subject to change at any time

Gestalt Overview

All Gestalt PCs begin at level 1

Upon gestalt prestige you can select a class to level alongside your current one.

The starting proficiencies, skills, and other benefits are granted to the character. See Here for a detailed explanation of how class features stack.

When you level up, both classes level simultaneously, and you gain the benefits from both.

Put simply, you have build A which was prestiged and locked in, getting added to build B. This is similar to if you had two separate characters who were merged into one.

ASIs granted through level ups can be reassigned.

Original class and subclass levels are locked in.

This process can be repeated, allowing for a singular character to slowly grow in power over the years as they grow more involved in the world at large.

Cumulative Level

Cumulative Level is the total number of levels from all your classes combined.

Cumulative Level is used to calculate what trials, hunts, and quests you can be involved in.

Current Level

Current Level is the current base level of the character and calculated as it would be normally, as though you were leveling a normal character.

The Current Level is what is used to calculate proficiency bonus, character progression, and RP experience gains. Things that scale based on level use your Current Level.

Gestalt Reversion

At any time a character can revert a gestalt prestige. This will reset the character to a level 1 class of their choice akin to a normal prestige, provide zero cosmetic and stat benefits, and allow the character to once again gain experience from trials, hunts, etc.

The character will then be locked out of the gestalt prestige system for 6 months.

This can be done at any time and at any level.

Restrictions

Class levels do not mix between Gestalt Prestiges. Each prestige is treated as a unique PC build.

To qualify a PC must be fully leveled, meaning level 20 with all post 20 levels completed.

Gestalt PCs cannot gain experience from hunts, trials, DM-XP, Transcript-XP, etc. They can only gain experience from RP-XP or Quests.

In quests that involve combat, while you will receive XP for the RP, you will receive no XP for the creatures killed.

Gestalt PCs may not change their race, background, Racial ASIs, class or subclass choice, or anything else regarding the basis of the character which was set during their initial creation.

On level up, the initial class chosen will follow the same build path (for example Fighter Champion) and multi class level split (if applicable) that the character had PRIOR to that prestige.

Gestalt hit dice are restricted to the two highest hit dice per level (as opposed to gestalts getting all hit dice per level).

Rather than gaining the save proficiencies of all classes, Gestalts choose one strong save and one weak save from the options given to them by their classes:

Strong Saves Weak Saves

DEX STR

CON INT

WIS CHA

Any changes to the locked classes or subclasses are allowed and follow the normal retraining rules based on the level of the class being retrained.

Due to the documentation required for this system, character sheets must be handled in G-Sheets.

ASIs stack, but do not stack past the normal cap of 20 unless otherwise specified. Stats may not exceed 30 for any reason.

You can not take the same feat multiple times unless otherwise specified. Feats that scale based on level are calculated based on your Current Level not your Total Level.

Gestalt PCs may attune to any item they own, however, Gestalt PCs may not use items which exceed their “Current Level” during hunts or trials with non-Gestalt PCs.

Gestalt PCs may choose to join hunts above their Current Level, but not if non-Gestalt PCs are present. This does not affect Body Retrieval Hunts. If a gestalt hunting party is a mix of tiers, they can not recover a body.

Spell save DCs and spellcasting follow multi classing rules. Spell Save DCs and Spell Attack Bonuses calculate based on the class providing the spell.

Combining Gestalt Classes

Class Features, Spell Slots, Proficiencies and Stat Changes generally stack unless otherwise specified.

Exceptions

The following features do NOT stack when creating a Gestalt PC:

Proficiency Bonus

Multi Attack

Unarmored Defense

Duplicated Paladin Auras

Movement speed increases from duplicate sources.

Bladesong, and other features with limited uses such as rage, do not get doubled buffs but do get a increased number of uses.

Gestalt FighterWatermark

Gestalt/Wish Patch:

tl;dr - Introducing a very arduous method to regain wish through a whole gestalt prestige and questline using a Post20 Blessing/Boon Slot.

Requirements

Gestalt prestige into a spellcasting class that also learns wish

Complete self RP and DM-led quests (at least 4) throughout your prestige that meet the following guidelines

Integrate with an existing group of worshipers for a particular deity

Receive character references from leadership within the church/group

Reach a level that would otherwise grant you wish from your prestige class

Travel to the chosen deity’s home plane and petition their aid directly with offerings and references prepared

Donate at least 2 items to the god directly, sacrificing them to prove your devotion. One item must be of legendary power and the second must be of great personal importance to your PC.

Perform a quest for that god directly, run by a Dungeonmaster and approved by at least 2 more DMs or LMs

Regaining Wish

Once all of the requirements have been met and your PC is eligible for a Post20 Boon/Blessing Slot, the God will decide whether or not to grant you the Blessing of Forgiveness:

Blessing of Forgiveness - This blessing removes one existing instance of permanent loss of wish. Once a creature has received this blessing, they can no longer receive it from the same deity.

Note: It may not be possible to convince any other gods to grant this blessing or you may attract significant attention from your previous god if so. It would require unfathomable time and effort to regain wish a second time.

Regarding Simulacrums

  1. Sims Simulacrums are considered NPCs. Paragons will not be able to earn rpxp and quest xp by way of proxy

Retraining Rules

Retraining Rules

Retraining Rules

Class Retraining

By spending 10 workweeks of downtime, a character can choose to replace one of their levels in one class with a level in another class. This time is reduced by a number of workweeks equal to the character’s ability modifier in the key ability of the new class. If their new class has more than one key ability, the characters lowest ability modifier should be used for this calculation. The character must have a minimum of 13 in the key abilities of both their current class and their new class They must have an instructor of at least 1 level higher (or be level 20) than your new level in the new class and must spend 50gp per week for the instructor and relevant supplies.

Fighting Style Retraining

(For Fighters, Rangers, Paladins, Blood Hunters, and College of Swords Bards only) By spending a week of downtime, you can choose one of the (insert class name here) fighting style you know and replace it with another fighting style from the (insert class name here) class.

Feat / ASI Retraining

By spending a week of downtime, you can choose to replace one Feat or ASI you qualify for with another Feat or ASI you qualify for. Post20 ASIs can be retrained only to ASIs, and Post20 Feats can be retrained only to Boons or Feats.

Spell Retraining

(For sorcerers, warlocks, bards and rangers only) By spending a week of downtime,you can choose one of the (insert class name here) spells you know and replace it with another spell from the (insert class name here) spell list, which also must be of a level for which you have spell slots.

Mystic Arcanum Retraining

Warlocks can spend 1 week of downtime to retrain one of their mystic arcanum spells for another spell that is applicable for that version of the mystic arcanum classfeat.

RP Reduction

When you undergo retraining, you can submit an RP-XP request for roleplay related to the retraining and receive a reduction in the overall time spent retraining. Each RP-XP request is worth a 5% reduction, up to a maximum of 25%.

Core

Retroactive Downtime

Retroactive Downtime

We get it, you can’t always plan your character’s lives in real time. That’s why we’ve designed Retroactive Downtime, which lets you apply unused downtime at a reduced wait to cover gaps in gameplay and incetivize coming back to TWR!

Starting from the last date your PC used their downtime, you can now file a report to use 1/3 of the total days (rounded down) on a single goal or downtime activity with staff approval.

How does it work?

Players wishing to file for retroactive downtime must complete the report on the right and submit it to #transcript. Staff will determine the appropriate daily value for your character and resources and return the report with any important notes.

Custom Retroactive Downtime

We are also introducing a few new forms of “retroactive” downtime you can add to the report:

General Adventuring: XP Bonus

Characters who spend their time hunting, traveling, or otherwise generally adventuring receive bonus XP:

Tier Bonus XP Cap (Per Day)
1 5 xp
2 20 xp
3 100 xp
4 200 xp
Post-20 300 xp
Service to a Deity: Favor Bonus

Characters who spend time in service of a deity will be rewarded for their faith with favor:

Tier Bonus Favor Cap (Per Day)
1 1 Favor
2 3 Favor
3 5 Favor
4 8 Favor
Post-20 10 Favor
The Career Path: Gold Bonus

Through smart investments, performance bonuses, side hustles and promotions, business ownership, etc., you receive bonus Gold:

Tier Bonus Gold Cap (Per Day)
1 5 gp
2 25 gp
3 50 gp
4 200 gp
Post-20 250 gp

Roleplay Bonuses

Players who perform roleplay with themselves or others to justify their downtime may include a summary and link to the roleplay for additional rewards.

Specifics: If you are selecting a specific downtime option as outlined in the source books, this document, or other TWR systems, include the report here using the “Retroactive Downtime” value above as the number of days spent. Then perform any rolls, checks, transactions, etc. as necessary here. You may also choose to perform more complicated projects such as starting a business, building a home, making friends in the form of NPCs, etc. through expanded roleplay.

Staff Review: Craftmasters and Dungeonmasters will review the report and consider any complications, necessary materials, or other concerns and work with you to apply your downtime in a reasonable way.

Core

Soulbound Item

Soulbound Item

Soulbound Items

In the ancient epochs, when the world was young and the weave of magic was still being shaped, the gods and primordial forces sought to leave their mark upon the mortal realm. They imbued certain objects with Runes of their essence, creating artifacts that resonated with the very souls of those who wielded them. These are the Soulbound Items.

A Soulbound Item is more than just a tool; it is a companion, a reflection of the bond between the bearer and the object. To attune to such an item is to forge a pact, intertwining one's fate with the artifact's power. As the wielder grows in strength and experience, so too does the Soulbound Item, awakening latent abilities and evolving in response to the challenges faced together.

However, this bond is not without its trials. The path to unlocking a Soulbound Item's full potential is fraught with challenges, requiring the bearer to prove their worth and commitment. Only through perseverance, valor, and a deep connection can the true power of the Soulbound Item be realized.

Soulbound Item Mechanics

  1. A Player Character can only ever be attuned to one Soulbound Item
  2. The Item is a relic

Progressing the Soulbound Item

  1. Each Soulbound Item has its progression on the relevant Item Progression table
  2. At certain levels the weapon gains one of 4 types of features, Base, Ability, Unique and Runes. Each feature will have options to choose from.
  3. For Ability and Unique features, The player can decide whether to take a Novice Rank option or to promote an previously chosen option to the next rank
  4. Runes provide minor benefits, where some Runes you need more than 1 before unlocking its benefits
  5. When you choose an option as part of a feature you cannot choose that option again, other to promote it, unless it's stated otherwise.
  6. Ability and Unique feature ranks are constrained limited by the strength of its owner. To unlock an Expert feature the owner must be level 11 or higher, to unlock a Master feature they must be level 17 or higher
  7. The Weapon can at no point be at a higher level than it's owner

Item Leveling

  1. While the item is attuned to a character, any experience that the player gains while attuned to the item is split 50/50 between the player and their soulbound item
    1. The XP will be scaled to the item's level via an alias.
    2. This includes XP from random hunts, dungeons, raids and quests.
    3. It is the players choice if up to 50% of RPXP goes to the weapon
    4. Example:
      1. If a level 8 Player gets 5000XP for Killing a Monster in a hunt and the item is also level 8, the Player and the Item each gets 2500XP
      2. If the weapon was at level 5, Player would get 2500XP which is 18% of XP Required to level to level 9. Thus the Item will get 18% of the exp required to go from level 5 to level 6, which is 1350 XP.
    5. When a player caps their level, the Item will still get 50% of the Exp that the player would have received
    6. This seems like complicated math, but there will be an alias to take care of all that
  2. Paragons:
    1. 50% of the experience gained from non-hunt combat participation can still go towards the weapon, this will be scaled for the Weapons level
    2. Paragon's Soulbound Items receive 50% of the Experience they would have gotten from combat. This includes Non-targetted hunts, Delves, Trials and Raids

Obtaining a Soulbound Item

  1. The secret of creating a soulbound item has been unlocked, but as the magic is tied to the wielder and not the crafting they can only be crafted at its common stage.
  2. In lieu of choosing an uncommon item tied to the backstory of a submitted character, a player can choose a Soulbound* item, with the item starting at the same level of the Character, however this should be covered in the backstory
  3. Soulbound Items can be traded, but they will start at level 1 for a new PC and progress will be reset. For all intents and purposes when being traded, they use common item selling values.

Retraining Item Levels

  1. By spending 1 workweek of downtime a Level feature can be retrained to a different option for that level.
  2. Only a single level can be retrained at a a time
    • If you are Master of item Feature A, and want to retrain the weapon into a Journeyman of Path B and Path A, you will spend 1 workweek to go to Expert Path A and Novice Path B and then another workweek to reach Journeyman Path A and Journeyman Path B

Reset

  1. A soulbound weapon can be reset at anytime. This does mean that that it restarts at level 1, and any progress or experience it gained will be lost.

Homebrewing

  1. Players are Encouraged to Homebrew their own Unique Features and Runes via Homebrew System & Index, this will expand the options for other players as well

Future Updates

  1. As this is a new system, it may receive some balancing updates, either with nerf, buffs or sideways adjustments. Participation in this system acknowledges that your Item may change.

The page will first look at the Base and Ability Features, then it will list the Runes, First general and then the different type Runes. Lastly we will look at the available Unique features for each type of item.

Base and Ability Features

Soulbound Weapons

"To draw steel that bleeds with your soul is to accept its hunger. A soulbound weapon is not a weapon forged in a smith’s fire but in the crucible of oath and intent. The weapon listens to its wielder’s will, whispering back in sparks of battle-born instinct. As its bearer grows, the weapon awakens, reshaping itself to mirror the paths chosen. In time, the warrior and the weapon are no longer two, but one sharpened edge against fate itself."

Base:

Each weapon starts with the following Base Stats, when you unlock a Ability feature, you can choose one of the below options to promote to a higher rank.

Base Attack: Attacks made with this weapon is considered to be magical

Path Die: D4, this applies anytime a Path option references Path Damage Die

Weapon DC: 8 + Wielder Proficiency Bonus, whenever a Path feature requires a saving throw or allows the casting of a spell, it will use the Weapon DC has it's DC

Charges: 2, Some Path option may Require the use of Charges. Charges reset to full at dawn.

Ability Features

Rank Base Attack Path Die Weapon DC Charges
Novice +1 Attack Bonus d6 Base + 2 Base + 2
Journeyman +1 Attack and Damage Bonus d8 Base + 3 Base + 3
Expert +2 Attack and Damage Bonus d10 Base + 4 Base + 4
Master +3 Attack and Damage Bonus d12 Base + Wielders Choice of Ability Modifier, set when choosing Wielders Choice of Ability Modifier, set when choosing

Soulbound Armor and Soulbound Shields

To carry a soulbound ward is to carry more than protection — it is a covenant between bearer and bulwark. These wards are not merely hammered plates or shaped wood; they are vessels of resolve, tempered by sacrifice and sealed with spirit. At first they guard as any armor or shield might, but as the bond deepens, the ward awakens — answering the bearer’s instincts, hardening in defiance, softening in stealth, or shining in defense of others. In time, the warrior is no longer clad in armor, but in a living testament of their soul’s endurance.

Base:

Each armor or shield starts with the following Base Stats, when you unlock a Ability feature, you can choose one of the below options to promote to a higher rank

  • Base AC Bonus: determined by the armor type (light, medium, heavy) or shield.

  • Ward Die: d4,

  • Armor DC: Used for any feature that requires a saving throw or reactive effect. Starts at 8 + Wielder proficiency bonus.

  • Charges: 2 (for active Ward abilities).Charges reset to full at dawn.

Physical and Mental Features

Rank AC Bonus Ward Die Armor DC Charges

Shield: +1 AC

Soulbound Foci

To wield a conduit is to place your soul in the current of the unseen. A staff, gem, or relic can be bound not by chains, but by resonance—its lattice aligned with the bearer’s essence. At first, it channels spells as any focus would, but soon the conduit hums with hidden voices, amplifying thought, bending the weave, answering only to the one who claimed it. By journey’s end, mage and conduit are indistinguishable: the caster’s will flows as lightning, and the relic itself becomes the echo of their soul.

A Soulbound focus can be any focus as determined by the Spellcasting feature of class. However the Owner can only attune to it if the item is an acceptable focus. This does include instruments and tools as well.

If the player character can use a weapon as a spellcasting focus, they can choose whether to use it as a soulbound focus or weapon. However once the choice is made the item will be locked into either a soulbound focus or soulbound weapon. For example if a player decided to make their weapon a soulbound focus, the progression is locked into conduit and focus abilities.

Base:

Each Focus starts with the following Base Stats, when you unlock a Ability feature, you can choose one of the below options to promote to a higher rank.

Base Focus: 0. Spell Save DC granted by class items do not stack with this focus. The Spell Save DC and spell attack bonus only applies if using the focus to cast.

Conduit Die: d4, this applies anytime a Conduit option references Conduit Die

Focus DC: 8 + Wielder Proficiency Bonus, whenever a Conduit feature requires a saving throw or allows the casting of a spell, it will use the Focus DC as it's DC

Charges: 2, Some Path option may require the use of Charges. Charges reset to full at dawn.

Physical and Mental Features

Rank Base Focus Conduit Die focus DC Charges
Novice +1 Spell Attack d6 Base + 2 Base + 2
Journeyman +2 Spell and +1 Spell Save DC d8 Basic + 3 Basic + 3
Expert +3 Spell and +2 Spell Save DC d10 Base + 4 Base + 4
Master +3 Spell Save DC d12 Spell Save DC Wielders Choice of Ability Modifier, set when choosing

Runes

As the Soulbound Item grows in power, etchings, runes or engraving may appear on it, this will either directly confer benefits, or in combination with other runes provide additional benefits.

Universal Runes:

These Runes can be used on weapon, armor, shields and foci:

  • Reclamation Rune - You can return the item to your hand (or your body in the case of armor) as an action.
  • Quick Reclamation Rune - You can return the item to your hand (or your body in the case of armor) as a bonus action, requires Reclamation Rune
  • Glamour Rune - You can freely change the appearance of the item as an action.
  • Compass Rune - While holding or wearing the item, you can determine the direction of true north, or the direction to a creature of which you speak its name.
  • Echo Rune - You can cast the message cantrip while the item is on your person.
  • Skill Runes - Once the item has accumulated two skill Runes, you gain proficiency in one skill of your choice while attuned to the item. An item can take skill Runes more than two times, and grant a new skill for every two of them it has accumulated.
  • Shifting Rune - Once the item has two shifting Runes, over the course of a long rest, you can move the properties of the item to another of the same category, in your possession, making the new item your soulbound item. For example, you can move the properties of a soulbound dagger onto a mundane spear, receiving a soulbound spear.
  • Shining Rune - The item sheds bright light out 10 feet, and dim light another 10 feet. This Rune can be taken a second time, doubling the radius of the light.
  • Specialization Rune - Once an item has accumulated four specialization Runes, the item gains one level of any path, ward, or conduit.
  • Intricate Rune - Once an item has accumulated four intricate Runes, the item gains one point to spend on any base feature.
  • Mnemonic Rune (2x) – The item can “store” one memory you designate. At 2 Mnemonic Runes, you can replay it vividly.
  • Expertise Runes - Once the item has accumulated two skill Runes, and two expertise Runes, you can add double your proficiency to the skill Rune skill, instead of normal proficiency.
  • Awakening Rune - When you have two Awaking Runes, your weapon gains sentience. See link for detail information Awakening Rune

Weapon Runes:

These Runes can only be taken on weapons:

  • Twin Rune - When you have 2 Twin Runes, as a bonus action, you may split your weapon into two identical light versions for two-weapon fighting. They recombine as a bonus action, only works with weapons with the light property. Each of these weapons function as your Soulbound weapon, but still only requires one attunement slot.
  • Master Reclamation Rune - Immediately after hitting or missing, the weapon flies back to your hand, this requires a Quick Reclamation Rune, Thrown Property and a Level 12+ Soulbound weapon
  • Identical Rune -When you have 2 Identical runes and 2 Twin Runes, as a bonus action, you may split your weapon into two identical versions for two-weapon fighting. They recombine as a bonus action. It only works if your soulbound weapon is light, versatile or lacks the heavy property.
  • Hunter’s Rune - While attuned, you can spend 1 minute studying a creature’s tracks or remnants to learn the direction it traveled within the past 24 hours.
  • Sanguine Rune - Once per short rest, when you reduce a creature to 0 HP, you get THP equal to your Path Die.
  • Dueling Spirit Runes - With 2 Deuling Spirit Runes, while fighting with the weapon in one hand and no other weapon or shield in the other, you gain +1 AC. With 4 invested, increase it to +2 AC.
  • Thrown Rune - After taking this rune a second time, your Weapon gains the following thrown properties based on its properties:
    • Finesse: 30/60
    • Heavy: 10/20
    • Else: 20/40
    • Additionally, if the weapon already has the thrown property, you instead add these distances to the weapon's base distances. Each additional time you take this rune after the second, you add the following distances:
      • Finesse: 10/20
      • Else: 5/10

Armor/Shield Runes:

These Runes can only be taken on Armor or Shields:

  • Defiant Rune – When you have 2 Defiant Runes, Once per long rest, when reduced to 0 HP while wearing the ward, you drop to 1 HP instead.
  • Aegis Rune – When you have 2 Aegis Runes and you succeed on a saving throw against a spell, you can use your reaction to grant advantage to one ally within 10 feet against the same effect.
  • Mirrorplate Rune – As a reaction once per short rest, impose disadvantage on an attack against you.
  • Beacon Runes – When you have 2 Beacon Runes, allies within 5 feet gain +1 on saving throws against being frightened. At 4 Runes, the aura extends to 10 feet and grants advantage instead.
  • Masterwork Rune - If you have 3 Masterwork Runes, you can upgrade your armor to highest tier armor of its type, any light armor, becomes studded leather, medium armor becomes half-plate and heavy armor becomes plate.

Focus Runes:

These Runes can only be taken on a focus:

  • Sigil Rune – While holding the conduit, you can inscribe temporary glowing runes that last 1 hour. You may leave one “mark” at a time that sheds dim light in 5 feet.
  • Spellkeeper Rune – You may store a cantrip in the conduit each long rest. You can cast it once as if you knew it, you can take this Rune again. If you have more than 1 you can store a spell you know during a long rest. The maximum level of spell you can store is equal to the number of Spellkeeper Runes minus 1. Regardless of how many Runes you have, you can only store 1 spell, and you can cast the spell without expending a spell slot.
  • Scryer’s Rune – Once per long rest, you can use the conduit as a divining rod, giving you advantage on a single Wisdom (Perception) or (Survival) check.
  • Resonance Runes – (Requires 2+) When you cast a spell, faint motes of energy linger. Allies within 5 feet gain +1 to their next attack roll. At 4 resonance Runes, the bonus is +1d4 instead.

Unique Features

Unique can bee seen on the following Pages:

  • Weapons: Soulbound Paths
  • Armor and Shields: Soulbound Wards
  • Foci: Soulbound Conduits

Staff Disciplinary Process

Staff Disciplinary Process

Staff Disciplinary Process

This is the general process through which our staff process any complaints or necessary review of a player's actions.

Moderators - Warnings and Strikes

  1. In the event that a Warning or strike is needed, the person first calling for a vote will create the poll in the Moderator Votes thread with a Moderator role ping, a brief description and a link to the comment.  A 24 hour period will be given for moderators to discuss or vote.  At the end of the 24 hours, or a majority is reached whichever comes first, the Moderator creating the poll will issue the action to the player and post in #The-Strike-Zone.

Bans

  1. In the event a player incurs a 3rd strike, the moderator issuing the strike will instead issue the ban message from the template, ban the player, and make the record in the strike zone.
  2. If it is for a major event, or other concern, any moderator may open a discussion and call for a vote.  Once the vote is open with the ping, the issue is decided as soon as there is a majority vote or super majority vote either direction.
    1. The three strike process may be bypassed if especially toxic or repeated inappropriate behavior is present, to the discretion of a supermajority of the Mods.
    2. A supermajority is 70% of available persons voting in favor of a particular position.
  3. A majority vote is required for Moderators to escalate such a case to Admins for final vote approval to ban or not.
  4. IF a Supermajority for Ban is reached by Moderators then the moderator starting the vote will ban the player, record the reason in Strike Zone, and ping admins with a summary so they’re aware.
