Animal Taming Rules

Animal Taming Rules

Animal Taming Rules

Overview

  • A PC may attempt to tame animals over an extended period of time.

Taming Check

Check: Wisdom (Animal Handling)

Tame DC: 15 + (2 * CR) (minimum 11)

Time: 1 full day of calm interaction (one day of downtime)

Initial Tame

Before training begins, the creature must first be made non-hostile through patience, calmness, or courage.

Roll Result
Natural 20 Start at 25% Bond Progress
Success Creature becomes non-hostile and open to training
Fail by 5 or less You fail to train the creature, you may retry after 1 day
Fail by 5 or more You fail to train the creature, you may retry after 3 days
Natural 1 The creature flees or attacks, you may retry after 1 week

Long-Term Bond Training

Each day requires 8 hours of focused interaction. You can train only one creature at a time. Each success adds your roll to a cumulative total.

Roll Result
Natural 20 Add roll plus 10% of total progress threshold
Success You Progress your bond with the creature
Fail by 5 or less Your bond with the creature does not progress
Fail by 5 or more The creature refuses training, you may retry after 3 days
Natural 1 The creature flees or attacks, you may retry after 1 week

Progress cannot fall below your current bond stage unless broken by neglect or narrative reason.

Bond Progression

Bond Stage Progress Threshold
Non-Hostile Success on Initial Tame
Sociable 10 + (10 * CR)
Basic Commands
Stay. Come. Stop. 15 + (15 * CR)
Complex Commands
Dodge. Attack X creature. Hide. 20 + (20 * CR)
Mounted / Complex Tasks
Scout X area. Return to X location. Find X person. 25 + (25 * CR)

Example: A CR 3 beast needs 80 total progress to reach Complex Commands.

Once a stage is reached, it remains permanent unless broken through RP.

Food and Shelter

Proper care sustains trust.

Food

Creature Size Daily Cost
Tiny 10gp
Small 30gp
Medium 50gp
Large 100gp
Huge 150gp
Gargantuan 200gp

Unique Diets: Costs may be altered at DM Discretion

Shelter: Will be determined by DM

Luxury Care: Double Daily Cost

Care Factors

  • One day without care: Lose 10% Progress
  • Two days without care: Creature may flee and reset to 0%
  • Luxury Care: After 3 days of Luxury Care you gain advantage on the next training roll

Class and Subclasses Modifiers

Class/Sub-class Benefit
Ranger (Any) Advantage on Initial Tame for beasts with CR level beasts with CR ≤ half proficiency bonus
Ranger (Beast Master) Advantage on Initial Tame for equal to or less than half your ranger
Ranger (Drakewarden) Advantage on Initial Tame for draconic creatures or wyrmlings with CR equal to or less than half your level
Druid (Any) +2 to one Animal Handling check per long rest; reduce daily food cost by 25%
Druid (Circle of the Shepherd) Add 1d4 once per day to a training check.
Barbarian (Totem Warrior) Advantage when taming beasts matching your Totem Spirit
* Only one class bonus applies at a time.

Tamable Creatures

  • Beasts & Monstrosities comprised of Beasts (ex: Griffon, Hippogriff)
  • Subject to DM discretion. A number of monsters that may technically fit the criteria may not be tamable for lore reasons, or may otherwise be inaccessible due to where they may be located.
  • Young Griffin (CR 0, ¼, 1)
  • Griffon (CR 2)
  • Owlbear (CR 3)
  • Amphisbaena (CR ½)
  • Peryton (CR 2)
  • Kamadan (CR 4)
  • Death Dog (CR 1)
  • Shadow Mastiff (CR 2)
  • Giant Strider (CR 1)
  • Skyjek Roc (CR 2)
  • Two-Headed Owlbear (CR 3)
  • Hippogriff (CR 1)
  • Giant Ice Toad (CR 3)
  • Two-Headed Cerberus (CR 2)
  • Snowy Owlbear (CR 3)

Limitations

  • It must be reasonable for the creature to be tamed, per DM discretion.
  • It must make sense within the context of TWR lore, per DM discretion.
  • The creatures you can potentially tame are limited by the CR. In order to have the skill necessary to safely handle a creature, you must be capable of hitting the initial tame DC through just a straight animal handling roll without additional modifiers from items, spells, abilities, etc.

Maximum Tamable CR = (5 + Your Base Animal Handling Modifier) / 2

  • Creatures with legendary or mythic abilities can not be tamed.
  • Creatures with an INT of 1 can not be tamed.
  • Creatures with an INT of 4+ can not be tamed.
  • The initial tame, and subsequent checks, must be RPed for and submitted in transcript.
  • For CR 1+ The initial tame must occur in a mini-quest or RPed targeted hunt run by DM. A DM can not run their own quest if they are attempting to tame a creature.
  • For any creatures intended as a mount, the initial tame must occur in a mini-quest or RPed targeted hunt run by DM. A DM can not run their own quest if they are attempting to tame a creature.
  • Purchasable domesticated mounts are an exception, and can be purchased as normal.
  • No more than 1 creature can be tamed per day.
  • Exceptions may exist for things such as domesticated animals, per discretion of the DM.
  • Only creatures at least one size larger than a PC are mountable.
Owl-Bear Taming Example Steps
  • Go on a mini quest hosted by a DM.
  • RP to find and convince the Owl-Bear that you are both not food and non hostile.
  • CR3 creature, so DC 30 animal handling check for an adult Owl-Bear.
  • Upon success, it will be non hostile but still aggressive.
  • Cumulative DC of 300. The daily RPed animal handling checks would be added together.
  • With an average roll of 10, with the +10 modifier required to initially tame the creature, it would take 15 days in real life of daily checks and RP to tame the creature.
  • At 75 points, it would become sociable
  • At 150 points, it would accept simple commands
  • At 225 points, it would accept complex commands and barding
  • At 300 points, it would accept complex tasks and be mountable

To be updated

Use of Tamed Creatures In Combat

The creature acts on its own initiative. You control it as you would a summon RAW from spells such as Conjure Animals.

Mounted Combat for Tamed Creatures

  • Because of the inherent danger of things such as meteor swarms, when you are mounted the creature shares your HP.
  • If you fall to zero HP, your mount falls to 1 HP, you are dismounted if on land, and if it is a flying creature it begins to crashland at 60ft/round.
  • For the purposes of movement, the mount replaces your move speed(s).
  • HP when dismounting: When you dismount, if your HP is lower than the mount's HP, the mount will adopt the same current HP as you.
  • If you choose to have the mount attack, take any action, or otherwise treat it as a separate creature, ignore points 1~4 and it will be treated as a normal mount RAW.
Mounted Combatant Feat interaction

Under this system you can use either RAW and risk damage to the mount or the alternative rules in the Animal Taming doc. If you're using the alternative rules only point 1 of the feat pertaining to advantaged against creatures is applicable, the other two are nullified.

Sale and Transfer of Animals

  • The recipient must be capable of hitting the initial tame DC to be capable of controlling the creature in any way.
  • By default, the bond level resets to zero. If you are proficient in Animal Handling, it resets to 25%. If you have expertise in Animal Handling, it resets to 50%

Tame Death

If your tamed creature dies and is revived it will regress one cumulative level. If your tame is regressed past 0 the taming process with restart requiring a new initial tame roll.

Core / Systems

Paragon Systems

Paragon Systems

Prestige of the Gods

Prestige of the Gods

A character who has reached level 20 and achieved the 6 post-20 milestones may choose to undergo a divine transformation in which the gods revert their mind and body to the state of a neophyte adventurer. Starting again at level 1-3, a ‘prestiged’ adventurer may begin again - choosing any new class, feats, or even remodeling their own personal attributes. They retain all knowledge, wealth, and any items they had prior to this.

Upon choosing to undergo the transformation, the adventurer may choose a cosmetic effect to be bestowed upon them. This effect must be proposed by the player, and approved by a DM in the request to prestige the character (in #transcript). Examples of such an effect could include: Flittering sparkles that follow the character, an ethereal halo above their head, or a glowing/changing tattoo.

Paragon Systems: Gestalt and Ascendant

Gestalts are now considered a Paragon system, with the addition of Ascendants, which operate in a similar way - granting class levels past 20 - without having to reset.

A character’s Paragon stage represents the number of times they have completed a full class level system (finished p20), starting at a value of 1. This number is used to determine experience gain, and for communicating your character’s progress, as seen in “How are Levels Counted”. Such systems and changes can and will be subject to change and active monitoring.

How Levels are Counted

Levels are counted through the following format A#L#, where A represents your paragon stage, and L represents your remaining levels. For example, a P26 wizard with 10 additional levels from this system would be an A1L10. This can be similarly done with tiers.

This is similarly done with gestalt, in which the format is G#L#, where G represents your Paragon stage, and L represents your current level, up to 26. This can be similarly done with tiers.

Ascendant Paragon

Characters can now progress past level 20, continuing to gain character levels, being known as Ascendants rather than Gestalts. The character’s XP counter would reset to zero, though they would keep their character levels, proficiency bonus, and P20 rewards. Such Ascendants would proceed to level another class, starting from T1, and gaining an appropriate amount of XP, with the ability to do so again upon completing P20.

Build Rules

  • To qualify a PC must be fully leveled, meaning level 20 with all post 20 levels completed.

  • Ascendant PCs cannot gain experience from hunts, trials, DM-XP, Transcript-XP, etc. They can only gain experience from RP-XP or Quests.

  • In quests that involve combat, while you will receive XP for the RP, you will receive no XP for the creatures killed.

  • Ascendant hit dice are restricted to the two highest hit dice per level (as opposed to getting all hit dice per level).

  • Rather than gaining the save proficiencies of all classes, Ascendants choose one strong save and one weak save from the options given to them by their classes:

    • Strong Saves: Dex, Con, Wis
    • Weak Saves: Str, Int, Cha

  • Any changes to the locked classes or subclasses are allowed and follow the normal retraining rules.

  • Due to the documentation required for this system, character sheets must be handled in G-Sheets.

  • ASIs stack, but do not stack past the normal cap of 20 unless otherwise specified. Stats may not exceed 30 for any reason.

  • You can not take the same feat multiple times unless otherwise specified. Feats that scale based on level are calculated based on your class levels.

  • Ascendant PC's, May only hunt, trial or delve with PC's who are also Ascendant

  • Spell save DCs and spellcasting follow multi classing rules. Spell Save DCs and Spell Attack Bonuses calculate based on the class providing the spell.

  • Class features that references class levels are self contained for the applicable class and paragon cycle

Stacking

Class Features, Spell Slots, Proficiencies and Stat Changes generally stack unless otherwise specified.

Exceptions

The following features do NOT stack when creating a Ascendant PC:

  • Proficiency Bonus
  • Extra Attack
  • Unarmored Defense
  • Duplicated Paladin Auras
  • Movement speed increases from duplicate sources.
  • Bladesong, and other features with limited uses such as rage, do not get doubled buffs but do get a increased number of uses.

Prestige Classes

The Ascendant Paragon system also includes Prestige Classes, classes that have specific requirements for their use and play, but are generally stronger than the normal classes. Further information can be found at the Prestige Classes page.

Gestalt Paragon

This is a variant to the typical prestige system, and while it may grant great boons it also has great restrictions as well. When you Gestalt Paragon, you must post in #transcript including both the new and original sheets for reference.

Gestalt Overview

  • Upon gestalt prestige you can select a class to level alongside your current one.
  • The starting proficiencies, skills, and other benefits are granted to the character.
  • When you level up, both classes level simultaneously, and you gain the benefits from both.
  • Put simply, you have build A which was gestalted, getting added to build B. This is similar to if you had two separate characters who were merged into one.
  • ASIs granted through level ups can be reassigned.
  • This process can be repeated, allowing for a singular character to slowly grow in power over the years as they grow more involved in the world at large.

Cumulative Level

  • Cumulative Level is the total number of levels from all your classes combined.
  • Cumulative Level is used to calculate what trials, hunts, and quests you can be involved in.

Current Level

  • Current Level is the current base level of the character and calculated as it would be normally, as though you were leveling a normal character.
  • The Current Level is what is used to calculate proficiency bonus, character progression, and RP experience gains. Things that scale based on level use your Current Level.

Gestalt Reversion

  • At any time a character can revert a gestalt prestige. This will reset the character to a level 1 class of their choice akin to a normal prestige, provide zero cosmetic and stat benefits, and allow the character to once again gain experience from trials, hunts, etc.
  • The character will then be locked out of the gestalt prestige system for 6 months.
  • This can be done at any time and at any level.

Build Rules

  • All Gestalt PCs begin at level 1

  • Class levels do not mix between Gestalt Prestiges. Each prestige is treated as a unique PC build.

  • To qualify a PC must be fully leveled, meaning level 20 with all post 20 levels completed.

  • Gestalt PCs cannot gain experience from hunts, trials, DM-XP, Transcript-XP, etc. They can only gain experience from RP-XP or Quests.

  • In quests that involve combat, while you will receive XP for the RP, you will receive no XP for the creatures killed.

  • Gestalt PCs may not change their race, background, Racial ASIs, class or subclass choice, or anything else regarding the basis of the character which was set during their initial creation.

  • On level up, the initial class chosen will follow the same build path (for example Fighter Champion) and multi class level split (if applicable) that the character had PRIOR to that prestige.

  • Gestalt hit dice are restricted to the two highest hit dice per level (as opposed to gestalts getting all hit dice per level).

  • Rather than gaining the save proficiencies of all classes, Gestalts choose one strong save and one weak save from the options given to them by their classes:

    • Strong Saves: Dex, Con, Wis
    • Weak Saves: Str, Int, Cha

  • Gestalt PC's may choose to redistribute their ASI's and redo their first class in any way that is within the rules.

  • Due to the documentation required for this system, character sheets must be handled in G-Sheets.

  • ASIs stack, but do not stack past the normal cap of 20 unless otherwise specified. Stats may not exceed 30 for any reason.

  • You can not take the same feat multiple times unless otherwise specified. Feats that scale based on level are calculated based on your Current Level not your Total Level.

  • Gestalt PCs may attune to any item they own, however, Gestalt PCs may not use items which exceed their “Current Level” during hunts or trials with non-Gestalt PCs.

  • Gestalt PCs may choose to join hunts above their Current Level, but not if non-Gestalt PCs are present. This does not affect Body Retrieval Hunts. If a gestalt hunting party is a mix of tiers, they can not recover a body.

  • Spell save DCs and spellcasting follow multi classing rules. Spell Save DCs and Spell Attack Bonuses calculate based on the class providing the spell.

Stacking

Class Features, Spell Slots, Proficiencies and Stat Changes generally stack unless otherwise specified.

Exceptions

The following features do NOT stack when creating a Gestalt PC:

  • Proficiency Bonus
  • Extra Attack
  • Unarmored Defense
  • Duplicated Paladin Auras
  • Movement speed increases from duplicate sources.
  • Bladesong, and other features with limited uses such as rage, do not get doubled buffs but do get a increased number of uses.

Paragon Wish Patch:

tl;dr - Introducing a very arduous method to regain wish through a whole gestalt prestige and questline using a Post20 Blessing/Boon Slot.

Requirements

  1. Paragon into a spellcasting class that also learns wish
  2. Complete self RP and DM-led quests (at least 4) throughout your prestige that meet the following guidelines
    1. Integrate with an existing group of worshipers for a particular deity
    2. Receive character references from leadership within the church/group
    3. Reach a level that would otherwise grant you wish from your prestige class
    4. Travel to the chosen deity’s home plane and petition their aid directly with offerings and references prepared
    5. Donate at least 2 items to the god directly, sacrificing them to prove your devotion. One item must be of legendary power and the second must be of great personal importance to your PC.
    6. Perform a quest for that god directly, run by a Dungeon master and approved by at least 2 more DMs or LMs

Regaining Wish

Once all of the requirements have been met and your PC is eligible for a Post20 Boon/Blessing Slot, the God will decide whether or not to grant you the Blessing of Forgiveness:

Blessing of Forgiveness - This blessing removes one existing instance of permanent loss of wish. Once a creature has received this blessing, they can no longer receive it from the same deity.

Note: It may not be possible to convince any other gods to grant this blessing or you may attract significant attention from your previous god if so. It would require unfathomable time and effort to regain wish a second time.

Gestalt and Ascension Interaction:

Gestalt or Ascension can be chosen when a character finishes p20 or completes a paragon cycle (finishes p20 on another class system). In doing so, a character may choose to Gestalt as a way to prestige and change through their class choices, though would still level according to their paragon cycle number.

For example, a P3L0 (has finished this cycle but has not started a new one) may choose to Gestalt, and become a G4L1, where they may again choose to move back into ascension after leveling to p20.

Core / Systems

Prestige Systems

Prestige Systems

Prestige of the Gods

Prestige of the Gods

A character who has reached level 20 and achieved the 6 post-20 milestones may choose to undergo a divine transformation in which the gods revert their mind and body to the state of a neophyte adventurer. Starting again at level 1-3, a ‘prestiged’ adventurer may begin again - choosing any new class, feats, or even remodeling their own personal attributes. They retain all knowledge, wealth, and any items they had prior to this.

Upon choosing to undergo the transformation, the adventurer may choose a cosmetic effect to be bestowed upon them. This effect must be proposed by the player, and approved by a DM in the request to prestige the character (in #transcript). Examples of such an effect could include: Flittering sparkles that follow the character, an ethereal halo above their head, or a glowing/changing tattoo.

Paragon Systems: Gestalt and Ascendant

Gestalts are now considered a Paragon system, with the addition of Ascendants, which operate in a similar way - granting class levels past 20 - without having to reset.

A character’s Paragon stage represents the number of times they have completed a full class level system (finished p20), starting at a value of 1. This number is used to determine experience gain, and for communicating your character’s progress, as seen in “How are Levels Counted”. Such systems and changes can and will be subject to change and active monitoring.

Ascendant

Characters can now progress past level 20, continuing to gain character levels, being known as Ascendants rather than Gestalts. The character’s XP counter would reset to zero, though they would keep their character levels, proficiency bonus, and P20 rewards. Such Ascendants would proceed to level another class, starting from T1, and gaining an appropriate amount of XP, with the ability to do so again upon completing P20.

How can you Swap

For Gestalts currently in place, they may choose to revert to P20 and take 20 levels in each class system they have already finished leveling. They would take levels equal to their level before the shift in the class levels they had taken. For example, an A2 Level 13 whose base classes are 20 Fighter and 20 Wizard, and is currently leveling Artificer, would revert to 20 Fighter, 20 Wizard, and 13 Artificer, along with P20 rewards.

How Levels are Counted

Levels are counted through the following format A#L#, where A represents your paragon stage, and L represents your remaining levels. For example, a P26 wizard with 10 additional levels from this system would be an A1L10. This can be similarly done with tiers.

This is similarly done with gestalt, in which the format is G#L#, where G represents your Paragon stage, and L represents your current level, up to 26. This can be similarly done with tiers.

After Ascension:

When a pre-existing character begins their first ascension cycle (starting to level a new class system) or converts from gestalt, they can choose to adjust their base ability scores through point buy and may choose to swap current feats, asi, and p20 asi at no penalty. This must be submitted through transcript

Gestalt and Ascension Interaction:

Gestalt or Ascension can be chosen when a character finishes p20 or completes a paragon cycle (finishes p20 on another class system). In doing so, a character may choose to Gestalt as a way to prestige and change through their class choices, though would still level according to their paragon cycle number.

For example, a P3L0 (has finished this cycle but has not started a new one) may choose to Gestalt, and become a G4L1, where they may again choose to move back into ascension after leveling to p20.

Changes to Gestalt System:

Gestalt would remain with the ability to adjust stats upon reset, as stated previously. In addition, they would no longer be required to level their base class as they would normally, and may choose to level a different class instead.

Retroactive Adjustments:

For those who choose to stay in gestalt, characters may receive retroactive rewards. Firstly, a character may adjust base stats and character levels, submitting a new sheet to transcript along with the old (make a copy and do changes from there) to be used as a reference. Additionally, players may reclaim downtime for changing class levels for characters or training characters, since the gestalt system was first introduced. Players must submit the time they would receive to transcript, with relevant links, where they would then be able to use that time in the future. Players may complete this same process for the gold cost.

Note:

All character changes must be done through the transcript. It is recommended that you make a copy of your old gsheet when adjusting things.

PART 6 | GESTALT PRESTIGE

Gestalt Prestige System

This is a variant to the typical prestige system, and while it may grant great boons it also has great restrictions as well. When you Gestalt Prestige, you must post in #transcript including both the new and original sheets for reference. Once approved, the new sheet will be posted in #3-gestalt-pc-links

Please note this system is still in playtesting and is subject to change at any time

Gestalt Overview

All Gestalt PCs begin at level 1

Upon gestalt prestige you can select a class to level alongside your current one.

The starting proficiencies, skills, and other benefits are granted to the character. See Here for a detailed explanation of how class features stack.

When you level up, both classes level simultaneously, and you gain the benefits from both.

Put simply, you have build A which was prestiged and locked in, getting added to build B. This is similar to if you had two separate characters who were merged into one.

ASIs granted through level ups can be reassigned.

Original class and subclass levels are locked in.

This process can be repeated, allowing for a singular character to slowly grow in power over the years as they grow more involved in the world at large.

Cumulative Level

Cumulative Level is the total number of levels from all your classes combined.

Cumulative Level is used to calculate what trials, hunts, and quests you can be involved in.

Current Level

Current Level is the current base level of the character and calculated as it would be normally, as though you were leveling a normal character.

The Current Level is what is used to calculate proficiency bonus, character progression, and RP experience gains. Things that scale based on level use your Current Level.

Gestalt Reversion

At any time a character can revert a gestalt prestige. This will reset the character to a level 1 class of their choice akin to a normal prestige, provide zero cosmetic and stat benefits, and allow the character to once again gain experience from trials, hunts, etc.

The character will then be locked out of the gestalt prestige system for 6 months.

This can be done at any time and at any level.

Restrictions

Class levels do not mix between Gestalt Prestiges. Each prestige is treated as a unique PC build.

To qualify a PC must be fully leveled, meaning level 20 with all post 20 levels completed.

Gestalt PCs cannot gain experience from hunts, trials, DM-XP, Transcript-XP, etc. They can only gain experience from RP-XP or Quests.

In quests that involve combat, while you will receive XP for the RP, you will receive no XP for the creatures killed.

Gestalt PCs may not change their race, background, Racial ASIs, class or subclass choice, or anything else regarding the basis of the character which was set during their initial creation.

On level up, the initial class chosen will follow the same build path (for example Fighter Champion) and multi class level split (if applicable) that the character had PRIOR to that prestige.

Gestalt hit dice are restricted to the two highest hit dice per level (as opposed to gestalts getting all hit dice per level).

Rather than gaining the save proficiencies of all classes, Gestalts choose one strong save and one weak save from the options given to them by their classes:

Strong Saves Weak Saves

DEX STR

CON INT

WIS CHA

Any changes to the locked classes or subclasses are allowed and follow the normal retraining rules based on the level of the class being retrained.

Due to the documentation required for this system, character sheets must be handled in G-Sheets.

ASIs stack, but do not stack past the normal cap of 20 unless otherwise specified. Stats may not exceed 30 for any reason.

You can not take the same feat multiple times unless otherwise specified. Feats that scale based on level are calculated based on your Current Level not your Total Level.

Gestalt PCs may attune to any item they own, however, Gestalt PCs may not use items which exceed their “Current Level” during hunts or trials with non-Gestalt PCs.

Gestalt PCs may choose to join hunts above their Current Level, but not if non-Gestalt PCs are present. This does not affect Body Retrieval Hunts. If a gestalt hunting party is a mix of tiers, they can not recover a body.

Spell save DCs and spellcasting follow multi classing rules. Spell Save DCs and Spell Attack Bonuses calculate based on the class providing the spell.

Combining Gestalt Classes

Class Features, Spell Slots, Proficiencies and Stat Changes generally stack unless otherwise specified.

Exceptions

The following features do NOT stack when creating a Gestalt PC:

Proficiency Bonus

Multi Attack

Unarmored Defense

Duplicated Paladin Auras

Movement speed increases from duplicate sources.

Bladesong, and other features with limited uses such as rage, do not get doubled buffs but do get a increased number of uses.

Gestalt FighterWatermark

Gestalt/Wish Patch:

tl;dr - Introducing a very arduous method to regain wish through a whole gestalt prestige and questline using a Post20 Blessing/Boon Slot.

Requirements

Gestalt prestige into a spellcasting class that also learns wish

Complete self RP and DM-led quests (at least 4) throughout your prestige that meet the following guidelines

Integrate with an existing group of worshipers for a particular deity

Receive character references from leadership within the church/group

Reach a level that would otherwise grant you wish from your prestige class

Travel to the chosen deity’s home plane and petition their aid directly with offerings and references prepared

Donate at least 2 items to the god directly, sacrificing them to prove your devotion. One item must be of legendary power and the second must be of great personal importance to your PC.

Perform a quest for that god directly, run by a Dungeonmaster and approved by at least 2 more DMs or LMs

Regaining Wish

Once all of the requirements have been met and your PC is eligible for a Post20 Boon/Blessing Slot, the God will decide whether or not to grant you the Blessing of Forgiveness:

Blessing of Forgiveness - This blessing removes one existing instance of permanent loss of wish. Once a creature has received this blessing, they can no longer receive it from the same deity.

Note: It may not be possible to convince any other gods to grant this blessing or you may attract significant attention from your previous god if so. It would require unfathomable time and effort to regain wish a second time.

Regarding Simulacrums

  1. Sims Simulacrums are considered NPCs. Paragons will not be able to earn rpxp and quest xp by way of proxy

Core

The Cursed Role

The Cursed Role

The @Cursed Role

  1. If a player leaves during a quest, trial, or other event without the permission of the DM or person running it, they will be cursed, and put into the @Cursed role for two weeks.
  2. During this time, all characters belonging to the player receive only half XP and gold rewards, and cannot be resurrected if killed (except via Revivify spell).
  3. The @cursed role may also be given for other offenses at the discretion of the DM, Moderator, and Admin teams.
Core

Training Downtime

Training Downtime

Training Downtime

Characters can perform activities to train and practice in their free time, those who do not wish to hunt can spend time training themselves as well, this could be tinkering and experimenting for Artificers, praying and studying for Clerics, scribing and practicing spells for Wizards, sparring for fighters, and stealthing around for rogues, all forms of training are applicable and make no mechanical difference

Characters can choose to spend 5 Hunting Tags or expend 8 hours of downtime in training which awards experience points to reflect the development of skills. Players who choose to roleplay the lessons will be awarded with additional RPXP as per usual

Tier | XP Per Day (not RPXP) 1 | 100 xp 2 | 250 xp 3 | 500 xp 4 | 1,000 xp Post-20 | 2,000 xp

TWR DM

TWR DM's Guide

TWR DM's Guide

What is this Guide?

This page is a guide to getting started running Quests on TWR, a discord-based Westmarches campaign. Quests can be run by any player, with certain exceptions where the player may need to seek approval from staff for lore/balance reasons. As noted in our Code of Conduct, while running a quest or other content, the player acts as the DM and is considered such during play.

Preparing to DM

Being a DM on TWR is easy and fun. Most of the adventures can be prepared in a short period of time, and you don’t have to create an entire setting and form a campaign or spend a ton of time plotting out a large overarching plot. Most Quests on TWR are run as “one-shots,” though more advanced DMs may choose to run quests in a series to tell a more intricate story.

What you Need to Run a Game

In order to run a game as a DM on TWR, you’ll need the following:

Players

The #quest-board channel is the perfect place to seek out players, if you do not have a full group in mind already. For traditional adventures a group of 4-6 players is recommended, but there is no specific number of players required to participate in a quest. Just be sure to balance any potential combat or roleplay encounters around the number of participants to ensure everyone gets to play.

A Plot

Balance the three pillars of gameplay (Roleplay, Adventuring, Combat) to your liking and create a plot for your quest. It is best to keep plots simple at first until you’ve got some practice running Quests. Consider what type of story you want to tell, what type of rewards might fit with the quest, Prepare any puzzles, difficult choices, or monster statblocks for combat ahead of time so that you can spend gameplay time interacting with the players and building the story. Remember, CR values translate to what an average difficulty is for a group of 4 well balanced adventurers. Though combat should be challenging, it should still be possible to win (unless your story dictates that the party loses!).

A Format

Some DMs prefer to run quests in a dedicated session for a more traditional experience, planning a start and end time. Others prefer a play-by-post (PBP) format, which can span multiple days or weeks and provide a more relaxed pace. Each option has benefits and detriments, so it's important to specify which one in your #quest-board post to attract the right players.

Other Tools

Avrae

For combat, spellcasting, and other mechanical functions it is highly recommended that you use Avrae which will automate the majority of tracking and run combat. You can also upload maps to use for tactical placement during combat.

Tupperbot

You will want to set up at least a "Narrator Tupper" to describe scenes, effects and other miscellaneous actions during play. You may also consider creating specific Tuppers for your NPCs to improve immersion and create a more aesthetically pleasing experience.

Group Composition

There’s no general rule that requires members of a group be of the same level. In quests that revolve around combat, we recommend restricting them by Tier as defined in the Player’s Handbook and Rules Compendium. For quests that are more roleplay-centric, this is less necessary, but bear in mind that some high level PCs may have spells and abilities that far outshine the rest of the group.

Facilitator of Fun

You have the most important role. You guide the narrative and provide the players with an immersive and enjoyable quest. While guiding the players, it is also your responsibility to make everyone feel welcomed, creating a fun and fair environment. Here are some things to keep in mind:

You are Empowered

Make decisions about how the group interacts with the quest; adjust or improvise your plan as needed. You have the ability to create NPCs, locations, challenges and scenarios with broad authority within your quest. Interacting with official D&D NPCs, Factions, Deities and other key lore entities may require approval from Staff; we encourage DMs who are concerned that their content may not accurately reflect the setting reach out to an official Dungeonmaster or Loremaster for guidance. See the "When to Seek Staff Approval" section below for a better understanding of when to reach out. Be aware that, in the instance of particularly challenging deviations from the setting Staff may have to retcon the contents of your quests to maintain fairness and server continuity.

Challenge your Players

Gauge the experience level of your players, as well as what they enjoy in a game and attempt to deliver what they’re after; everyone should be able to shine. You can adjust an encounter’s difficulty by adding or removing thematically appropriate monsters but can’t create new monsters or modify them in such a way that modifies their challenge rating (aside from changing their hit points within the range afforded by their hit dice). Be careful of going too far, however. The intent is to have a collaborative and challenging story-telling experience; it’s not to do everything you can to kill your players’ characters. Similarly, destroying equipment generally shouldn’t happen unless an encounter specifically directs you to. In fact, unless they have conditions detailing their destruction (such as an ioun stone), permanent magic items can’t be destroyed.

Dealing with Disruptive Players

If a player is acting in a disruptive manner during a play session, attempt to address the issue as soon as it becomes clear that someone (including you) might be uncomfortable. Take the player aside and explain why the behavior might be causing others to feel uncomfortable. If the problem persists, contact a Moderator or Admin for help with resolution.

Disruptive Magic Items, Spells or Class Features

There are several magic items, spells, class features and homebrew submissions within the rules of TWR that might become disruptive to the overall enjoyment of others at the table. If use of any personal equipment, features etc. through play leads to an uncomfortable play experience, take the player aside and explain the issue. You may wish to discuss temporarily removing the item or ability from the character and providing them an alternative replacement instead. You may choose to review a character’s sheet prior to play to help identify any potential issues, You should not mandate removal of magic items or gear solely on your preferences, but rather on their impact to the story and enjoyment of the players/DM as a group.

Safety Tools

Safety tools help ensure players aren’t pushed beyond their comfort levels. These tools let your players know you want them to have a positive experience. Some common safety tools are provided below, each with a summary of how they work. An article about one such safety kit is provided to help with further information. Ensure that you discuss these tools with your players before the game:

  • Code of Conduct: TWR has a code of conduct that outlines rules for play across the server. It defines desired and prohibited behaviors and possible consequences. Familiarize yourself with the Code of Conduct before running a quest to help understand what is acceptable and what is not.
  • Pregame, Postgame, and Out of Character Discussions: Use time before the game to explain content warnings and set boundaries. This helps you understand the players' various goals and comfort levels. Be sure to discuss the possibility of lethal combat, if applicable, as many players prefer to avoid risking the safety of their long-running PCs. During play, most DMs prefer to have an Out of Character (OOC) thread for combat and ongoing discussion of the story. After the quest, decompress and discuss what worked and what didn't with the players.
  • Be Welcoming: Welcome and encourage respectful and open conversations about issues as they arise. Show that you’re listening by avoiding defensive responses.
  • Direct Communication: Allow direct messaging between the players and yourself as the DM. Generally, do not share information sent to you in private with the rest of the group without permission.

Keep the Game Moving

If the game gets bogged down, provide hints and clues to your players facing puzzles or engaging in combat and roleplay interactions that get frustrating. This gives players “little victories” for making good choices based on clues. Don't be afraid to skip someone's turn or allow them the ability to act retroactively in the future if one player is unavailable and disrupting the flow of play.

Running the Game

As the DM, you are charged with not only guiding the story, but also fairly adjudicating the game’s rules and rewarding your players’ characters for their accomplishments.

The Rules of the Game

TWR generally uses Dungeons & Dragons 5th Edition (2014) with some added Homebrew Rules. You can issue rulings to your table when the rules of the game are ambiguous or vague, but you must otherwise adhere to the rules as they are provided in the core rulebooks and can’t change them or make up your own. You must always use the most current incarnation of a rule. Oftentimes, if a rule is in dispute, you can go to the #questions channel or ping a Dungeonmaster for assistance; generally, we follow Sage Advice for clarification from the game developers and, in some cases, Homebrew or #town-hall posts will include rules clarifications. Don't be afraid to ask for help, or issue a temporary ruling while you wait to maintain the flow of play. Otherwise, the rules as written in the rulebooks always take precedence.

Quest Locks

Depending on the content of your quest, you have the ability to "Quest Lock" PCs who are participating. Locked PCs cannot gain experience from or participate in Hunts, Trials, or any form of activity outside of your quest. They are also unable to benefit from downtime while engaged in your quest. Whether or not to lock a PC is up to you, as is whether or not their possible progression applies within your quest. Keep in mind travel, in-character duration, and mechanical balance when deciding whether or not to lock the PCs, and be sure to communicate a quest lock during your original post or pregrame discussion.

Death, Disease and Curses

Adventuring is a risky job, and bad things often happen to adventurers. Diseases, poisons, and other similar effects persist until they’re removed, and death within a quest applies to a PC outside of the quest as well. However, thanks to the proliferation of healing and revival services from players in our setting, they are often simple to overcome. If you wish to enact permanent effects, be sure to communicate that possibility to the players during your original post or pregame discussion.

Character Rewards

You award the players rewards for their accomplishments in the form of experience, gold, and magic items for their characters, which must be detailed in your #story-log post recording the quest.

Experience

Players should receive experience for participating in combat and for engaging in good roleplay. DMs should follow the usual guidelines for granting Experience, and are encouraged to request approval for more than the general amount in quests which are long-running or highly impactful.

Magic Items

Player generally expect to receive a Magic Item as a reward for their participation in your quest. It is often most exciting to include these items as possible rewards within the quest which they can then use or keep, but sometimes it is most appropriate to provide the items as a form of payment at the end. Regardless of the source, the below table outlines what rarity of items can be rewarded per PC without Staff Approval, provided that the items are available on the loot list:

Tier Rarity
Tier 1 Uncommon
Tier 2 Rare
Tier 3 Very Rare
T4 and Above Legendary
Misc. Treasure

You may wish to award the players with gold or valuable treasures which they may keep or sell as an additional reward from the questgiver or discovery during play. The below table outlines what the maximum amount of additional treasure which can be rewarded per PC without Staff Approval. If no Magic Items are awarded, you may increase this amount by the item's trade value:

Tier Amount Item Trade Value
Tier 1 200 gp 400 gp
Tier 2 2,000 gp 4,000 gp
Tier 3 20,000gp 40,000gp
Tier 4+ 100,000 gp 200,000 gp

Cosmetic Rewards

DMs may provide cosmetic rewards such as eye color changes, floating halos, or other thematically appropriate character options as they see fit, provided that they do not allow for any mechanical benefits.

When to seek Staff Approval

As mentioned throughout the above document, there are a number of times when it is appropriate to seek approval from Staff to assist with running your quest or to ensure that your quest is in-line with the general lore and balance expectations of our server. The following list outlines the most common reasons you may need to request Staff oversight:

  • Running named NPCs, Deities or important factions from the Forgotten Realms setting
  • Providing players with information relevant to ongoing Questlines or content provided by members of staff
  • Running content inside of an area of the Forgotten Realms which a staff member is currently focused on
  • Attempting to exceed the XP, Item or Gold reward limits for long-running quests or exemplary gameplay
  • Rewarding magic items which do not appear on the existing loot lists
  • Rewarding high-level awards such as Super Legendary items, Artifacts or Boons
  • Rewarding items which provide a permanent stat boost
  • Providing other custom rewards such as automatons, legendary crafting materials, custom items, or anything that may impact future gameplay on TWR
  • Including homebrewed monsters or equipment within your quest (if included, such additions cannot leave your quest without majority Dungeonmaster approval)

DM Rewards

Running a quest takes time and effort that we feel should be rewarded. Rewards for running a quest come in two main ways:

Omni-XP

Omni-XP is awarded to the DM based on the average amount of XP delivered to their players. Omni-XP is restricted by tier and only applies to non-Paragon PCs.

Paragon Tokens

Paragon Tokens can be taken in lieu of Omni-XP and can be applied to future roleplay to increase the amount of RP-XP rewarded to one of your Paragon PCs.

Please note that you MAY choose instead to have one of your PCs participate in the request and receive the same rewards as the players, instead of choosing one of the above rewards. If you do so, Staff must approve the rewards whether they fall within the otherwise stated limits or not.

Blessing of the Masked Lord (Soulbind)

Blessing of the Masked Lord (Soulbind)

Prerequisite: Blessing of the Masked Lord (Soultheft)

The practice of Soultheft has become second nature to you, allowing you to better subjugate the souls you capture and extract even greater potential.

When you use Soultheft, and you can exploit a soul up to 12 times before the soul is released instead of 6. In addition you gain two new ways in which you may exploit souls:

  • Ethereal Stride (2 uses). As a Bonus Action you can teleport to the Ethereal Plane from the Material Plane for up to 1 minute or until you end the effect (no action required). You can expend another use of this exploit to extend the duration by up to 1 minute per use expended. At the end of the duration, you reappear in the same location on the Material Plane, or the nearest unoccupied space if that space is occupied.,

  • Soul Mask (3 uses). You can use an action to call the Soul to you and disguise your appearance. When you do so, your appearance magically transforms into the souls as it was in life, healthy and alive. Another creature can see through this disguise by succeeding on a Wisdom (Insight) check contested by your Charisma (Deception) check. You gain a +5 bonus to your check. This disguise lasts for 1 hour or until you end it as a bonus action. You can expend another use of this exploit to extend the duration by up to 1 hour per use expended.

Homebrew / Boons

Blessing of the Masked Lord (Soultheft)

Blessing of the Masked Lord (Soultheft)

Guided by the Masked Lord himself, the caster can snare a departing soul to fuel their spells, a practice called Soultheft.

  • Once per day as an action, the caster can touch their holy symbol to a creature that’s been dead no longer than 1 minute, and capture their departing soul into the holy symbol, placing them under the effects of the ‘Soul Cage’ spell until the soul is released, or this blessing is used again.
  • In addition to the spell's normal effects, the caster can also dispel the effects to cast a spell they know or have prepared without expending a spell slot, of a level equal to proficiency bonus of the captured creature. When casting a spell in this way, the creatures soul is damaged, and cannot be revived by any means short of a wish or divine intervention.

Souls obtained via the Soultheft blessing MUST be canon. Hunts, Trials, Delves or Raids do not count, the usage must explicitly be approved by staff

Blessing of the Metallic Dragon

Blessing of the Metallic Dragon

This blessing is bestowed by a powerful metallic dragon upon a creature it recognizes as a dragon friend—one who has proven loyalty, courage, or respect worthy of draconic favor.

Draconic Recognition

Other metallic dragons instinctively recognize the bearer of this blessing as friendly, unless the bearer acts with obvious hostility. This recognition does not compel obedience or trust, but it greatly improves initial attitudes.

Draconic Transformation

You learn the Draconic Transformation spell. Once per long rest, you can cast a special version of the Draconic Transformation spell without expending a spell slot or material components. Charisma is your spellcasting ability for this spell. While concentrating on the Special Draconic Transformation spell cast in this way, you gain the following additional benefits:

  • Scaled Majesty. You gain 60 Temporary Hit Point as scales harden around your skin.
  • Draconic Potency. Whenever you roll damage dice of the same type as the dragon that granted this blessing (such as fire for a gold dragon or lightning for a bronze dragon), any roll of 1 or 2 on a damage die is treated as a 3.
  • Altered Breath: You can change the damage type of the Draconic Transformation spell's breath to the type associate to the dragon that granted the blessing.

Draconic Gift

This blessing can only be granted directly by a dragon. It cannot be replicated, transferred, or bestowed through training, magic items, divine intervention, or the wish spell. OOC clarification, you cannot learn this blessing via wish or the free boon or blessing, it must be quested for.

Blessing of the Moon Weaver

Blessing of the Moon Weaver

The blessings of a deity aligned to the moon protect and empower you. You gain resistance to radiant damage, and are empowered in the following ways at night:

Lunar Magic

Your learn the Moonbeam (DC19) and the Healing Spirit spells, and they are always prepared for you. You can cast each of these once per Short Rest without expending a spell slot, empowering it. While empowered, these spells are centered on and follow you, and their radius is increased to 15ft instead of 5 ft. You are immune to the damage caused by your own Moonbeam cast in this way.

Moon Fever

As a reaction immediately after you take damage or fail a saving throw against a creature you can see within 60 feet of yourself, you can force the creature to make a Wisdom saving throw (DC19). On a failed save, the creature feels an intense urge to move towards or away from you (your choice). It must move as close or as far (depending on your choice) as its movement allows on its turn, taking the safest and most direct path available. You can use this feature a number of times equal half to your proficiency bonus. You regain all expended uses when you finish a short or long rest.

This aura remains active until you dismiss it as a free action or until you become incapacitated, at which point you must reactivate it to regain its effects. While this boon is active, any creature that touches you or hits you with a melee attack takes 10 (3d6) cold damage. Additionally, any creature or object that is grappling, restraining, carrying, or otherwise holding you takes the same cold damage at the start of each of your turns.

Boon of Implacable Terror

You can bypass the frightened condition immunity of creatures

Homebrew / Boons

Boon of Legend Slaying

Boon of Legend Slaying

Once per turn, if a legendary monster would use a legendary resistance to succeed on a saving throw, you can use your reaction to have them use a second legendary resistance to succeed on that save. If they cannot, they fail the save.

Homebrew / Boons

Boon of Life

Boon of Life's Embrace

You have a certain level of mastery over positive energies.  You have resistance to necrotic damage, and your maximum hp cannot be reduced.  Additionally, when you cast a spell or use an ability that restores hit points to other creatures, you may apply one of the following additional effects to targets other than yourself:

  • One of the targets gains double the hit points.
  • All of the targets benefit from a Lesser Restoration
  • The targets regain lost maximum hp equal to twice the healing done.

Adding on an effect can be done an amount of times equal to your proficiency bonus, resetting upon finishing a long rest.

Boon of Limited Magic Immunity

Boon of Limited Magic Immunity

Prerequisite: Boon of Magic Resistance

You may not be affected or detected by spells of 3rd level and lower unless you choose to be. (Disclaimer that upcasting spells past third level bypasses this immunity)

Homebrew / Boons

Boon of Many Forms

Boon of Many Forms

Prerequisite: Boon of the Shapechanger

Your mastery over transformation deepens. The CR increase granted by your Boon of the Shapechanger is now equal to your full post-20 level, rather than half your post-20 level.

For example, an effect normally limited to CR 20 can access CR 22 at level 20p2, CR 24 at level 20p4, and CR 26 at level 20p6.

This increase only modifies the original CR limit of wild shape, shapechange, or polymorph. It cannot be applied repeatedly through chained transformations. Transforming into a CR 26 creature does not allow that creature's level or CR to establish a new transformation limit. This does not function for things such as chain polymorphing.

Homebrew / Boons

Boon of Poison Mastery

Boon of Poison Mastery

Prerequisites: Poisoner Feat

You can treat immunity to poison damage as resistance. This resistance cannot be overcome by the poisoner feat.

  • When you cast a spell of 5th level or lower that deals poison damage, you can choose to treat all damage dice rolled as their maximum amount.
  • When you hit with a weapon attack that deals poison damage, you can choose to treat all damage dice rolled as their maximum amount.

Once you use one of these features, you cannot use either again until you finish a long rest.

Homebrew / Boons

Boon of Reactivness

Boon of Reactivness

You gain one additional reaction per round. This additional reaction is subject to the following restrictions:

Diminishing Returns: You cannot use this reaction to take a Reaction Option that you have already taken this round (such as Cast a Spell, Opportunity Attack, or a specific class feature), nor can you take it in response to a trigger you have already reacted to.

Defense Limit: You cannot apply a bonus to your Armor Class if you have already done so since the start of your last turn.

Boon of Resilience (Update)

Boon of Resilience (Update)

You have resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from weapon attacks.

Boon of Resilience (Update)

Boon of Resilience (Update)

You have resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from weapon attacks.

Homebrew / Boons

Boon of the Cloud Scion

Boon of the Cloud Scion

Prerequisite: Boon of the Storm Born

Calamity of the Storm: First there was lightning…then there was thunder! Once per turn, you may add 10 extra lightning damage to an attack . After you've dealt this damage three times you become supercharged allowing the recipient as a bonus action to emit a wave of thunder dealing 2d8 thunder damage in a 15 ft cube originating from the recipient. When you would take lightning damage you may instead add half of that damage to your next thunder wave.

Cloud Jumper: The recipient of this boon gains a flight speed equal to half their movement speed

Where the wind takes you:  As an action the recipient of this boon to assume the form of a cloud. While in this cloud form, a creature has a flying speed of 150 feet and has resistance to damage from nonmagical weapons. The only actions a creature can take in this form are the Dash action or to revert to its normal form. Reverting back take a full round during which time the recipient is incapacitated as they reconstitute themselves. If hit by lightning while in cloud form the recipient becomes 'Charged' for 1 minute, while Charged they may cast call lightning at will in the area directly below them (dc 15)

Homebrew / Boons

Boon of the Empath

Boon of the Empath

Awareness. You automatically know the strongest emotion being experienced by any creature within 30 feet of you. You have advantage on Wisdom (Insight) checks.

Connection. As a bonus action, you can establish a telepathic bond with one creature you can see within 60 feet for 1 minute. You do not need to share a language with the target, but the target must know at least one language. While bonded, you can communicate telepathically and know whenever the creature is frightened, charmed, stunned, or reduced below half its hit points.

Protection. When a creature bonded to you fails a saving throw made to frighten, charm, or stun them, you can use your reaction to allow them to reroll the save, adding your Wisdom modifier as a bonus. If the creature succeeds, the creature that invoked the saving throw takes the same amount of psychic damage as the new save rolled (including modifiers). You can use this effect a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, resetting on a Long Rest.

Homebrew / Boons

Boon of the Magical Gardener

Boon of the Magical Gardener

  • You gain a +5 bonus on Arcana, Nature, or Survival checks made to discern plants.
  • In addition, you may cast the spell Find Familiar and summon a Chwinga (Missing it's magical gift) using it
Homebrew / Boons

Boon of the Phoenix

Boon of the Phoenix

Prerequisite: Boon of the Fire Soul

Whenever you are subjected to fire damage, you take none of that damage and regain a number of hit points equal to half the fire damage dealt.

Fire Form. The recipient of this boon can move through a space as narrow as 1 inch wide without squeezing. Any creature that touches the phoenix or hits it with a melee attack while within 5 feet of it takes 5 (1d10) fire damage. In addition, the recipient of this boon can enter a hostile creature’s space and stop there. The first time it enters a creature’s space on a turn, that creature takes 5 (1d10) fire damage. With a touch, the recipient of this boon can also ignite flammable objects that aren’t worn or carried (no action required).

Fiery Death and Rebirth. When the recipient of this boon dies, it explodes. Each creature within 60-feet of it must make a DC 20 Dexterity saving throw, taking 22 (4d10) fire damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. The fire ignites flammable objects in the area that aren’t worn or carried.

The explosion destroys the recipient's body and carried items and leaves behind an egg-shaped cinder that weighs 5 pounds. The cinder is blazing hot, dealing 21 (6d6) fire damage to any creature that touches it, though no more than once per round. The cinder is immune to all damage, and after 1d6 days, it hatches a new Phoenix. Due to the strain put on the Phoenix’s soul, this forces a new prestige, requiring a small tattood Roman numeral on their body to increase by one. The tattoo can be placed wherever this boon recipient wishes. If the recipient of this boon has paragon levels, they are reset to the beginning of a gestalt prestige in their current Paragon.

Homebrew / Boons

Boon of the Shapechanger

Boon of the Shapechanger

The CR range for wildshape, shapechange, and polymorph is increased by half of your post 20 lvl rounded down.

This does not function for things such as chain polymorphing, shapechanging, etc; For example you can not poly into a CR23 creature, then a CR26, then CR29. You are limited to CR23 at lvl 20 with 6 post 20 lvls. For clarity, avilable CR is 21 at lvl 20p2, 22 at 20p4, and 23 at 20p6.

Boon of the True Trickster

Boon of the True Trickster

Your illusions have become so perfectly crafted that even those with true sight have become impaired by their effects. Your illusion spells appear real to any creature.

Truesight no longer automatically succeeds through your illusions and will now provide only advantage on saving throws and checks made to discern your illusions.

Boon of Trolls Heart

You regain 5 hitpoints at the start of your turn. If you are damaged by fire, acid, or radiant damage, this trait ceases to function until your next short or long rest.

Boon of Vampiric Strikes

Boon of Vampiric Strikes

  • Your melee weapon attacks deal an additional 1d8 necrotic damage.
  • Additionally, you regain hit points equal to half the amount of necrotic damage dealt by this boon, unless the target is an undead or construct.
Homebrew / Boons

Boon of Wings

Boon of Wings

You sprout a pair of wings. You gain a flying speed equal to your walking speed. You can furl the wings against your back as a bonus action and unfurl them the same way — while furled, they don't interfere with armor, but you can't fly. Grounded: If you're incapacitated, restrained, or wearing armor you're not proficient with, your wings fail and you fall.

Wing Style (d8)

Roll or choose. Each grants a minor trait beyond flight.

d8 Wings Trait
1 Bat Blindsight 15 ft. while flying.
2 Eagle Advantage on Perception checks relying on sight in daylight.
3 Angelic Once per long rest, shed daylight out to 5 feet from your feathers for 1 minute.
4 Dragon Resistance to one damage type matching your scale color.
5 Spectral Your flight is silent; you can hover, and you leave no tracks in air or on soft ground.
6 Insectile Your flying speed increases by 10 ft., but you can't fly in strong wind.
7 Moth Advantage on Stealth checks in dim light or darkness while airborne.
8 Storm-torn When you take the Dash action while flying, lightning crackles: one creature you fly past takes 1d6 lightning damage.

Artificer: Artillirist Additions

Artificer: Artillirist Additions

Optional Additions

  • They are now granted proficiency with firearms if they do not already have it.
  • Eldritch Cannons, when tiny, can now be integrated into a firearm. They now move with you if integrated, but otherwise function RAW.
  • The Arcane Firearm feature can now be used on firearms as well, instead of just a wand, staff, or rod.
Homebrew / Class-features

Artificer: Spell-Storing Item

Artificer: Spell-Storing Item

Optional (Replaces Current Spell-Storing Item feature)

At 11th level, you learn how to store a spell in an object. Whenever you finish a long rest, you can touch one simple or martial weapon or one item that you can use as a spellcasting focus, and you store a spell in it, choosing a 1st- or 2nd-level spell from the artificer spell list that requires 1 action to cast (you needn't have it prepared).You may upcast a 1st level spell to use a 2nd level slot, if previous conditions are applicable.

While holding the object, a creature can take an action to produce the spell's effect from it, using your spellcasting ability modifier. If the spell requires concentration, the creature must concentrate. The spell stays in the object until it's been used a number of times equal to twice your Intelligence modifier (minimum of twice) or until you use this feature again to store a spell in an object.

Bard: Counter Charm

Bard: Counter Charm

Optional Class Feature (Replaces Counter Charm)

At 6th level, you gain the ability to use musical notes or words of power to disrupt mind-influencing effects. As a reaction when you or a creature within 30 feet of you fails a saving throw to prevent or remove the charm or frightened condition, you can have the creature reroll the saving throw with advantage. A creature must be able to hear you to gain this benefit.

Homebrew / Class-features

Bard: Everlasting Inspiration

Bard: Everlasting Inspiration

Optional Class Feature (Replaces Superior Inspiration)

At 20th level your inspiration becomes more than a just a short lived burst. When a creature uses your bardic inspiration, the effect is not expended, allowing for the creature to use it multiple times. Your bardic inspiration now only ends once used a number of times equal to your charisma modifier, or once ten minutes pass.

Homebrew / Class-features

Bard: Magical Secrets

Bard: Magical Secrets

Optional (Replaces standard Magical Secrets)

By 10th level, you have plundered magical knowledge from a wide spectrum of disciplines. Choose two spells from any classes, including this one. A spell you choose must be of a level you can cast, as shown on the Bard table, or a cantrip.

The chosen spells count as bard spells for you and are not included as part of the Spells Known column of the Bard table.

You learn two additional spells from any classes at 14th level and again at 18th level.

Ranger: Natural Explorer

Ranger: Natural Explorer

Optional (Replaces Natural Explorer)

You are particularly familiar with one type of natural environment and are adept at traveling and surviving in such regions. Choose one type of favored terrain: arctic, coast, desert, forest, grassland, mountain, swamp, ,Underdark, Hills, Underwater, or Urban. When you make an Intelligence or Wisdom check related to your favored terrain, your proficiency bonus is doubled if you are using a skill that you're proficient in.

While traveling for an hour or more in your favored terrain, you gain the following benefits:

  • Difficult terrain doesn't slow your group's travel.
  • Your group can't become lost except by magical means.
  • Even when you are engaged in another activity while traveling (such as foraging, navigating, or tracking), you remain alert to danger.
  • If you are traveling alone, you can move stealthily at a normal pace.
  • When you forage, you find twice as much food as you normally would.
  • While tracking other creatures, you also learn their exact number, their sizes, and how long ago they passed through the area.

You choose additional favored terrain types at 6th and 10th level.

Warlock 2024: Pact Boon, Pact of the Garb

Warlock 2024: Pact Boon, Pact of the Garb

Your patron bestows upon you special clothing in the form of ceremonial garbs or eldritch garments that can protect you and bolster your abilities. While not holding a shield, the garb is light armor with an AC of 10 + your charisma modifier + your dexterity modifier

You can don and doff the garb as an action, and it cannot be removed unless you wish it to be. If the garb is lost or destroyed, you can perform a 1 hour ceremony to receive another from your patron. This ceremony can be performed on a short or long rest, whereupon the previous garbs disappear. The garbs fade away when you die. You cannot benefit from the garbs or it's invocations while wearing other armor.

Invocations:

Weaver’s Birthright

Prerequisites: Pact of the Garb

While wearing your garb, you can use an action to transform your garb’s appearance to any form of mundane clothing you wish. This does not change the garb’s statistics or properties.

Eldritch Defense

Prerequisites: 5th level, Pact of the Garb

By spending an hour in ritual with any shield, you bind it to your eldritch garb, you can only bind a single shield to your garbs. You gain proficiency with shields and retain you garb AC, while wielding a shield.

Eldritch Armor

Prerequisites: 5th level, Pact of the Garb

Choose two damage types. You are resistant to those damage types while you are wearing your garb. At the end of a long rest, you may change the damage types you chose.

Insurmountable Linens

Prerequisites: 12th level, Pact of the Garb

When you are subjected to an effect that allows you to make a saving throw to take only half damage, you instead take no damage if you succeed on the saving throw.

Warlock: Eldritch Invocations: Eldritch Flux

Warlock: Eldritch Invocations: Eldritch Flux

Invocation Option

Requires 5th level, eldritch blast cantrip

Once per short rest, when you cast Eldritch Blast targeting more than one creature, each targeted creature hit must make a Charisma saving throw against your spell save DC. A creature failing this save is marked.

Once within the next minute, you can use a bonus action to trigger Eldritch Flux. When activated, you and all marked creatures within the Eldritch Blast range experience a dimensional shift. You may swap positions of yourself and the marked creatures within this range.

If the target would not have the space after being shifted, the target is unaffected.

Homebrew / Class-features

Warlock: Eldritch Invocations: Improved Pact Weapon

Warlock: Eldritch Invocations: Improved Pact Weapon

Optional (Replaces Improved Pact Weapon Invocation)

Prerequisite: Pact of the Blade feature

You can use any weapon you summon with your Pact of the Blade feature as a spellcasting focus for your warlock spells.

In addition, the weapon gains a +1 bonus to its attack and damage rolls, unless it is a magic weapon that already has a bonus to those rolls.

Finally, bows and firearms can be conjured or transformed into pact weapons.

Homebrew / Class-features

Warlock: Eldritch Invocations: Investment of the Chain Master

Warlock: Eldritch Invocations: Investment of the Chain Master

Optional (Replaces Investment of the Chain Master)

Prerequisite: Pact of the Chain feature When you cast find familiar, you infuse the summoned familiar with a measure of your eldritch power, granting the creature the following benefits:

  • The familiar gains either a flying speed or a swimming speed (your choice) of 40 feet.
  • As a bonus action, you can command the familiar to take the Attack action.
  • The familiar's weapon attacks are considered magical for the purpose of overcoming immunity and resistance to nonmagical attacks.
  • If the familiar forces a creature to make a saving throw, it uses your spell save DC.
  • When the familiar takes damage, you can use your reaction to grant it resistance against that damage
  • Your familiar obtains a bonus to hit equal to your charisma modifier.
Homebrew / Class-features

Warlock: Pact Boon: Pact of the Core

Warlock: Pact Boon: Pact of the Core

Pact of the Core

Your patron gives you a piece of itself that you can use to great benefit. At the end of a short or long rest, your patron gives you a core trinket that takes the form of a tiny object of your choosing. You can use a bonus action to consume this trinket, either by crushing it, eating it, or a similar action, restoring hit points and bestowing temporary hit points equal to your warlock level.

You may also use an action to create a core trinket by consuming one of your pact magic slots. You may consume the trinket as part of that action.

Invocations:

Sacrifice to Higher Power

Prerequisites: Pact of the Core

When you reduce a creature to 0 hit points, you can create a core trinket as a reaction. You may only use this invocation once per short or long rest.

Lifegiving Core

Prerequisites: 5th level, Pact of the Core

When you consume the core trinket, you may choose a creature within 60ft to benefit from its effects rather than yourself.

Core Herald

Prerequisites: 12th level, Pact of the Core

Consuming the core trinket grants advantage on your next attack roll, saving throw, or ability check.

Greater Trinket

Prerequisites: 15th level, Pact of the Core

When you use a pact magic slot to create and consume a core trinket, roll a number of d8s equal to the level of the slot used. That total is added to the temporary hp gained from consuming the core.

Homebrew / Class-features

Warlock: Pact Boon: Pact of the Garb

Warlock: Pact Boon: Pact of the Garb

Pact of the Garb

Your patron bestows upon you special clothing in the form of ceremonial garbs or eldritch garments that can protect you and bolster your abilities. The garb is light armor with an AC of 10 + your charisma modifier + your dexterity modifier.

You can don and doff the garb as an action, and it cannot be removed unless you wish it to be. If the garb is lost or destroyed, you can perform a 1 hour ceremony to receive another from your patron. This ceremony can be performed on a short or long rest, whereupon the previous garbs disappear. The garbs fade away when you die.

Invocations:

Weaver’s Birthright

Prerequisites: Pact of the Garb

While wearing your garb, you can use an action to transform your garb’s appearance to any form of mundane clothing you wish. This does not change the garb’s statistics or properties.

Thickened Garbs

Prerequisites: 5th level, Pact of the Garb

While wearing your garb, your AC increases by 1.

Eldritch Armor

Prerequisites: 5th level, Pact of the Garb

Choose two damage types. You are resistant to those damage types while you are wearing your garb. At the end of a long rest, you may change the damage types you chose.

Insurmountable Linens

Prerequisites: 12th level, Pact of the Garb

When you are subjected to an effect that allows you to make a saving throw to take only half damage, you instead take no damage if you succeed on the saving throw.
