Homebrew / Classes

Blood Hunter (Version X)

Blood Hunter (Version X)

This overhaul is mostly a buff to the base class as written by Matt Mercer. There were a number of features that went largely unused, were very situational, or generally underwhelming in practice. The main draw the class presents in this overhaul is that it leans more into the sacrificing of your hit points, using your health more as a typical mana pool for your abilities, and gives you more ways to spend your hit points to do so. Every other class resource the Blood Hunter had previously is gone.

This overhaul also features a true distinction between using intelligence and wisdom as your hemocraft modifier. Intelligence leads to a more monstrous take on your blood magic, granting you greater offensive ability as your hemocraft takes shape. Where wisdom takes a more defensive route, and later grants more control over your hemocraft.

The Blood Hunter Table

Level Proficiency Bonus Class Features Blood Curses Known Hemocraft Die
1 +2 Hunter’s Bane, Blood Maledict 2 1d6
2 +2 Fighting Style, Crimson Rite 2 1d6
3 +2 Blood Hunter Order 2 1d6
4 +2 Ability Score Improvement 2 1d6
5 +3 Extra Attack 2 1d8
6 +3 Brand of Castigation 3 1d8
7 +3 Blood Hunter Order Feature 3 1d8
8 +3 Ability Score Improvement 3 1d8
9 +4 Grim Psychometry 3 1d8
10 +4 Dark Augmentation 3 1d8
11 +4 Blood Hunter Order Feature 4 1d10
12 +4 Ability Score Improvement 4 1d10
13 +5 Tethering Brand 4 1d10
14 +5 Hardened Soul 4 1d10
15 +5 Blood Hunter Order Feature 4 1d10
16 +5 Ability Score Improvement 5 1d10
17 +6 Blood Price 5 1d12
18 +6 Blood Hunter Order Feature 5 1d12
19 +6 Ability Score Improvement 5 1d12
20 +6 Blood Hunter Order Feature 5 1d12

Class Features

As a Blood Hunter you gain the following class features.

Hit Points

Hit Dice: 1d12 per Blood Hunter Level

Hit Points at 1st Level: 12 + your constitution modifier

Hit Points at Higher Levels: 1d12 (or 7) + your constitution modifier per Blood Hunter level after 1st

Proficiencies

Weapons: Simple, Martial

Armor: Light, Medium, Shields

Tools: Alchemist’s Supplies

Saving Throws: Dexterity, Intelligence

Skills: Choose three from Acrobatics, Arcana, Athletics, History, Insight, Investigation, Religion, and Survival

Hunter’s Bane

At 1st level, you have survived the Hunter’s Bane - a dangerous, long guarded ritual that alters your life’s blood. You have advantage on Wisdom (Survival) checks to track fey, fiends, and undead, as well as Intelligence checks to recall information about such creatures.

The Hunter’s Bane also empowers your body to control and shape hemocraft magic, using your own blood and life-essence to fuel your abilities. Choose either your intelligence or your wisdom score. Your hemocraft modifier is equal to the modifier of the chosen ability. The ability you choose also determines the effects of features you gain at later levels. When you reach a feature that has [Monstrous] or [Stable] options, you gain the [Monstrous] option if your hemocraft modifier uses your intelligence, or the [Stable] options if your hemocraft modifier uses your wisdom.

Some of your Blood Hunter features require you to sacrifice hit points in order to activate or sustain. When a feature asks you to sacrifice hit points, your hit points are lowered by that amount. This sacrifice cannot be reduced in any way. If the sacrifice would leave you with 0 hit points, you fall unconscious as normal, and the ability fails.

When any of your Blood Hunter features require a target to make a saving throw, the save DC is calculated with the following:

Hemocraft save DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your hemocraft modifier

Blood Maladict

Also at 1st level, you gain the ability to sacrifice your vital essence to curse and manipulate creatures through hemocraft magic.

Blood Curses Known: You know two Blood Curses of your choice, and learn additional blood curses at later levels as shown by the “Blood Curses Known” column of the Blood Hunter Table.

Invoking a Blood Curse: To use a Blood Curse, you must roll your hemocraft die, sacrificing hit points equal to the number rolled.

Amplifying a Blood Curse requires you to roll three hemocraft dice instead of one.

You can Invoke or Amplify your known Blood Curses as many times as you like, so long as you pay the hit point cost each time.

Fighting Style

At 2nd Level, you adopt a particular style of fighting as your specialty. Choose one of the following options.

You can’t take a Fighting Style option more than once, even if you later get to choose again.

Archery: You gain a +2 bonus to attack rolls you make with ranged weapons.

Blind Fighting: You have blindsight with a range of 10 feet. Within that range, you can effectively see anything that isn’t behind total cover, even if you’re blinded or in darkness. Moreover, you can see an invisible creature within that range, unless the creature successfully hides from you.

Defense: While you are wearing armor, you gain a +1 bonus to AC.

Dueling: When you are wielding a melee weapon in one hand and no other weapons, you gain a +2 bonus to damage rolls with that weapon.

Great Weapon Fighting: When you roll a 1 or 2 on a damage die for an attack you make with a melee weapon that you are wielding with two hands, you can reroll the die and must use the new roll. The weapon must have the two-handed or versatile property for you to gain this benefit.

Crimson Rite

Also at 2nd level, you learn to invoke a rite of hemocraft that infuses your weapon strikes with energy. As a bonus action, you can activate any rite you know, enhancing one weapon that you are holding. The rite remains in effect until you finish a short or long rest. When you activate a rite, you sacrifice hit points equal to one roll of your hemocraft die.

While a rite is in effect, attacks made with that weapon are considered magical for the purposes of overcoming resistance and immunity to non-magical damage, and deal extra damage equal to one roll of your hemocraft die of a damage type determined by the chosen rite.

When you attack a creature with a weapon affected by any of your Crimson Rites, and deal damage to them, you can choose to amplify the effect. Doing so causes you to sacrifice hit points equal to one roll of your hemocraft die.

A single weapon can only hold one rite at any given time, and other creatures cannot benefit from your rite.

Choose one of the following rites when you gain this feature. You learn one additional rite at 7th and 14th level:

Rite of the Flame - The extra damage dealt by your rite is fire damage.

When amplified, the target is burned, taking fire damage equal to your hemocraft modifier at the start of each of it’s turns. You may stack this effect on a single creature up to a number of times equal to half your proficiency bonus. The burning creature, or a creature within 5 feet of it can use an action to douse the flames.

Rite of the Frozen - The extra damage dealt by your rite is cold damage.

When amplified, the target’s move speed is reduced by 5 times your hemocraft modifier, to a minimum of 0 feet.

Rite of the Storm - The extra damage dealt by your rite is lightning damage.

When amplified, electricity arcs to other targets within 20 feet of your choice. You can target a number of creatures equal to your hemocraft modifier. Each extra target takes lightning damage equal to one roll of your hemocraft die.

Rite of the Dead - The extra damage dealt by your rite is necrotic damage.

When amplified, the target has its strength sapped until the end of its next turn. While sapped, it has disadvantage on Strength and Dexterity checks and saving throws.

Rite of the Oracle - The extra damage dealt by your rite is psychic damage.

When amplified, visions of dread flood your target’s mind. The target is frightened of you until the end of their next turn.

Rite of the Roar - The extra damage dealt by your rite is thunder damage.

When amplified, a thunderous crash slams into your target. The target is either pushed up to 10 feet away from you or knocked prone (your choice).

Rite of the Dawn (Order of the Ghostslayer) - The extra damage dealt by your rite is radiant damage. Additionally, while the rite is active, you gain the following benefits.

  • Your weapon sheds bright light out a range of 20 feet, and dim light out 20 past that.
  • You have resistance to necrotic damage.
  • When you hit an undead creature with a weapon effected by this rite, roll one additional hemocraft die when determining the extra damage.

When amplified, if the target is an undead, they are placed under the effect of turn undead.

Rite of the Blighted (Order of the Symbiote) - The extra damage dealt by your rite is poison damage. Additionally, hitting a creature with a weapon affected by this rite that is neither undead or a construct deals extra poison damage equal to your hemocraft modifier.

When amplified, the target suffers the poisoned condition until the start of your next turn, bypassing immunity to the condition.

Blood Hunter Order

At 3rd level, you commit to an order of blood hunters whose philosophy will guide you throughout your life. Your choice grants you features at 3rd level, and again at 7th, 11th, 15th, and 18th level.

Ability Score Improvement

When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can’t increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.

Using the optional feats rule, you can forgo taking this feature to take a feat of your choice instead.

Extra Attack

Starting at 5th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the attack action on your turn.

Brand of Castigation

At 6th level, when you damage a creature with your crimson rite, you can channel hemocraft magic to sear an arcane brand into that creature (no action required). Doing so requires you to sacrifice hit points equal to two rolls of your hemocraft die. You always know the direction to the branded creature, so long as it is on the same plane as you.

Additionally, each time the branded creature damages you or creatures of your choice within 30 feet of you, it takes psychic damage equal to your hemocraft modifier (minimum of 1).

Your brand lasts until you dismiss it or until you use this feature to brand another creature. Your brand can be removed with a [Remove Curse] spell or similar effects.

Grim Psychometry

When you reach 9th level, you gain a supernatural talent for discerning secrets surrounding relics or places touched by evil. You can cast the [Contact Other Plane] spell without needing to make an intelligence save. When you do so, you may ask only about your immediate surroundings, but you will only receive clear answers if what you are asking about is linked to evil. Once you cast the spell in this way, you cannot do so again until you finish a long rest.

You also learn the Identify spell, and can cast it as a ritual. The spell fails if the item you attempt to identify is not linked to evil in some way.

Dark Augmentation

When you reach 10th level, the magic of hemocraft suffuses your body. You either control it, or let it control you. You gain a bonus to strength, dexterity, and constitution saving throws equal to your hemocraft modifier.

Additionally, your hemocraft begins to warp your body and mind, the way you channel your blood magic determines how. You gain one of the following benefits:

Monstrous: You gain a bonus to weapon damage rolls equal to your hemocraft modifier.

Stable: Your walking speed increases by 10 feet.

Tethering Brand

Starting at 13th level, your brand works to bind your foes. The damage dealt by your Brand of Castigation doubles to twice your hemocraft modifier (minimum of 2).

Additionally, creatures branded by it cannot take the dash or disengage actions. If a branded creature attempts to teleport, or leave its current plane by any means, it takes 4d6 psychic damage and must succeed on a wisdom saving throw. On a failure, the teleportation or attempt to leave the plane fails.

Hardened Soul

Your mind hardens to external influence when you reach 14th level. How you channel your blood magic determines its effect. Gain one of the following benefits:

Monstrous: You are immune to the frightened condition, and you have advantage on saving throws to end or resist the charmed condition.

Stable: You are immune to the charmed condition, and you have advantage on saving throws to end or resist the frightened condition.

You also gain resistance to psychic damage, regardless of how your hemocraft takes shape.

Blood Price

When you reach 17th level, you gain the ability to fuel your magic more efficiently, so long as your wounds remain open. While you have half your maximum hit points or less, you roll one less hemocraft die when determining the hit point cost of your hemocraft abilities (to a minimum of 0).

The Cost of Power

Upon reaching 20th level, your blood magic reaches its height, and either grants you mastery over it, or consumes you. How you channel your blood magic determines the effect. Gain one of the following benefits:

Monstrous: You roll one additional hemocraft die when determining the damage dealt by your crimson rites, including their amplified effects.

The cost of amplifying blood curses increases by one roll of your hemocraft die.

Stable: When you use a blood curse and roll a hemocraft die, you can choose to reroll the die and use either result. You can only reroll each die once.

The cost of amplifying crimson rites increases by one roll of your hemocraft die.

Blood Curses

As a blood hunter, you have access to a range of blood curses that can tax the resilience of any foe.

Blood Curse of the Anxious

As a bonus action, you harry the body or mind of a creature within 30 feet of you, making them susceptible to forceful influence. Until the end of your next turn, Charisma (Intimidation) checks made against the cursed creature have advantage.

Amplify. The next Wisdom saving throw the cursed creature makes before this curse ends has disadvantage.

Blood Curse of Binding

As a bonus action, you attempt to bind a Large or smaller creature you can see within 30 feet of you, which must make a Strength saving throw. On a failure, the cursed creature’s speed is reduced to 0 and it can’t use reactions until the end of your next turn.

Amplify. This curse lasts for 1 minute and can affect any creature regardless of size. The cursed creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the curse on itself on a success.

Blood Curse of Bloated Agony

As a bonus action, you curse a creature that you can see within 30 feet of you, causing its body to swell until the end of your next turn. For the duration, the creature has disadvantage on Strength checks and Dexterity checks, and takes 1d8 necrotic damage if it makes more than one attack during its turn.

Amplify. This curse lasts for 1 minute. The cursed creature can make a Constitution saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the curse on itself on a success.

Blood Curse of Corrosion

Prerequisite: 15th level, Order of the Mutant

As a bonus action, you cause a creature within 30 feet of you to become poisoned. The cursed creature can make a Constitution saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the curse on itself on a success.

Amplify. The cursed creature takes 4d6 necrotic damage when you inflict this curse, and it takes this damage again each time it fails a Constitution saving throw to end the curse.

Blood Curse of the Exorcist

Prerequisite: 15th level, Order of the Ghostslayer

As a bonus action, you choose one creature you can see within 30 feet of you that is charmed or frightened, or which is under a possession effect. The target creature is no longer charmed, frightened, or possessed.

Amplify. A creature that charmed, frightened, or possessed the target of your curse takes 3d6 psychic damage and must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or be stunned until the end of your next turn.

Blood Curse of Exposure

When a creature you can see within 30 feet of you takes damage from an attack or spell, you can use your reaction to temporarily weaken its resilience. Until the end of the target’s next turn, it loses resistance to all the damage types dealt by the triggering attack or spell (including for that triggering effect).

Amplify. The target instead loses invulnerability to the damage types of the triggering attack or spell, but has resistance to those damage types until the end of its next turn.

Blood Curse of the Eyeless

When a creature you can see within 30 feet of you makes an attack, you can use your reaction to roll one hemocraft die and subtract the number rolled from the creature’s attack roll. You can choose to use this feature after the creature’s roll, but before the DM determines whether the attack hits or misses. The creature is immune to this curse if it is immune to the blinded condition.

Amplify. You apply this curse to all the creature’s attack rolls until the end of the creature’s turn. You roll separately for each affected attack.

Blood Curse of the Fallen Puppet

When a creature you can see within 30 feet of you drops to 0 hit points, you can use your reaction to instill that creature with a final act of aggression. The creature immediately makes one weapon attack against a target of your choice within its range.

Amplify. You can first cause the cursed creature to move up to half its speed, and you grant a bonus to its attack roll equal to your Hemocraft modifier (minimum of +1).

Blood Curse of the Howl

Prerequisite: 18th level, Order of the Lycan

As an action, you unleash a bloodcurdling howl. Each creature within 30 feet of you that can hear you must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or become frightened of you until the end of your next turn. If a creature fails its saving throw by 5 or more, it is stunned while frightened in this way. A creature that succeeds on its saving throw is immune to this blood curse for the next 24 hours.

You can choose any number of creatures you can see to be unaffected by the howl.

Amplify. The range of this curse increases to 60 feet.

Blood Curse of the Marked

As a bonus action, you mark a creature that you can see within 30 feet of you. Until the end of your turn, whenever you hit the cursed creature with a weapon for which you have an active crimson rite, you roll an additional hemocraft die when determining the extra damage from the rite.

Amplify. The next attack roll you make against the target before the end of your turn has advantage.

Blood Curse of the Muddled Mind

As a bonus action, you curse a creature that you can see within 30 feet of you that is concentrating on a spell or using a feature that requires concentration. That creature has disadvantage on the next Constitution saving throw it makes to maintain concentration before the end of your next turn.

Amplify. The cursed creature has disadvantage on all Constitution saving throws made to maintain concentration until the end of your next turn.

Blood Curse of the Soul Eater

Prerequisite: 18th level, Order of the Profane Soul

When a creature that isn’t a construct or undead is reduced to 0 hit points within 30 feet of you, you can use your reaction to offer their life energy to your patron in exchange for power. Until the end of your next turn, you make attacks with advantage and you have resistance to all damage.

Amplify. Additionally, you regain an expended warlock spell slot. Once you’ve amplified this blood curse, you must finish a long rest before you can amplify it again.

Missing.

Hunter’s Bane

At 1st level, you have survived the Hunter’s Bane - a dangerous, long guarded ritual that alters your life’s blood. You have advantage on Wisdom (Survival) checks to track fey, fiends, and undead, as well as Intelligence checks to recall information about such creatures.

The Hunter’s Bane also empowers your body to control and shape hemocraft magic, using your own blood and life-essence to fuel your abilities. Choose either your intelligence or your wisdom score. Your hemocraft modifier is equal to the modifier of the chosen ability. The ability you choose also determines the effects of features you gain at later levels. When you reach a feature that has [Monstrous] or [Stable] options, you gain the [Monstrous] option if your hemocraft modifier uses your intelligence, or the [Stable] options if your hemocraft modifier uses your wisdom.

Some of your Blood Hunter features require you to sacrifice hit points in order to activate or sustain. When a feature asks you to sacrifice hit points, your hit points are lowered by that amount. This sacrifice cannot be reduced in any way. If the sacrifice would leave you with 0 hit points, you fall unconscious as normal, and the ability fails.

When any of your Blood Hunter features require a target to make a saving throw, the save DC is calculated with the following:

Hemocraft save DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your hemocraft modifier

Blood Maladict

Also at 1st level, you gain the ability to sacrifice your vital essence to curse and manipulate creatures through hemocraft magic.

Blood Curses Known: You know two Blood Curses of your choice, and learn additional blood curses at later levels as shown by the “Blood Curses Known” column of the Blood Hunter Table.

Invoking a Blood Curse: To use a Blood Curse, you must roll your hemocraft die, sacrificing hit points equal to the number rolled.

Amplifying a Blood Curse requires you to roll three hemocraft dice instead of one.

You can Invoke or Amplify your known Blood Curses as many times as you like, so long as you pay the hit point cost each time.

Fighting Style

At 2nd Level, you adopt a particular style of fighting as your specialty. Choose one of the following options.

You can’t take a Fighting Style option more than once, even if you later get to choose again.

Archery: You gain a +2 bonus to attack rolls you make with ranged weapons.

Blind Fighting: You have blindsight with a range of 10 feet. Within that range, you can effectively see anything that isn’t behind total cover, even if you’re blinded or in darkness. Moreover, you can see an invisible creature within that range, unless the creature successfully hides from you.

Defense: While you are wearing armor, you gain a +1 bonus to AC.

Dueling: When you are wielding a melee weapon in one hand and no other weapons, you gain a +2 bonus to damage rolls with that weapon.

Great Weapon Fighting: When you roll a 1 or 2 on a damage die for an attack you make with a melee weapon that you are wielding with two hands, you can reroll the die and must use the new roll. The weapon must have the two-handed or versatile property for you to gain this benefit.

Crimson Rite

Also at 2nd level, you learn to invoke a rite of hemocraft that infuses your weapon strikes with energy. As a bonus action, you can activate any rite you know, enhancing one weapon that you are holding. The rite remains in effect until you finish a short or long rest. When you activate a rite, you sacrifice hit points equal to one roll of your hemocraft die.

While a rite is in effect, attacks made with that weapon are considered magical for the purposes of overcoming resistance and immunity to non-magical damage, and deal extra damage equal to one roll of your hemocraft die of a damage type determined by the chosen rite.

When you attack a creature with a weapon affected by any of your Crimson Rites, and deal damage to them, you can choose to amplify the effect. Doing so causes you to sacrifice hit points equal to one roll of your hemocraft die.

A single weapon can only hold one rite at any given time, and other creatures cannot benefit from your rite.

Choose one of the following rites when you gain this feature. You learn one additional rite at 7th and 14th level:

Rite of the Flame - The extra damage dealt by your rite is fire damage.

When amplified, the target is burned, taking fire damage equal to your hemocraft modifier at the start of each of it’s turns. You may stack this effect on a single creature up to a number of times equal to half your proficiency bonus. The burning creature, or a creature within 5 feet of it can use an action to douse the flames.

Rite of the Frozen - The extra damage dealt by your rite is cold damage.

When amplified, the target’s move speed is reduced by 5 times your hemocraft modifier, to a minimum of 0 feet.

Rite of the Storm - The extra damage dealt by your rite is lightning damage.

When amplified, electricity arcs to other targets within 20 feet of your choice. You can target a number of creatures equal to your hemocraft modifier. Each extra target takes lightning damage equal to one roll of your hemocraft die.

Rite of the Dead - The extra damage dealt by your rite is necrotic damage.

When amplified, the target has its strength sapped until the end of its next turn. While sapped, it has disadvantage on Strength and Dexterity checks and saving throws.

Rite of the Oracle - The extra damage dealt by your rite is psychic damage.

When amplified, visions of dread flood your target’s mind. The target is frightened of you until the end of their next turn.

Rite of the Roar - The extra damage dealt by your rite is thunder damage.

When amplified, a thunderous crash slams into your target. The target is either pushed up to 10 feet away from you or knocked prone (your choice).

Rite of the Dawn (Order of the Ghostslayer) - The extra damage dealt by your rite is radiant damage. Additionally, while the rite is active, you gain the following benefits.

  • Your weapon sheds bright light out a range of 20 feet, and dim light out 20 past that.
  • You have resistance to necrotic damage.
  • When you hit an undead creature with a weapon effected by this rite, roll one additional hemocraft die when determining the extra damage.

When amplified, if the target is an undead, they are placed under the effect of turn undead.

Rite of the Blighted (Order of the Symbiote) - The extra damage dealt by your rite is poison damage. Additionally, hitting a creature with a weapon affected by this rite that is neither undead or a construct deals extra poison damage equal to your hemocraft modifier.

When amplified, the target suffers the poisoned condition until the start of your next turn, bypassing immunity to the condition.

Blood Hunter Order

At 3rd level, you commit to an order of blood hunters whose philosophy will guide you throughout your life. Your choice grants you features at 3rd level, and again at 7th, 11th, 15th, and 18th level.

Ability Score Improvement

When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can’t increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.

Using the optional feats rule, you can forgo taking this feature to take a feat of your choice instead.

Extra Attack

Starting at 5th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the attack action on your turn.

Brand of Castigation

At 6th level, when you damage a creature with your crimson rite, you can channel hemocraft magic to sear an arcane brand into that creature (no action required). Doing so requires you to sacrifice hit points equal to two rolls of your hemocraft die. You always know the direction to the branded creature, so long as it is on the same plane as you.

Additionally, each time the branded creature damages you or creatures of your choice within 30 feet of you, it takes psychic damage equal to your hemocraft modifier (minimum of 1).

Your brand lasts until you dismiss it or until you use this feature to brand another creature. Your brand can be removed with a [Remove Curse] spell or similar effects.

Grim Psychometry

When you reach 9th level, you gain a supernatural talent for discerning secrets surrounding relics or places touched by evil. You can cast the [Contact Other Plane] spell without needing to make an intelligence save. When you do so, you may ask only about your immediate surroundings, but you will only receive clear answers if what you are asking about is linked to evil. Once you cast the spell in this way, you cannot do so again until you finish a long rest.

You also learn the Identify spell, and can cast it as a ritual. The spell fails if the item you attempt to identify is not linked to evil in some way.

Dark Augmentation

When you reach 10th level, the magic of hemocraft suffuses your body. You either control it, or let it control you. You gain a bonus to strength, dexterity, and constitution saving throws equal to your hemocraft modifier.

Additionally, your hemocraft begins to warp your body and mind, the way you channel your blood magic determines how. You gain one of the following benefits:

Monstrous: You gain a bonus to weapon damage rolls equal to your hemocraft modifier.

Stable: Your walking speed increases by 10 feet.

Tethering Brand

Starting at 13th level, your brand works to bind your foes. The damage dealt by your Brand of Castigation doubles to twice your hemocraft modifier (minimum of 2).

Additionally, creatures branded by it cannot take the dash or disengage actions. If a branded creature attempts to teleport, or leave its current plane by any means, it takes 4d6 psychic damage and must succeed on a wisdom saving throw. On a failure, the teleportation or attempt to leave the plane fails.

Hardened Soul

Your mind hardens to external influence when you reach 14th level. How you channel your blood magic determines its effect. Gain one of the following benefits:

Monstrous: You are immune to the frightened condition, and you have advantage on saving throws to end or resist the charmed condition.

Stable: You are immune to the charmed condition, and you have advantage on saving throws to end or resist the frightened condition.

You also gain resistance to psychic damage, regardless of how your hemocraft takes shape.

Blood Price

When you reach 17th level, you gain the ability to fuel your magic more efficiently, so long as your wounds remain open. While you have half your maximum hit points or less, you roll one less hemocraft die when determining the hit point cost of your hemocraft abilities (to a minimum of 0).

The Cost of Power

Upon reaching 20th level, your blood magic reaches its height, and either grants you mastery over it, or consumes you. How you channel your blood magic determines the effect. Gain one of the following benefits:

Monstrous: You roll one additional hemocraft die when determining the damage dealt by your crimson rites, including their amplified effects.

The cost of amplifying blood curses increases by one roll of your hemocraft die.

Stable: When you use a blood curse and roll a hemocraft die, you can choose to reroll the die and use either result. You can only reroll each die once.

The cost of amplifying crimson rites increases by one roll of your hemocraft die.

Blood Curses

As a blood hunter, you have access to a range of blood curses that can tax the resilience of any foe.

Blood Curse of the Anxious

As a bonus action, you harry the body or mind of a creature within 30 feet of you, making them susceptible to forceful influence. Until the end of your next turn, Charisma (Intimidation) checks made against the cursed creature have advantage.

Amplify. The next Wisdom saving throw the cursed creature makes before this curse ends has disadvantage.

Blood Curse of Binding

As a bonus action, you attempt to bind a Large or smaller creature you can see within 30 feet of you, which must make a Strength saving throw. On a failure, the cursed creature’s speed is reduced to 0 and it can’t use reactions until the end of your next turn.

Amplify. This curse lasts for 1 minute and can affect any creature regardless of size. The cursed creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the curse on itself on a success.

Blood Curse of Bloated Agony

As a bonus action, you curse a creature that you can see within 30 feet of you, causing its body to swell until the end of your next turn. For the duration, the creature has disadvantage on Strength checks and Dexterity checks, and takes 1d8 necrotic damage if it makes more than one attack during its turn.

Amplify. This curse lasts for 1 minute. The cursed creature can make a Constitution saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the curse on itself on a success.

Blood Curse of Corrosion

Prerequisite: 15th level, Order of the Mutant

As a bonus action, you cause a creature within 30 feet of you to become poisoned. The cursed creature can make a Constitution saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the curse on itself on a success.

Amplify. The cursed creature takes 4d6 necrotic damage when you inflict this curse, and it takes this damage again each time it fails a Constitution saving throw to end the curse.

Blood Curse of the Exorcist

Prerequisite: 15th level, Order of the Ghostslayer

As a bonus action, you choose one creature you can see within 30 feet of you that is charmed or frightened, or which is under a possession effect. The target creature is no longer charmed, frightened, or possessed.

Amplify. A creature that charmed, frightened, or possessed the target of your curse takes 3d6 psychic damage and must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or be stunned until the end of your next turn.

Blood Curse of Exposure

When a creature you can see within 30 feet of you takes damage from an attack or spell, you can use your reaction to temporarily weaken its resilience. Until the end of the target’s next turn, it loses resistance to all the damage types dealt by the triggering attack or spell (including for that triggering effect).

Amplify. The target instead loses invulnerability to the damage types of the triggering attack or spell, but has resistance to those damage types until the end of its next turn.

Blood Curse of the Eyeless

When a creature you can see within 30 feet of you makes an attack, you can use your reaction to roll one hemocraft die and subtract the number rolled from the creature’s attack roll. You can choose to use this feature after the creature’s roll, but before the DM determines whether the attack hits or misses. The creature is immune to this curse if it is immune to the blinded condition.

Amplify. You apply this curse to all the creature’s attack rolls until the end of the creature’s turn. You roll separately for each affected attack.

Blood Curse of the Fallen Puppet

When a creature you can see within 30 feet of you drops to 0 hit points, you can use your reaction to instill that creature with a final act of aggression. The creature immediately makes one weapon attack against a target of your choice within its range.

Amplify. You can first cause the cursed creature to move up to half its speed, and you grant a bonus to its attack roll equal to your Hemocraft modifier (minimum of +1).

Blood Curse of the Howl

Prerequisite: 18th level, Order of the Lycan

As an action, you unleash a bloodcurdling howl. Each creature within 30 feet of you that can hear you must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or become frightened of you until the end of your next turn. If a creature fails its saving throw by 5 or more, it is stunned while frightened in this way. A creature that succeeds on its saving throw is immune to this blood curse for the next 24 hours.

You can choose any number of creatures you can see to be unaffected by the howl.

Amplify. The range of this curse increases to 60 feet.

Blood Curse of the Marked

As a bonus action, you mark a creature that you can see within 30 feet of you. Until the end of your turn, whenever you hit the cursed creature with a weapon for which you have an active crimson rite, you roll an additional hemocraft die when determining the extra damage from the rite.

Amplify. The next attack roll you make against the target before the end of your turn has advantage.

Blood Curse of the Muddled Mind

As a bonus action, you curse a creature that you can see within 30 feet of you that is concentrating on a spell or using a feature that requires concentration. That creature has disadvantage on the next Constitution saving throw it makes to maintain concentration before the end of your next turn.

Amplify. The cursed creature has disadvantage on all Constitution saving throws made to maintain concentration until the end of your next turn.

Blood Curse of the Soul Eater

Prerequisite: 18th level, Order of the Profane Soul

When a creature that isn’t a construct or undead is reduced to 0 hit points within 30 feet of you, you can use your reaction to offer their life energy to your patron in exchange for power. Until the end of your next turn, you make attacks with advantage and you have resistance to all damage.

Amplify. Additionally, you regain an expended warlock spell slot. Once you’ve amplified this blood curse, you must finish a long rest before you can amplify it again.

Homebrew / Classes

Bombardier

Bombardier

Description

Where the Alchemist brings life, the Bombardier brings ruin. Bombardiers are masters of volatile reagents, crafting incendiary flasks, caustic vials, and toxic brews designed to engulf their foes in lingering devastation. On the battlefield, they are walking arsenals, hurling explosive concoctions that set the world ablaze.

Features:

  • 3rd Level - Tool Proficiency
  • 3rd Level - Bombardier Spells
  • 3rd Level - Experimental Bomb
  • 5th Level - Volatile Savant
  • 9th Level - Corrosive Concoctions
  • 9th Level - Rapid Alchemy
  • 15th Level - Master of Ruin

3rd Level - Tool Proficiency

When you adopt this specialization at 3rd level, you gain proficiency with alchemist’s supplies. If you already have this proficiency, you gain proficiency with another type of artisan’s tools of your choice.

3rd Level - Bombardier Spells

You always have certain spells prepared after you reach particular levels in this class, as shown in the Bombardier Spells table. These spells count as artificer spells for you and don’t count against the number of artificer spells you prepare.

Artificer Level | Spells

  • 3rd | grease, inflict wounds
  • 5th | web, Melf's acid arrow
  • 9th | gaseous form, stinking cloud
  • 13th | greater invisibility, vitriolic sphere
  • 17th | wall of force, immolation

3rd Level - Experimental Bomb

Starting at 3rd level, whenever you finish a long rest, you can magically produce an experimental bomb in an empty flask or vial you touch. Roll on the Experimental Bomb table to determine its effect, which is triggered when you throw it.

As an action, you or another creature can throw the bomb up to 30 feet, where it shatters and releases its effect. A creature in the bomb’s area must make a saving throw against your artificer spell save DC to avoid or reduce its effects.

You can create additional experimental bombs by expending a spell slot of 1st level or higher for each one. When you do so, you use your action to create the bomb and roll for its effect on the Experimental Bomb table.

Creating a bomb requires alchemist’s supplies on your person, and any bomb you create with this feature lasts until it is thrown or until the end of your next long rest.

Experimental Bomb Table

  1. Corrosive Acid. Deals 2d6 acid damage in a 5-foot radius (Dex save for half). On a failed save, the acid clings to creatures, dealing 1d6 acid damage at the start of each of their turns until a creature uses its action to scrape or wash it off.
  2. Incendiary Fire. Deals 2d6 fire damage in a 5-foot radius (Dex save for half). On a failed save, creatures are set ablaze, taking 1d6 fire damage at the start of each of their turns until they or an ally uses an action to douse the flames.
  3. Toxic Gas. Creates a 10-foot radius cloud of poisonous gas that lasts for 1 minute. (Con save or be poisoned until the start of your next turn; repeat the save at the end of each turn). A creature must make the save whenever it enters the gas or starts its turn in the gas.
  4. Cryo Flask. Deals 2d6 cold damage in a 5-foot radius (Dex save for half). On a failed save, a creature is hindered by ice formations for 1 minute, or until it or another creature within reach uses an action to break the ice.
  5. Shrapnel Bomb. Deals 2d6 piercing damage in a 10-foot radius (Dex save for half). On a failed save, the creature takes 1d6 slashing damage the first time on each turn it moves 1 foot or more without teleporting. An affected creature or ally can use its action to remove the shrapnel.
  6. Sonic Blast. Deals 2d8 thunder damage in a 10-foot radius (Str save for half). Creatures that fail the save are pushed 10 feet from the center of the blast and are deafened until the start of your next turn.

Scaling: The initial and persistent damage increase at higher levels:

  • 6th level: +1d6 (or +1d4/+1d8 for relevant bombs)
  • 11th level: +2d6
  • 16th level: +3d6

5th Level - Volatile Savant

At 5th level, you have mastered the art of combining spellwork and alchemical destruction into seamless attacks.

  • Whenever you cast an artificer spell or cantrip on your turn, you can throw one of your Experimental Bombs as a bonus action.

You can treat any alchemical item (such as alchemist’s fire, acid vial, or an experimental bomb) as a simple ranged weapon with a range of 30/90 feet, using your Dexterity or Strength modifier for attack rolls. Damage dealt by the throw is 1d4 slashing damage plus your Dexterity or Strength modifier, in addition to the damage or effect normally dealt by the item.

9th Level - Corrosive Concoctions

At 9th level, your concoctions weaken enemy defenses and allow you to control the battlefield:

  • Creatures that fail their saving throw against one of your bombs have disadvantage on saving throws against the next alchemical effect you deal to them (from your bombs or alchemical items such as acid vial or alchemist’s fire) before the end of your next turn.

9th Level - Rapid Alchemy

Also at 9th level, you are able to craft bombs with remarkable speed:

  • You can use a bonus action instead of an action to craft your Experimental Bombs.

15th Level - Master of Ruin

At 15th level, your expertise in destruction allows you to maximize the potency of your creations and have better control over what you use:

  • You gain resistance to fire, and acid damage.
  • When a creature takes persistent damage from one of your Experimental Bombs (acid or fire) or an alchemical item (alchemist’s fire, acid vial), you can use your reaction to make the creature take maximum damage instead of rolling. You can use this ability a number of times equal to half your Intelligence modifier (minimum of 1). All expended uses are restored when you finish a long rest.
Homebrew / Classes

Bulwark

Bulwark

The Bulwark Class

Outside the king’s chambers, still as an armor display, the royal guard stands post as they await the coming rebelion force. Ready to meet it head on, no matter the result.

A scrappy militiaman clad in chainmail stands on the battlefield, now alone and bloodied, having outlasted all others through wit and defensive positioning.

Beneath a greathelm, the dwarf’s face pools with sweat as he crosses the great desert, sent on a mission to deliver an important message that cannot afford to fall into the wrong hands

Bulwarks spend large portions of their lives covered in heavy armor to the point that they are seldom ever seen without it. Their mastery over using it fully to their advantage naturally comes as second nature, allowing them to outperform nearly any other. What truly distinguishes a bulwark from other users of heavy armor is their distinct focus on making the absolute most of the defense it offers, knowing how best to move themselves to avoid or block incoming assaults. Bulwarks are often kept as personal guards to high ranking officials, as front-liners in the field of battle, or even as couriers who’s senders need certainty their message will arrive. Adventuring parties who are graced with the inclusion of one of these masters of defense can rest assured that at least one of them will be making it back alive.

The Best Offense...

A Bulwark will tend to focus fully on a defensive standpoint in battle, as an overtly pressing offense might lead to gaps in your attention. In fact, some Bulwarks even refrain from having an actual offense entirely, relying on those around them to defeat their enemies while they spend their attention and energy on lasting as long as possible.

Creating a Bulwark

When creating a Bulwark, consider why your character might have needed to train such a rigorous defense. What training have they undergone to truly set themselves ahead of their peers? Perhaps you were a member of a royal guard, someone trained to protect at any cost. Or rather just a soldier who has taken to protecting themselves a bit further than most. A Bulwark could be anyone of the great strength needed to use heavy armors, and utilizes it to the fullest, and you get to decide just how your character does that.

Bulwark Table

Level Proficiency Bonus Features
1st +2 Defensive Stance, Weapon Mastery
2nd +2 Fortitude
3rd +2 Defensive Specialization
4th +2 Ability Score Improvement
5th +3 Extra Attack, Emissary
6th +3 Conditioning
7th +3 Specialization Feature
8th +3 Ability Score Improvement
9th +4 Dueling Stance
10th +4 Mental Fortitude
11th +4 Shattering Stance
12th +4 Ability Score Improvement
13th +5 Specialization Feature
14th +5 Reinforcing Fortitude
15th +5 Steel Endurance
16th +5 Ability Score Improvement
17th +6 Mountain Stance
18th +6 Specialization Feature
19th +6 Ability Score Improvement
20th +6 Adamantine Endurance

Class Features

As a Bulwark, you gain the following class features.

Hit Points

Hit Dice: 1d10 per bulwark level

Hit Points at 1st Level: 10 + your constitution modifier

Hit Points at Higher Levels: 1d10 (or 6) + your constitution modifier per Bulwark level after first.

Proficiencies

Armor: Light, Medium, and Heavy Armor, Shields

Weapons: Simple Weapons, Warhammers, Heavy Crossbows

Tools: none

Saving Throws: Constitution and Charisma

Skills: Choose two from Animal Handling, Athletics, Insight, Intimidation, Medicine, Persuasion, and Religion

Equipment

You start with the following equipment, in addition to any equipment granted by your background:

  • (a) a warhammer or (b) a simple weapon of your choice and a shield
  • A suit of chainmail armor
  • (a) an explorer’s pack or (b) a diplomat’s pack
  • (a) a light crossbow and 20 bolts or (b) a shortbow and 20 arrows

Defensive Stance

While you are wearing heavy armor, you can choose to take up a defensive stance to bolster yourself for incoming force. As an action, you can give yourself a +2 bonus to your armor class and resistance to force damage for 1 minute, or until you are no longer wearing heavy armor.

You can use this feature a number of times equal to your constitution modifier before completing a long rest.

Weapon Mastery

Your training with weapons allows you to use the mastery properties of two kinds of weapons of your choice that you have proficiency with, such as maces and light crossbows.

Whenever you finish a long rest, you can change the kinds of weapons you chose. For example, you could switch to using the mastery properties of warhammers and handaxes.

Fortitude

At 2nd level, you can lessen the impact of weapons against you. While you are wearing heavy armor, and are hit by a weapon attack, you can use your reaction to reduce the damage by an amount equal to your bulwark level.

Dueling Stance

Additionally at 2nd level, you radiate an aura that compels your foes to battle against you, and you alone. While your defensive stance is active, enemies that start their turn within 10 feet of you must make a charisma saving throw (DC 8 + your strength modifier + your proficiency bonus) or be forced to use their action to attack, or otherwise harm you.

Defensive Specialization

When you reach 3rd level, you choose a defensive specialization that dictates the types of strategies you employ to protect yourself and others.

  • Juggernaut
  • Phalanx
  • Rook
  • Spellbreaker
  • Unfettered
  • Templar

Your choice grants you features at 3rd level and again at 7th, 13th, and 18th level.

Ability Score Improvement

When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase two ability scores of your choice by one. As normal, you can’t increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.

Using the optional feats rule, you can forgo taking this feature to take a feat of your choice instead.

Extra Attack

Beginning at 5th level, you can attack twice instead of once whenever you take the attack action on your turn.

Emissary

Additionally at 5th level, your voice carries with you a supernatural sense of purpose and authority. You gain a bonus to all charisma (intimidation and persuasion) checks equal to your strength modifier (minimum bonus of +1).

Conditioning

At 6th level, you gain an uncanny knack for endurance. You no longer suffer the adverse effects of a forced march, and are treated as having two less levels of exhaustion than you normally would.

Dueling Draw

At 9th level, you become harder to ignore by those you are engaged with. Creatures have disadvantage on the saving throw against your Dueling Stance feature if you have dealt damage to them since the start of your last turn.

Mental Bastion

At 10th level, you gain the ability to harden your mind to attacks with a similar effectiveness as your armor can block physical blows. You gain proficiency in intelligence or wisdom saving throws (your choice). You can replace your selection with the other whenever you finish a long rest.

Shattering Stance

When you reach 11th level, you learn to redirect the energy meant for you back to your attacker. While your defensive stance is active, you deal extra damage equal to your proficiency bonus when you attack with a weapon. You can deal this extra damage only once per turn.

Reinforcing Fortitude

Starting at 14th level, your ability to shrug off attacks extends to even the mightiest of blows. When you use your Fortitude feature, you gain a number of temporary hit points equal to the amount of damage you prevented. Once you gain these temporary hit points, you cannot do so again until you finish a short rest, or enter a new defensive stance.

Steel Endurance

At 15th level, when you roll initiative and have no remaining uses of your defensive stance, you regain one use.

Mountain Stance

When you reach 17th level, your stance becomes as unbreakable as the very earth itself. While your defensive stance is active, you cannot be moved against your will, and you are immune to the frightened condition and critical hits.

Adamantine Endurance

At 20th level, the duration of your defensive stance increases to 10 minutes, and the bonus it confers to your armor class increases to +4.

Multiclassing

When multiclassing with the Bulwark class, use the following:

Prerequisite: Strength 13 and Constitution 13

Proficiencies Gained: Light armor, Medium armor, Shields, and Heavy armor

Homebrew / Classes

Channeler

Channeler

The Channeler Class

Clad in rusted armor with a fizzling blade in their right hand, a warrior strikes down their goblin foe with the crackling might of a bolt of lightning. Electricity arcs up and down their blade, converging on the tip and electrocuting its unassuming victim. Laughter echoes across the dank walls of a dungeon as an elf sits, cross-legged, amongst the bodies of her victims, eyes clouded by maddening power. Though her victims show little signs of external damage, their eyes roll up into their sockets, leaving behind only a white gleam. Snowflakes whiz across the air in a beautiful miniature blizzard, centered on a Dragonborn with scales as white as the snow surrounding him. Raising his twin daggers, he weaves together a pattern of rime and frost that leaves his enemies disoriented in a dazzling display of elemental prowess.

These individuals, regardless of origin, share one point in common; pure energy flows through their veins, seemingly bursting from their bodies with little control or conviction. Whether they’ve received this energy through a higher power’s blessing, an experiment gone terribly wrong, or were born as natural capacitors for magic, each of these individuals must quickly learn to channel their internal energy, else it burns them up from the inside.

A Channel for the Arcane Arts

A channeler is forced to learn to control their energy, as it can be dangerous to both themselves and others to leave it unmanaged and unchecked. How they choose to do so differs from channeler to channeler: some embrace the chaos caused by their energy, some try to hide it and seal it away as much as they can. Some notice the value of the power they hold and try to shape it to their whims, while others still allow their energy to shape themselves and their actions. Regardless of how they decide to use their power, there still comes the issue of channeling it in the first place.Channelers generally train their whole lives to control their energy, from the moment they receive it onwards. Particularly talented channelers might be able to channel their power into objects at will, though regardless of talent, mastery over their power requires hard work. What constitutes ‘mastery’, however, is different from channeler to channeler; some may tell you complete control represents mastery, while another may tell you that you’re not a master lest your mind and body are completely broken under the weight of your own might.

Imbued Weaponry

Most commonly, channelers use weapons to control their abilities. Channelers use the same martial training these swordsmen and soldiers use to visualize and concentrate their own energy. As martial warriors consider their weapons as extensions of their own body, it’s the easiest for channelers to use weapons as a focus. A trained channeler is as deft with a weapon as any other combatant, and can use their energy to amplify their combat abilities to their liking.

Creating a Channeler

As you’re making a channeler, you must take a few things into consideration; where did the source of their internal energy come from? Was it the result of a deal with a higher being? A curse put on them by a practiced mage? An artificer’s experiment on humanoid test subjects? These may have all been reasons for the extensive energy you find yourself containing. In addition, think about the method that you used to channel your energy. How you managed to circumvent your energy destroying you internally is just as important as how you managed to receive that energy in the first place.
