Class Features

As a channeler, you gain the following class features.

Hit Points

Hit Dice: 1d10 per channeler level

Hit Points at 1st Level: 10 + your Constitution Modifier

Hit Points at Higher Levels: 1d10 (or 6) + your

Constitution modifier per (your class) level after 1st.

Proficiencies

Armor: Light armor, medium armor

Weapons: Simple weapons, longswords, rapiers

Tools: None

Saving Throws: Constitution, Intelligence

Skills: Choose two from Acrobatics, Arcana, Athletics,

Insight, Intimidation, Investigation, Perception, and

Survival.

Equipment

You start with the following equipment, in addition to the equipment granted by your background:

  • (a) chain mail and a shield (if proficient) or (b) scale mail or (c) leather armor and 2 daggers
  • (a) a longsword or (b) a rapier or (c) a martial weapon (if proficient)
  • (a) a light crossbow and 20 bolts or (b) two handaxes
  • (a) a scholar’s pack or (b) an explorer’s pack

Spellcasting Ability

Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for your channeler spells. The way you channel your innate abilities relies greatly on your experience. You use your Intelligence whenever a spell refers to your spellcasting ability. In addition, you use your Intelligence modifier when setting the saving throw DC for a channeler spell you cast and when making an attack roll with one

Spell save DC = 8 + your Proficiency Bonus + your Intelligence modifier

Spell Attack modifier = your Proficiency Bonus + your Intelligence modifier

Arcane Channel

Choose one outlet in which to channel your energy. Your choice grants you certain features and proficiencies when you choose it at 1st level. It also grants you additional features at 6th, 11th, and 17th level. The choices are detailed at the bottom of this document.

  • Channel of Artistry
  • Channel of Madness
  • Channel of Volatility
  • Channel of Containment
  • Channel of Devastation

Elemental Imbuement

Your arcane energy is beginning to leak uncontrollably, forcing you to find a focus to channel it through. Starting at 1st level, whenever you finish a long rest, you can imbue your energy in one weapon you are proficient with. Choose a damage type from acid, fire, cold, lightning, or thunder. The weapon deals an additional 1d4 damage of the chosen type. This damage increases when you reach certain levels in this class: to 1d6 at 10th level, and to 1d8 at 17th level.

When an effect would deal damage using your Elemental Imbuement die, the damage type is the same as your Elemental Imbuement unless stated otherwise.

Arcane Attraction

At 2nd level, your internal magical power tends to seek out various sources through which to channel itself to, allowing you to get a sense for what is magical and what’s not. As an action, you can sense the presence of magic in the area. Until the end of your next turn, you know the location of each source of magic within 30 feet of you— whether it’s a magic item, a spell, or a creature created by a spell. You know which kind of magic source it is, but you do not know the details of the source; you can’t tell the type of magic item, the specifics of the spell, or the kind of creature.

Once you use this feature, you cannot use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

Fighting Style

At 2nd level, you adopt a style of fighting as your specialty. Choose one of the following options. You can’t take a Fighting Style option more than once, even if something in the game lets you choose again.

Archery

You gain a +2 bonus to attack rolls you make with ranged weapons.

Dueling

When you are wielding a melee weapon in one hand and no other weapons, you gain a +2 bonus to damage rolls with that weapon.

Great Weapon Fighting

When you roll a 1 or 2 on a damage die for an attack you make with a melee weapon that you are wielding with two hands, you can reroll the die and must use the new roll, even if the new roll is a 1 or a 2. The weapon must have the two-handed or versatile property for you to gain this benefit.

Two-Weapon Fighting

When you engage in two-weapon fighting, you can add your ability modifier to the damage of the second attack.

Unarmed Fighting

Your unarmed strikes can deal bludgeoning damage equal to 1d6 + your Strength modifier on a hit. If you aren’t wielding any weapons or a shield when you make the attack roll, the d6 becomes a d8.

At the start of each of your turns, you can deal 1d4 bludgeoning damage to one creature grappled by you.

Ante

At 3rd level, your elemental energy burns and crackles within you, proving to be a fickle source of power. You can use the energy to empower yourself, but you run the risk of your power backfiring on you. You gain three Ante options of your choice, detailed at the bottom of this document. You gain another at 7th level, 12th level, and 17th level.

You have an amount of Ante charges equal to your Intelligence modifier. Each use of an Ante consumes a charge. You may not use more than one Ante at the same time. You replenish Ante charges on a short or long rest.

Additionally, when you gain a level in this class, you may replace one Ante option with another that you meet the prerequisites for. A level prerequisite refers to your level in this class.

Ability Score Improvement

When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can’t increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.

Overchanneled Imbuement

Starting at 5th level, you gain more control over the energy channeled through your weapon of choice. Whenever you finish a long rest, choose two cantrips that share a damage type with your chosen Elemental Imbuement and have a casting time of one action or bonus action. Immediately after you hit with an attack from your imbued weapon, you may cast one of the chosen cantrips as a bonus action. If a spell allows you to choose the damage type you deal, the chosen type must match your Elemental Imbuement.

At 9th level, you may choose two 1st level spells that share a damage type with your chosen Elemental Imbuement. You may cast either of those spells rather than a cantrip without expending a spell slot.

Elemental Boon

Starting at 7th level, your experience with channeling your energy through weapons is beginning to allow you to channel your energy through living beings as well. As a reaction whenever another ally within 30 feet hits with an attack roll, you can channel your energy through their attack. The attack deals bonus damage equal to your Elemental Imbuement die, and shares the damage type you’d chosen for your Elemental Imbuement.

You may use this feature a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier, and you regain all expended uses on a short or long rest.

Raze

Starting at 10th level, your imbued weapons are growing in destructive force, letting you use them to tear objects to shreds. Attacks made using your imbued weapons deal twice as much damage to objects and structures.

Up The Ante

Starting at 13th level, the power of your Antes grows, but so do their destructive effects. When you use an Ante, you may choose to Up The Ante, making you roll your Elemental Imbuement die an extra time, adding it to the effect. If the Ante cares about whether the total is even or odd, rather than adding the die an extra time, you instead may use either roll.

Once you use this feature, you must finish a short or long rest before you can use it again.

Flash Charge

At 14th level, you’ve learned to quickly and deftly control the elemental energies inside of you. Once per day, as an action, you may change the damage type of your Elemental Imbuement, as well as the spells you’d chosen for your Overchanneled Imbuement. You may optionally also choose to imbue your energy in a different weapon.

Greater Boon

At 15th level, the boons you bestow upon others strengthen to their peak. The elemental boon now deals extra damage equal to twice your Elemental Imbuement die, and the attack ignores damage resistances.

Ruin

At 18th level, your magic energies can bring down the very foundations of structures around you. By spending one minute concentrating as if concentrating on a spell, you can plunge your imbued weapon into the ground and begin breaking the foundations of nearby buildings.

Once one minute has passed, choose a non-magical object or structure within 60 feet. If that structure can fit within a 30 foot cube, it is immediately destroyed, crumbling to dust. If it is any larger, you can instead destroy a 30 foot cube portion of it within range.

Pinnacle Channel

At 20th level, you’ve reached the height of elemental control, and can display your mastery on a consistent basis. At the end of a long rest, choose two 2nd or 3rd level spells that share a damage type with your Elemental Imbuement; you may cast those spells at will or any time you can cast one of your Overchanneled Imbuements.

If you use your Flash Charge feature, you may also exchange these spells for any others that fit the prerequisites. Additionally, you may upcast your 1st and 2nd level channelers spells to 3rd level.

Antes

Antes are a core part of a channeler’s toolkit, and are the representation of their capricious magic. Each ante provides some sort of benefit to you that can help you accomplish certain tasks or utilize certain abilities, but every single one runs the risk of backfiring, leading to inconvencience, injury, or even certain death.

A good channeler knows when to use an ante and when not to take needless risks, but each and every channeler would do well to understand that no matter how many steps one might take to mitigate risk, chances of failure are never zero.

Pinpoint Ante

When you make an attack roll, you may add your Elemental Imbuement die to it. If the attack misses, your AC decreases by an amount equal to the Elemental Imbuement die’s result until the end of your next turn.

Reflex Ante

When you make a dexterity saving throw, you may add your Elemental Imbuement die to the save. If the save fails, you take damage equal to twice the Elemental Imbuement die’s result.

Prodigious Ante

When you make a skill check in a skill you’re not proficient in, you may add your Elemental Imbuement die to the check. If the check fails, you subtract the Elemental Imbuement die’s result from all ability checks for the next hour.

Quickstep Ante

When someone makes an opportunity attack against you, you may add your Elemental Imbuement die to your AC. If the attack hits, your speed is reduced by five times the result until the end of your turn.

Blasting Ante (Prerequisite: Channel of Devastation)

When you make an attack roll, you may roll your Elemental Imbuement die. If the attack hits, each creature of your choice other than the target within 15 feet takes damage equal to the result. If the attack misses, each creature other than the target within 15 feet of you takes damage equal to the result.

Mindmeld Ante (Prerequisite: Channel of Madness)

When a creature makes a saving throw against a channeler spell you cast, you may subtract your Elemental Imbuement die from the save. If the save succeeds, you become the spell’s target, and your saving throw against the spell’s effect is reduced by your Elemental Imbuement die’s result. If the spell would require you to concentrate, it doesn’t require concentration when cast against you.

Curtain-raiser Ante (Prerequisite: Channel of Artistry)

When you roll initiative, you may add your Elemental Imbuement die to the result. If you’re in the top half of initiative, you have advantage on attack rolls against each creature below you in the initiative order until the end of your next turn. If you’re in the bottom half of initiative, each creature above you in initiative has advantage on attack rolls against you until the end of your next turn.

Unstable Ante (Prerequisite: Channel of Volatility)

Before you make an attack roll, call if the result will be even or odd. If the result matches your guess, add another Elemental Imbuement die to your Volatile Charge feature. If the results don’t match your guess, you take damage equal to one roll of your Elemental Imbuement die.

Fray Ante (Prerequisite: Channel of Containment)

If you’re within 5 feet of an enemy, roll your Elemental Imbuement die. If the result is even, you regain hit points equal to three times the roll’s result. If the result is odd, your AC decreases by the roll’s result.

Arcane Ante (Prerequisite: 5th Level)

Whenever you cast a channeler spell, you may use this Ante. If the spell hits or if the target fails the save against it, you may add two rolls of your Elemental Imbuement die to that spell’s damage. If the spell misses or the target passes the save, you take damage equal to one roll of your Elemental Imbuement die.

Reactive Ante (Prerequisite: 5th Level)

Whenever an attack roll is made against you, you may use this Ante as a reaction. Roll your Elemental Imbuement die; if the result is even, you gain immunity to the triggering attack’s damage until the end of the turn. If the result is odd, you gain vulnerability to the triggering attack’s damage until the end of the turn.

Goading Ante (Prerequisite: 7th Level, Channel of Devastation)

When a creature rolls a saving throw against your Devastating Presence feature, you may force them to subtract your Elemental Imbuement die from the result. If they succeed, they add the Elemental Imbuement die’s result to their attack and damage rolls that target you until the end of their turn.

Headspin Ante (Prerequisite: 7th Level, Channel of Madness)

If a creature within 30 feet of you rolls an Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma saving throw with advantage, you may add your Elemental Imbuement die to the result. If they fail the save, you subtract the Elemental Imbuement die’s result from your saving throws for the next minute.

Blitzkrieg Ante (Prerequisite: 7th Level, Channel of Artistry)

If you make an attack roll against a creature, you may roll your Elemental Imbuement die. If you hit, your speed increases by an amount equal to five times the result until the end of your turn. If you miss, you fall prone and your speed is reduced by an amount equal to five times the result until the end of your turn.

Surge Ante (Prerequisite: 7th Level, Channel of Volatility)

After you roll on the Volatile Surge table, you may use this ante. Roll your Elemental Imbuement die and call if the result will be odd or even. If you guess correctly, you may use the effects of both the new and the old roll. If you guess incorrectly, you may use neither effect.

Grasp Ante (Prerequisite: 7th Level, Channel of Containment)

When you make a Strength (athletics) check to grapple a creature, you can add your Elemental Imbuement die to the check’s result. If the creature succeeds against the grapple, you are restrained until the start of your next turn.

Mental Ante (Prerequisite: 11th Level)

When you make an Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma saving throw, you may reduce the result by your Elemental Imbuement die. If you pass the save, you may add the Elemental Imbuement die’s result to the failed saving throw of a creature of your choice within 60 feet of you.

Proactive Ante (Prerequisite: 11th Level)

Whenever an attack roll is made against a creature other than you within 60 feet, you may use this Ante as a reaction. Roll your Elemental Imbuement die; if the result is even, they gain resistance to the triggering attack’s damage until the end of the turn. If the result is odd, you take damage equal to the triggering attack’s damage.

Sticky Ante (Prerequisite: 13th Level, Channel of Devastation)

You may use this Ante at the start of a creature’s turn. If the creature ends their turn within 5 feet of you, they take damage equal to three rolls of your Elemental Imbuement die. If the creature ends their turn more than 5 feet away from you, you take force damage equal to three rolls of your Elemental Imbuement die.

Hivemind Ante (Prerequisite: 13th Level, Channel of Madness)

When a creature you can see within 60 feet of you makes a saving throw or ability check that they’re not proficient in, if you’re proficient in that saving throw or ability check, you can roll your Elemental Imbuement die and add the result to their roll. If they fail, you take force damage equal to three times the result.

Haphephobic Ante (Prerequisite: 13th Level, Channel of Artistry)

When you hit with an attack roll, you may roll your Elemental Imbuement die. If the target damages you before the start of your next turn, you take force damage equal to five times the result. If the target does not damage you before the start of your next turn, they take damage equal to five times the result.

Anti-Ante (Prerequisite: 13th Level, Channel of Volatility)

You may use this ante immediately after using another ante. Roll your Elemental Imbuement die; if the result is even, neither this Ante nor that Ante consumes an Ante charge. If the result is odd, you lose one Ante charge.

Stance Ante (Prerequisite: 13th Level, Channel of Containment)

When a creature hits you with an attack, roll a concentration check and add your Elemental Imbuement die. If the check succeeds, you gain resistance to the attack’s damage. If the check fails, you gain vulnerability to the attack’s damage.

Gambler’s Ante (Prerequisite: 18th Level)

When you use your last Ante charge, you may roll your Elemental Imbuement die; If the result is even, you regain an amount of Ante charges equal to the roll. This amount cannot exceed your maximum. If the result is odd, your hit point total is set to 1. You may only use this Ante once per long rest.

God Ante (Prerequisite: 18th Level)

You may use this Ante as an action. Roll your Elemental Imbuement die; if the result is even, you may immediately cast a ninth level spell with a casting time of one action from any spell list without expending a spell slot. If the result is odd, you die and cannot be revived except by the effects of a wish spell. You may only use this Ante once per long rest.

Warmind Ante (Prerequisite: 20th Level, Channel of Devastation)

When you make a melee weapon attack, you may roll your Elemental Imbuement die. Up to that many other willing creatures of your choice within 30 feet of you may make one melee weapon attack as a reaction. If any of them miss, each creature takes damage equal to five times the result.

InsanAnte (Prerequisite: 20th Level, Channel of Madness)

When you cast an enchantment spell on one or more creatures, you may roll your Elemental Imbuement die. If they fail the save, they take psychic damage equal to four times the result, and if any of them pass the save, you take force damage equal to four times the result.

Masterpiece Ante (Prerequisite: 20th Level, Channel of Artistry)

When you use your Flash Charge feature, roll your Elemental Imbuement die. The next time you cast a channeler spell, if it hits or if the spell’s target fails its save against it, you gain hit points and temporary hit points equal to three times the result. If it doesn’t hit or the target’s save is successful, you take damage equal to three times the result.

Soulshredder Ante (Prerequisite: 20th Level, Channel of Volatility)

When you use your Culmination of Volatility feature, you may roll your Elemental Imbuement die. If the result is even, rather than dying immediately, you regain half of your maximum hit points and your gear and equipment aren’t destroyed. If the result is odd, your soul is shredded into nonexistence and you cannot be revived by any means, even through divine intervention or a wish spell.

Havoc Ante (Prerequisite: 20th Level, Channel of Containment)

When you make an unarmed strike against a creature, they must make a strength saving throw against your spell save DC. Roll your Elemental Imbuement die and subtract it from the save. If they fail, they are knocked back a distance equal to ten times the die’s result. If they succeed, you are knocked back a distance equal to ten times the die’s result. The one knocked back by this effect takes 1d6 bludgeoning damage for every 10 feet they traveled.

Multiclassing

Ability Score Minimum: STR 13 or DEX 13, and INT 13

Armor: light armor, medium armor

Weapons: simple weapons, longswords, rapiers

Homebrew / Classes

Drifter

Drifter

Descriptions

Those that follow this path believe that rather than hard training, true mastery comes with application. Like a branch drifting across a river, such practitioners make do with what’s thrown at them, adapting to the issues they are faced with and prospering in the worst of conditions.

Thus, the Branch Drifts

At 2nd level, you find it easy to manipulate your techniques to fit their situations. As a bonus action, you can enter the flowing river stance for 1 minute, gaining the following benefits:

  • If you focus a technique, you can choose whether it’s a mental or physical type for you.
  • When you make a weapon attack with a technique, you can use your mental ability for attack and damage rolls rather than Strength or Dexterity.
  • If a creature fails its save against your technique, you can use a reaction to regain mastery points equal to half your maximum (rounded up). After you use this feature, you must take a short or long rest before you can use it again.

You can exit the flowing river stance as a bonus action. It ends early if you are incapacitated or if your turn ends and you haven’t used a technique since your last turn. You can enter the flowing river stance a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, regaining all uses on a long rest.

The Stone Remains Unmoved

At 6th level, you improve upon your ability to adapt to change. When you enter the flowing river stance, choose a damage type aside from bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing damage. You become resistant to that damage type until the flowing river stance ends.

A Fork in the River

At 14th level, you become adept at stringing techniques from different forms together. After spending mastery points to focus a technique while in the flowing river stance, you can use a bonus action to use another technique from a different martial form.

Laminar Flow

At 18th level, if you use three physical techniques or three mental techniques in a row, you gain a benefit:

Physical. The next time a creature hits you with an attack until the end of your next turn, you can use your reaction to make one weapon attack against them.

Mental. The next time you use a technique that forces a creature to make a save until the end of your next turn, they have disadvantage on that save.

Martial Form - Drifting River

Form 1: Floating Pebble

Type:

Varies

Prerequisites:

Novice, Drifter

Make a weapon attack against a creature or object. The attack deals an amount of d6s equal to your proficiency bonus in additional psychic damage if this technique is mental or bludgeoning damage if this technique is physical.

Focused (1 point, or 0 points if in flowing river stance). If the target is a creature, they must make a Constitution saving throw or have their speed halved until the end of their next turn. Your movement speed increases by the same amount until the end of your turn.

Form 2: Liquid Rebuttal

Type:

Varies

Prerequisites:

Intermediate, Drifter, Flowing river stance

If you take damage that matches the damage type you chose for your flowing river stance, you can use your reaction to become immune to that damage instead.

Focused (1 point). In the same reaction, you can use another technique that includes a weapon attack.

Form 3: Hyperfocus

Type:

Varies

Prerequisites:

Advanced, Drifter

The next technique you use from a different form until the end of your next turn can be focused with 1 less mastery point (min. 1)

Focused (1 point). The next technique you focus does not require mastery points, and once performed, you can immediately make a weapon attack against a creature or object.

Form 4: The River’s Song

Type:

Varies

Prerequisites:

Master, Drifter, Flowing river stance

Duration:

Concentration, 1 min.

If you use a physical or mental technique, you gain a benefit.

Physical. If you hit a creature with a weapon attack during this technique, they must succeed on a wisdom saving throw or be forced to use their action to make one melee weapon attack against you on their next turn.

Mental. When you hit a creature with a weapon attack during this technique, they must succeed on a Strength saving throw or be knocked prone.

Focused (1 point).

Whenever you use a physical or mental technique, it counts as if you had used three physical or three mental techniques respectively.

Homebrew / Classes

Exorcist

Exorcist

Exorcists use their spiritual abilities to purge the lands of evil spirits and those that would do harm to society. With pure souls and unmatched bravery, they face the most vile of creation head-on.

Horror Hunter

At 3rd level, you become adept in tracking down and hunting all manners of evil. You gain proficiency in Investigation and Survival, and undead and fiends have disadvantage on saving throws against your exorcist arts.

If the target of your spirit tether is a creature and is reduced to 0 hit points, you can regain a number of spirit points equal to half your spiritualist level (rounded down). If the target was an undead or a fiend, you regain additional spirit points equal to your wisdom modifier. Once you use this feature, you must finish a short or long rest before you can use it again.

Exorcist Arts

Also at 3rd level, you gain access to new spirit arts that reflect your power over evil forces.

Spirit Leash

If your tethered target is a creature, you can use your action to spend 1 spirit point to root your target in place. The target must make a strength saving throw or be restrained for one minute and take 2d6 radiant damage at the start of each of its turns. A target can repeat this saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending this effect on a success.

Radiant Lash

You can use an action and spend 1 spirit point to lash out at your target with your righteous spirit. The target must make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failure, the target takes 4d6 radiant damage, taking half of the damage on a success.

Spirit Flare

You can use an action and spend 1 spirit point to cover your target in radiant light. The target must make a Charisma saving throw or be covered in an aura of light that emits bright sunlight for 30 feet and dim light for another 30 feet. When the target fails its saving throw against your radiant lash while this sunlight persists, you can blind them until the end of its next turn.

Exorcize

At 6th level, you can use an action to exorcise creatures of your choice that you can see within 60 feet of yourself. For each creature, you can spend 1 spirit point to end one effect that’s causing the creature to be charmed, frightened, or possessed.

Cleansing Field

At 13th level, you can cleanse an area and temporarily ward it from evil. As an action, you can spend 3 spirit points to create a field in a 20-foot-radius sphere at a point you can see within 120 feet of yourself. The area becomes pure, and creatures of your choice within the area cannot be frightened, charmed, or possessed, and have advantage on Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma saving throws. The field lasts for one minute, whereupon its cleansing abilities fade and its effects end.

Master Exorcist

At 18th level, you master your abilities to drive evil from this world. You learn the following spirit art:

True Banishment

You can use 10 minutes of chanting and 20 spirit points to attempt to banish a creature from existence. At the end of the ten minutes, the target must make a Charisma saving throw or be banished. Regardless of the target’s native plane, they are banished to an empty and infinite demiplane that is accessible by nothing less than a god. It is impossible for the creature to leave the demiplane from the inside by any means. While banished, the target does not need to breathe, eat, or sleep, and it doesn’t age. Divination spells can’t locate or perceive the target.

You can spend 10 minutes to bring a banished creature back from its banishment. If you’re within 30 feet of the location the target was originally banished from, you can bring them back to a point you can see within 30 feet of you.

Homebrew / Classes

Greaser

Greaser

Description:

Since the dawn of humanity, there has always been a frontier to conquer. Between the wastes of the east, the fires of the hells, and the vastness of the astral plane, there has always been those that dared to tread the road less traveled. Traversing each regional obstacle brings with it a unique solution— the hellfire engines of Avernus, the spelljammers of the astral sea, and the machinations inspired by the great inventor Kwalish, all formed to blaze a trail through every path they come across.

Through the use of arcane influence and artificing prowess, a new school of thought has arisen among artificers; why spend your days walking through the most hazardous conditions when you can drive, sail, or fly through them instead? Thus, under the influence of vehicles from all different planes, the most ingenious of traveling artificers got to work.

Features:

  • 3rd Level - Bonus Proficiency
  • 3rd Level - Greaser Spells
  • 3rd Level - Arcane Vehicle
  • 5th Level - Extra Attack
  • 9th Level - Enhanced Modifications
  • 15th Level - Overdrive

3rd Level - Bonus Proficiency

When you adopt this specialization at 3rd level, you gain proficiency with smith’s tools. If you already have this proficiency, you gain proficiency with one other type of artisan’s tools of your choice. In addition, you gain proficiency in land and water vehicles

3rd Level - Greaser Spells

Starting at 3rd level, you always have certain spells prepared after you reach particular levels in this class, as shown in the Greaser Spells table. These spells count as artificer spells for you, but they don’t count against the number of artificer spells you prepare.

Artificer Level Spells

3rd Level - Burning Hands, Fog Cloud

5th Level - Locate Object, Dust Devil

9th Level - Slow, Stinking Cloud

13th Level - Hallucinatory Terrain, Sickening Radiance

17th Level - Passwall, Rary's Telepathic Bond

3rd Level - Arcane Vehicle

By 3rd level, you’ve successfully managed to create your first vehicle for traversal. At the end of a long rest, you may create a vehicle by choosing one of each of the following vehicle mod options below. The vehicle is a large magical object that can be mounted as if it were a creature, after which it acts as a controlled mount. It shares its turn with you, and can only take the dash and disengage actions. It is immune to psychic damage and uses your saving throw bonuses when applicable.

If the mending spell is cast on it, it regains 2d6 hit points. If it has been destroyed within the last hour, you can use your smith’s tools as an action to repair it, provided you are within 5 feet of it and you expend a spell slot of 1st level or higher. The vehicle returns to working order after 1 minute with half of its hit points restored.

At the end of a long rest, you can create a new arcane vehicle if you have your smith’s tools with you. If you already have an arcane vehicle from this feature, the first one is immediately destroyed. The vehicle is also destroyed if you die.

Vehicle Mods

Each vehicle can only have one vehicle mod of each option listed below active at one time. At the end of a short rest, you can use your smith’s tools to replace one vehicle mod of your choosing with another eligible of the same category. If a vehicle mod has prerequisites, you must meet them to learn it. A level prerequisite refers to your level in this class.

Vehicle Frame

Frame Type | Level | Speed | Hit Points | AC

  • Trailblazer| N/A | 60ft.| 5 x artificer level | 13 + PB
  • Seafarer | 5th level | 10ft., swim 50ft. | 4 x artificer level"\t"| 12 + PB
  • Cloudstrider | 9th level | 0ft., fly 40ft. | 3 x artificer level | 11 + PB

Vehicle Archetype

Archetype | Prerequisite | Details

  • Assault | N/A | The vehicle’s maximum hit points increase by 2 x artificer level.
  • Transport | N/A | The vehicle can hold up to 500lbs of items in a 5ft. cube of space.
  • Transit | 5th level | The vehicle’s speed increases by 10ft.

Mounted Weapon

Weapon | Prerequisite | Details

  • Skewer | N/A | Melee. The skewer deals 1d6 piercing damage for every 10ft. of movement used immediately before the attack, up to 3d6 piercing damage.
  • Glob Launcher | N/A | Ranged (60/120). The glob launcher deals 1d10 bludgeoning damage. A creature hit by this weapon has its movement speed reduced by 10ft. until the end of its turn.
  • Gas Sprayer | 5th level |15ft. cone. Creatures in the area must make a Constitution save against your spell save DC or take 2d8 poison damage and be poisoned until the end of their next turn.
  • Bombard | 9th level | Ranged (30/60). The bombard deals 2d6 fire damage. When you hit with an attack, all creatures within 5ft. of the target must succeed on a Dexterity save or take 2d6 fire damage.
  • Sol Spear | 15th level | Ranged (40/80.) The sol spear does 1d8 radiant damage. The first creature hit by the spear each turn must succeed on a Constitution save or be blinded until the end of its next turn.

Weapons mounted on your vehicle are simple weapons you are proficient in that can only be used by yourself while you are mounted. If the weapon requires an attack roll, you can add your Intelligence modifier, instead of your Strength or Dexterity, to the attack and damage rolls. Use your spell save DC for any saving throw related to your weapon. These weapons can be infused.

Specialized Modification

Mod | Prerequisite | Details

  • Bladed Edge |N/A| Creatures you move within 5ft of take 5 slashing damage. A creature can only take this damage once per turn.
  • Seatbelts | N/A |You automatically succeed on any checks you make to remain mounted.
  • Improved Treading | 5th level | Your vehicle’s movement ignores difficult terrain.
  • Sealed Cockpit | 5th level | You ignore the effects of extreme heat and extreme cold while mounted on your vehicle, and have access to a constant supply of fresh air.
  • Overtuned Engine | 9th level | The vehicle’s speed increases by 20ft.
  • Grappling Hook | 9th level | You can use an action to launch a grappling hook attached to a chain up to 50ft. away.
  • Heavy Shielding | 9th level | You have half cover while riding your vehicle.
  • Self-Repair Module | 15th level | If your vehicle has lower than half of its maximum hit points, it regains 5 hit points at the start of each of your turns. |Drop Compartments|15th level|Adds six small compartments that can each release their contents (such as caltrops/ball bearings) on the ground within 5ft. of the vehicle as a bonus action.

5th Level - Extra Attack

Beginning at 5th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn. Additionally, attacks from your mounted weapons count as magical for the purposes of overcoming resistance and immunity to nonmagical attacks and damage.

9th Level - Enhanced Modifications

At 9th level, you’re able to fit more modifications on your vehicle. You may now have two specialized modifications and two mounted weapons active at once.

15th Level - Overdrive

At 15th level, you learn to overclock your vehicle to force it to perform past its peak temporarily. As a bonus action, you can send your vehicle into overdrive for one minute. Doing so doubles its movement speed, makes it immune to all damage, and allows you to make up to three attacks with your mounted weapon each turn. At the end of the minute, your vehicle is immediately destroyed. You must finish a long rest to use this feature again, unless you spend a spell slot of 5th level or higher to use it again.

Homebrew / Classes

Harbinger

Harbinger

Harbingers are foretellers of death and destruction, serving as a warning for disaster and ruin. Oftentimes, they take it upon themselves to cause the catastrophes themselves.

For Whom the Bell Tolls

At 3rd level, you learn the toll the dead and sacred flame cantrips, which counts as a spiritualist cantrip for you. When you cast a spiritualist cantrip, the DC is equal to your Art save DC.

Whenever you activate your spirit tether, the target has disadvantage on the saving throw against spiritualist cantrips you cast until the end of your turn.

Harbinger Arts

Also at 3rd level, you gain access to new spirit arts that reflect your penchant for bringing about tragedy.

Mark of Suffering

As an action, you can spend 1 spirit point to attempt to imbue your target with a Suffering mark. The target must make a Wisdom saving throw or be marked and take 2d6 necrotic damage.

Whenever you cast a spiritualist cantrip on the marked target, you may trigger this spirit art’s effect again without spending spirit points.

Mark of Ruination

As an action, you can spend 1 spirit point to attempt to imbue your target with a Ruination mark. The target must make an Intelligence saving throw or be marked and subtract 1d6 from each saving throw it makes against your harbinger arts or spiritualist cantrips until the end of its next turn.

Whenever you cast a spiritualist cantrip on the marked target, you may trigger this spirit art’s effect again without spending spirit points.

Mark of Tragedy

As an action, you can spend 1 spirit point to attempt to imbue your target with a Tragedy mark. The target must make a Charisma saving throw or take 1d6 psychic damage each time it attacks or casts a spell until the end of its next turn.

Whenever you cast a spiritualist cantrip on the marked target, you may trigger this spirit art’s effect again without spending spirit points.

Enervating Marks

At 6th level, whenever the target of your spiritualist cantrips has a Suffering, Ruination, and Tragedy mark, you can add an additional 2 damage dice to the cantrip’s damage roll.

The Ninth Bell Tolls True

At 13th level, you find new ways of inflicting woe upon foes. The damage from your Suffering and Tragedy marks increase by 2d6.

In addition, when a target fails its saving throw against one of your marks, you can consume the mark. The mark is removed from the target, and you regain 2d6 hit points.

Master Harbinger

At 18th level, you master your prowess at bestowing tribulation. You learn the following spirit art:

Mark of Calamity

As an action, you can spend 5 spirit points to imbue your target with a Calamity mark. The target must make a Constitution saving throw or be marked, taking 4d6 force damage and suffering one level of exhaustion.

Whenever you cast a spiritualist cantrip on the marked target, you may trigger this spirit art’s effect again without spending spirit points. This mark can count as a Suffering, Ruination, or Tragedy mark for the purposes of satisfying the requirements of your enervating marks feature, but only one of the three at a time.

Homebrew / Classes

Jade Lord

Jade Lord

Throughout the continent of kara-tur, one mineral stands above all else in terms of status. Where in the west you would display decadence with gold, in the east, the truest symbol of power is jade. Legends tell of warriors embellished with regality, often proud in status and seeped in regality. The Jade Lords of Shou Lung were legendary figures that displayed power and wealth in equal measure, fighting with both honor and flair.

Regal Countenance

Even at 3rd level, you carry yourself with grace and nobility. You gain proficiency in either Persuasion or Intimidation. If you already have both of those proficiencies, you can choose a different proficiency instead.

Jade Shards

At 3rd level, the gutteral flow of combat splinters jade around you. When you hit a creature with a weapon attack or a creature hits you with an attack, a jade shard splinters off of you and orbits you for the duration. You can only have a number of jade shards equal to half your fighter level (rounded up) at a time. When initiative ends, any remaining jade shards drop to the floor and disappear.

You can expend any number of these shards to take special actions called jade tricks. If the trick requires the target to make a saving throw, the DC is calculated as follows:

Jade Trick DC

= 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Strength or Dexterity modifier (your choice)

If you’re able to make multiple attacks with the Attack action, a trick replaces one of them. You can only use a trick once per attack action.

Jade Blade.

Make a melee attack with a melee weapon you are holding against a target within range. On a hit, the target suffers the weapon attack’s normal effects and takes a number of d6s in additional damage equal to the amount of shards spent.

Nephrite Burst.

Make a ranged or thrown weapon attack (your choice) against a target within 120 feet of you. The attack deals a number of d8s of piercing damage equal to the amount of shards spent.

Jadeite Blast.

Choose a point you can see within 60 feet of you. Creatures within 10 feet of that point must make a Dexterity saving throw or take a number of d10s in slashing damage equal to the jade shards spent.

Mystic Stone

At 7th level, the jade you create is fortified. Damage from jade tricks count as magical for the purposes of overcoming resistance and immunity to non-magical damage.

Jade Armor

At 10th level, you learn to pull in the jade shards orbiting you to use as armor. As a bonus action, you can expend any number of jade shards to create jade armor. While this armor is active, you have half cover, or 3/4ths cover if you spent five or more shards. This armor lasts for a number of rounds equal to the jade shards spent or until the end of initiative.

Verdant Generosity

At 15th level, you are able to protect allies with your jade armor as well. If any ally is attacked or is forced to roll a saving throw, you can use your reaction to expend any amount of jade shards and encase them in jade armor. This armor confers the same amount of cover as your jade armor feature, but only lasts until the end of that ally’s next turn.

Jade Emperor

At 18th level, you learn a new jade trick.

Jadestorm.

By expending any amount of jade shards, you can create a jadestorm around you in a 20 foot radius, designating any creatures you wish to be unaffected by it. The storm travels with you, with its area being lightly obscured. An affected creature that begins its turn within the jadestorm takes bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage equal to the shards expended. Additionally, their AC is reduced by half the expended amount (rounded down) until the start of their next turn or until they leave the jadestorm. The jadestorm lasts for the expended amount of rounds or until the end of initiative.

Homebrew / Classes

Juggernaut

Juggernaut

Description

While in many cases using heavier two-handed weapons would put the user at a disadvantage defensively, Juggernauts utilize this augment to their offensive capabilities to compliment their defenses with little tradeoff.

Features:

  • 3rd Level - Martial Training
  • 3rd Level - Defensive Battering
  • 5th Level - Crushing Force
  • 13th Level - Demolishing Stance
  • 18th Level - Raw Terror

3rd Level - Martial Training

When you select this specialization at 3rd level, you gain proficiency in martial weapons.

3rd Level - Defensive Battering

Additionally at 3rd level, you have the ability to use larger weapons to block and deflect incoming attacks. While you are wielding a weapon with two hands, you gain a +1 bonus to your armor class.

7th Level - Crushing Force

Starting at 7th level, the sheer force you deliver with your attacks is enough to shatter your foe’s defenses. When you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can reduce the effectiveness of their armor, if they are wearing any, reducing their armor class by 3. Shields, and armor created by spells or other magic are unaffected, and you cannot reduce a creature’s armor class below what it would be without armor. This reduction lasts until the end of the creature’s next turn.

13th Level - Demolishing Stance

When you reach 13th level, your martial capability reaches new heights in conjunction with your defenses. While your defensive Stance is active, you gain a bonus to damage rolls with weapons equal to the armor class bonus given to you by your stance.

18th Level - Raw Terror

At 18th level, your very presence strikes terror into your foes. While your defensive stance is active, you can use a bonus action to force each creature of your choice within 30 feet of you to make a wisdom saving throw (DC 8 + your strength modifier + your proficiency bonus) or be frightened of you for one minute. An affected creature can repeat this save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a successful save. Once you use this feature, you cannot do so again until you take up a new defensive stance.

Homebrew / Classes

Justiciar

Justiciar

Description

The oath was never the end of it. It was the apprenticeship.

Prerequisites: Paladin 20

As a Justiciar, you gain the following features.

Proficiencies

You gain proficiency in two skills of your choice from the Paladin skill list.

Ascendant Spellcasting

Additionally when you take this prestige class, you gain an increased capacity for spellcasting. You now use half your prestige level (rounded up) on the generic spellcaster level table when determining the amount of spell slots you have available. When you prepare spells for the day, you may now prepare a number of spells equal to half your prestige level + your Charisma modifier.

When preparing spells, you now have access to the Cleric spell list for your 6th- to 9th-level spells. You must have spell slots of the spell's level in order to prepare it as normal.

Righteous Cantrip

At 21st level, you learn one cantrip of your choice from the Cleric spell list. These cantrips count as Paladin/Justiciar spells for you, and Charisma is your spellcasting ability for them.

Divine Sense II

At 21st level, you gain twice the number of uses of your Divine Sense feature.

Lay on Hands II

At 21st level, your blessed touch can heal wounds better than before. Your pool of healing power is instead a total number that is now equal to your prestige level x 5.

As an action, you can touch a creature and draw power from that pool to restore a number of hit points to that creature, up to a maximum amount remaining in your pool. When expending the last point in your healing pool to do so, it will heal that creature by the maximum number of hit dice that creature has. Additionally, in exchange for one of your attacks during an Attack action you may use Lay on Hands targeting yourself only; doing it this way takes 2 points per 1 hit point healed.

Alternatively, you can expend 5 hit points from your pool of healing to cure the target of one disease or neutralize one poison affecting it. You can cure multiple diseases and neutralize multiple poisons with a single use of Lay on Hands II, expending hit points separately for each one.

Alternatively, you can expend 10 hit points from your pool of healing to cure the target of one condition affecting it. You can cure multiple conditions with a single use of Lay on Hands, expending hit points separately for each one.

Alternatively, you can expend 20 points to remove 1 level of exhaustion from a willing creature.

Godly Smite

Starting at 22nd level, this feature replaces your Paladin's 2nd-level Divine Smite feature.

When you hit a creature with a melee weapon attack, you can expend one spell slot to deal radiant damage to the target, in addition to the weapon's damage. The extra damage is now 3d8 for a 1st-level spell slot, plus 1d8 for each spell level higher than 1st, to a maximum of 8d8. The damage increases by 3d8 if the target is an undead or a fiend, to a maximum of 11d8.

This feature counts as Divine Smite for prerequisites and interactions with other class or subclass features.

Everlasting Oath

When you reach 23rd level, you reaffirm your prior oath and swear another oath that binds you as a Justiciar forever. Up to this time, you have been faithfully carrying out your former oath. Now you rededicate yourself to your former oath, and swear another paladin's oath. Choose from the list of available oaths.

Your choice grants you features at 23rd, 27th, 35th, and 40th level.

Divine Health II

By 23rd level, the divine magic flowing through you makes you immune to the Poisoned condition and grants you resistance to poison damage.

Channel Divinity

At 23rd level, you gain one additional use of your Channel Divinity per rest.

Ability Score Improvement

When you reach 24th level, you gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at Justiciar levels 28, 32, 36, and 39.

Extra Attack (3)

At 25th level, you can attack three times instead of twice whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

Aura of the Guardian

At 26th level, the range of your Aura of the Guardian extends to 40 feet.

Aura Expansion

At 27th level, the range of all your Paladin subclass auras extends to 40 feet.

Aura of Bravery

At 30th level, creatures retain the effects of your Aura of Courage for 1 round after leaving it.

At 38th level, this extends to 1 minute after leaving your aura.

Improved Divine Smite II

By 31st level, you are so suffused with righteous might that all your melee weapon strikes carry divine power with them. Whenever you hit a creature with a melee weapon, the creature takes an extra 2d10 radiant damage instead of 1d8.

Warding Touch

At 34th level, you can, as a reaction, reflect 1st- and 2nd-level spells back at their caster for a charge of Cleansing Touch. For each additional charge used, this increases the maximum level by 2, up to a maximum of 8th level. This use of Cleansing Touch is a reaction.

You may now use your Cleansing Touch feature as a bonus action, and you gain a number of uses of that feature equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of one).

Aura Improvements II

At 38th level, extend the range of any and all auras from your Paladin/Justiciar class, or its subclasses, to 50 feet.

Avatar State

At 40th level, when you activate one of your 20th-level subclass features that requires activation, you may also activate your other 20th-level subclass feature (should it require activation). Both last for the longer of the two features' durations.

Medic

Medic

Description

You master the physician's arts, gaining the following benefits:

  • Increase your Wisdom score by 1, to a maximum of 20.
  • You gain proficiency in the Medicine skill. If you are already proficient in the skill, you add double your proficiency bonus to checks you make with it.
  • During a short rest, you can clean and bind the wounds of up to six willing beasts, fey, and humanoids. Make a DC 15 Wisdom (Medicine) check for each creature. On a success, if a creature spends a Hit Die during this rest, that creature can forgo the roll and instead regain the maximum number of hit points the die can restore. A creature can do so on a number of Hit Dice equal to half your Wisdom modifier, regardless of how many Hit Dice it spends.
Homebrew / Classes

Medium

Medium

Mediums are the bridge between life and death, often treading over the gap between the two. They call forth spirits of the past, using them for power and knowledge.

Seance

At 3rd level, you are able to tap into knowledge from spirits that you know of. You learn speak with dead and can cast it only as if it were a ritual spell. Rather than targeting a corpse, you can speak the name of a deceased individual who died within 1 mile. If their soul is able, they can choose to manifest in an empty space within 5 feet of you and answer your questions.

Once a soul is manifested in this way, you can’t manifest the same soul again for 24 hours.

Medium Arts

Also at 3rd level, you gain access to new spirit arts that reflect your capacity to channel souls.

Channel Warrior

As an action, you can spend 1 spirit point to channel the spirit of a warrior. The spirit manifests as a spectral fighter that is always 5 feet away from your target. Whenever you activate your spirit tether, you can have the warrior strike at the target in the same action. The target must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or take 2d6 force damage. If you use this spirit art again on the same target, you can channel another warrior, up to a maximum of 3 total. Each new warrior increases the force damage dealt to the target by an extra 2d6.

Channel Trickster

As an action, you can spend 1 spirit point to channel the spirit of a trickster. The spirit manifests in the form of an imp, fairy, or any other tricky creature that is always 5 feet away from your target. Whenever you activate your spirit tether, you can have the trickster distract at the target in the same action. The target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or have disadvantage on attack rolls and Perception checks until the end of its next turn.

Channel Guardian

As an action, you can spend 1 spirit point to channel the spirit of a guardian. The spirit manifests as an ancestor, patron, or angel that is always within 5 feet of you. Whenever you activate your spirit tether, the guardian bestows 1d6 temporary hit points to you. If you use this spirit art again, you can channel another guardian, up to a maximum of 3 total. Each new guardian increases the temporary hit points gained by an extra 1d6.

Eternal Spirit

At 6th level, your frequent interactions with other spirits has strengthened your own considerably. The range of your spirit tether increases to 300 feet. In addition, if

your tether breaks while you have at least one active spirit art, you regain one spirit point.

Claircognizance

At 13th level, by drawing upon the experiences of the dead, you become temporarily able to utilize their skills. If you make a skill check in any skill you’re not proficient in, you can spend a spirit point to add your proficiency bonus to the roll. You can use this feature after the roll is made, but only before you know the results.

Master Medium

At 18th level, you master your influence over the souls of others. You learn the following spirit art:

Possession

If your target is a creature, you can use an action and spend 5 spirit points to attempt to possess them temporarily. The target must succeed on a Charisma saving throw or be possessed by you for a minute. During this time, your soul is transferred into the target’s form, and your original body is left paralyzed. You now control the body but you don’t deprive the target of awareness. You use the possessed target’s statistics, but you retain your alignment, Wisdom, Intelligence, and Charisma. You don’t gain access to the target’s knowledge, class features, or proficiencies.

You may end the possession at any time, upon which you return to your body without harm. At the end of each of their turns, the target can repeat the Charisma save, ending the possession on a success. If the target dies while you possess it, your soul is returned to your body without harm. However, if your body dies while possessing the target, the possession ends and you die.

Homebrew / Classes

Oracle

Oracle

Oracles are seers, soothsayers, and augurs, glimpsing into the future and oftentimes attempting to shape it. Whether your goal lies in preventing horrid events or keeping the future pure and unadulterated, an oracle bears the responsibility of influencing fate itself.

Fate Seer

At 3rd level, you are able to predict the future to an extent. You can cast augury at will, using your spiritual focus in place of material components.

Future Proofing

At 3rd level, you can subtly tug on the strings of fate to lessen the burden on your allies. Whenever you activate your spirit tether, you can choose whether to deal damage to a target or give them an equal amount of temporary hit points. These temporary hit points disappear if the tether breaks.

Oracle Arts

Also at 3rd level, you gain access to new spirit arts that reflect your ability to shape the future.

Predestined Strike

When your linked target hits with an attack, you can use your reaction to spend 1 spirit point and choose between these options:

Fortune. Roll a d20. On a roll of 10 or above, the attack becomes a critical hit.

Disaster. Roll a d20. On a roll of 10 or below, the attack becomes a critical miss.

Eyes of Prescience

You can use an action and spend 1 spirit point to forsee any harm that might befall your target. Choose between these options:

Fortune. Until the beginning of your next turn, attack rolls against your target have disadvantage and the target makes Dexterity saving throws with advantage.

Disaster. Until the beginning of your next turn, the first attack roll against your target each turn has advantage.

Rewound Wounds

When you activate your spirit tether, you can spend 1 spirit point to use the following effects:

Fortune. If your target has taken damage within the last round, you can restore their hit points equal to 2d6 + your wisdom modifier, up to the total damage taken.

Disaster. If your target has had hit points restored or has gained temporary hit points within the last round, you can deal necrotic damage equal to 2d6 + your wisdom modifier up to the amount healed or the temporary hit points gained.

Soothe-saying

At 6th level, your experience with fortune telling allows you to gain a deeper insight into the emotional states of others. While tethered to a creature, you gain an understand of their emotions, giving you insight into fine details. You know how they feel about their current situation, how they react to events that transpire around them, and are able to recognize how they feel about other people, yourself included.

Spool of Fate

At 13th level, fate bows to your will. If you or an ally within 30 feet misses with an attack roll or fails an ability check or saving throw, you can use your reaction to allow that ally to reroll, potentially succeeding. The ally must use the new roll. You can only use this feature once per short rest, unless you spend 3 spirit points to use it again.

Master Oracle

At 18th level, you master your influnece over controlling fate. You learn the following spirit art:

Divergence

If your tethered target becomes critical (10% or fewer hit points) or dies, you can use your reaction to spend 5 spirit points and use one of the following effects:

Fortune. You can shift fate so that such an event never occured. If dead, the target is brought back to life, all conditions on the tethered target are ended, and it regains 50 hit points.

Disaster. You can use the event to spell disaster for enemies. Tethered targets of your choice take 50 force damage and must succeed on a Charisma saving throw or be stunned. If this damage reduces the target to 0 hit points, the target is disintegrated along with every nonmagical object it is wearing or carrying.

Each successful use of this spirit art each day increases its chance to fail by 33%. After three sucessful uses of this spirit art, further uses will fail automatically.

Homebrew / Classes

Pathfinder

Pathfinder

“Roads are for people who already know where they’re going.”

The Pathfinder is the one who goes first. Where the maps end, where the trail is cold, where the pass is choked with something that eats scouting parties — that is where a Pathfinder is sent, and where a Pathfinder comes back from. They are the marriage of the soldier and the tracker: the discipline, footwork, and weapon craft of a veteran warrior welded to the instincts of a hunter who has never lost a foe. Armies follow the lines they draw. Caravans survive the passes they clear. Things that hide in the deep places have learned to move when a Pathfinder takes an interest.

Prerequisites

Level 20 Cycle: Ranger 7+, Fighter 7+

The cycle must consist of exactly 20 levels split between Ranger and Fighter only, with at least 7 levels in each (e.g. 10/10, 13/7, 7/13). No other class levels may appear in the cycle.

Ranger Version: This prestige class is built on X’s Revised (Again) Ranger. Its features assume the Favored Foe and Warden Specialization systems from that revision.

Hit Die: 1d10 per Pathfinder level

The Pathfinder Table

17 37 — 1d12 17th
18 38 The Untrodden Way, Peerless Hunter 1d12 18th

20 40 First and Last 2d8 20th

PL 21: Pathfinder Skill

You gain proficiency in Wisdom (Survival) and Wisdom (Perception). If you are already proficient in one or both, you gain Expertise in it instead, doubling your proficiency bonus for ability checks using it.

You can also choose one other skill from the Ranger or Fighter skill list, gaining proficiency in it.

PL 21: Prestige Scaling

This class is measured in Pathfinder Levels (PfL), numbered 1 through 20 as you advance in it. Your Prestige Level (PL) is always 20 + your Pathfinder Level — it exists to describe your total standing among prestige classes and is what features in this class mean when they scale off “your Prestige Level” (Prestige Level 21 through 40, matching PfL 1 through 20).

Your Pathfinder Save DC is 8 + your Proficiency Bonus + your Wisdom modifier.

PL 21: Ascendant Spellcasting

Your Ranger spellcasting continues past where your qualifying cycle left off, keyed to your Ranger levels rather than your total character level.

Calculate your Effective Caster Level: your Ranger levels + your Pathfinder Level (PfL), to a maximum of 33. A 7th-level Ranger entering this class at PfL 1 has an Effective Caster Level of 8; a 13th-level Ranger entering at PfL 1 has an Effective Caster Level of 14. Either way, your first Pathfinder level always picks up exactly one step past where your Ranger spellcasting left off, and every Pathfinder level thereafter advances it by one more — a 13th-level Ranger reaches the table’s cap of 33 at PfL 20, no matter how it’s split.

Consult the Pathfinder Ascendant Casting table below using your Effective Caster Level. This replaces your Ranger slots and Spells Known entirely — don’t stack it with your base Ranger table.

Wisdom remains your spellcasting ability. As normal, whenever you gain a Pathfinder level you can swap one Ranger spell you know for another.

Pathfinder Ascendant Casting

Rows 8–20 are the standard Ranger half-caster progression, unchanged. From 21 onward this class never opens a 6th-level slot — Spells Known and your existing slots keep widening instead, topping out at 33, the highest Effective Caster Level any Pathfinder can reach (a 13th-level Ranger at Pathfinder Level 20), with a final spread of 7/6/6/5/5 slots and 20 Spells Known.

PL 21: Perfected Favored Foe

When your Favored Foe dies, you can use a Reaction to designate a new creature within 60 feet as your Favored Foe. You can also designate a creature whose tracks or remains you have examined within the last hour, even if you cannot see it.

Your attack bonus against your Favored Foe is equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum +2), if it is not already.

Once per turn when you hit your Favored Foe with a weapon attack, it takes extra damage equal to one roll of your Trailblazer Die.

While your Favored Foe is on the same plane of existence, you know its direction and rough distance at all times, and you have advantage on checks to track or find it.

Your attacks against your Favored Foe ignore all cover except Total Cover, and are unaffected by the Invisible condition or by magical concealment.

PL 22: Unerring Step

You gain the Land’s Stride feature if you do not have it. If you do, it improves: difficult terrain of any kind — natural, magical, or conjured — never costs you extra movement, and you leave no tracks unless you choose to. You gain a Climb Speed and Swim Speed equal to your Speed, and you can move across liquid, snow, and other unstable surfaces without sinking, provided you end your turn on solid ground.

Additionally, you can use the Search action as a Bonus Action.

PL 22: Second Wind (Prestige)

Your Second Wind now restores Hit Points equal to 2d10 + your Prestige Level. When you use Second Wind, you may also end one of the following conditions on yourself: Frightened, Poisoned, or Prone.

PL 23: Warden’s Continuum

You gain the next tier of your Warden Specialization that your qualifying cycle hadn’t reached — and only that one. If your Ranger levels were below 9th, you gain Warden’s Covenant (9th). If your Ranger levels were 9th or higher, you gain Warden’s Pinnacle (14th) instead.

You cannot switch to a different Warden Specialization with this feature

PL 23: Adopted Discipline

Whatever subclass you finished your qualifying cycle with stops there — it does not keep progressing on its own. The only way to unlock any further subclass tier is through this feature.

Choose any Ranger archetype or any Fighter subclass — the one you already had, or a new one entirely. You gain its features at the matching Pathfinder Level:

Ranger archetype: Pathfinder Level 3rd, 7th, 11th, and 15th.

Fighter subclass: Pathfinder Level 3rd, 7th, 10th, 15th, and 18th.

PL 24: Ability Score Improvement

At Pathfinder Level 4, 8, 12, 16, and 19, you can increase one ability score by 2, or two ability scores by 1, to a maximum of 20 (unless another feature allows otherwise). You may take a Feat instead.

PL 25: Hounding Strikes

When you take the Attack action, you can make one additional attack with the weapon you are wielding, provided at least one of the attacks in that action targets your Favored Foe.

This is not an Extra Attack feature and does not interact with the rule against stacking them. It adds one attack to however many the Attack action already grants you, whether that is two or three.

PL 25: Ascendant Surge

You gain one additional use of Action Surge between rests. When you use Action Surge, you can also move up to your Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks, and the first attack you make during the surged action against your Favored Foe is a Critical Hit on a roll of 18–20.

PL 26: Relentless Pursuit

When a creature you can see within 60 feet moves, you can take a Reaction to move up to half your Speed toward it. If you end this movement within 30 feet of your Favored Foe, you may make one weapon attack against it as part of that Reaction.

Additionally, you can follow your Favored Foe through teleportation or onto the Ethereal Plane — no other form of planar travel. When it teleports or shifts to the Ethereal Plane while you are within 60 feet, you may immediately follow, appearing in an unoccupied space within 10 feet of it. You can only return to the space you left (or the nearest unoccupied space to it) once your Favored Foe is dead, as a Bonus Action.

PL 27: Trailcraft Evasion

You gain the Evasion feature: when you make a Dexterity saving throw against an effect that deals half damage on a success, you instead take no damage on a success and half damage on a failure.

Additionally, Opportunity Attacks against you are made with disadvantage.

PL 29: The Foe’s Undoing

Your Favored Foe’s defenses fail against you. Your attacks against it ignore Resistance to the damage type dealt, and reduce Immunity to Resistance. Your Favored Foe has disadvantage on saving throws against your Ranger spells and Pathfinder features.

Additionally, your Primeval Awareness has no daily limit, and its range extends to 20 miles.

PL 30: Dominion of the Wild

You have walked enough of the world that it answers to you. You are immune to Exhaustion from environmental sources and to extreme heat and cold, and you no longer need to eat or drink (you still require a Long Rest’s worth of rest).

You may cast Commune with Nature, Find the Path, and Nondetection (self only) at will, without expending a spell slot or material components.

PL 30: Indomitable (Prestige)

You gain the Indomitable feature with one use if you do not have it; if you do, you gain one additional use. When you use it, you may instead choose to automatically succeed on the saving throw if the effect came from your Favored Foe. Once you use that improvement, you can’t do so again until you finish a Long Rest.

PL 31: Ceaseless Assault

Your Extra Attack feature lets you attack three times instead of twice when you take the Attack action. As normal, this does not stack with other features that set your number of Extra Attacks — if you already attack three times (from Fighter’s Extra Attack (2), for example), you instead add your Wisdom modifier to the damage of the final attack in the action.

Hounding Strikes is separate and still adds its attack on top, putting every Pathfinder at four attacks by this level.

PL 33: Ambusher’s Certainty

When you attack a creature that has not yet taken a turn in combat, or a creature that cannot see you, your attack roll cannot miss on anything other than a natural 1, and you deal an additional Trailblazer Die of damage on a hit.

PL 35: Honed Training

Your years of experience sharpen into real mastery. Choose two skills you’re proficient in — you gain Expertise in both, doubling your proficiency bonus for ability checks using them.

You also gain a third Fighting Style option (see Fighting Style) and one additional Weapon Mastery property choice.

PL 38: The Untrodden Way

You can spend 1 minute to open a path where none exists. You and up to twelve willing creatures travel to any location you have personally visited, or any location described to you in precise detail, arriving there after 1d4 hours. The journey passes through a shifting corridor of trails between places; you cannot be intercepted, tracked, or scried during the passage.

Once you use this feature, you cannot use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

PL 38: Peerless Hunter

You have advantage on all attack rolls against your Favored Foe, and it has disadvantage on all attack rolls against you.

PL 40: First and Last

You are the first through the door and the last one standing in it.

Foe Slayer. Add your Wisdom modifier to all damage rolls you make against your Favored Foe, weapon and spell alike.

Nowhere Is Far Enough. Your Relentless Pursuit now lets you follow your Favored Foe through any form of planar travel, not just teleportation or the Ethereal Plane.

The Next One. When your Favored Foe drops to 0 Hit Points, you can immediately designate a new creature and make one weapon attack against it, no action required. Once per turn.

Last Standing. When you would be reduced to 0 Hit Points while your Favored Foe remains alive, you instead regain Hit Points equal to your Prestige Level and can immediately move up to your Speed towards your Favored Foe and make one attack against them. Once per Long Rest.

Performer

Performer

Description

You master performance so that you can command any stage. You gain the following benefits:

  • Increase your Charisma score by 1, to a maximum of 20.
  • You gain proficiency in the Performance skill. If you are already proficient in the skill, you add double your proficiency bonus to checks you make with it.
  • While performing, you can try to distract one humanoid you can see who can see and hear you. Make a Charisma(Performance) check contested by the humanoid’s Wisdom (Insight) check. If your check succeeds, you grab the humanoid’s attention enough that it makes Wisdom (Perception) and Intelligence (Investigation) checks with disadvantage until you stop performing.
Homebrew / Classes

Physicist

Physicist

Description

The world we know has many rules and laws that dictate how it functions. Some explain why the sky is blue, others dictate how things fall, some even to help understand the best trajectory for a bolt or bullet. Regardless of what it may be, a Physicist is a specialized artificer that takes study of these natural laws to even greater lengths than most, learning to exploit them to achieve things previously thought impossible. While they may shy away from a technological side of artifice, make no mistake that the work of physicists is invaluable to almost all fields.

Features

  • 3rd Level - Analytic
  • 3rd Level - Physicist Spells
  • 3rd Level - Experimental Formulas
  • 5th Level - Kinetic Bombard
  • 9th Level - Advanced Formulas
  • 15th Level - Newtonian Defiance

3rd Level - Analytic

When you choose this specialization at 3rd level, you can add half your proficiency bonus (rounded down) to any Intelligence check you are not already proficient with.

3rd Level - Physicist Spells

You always have certain spells prepared after you reach particular levels in this class, as shown in the Physicist Spells table. These spells count as artificer spells for you, but they don’t count against the number of artificer spells you prepare.

Artificer Spell List

  • 3rd Level: Magnify Gravity, Magic Missile
  • 5th Level: Borrowed Knowledge, Immovable Object
  • 9th Level: Counterspell, Pulse Wave
  • 13th Level: Gravity Sinkhole, Fire Shield
  • 17th Level: Antilife Shell, Telekinesis

3rd Level - Experimental Formulas

Starting at 3rd level, you learn various formulas that can be used to alter or improve your performance. You have a number of experiment points equal to half your artificer level (rounded down) and regain all expended points when you finish a long rest. Alternatively, you can expend a spell slot as an action to regain experiment points equal to the slot's level.

You spend experiment points on different formulas, of which you learn three from the following list:

  • Alternate Angle: When you make an attack with a weapon that deals bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing damage, you can expend one experiment point to change the damage type to a different type from the same list. The attack also deals an extra 3 damage.
  • Thermodynamics: When you take fire or cold damage, you can use your reaction to expend one experiment point to deal half that damage of the opposite type to the creature that dealt the damage to you.
  • Conservation of Energy: When you deal force damage to a creature or object, you can expend one experiment point to deal extra damage equal to half your artificer level. Doing so reduces your speed to 0 until the end of your next turn.
  • Electron Shell: As an action, you can expend one to five experiment points to create a shell around you, which has 4 charges, plus one for every additional point spent. When you take damage, the damage is reduced by the amount of charges, and one is expended. All remaining charges dissipate after one hour.
  • Polarize: When you make an attack or cast a spell that deals damage, you can expend an experiment point to forgo rolling damage to deal the average damage.
  • Applied Science: When you make an ability check, you can expend an experiment point to predict the result before seeing it. If you are correct, you gain a +10 bonus to the roll. If you are within 1, you gain a +5 bonus instead.

5th Level - Kinetic Bombard

Starting at 5th level, you are able to harness the outgoing kinetic energy of attacks. Once per round, when you make a weapon or spell attack, you can increase the damage of the attack by 2d4, this damage is force damage.

The damage dealt by this ability increases to 3d4 at 9th level, and to 4d4 at 15th level.

9th Level - Advanced Formulas

A breakthrough has led to your creation of even further refined formulas. At 9th level you learn two of the following advanced formulas:

  • Genius Precision: When you or a creature you can see within 30 ft of you make an attack roll, you can expend one experiment point to apply your flash of genius to the attack roll.
  • Kinetic Battery: As a bonus action, you can expend one experiment point to begin storing kinetic energy. For every 10 feet you move, you add 1d6 to the total stored kinetic energy, up to 10d6. The next time you damage a creature or object, the target takes damage equal to your kinetic energy. The battery lasts for 1 minute, and if the battery expires before you deal damage, you take force damage equal to your kinetic energy.
  • Meltdown: As an action, you can expend 2 experiment points to deal acid damage to a creature you can see within 60 ft equal to twice the amount of hit dice it has. This formula does not effect targets resistant or immune to acid damage.
  • Super-Magnetism: If a spell or effect you create would move a creature on a failed saving throw, you can expend one experiment point to move the creature even if they succeed. You must use this formula before the creature makes the saving throw.

15th Level - Newtonian Defiance

At 15th level, the natural laws of the world begin to bend at your command. You can cast the following spells with the following changes:

  • Reverse Gravity: The spell has the normal effect, except that you can orient the area in any direction and creatures and objects fall toward the end of the area.
  • Arcane Gate: The portals created by this spell can be oriented in any direction you choose, but must be created flat against a solid surface large enough to hold it.
  • Telekinesis: You can manipulate up to three objects at once. If one of those objects is a weapon, you can attack with that weapon as if you were holding it.

You can cast each of these spells once in this way, and must finish a long rest to do so again.

Homebrew / Classes

Practitioner

Practitioner

Practitioner (Banned from 2026/01/04)

Facing a horde of demons, a lone warrior raises their blade high. With a single cleave, the demonic horde is silenced, their ranks having been cleft in two without mercy nor hesitation.

Pursued by the local militia, a figure dressed in black, ragged attire performs an ancient technique. With a dagger whirling about, she spins in a perfect arc and vanishes into thin air, losing her hunters with ease.

Facing down his mortal enemy, a martial practitioner displays the ultimate killing technique that he had spent his entire life perfecting, just for this moment. In exactly ten steps, he thrusts his blade with the force of the very heavens, impaling the man who had taken his family from him.

These warriors go by many names; the ninjas of Kozakura, the daoists of Shou Lung, and even the henshin mystics of Tabot. Focused on practicing various martial forms to employ in battle, subterfuge, or survival, this archetype of combatant hailing from the east is most commonly referred to under one name— the practitioner.

Form and Tradition

The martial forms trained by practitioners are rooted very heavily to worldly practices. Unlike a monk’s training, which is focused on spiritualism and purifying the soul, these forms are tied to more earthly aspects.

Many martial forms are passed down through generations, existing as deep-rooted tradition, and others are lost arts created by long-forgotten ancestors. These forms spread throughout regions, often going by different names with various cultural adjustments made depending on their respective uses.

Martial Peak

For a practitioner, training in specific arts defines their existence. Whether it be making use of their ki, training their bodies to withstand the force of their forms, or perfecting the use of weaponry to their absolute peak, practitioners can eventually perform impossible feats and earth-shattering deeds.

The Practitioner Class Table

Level Proficiency Bonus Feature Mastery

2nd +2 Martial Path 1
3rd +2 Cleanse, Fighting Style 2
4th +2 Ability Score Improvement 2
5th +3 - 3

18th +6 Martial Path Feature 9
