19th +6 38 S Ability Score Improvement
20th +6 40 S Nindo Capstone

Class Features

As a Shinobi, you gain the following class features.

Hit Points

  • Hit Dice: 1d8 per Shinobi level
  • Hit Points at 1st Level: 8 + your Constitution modifier
  • Hit Points at Higher Levels: 1d8 (or 5) + your Constitution modifier per Shinobi level after 1st

Proficiencies

  • Armor: Light armor, medium armor
  • Weapons: Simple weapons, shortswords, scimitars, hand crossbows, kusarigama
  • Tools: Calligrapher's Supplies, Herbalism kit
  • Saving Throws: Dexterity, Intelligence
  • Skills: Choose three from Acrobatics, Athletics, Deception, History, Insight, Investigation, Perception, Sleight of Hand, and Stealth

Equipment

You start with the following equipment, in addition to the equipment granted by your background:

  • (a) a shortsword and 5 Kunai or (b) two simple weapons and 5 shuriken
  • (a) a dungeoneer's pack or (b) an explorer's pack
  • (a) leather armor or (b) chain Shirt
  • (a) Calligrapher's Supplies and 10x tags (empty scrolls) (b) herbalism Kit

Level 1 - Shinobi Training

You have undergone rigorous conditioning in the arts of the silent kill and tactical movement. You gain the following benefits:

  • Shinobi Weapons: You are a master of small, concealable arms. When you wield a kunai, kama, or shuriken, its damage die changes to a d6. These weapons, along with tanto, wakizashi and Kusarigama count as "Shinobi Weapons" for you, Shinobi Weapons are used when performing Bukijutsu.
    • Kunai = Dagger
    • Kama = Sickle
    • Shuriken = Dart
    • Tanto = Shortsword
    • Wakizashi = Scimitar
  • Ballistics: If a Shinobi Weapon has the Thrown property, its normal range increases to 30 feet and its long range increases to 90 feet.
  • Armored Agility: Your conditioning allows you to move unrestricted. You can use your Dexterity score instead of Strength for calculating jumping distances and climbing checks, even while wearing Light or Medium armor.

Level 1 - Nature Affinity

Every Shinobi has an innate elemental affinity, determined by the alignment of their chakra at birth. Choose one of the following natures, alternatively roll a d8 to randomly select a nature.

Random (D8) Nature Associated Element
1 Fire (Katon) Flame and Heat
2 Water (Suiton) Liquid and Ice
3 Earth (Doton) Soil and Stone
4 Wind (Futon) Air and Sound
5 Lightning (Raiton) Electricity
6 Yin (Genjutsu) Mind and Shadow
7 Yang Life and Vitality
8 Taijutsu & Bukijutsu Body and Force
  • Primary Nature Efficiency: You are most efficient when molding chakra for your natural affinity. When you cast a Jutsu that matches the Primary Nature you selected at 1st Level, you reduce the Chakra cost by 1 (to a minimum of 1 Chakra).
  • Primary Nature Technique: You learn a D Rank Jutsu of your Chosen Nature. This Jutsu doesn't count against the amount of Jutsu known

Level 1 - Chakra Molding

You have learned to mold your physical stamina and spiritual energy into Chakra, the fuel for your techniques.

  • Chakra Points: You have a pool of Chakra points represented by the following formula: Chakra Maximum = Shinobi Level × 2
  • Recovery: You regain all expended Chakra points when you finish a Long Rest.

Level 1 - Jutsu Casting

You have trained your memory and dexterity to weave Hand Signs, manifesting reality-warping effects known as Jutsu.

  • Jutsu Known: You know a number of Jutsu equal to half your Shinobi level (rounded up) (minimum of 1).
    • Learning New Jutsu: Whenever you gain a level in this class, you can replace one Jutsu you know with another Jutsu of a Rank you can cast.
  • Jutsu Ranks: Jutsu are organized by Rank, which corresponds to their power level and Chakra cost. At 1st Level, you can learn and cast D-Rank Jutsu. You unlock higher ranks as you level up.
  • Spellcasting Ability: Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for your Jutsu.
    • Jutsu Save DC = 8 + your Proficiency Bonus + your Intelligence modifier
    • Jutsu Attack Modifier = your Proficiency Bonus + your Intelligence modifier
  • Jutsu Components:
    • Hand Signs (Somatic Components): Casting a Jutsu requires you to weave complex hand signs. You must have two free hands to cast a Jutsu, unless a feature allows otherwise. You cannot cast Jutsu while holding a shield or a two-handed weapon, unless you drop it or put it away first.
    • Material: These are varying components required when casting a jutsu
      • Motion: Cannot perform with a speed of 0
      • Items: An Item that is required
      • Gaze: Requires direct line of sight to the target
    • Weapon: You must wield or have a weapon available to use a jutsu with a weapon component

Jutsu and Magic: Jutsu count as spells, and casting a Jutsu counts as casting a spell, for the purpose of any effect that prevents, suppresses, or restricts spellcasting (such as an antimagic field or a raging Barbarian's restriction). Hand Signs count as Somatic components, so anything that prevents Somatic components also prevents Jutsu casting. Where an effect cares about spell level (such as Counterspell or Dispel Magic), a Jutsu's Rank counts as its Equivalent Spell Level from the Jutsu Rank & Cost Table (treat A-Rank as 5th level).

Overcharging: Some Jutsu list an Overcharge option. When you cast such a Jutsu, you can spend additional Chakra on it, up to a maximum of additional Chakra equal to your Proficiency Bonus per casting. Extra damage dice gained from Overcharging always use the Jutsu's own damage die. Chakra cost reductions (such as Primary Nature Efficiency, Bloodline Efficiency, or Sannin Mode) apply only to a Jutsu's base cost, never to Overcharge Chakra. Standard Overcharge rates: +1 damage die costs 1 Chakra for a d4 or d6, 2 Chakra for a d8, or 3 Chakra for a d10; +1 target, projectile, or attack costs 2 Chakra; other effects (size, duration, wall HP, and so on) cost 2 Chakra per step.

Basic Techniques: The basic utility technique of each nature (Basic Flame Control and the Basic Earth, Lightning, Water, Wind, Yin, and Yang Style Techniques) costs 1 Chakra to cast.

Jutsu Rank & Cost Table

Jutsu Rank Equivalent Spell Level Chakra Cost Level Unlocked
D-Rank 1st Level 2 1st
C-Rank 2nd Level 3 5th
B-Rank 3rd Level 5 8th
A-Rank 4th-5th Level 6 13th
S-Rank 6th Level 7 17th

Level 2 - Shinobi Bloodline

Your capabilities are defined by your genetics or clan origin. Choose one Bloodline from the list below. This choice is permanent and cannot be changed. You automatically learn the Bloodline Jutsu associated with your chosen bloodline at the applicable Rank level. These do not count against your Jutsu Known.

Bloodline Efficiency: When you cast one of your Bloodline Jutsu, reduce its Chakra cost by 1 (to a minimum of 1). Bloodline Jutsu have no elemental nature and do not benefit from Primary Nature Efficiency.

Optional Rule: For Characters that do not know their genetic origin or who got the bloodline through far of generational mean, roll a d10 and divide it by 2 (rounded up) to determine your Bloodline

Random Roll (1d10/2) Bloodline
1 The Copy Eye
2 The White Eye
3 The Whirlpool
4 The Shadow
5 The Prodigy

The Copy Eye

Descendants of a clan known for intense emotions and the Sharingan, an eye that sees chakra and mimics movement, when awakened the eye turns red with a single rain drop pattern. At each Bloodline level, you gain another raindrop.

  • Kinetic Vision: You can briefly read the muscle tension of your enemies. When a creature you can see makes an attack roll against you, you can use your Reaction to impose Disadvantage on that attack roll. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, regaining all expended uses on a Long Rest.

The White Eye

Descendants of a noble clan possessing the Byakugan, capable of seeing long distances and through objects. Their eyes, pupils and irises are permanently white.

  • All-Seeing: You cannot be Surprised while you are conscious.

The Whirlpool

Descendants of a fallen clan renowned for their sealing jutsu and immense longevity and larger than normal chakra pools.

  • Massive Reserves: Starting at 2nd Level, you add your Proficiency Bonus to your Maximum Chakra Points.

The Shadow

Descendants of a clan of high-IQ tacticians who manipulate shadows to bind enemies.

  • Shadow Arts: You learn the Minor Illusion cantrip. Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for it. You can cast it using only Somatic components (your shadow).

The Prodigy (Natural Genius)

You possess no special surname, but you were born with a freakish talent for chakra manipulation

  • Precision: When you roll damage for a Jutsu or a Shinobi Weapon attack, you can reroll any 1s on the damage dice. You must use the new roll.

Level 3 - Shinobi Nindo

At 3rd level, you choose the personal philosophy that guides your actions and techniques. Your choice grants you features at 3rd, 7th, 15th, and 20th Level.

Nindo Efficiency: Once per Long Rest, when you use a Nindo feature (not a Jutsu) that requires you to spend Chakra, you can use it without spending Chakra.

  • Nindo of the Iron Fist
  • Nindo of the Battlemind
  • Nindo of the Elementalist
  • Nindo of the Illusionist
  • Nindo of the Healer
  • Nindo of the Assassin

Level 4 - Ability Score Improvement

When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.

Using the optional feats rule, you can forgo taking this feature to take a feat of your choice instead.

Level 5 - Extra Attack

Beginning at 5th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

Level 6 - Bloodline Awakening

The latent power in your genetics begins to manifest more potent abilities. You gain the feature corresponding to the Bloodline you chose at 2nd Level.

The Copy Eye

  • Visual Insight: You can focus your chakra to see the unseen. You can cast See Invisibility or Detect Magic by spending 2 Chakra. You do not need material components for these castings.
  • Reflexive Analysis: You gain proficiency in the Insight skill. If you are already proficient, you gain Expertise (doubling your proficiency bonus).

The White Eye

  • Piercing Sight: As a Bonus Action, you can activate your X-Ray vision for 1 minute. For the duration, you can see through solid objects to a range of 30 feet. Within that range, you have Blindsight. You can use this feature once per long rest, unless you spend 3 Chakra for each subsequent use.
  • Reflexive Analysis: You gain proficiency in the Perception skill. If you are already proficient, you gain Expertise (doubling your proficiency bonus).

The Whirlpool

  • Vigorous Casting: Your chakra is so dense that it physically reinforces your body. Whenever you spend Chakra to cast a Jutsu of C-Rank or higher, you gain Temporary Hit Points equal to Your Constitution Modifier + The Jutsu's Chakra Cost.

The Shadow

  • Split Shadow: When you cast the Shadow Bind Jutsu, you can target two creatures instead of one, provided the targets are within 10 feet of each other. The chakra cost remains the same.

The Prodigy

  • Polymath: You gain Expertise in two skills of your choice in which you are proficient. Your proficiency bonus is doubled for any ability check you make that uses either of the chosen skills.

Level 6 - Tactical Recovery

You have learned to center your breathing and stamina to recover quickly during downtime.

  • Chakra Recovery: Once per day when you finish a Short Rest, you can meditate to regain expended Chakra equal to your Shinobi level.

Centered Breathing: You have Advantage on Constitution saving throws made to maintain Concentration on a Jutsu.

Level 10 - Improved Nature Affinity

Primary Nature: You gain more control over your Primary Nature and your jutsu becomes more powerful. You gain a +1 to any Jutsu attack rolls and +1 to the Save DC of any Jutsu you cast from your Primary Nature.

Secondary Nature: You can choose any other Nature, or roll on the nature table (rerolling if you roll the same as your Primary) to be your Secondary, or secondary nature. You learn a D- Rank Jutsu from this nature, that does not count as one of your known jutsu

Level 10 - Surface Walking

At 10th level, you master the art of focusing chakra into the soles of your feet to defy gravity and surface tension. You can move up, down, and across vertical surfaces and upside down along ceilings, as well as across liquids, without falling during the move. When you end your turn on a vertical surface, or upside down, you must spend 1 chakra to maintain the position or fall to the ground

Level 11 - Advanced Scouting

At 11th level, your senses have become so attuned to the flow of chakra and the natural world that you can detect hidden threats and move unseen. You gain the following benefits:

  • Chakra Sense: As an Action, you can open your mind to detect the presence of chakra for 1 minute. For the duration, you know the location of any creature within 60 feet of you that is not a Construct or Undead, even if the creature is hidden or invisible. You also detect the presence of magical objects or active spells/jutsu within the same range. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once), regaining all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.
  • Traceless Step: You leave no physical tracks, and you cannot be tracked by non-magical means unless you choose to leave a trail.
  • Silent Signaling: You can communicate simple ideas (such as "Stop," "Enemy Ahead," "Go," or "Help") to your allies using only hand signs and body language. Allies who can see you understand these signals automatically; other creatures must make an Insight check (DC equal to your Jutsu Save DC) to decipher them.

Level 14 - Bloodline Mastery

Your genetic abilities have reached their mature state. You gain the feature corresponding to the Bloodline you chose at 2nd Level.

The Copy Eye

Susanoo Ribcage: You can manifest a spectral avatar of chakra to protect you from harm.When you take damage, you can use your Reaction and spend 4 Chakra to reduce the damage by 4d10 + your Intelligence modifier. If the damage is reduced to 0, you suffer no secondary effects from the attack (such as being pushed or poisoned).

The White Eye

Tenketsu Needle (Chakra Blocking): You can inject chakra into an opponent's pressure points to shut down their body. When you hit a creature with an Unarmed Strike or a Shinobi Weapon, you can spend 3 Chakra to force the target to make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, the target is Stunned until the end of your next turn. Additionally, whether they save or fail, they cannot take Reactions until the start of your next turn.

The Whirlpool

Hereditary Fortitude: You gain a bonus to your maximum hitpoint equal to the size of your Chakra pool

The Shadow

Shadow Strangle: You can crush the life out of those caught in your trap. As a Bonus Action, you can constrict the shadows around any creature currently Restrained by any of your bloodline jutsu. The target takes Necrotic damage equal to 3d8 + your Intelligence modifier. This damage does not break the hold or grant a new saving throw.

The Prodigy

Perfect Recall: Your understanding of chakra theory is absolute. You can cast a Jutsu from the Shinobi class list that you do not know. To do so, you must spend the standard Chakra cost of the Jutsu plus 2 additional Chakra. (e.g., Casting an unknown C-Rank Jutsu costs 3 + 2 = 5 Chakra).

Mental Fortitude: You gain proficiency in Wisdom saving throws.

Level 17 - Persistent Nature

Primary Nature: The Bonus to your Jutsu Attack rolls and saving DC increases to 2 for All Jutsu tied to your Primary nature.

Secondary Nature: You add a +1 to your jutsu attack rolls and Save DC for your Secondary Nature

Level 18 - Jonin Commander

At 18th level, your experience and efficiency in combat are second to none. You have mastered the art of weaving signs with minimal movement and blistering speed.

  • One-Handed Seals: You can perform the Somatic components (hand signs) of a Jutsu with only one free hand. This allows you to cast Jutsu while grappling a creature, holding an object, or wielding a weapon in your other hand.
  • Swift Tactics: You can alter the flow of your chakra to accelerate or delay the speed of your techniques to fit the situation.
    • When you cast a Jutsu that has a casting time of 1 Action, you can change the casting time to 1 Bonus Action for this casting.
    • When you cast a Jutsu that has a casting time of 1 Bonus Action, you can change the casting time to 1 Action for this casting.
    • Cost: To utilize this speed change, you must spend 2 additional Chakra point on top of the Jutsu's standard cost.
Homebrew / Classes

Spiritualist

Spiritualist

The Spiritualist Class

Spreading a deck of cards out on a table, a fortune teller smiles at her guest, flipping three of the cards over one by one. With a silky voice and a flourished hand, she speaks of events that have transpired, events that weigh heavy on her guest’s mind, and of events yet to come.

Facing down a malevolent spirit, a man in clergical robes watches as it takes control of his companion’s movements. The man thrusts his spirit out towards his ally, wrenching the ghost’s grip away from her mind and allowing her the opportunity to cut the evil being down with a radiant blade.

Standing amidst candles and blood, a medium speaks words into the realm beyond life, listening for a response. The soul of an elder, long deceased, pools into existence next to him, giving him advice and information on how to defeat his greatest foe.

Regardless of the profession they take up, spiritualists utilize the power of their spirit to influence others, both in this world and the next. Whether they specialize in speaking to those long past, hunting down evil wherever it may rear its head, or taking subtle glances into the future to attempt to shape fate, these masters of souls seek to strengthen their ties to the world, both material and ethereal.

Earthly Ambitions

Spiritualists are masters of their own spirits. Similar to monks that seek spiritual peace, spiritualists spend their lives dedicated to cultivating their souls through exercises and manipulation. Unlike monks, who care little for wealth or power, many spiritualists are driven by earthy goals and ambitions.

Some spiritualists cultivate their abilities to seek vengeance for being wronged, using their spiritual power to further their own agendas. Some have seen a grim future for themselves, and stop at nothing to prevent seeing that future come to pass. Others still are in the profession for material gain, using the opportunities from reading fortunes and hunting evil to fill their coffers with gold. Adventuring is just another means to an end for many of these individuals, often proving to be a quick (yet perilous) path to power.

Mastery Over Spirit

Constant training and practice allows a spiritualist to use their souls to manipulate the material plane, offering powerful results. The majority of them draw power from the ethereal plane, manipulating the borders between this world and that to gain strange and unconventional abilities. By linking their souls to entities in the material plane, they can influence such entities in a variety of ways, both beneficially and detrimentally. As they learn to control their spirit more effectively, a spiritualist can exploit and influence the world around them in peculiar ways.

Creating a Spiritualist

As you make a spiritualist, think of what drives you to cultivate your soul and gain power. Are you trying to get revenge on an evil spirit that hurt your friends or family? Do you want to vanquish anything you percieve as evil on your own terms, without the need to be tied down to oath or order? Do you want to make a fortune as a famed seer, that thousands flock towards to find out what lies ahead for their futures? Your motivations may have a big part in deciding the profession you eventually select for yourself.

Besides the things that drive you, it’s also important to decide what extent you’ll go to achieve your ambitions, as well as the methods you might take. Are you willing to make necessary sacrifices to come out ahead? Will you find allies to surround yourself with, and rely on them to assist you with your goals? Maybe you put more of your faith with the dead, and look to them for answers to your problems.

Quick Build

You can make a spiritualist quickly by following these suggestions. First, Wisdom should be your highest ability score, followed by Dexterity or Constitution. Second, choose the Haunted One background.

Spiritualist Table

Level Proficiency Bonus Spirit Points Features
1st +2 - Spirit Tether, Soul Sense
2nd +2 4 Spirit Arts, Soul Exertion
3rd +2 6 Spiritual Profession
4th +2 8 Ability Score Improvement
5th +3 10 Otherworldly Tenacity
6th +3 12 Profession Feature
7th +3 14 Twin Spirit
8th +3 16 Ability Score Improvement
9th +4 18 Advanced Spirit Arts
10th +4 20 Improved Spirit Jolt
11th +4 22 Heightened Spirit Arts
12th +4 24 Ability Score Improvement
13th +5 26 Profession Feature
14th +5 28 Master Spirit Arts
15th +5 30 Ether Walker
16th +5 32 Ability Score Improvement
17th +6 34 Soul Trinity
18th +6 36 Profession Feature
19th +6 38 Ability Score Improvement
20th +6 40 Soulcast

Class Features

As a spiritualist, you gain the following class features.

Hit Points

Hit Dice:

1d6 per spiritualist level

Hit Points at 1st Level:

6 + your Constitution modifier

Hit Points at Higher Levels:

1d6 (or 4) + your Constitution modifier per spiritualist level after 1st

Proficiencies

Armor:

Light armor

Weapons:

Daggers, darts, slings, quarterstaffs, light crossbows

Tools:

none

Saving Throws:

Wisdom, Charisma

Skills:

Choose two from Arcana, Deception, Insight, Investigation, Perception, Persuasion, Religion, and Sleight of Hand.

Equipment

You start with the following equipment, in addition to the equipment granted by your background:

  • (a) a dagger or (b) a quarterstaff
  • (a) a light crossbow and 20 bolts or (b) a sling with 20 bullets
  • (a) a scholar’s pack or (b) an explorer’s pack
  • leather armor and a spiritual focus

Spirit Tether

At 1st level, you learn to project your own spirit outwards, allowing it to manipulate the material plane. This tether represents your soul’s influence and will be the baseline for your spiritualist abilities.

Spiritual Focus

You employ unorthodox tools through which to channel your spirit. You must have a spiritual focus to use your spirit tether, which can take the form of the following objects: a candle, crystal ball, skull, spirit board, or tarokka deck. Alternatively, you may choose a different object you and your DM agree on.

Activating the Spirit Tether

As a bonus action, you can use your spiritual focus to choose a creature or object other than yourself you can see within 120 feet to latch an invisible spirit rope onto. A creature that can see invisible objects sees a thin, spectral thread directly connecting you to the target. The tether exists in the ethereal plane, and is blocked by any effect that prevents ethereal travel.

You must concentrate to maintain the tether as if concentrating on a spell. The spirit rope breaks if you lose concentration, if you are ever more than 120 feet from the target, if it’s blocked in the ethereal plane, if you create another spirit tether, or if you end the connection as a bonus action.

When you create your tether or as a bonus action on your turn, you can deal 1d4 force damage to the target. The damage increases when you reach certain levels in this class, increasing to 2d4 at 5th level, 3d4 at 11th level, and 4d4 at 17th level.

While you’re tethered to a creature, you can communicate with it telepathically. As long as the creature can understand language, it understands what you communicate even if you don’t share a language and vice versa.

Soul Sense

Also at 1st level, you have a heightened sensitivity to spirits and souls in your area. As an action, you can sense the general location of any souls within 30 feet of you, including creatures or objects that contain souls. You learn the direction as well as the quantity of the souls you sense, but cannot determine any other properties. This special vision can see through most barriers, but it is blocked by 1 foot of stone, 1 inch of common metal, a thin sheet of lead, or 3 feet of wood or dirt. This effect lasts for one minute and can only be used again after a short or long rest.

Spirit Arts

At 2nd level, you can manipulate your spirit tether to accomplish feats unrestrained by your mortal body. The extent to which you can manipulate your spirit without exerting yourself is represented by a number of spirit points.

You can spend these spirit points on various spirit arts, which are detailed below. When you spend a spirit point, it is unavailable until you finish a long rest, upon which your spirit is revitalized enough to be utilized further. You can never have more spirit points than shown on the table for your level. Spirit arts can only ever target creatures and objects your spirit tether is connected to. If your spirit tether breaks, the effect of any spirit arts are immediately ended.

Some spirit arts require your target to make a saving throw to resist the art’s effects. The saving throw DC is calculated as follows:

Art save DC = 8 + your Proficiency Bonus + your Wisdom modifier

Corpus Enforcement

When your tethered target deals damage to you, you can spend 1 spirit point to halve the damage you take.

Spirit Jolt

As an action, you can spend up to 3 spirit points (min. 1) and force the target to make a Charisma saving throw. The target takes 3d6 force damage for each point you spend on a failed save, and half as much on a successful one.

Spirit Resonance

As an action, you can spend 1 spirit point to strengthen the tether between yourself and the tethered target. For one minute, both you and the target can add 1d4 to each saving throw or ability check you make.

Corrupt Spirit

As an action, you can spend 1 spirit point to corrupt the tethered target. It must make a Charisma saving throw. On a failure, the target must roll a d4 and subtract the amount from each ability check, attack roll, or saving throw it makes until the end of your next turn.

Spirit Influence

If the tethered target is a creature, you can use an action to spend 1 spirit point and make the target more malleable to influence. For one minute, your checks made against the target have advantage.

Soul Exertion

At 2nd level, you can exert your spirit past its normal limits with some effort. When you finish a short rest, you can spend any number of hit dice. Rather than regaining hit points, you regain an amount of spirit points equal to the amount you spent.

Spiritual Profession

At 3rd level, you select a profession to undertake that decides the nature of how you use your spiritual abilities. Your profession grants you features at 3rd level and then again at 6th, 13th, and 18th level.

  • Avenger
  • Exorcist
  • Harbinger
  • Medium
  • Oracle

Ability Score Improvement

When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can’t increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.

Otherworldly Tenacity

At 5th level, if your concentration is broken and you’re not incapacitated, you can spend 1 spirit point to maintain concentration.

Twin Spirit

At 7th level, when you create a spirit tether, you can target an additional target within range. Whenever you use a spirit art, you can decide if it targets one or both of the targets. If you target multiple creatures or objects with a spirit art, you only have to spend spirit points once. If the tether breaks for a target, only the spirit arts applied to that tether are ended.

Advanced Spirit Arts

At 9th level, you further hone your spirit arts, allowing you to access more refined techniques. You have access to the following spirit arts:

Soul Blight

If your tethered target is a creature, you can use an action and spend 2 spirit points to attempt to taint them. The target must make a constitution saving throw or take 5d6 poison damage at the start of each of their turns. The creature can use an action to purge the blight from their body, ending this spirit art.

Tether Swap

As an action, you can spend 2 spirit points to force the target to make a Charisma save (the target may choose to fail). On a failure, you switch places with the target. If the target is too large to fit in your space or vice versa, the art fails and your spirit points remain unspent.

Panic

As an action, you can spend 2 spirit points to force the target to make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failure, the target is frightened. While frightened, the target must use all of its movement at the start of its turn to move away from you unless there is nowhere else to move. The target can make a Wisdom saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending this spirit art on a success.

Improved Spirit Jolt

At 10th level, your spirit jolt strengthens in power. Its damage increases to 4d6 force damage for each point you spend.

Heightened Spirit Arts

Once per turn starting at 11th level, when you use a spirit art that takes an action, you can immediately use a different spirit art that also requires an action. You expend spirit points from both arts.

Master Spirit Arts

At 14th level, you master control over your spirit, culminating in powerful spirit arts.

Spirit Beyond Form

If the tethered target would reduce you to 0 hit points, you can spend 3 spirit points as a reaction to drop to 1 hit point instead.

Soul Surge

If your tethered target is a creature, you can use your action to spend 3 spirit points and strengthen their soul. During their next turn, they may take an extra action. That action can be used only to take the Attack (one weapon attack only), Dash, Disengage, Hide, or Use an Object action.

Oversoul Burst

If your tethered target is reduced to zero hit points, you can spend 3 spirit points to detonate your soul from its location. Each creature within 10 feet of the target must make a Charisma saving throw. On a failure, the target takes 8d6 force damage, taking half that damage on a success.

Ether Walker

At 15th level, your spirit can slip into the ethereal without trouble. You can cast the etherealness spell on yourself without expending a spell slot. Once you do so, you cannot do so again until you finish a long rest or spend 5 spirit points to cast it again.

Soul Trinity

At 17th level, you can split your soul tether even further. You can now target up to three creatures or objects within range when you use your soul tether. Whenever you use a spirit art, you can choose which targets are affected by it.

Soulcast

At 20th level, you fully master control over your spirit. When you use your soul tether, you can cast your soul out to instantaneously tether to any willing creature on the same plane as yourself. When using your tether in this way, it doesn’t break as a result of being out of range. A creature tethered in this manner can use an action to break the tether at will.

Sublime Bard

Sublime Bard

Is that a dragon I see?

The Bard Sublime is a master of the cosmic song, a living library of every melody ever hummed and every spell ever woven. At this level of prestige, you are no longer just a performer; you are the conductor of reality itself.

Prerequisites

  • Level 20 Cycle: You must have completed 20 levels of Bard with no multiclassing.

The Bard Sublime Table

Class Features

PL 21: Proficiencies

When you take this prestige class, choose two additional skills from the Bard skill list. You gain proficiency in both.

PL 21: Ascendant Spellcasting

You gain a new set of spell slots to fuel your magic. You gain spell slots as per the Bard table based on your Prestige Level minus 20 (e.g., at PL 25, you have additional slots equal to the slots of a 5th-level Bard).

  • Cantrips: You learn one Bard cantrip of your choice. You learn additional cantrips at PL 24 and PL 30 (the PL 30 cantrip may be from any spell list available via Magical Secrets).
  • Magical Secrets: If using the 2024 rules, your Magical Secrets feature applies when preparing any new spells from this table.

PL 21: Resonant Inspiration

Your Bardic Inspiration die is now 2d6. As you reach higher levels, the size of these dice increases: 2d8 at PL 25, 2d10 at PL 30, and 2d12 at PL 35.

PL 22: Expertise

Choose two skills in which you are proficient. Your Proficiency Bonus is doubled for any ability check you make that uses either of the chosen proficiencies.

PL 22: Master of None

You gain "Floating Expertise." At the end of a Short Rest, choose one skill or tool in which you are proficient. You gain Expertise in that skill/tool until the end of your next Short or Long Rest.

PL 23: Expanded Bardic College

Your talents expand, You may choose the same bardic college, or you may choose a new one to reflect the different talents learned from another colelge. At PL 23, PL 26, and PL 34, you gain more features from your Bardic College.

PL 24: Ability Score Improvement

At PL 24, 28, 32, 36, and 39, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or two ability scores by 1. As normal, you cannot increase a score above 20 (unless another feature allows it). You may select a Feat instead of an ASI.

PL 25: Orchestral Flourish

When you use a feature that grants a Bardic Inspiration die to another creature, you can expend a number of additional uses up to half your Proficiency Bonus (rounded down) to grant dice to that many additional targets within 60 feet.

PL 27: Captivating Counter Charm

When you use your Countercharm, you add your Charisma modifier to the reroll. Additionally, this is now a Special Reaction; you can use it once per round without expending your normal Reaction for that round.

PL 29: Superior Expertise

Choose two skills in which you already have Expertise. Your Proficiency Bonus is now tripled for those skills instead of doubled.

PL 30: Infinite Secrets

  • 2024 Version: You add the Sorcerer and Warlock spell lists to your Bard spell list. You can learn from these lists whenever you gain a "Prepared Spell" on the table.
  • 2014 Version: You learn two additional spells from any list. You learn two more at PL 34 and PL 38. These do not count against your spells known.

In Addition, At the end of a Long Rest, you can replace one spell learned through your Magical Secrets feature with any other spell of the same level from your magical secrets class list.

PL 38: Expansive Inspiration

You have mastered the efficiency of the song. You can now grant Bardic Inspiration dice to a number of creatures equal to half your Proficiency Bonus (rounded down) by expending only a single use of your Bardic Inspiration.

PL40: Sublime

You have mastered two more of the Words of Creation: the words of pain and rest. You always have the power word pain and power word stun spells prepared, and they do not count against the number of spells you can have prepared. When you cast either of these spells, you can target a second creature with it, provided that the second creature is within 10 feet of the first target. Additionally, your inspiration carries a lingering, harmonic echo. Whenever an ally successfully uses one of your Bardic Inspiration dice, you can choose another ally within 30 feet of the first. That chosen ally gains a Bardic Inspiration die of the same size, which expires at the end of their next turn.

Homebrew / Classes

Swindler

Swindler

Description

Cheaters go by many names; swindlers, con-artists, charlatans. Whatever they may call you, whoever you might be perceived as, you’ll always be the first to let the world know that the cards in your hand are there entirely legitimately— you couldn’t have stacked the deck, the dealer shuffled beforehand! You weren’t responsible for the incomprehensibly lucky die rolls, either— you were borrowing the dealer’s dice, after all. Oh, and the drinking game you outlasted the dwarf barbarian in? You couldn’t have watered your drink down, the dealer poured it out for you!

…What? You’re being accused of paying off the dealer? Poppycock.

Features:

  • 3rd Level - Swindler’s Luck
  • 9th Level - Loaded Dice
  • 13th Level - Sure Shot
  • 17th Level - Don of Con

3rd Level - Swindler’s Luck

At 3rd level, luck seems to appear whenever it benefits you, almost as if you’re cheating. Whenever you make a roll with advantage, you may meddle with the roll, forgoing that advantage, and roll normally. The next time you roll without advantage, you roll with advantage.

9th Level - Loaded Dice

At 9th level, you cheat  act with more finesse, giving you more control over your actions. Whenever you make a roll with advantage, you may forgo that advantage to create a loaded die. You may store a number of loaded dice equal to half your proficiency bonus, rounded down. These loaded dice disappear on a short or long rest.

Whenever you roll an attack roll, ability check, or saving throw, you may spend one of your loaded dice to give yourself advantage on that roll. You may only spend one loaded die per turn.

13th Level - Sure Shot

By 13th level, your “luck” is far too consistent to be inconspicuous. When you roll with advantage, you may forgo that advantage to add +3 to the roll’s total. If the roll succeeds, you gain one loaded die.

17th Level - Don of Con

At 17th level, it’s quite clear you’ve been cheating all this time, some way, somehow. On the bright side, you don’t have to hide it anymore— whenever you miss with an attack roll, you can spend 3 loaded dice to turn that miss into a hit. When you fail a saving throw, you can spend 2 loaded dice to succeed automatically. When you fail an ability check, you can spend 1 loaded die to make the result 20.

The Gunslinger

The Gunslinger

A master of powder, precision, and pressure.

Gunslingers are elite martial combatants who specialize in firearms. Whether a patient sharpshooter, a lightning-fast revolver duelist, or a battlefield suppressor, the Gunslinger dominates ranged combat through discipline, tactical positioning, and superior weapon mastery.

Class Features

Hit Points

Missing.

Grit

Level 1

You gain a pool of Grit Points equal to:

Proficiency Bonus + Dexterity modifier (minimum 2.)

You regain all Grit on a long rest.

Some features require Grit to use or activate.

Called Shots

Level 1

When you hit a creature with a firearm attack, you may spend 1 Grit to apply one of the following effects. This list will expand when you reach higher levels of this class (levels 9 and 11). The effects of these shots are until the end of the targets turn if they hit. The DC for your Called Shots is equal to 8 + proficiency bonus + Dexterity modifier:

As a bonus action, enter one stance. You may switch stances as a bonus action. The duration is for 1 minute. If knocked unconscious or incapacitated your stance breaks. Spend 1 Grit to enter or change stances. 1 Stance can be active at a time.

Deadeye Stance

If you do not move this turn, your first hit with a Sights weapon deals +1d6 damage.

After making an attack, you may move up to 10 feet without provoking opportunity attacks once per turn.

If you did not move on your turn, gain +2 AC until the start of your next turn.

Homebrew / Classes

Undead Sovereign

Undead Sovereign

An Undead Sovereign commands death beyond the boundaries of ordinary necromancy. Beasts, giants, dragons, and extraplanar creatures become vessels for their power. Their servants sustain them, their command strengthens the dead, and their own body grows increasingly resistant to death.

Prerequisites

You must complete a pure first cycle—20 levels in a single class—with one of the following subclasses:

  • Wizard: School of Necromancy.
  • Druid: Circle of Spores.
  • Cleric: Death Domain.
  • Paladin: Oathbreaker.
  • Warlock: The Undead, The Undying, or The Hexblade.

Other subclasses require staff approval to qualify.

Class Basics

Hit Dice: 1d8 per Undead Sovereign level.

Hit Points: 1d8 (or 5) + your Constitution modifier per Undead Sovereign level.

Additional Proficiencies: Two skills of your choice from Arcana, History, Insight, Medicine, and Religion.

Choose Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma as your Sovereign ability when you enter this class. It is used by your Undead Sovereign spells and features.

Sovereign save DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Sovereign ability modifier.

Spell attack modifier = your proficiency bonus + your Sovereign ability modifier.

Subclass Selection and Progression

When you enter Undead Sovereign, you may choose an additional subclass from the class in which you completed your first cycle. You retain your existing subclass.

You gain the additional subclass’s features when your Undead Sovereign class level reaches the level at which the parent class normally grants them.

For example, an additional wizard subclass grants its features at Undead Sovereign class levels 2, 6, 10, and 14—progression levels 22, 26, 30, and 34.

When an additional subclass feature refers to your level in its parent class, use your Undead Sovereign class level. Your original subclass continues to use your actual levels in its parent class.

This progression grants only the additional subclass’s features. It does not grant other parent-class features, spell slots, or increases to parent-class resources unless the additional subclass feature explicitly grants them.

Progression

Your progression level equals 20 + your Undead Sovereign class levels. All feature levels below refer to progression level.

Your additional subclass follows the Subclass Selection and Progression rules above.

Progression Level Features
21 Spellcasting, Greater Reanimation, Grave Command
22 Greater Grim Harvest
23 Graveborn Resilience
24 Ability Score Improvement
25 Unhallowed Might, Reanimation Improvement
26 Eternal Legion
27 Grave Command Improvement
28 Ability Score Improvement
29 Withering Power, Reanimation Improvement
30 Beyond Undeath
31 Graveborn Resilience Improvement
32 Ability Score Improvement
33 Titanic Reanimation, Reanimation Improvement
34 Sovereign Command
35 Greater Grim Harvest Improvement
36 Ability Score Improvement
37 Grave Renewal, Reanimation Improvement
38 Deathless Command
39 Ability Score Improvement
40 Necromantic Ascension

PL 21: Spellcasting

You gain spell slots and can prepare spells from the Undead Sovereign spell list.

Spell Slots

The table shows the number and level of spell slots this feature grants. All these slots are the same level. You regain expended slots when you finish a long rest.

Progression Level Spell Slots Slot Level
21–22 2 1st
23–24 2 2nd
25–26 2 3rd
27–28 2 4th
29–30 2 5th
31–36 3 5th
37–40 4 5th

These slots are additional to those granted by your other classes. Undead Sovereign levels do not otherwise advance another class’s spellcasting or spell-slot progression.

Preparing Spells

When you finish a long rest, prepare a number of spells from the Undead Sovereign spell list equal to your Sovereign ability modifier plus half your Undead Sovereign class level, rounded down (minimum of one spell).

Each spell must be of a level no higher than the slot level shown in the table. Casting a spell does not remove it from your prepared spells.

Spellcasting Ability and Focus

Your Sovereign ability is your spellcasting ability for these spells. They use your Sovereign save DC and spell attack modifier.

You can use an arcane focus or holy symbol as a spellcasting focus for your Undead Sovereign spells.

Using Your Slots

You can use these slots to cast your prepared Undead Sovereign spells or spells you know or have prepared through another class, following that spell’s normal casting rules.

You can also expend these slots for Undead Sovereign features, including Draconic Breath recovery and additional uses of Grave Renewal. Slots from your other classes can also pay these costs.

Undead Sovereign Spell List

Spell Level Spells
1st bane, false life, inflict wounds, protection from evil and good, ray of sickness
2nd blindness/deafness, darkness, gentle repose, ray of enfeeblement, silence
3rd animate dead, bestow curse, fear, speak with dead, vampiric touch
4th blight, death ward, Evard’s black tentacles, phantasmal killer
5th antilife shell, cloudkill, contagion, danse macabre, negative energy flood

The free castings granted by Withering Power are separate from your prepared spells and spell slots.

PL 21: Greater Reanimation

You perform a 10-minute ritual over eligible corpses within 30 feet of you. Each rises as an undead under your control, using its original stat block with the changes below.

A corpse must retain enough of its body to support its attacks and movement. Creatures with class levels and remains produced by temporary summoning effects are ineligible. The ritual does not create equipment.

Reanimation Limits

New creature types are added to those already unlocked. Reanimation Improvements increase your limits as shown below.

Progression Level New Creature Types Maximum CR per Creature Total CR Budget
21 Humanoids, Beasts 2 4
25 Monstrosities 4 8
29 Giants 6 12
33 Dragons 14 16
37 Fiends, Celestials 18 20

You can control up to twice your proficiency bonus in undead through Greater Reanimation. Each must meet your maximum CR per creature, and their combined CR cannot exceed your total CR budget.

Use each creature’s original CR before reanimation, counting CR below 1 as CR 1.

The total CR of creatures you animate between long rests also cannot exceed your budget. Destroying or releasing undead does not refund this allowance. Renewing control does not spend it.

These limits apply only to Greater Reanimation.

Reanimated Creatures

Use the creature’s original stat block with these changes:

  • Its creature type becomes Undead.
  • Its hit-point maximum becomes half its original average hit points, rounded down (minimum 1). Apply bonuses afterward. It rises with this many hit points.
  • Its Intelligence becomes 6 if it was higher. It understands your languages and can speak any languages it could speak in life.
  • It gains immunity to poison damage and the poisoned condition. It requires no air, food, drink, or sleep.
  • It retains its size, Armor Class, movement, senses, other ability scores, saving throw and skill bonuses, damage resistances, damage immunities, damage vulnerabilities, and condition immunities.
  • It retains weapon attacks and Multiattack. Retained attacks keep their damage, reach, range, and any effects that grapple, restrain through a grapple, knock prone, or swallow. They lose all other additional effects. Multiattack allows only retained weapon attacks.
  • It loses all original traits and all other original actions, bonus actions, and reactions, including spellcasting, Legendary Resistance, legendary actions, mythic actions, and lair actions.
  • If it is proficient with a weapon it gains the ability to use that weapons mastery.
  • It can take ordinary actions such as Dash, Disengage, and Dodge, make opportunity attacks, and use abilities granted by Undead Sovereign.

Prepare its modified stat block when you animate it and reuse that stat block during play.

Initiative

Undead created through Greater Reanimation take their turns immediately after yours. You choose their order each round. Each has its own movement, action, bonus action, and reaction.

Control

Your control lasts for 24 hours. Another 10-minute ritual renews control over any number of these undead within 30 feet for a further 24 hours.

You can release an undead at any time without an action. If released or your control expires, it becomes an inanimate corpse.

This feature cannot take control of another creature’s undead.

PL 21: Grave Command

As a bonus action, mentally issue orders to any or all undead under your control within 60 feet. They follow those orders on their turns until completed or replaced. Without orders, undead created through Greater Reanimation defend themselves.

Orders can direct any action available to the undead, including Draconic Breath. The undead must expend any required use.

This replaces their usual command range and action requirement. It does not extend their existence or your control.

At progression level 27, the range increases to 120 feet. When you use this bonus action, you can also choose one commanded undead. It can immediately use its reaction to move up to half its speed without provoking opportunity attacks.

This movement still requires your bonus action when you gain Deathless Command.

PL 22: Greater Grim Harvest

When you or an undead under your control reduces a creature within 60 feet of you to 0 hit points, you can regain hit points equal to your Sovereign ability modifier plus twice your proficiency bonus.

Once you use this feature, you cannot use it again until the start of your next turn.

Constructs, Undead, and creatures you summoned or control do not trigger this healing. You cannot benefit from both this feature and Grim Harvest on the same turn.

At progression level 35, the healing increases to your Sovereign ability modifier plus three times your proficiency bonus. Any healing beyond your hit-point maximum becomes temporary hit points, which last for 1 minute.

PL 23: Graveborn Resilience

You gain resistance to necrotic and poison damage, and advantage on saving throws to avoid or end the poisoned condition.

At progression level 31, you become immune to poison damage and the poisoned condition.

PL 24: Ability Score Improvement

At progression levels 24, 28, 32, 36, and 39, increase one ability score by 2, or two ability scores by 1 each.

You cannot increase a score above 20 using this feature. Any option to choose a feat instead follows TWR’s rules.

PL 25: Unhallowed Might

Weapon attacks made by undead under your control count as magical for overcoming resistance and immunity to nonmagical attacks and damage.

When one of these undead hits with a weapon attack, you can replace all of that attack’s damage types with necrotic damage. Choose before rolling damage; the amount is unchanged.

PL 26: Eternal Legion

During a 10-minute ritual, designate up to your proficiency bonus in undead you created and currently control as your Eternal Legion.

Your control over them no longer expires with time. This does not extend a temporary summon’s duration or prevent another effect from ending your control. Undead created through Greater Reanimation still count toward its limits.

You can replace members during another 10-minute ritual. Removing a member ends this indefinite control; any unexpired control from its original spell or feature remains.

You cannot have more members of your Eternal Legion than your proficiency bonus.

PL 29: Withering Power

When you or an undead under your control deals necrotic damage to a creature, you can prevent that creature from regaining hit points until the start of your next turn.

Once you use this effect, you cannot use it again until the start of your next turn.

You can also cast animate dead at 3rd level and create undead at 6th level once each without expending a spell slot or preparing the spell. You regain both castings when you finish a long rest. Their normal components, casting times, and restrictions apply.

These castings use your Sovereign ability. This feature does not add create undead to your prepared spells or grant a 6th-level spell slot.

Undead created by these spells follow their normal rules, except where another Undead Sovereign feature explicitly changes them.

PL 30: Beyond Undeath

You become immune to necrotic damage. Your hit-point maximum cannot be reduced, and you cannot be aged magically.

When you would drop to 0 hit points without being killed outright, you can destroy an undead under your control within 120 feet that has at least 1 hit point. You drop to 1 hit point instead. This requires no action.

Once you preserve yourself this way, you cannot do so again until you finish a long rest.

PL 33: Titanic Reanimation

Undead created through Greater Reanimation gain a bonus to their hit-point maximum equal to twice your Undead Sovereign class level.

Apply this bonus after halving their original hit points. The bonus updates as you gain levels in this class.

Draconic Breath

When you animate a dragon through Greater Reanimation, choose one damaging breath weapon it possessed in life that used a cone or line. If it had an eligible breath weapon, it gains the following action:

Draconic Breath. As an action, the dragon exhales in a 30-foot cone or a 60-foot-long, 5-foot-wide line, matching the chosen breath’s shape.

Each creature in the area must make a saving throw against your Sovereign save DC, using the original breath’s saving throw ability. A creature takes 8d8 damage on a failed save, or half as much on a success.

The breath retains its original damage type, but loses its additional effects and recharge.

Shared Breath Uses

You have three uses of Draconic Breath shared among all dragons under your control that possess this action. Each activation expends one use.

You regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest. As a bonus action, you can expend a spell slot of 3rd level or higher to restore one expended use, up to a maximum of three available uses.

Creating, replacing, or reanimating undead does not restore uses.

PL 34: Sovereign Command

Starting at 34th level, you can use magic to bring undead under your control, even those created by other necromancers. As an action, you can choose two undead that you can see within 60 feet of you. That creature must make a Charisma saving throw against your undead sovereign spell save DC. If it succeeds, you can't use this feature on it again. If it fails, it becomes friendly to you and obeys your commands until you use this feature again.

Intelligent undead are harder to control in this way. If the target has an Intelligence of 8 or higher, it has advantage on the saving throw. If it fails the saving throw and has an Intelligence of 12 or higher, it can repeat the saving throw at the end of every hour until it succeeds and breaks free.

PL 37: Grave Renewal

When you use Greater Grim Harvest, you can give its healing to one undead under your control within 60 feet instead of yourself. Any healing beyond that undead’s hit-point maximum becomes temporary hit points, which last for 1 minute.

You can do so even if you are at your hit-point maximum.

Additionally, as an action, choose a number of undead under your control within 60 feet up to your Sovereign ability modifier (minimum of one). Each regains hit points equal to twice your Undead Sovereign class level.

You can use this action once without expending a spell slot, regaining that use when you finish a long rest. Additional uses each require a spell slot of 5th level or higher, expended as part of the action.

Neither benefit restores a destroyed undead.

PL 38: Deathless Command

You can issue orders through Grave Command anywhere on the same plane of existence without using an action or bonus action.

The reaction movement granted by Grave Command at progression level 27 gains this range but still requires your bonus action and the undead’s reaction.

Sovereign Command also gains this range but still requires your action action.This feature does not extend an undead’s existence or the duration of your control.

PL 40: Necromantic Ascension

Your Sovereign ability score and Constitution score each increase by 4, to a maximum of 30.

Homebrew / Classes

Warmage

Warmage

THE WARMAGE

A Complete Class for Fifth Edition

An elf recites the motions for the simplest spell she knows, repeating them until she knows they are perfect. With a single precise stroke she unleashes a wave of arcane energy, focused into a searing blue beam.

A tiefling waves her hands to conjure floating greatswords of humming blue energy that dance about in mesmerizing and deadly arcs. One blade takes on an aspect of fire, the other lightning, as she begins to cleave through the goblinoid horde.

Waving a black-and-red checkered banner, a dragonborn king charges into the fore. At his sides are warmages of all houses, a chessboard of elite arcanists poised to turn the tide of battle.

Cantrip Masters

While other spellcasters aspire to grander and more complex spells, warmages refine and master the most fundamental magic: cantrips. A warmage wields magic the way a warrior uses a sword, a bow or an axe — as a weapon to be perfected, not as an unknowable force to be feared. In contrast to sorcerers and wizards, their magic is a trainable skill, one that can be mastered by almost anyone with discipline and aptitude. Warmages therefore stand among the most fearsome of spellcasters while commanding only the most rudimentary of spells.

A warmage does not out-damage a wizard. She out-manoeuvres one. The same fire bolt that a first-year apprentice throws becomes, in a warmage’s hands, a cone of flame, a spray of embers that catches three goblins at once, a shot that punches through a stone pillar, or a blast that knocks a troll flat on its back — because she has spent years learning what the spell can be made to do rather than searching for a bigger one.

Strategic Geniuses

Warmages have a long and storied history as masterful strategists and tacticians, both in grand battles and in personal skirmishes. If a warmage is outgunned or outnumbered, they will try to outthink their foes, which works more often than not. Warmages demonstrate an efficient kind of pragmatism, owing perhaps to their ability to solve many problems with just a few magical tools.

Aligned Free Agents

While some warmages are fully self-taught, the majority join a house: a loose confederation of warmages who practise together and share secrets of the trade. Houses teach invaluable battlefield strategy, but each house also touts its own brands of tactics and styles of magical trickery. The House of Knights emphasises armour and martial prowess; the House of Kings emphasises battlefield command.

By way of metaphor, houses that value honour and teamwork above all else brand themselves after games of strategy — the Bishops, Kings, Knights, Pawns and Rooks — whereas those who epitomise self-reliance name themselves for games of chance. This division dates back to the earliest warmage masters. Legend has it that the first two masters separated when one decided to found a college; the other, out of spite, built a casino outside its grounds. The gamblers of that casino are the House of Fortune, and they have never once apologised.

Creating a Warmage

Warmages come from all walks of life, so as you build yours, consider where you first learned the fundamentals of magic. You might have picked up cantrips from a fellow adventurer or in the early stages of wizarding training. You could be entirely self-taught. Choose an Arcane Initiation that best fits your character’s history with magic.

Consider also how you feel about magic as a whole. Are you envious of other spellcasters, or confident you could best them regardless? Did you once pine to be a wizard, but find you could never muster enough true magic to form a spell slot? Did you choose warmagistry to hone your talents to their absolute peak, or to wield power no warrior can equal?

Lastly, consider your prospective House. Though you do not choose one until 3rd level, your aspirations might shape which you favour. If you would like to dabble in greater arcane magic, the House of Bishops is the best fit. If the clashing of swords at the frontline piques your interest, consider the House of Knights. If you would rather not be told which of the two you are, the House of Pawns will have you.

Quick Build

Make Intelligence your highest ability score, followed by Constitution. Make Strength your third highest if you plan to take the House of Knights, or Dexterity otherwise. Choose the chill touch, force dart, force weapon and phantom grapnel cantrips, and the Adventurer Arcane Initiation. Take the Blaster or Resistive fighting style, and pick any background that emphasises magical discipline. At 2nd level, take the Blasting Flourish and Mystical Armor.

Class Features

As a warmage, you gain the following class features.

The Warmage table

1st +2 Spellcasting, Arcane Initiation, Arcane Fighting Style 4 — —
2nd +2 Warmage Edge, Warmage Tricks, Cantrip Flourishes 4 — 2
3rd +2 Warmage House 5 — 3
