20th +6 Master Warmage 10 5 10

Hit Points

Hit Dice: 1d8 per warmage level.

Hit Points at 1st Level: 8 + your Constitution modifier.

Hit Points at Higher Levels: 1d8 (or 5) + your Constitution modifier per warmage level after 1st.

Proficiencies

Armor: Light armor

Weapons: Simple weapons

Tools: One artisan’s kit of your choice, one gaming set of your choice

Saving Throws: Constitution, Intelligence

Skills: Choose two from Acrobatics, Animal Handling, Arcana, Athletics, History, Investigation, Medicine, Perception and Survival

Equipment

You start with the following equipment, in addition to the equipment granted by your background:

  • Leather armor, a dagger, and any simple weapon

  • (a) a component pouch or (b) an arcane focus

  • (a) an explorer’s pack or (b) a scholar’s pack

  • A gaming set

Spellcasting

At 1st level you begin to learn the simple yet potent brand of spellcasting for which warmages are known.

Cantrips

You know four cantrips of your choice from the warmage spell list. You learn additional warmage cantrips of your choice at higher levels, as shown in the Cantrips Known column of the Warmage table. Additionally, when you gain a level in this class you can replace one warmage cantrip you know with another from the warmage spell list.

Spellcasting Ability

Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for your warmage spells, since you learn your spells through practice and mental discipline. You use your Intelligence whenever a spell refers to your spellcasting ability, and you use your Intelligence modifier when setting the saving throw DC for a warmage spell and when making an attack roll with one.

Spell save DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Intelligence modifier

Spell attack modifier = your proficiency bonus + your Intelligence modifier

Spellcasting Focus

You can use an arcane focus as a spellcasting focus for your warmage spells.

Arcane Initiation

Warmages come from all backgrounds and walks of life. At 1st level, choose where you first learned the basics of magic. The two cantrips your initiation grants do not count against your number of cantrips known.

  • Adventurer. You picked up your magic informally by travelling with a dozen different mages over the years. You learn mage hand and ray of frost.

  • Circus Performer. You learned a few simple tricks to participate in a sideshow act. You learn dancing lights and minor illusion.

  • Eldritch Event. An influx of insidious magic left an imprint on you. You learn chill touch and message.

  • Mercenary. You mastered the fundamentals of war magic to engage in battle with similarly armed arcanists. You learn arc blade and true strike.

  • Self-Taught. You taught yourself the fundamentals from a dusty tome or an abandoned scroll. You learn fire bolt and light.

  • Survival. To stay alive in the wilderness, you taught yourself to cast simple spells. You learn druidcraft and shillelagh.

  • Temple. A monastery or temple educated you in the ways of gentle healing magic. You learn sacred flame and spare the dying.

  • Tower Apprentice. You apprenticed under a spellcaster who taught you the fundamentals of arcana. You learn prestidigitation and shocking grasp.

Arcane Fighting Style

Warmages learn that magic is the purest of weapons and can be wielded as easily as any other. At 1st level, choose one of the following fighting styles.

  • Blaster. You gain a +1 bonus to the saving throw DCs of your warmage spells.

  • Deflector. When you have at least one hand free and a creature hits you with a spell attack or a ranged weapon attack, you can use your reaction to add 3 to your Armor Class against that attack, potentially causing it to miss.

  • Resistive. While you are wearing light armor or are under the effects of the mage armor spell, you gain a +1 bonus to your Armor Class.

  • Sniper. You gain a +1 bonus to ranged spell attack rolls, and your warmage cantrips ignore half cover.

  • Striker. When you hit a creature with a cantrip that requires a melee attack and you exceed the target’s Armor Class by 5 or more, or you score a critical hit, you can add your proficiency bonus to the damage roll.

Warmage Edge

Starting at 2nd level, you can channel raw arcane pressure into the cantrips you have perfected. Once on each of your turns when you deal damage with a warmage cantrip, choose one of that cantrip’s damage rolls and add your Intelligence modifier to it.

At 11th level, you can add your Intelligence modifier to two of that cantrip’s damage rolls, and at 17th level, three. If the cantrip has fewer damage rolls than that, add your Intelligence modifier to the same roll for each remaining application.

For example, a 17th-level warmage casting fire bolt makes one damage roll and so deals 4d10 + three times her Intelligence modifier. The same warmage casting magic daggers makes four separate damage rolls, and adds her Intelligence modifier to three of them.

Cantrip Flourishes

Also at 2nd level, you learn to hang a small piece of battlefield craft off the end of a cantrip. Certain warmage tricks are Flourishes, identified as such in their descriptions. Once on each of your turns, when you deal damage to a creature with a warmage cantrip, you can apply one Flourish you know to that creature.

You can apply only one Flourish on each of your turns, no matter how many you know. A Flourish requires no action and can be applied in the same turn you use Warmage Edge or an Overcharge.

Warmage Tricks

Beginning at 2nd level, you learn to use warmage tricks: special techniques that alter the way you fight, move and cast your spells. You learn two tricks of your choice for which you meet the prerequisites, and you learn additional tricks as shown in the Tricks Known column of the Warmage table. Flourishes are tricks and count against this number.

When you gain a level in this class, you can choose one of the tricks you know and replace it with another trick for which you meet the prerequisites. A level prerequisite refers to your level in this class.

Warmage House

Upon reaching 3rd level, you choose a Warmage House that teaches you a suite of magical strategies: the House of Bishops, Fortune, Kings, Knights, Pawns or Rooks. Your choice grants you features at 3rd level and again at 7th, 10th, 15th and 18th level.

Ability Score Improvement

When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 12th, 16th and 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can’t increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.

Overcharge

Starting at 5th level, you can force more out of a cantrip than it was ever built to carry — not more power, but a different shape entirely. You have a number of Overcharge uses shown in the Overcharge Uses column of the Warmage table. You regain all expended uses when you finish a short or long rest.

When you cast a warmage cantrip, you can expend one use of Overcharge to apply one Overcharge option you know to that casting. You know all of the Lesser Overcharges from 5th level, you learn the Greater Overcharges at 11th level, and you learn the Master Overcharges at 17th level. Where an Overcharge calls for a saving throw, the DC equals your spell save DC.

You can apply only one Overcharge to a single casting of a cantrip until 20th level, and applying an Overcharge does not change the cantrip’s casting time unless the Overcharge says so.

The Overcharge options are described in their own section, following the Flourishes.

Deflective Instinct

At 6th level, you learn to shed hostile magic rather than merely endure it. When you succeed on a saving throw against a spell or other magical effect that would still deal half damage to you on a successful save, you take no damage from it instead.

Strategic Deflection

Starting at 14th level, when a creature casts a spell that forces you to make a saving throw to avoid damage, you can use your reaction to attempt to redirect some of the spell’s energy to a new target. If you succeed on your saving throw against the spell, choose another creature you can see within the spell’s range or up to 30 feet away from you, whichever is closer, to make a saving throw against your spell save DC. The chosen creature can be the original spellcaster.

On a failed save, the creature suffers the effects of the spell as if you had cast it and it had been the original target or been within the area of the spell. Once you use this feature, you can’t use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

Master Warmage

At 20th level, you reach the pinnacle of your warmage prowess. You can apply two different Overcharges to the same casting of a cantrip, expending one use of Overcharge for each. In addition, when you roll initiative and have no uses of Overcharge remaining, you regain two uses.

Multiclassing

To take a level in this class as a multiclass character, you must have an Intelligence score of 13 or higher. You gain proficiency with light armor, simple weapons and one gaming set of your choice. Your warmage cantrips do not count against the number of cantrips you know from other classes, and levels in this class do not contribute to your spellcaster level for the purposes of the Multiclass Spellcaster table — except for levels in the House of Bishops, which count as one third of a level, rounded down, in the same manner as an Eldritch Knight.

Cantrip Flourishes

Each Flourish below is a warmage trick. You apply one Flourish on each of your turns, when a warmage cantrip you cast deals damage to a creature. Each Flourish requires the cantrip to have dealt damage of the listed type to that creature. Where a Flourish calls for a saving throw, the DC equals your spell save DC.

Blasting Flourish

Prerequisite: force damage. You push the creature up to 10 feet away from you in a straight line.

Concussive Flourish

Prerequisite: thunder damage. A 15-foot-diameter sphere of magical silence, as per the silence spell, is centred on the creature or on yourself (your choice) and lasts until the start of your next turn.

Corrosive Flourish

Prerequisite: acid damage. The acid eats into the creature’s defences. The next attack roll made against it before the start of your next turn treats its Armor Class as 2 lower.

Draining Flourish

Prerequisite: necrotic or poison damage. You siphon some of the creature’s life force and gain temporary hit points equal to your Intelligence modifier, which last for 1 minute. Temporary hit points from this Flourish don’t stack with themselves.

Explosive Flourish

Prerequisite: fire damage. The fire detonates. Each creature within 5 feet of the target other than you and the target must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or take half the fire damage dealt to the target.

Icy Flourish

Prerequisite: cold damage. Until the start of your next turn, the creature’s speed is reduced by 10 feet and it takes a −2 penalty to the next attack roll it makes.

Radiant Flourish

Prerequisite: radiant damage. Until the start of your next turn, the creature sheds dim light in a 10-foot radius and can’t benefit from being invisible or from being hidden.

Rending Flourish

Prerequisite: bludgeoning, piercing or slashing damage. The creature can’t take reactions until the start of your next turn.

Static Flourish

Prerequisite: lightning damage. You sap part of the energy into a charge that clings to your body until the start of your next turn. While charged, you can use your reaction when you take damage from a creature you can see within 5 feet of you to deal lightning damage equal to your Intelligence modifier to that creature.

Suppressing Flourish

Prerequisite: 5th level, any damage type. The creature has disadvantage on the next attack roll it makes against a target other than you before the start of your next turn.

Overcharges

You expend one use of Overcharge to apply one of these options to a warmage cantrip as you cast it. Where an Overcharge calls for a saving throw, the DC equals your spell save DC.

Lesser Overcharges

You know all of these from 5th level.

Barrage

If the cantrip requires a single attack roll, make one additional attack roll against a different creature within 15 feet of the original target. On a hit, that creature takes the cantrip’s damage. Warmage Edge can enhance the damage of only one of the two attacks.

Breach

The cantrip ignores cover, and the target’s resistance to the cantrip’s damage type has no effect against it. If the cantrip damages an object, it deals double damage to it.

Concussion

The target must succeed on a Strength saving throw or be pushed 10 feet away from you and knocked prone.

Quicken

You cast the cantrip as a bonus action instead of an action. You can use this Overcharge only once on each of your turns.

Refract

A cantrip that targets a single creature instead fills a 15-foot cone originating from you. Each creature in the cone must make a Dexterity saving throw, taking the cantrip’s damage on a failed save and half as much damage on a successful one. Warmage Edge can enhance the damage against only one creature. If the cantrip normally requires an attack roll, you make no attack roll when you use this Overcharge.

Snare

The target must make a Strength or Dexterity saving throw (its choice). On a failed save, its speed becomes 0 until the start of your next turn.

Greater Overcharges

You learn these at 11th level, in addition to the Lesser Overcharges.

Displace

After the cantrip resolves, either you or the target teleports up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space that you can see. An unwilling target can resist with a Charisma saving throw.

Overload

Treat each of the cantrip’s damage dice against one target of your choice as having rolled the highest number possible. You can’t apply this Overcharge to a cantrip that has scored a critical hit.

Rupture

Until the start of your next turn, the target has disadvantage on the next saving throw it makes and it can’t regain hit points.

Master Overcharges

You learn these at 17th level, in addition to the Lesser and Greater Overcharges.

Cataclysm

A cantrip that targets a single creature instead fills a 20-foot-radius sphere centred on a point you can see within the cantrip’s range. Each creature in the area must make a Dexterity saving throw, taking the cantrip’s damage on a failed save and half as much damage on a successful one. Warmage Edge can enhance the damage against only one creature. If the cantrip normally requires an attack roll, you make no attack roll when you use this Overcharge.

Unmake

Until the end of your next turn, the target’s Armor Class is reduced by 2 and it has disadvantage on attack rolls.

Warmage Tricks

The tricks below are presented in alphabetical order. The ten Flourishes described earlier are also warmage tricks. If a trick has prerequisites, you must meet them to choose it; you can choose the trick at the same time you meet its prerequisites.

Bishop’s Maneuver

Prerequisites: 10th level, House of Bishops

You can take the Disengage action as a bonus action. When you do so, your walking speed increases by 10 feet until the end of your turn.

Blinding Light

Prerequisite: light cantrip

When you use the light cantrip to target an object you are holding, you can direct a flare at a creature you can see within 10 feet of you. That creature must make a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC, and on a failed save it is blinded until the start of your next turn.

After a creature has failed a saving throw against this trick, it has advantage on all saving throws against it for the next 24 hours.

Castle

Prerequisites: 10th level, House of Rooks

As an action, you can choose a willing Small or Medium creature you can see within 120 feet of you. You both teleport, swapping places. Once you use this trick, you can’t use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

Chivalrous Presence

Prerequisite: House of Knights

You gain proficiency in the Insight and Persuasion skills, and you have advantage on ability checks you make to interact with nobility.

Commander’s Steed

Prerequisite: House of Kings

You learn the find steed spell. You can cast it once without expending a spell slot, and you regain the ability to do so when you finish a long rest. Your steed is more resilient than most: its hit point maximum increases by an amount equal to your warmage level.

Encryptogram

Prerequisite: cryptogram cantrip

Your knowledge of ciphers has improved your magically clandestine communications. When you cast cryptogram, its limit is 20 characters instead of 8, and only the specified recipient can read the message.

Extended Range

Whenever you cast a warmage cantrip that has a range of 5 feet or greater, its range is doubled.

Field Medic

Prerequisite: House of Bishops

You learn the spare the dying cantrip, which doesn’t count against your number of cantrips known. Additionally, when you cast spare the dying on a creature that has 0 hit points, the target regains 1 hit point and gains temporary hit points equal to your warmage level, which last for 1 minute. Once a creature regains hit points from this trick, it can’t do so again until it finishes a long rest.

Flexible Range

Being within 5 feet of a hostile creature doesn’t impose disadvantage on your ranged spell attack rolls. Additionally, when you cast a warmage cantrip that requires a melee spell attack, its range increases to 10 feet.

Fold

Prerequisites: 10th level, House of Fortune

You have learned to accept defeat graciously. As a reaction when you are hit by an attack, you can expend three Fate Dice to cast the shield spell without expending a spell slot. Once you use this trick, you can’t use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

Gamble

Prerequisites: House of Fortune, cheat cantrip

You are always under the effects of the cheat cantrip. Additionally, when you miss with an attack roll or you fail an ability check or saving throw, you can reroll the d20 and must use the new roll. Once you use this ability, you can’t use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

Infinite Variation

Prerequisite: prestidigitation cantrip

You have become exceptionally skilled at using prestidigitation to mimic other spells. When you cast prestidigitation, you can use it to emulate the effects of any cantrip that doesn’t deal damage from the bard, sorcerer, warlock or wizard spell list, even one you don’t know. To do so, you must succeed on a DC 15 Intelligence (Arcana) check, otherwise the spell fails. Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for a cantrip cast using this trick, and it counts as a warmage cantrip for you.

Knight’s Aegis

Prerequisites: 10th level, House of Knights, force buckler cantrip

When you cast the force buckler cantrip, it lasts until the end of your next turn and it doesn’t end early if you are hit by an attack.

Leading Edge Tactics

Prerequisite: House of Kings

You always have a plan when engaging the enemy. Attacks against you have disadvantage during the first round of combat. You can’t use this feature when you are surprised.

Lieutenant’s Demand

Prerequisites: 10th level, House of Kings

You can cast the command spell without expending a spell slot, using your Intelligence as your spellcasting ability for it. Once you use this trick, you can’t use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

Mage Hand Knack

Prerequisite: mage hand cantrip

Your skill with mage hand allows you to use it as an extension of yourself. When you cast the spell, and as a bonus action on your subsequent turns, you can use one of the following effects with the hand.

  • Press. The hand pushes against a Large or smaller creature within 5 feet of it. Choose a direction away from that creature. Every foot of movement in that direction while the hand is pressing against it costs the creature 1 extra foot of movement. The hand continues to press until the spell ends or you use your bonus action to use a different effect.

  • Punch. The hand strikes one creature or object within 5 feet of it. Make a melee spell attack for the hand. On a hit, the target takes 1d6 force damage.

  • Seize. The hand grabs a Small or smaller creature and attempts to grapple it. The creature must succeed on a Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics) check of its choice against your spell save DC or be grappled by the hand. The hand continues to grapple until the target uses an action to break the grapple on its turn, the spell ends, or you use your bonus action to use a different effect.

Minor Shadow Illusion

Prerequisite: minor illusion cantrip

When you create the image of an object in an unoccupied space using minor illusion, you can fill it with fibres of shadowstuff, causing it to become partially real. No matter what form the semi-real object takes, it must be no larger than a 5-foot cube. It has AC 10 and 5 hit points and it weighs 5 pounds. You can have only one semi-real illusion at a time, and while it exists the cantrip requires your concentration.

The illusion can’t replicate a creature, but it can deal damage to a creature within its 5-foot cube. If the illusion is of an object that could deal damage, a creature that enters the object’s cube for the first time on a turn or begins its turn there must make an Intelligence saving throw against your spell save DC, taking 1d6 damage of a type appropriate to the illusion on a failed save. This damage increases to 2d6 at 5th level, 3d6 at 11th level and 4d6 at 17th level. This damage can’t trigger Warmage Edge, a Flourish or an Overcharge.

Mystical Armor

You can cast the mage armor spell on yourself at will, without expending a spell slot and without spell components.

Mystical Athlete

Prerequisite: quickstep or springheel cantrip

When you cast quickstep, your speed increases by 20 feet instead of 10 feet. When you cast springheel, your jumping distance increases by 20 feet instead of 10 feet. If you know both of these cantrips, you can cast both of them as part of the same bonus action.

Mystical Vision

You can cast the detect magic spell at will, without expending a spell slot.

Mystical Weaponmaster

Prerequisite: force weapon or magic daggers cantrip

When you roll a 1 on the d20 for an attack roll with force weapon or magic daggers, you can reroll the die and must use the new roll.

Phantom Hookshot

Prerequisite: phantom grapnel cantrip

You can cast the phantom grapnel cantrip as a bonus action. If you do so, its range is reduced to 15 feet. When you cast the spell as an action, creatures are pulled an extra 10 feet toward you by the spell.

Rapid Fortification

Prerequisite: mending cantrip

You can cast the mending cantrip as an action or a bonus action. If you cast it as an action, you can use one of the following effects.

  • You restore a single nonmagical object, such as a door, cart or window, to pristine condition if at least half of its parts are present. The object can be no larger than 10 cubic feet, or 1 cubic foot if it is exceptionally complex, such as a clock.

  • You create simple fortifications, such as sealing a door shut, adding wooden planks to a window, or building a short stone wall no larger than 10 cubic feet. You must have the materials present to use this ability.

Severe Cantrip

When a creature rolls a 1 on a saving throw against one of your warmage cantrips, it automatically fails the save and takes twice the number of damage dice dealt by the spell, as if you had scored a critical hit. The additional damage applies only to the creature that rolled a 1.

Signature Focus

Prerequisite: 5th level

When you finish a long rest, you can place a unique sigil on a simple or martial weapon, which becomes your signature focus until you use this ability again. The weapon becomes magical, and you can use it as a spellcasting focus for your warmage spells. Your signature focus is bonded to you and gains the following properties.

  • As a bonus action, you can call your signature focus to your hand, as long as you are on the same plane of existence as it.

  • You can add your Intelligence modifier, instead of your Strength or Dexterity modifier, to attack and damage rolls made with it.

  • Your signature focus has a number of charges equal to your Intelligence modifier, minimum 1. Once on each of your turns, when you deal damage to a creature with the focus or with a cantrip cast through it, you can expend 1 charge to deal an extra 1d8 force damage to that creature. The focus regains all expended charges when you finish a long rest.

Snake Eyes

Prerequisites: 10th level, House of Fortune

If you roll a 1 or a 2 on a Fate Die, you keep the die instead of giving it to the GM.

Unerring Strike

Prerequisites: 10th level, true strike cantrip

When you cast the true strike cantrip, you can concentrate on it for up to 1 minute. You gain advantage on the first attack roll you make against the target on each of your turns while you maintain concentration on it.

Vanguard Rush

Prerequisite: House of Knights

Once on each of your turns, when you make a melee attack against a creature you can see, you can move up to 10 feet toward that creature immediately before making the attack. This movement doesn’t provoke opportunity attacks and doesn’t count against your movement for the turn.

Warmage Spells

Unlike other spellcasters, warmages learn only cantrips, which they pick from the following list as they gain levels in this class. Cantrips marked with an asterisk are described in full in this document; the rest are standard cantrips found in the core rules. If a cantrip appears on the wizard spell list that is not represented here, the GM can allow it to be a warmage spell as well.

Acid Splash Force Weapon * Poison Spray
Arc Blade * Frigid Blade * Prestidigitation
Burning Blade * Light Produce Flame
Card Trick * Lightning Surge * Quickstep *
Caustic Blade * Mage Hand Ray of Frost
Cheat * Magic Daggers * Shocking Grasp
Chill Touch Mending Sonic Pulse *
Cryptogram * Minor Illusion Springheel *
Finger Guns * Moment to Think * Thunderous Distortion *
Fire Bolt Phantom Grapnel * True Strike
Force Buckler *
Force Dart *

The cantrips granted by an Arcane Initiation — dancing lights, druidcraft, message, sacred flame, shillelagh and spare the dying — are also warmage spells for you if your initiation grants them.

Warmage Houses

Each warmage is defined by their chosen House, which teaches them valuable skills and offers a confederation of allies they will keep for the rest of their lives. Five are named for the pieces of the board; the sixth is named for the wheel.

  • House of Bishops
  • House of Fortune
  • House of Kings
  • House of Knights
  • House of Pawns
  • House of Rooks
Homebrew / Classes

Wizard (Version X)

Wizard (Version X)

The Wizard Class

Dungeons and Dragons 5e’s Wizard has always felt underwhelming to me. Not in terms of power, mind you, wizards are certainly strong in their own rights. Nor in their flavor, the flavor of an arcane scholar and pursuer of knowledge is a great draw... However, the wizard’s ability to mirror that flavor mechanically has always felt less than adequate in my eyes.

This overhaul of the wizard class aims to reinforce the wizard’s scholarly nature, along with giving them a sense of experimentation that was missing from the source material. After all, what’s a wizard without some crazy magical experiments to keep them occupied?

Creating a Wizard

Missing.

Wizard Table

Missing.

Class Features

As a Wizard, you gain the following class features

Hit Points

Hit Dice: 1d6 per wizard level

Hit Points at 1st Level: 6 + your Constitution modifier

Hit Points at Higher Levels: 1d6 (or 4) + your constitution modifier per wizard level after 1st

Proficiencies

Armor: None

Weapons: Simple Weapons

Tools: Calligraphy Tools

Saving Throws: Intelligence, Wisdom

Skills: Choose two from Arcana, History, Insight, Investigation, Medicine, and Religion

Equipment

Missing.

Spellcasting

As a student of arcane magic, you have a spellbook containing spells that show the first glimmerings of your true power. See Spell Rules for the general rules of spellcasting and the Spells Listing for the wizard spell list. Use the 2014 PHB’s Wizard table where applicable.

Cantrips

At 1st level, you know three cantrips of your choice from the wizard spell list. You learn additional wizard cantrips of your choice at higher levels, as shown in the Cantrips Known column of the Wizard table.

Spellbook

At 1st level, you have a spellbook containing six 1st-level wizard spells of your choice. Your spellbook is the repository of the wizard spells you know, except your cantrips, which are fixed in your mind.

Preparing and Casting Spells

The Wizard table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your wizard spells of 1st-level and higher. To cast one of these spells, you must expend a spell slot of the spell’s level or higher. You regain all expended spell slots when you finish a long rest.

You prepare the list of wizard spells that are available for you to cast. To do so, choose a number of wizard spells from your spellbook equal to your Intelligence modifier + your wizard level (minimum of one spell). The spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots.

For example, if you’re a 3rd=level wizard, you have four 1st-level and two 2nd-level spell slots. With an Intelligence of 16, your list of prepared spells can include size spells of 1st or 2nd level, in any combination, chosen from your spellbook. If you prepare the 1st-level spell magic missile, you can cast it using a 1st-level or a 2nd-level spell slot. Casting the spell does not remove it from your list of prepared spells.

You can change your list of prepared spells when you finish a long rest. Preparing a new list of wizard spells requires time spent studying your spellbook and memorizing the incantations and gestures you must make to cast the spell: at least 1 minute per spell level for each spell on your list.

Spellcasting Ability

Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for your wizard spells, since you learn your spells through dedicated study and memorization. You use your Intelligence whenever a spell refers to your spellcasting ability. In addition, you use your Intelligence modifier when setting the saving throw DC for a wizard spell you cast, and when making an attack roll with one.

Spell Save DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Intelligence modifier

Spell Attack Modifier = your proficiency bonus + your Intelligence modifier

Spellcasting Focus

You can use an arcane focus (see the Adventuring Gear section) as a spellcasting focus for your wizard spells.

Learning Spells of 1st Level and Higher

Each time you gain a wizard level, you can add two wizard spells of your choice to your spellbook for free. Each of these spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots, as shown on the Wizard table. On your adventures, you might find other spells that you can add to your spellbook.

Spellbook

The spells you add to your spellbook as you gain levels reflect the arcane research you conduct on your own, as well as intellectual breakthroughs you have had about the nature of the multiverse. You might find other spells during your adventures. You could discover a spell recorded on a scroll in an evil wizard’s chest, for example, or in a dusty tome in an ancient library.

Copying a Spell into the Book

When you find a wizard spell of 1st level or higher, you can add it to your spellbook if it is of a spell level you can prepare and if you can spare the time to decipher and copy it.

Copying that spell into your spellbook involves reproducing the basic form of the spell, then deciphering the unique system of notation used by the wizard that wrote it. You must practice the spell until you understand the sounds or gestures required, then transcribe it into your spellbook using your own notation.

For each level of the spell, the process takes 2 hours and costs 50 gp. The cost represents material components you expend as you experiment with the spell to master it, as well as the fine inks you need to record it. Once you have spent this time and money, you can prepare the spell just like your other spells.

Replacing the Book

You can copy a spell from your own spellbook into another book-for example, if you want to make a backup copy of your spellbook. This is just like copying a new spell into your spellbook, but faster and easier, since you understand your own notation and already know how to cast the spell. You need spend only 1 hour and 10 gp for each level of the copied spell.

If you lose your spellbook, you can use the same procedure to transcribe the spells that you have prepared into a new spellbook. Filling out the remainder of your spellbook requires you to find new spells to do so. For this reason, many wizards keep backup spellbooks in a safe place.

The Book’s Appearance

Your spellbook is a unique compilation of spells, with its own decorative flourishes and margin notes. It might be a plain, functional leather volume that you received from a gift from your master, a finely bound gilt-edged tome you found in an ancient library, or even a loose collection of notes scrounged together after you lost your previous spellbook in a mishap.

Arcane Recovery

You have learned to regain some of your magical energy by studying your spellbook. You have a pool of spell levels equal to half your wizard level (rounded up), which you can use to recover your expended spell slots. When you finish a short rest, you can spend any number of spell levels from the pool to regain expended spell slots of a combined spell level equal to the amount of levels you expended.

For example, if you’re a 4th-level wizard, you have a pool of two spell levels. You can spend these to regain a 2nd-level spell slot, or two 1st-level spell slots.

You regain all expended spell levels from this pool when you finish a long rest.

Ritual Master

You can cast any spell in your spellbook with the ritual tag as a ritual, even if you don’t have it prepared.

Arcane Tradition

When you reach 2nd level, you choose an arcane tradition, shaping your practice of magic through one of the eight schools: Abjuration, Conjuration, Divination, Enchantment, Evocation, Illusion, Necromancy, or Transmutation. Alternate traditions are also available, and grant their own features.

Your choice grants you features at 2nd level, and again at 6th, 10th, and 14th level.

Signature Spells

At 3rd level, your mastery over certain spells grows onto you, and you can cast them with little effort. Choose one 1st-level spell from your spellbook. You always have the chosen spell prepared, and it does not count towards your total number of spells prepared.

You can cast a signature spell at its lowest level without expending a spell slot. Once you cast a signature spell in this way, you cannot do so again until you finish a short or long rest.

When you reach higher levels, you gain additional signature spells of higher levels. You gain one 2nd-level signature spell at 7th level, and one 3rd-level signature spell at 13th level.

Ability Score Improvement

When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can’t increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.

Using the optional feats rule, you can forgo taking this feature to take a feat of your choice instead.

Memorize Spell

At 5th level, your ability to adapt your spells throughout the day increases. Whenever you finish a short rest, you can study your spellbook and replace one of the spells you have prepared for another spell from the book.

Spellforge

When you reach 7th level, your understanding of magic has come to the point where you can modify some of the properties of the spells you know.

You can spend 10 minutes in study, requiring your full concentration and attention (as if concentrating on a spell) to modify one of the spells you have prepared. At the end of the 10 minutes, the chosen spell gains one cosmetic effect of your choice, and one of the following changes of your choice:

  • Components: Remove one of the spell’s components; Verbal, Somatic, or Material. You cannot remove the Material component of a spell that consumes the component.
  • Concentration: If the spell requires Concentration, damage can’t break your concentration on the spell.
  • Damage Type: If the spell has a damage type, replace it with one of the following types: Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, Necrotic, Poison, or Thunder. If the spell has multiple damage types, you change only one of them.
  • Range: If the spell has a range of at least 5 feet and doesn’t have a range of self, increase its range by five times your wizard level.
  • Ritual: If the spell lacks the ritual tag and has a casting time of at least one minute, give it the ritual tag, unless the spell is of 9th level.
  • Targets: If the spell affects one or more creatures and doesn’t have a range of self, it now affects only your allies or enemies (your choice when you cast the spell).

This modification lasts until you modify a spell again or until you finish a long rest. The altered spell cannot be added to your spellbook.

Spellset

Your capacity to experiment with spells has reached new heights at 13th level, granting you the ability to save your work for future use.

While a spell is modified with your Spellforge feature, you can copy it into your spellbook as if it were a normal spell. Doing so requires 30 minutes of work and costs 1,000 gp per spell level, representative of your work grounding the spell in your own notation.

Upon completion, give the spell a name, and the spell is added to your spellbook. It is considered a wizard spell, and you are thereafter able to prepare the spell as normal.

A spell created by this feature can only ever hold two modifications from your Spellforge feature. Any attempts to add more than two modifications to the same spell will fail.

Spell Mastery

At 18th level, you have achieved such mastery over certain spells that you can cast them at will. Your 1st and 2nd level signature spells, as well as any created spell based on them, are able to be cast at will.

Signature Spellforge

When you reach 20th level, your capacity to work with and create branching spells based upon your signature spells reaches untold heights. When you use your spellforge and spellset features on a signature spell, or a spell based on your signature spells, the new limit of modifications is 4, instead of 2.

Additionally, you can prepare a number of extra spells equal to your intelligence modifier. These extra spells must be spells created by spellset based on your signature spells.

Daredevil

Daredevil

Daredevil

The Daredevil fighter thrives on style, versatility and unpredictably. Their use of different weapon types makes them dangerous to any foe and they gain more confidence the more stylish their fighting is.

Daredevil impulse

Starting at 3rd level, every time you make an attack of a type different from the previous attack in the current combat, you gain one Style point. You have a maximum amount of style points equal to your proficiency bonus. When you roll Initiative your Style points reset to 0.

Attack types are classified as: Melee weapon attack, Ranged weapon attack and thrown attacks.

Style Points can be used to power your Flairs.

Flairs:

  • Wide attack: If you hit with a melee attack, you may spend 2 Style points to deal melee damage equal to half your Fighter level to all foes within 5 feet of your target.
  • Laser Focus: Spend 2 Style Points to gain advantage on your next attack roll.
  • Range Extender: You can add 10 feet to any ranged or thrown weapon's normal range for every point spent
  • Rush: Gain 10 feet of movement speed for each Style Point spent until the end of your turn.
  • Burst (4th level and up): As a bonus action, Spend 3 Style points to make a weapon attack.

Hotswap:

At 3rd level, whenever you make an attack roll with a weapon, you can sheathe it and draw another in the same action. You can only do this once per action.

Fight or Flight

From 7th level you have a choice between staying in action and fighting defensively or moving around or to continue as is.  As a bonus action you can choose to either fight or flee from combat.

  • Fight: As a Bonus action you can give yourself a Bonus to your AC equal to the amount of Style Points you spend. This bonus lasts until the end of your next turn or until you are incapacitated. While Fight is active you cannot gain more Style points.
  • Flight: You can spend 2 Style points to disengage, you can't be targeted by opportunity attacks. You gain an additional 10 feet of movement until the end of your turn for every additional Style Point spent.

Double Trouble

You can choose an additional Fighting Style.

Additionally, using the Disengage, Dodge or Dash actions also builds your Style chain. For example: If you use a dodge action and make an attack on your next turn or vice versa you also gain a Style Point

Wild Rush:

Starting at 15th level, when an enemy within 30 feet of you gets incapacitated or restrained you can use 2 Style Points as an reaction to dash straight toward the enemy. You move 10 feet for every point spent (minimum 2 points) and can spend additional Style for added Rush movement. You can  sheath your current weapon and draw another as part of the dash and make a single attack against that target.

Inferno Trigger:

From 18th level, once per short rest you can expend 6 Style points as an action to trigger your Inferno action.

Inferno action: Can attack 6 times, ignore the loading and ammunition properties if the weapon has it. Any Critical hit deals an additional 10 damage of the weapons damage type. These attacks don't provide any Style points

Homebrew / Feats

Deadeye

Deadeye

The Deadeye

The embodiment of grit, luck, and a well-placed shot, fighters who choose this martial archetype strive to emulate paradigms of accuracy. Deadeyes generally prefer fighting from comfortable ranges, employing the use of crossbows, firearms, and even throwing knives if a situation calls for them.

  • 3rd Level - Perfect Sixth
  • 7th Level - Line ‘em Up
  • 10th Level - Gambit
  • 15th Level - Duelist’s Aim
  • 18th Level - High Noon

3rd Level - Perfect Sixth

Once per attack action beginning at 3rd level, when you make a ranged weapon attack roll against a creature, you can add a d6 to the result. You can add the d6 before or after seeing the results of the attack roll, but before the effects are applied. If the result of the d6 is a 6, you severely injure your target. Roll on the severe injury table to see the effect of the injury.

Severe Injury Table

2d6 | Severe Injury

2 | Shock. The target is stunned until the end of its next turn.

3 | Fracture. The target can only take either an action, bonus action, or move on its next turn.

4 | Punctured Lung. The target gains one level of exhaustion for the next minute.

5 | Crushed Throat. The target cannot speak, use verbal components, or use any features that involve its voice until the end of its next turn.

6 | Crushed Grip. The target drops anything it is currently holding, including grappled creatures.

7 | Whiplash. The attack deals one additional die of weapon damage.

8 | Broken Leg. The target’s movement speed is halved until the end of its next turn.

9 | Embedded Ammunition. Until the end of its next turn, for every 5 feet the target moves, it takes 1d6 slashing damage.

10| Tear. The target has disadvantage on melee attacks until the end of its next turn.

11| Blind. The target is blinded until the end of its next turn.

12| Dead Shot. The triggering hit becomes a critical hit.

  • Before you make a ranged weapon attack, you can take a -5 penalty to the attack roll. If you hit, you apply a severe injury immediately. You can only apply one severe injury with each attack action.
  • A creature cannot be affected by the same severe injury more than once at a time, and a creature can expend one use of legendary resistance to ignore a severe injury’s effect.

7th Level - Line ‘em Up

At 7th level, you become a master at hitting successive targets. When you take the attack action on your turn, each time you target a different creature than any other you’ve targeted this turn, you gain a cumulative +1 bonus to the attack roll.

10th Level - Gambit

At 10th level, when you roll initiative, you can gambit a d4, d6, d8, or d10. Roll the chosen die and subtract it from your initiative. Until the end of your next turn, every creature below you in initiative takes extra damage when hit with your ranged attack rolls equal to the chosen die.

15th Level - Duelist’s Aim

At 15th level, when you use the attack action to make a ranged weapon attack and you hit at least three consecutive attacks, your third attack inflicts a severe injury.

18th Level - High Noon

At 18th level, you are adept at ending multiple targets at once. As an action, choose any number of targets that you can see within a cone the size of your weapon’s short range, up to 60 feet. You may make one ranged weapon attack against each target you chose inflicting the Dead Shot severe injury with each of them. You may use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, regaining all uses on a long rest.

Homebrew / Feats

Gladiator (UA)

Gladiator (UA)

Description

Master Brutality and Blood Sport

Gladiators are just as much performers as they are warriors. Whether brawling in underground fighting rings or fighting for survival in bloodstained arenas, a Gladiator combines martial skill with theatrics to awe and intimidate their audiences.

Features:

  • Level 3 - Brutality
  • Level 3 - Combat Theatrics
  • Level 7 - Flourish Parry
  • Level 10 - Bolder Brutalities
  • Level 15 - Brutal Resurgence
  • Level 18 - Mutilate

Level 3 - Brutality

Shaped by the intensity of the arena, you’ve learned to execute brutal martial moves. Once per turn, when you hit a creature with an attack roll using a Melee weapon, you can add one of the following Brutality effects of your choice. You can do this a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Short or Long Rest.

Bleed. You can activate the Sap mastery property in addition to a different mastery property you’re using with that weapon, and the target takes extra damage equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of 1 damage). The extra damage’s type is the same type as the weapon’s type.

Bluff. You can activate the Vex mastery property in addition to a different mastery property you’re using with that weapon, and you have Advantage on the next saving throw you make before the end of your next turn.

Stumble. You can activate the Topple mastery property in addition to a different mastery property you’re using with that weapon, and on its next turn, the target can take only an action or a Bonus Action, not both.

Level 3 - Combat Theatrics

You’ve honed your combat skills to entertain, devastating opponents and dazzling onlookers. You gain the following benefits.

Athletic Flair. Whenever you make a Dexterity (Acrobatics) or Strength (Athletics) check, you gain a bonus to the check equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of +1).

Bonus Proficiency. You gain proficiency in one of these skills of your choice: Acrobatics, Athletics, Deception, Intimidation, or Performance.

Level 7 - Flourish Parry

You’ve learned to stylishly counter blows from your opponents. When an enemy hits you with a melee attack roll, you can take a Reaction to add your Charisma modifier (minimum of +1) to your AC against the attack, potentially causing the attack to miss.

Flourish Counter. If this Reaction causes the attack to miss, you can retaliate with a powerful counterattack as part of the same Reaction. Make an attack roll with a Melee weapon against the triggering creature. If this attack hits, you can use one of your Brutality effects on the target without expending a use of that feature. Once this counterattack hits, you can’t use this feature to make another counterattack until you finish a Long Rest. You can also restore your use of this counterattack by expending a use of Second Wind (no action required).

Level 10 - Bolder Brutalities

Your brutal martial prowess has improved. The following effects are added to your Brutality options.

Rive. You can activate the Cleave mastery property in addition to a different mastery property you’re using with that weapon, and you can add your ability modifier to the damage of the additional attack made as part of that property’s activation.

Rush. You can activate the Push mastery property in addition to a different mastery property you’re using with that weapon, and you can immediately move up to your Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks.

Stagger. You can activate the Slow mastery property in addition to a different mastery property you’re using with that weapon, and the target has Disadvantage on the next saving throw it makes before the end of your next turn.

Level 15 - Brutal Resurgence

Whenever you use your Second Wind to regain Hit Points, you regain an expended use of Brutality. You also regain an expended use of Brutality whenever you use your Action Surge.

Level 18 - Mutilate

When you hit a Bloodied creature with an attack roll, you can attempt to critically injure it. The target makes a Constitution saving throw (DC 8 plus your Charisma modifier and Proficiency Bonus). On a failed save, the target suffers the following effects:

Maimed. If the target takes the Attack action, it can make only one attack.

Sluggish. The target’s Speed is halved, and it has a −2 penalty to its Armor Class.

These effects last until the target regains Hit Points. Once a target fails its saving throw against this feature, you can’t use it again on that creature until you finish a Long Rest.

Homebrew / Feats

Phalanx

Phalanx

Description

A Phalanx draws their strength from their allies and coordination. Phalanx make excellent commanders as their leadership and guidance helps to assure not only their own success, but their entire unit’s as well.

Features:

  • 3rd Level - Tactical Commander
  • 3rd Level - Unbreakable Formation
  • 7th Level - Tactical Authority
  • 13th Level - Perfect Block
  • 18th Level - Battle Tide

3rd Level - Tactical Commander

When you select this specialization at 3rd level, you gain access to your cohesion die, which is a d4. Other features will refer to your cohesion die, and will allow you to roll it. Your cohesion die is not expended when rolled.

Your cohesion die increases to a d6 at 7th level, to a d8 at 13th, and to a d10 at 18th.

3rd Level - Unbreakable Formation

Additionally at 3rd level, you learn to weave your own defenses into those around you, resulting in a stronger whole for both you and your allies. Each creature of your choice within 10 feet of you gains a bonus to saving throws equal to one roll of your cohesion die. Additionally, creatures of your choice that start their turn within that range gain a +1 bonus to their armor class for each creature within 10 feet of you, with a maximum bonus equal to half your proficiency bonus.

7th Level - Tactical Authority

At 7th level, you gain the ability to have greater control over how a fight will play out. When you enter your defensive stance, choose either the dodge, disengage, or dash action. Creatures of your choice within 5 feet of you while your stance is active will be unable to take the chosen action. You may select a new action from the specified list at the start of each of your turns until your stance ends (no action required).

Additionally, creatures of your choice within the same range (other than you) gain a bonus to damage rolls equal to a roll of your cohesion die. They can use this bonus no more than once per turn.

13th Level - Perfect Block

Your ability to use shields extends to protecting your allies as well as you beginning at 13th level. When an ally within 5 feet of you is hit by an attack, you can use your reaction to give them a bonus to their armor class equal to one roll of your cohesion die. If this bonus causes the attack to miss, you may use this reaction again, even if you have already used your reaction this round.

18th Level - Battle Tide

When you reach 18th level, your ability to shift the tide of battle with your presence alone has been realized. As an action, you can grant each creature of your choice within 20 feet of you temporary hit points equal to twice your Bulwark level, and remove all conditions of your choice from them. Once you use this feature, you cannot do so again until you finish a long rest.

Homebrew / Feats

Weapon Master

Weapon Master

Deft Grip

Starting at 3rd level, after you make a weapon attack using the attack action you can use a free action to swap to another weapon.

When you attack with a weapon, you receive a bonus to the attack based on the list below, however you may only benefit from a single bonus once per turn, even if your attack misses; You can however receive an additional bonus if you attack with a different weapon that causes a different type of damage. Ranged weapons do not benefit from Deft Grip, nor do generic “Elemental Weapons” (which collectively count as a single weapon), consumable items that grant additional damage, or spells.

Deft Grip DC: 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Dexterity modifier

Damage Type Effect Bonus Damage
Bludgeoning The heavy blow causes both stone and steel to crumple. Additional 1d6 damage if AC ≥ 15 1d6 or 2d6 bludgeoning damage
Piercing A swift thrust gives you extra reach. +5ft attack range 1d6 piercing damage
Slashing A swift slice carves through lightly armored opponents with ease. Additional 1d6 damage if AC ≤ 15 1d6 or 2d6 slashing damage
Acid The acid begins to eat away at flesh and damage armor. Dexterity saving throw. Upon a failure, the creature’s AC is reduced by 1 until the end of your next turn. At level 10 the AC reduction is increased to 2, and at level 20 it is increased to 3. 1d6 acid damage
Cold Frost begins to coalesce around the creature’s body, restricting movement. Constitution saving throw. Upon a failure the creature’s speed is reduced by half until the end of your next turn. 1d6 cold damage
Fire Flames engulf the target. Dexterity saving throw. Upon a failure the creature is set ablaze and takes 1d6 fire damage at the end of their turn. The fame can be put out by a suitable liquid or by using an action to extinguish it. 1d6 fire damage
Force The weapon impacts with incredible force. Strength saving throw. Upon a failure the creature is knocked prone. 1d6 force damage
Lightning Lightning arcs to the flesh of another creature on impact. A random hostile creature within 10ft is chosen. That creature makes a dexterity saving throw. Upon a failure, they take the full damage of the attack. 1d6 lightning damage
Necrotic The necrotic energy tears apart facsimiles of life. Doubled damage against temporary hp and creatures not in their original form (wildshape, poly, true-poly, shapechange, etc). Any damage that goes over the temp HP or the HP of the transformed creature is not doubled when applied to their HP/base form. 1d6 necrotic damage
Poison Poison seeps into the wound. Constitution saving throw. Upon a failure the creature suffers from the poisoned condition. The creature can repeat the save at the end of each of their turns. 1d6 poison damage
Psychic Psychic damage racks the mind of the target. The creature has disadvantage on any concentration saving throws for the damage caused by this attack. 1d6 psychic damage
Radiant Radiant light bursts from the weapon. Constitution saving throw. Upon a failure the creature is blinded. The creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns. 1d6 radiant damage
Thunder A thundercrack roars forth from the weapon. Constitution saving throw. Upon a failure the creature is deafened. The creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns. 1d6 thunder damage

Flowing Stance

At 3rd level, when you successfully hit another creature with a weapon that benefits from the Deft Grip bonus you receive a +1 to hit and to damage for your next attack if your next attack will also benefit from the Deft Grip bonus. These bonuses stack then reset to zero at the end of your turn.

Rapid Strike

Starting at 7th level, you learn to trade accuracy for swift strikes. If you take the Attack action on your turn and have advantage on an attack roll against against one of the targets, you can forgo the advantage for that roll to make an additional weapon attack against that target, as part of the same action. You can do so no more than once per turn.

Shatter the Horde

Starting at 10th level you can expend a use of your Action Surge to cause your melee attacks to strike any number of creatures within 5 feet of you, with a separate attack roll for each target. This benefit lasts for a single turn. This does not prevent a second Action Surge from being used on the same turn.

Focused Strike

Starting at level 15 you can expend a use of your Action Surge to focus all of your ability into a singular strike. Instead of making multiple attacks, you make a single attack against a target, and if it hits that attack is essentially multiplied by however many attacks you have remaining, including bonuses for each attack from Deft Grip and Flowing Stance; Additionally, after you use this ability, you can make no more attacks on the same turn. This does not prevent a second Action Surge from being used on the same turn. This ability must be declared prior to knowing if the Focused Strike hits.

Omnipath

At level 18, attunement slots for weapons that require attunement can shared in a single slot however, you can not dual wield weapons that require attunement without using a second slot, you receive no benefit from the weapon when it is not in use (such as auras or other passive buffs), and you can use one of the weapons at a time.

Homebrew / Items

Arcane Guardian

Arcane Guardian

Description

A sorcerer of selfless nature and protective pursuit, your magic manifests itself through your desire to support others, bringing you safety and security in the process. Imbuing allies with the same magic that suffuses themselves, these sorcerers augment their strengths, covering their weaknesses, and upon reaching mastery, become catalyst for the inevitable success of everyone under their influence.

Often called Arcane Guardians these sorcerers take a backseat to the events of life, letting others shine while they lift them higher, watching and protecting them. Many a hero was made by the hands of an Arcane Guardian.

Features:

  • 1st Level - Guardian Magic
  • 1st Level - Loving Protection
  • 6th Level - Gifting Inner Strength
  • 14th Level - Altruistic Splinter
  • 18th Level - Arcane Enlightenment

1st Level - Guardian Magic

You learn additional spells when you reach certain levels in this class, as shown on the Guardian table. Each of these spells counts as a sorcerer spell for you, but it doesn't count against the number of sorcerer spells you know.

Whenever you gain a sorcerer level, you can replace one spell you gained from this feature with another spell of the same level. The new spell must be an abjuration or a transmutation spell from the sorcerer, warlock, or wizard spell list.

Arcane Guardian Spells

  • 1st: bless, protection from evil and good
  • 3rd: aid, pass without trace
  • 5th: aura of vitality, protection from energy
  • 7th: aura of life, aura of purity
  • 9th: mass cure wounds, skill empowerment

1st Level - Loving Protection

Starting at 1st level, your selfless nature begins to show in your spellcasting. Whenever an ally within 30 feet of you fits the casting requirements for a spell with a casting time of 1 Reaction, you can spend an amount of sorcery points equal to the spell level to cast the spell and give the effects to them. You can do this an amount of times equal to your Charisma modifier, resetting when you finish a long rest.

6th Level - Gifting Inner Strength

Starting at 6th level, you harness the ability to spread your talents to your allies. Once per turn, as a bonus action, you can strengthen an ally's next spell or attack with a Metamagic option you have access to, spending sorcery points as you would to use the options normally. These options last for a minute. The viable Metamagic options are as listed:

Quickened Assault

When your target casts a spell that has a casting time of 1 action, they can choose to change the casting time to 1 bonus action for this casting.

Alternatively, they can make one melee or ranged weapon attack as a bonus action.

Subtle Assault

When the target casts a spell, they can choose to cast it without any somatic or verbal components.

Alternatively, they can give themself advantage on one melee or ranged weapon attack roll.

Empowered Assault

When the target rolls damage for a spell or weapon attack, they can reroll a number of the damage dice up to your Charisma modifier (minimum of one). They must use the new rolls.

Heightened Assault

When the target casts a spell that forces a creature to make a saving throw to resist its effects, they can give one target of the spell disadvantage on its first saving throw made against the spell.

Alternatively, if they make a melee or ranged weapon attack and hit, they can add your Charisma modifier to one of the damage rolls (minimum of one).

14th Level - Altruistic Splinter

Starting at 14th level, you learn to manipulate the bounds of your sorcery. Whenever you cast a spell that has a range of Self, you can spend an amount of sorcery points equal to twice the spell's level to change the range to Touch as long as the target is a willing creature. The spell level limit of this feature is half your Charisma modifier.  You can do this an amount of times equal to half your proficiency bonus, resetting when you finish a long rest.

18th Level - Arcane Enlightenment

Starting at 18th level, you gain the ability to funnel your strength into your allies. As an action on your turn, you can boost your allies' power until the end of your next turn. Every creature of your choice that is currently under the effects of a concentration spell cast by you receives the following additional effects:

  • Their speed is increased by 30 feet.
  • Every melee and ranged weapon attack roll they make is made with advantage. This advantage ignores any disadvantage also being applied to the target.
  • Any attacks the target makes that hit receive a damage bonus equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of one).
  • The target gains a bonus to AC equal to half your Charisma modifier (minimum of one).

This feature can be used a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, resetting on a long rest. Simulacrums are unable to use this feature.

Arcane Tent

Arcane Tent

Wondrous Item, rare

Description

This wondrous item takes the form of a normal-sized two-person tent. Setting up the tent takes ten minutes of effort. What appears to be an ordinary tent, yurt, or otherwise culturally appropriate transient dwelling from the outside is revealed to be significantly larger on the inside. Upon stepping through the entrance flap the individual finds themselves in a larger than expected space - containing 240 sqft of floor room and a 15ft high ceiling, with a small kitchen, separated outhouse, and a central hearth and sitting area. There are enough beds and accommodations for 4-6 people to sleep comfortably, even if more may fit physically. Rain will not enter through the roof, but the tent is not waterproof and will flood if submerged. Air also enters the tent from outside, leaving those within vulnerable to suffocation or otherwise if something should happen to that air.

If the tent is punctured or damaged to a significant degree (AC 11, HP 15, resistant to all damage except fire and acid), the magic will cease to function until repaired with the mending spell. All creatures and objects inside will be dumped into the space of the two-person tent, possibly breaking it further, and until repaired it will function like the tent it appears to be. Additionally, the tent has a number of furnishings and furniture which are bound to it; these will remain inside at all times, and cannot be removed. If destroyed, the furniture will reappear the next time the tent is set up. Any objects left inside will be dumped out after the tent is dismantled.

Augmenter

Augmenter

Description

The Augmenter is a unique blend of artificer and psychic, merging technology with mental prowess. These specialists understand the psyche and wield their own bodies as tools for both combat and manipulation. Whether augmenting their limbs or delving into the minds of others, Augmenters are masters of self-enhancement

Features:

  • 3rd Level - Augmenter Spells
  • 3rd Level - Self Augmentation
  • 5th Level - Extra Attack
  • 9th Level - Mind Over Matter
  • 15th Level - Master Augmenter
  • Augmenter Infusions

3rd Level - Augmenter Spells

You always have certain spells prepared after you reach particular levels in this class, as shown in the Augmenter Spells table. These spells count as artificer spells for you, but they don’t count against the number of artificer spells you prepare.

Augmenter Spells reflect your understanding of the psyche and allows you to influence the mind of others.

Augmenter Spells

3rd Level - Command, Dissonant Whispers

5th Level - Tasha’s Mind Whip, Crown of Madness

9th Level - Antagonize, Fast Friends

13th Level - Raulothim’s Psychic Lance, Compulsion

17th Level - Synaptic Static, Modify Memory

3rd Level - Self Augmentation

Starting at 3rd level, you master the technique of augmenting your own body. Each of the following parts of your body can be infused using your artificer Infusions; Torso, Head, Legs. You also gain access to Augmenter Infusions, these infusions are known and does not count toward your total of known infusions. For the purposes of normal Infusions, the Torso is seen as Armor, head as a Helmet or any peripheral that is worn on the head, and legs are seen as boots.

You also learn how to augment your arms with special arm weapons. These can also be infused, and you can only have one arm enhancement active at a time. Whenever you finish a long rest you can swap arm enhancements.

Arm Enhancements

These Enhancements count as weapons and infusions can be applied to them. Each enhancement grants the artificer an applicable fighting Style based on the installed enhancement.

Mantis Blade

You gain retractable blade attachments on either of your arms

Properties: Finesse

Fighting Style: Dueling

Damage: 1d6 piercing

Special: The blade can be retracted or unsheathed as a bonus action, leaving the hand free to wield other items. When you score a critical hit with the mantis blade the target needs to make a constitution save against your Spell DC or start to bleed. When bleeding the target loses hp equal to your proficiency bonus at the start of each of its turn. It can make the save again at the end of each turn.

Monowire Attachment

These fine wires get pulled from your wrists and are wielded like a whip.

Properties: Finesse, Reach

Fighting Style: Two-Weapon Fighting

Damage: 1d4 slashing

Special: The wires count as two separate weapons for the purpose of two weapon fighting, but only require a single infusion. The wires use Intelligence for its attack and damage modifiers.

Gorilla Arms

Your Hands and forearms are augmented with heavier metals and mechanical support.

Properties: Heavy

Fighting Style: Unarmed Fighting

Damage: Unarmed Strike, Bludgeoning

Special: You make your attacks with the Gorilla Arms as unarmed strikes. You also have advantage on Strength( Athletics) checks to escape, attempt, maintain grapples.

Arm Launcher

You can load bolts or sling bullets into your arm and fire them as projectiles.

Properties: Ranged (40/80), Reload (6)

Fighting Style: Archery

Damage: 1d8 piercing (bolts), bludgeoning (sling bullets)

Special: The Launcher leaves your hands open while firing. On a hit, the launcher does 1d4 force damage to the target, all creatures within 5ft of the target must make Dexterity save against your spell save DC or take 1d4 force damage.

5th Level - Extra Attack

Beginning at 5th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

9th Level - Mind Over Matter

At 9th level, your deep understanding of the mind allows you to manipulate the physical world with your thoughts. You gain the following abilities:

  • Mental Shield: You gain resistance to psychic damage. Additionally, when you take psychic damage, you can use your reaction to reflect half of that damage back to the attacker.
  • Psychic Insight: You can use your action to read the surface thoughts of a creature you can see within 30 feet. This effect lasts for 1 minute, and the target must make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, you can also implant a simple suggestion (as per the Suggestion spell) into their mind. This ability can be used once per short rest.

15th Level - Master Augmenter

At 15th Level your ability to enhance your augmentations has reached unparalleled heights:

  • You can now add 2 infusions to any of your augmentations.
  • You are able to use master properties for your arm augmentations. Each arm augmentation has two possible properties. When you switch out your arm augmentation you can choose which master property to use.
    • Mantis Blades: Graze, Sap
    • Monowire: Nick, Slow
    • Gorilla Arms: Sap, Push
    • Arm Launcher: Push, Vex

Avenger

Avenger

Avengers seek to right a wrong, stopping at nothing to correct a past sleight. They dole out their revenge with their own hands, using steel just as much as spirit to forward their goals.

Soul of Vengeance

At 3rd level, you gain proficiency with medium armor, shields, and martial weapons, and you can use weapons as your spiritual focus. When you activate your spirit tether, you gain an amount of temporary hit points equal to 1d6 + half your spiritualist level (rounded down).

Avenger Arts

Also at 3rd level, you gain access to new spirit arts that reflect your soul’s hunger for vengeance.

Duel of the Fates

As an action, you can spend 1 spirit point to initiate a spirit duel with your target. The target must make a Charisma saving throw or be blinded. While the target is blinded this way, you are also blinded, except you and your target can still see each other normally. As long as this blindness persists, your weapon attacks deal an additional 1d6 damage.

Spirit Shield

When you are attacked by your tethered target while you are holding a shield, you can use your reaction to spend 1 spirit point and force the target to make a Charisma saving throw. On a failure, the attack misses, and the next attack you make against the tethered target has advantage.

Phantom Pain

As an action, you can spend 2 spirit points to share your suffering with the tethered target. For the next minute, whenever you take damage, the target takes half as much necrotic damage.

Extra Attack

Beginning at 6th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn. Moreover, you can use a spirit art that uses an action in place of one of these attacks.

Avenging Link

At 13th level, your soul lashes out at any creature that would harm you or your allies. Whenever a creature you can see within range of your spirit tether damages you or an ally within 30 feet, you can use your reaction to immediately create a spirit tether. The creature must be one of the targets.

Master Avenger

At 18th level, you master the art of vengeance. You learn the following spirit art:

Soul Coating

You can use 5 spirit points as an action to empower your weapon. For the next minute, whenever you hit a tethered target with a weapon attack, the attack deals an additional 3d6 force damage. The first time you hit a tethered target after using this art, it must make a Charisma saving throw. On a failure, the target is rended by your spirit, and cannot restore hit points or gain temporary hit points as long as your spirit tether lasts.

At Higher Levels:

When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd or 4th level, this spell lasts up to 8 hours. When you use a spell slot of 5th or 6th level, this spell lasts up to 24 hours. When you use a spell slot of 7th level or higher, this spell lasts until dispelled.

Homebrew / Items

Blood Magic

Blood Magic

Description

Considered taboo by many societies and magic practitioners, the use of blood magic—also known as hemocraft—is a rare art that harnesses the latent powers of a creature’s vitality to fuel and amplify the caster’s own capabilities, while manipulating and weakening the bodies of enemies from the inside. Some of the more macabre mages seeking to empower their arcane pursuits turn to hemocraft as a means of bolstering their spells, giving their own life’s blood to reach new heights of frightening magical prowess.

The secrets of hemocraft and other forms of blood magic were once the sole purview of the mysterious Claret Orders. In recent years, however, these secrets have begun to spread beyond the order’s members and into the hands of less scrupulous mages. Blood magic has a bad reputation in Tal’Dorei, even though its powers can be used for much more than evil.

Features:

  • 2nd Level - Blood Channeling
  • 2nd Level - Sanguine Burst
  • 6th Level - Bond of Mutual Suffering
  • 10th Level - Glyph of Hemorrhaging
  • 14th Level - Thicker than Water

2nd Level - Blood Channeling

When you choose this arcane tradition at 2nd level, you are able to use your own depleted life essence to channel your magical abilities. Whenever your current hit points are below your hit point maximum, you can use your own body as an arcane focus.

In addition, when casting a wizard spell that requires a costly material component, you can forego the component by taking 1d10 necrotic damage per 50 gp of the cost of the component (minimum 1d10). This damage can’t be reduced in any way. If this damage reduces you to 0 hit points, the spell fails but the spell slot is not expended.

2nd Level - Sanguine Burst

Also at 2nd level, you learn how to weave your life force into a spell you cast, boosting its intensity at the cost of your vitality. Whenever you roll damage for a spell you’ve cast of 1st level or higher, you can choose to take necrotic damage equal to the spell’s level to reroll a number of the damage dice up to your Intelligence modifier (minimum one). This damage can’t be reduced in any way, and you must use the new rolls.

6th Level - Bond of Mutual Suffering

At 6th level, when a creature you can see hits you with an attack, you can use your reaction to bind your vitality to the attacker and force them to share your pain. The attacker takes damage equal to the damage you took.

This feature cannot be used against constructs or undead. You can use this feature once. You must finish a short or long rest before you can use it again.

At 14th level, you can use this feature twice between rests.

10th Level - Glyph of Hemorrhaging

Starting at 10th level, when you damage a creature with a spell, you can choose to curse that creature for 1 minute. While cursed in this way, whenever the creature is hit by an attack, it takes an extra 1d6 necrotic damage. At the end of each of the creature’s turns, it can make a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC, ending the curse on a success.

This feature cannot be used against creatures that are undead or constructs. Once you use this feature, you can’t use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

14th Level - Thicker than Water

Upon reaching 14th level, the blood that flows through your veins is empowered with arcane vigor that mends wounds and helps preserve your life. Whenever a spell or magical effect causes you to regain hit points, you regain an additional number of hit points equal to your proficiency bonus.

In addition, while you are concentrating on a spell, you have resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical attacks.

Bulwark

Bulwark

The Bulwark Class

Outside the king’s chambers, still as an armor display, the royal guard stands post as they await the coming rebelion force. Ready to meet it head on, no matter the result.

A scrappy militiaman clad in chainmail stands on the battlefield, now alone and bloodied, having outlasted all others through wit and defensive positioning.

Beneath a greathelm, the dwarf’s face pools with sweat as he crosses the great desert, sent on a mission to deliver an important message that cannot afford to fall into the wrong hands

Bulwarks spend large portions of their lives covered in heavy armor to the point that they are seldom ever seen without it. Their mastery over using it fully to their advantage naturally comes as second nature, allowing them to outperform nearly any other. What truly distinguishes a bulwark from other users of heavy armor is their distinct focus on making the absolute most of the defense it offers, knowing how best to move themselves to avoid or block incoming assaults. Bulwarks are often kept as personal guards to high ranking officials, as front-liners in the field of battle, or even as couriers who’s senders need certainty their message will arrive. Adventuring parties who are graced with the inclusion of one of these masters of defense can rest assured that at least one of them will be making it back alive.

The Best Offense...

A Bulwark will tend to focus fully on a defensive standpoint in battle, as an overtly pressing offense might lead to gaps in your attention. In fact, some Bulwarks even refrain from having an actual offense entirely, relying on those around them to defeat their enemies while they spend their attention and energy on lasting as long as possible.

Creating a Bulwark

When creating a Bulwark, consider why your character might have needed to train such a rigorous defense. What training have they undergone to truly set themselves ahead of their peers? Perhaps you were a member of a royal guard, someone trained to protect at any cost. Or rather just a soldier who has taken to protecting themselves a bit further than most. A Bulwark could be anyone of the great strength needed to use heavy armors, and utilizes it to the fullest, and you get to decide just how your character does that.

Multiclassing

When multiclassing with the Bulwark class, use the following:

Prerequisite: Strength 13 and Constitution 13

Proficiencies Gained: Light armor, Medium armor, Shields, and Heavy armor
