Class Features

As a Bulwark, you gain the following class features.

Base Class Features

Hit Points

Hit Dice: 1d10 per bulwark level

Hit Points at 1st Level: 10 + your constitution modifier

Hit Points at Higher Levels: 1d10 (or 6) + your constitution modifier per Bulwark level after first.

Proficiencies

Armor: Light, Medium, and Heavy Armor, Shields

Weapons: Simple Weapons, Warhammers, Heavy Crossbows

Tools: none

Saving Throws: Constitution and Charisma

Skills: Choose two from Animal Handling, Athletics, Insight, Intimidation, Medicine, Persuasion, and Religion

Equipment

You start with the following equipment, in addition to any equipment granted by your background:

  • (a) a warhammer or (b) a simple weapon of your choice and a shield
  • A suit of chainmail armor
  • (a) an explorer’s pack or (b) a diplomat’s pack
  • (a) a light crossbow and 20 bolts or (b) a shortbow and 20 arrows

Defensive Stance

While you are wearing heavy armor, you can choose to take up a defensive stance to bolster yourself for incoming force. As an action, you can give yourself a +2 bonus to your armor class and resistance to force damage for 1 minute, or until you are no longer wearing heavy armor.

You can use this feature a number of times equal to your constitution modifier before completing a long rest.

Weapon Mastery

Your training with weapons allows you to use the mastery properties of two kinds of weapons of your choice that you have proficiency with, such as maces and light crossbows.

Whenever you finish a long rest, you can change the kinds of weapons you chose. For example, you could switch to using the mastery properties of warhammers and handaxes.

Fortitude

At 2nd level, you can lessen the impact of weapons against you. While you are wearing heavy armor, and are hit by a weapon attack, you can use your reaction to reduce the damage by an amount equal to your bulwark level.

Defensive Specialization

When you reach 3rd level, you choose a defensive specialization that dictates the types of strategies you employ to protect yourself and others.

  • Juggernaut
  • Phalanx
  • Rook
  • Spellbreaker
  • Unfettered

Your choice grants you features at 3rd level and again at 7th, 13th, and 18th level.

Ability Score Improvement

When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase two ability scores of your choice by one. As normal, you can’t increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.

Using the optional feats rule, you can forgo taking this feature to take a feat of your choice instead.

Extra Attack

Beginning at 5th level, you can attack twice instead of once whenever you take the attack action on your turn.

Emissary

Additionally at 5th level, your voice carries with you a supernatural sense of purpose and authority. You gain a bonus to all charisma (intimidation and persuasion) checks equal to your strength modifier (minimum bonus of +1).

Conditioning

At 6th level, you gain an uncanny knack for endurance. You no longer suffer the adverse effects of a forced march, and exhaustion does not affect you until you have at least three levels.

Dueling Stance

Starting at 9th level, you radiate an aura that compels your foes to battle against you, and you alone. While your defensive stance is active, enemies that start their turn within 10 feet of you must make a charisma saving throw (DC 8 + your strength modifier + your proficiency bonus) or be forced to use their action to attack, or otherwise harm you.

Mental Bastion

At 10th level, you gain the ability to harden your mind to attacks with a similar effectiveness as your armor can block physical blows. You gain proficiency in intelligence or wisdom saving throws (your choice). You can replace your selection with the other whenever you finish a long rest.

Shattering Stance

When you reach 11th level, you learn to redirect the energy meant for you back to your attacker. While your defensive stance is active, you deal extra damage equal to your proficiency bonus when you attack with a weapon. You can deal this extra damage only once per turn.

Reinforcing Fortitude

Starting at 14th level, your ability to shrug off attacks extends to even the mightiest of blows. When you use your Fortitude feature, you gain a number of temporary hit points equal to the amount of damage you prevented. Once you gain these temporary hit points, you cannot do so again until you finish a short rest, or enter a new defensive stance.

Steel Endurance

At 15th level, when you roll initiative and have no remaining uses of your defensive stance, you regain one use.

Mountain Stance

When you reach 17th level, your stance becomes as unbreakable as the very earth itself. While your defensive stance is active, you cannot be moved against your will, and you are immune to the frightened condition and critical hits.

Adamantine Endurance

At 20th level, the duration of your defensive stance increases to 10 minutes, and the bonus it confers to your armor class increases to +4.

Channel of Artistry

Channel of Artistry

Artistry Channeler

Description

The Channel of Artistry represents channelers who want to master controlling the flow of their arcane energy, manipulating their power with finesse and elegance. They weave through combat like dancers and cast spells with the delicacy of an accomplished maestro.

Features

  • 1st Level - Armaments of Artistry
  • 1st Level - Elemental Savant
  • 6th Level - Weaving Strike
  • 11th Level - Beautiful Virtuosity
  • 11th Level - Harmonized Strikes
  • 17th Level - Culmination of Artistry

1st Level - Armaments of Artistry

When you pick this channel at 1st level, you gain proficiency in shortswords, scimitars, and whips. You also gain proficiency in one type of artisan’s tools of your choice.

1st Level - Elemental Savant

Your use and control of elemental energy is beautiful to many, and distracting to your opponents. Starting at 1st level, when you hit a creature with an attack, you have resistance to the first attack they make against you until the beginning of your next turn. Additionally, you may imbue two weapons instead of one. The imbued damage types must be the same for both weapons.

6th Level - Weaving Strike

At 6th level, you can sculpt your elemental energy with your weapon, enhancing both your own movements and your energy’s potency. When you deal damage with your Elemental Imbuement, the next attack roll you make during this turn has advantage, and your movement doesn’t provoke opportunity attacks until the beginning of your next turn.

11th Level - Beautiful Virtuosity

At 11th level, the beauty of your movement and the flow of your energy is entrancing and inspiring to allies. When you deal damage with your Elemental Imbuement, you may choose a creature within 30 feet that can see you. That creature may add your Elemental Imbuement die to the next attack roll, saving throw, or ability check they make until the beginning of your next turn.

11th Level - Harmonized Strikes

At 11th level, if you hit with a weapon attack from your attack action and hit with a spell attack roll made with your Overchanneled Imbuement in one turn, you may take a second bonus action that turn.

17th Level - Culmination of Artistry

At 17th level, you’ve perfected your casting as a form of art. You may use your Flash Charge feature an unlimited amount of times per day. When you hit with an attack, you may use your Flash Charge feature as a reaction. When you do, the attack deals additional damage equal to two rolls of your new Elemental Imbuement die.

Channel of Containment

Channel of Containment

Description

Features:

  • 1st Level - Armaments of Containment
  • 6th Level - Brawl Binding
  • 11th Level - Elemental Fortitude
  • 11th Level - Extra Attack
  • 17th Level - Culmination of Containment

1st Level - Armaments of Containment

When you pick this channel at 1st level, you gain proficiency in improvised weapons. You also gain proficiency in heavy armor. Elemental Core You learn to confine your arcane energy within your body, empowering your unarmed attacks. You may choose to Imbue your body with elemental energy as opposed to a weapon. While imbued, you gain the following benefits:

  • Your unarmed strikes use your Elemental Imbuement dice for its damage type.
  • When you attack with an unarmed strike, you may use your Intelligence modifier, rather than your strength modifier, for attack and damage rolls.
  • You gain resistance to the damage type you chose for your Imbuement
  • You can use your body as a focus for your Channeler spells

6th Level - Brawl Binding

Beginning at 6th level, when you use the attack action to grapple a creature, the target takes damage equal to one roll of your Elemental Imbuement die if the grapple succeeds. Whenever you take the attack action against the creature on subsequent turns, if you are still grappling the creature, you may choose to deal this damage again. Additionally, if you succeed on grappling a creature, you can use your Overchanneled Imbuement as a bonus action. Creatures you grapple have disadvantage on saving throws against spells you cast.

11th Level - Elemental Fortitude

At 11th level, your contained energy provides a defensive ward that sits just under your skin, protecting you from harm. When you are subjected to an effect that has you roll a saving throw to take half damage, if the damage type is acid, cold, fire, lightning, or thunder, you instead take no damage if you succeed on the saving throw, and only half damage if you fail.

11th Level - Extra Attack

Beginning at 11th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the attack action on your turn.

17th Level - Culmination of Containment

Beginning at 17th level, your arcane energy binds perfectly to your flesh. You gain the following benefits while Imbued:

  • You gain immunity to the damage type you chose for your Imbuement
  • Your walking speed increases by 20 feet
  • You no longer need to hit with an Imbued weapon attack to cast Channeler spells as a bonus action.
  • When you cast a Channeler spell, add your Intelligence modifier to your unarmed strike damage and any Strength, Dexterity, or Constitution checks you make until the end of your next turn.

Channel of Devastation

Channel of Devastation

Devastation Channeler

Description

The Channel of Devastation represents channelers who prefer focusing their energy in short, powerful bursts, often leading to disastrous results. Those who choose this channel work tirelessly to keep their energy concealed and suppressed, until they can let it all out in a violent burst.

Features

  • 1st Level - Armaments of Devastation
  • 1st level - Accelerant
  • 6th Level - Devastating Presence
  • 11th Level - Devastating Strikes
  • 11th Level - Extra Attack
  • 17th Level - Culmination of Devastation

1st Level - Armaments of Devastation

When you pick this channel at 1st level, you gain proficiency in glaives, greataxes, greatswords, halberds, and pikes. You also gain proficiency in heavy armor and shields.

1st level - Accelerant

At 1st level, you’ve learned how to create an accelerant with your devastating energy, overcharging your attacks. When you hit with a melee weapon attack, you can force the target to roll a strength saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failure, the target is knocked prone and suffers an additional effect depending on your imbuement. You may use this feature a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier. When you take a short or long rest, you regain all expended uses.

Accelerant Effect
Damage Type Effect
Acid The target’s AC is reduced by 1 until the end of your next turn.
Fire The target takes additional fire damage equal to one roll of your Elemental Imbuement die.
Cold The target’s speed is reduced by half of their maximum until the end of your next turn.
Lightning You may force one other creature of your choice within 10 feet of the target to take lightning damage equal to two rolls of your Elemental Imbuement die.
Thunder The target is pushed back 15 feet.

6th Level - Devastating Presence

At 6th level, your mere presence is recognized as a threat, inciting opponents to focus their aggression on you. Each creature of your choice that starts its turn within 30 feet of you and can see you must roll a Wisdom saving throw against to your spell save DC. On a failure, the creature has disadvantage on attacks that don’t target you until the end of that creature’s turn. If a creature succeeds on this saving throw, they are immune to this effect for the next 24 hours.

11th Level - Devastating Strikes

Starting at 11th level, whenever you deal damage with your Elemental Imbuement or a channeler spell that shares a damage type with your chosen Elemental Imbuement, you ignore resistance to that damage type, and you may treat immunity to that damage type as resistance.

11th Level - Extra Attack

Beginning at 11th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the attack action on your turn.

17th Level - Culmination of Devastation

At 17th level, you’ve wrought elemental devastation everywhere you’d gone, and have found the perfect way to channel it. When you hit with a melee weapon attack, you can reroll that attack against any number of other targets within 30ft, hitting each target simultaneously. You may use this feature a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier. When you finish a long rest, you regain all expended uses.

Channel of Madness

Channel of Madness

Madness Channeler

Description

The channel of Madness represents a rare and often fanatical sect of channelers that believe in submitting control over their mind and actions to the powers within themselves, even to their own detriment

Features

  • 1st Level - Armaments of Madness
  • 1st Level - Medium For Madness
  • 6th Level - Braincharge
  • 11th Level - Mental Overchannel
  • 11th Level - Psychic Armaments
  • 17th Level - Culmination of Madness

1st Level - Armaments of Madness

When you pick this channel at 1st level, you gain proficiency in hand crossbows, heavy crossbows, and longbows.

1st Level - Medium For Madness

At 1st level, you may select two 1st level enchantment spells. You learn these spells and may cast each of them once per day without expending a spell slot. At 6th level, you may choose two 2nd level enchantment spells, two 3rd level enchantment spells at 11th level, and two 4th level enchantment spells at 17th level.

Additionally, you may pick psychic damage as the damage type for your Elemental Imbuement.

6th Level - Braincharge

At 6th level, you’re able to overload the minds of others, driving them further towards insanity. When a creature fails the first save from an enchantment spell you cast, they take extra psychic damage equal to your Elemental Imbuement die. Then, you may have one creature you can see within 30 feet of you gain advantage on the next Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma saving throw they make until the beginning of your next turn.

11th Level - Mental Overchannel

At 11th level, when you deal psychic damage to a creature, you may choose to deal maximum psychic damage rather than rolling. If you do, the target is stunned until the beginning of your next turn. You cannot use this feature again until you finish a long rest.

11th Level - Psychic Armaments

At 11th level, when you imbue a weapon with psychic damage, you can change that weapon’s base damage type to psychic for as long as it’s imbued. Add your Intelligence modifier (minimum of +1) to the damage of your weapon attacks imbued with psychic damage.

17th Level - Culmination of Madness

At 17th level, it’s hard to tell if you’re still sane or not; your internal energy has corroded your mind past the point of no return. You gain advantage on saving throws against enchantment spells. In addition, you gain immunity to psychic damage and immunity to effects that would charm or frighten you. Once per day, when you cast an enchantment spell, if it would target only one creature and no other creatures, you can instead make it target as many creatures as you can see within 60 feet of you.

Channel of Volatility

Channel of Volatility

Description

The Channel of Volatility is a controversial path to undertake, as though it is the easiest channel to ‘master’, it may prove most perilous to the channeler using it. Those who practice the channel of Volatility must exercise extreme caution, else they risk losing control of their magic to horrific consequence.

Features:

  • 1st Level - Armaments of Volatility
  • 1st Level - Volatile Charge
  • 6th Level - Volatile Surge
  • 11th Level - Risk and Reward
  • 11th Level - Extra Attack
  • 17th Level - Culmination of Volatility

1st Level - Armaments of Volatility

When you pick this channel at 1st level, you gain proficiency in flails, mauls, and warhammers. You also gain proficiency in heavy armor and shields.

1st Level - Volatile Charge

Your internal energy is difficult to predict and control, yet it assists you when you need it most. Starting at 1st level, whenever you hit with a weapon attack using your imbued weapon, note the result of the attack roll and your Imbuement die roll.

Odd. If the result of the attack roll is odd, you gain temporary hit points equal to the result of your Imbuement die, which disappears whenever you take a short or long rest.

Even. If the result of the attack roll is even, the attack deals extra damage equal to the result of your Imbuement die.

6th Level - Volatile Surge

The unpredictable effects of your magic have branched into even more peculiar effects. Starting at 6th level, when you cast a channeler spell, roll your Elemental Imbuement die and note the result. Consult the Volatile Surge table for additional effects.

Surge Effect
Result Effect
1 You take damage equal to one roll of your Elemental Imbuement die.
2 You add another roll of your Elemental Imbuement die to the spell’s damage.
3 Your AC increases by 1 until the start of your next turn.
4 You gain advantage on your next attack roll until the end of your next turn.
5 You gain additional temporary hit points equal to one roll of your Elemental Imbuement die.
6 You can make an additional weapon attack as part of the same bonus action.
7 You gain resistance to the next attack that hits you until the start of your next turn.
8 Reroll on this table twice, and the effects of both rolls occur. If you roll the same effect twice, the effect only applies once.

11th Level - Risk and Reward

At 11th level; your frequent interactions with fickle energies have allowed you to lean further into their volatility. You learn one additional Ante option, and gain an additional Ante charge.

11th Level - Extra Attack

Beginning at 11th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the attack action on your turn.

17th Level - Culmination of Volatility

At 17th level, your destructive magic is longing for escape from your mortal shell. Once per day, when you’re reduced to zero hit points, you may choose to release all of your internal energy in one burst. Each creature of your choice within 30 feet of you must roll a dexterity saving throw equal to your spell save DC. On a failed save, a target takes 15d10 damage and is stunned until the end of their next turn. On a successful save, the target takes half as much damage and isn’t stunned. The damage type is the same as your elemental Imbuement. In either case, the explosion kills you immediately, disintegrating all non-magical gear and equipment you’re carrying and wearing.

Clawshot

Clawshot

Wondrous Item, very rare

Description

This magical item is made up of two distinct parts, the first being a claw-like structure, and the second being a handle. The two pieces fit together in such a way that the open claw points away from your hand when held.

While you are holding the handle, and the claw is attached, you can use a bonus action to speak the items command word, causing the claw to be magically propelled up to 30 feet. When you do so, you may target either an object or creature. At the end of the claws journey, the claw embeds itself harmlessly into the target and two pieces are magically pulled back together. If the target object or creature is either your size or larger, you are pulled up to 30 feet towards it. Inversely, if the target object or creature is at least one size smaller than you, it is pulled up to 30 feet towards you.

If the target is a creature, make an attack roll with a +10 bonus against its armor class. If the attack misses, the claw returns to the handle without moving either you or the target. This movement does not provoke opportunity attacks.

The clawshot is a magical device first invented by the artificer Flare. The clawshot is used for quick movement and repositioning, and for getting past otherwise impassable obstacles. It is also quite effective in low gravity environments, like those it's inventor commonly reside.

"It's perfectly safe to use, I swear. Just look at me, I use it all the time!" - Flare

Cloak of Levitation

Cloak of Levitation

Wondrous Item, legendary

Attunement

Requires Attunement by a Sorcerer, Wizard, or Warlock of a Non-Evil Alignment

Description

The Cloak of Levitation is one of many items imbued with power to sustain magics that practitioners of the mystic arts cannot. While you wear this cloak, you have a fly speed equal to your walking speed. If you fall while in the air when wearing this cloak, you descend at a rate of 30 feet per round until you land, taking no fall damage. If you are not wearing armor, your base Armor Class is 13 + your Dexterity modifier while wearing this cloak. When a melee attack made against you would reduce you to 20 points or lower, you can use your reaction to have the cloak fly off of your shoulders and immediately attempt a grapple against the attacker. The cloak counts as a medium sized creature for the purposes of grappling and has a +8 modifier to Strength (Athletics) checks made to grapple. If the the grapple is successful the attacker also gains the Blinded condition for the duration of the grapple. As a bonus action you may call the cloak back to you if it is within 60 feet.

When targeted by an attack or by a feature that forces a Dexterity saving throw, you may use your reaction to have the cloak take the brunt of the attack, transferring half of the damage you take to the cloak. Once the cloak is used this way, it cannot be used to fly until the next dawn. Additionally, this property cannot be used again until the next dawn.

Sentience. The Cloak of Levitation is a sentient chaotic good wondrous item, with an Intelligence score of 16, a Wisdom score of 14, and a Charisma score of 17. It has hearing and blindsight out to a range of 120 feet. The cloak can communicate by transmitting basic emotion to its wielder and can communicate basic concepts through gestures. It can read and understand Common. While you are attuned to it, the Cloak of Levitation also understands every language you know.

Personality. The Cloak of Levitation has a flamboyant and playful personality, but is also a stout defender of its wearer. The cloak generally dislikes anyone of evil alignment, and tends to display said dislike to its wearer. The cloak's purpose is to protect its wearer, and assist in their pursuits in whatever way it can. The cloak is drawn towards assisting in academia and adventuring, being quick thinking in combat and unafraid to communicate its ideas in the study.

Homebrew / Items

Cloaks of the Platinum Ward

Cloaks of the Platinum Ward

Five legendary mantles, forged in answer to the Masks of the Dragon Queen

Lore: The Answering Gift

When word first reached the temples of Bahamut that the Cult of the Dragon had gathered five masks of chromatic power — one for each of the Dragon Queen’s brood — the Platinum Dragon’s clergy did not counsel the forging of five masks in reply. A mask hides the face. A mask makes the wearer into the dragon it depicts, and swallows the name beneath it. The cult’s champions had been happy to disappear into their masks. Bahamut’s would not.

So the Talons of Justice, that old and stubborn order of dragon knights, asked instead for cloaks. A cloak is worn openly. A cloak is a thing given, thrown over the shoulders of someone who has been recognized, and it leaves the wearer’s face bare to be seen and answered for. The petition was carried to the Monastery of the Yellow Rose and from there, by means no chronicle records plainly, into the presence of the Platinum Father himself.

Bahamut consented, but not alone. Five of his metallic children came to the anvil — gold, silver, bronze, copper, and brass — and each gave something of itself: a shed scale, a breath held in a stoppered horn, a drop of blood, a memory, a laugh. Bahamut set his own power over the working like a hand over a candle flame, and what came off the anvil were five mantles of woven metal, each light as a summer cloth and each carrying a fragment of the draconic soul that had answered the call.

He laid one condition on the gift, and the condition is the whole of its purpose. The cloaks cannot be combined. Where the cult’s masks could be gathered into a single crown for a single tyrant, the Platinum Ward was made to resist exactly that: the mantles cannot be merged, reforged, nested, or fused by any magic yet found, and no creature may be attuned to more than one of them at a time. Tiamat’s power concentrates. Bahamut’s distributes. Five champions, five names, five reasons to stand — and if one falls, four remain, and the cloak of the fallen will find another shoulder.

The Talons hold that this is why the Ward has never been broken. A cabal can be beheaded. A conspiracy of five friends who each hold one fifth of a weapon and none of the whole is a harder thing to unmake.

Each cloak also carries the last clause of its making, spoken by Bahamut over the finished work and known to every wearer the moment the clasp closes: stand always against the Dragon Queen. No wearer has ever needed the words explained.

Wearing the Cloaks

The following applies to all five Cloaks of the Platinum Ward.

Sized to the Wearer. The cloak reshapes itself to fit any creature Small, Medium, or Large that attunes to it, and cannot be damaged by ordinary means.

One Mantle, One Champion. You can’t be attuned to more than one Cloak of the Platinum Ward at a time. If you attempt it, the second attunement fails and you take no benefit from either cloak until you finish a long rest.

Singular. There is only ever one of each of the five cloaks, and their magic cannot be replicated, copied, or reproduced by any craft or spell.

Unjoinable. The cloaks cannot be combined, merged, reforged, or made into any other item, by any means. Attempts to do so fail, and the cloak is unharmed by the attempt.

Anathema to the Masks. A Cloak of the Platinum Ward and a Mask of the Dragon Queen cannot be borne by the same creature. If you are attuned to one, you can’t attune to the other, and while you carry both, the two items physically repel each other — clasps refuse to close, straps slip free, and the mask will not seat against the face of a cloaked wearer. Held forcibly together, they shed sparks of gold and black smoke and can’t be made to touch. No power short of a god has yet compelled them to share a wearer.

The Cloak’s Urging. The cloak is not sentient. It cannot speak, plan, or be reasoned with. But something of the dragon that gave its scale remains in the weave, and it leans. A wearer finds the merciful choice arriving in their mind a moment before the ruthless one, feels a reluctance they can’t quite source when they consider abandoning the helpless, and sleeps easier on the nights they did right. This is influence, not compulsion: the wearer keeps every scrap of free will, and a determined villain can wear a cloak and remain a villain. They will simply find it a slightly wearying garment.

Gold Cloak of the Platinum Ward

Wondrous item, legendary (requires attunement)

A mantle of burnished gold scales, each no larger than a thumbnail and each perfectly overlapping the last, so that the whole hangs like heavy silk and rings faintly when it moves. Fine metallic whiskers trail from the collar, and the clasp is worked in the shape of a dragon’s brow crowned with a fan of spines. It is warm to the touch at all hours, in all weather. While you are wearing the cloak and attuned to it, you gain the following benefits.

Damage Absorption. You have resistance against fire damage. If you already have resistance to fire damage from another source, you instead have immunity to fire damage. If you already have immunity to fire damage from another source, whenever you are subjected to fire damage, you take none of that damage and regain a number of hit points equal to half the fire damage dealt.

Draconic Majesty. While you are wearing no armor, you can add your Charisma bonus to your Armor Class.

Dragon Breath. If you have a breath weapon that requires rest to recharge, it gains a recharge of 6.

Dragon Sight. You gain darkvision out to 60 feet, or to an additional 60 feet if you already have that sense. Once per day, you can gain blindsight out to 30 feet for 5 minutes.

Dragon Tongue. You can speak and understand Draconic. You also have advantage on any Charisma check you make when interacting with gold dragons.

Legendary Resistance (1/Day). If you fail a saving throw, you can choose to succeed instead.

Weakening Flame. If you deal fire damage to a creature, then until the end of that creature’s next turn it has disadvantage on Strength-based attack rolls, ability checks, and saving throws.

Wondrous Item , Uncommon

Description

This 3' cube glows slightly with yellow light while active, which can be identified as a standard "hazard" symbol while in darkness.

The cube has 3 charges. As an action, you can touch the cube to a non-magical metallic object. Courier

Courier's Cradle

Wondrous Item, very rare

Description

A Couriers Cradle needs two pieces to have any sort of effect. A Sending Stone, and a Couriers Cradle. Without both components it has no function. A Courier's Cradle consists of three parts. A chassis, typically squared and made of polished stone, granite, or marble for particularly wealthy folk. A basin sat in the cubed bottom, around half a foot wide and typically filled with water. And lastly a bowl mounted over the basin, made of rare material such as gemstone, brass, or pure quartz. While a creature is within 5 feet of a cradle, it may place a sending stone into it's bowl. It then takes a minute to fasten and adjust the cradle for speaking. After this process is complete the cradle is assembled.

Connection A creature may connect to another Courier's Cradle within a distance of up to the plane they exist according to the following difficulties, using an Intelligence (Arcana) check. If another Cradle is connected to this one, they establish a line of communication. This allows each to hear from the other side as if they were in the same room.

Distance (Miles) DC
5 10
50 15
200 20
Planar 25

Disconnection A Courier's Cradle is automatically disconnected if both sides are not connected to one another or if the cradle is moved from where it was first activated.

Crown of the Four Seasons

Wondrous Item, Uncommon

Description

Control your emotions, sweetheart, or the witches will come and steal your feelings away.

Originally used as a toy to train young eladrin, this fey-infused flower crown changes appearance based on the wearer's mood. These moods also reflect the four seasons: winter, spring, summer, and autumn.

When the wearer undergoes a burst of any type of emotion (Flash of anger, sudden surprise etc), the flowers will wilt to a dull gray and the illusory effects will vanish to signify a loss of control. The next morning, the flowers will blossom to their full color after the lesson has been learned

Homebrew / Items

Cryomancy

Cryomancy

Specializing on ice magic, wizards that have learned from the Cryomancy arcane tradition manipulate the crystalline structure of ice and bend it to their will. Many foolishly only see this magic as beautiful, and it is, but within the beauty of all that shimmering ice, is a slow and shivering death.

Frigid Magic

Your manipulation of ice allow you to acclimate to it and change the properties of spells. When you cast a spell that deals damage, you are able to change the damage type to cold damage unless its bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing damage. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (a minimum of once). You regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

You gain resistance to cold damage. When you reach 13th level on this class, you also gain resistance to fire damage, and at 17th level, you gain immunity to cold damage and the area 5 feet of you has the effects of extreme cold.

Ice Sculpting

As an action, you can freeze a 5-foot cube of nonmagical water. The cube will remain frozen for one minute or until your concentration ends (as if you were concentrating on a spell). You can manipulate the ice as a bonus action to mold its shape to form objects or structures. The objects or structures you make have hit points equal to your wizard level. At 8th and 15th level, you freeze an area of 15-foot and 25-foot cube respectively. You can also create the ice out of moisture in the air, though the cubic footage you are able to manipulate is halved (i.e. you can produce a 7-foot cube from a 15-foot cube of air).

Additionally, when you reach 15th level you can also freeze magical water, manipulate magical ice, and the cube can now be frozen for up to 1 hour.

Cryostasis

Your body fills with ice magic and acts at times in preservation from external factors. When you become unconscious or asleep or are rendered unconscious or asleep, you are immediately encased in a layer of dense ice. This ice has hit points equal to twice your wizard level and an AC equal to your spell save DC.

When the ice encases you as a result of being reduced to 0 hit points, the ice will stabilize you and freezes the area around you. All creatures within 10 feet of you must make a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC or be restrained until the end of their next turn. On a successful save, they are not restrained but their speed is halved. When the restrained condition from this feature ends, the creature's speed is also halved. They can make another Constitution saving throw at the end of each of their turns. On a success, their speed returns to normal.

The ice lasts for 1 minute, until it is destroyed, or when you choose to break the ice upon regaining consciousness. Once this feature is used it cannot be used again until a long rest.

Absolute Zero

Your control over ice have reached to an abnormal extreme, even by magical standards. Choose one wizard spell that deals damage in your spellbook. That spell's damage type permanently becomes cold damage when you cast it without using your Frigid Magic feature or other similar effect. You can change the spell for a different spell by spending 8 hours in study.

The first time you deal damage to a creature that does not have resistance or immunity to cold damage on your turn, they take extra cold damage equal to your wizard level.

Whiteout

After extensive use of bending ice to your every whim, you understand all of its inner workings. You're able to apply this knowledge by performing grand feats on a monumental scale. As an action, you are able to freeze everything within a 60 foot radius sphere centered around you. This creates sleets of ice and snow on the ground and super chilling the air, rendering the area as difficult terrain. All creatures of your choice takes 3d6 cold damage upon activation and must make a Strength saving throw against your spell save DC or be frozen. While frozen, a creature is considered incapacitated and their speed is reduced to 0 until the end of their next turn.

Furthermore, you create a 30 foot radius sphere of a perpetual blizzard that is centered around and moves with you. When a creature of your choice enters the area for the first time or starts their turn in it, the creature must succeed on a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC or take cold damage equal to half your wizard level and have its speed halved until the start of its next turn. The area inside the blizzard acts as a heavily obscured area for all creatures except you.

Both the difficult terrain and blizzard lasts for 1 minute or when you end both effects using an action, afterwards you no longer gain the effects of the Frigid Magic feature until you take a short rest. Once this feature is used it cannot be used again until a long rest.

The first time a creature targets you with a melee attack and misses during this spell's duration, your shield bursts with divine radiance as you deflect the blow. The stored energy within releases and deals 1d6 radiant damage to any hostile creatures within 5 feet. When this blast hits an undead or a fiend, it deals an additional 1d6 radiant damage to it. After the blast, the spell ends.

At Higher Levels

When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 2nd level or higher, the radiant damage dealt by the blast increases by 1d6 for each slot level after the 1st.

False Razor

False Razor

Weapon (greataxe), artifact (requires attunement)

Forged from the remains of the nightmare known as False Razor, this alien weapon still hungers for life. False Razor has three forms, retaining all previous properties as it advances.

This weapon must be obtained in Chult from beating a Trial of Orolunga.

Form I — Base Form

+3 Weapon. You gain a +3 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with False Razor.

Damage. On a hit, False Razor deals:

1d12 slashing + 2d6 piercing + 1d8 necrotic + Strength modifier + 3

  • Siphoning Edge. Whenever you hit a creature with False Razor, you regain 1d4 hit points. If you are already at your hit point maximum, you instead gain 1d4 temporary hit points.

Form II — Mind Splitter

As a bonus action, choose one creature within 30 feet. It must make a DC 20 Constitution saving throw.

Failure: The creature is stunned until the end of its next turn.

Success: The creature takes 2d6 psychic damage, and its speed is halved until the end of its next turn.

You can use Mind Splitter a number of times equal to your Constitution modifier (minimum 1) per long rest.

Unlock: Complete a solo quest and kill a CR 25+ creature.

Form III — Existence Rend

Once per turn when you damage a creature with False Razor, you can force it to make a DC 23 Constitution saving throw.

On a failure, its hit point maximum is reduced by 3d4. This reduction can reduce a creature’s maximum HP to 0.

Unlock: Complete another solo quest, kill another CR 25+ creature, and personally kill a level 20+ good-aligned humanoid.

Sentience

Alignment: Neutral Evil

INT 16 | WIS 14 | CHA 18

False Razor has hearing and darkvision out to 120 feet and communicates telepathically with its wielder.

It speaks, reads, and understands Common, Abyssal, and Tabaxi.

False Razor is patient, predatory, and fascinated by killing. It has a particular hatred for Blackrazor, desiring the death of any creature wielding it and ultimately the destruction of Blackrazor itself.

Curse — The Razor’s Hunger

Once attuned, the wielder cannot willingly part with False Razor or end their attunement.

Whenever the wielder attempts a long rest, roll 1d3. On a 1, False Razor compels them to abandon the rest and seek out something to kill.

Breaking the Curse. The curse can only be broken by the attuned wielder using Wish specifically to sever their bond with False Razor.

Doing so permanently destroys False Razor. No other spell or effect can end the attunement or remove the curse.

Homebrew / Items

Fey Duelist

Fey Duelist

Description

The Fey Duelist archetype merges the cunning and agility of a rogue with the enchanting power of the Feywild. These rogues are gifted (or cursed) with the boons of Archfey patrons, weaving magic and mischief into their every movement. They are agile combatants and masters of manipulation, channeling Fey magic to outmaneuver foes, charm allies, and spread chaos on the battlefield.

Whether as emissaries of a Fey court, champions of their Archfey patron, or independent agents who stumbled into the gifts of the Feywild, Fey Duelists tread a fine line between mortal pragmatism and the capricious beauty of the Fey. Their motivations are as varied as the Feywild itself, often driven by a blend of personal ambition, devotion to their patron, or a desire to unweave the chains of mundane reality and reshape the world with Fey-inspired artistry.

Playstyle and Motivations

The Fey Duelist excels in roles that combine agility, cunning, and creativity. They bring versatility to combat and social interactions, offering a mix of mobility, control, and spellcasting that allows them to adapt to nearly any situation. Players who enjoy weaving spells and martial combat together will find the Fey Duelist a rewarding choice.

Motivations for a Fey Duelist might include:

  • Devotion to an Archfey: Serving a powerful Fey entity as a trusted agent or champion, spreading their influence or carrying out their will.
  • Personal Freedom: Using Fey gifts to escape or defy systems of control, embracing the chaotic and whimsical nature of the Feywild.
  • Vengeance or Redemption: Seeking to right a past wrong or balance a perceived injustice using the unique powers of the Fey.
  • Curiosity and Mischief: Exploring the boundaries of mortal and Fey realms, motivated by wonder and the joy of discovery.

Who Would Thrive as a Fey Duelist?

The Fey Duelist appeals to characters who want to:

  • Command the Social Arena: Features like Binding Words provide robust tools for persuasion, manipulation, and intrigue.
  • Outmaneuver and Disrupt Enemies: Abilities like Elusive Action and Distant Dodge emphasize mobility and tactical positioning.

Ideal Players and Characters

  • The Charismatic Manipulator: Players who enjoy talking their way out of trouble, influencing NPCs, and using charm to solve problems.
  • The Tactical Trickster: Players who like to use cunning, positioning, and the environment to control the flow of combat.
  • The Fey Enthusiast: Players who love the whimsical, mysterious, and chaotic themes of the Feywild and want to embody its spirit.

Features

  • 3rd Level - Spellcasting
  • 3rd Level - Vexing
  • 9th Level - Delicate Deception
  • 13th Level - Binding Words
  • 17th Level - Archfeys Guile

3rd Level - Spellcasting

When you reach 3rd level, you augment your martial prowess with the ability to cast spells.

Cantrips

You learn three cantrips: Vicious Mockery and two other cantrips of your choice from the warlock or bard spell list. You learn another warlock or bard cantrip of your choice at 10th level.

Spell Slots

The Fey Duelist Spellcasting table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your warlock or bard spells of 1st level and higher. To cast one of these spells, you must expend a slot of the spell's level or higher. You regain all expended spell slots when you finish a long rest.

For example, if you know the 1st-level spell Charm Person and have a 1st-level and a 2nd-level spell slot available, you can cast Charm Person using either slot.

Spells Known of 1st Level and Higher

You know three 1st-level warlock or bard spells of your choice, two of which you must choose from the enchantment and illusion spells on the warlock or bard spell list.

The Spells Known column of the Fey Duelist Spellcasting table shows when you learn more warlock or bard spells of 1st level or higher. Each of these spells must be an enchantment or illusion spell of your choice, and must be of a level for which you have spell slots. For instance, when you reach 7th level in this class, you can learn one new spell of 1st or 2nd level.

The spells you learn at 8th, 14th, and 20th level can come from any school of magic.

Whenever you gain a level in this class, you can replace one of the warlock or bard spells you know with another spell of your choice from the warlock or bard spell list. The new spell must be of a level for which you have spell slots, and it must be an enchantment or illusion spell, unless you're replacing the spell you gained at 3rd, 8th, 14th, or 20th level from any school of magic.

Spellcasting Ability

Charisma is your spellcasting ability for your warlock or bard spells, since you learn your spells through dedicated study and memorization. You use your Charisma whenever a spell refers to your spellcasting ability. In addition, you use your Charisma modifier when setting the saving throw DC for a warlock or bard spell you cast and when making an attack roll with one.

Spell save DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Charisma modifier

Spell attack modifier = your proficiency bonus + your Charisma modifier

3rd Level - Vexing

Start at 3rd level, when you cast Vicious Mockery, you can now cast it as a Bonus Action. Additionally, the first attack roll, ability check or saving throw you make against an affected creature before the end of your next turn is made with advantage.

9th Level - Delicate Deception

Starting at 9th level, you can weave Fey Magic into your movements and attacks, enhancing them. Once per turn, you can modify a rogue feature to add an additional effect, as listed below:

  • Fey Attack: Sneak Attack deals an additional 1d6 psychic damage. This additional damage is increased at 13th (2d6) level & 17th (3d6) level.

  • Elusive Action: Immediately before or after using Cunning Action, a 5ft cube surrounding you becomes Heavily Obscured to everyone except you until the start of your next turn.

  • Distant Dodge: Whenever you use Uncanny Dodge after being hit with an attack, you may teleport up to 10 feet to an unoccupied space you can see.

You can use this ability a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of once), and regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest. You can also regain uses by expending a spell slot for each use you want to restore (no action required).

13th Level - Binding Words

At 13th level, you can weave a magical enchantment into your words, undermining and binding those that hear it. As an action you can speak a word infused with fey magic to a creature within 30 feet that can hear you, forcing them to make a Wisdom saving throw (DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Charisma modifier). On a failed saving throw, fey magic binds it, and the only actions that it can take before the end of its next turn are the Attack (one weapon attack only), Dash, Disengage, or Hide action. If the target succeeds on its saving throw, it has no hint that you tried to bind it.

Any creature under the effect of Vicious Mockery cast via your Vexing feature automatically fails the saving throw for this feature.

Once you use this ability, you cannot use it again until you finish a short or long rest. You can also regain uses by expending a spell slot (3rd level) for each use you want to restore (no action required).

17th Level - Archfeys Guile

Starting at 17th level, as an action you can make a Charisma (Persuasion or Deception) check against a creature that you can see that isn’t incapacitated, contested by a Wisdom (Insight) check. If you succeed, for the next minute, any deception or suggestions you make towards that creature are suffused with fey magic, and that creature remembers the conversation in a way that favors your intent, even creating temporary artificial memories that support your statements. Any contradictory evidence to oppose your deception is disregarded and they will rationalize any memories or statements from friends as illogical or even possible attempts to deceive them. When presented with facts contradicting your deception, the target can repeat the Wisdom (Insight) check, ending the beguiling effects on a success.

This benefit lasts for 10 minutes or until you successfully use this feature against a different creature. The effects of your magic linger on the target for up to 1 hour after you’ve successfully used this feature, or until they have a Dispel Magic or Remove Curse cast upon them. If the target remained beguiled for the full duration, the affected memories and altered perceptions become permanent.

Final Messenger

Final Messenger

Wondrous item, uncommon (requires use by a warforged)

A final messenger is a tiny homunculus—a delicate winged creature designed to facilitate communication between warforged soldiers during the Last War.If you are a warforged, you can use an action to hold a final messenger and integrate it into your body. While it is part of your body, the messenger cannot be targeted by any attack. You can only have one messenger attached to your body at a time.

A final messenger holds four pieces of data, accessible only to the warforged it is attached to:

  • A destination for the messenger. This can be very specific (a particular apartment in Sharn) or more general (an open marketplace).
  • A target individual. This could be a specific person or a category (“Any Karrnathi warforged”).
  • A single image recorded through the eyes of a warforged attached to the messenger.
  • A message of up to 25 words.

While the messenger is attached to you, you can use an action to review the data currently stored within the final messenger, and if you choose, to change any or all of these data points. You can release the final messenger as a bonus action, at which point it flies to its destination by the most direct route possible. Once it reaches the destination it seeks the target individual; if no target has been set, it approaches the nearest warforged.

If you are reduced to 0 hit points while a final messenger is attached to you, it immediately detaches and seek out its target. It retains its stored message, but replaces its stored image with the last thing you saw before dropping to zero hit points.

A final messenger is a Tiny construct with an AC of 20, 6 hit points, and a flying speed of 60 feet. It is immune to poison damage, psychic damage, and all conditions other than unconsciousness. If it is forced to make an ability check or a saving throw, treat all its ability scores as 10 (+0). It has darkvision with a range of 60 feet. It has no limbs and the only action it can take on its turn is the Dash action. A messenger can only remain active for 8 hours after it detaches from a warforged body, after which time its energy dissipates and it falls unconscious. An unconscious messenger must complete a short or long rest attached to a warforged, after which it regains its energy, as well as regaining all lost hit points.

Fortune

Fortune's Shadow

In the clandestine world of rogues, a select few find themselves touched by the enigmatic forces of fate. These shadowy figures, known as Fortune’s Shadows, navigate the perilous dance of danger with a unique connection to the threads that weave destiny. Embracing Fortune’s Shadow means walking a razor’s edge, where every calculated risk and precise strike is a step further into the weave of destiny. Those who witness a Fortune’s Shadow in action may question whether their abilities are a result of skill, luck, or a mysterious force guiding their every move. One thing is certain – in the world of shadows and secrets, the Fortune’s Shadow is a rogue unlike any other, their fate entwined with the very essence of chance.

Fortune's Gambit

At 3rd level, upon dealing sneak attack damage with an even number, you gain a Fate Point.

As a bonus action, you can expend a Fate Point to make a daring gambit. Roll a d6 to determine the effect of the Gambit.

d6 : Gambit : Effect:

  1. Fleeting Shadows: You become invisible until the start of your next turn, you lose invisibility whenever you attack, or force a saving throw.
  2. Lucky Strike: Your next attack gains advantage.
  3. Evasive Maneuver: The next attack against you must be made with disadvantage.
  4. Weave of Fate: You gain temporary hit points equal to your rogue level.
  5. Deft Diversion: You can move up to half your speed without provoking opportunity attacks.
  6. Fortune's Grace: Add your proficiency bonus to your AC until the start of your next turn.

When rolling initiative your Fate Points reset to 0. You can a flip a coin, on a head to you gain a Fate point.

Fateful Escape

At level 9 when you are reduced to 0 hit points and not killed outright, you can expend a Fate Point to cheat death. Instead of falling unconscious, you remain conscious with 1 hit point, and can immediately use a reaction to move up to your speed, without provoking opportunity attacks. Additionally, you gain advantage on Dexterity ability checks and saving throws for 1 minute, representing the temporary escape from fate’s grasp. Once you use this feature, you can’t use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

Greater Gambit

At 13th level your Gambit's are improved. when you roll for a Gambit, you instead use the Greater gambit table:

d6 : Gambit : Effect:

  1. Persistent Shadows: You become invisible until the end of your next turn.
  2. Foretold Strikes: You gain advantage on attacks until the end of your next turn.
  3. Evasive Expert: You impose disadvantage on all attacks against you until the start of your next turn..
  4. Architect of Fate: You gain temporary hit points and regain hit point equal to your rogue level
  5. Perfect Diversion: You can move up to your speed without provoking opportunity attacks.
  6. Fortune's Gift: Add your proficiency bonus to your AC until the start of your next turn. Reduce damage taken from attacks by the same amount.

When rolling initiative you can now flip 2 coins, gaining a Fate point for each coin that lands on a head.

Uncanny Fate

At level 17, when you use your uncanny dodge feature to halve damage received, you can spend a Fate Point to roll a d6. On an even result, the attacker takes force damage equal to the damage you received. On an odd result, you don't take any damage from the attack.

Homebrew System & Index

Homebrew System & Index

How to Homebrew

In The Wandering Realms, we allow homebrew. Homebrew get approved in the server on a dual voting system. Any Player can submit homebrew in the #homebrew-ua-submissions Channel. Each homebrew submission follows the same method:

  1. A Player Creates a Post in the #homebrew-ua-submissions channel. They Ping @homebrewer in the post. And react on the post with a 1 and 2.
  2. Players then vote on the submission by reacting.
    1. Yes
    2. No
  3. Once the Submission reaches 10 Yes votes, the submission is moved to homebrew-ua-approver-votes where a team of staff members will either approve or deny the homebrew, if after a month a submission doesn't reach 10 votes, it gets denied.

Some Rules:

  1. A Player is allowed one submission per week. Unless their submission get's approved by staff, in which case they can submit another.
  2. #homebrew-ua-submissions is reserved for submissions only. Players can discuss or query active homebrew in #homebrew-ua-discussion.

In-Character Homebrew Creations:

When submitting Homebrew, a player can declare an item to be invented, or otherwise created by one or multiple characters. The creation or access to that Homebrew is then restricted to those with the same in-character access to it. In order to maintain this restriction, the actual creation must be roleplayed within a reasonable timeframe of the item's passing (no people rushing to craft an item the minute it passes before a person can rp)

ie: a wizard sharing a spell they created with another; an inventor selling items or sharing designs

Light Weaver

Light Weaver

Description

Your powers are drawn from the spark of light kindled within you. In places of great darkness, there are those born with an affinity for light, and every shadow has a source. The magic within you represents cosmic balance, flickering from radiance to darkness moment to moment.

Features:

1st Level - Trick of the Light

1st Level - Flickering Aura

6th Level - Refraction Shield

14th Level - Aura Magnification

18th Level - Light Weaver

1st Level - Trick of the Light

Starting at 1st level, you have darkvision out to a range of 60 feet. If you already have darkvision, it increases its range by 60 feet.

You learn the Light and Sacred Flame cantrips. At 3rd-level you learn the Darkness and  Faerie Fire spells, which are sorcerer spells and do not count against your spells known. They can cast normally, or by expending 2 sorcery points.

1st Level - Flickering Aura

Starting at 1st level, you can magnify the properties of light around you. At the end of a  short or long rest, you can choose whether your magic is light-shifted or dark-shifted.

While light-shifted you can use an action to emit an aura in a 15-foot radius around you.  This area is bright light. While the aura persist, you can use a bonus action to expand or reduce its radius by 5 feet, to a maximum of 30 feet each or a minimum of 10 feet. While dark-shifted you gain the same ability, but you project an aura of nonmagical darkness. This effect lasts for 1 minute, or until you are incapacitated.

Once used, you cannot use this ability again until you finish a short or long rest

6th Level - Refraction Shield

At 6th level, you can manipulate the light around you for protection. As a bonus action, you can spend 2 sorcery points to magically create a shield of light or dark. The shield lasts for 1 minute, or until you are incapacitated.

While this shield is in place, whenever a creature within 10 feet of you hits you with an attack, this shield flashes with searing energy, and the attacker takes 2d6 radiant damage if you are light-shifted or 2d6 necrotic damage if you are dark-shifted.

14th Level - Aura Magnification

While your Flickering Aura is active, you can now expand it up to 10 feet as a bonus action, up to a maximum of 60 feet. While within the aura, a number of creatures equal to your Charisma modifier also gain the benefit of your Refraction Shield, but no more than once per turn.

Additionally, you and those creatures have advantage on Wisdom (Perception) skill checks made while light-shifted, or Dexterity (Stealth) checks made while dark-shifted. You can add your proficiency bonus when making these skill checks by expending a sorcery point.

18th Level - Light Weaver

Embodying both aspects of Light and Dark, you gain resistance to both radiant and necrotic damage. Additionally, as part of the action to activate your Flickering Aura, you can transform yourself and gain the following benefits for up to 1 minute:

Upon activation or as part of the bonus action to expand or reduce it's radius, you can switch to either light-shifted or dark-shifted. Each creature of your choice within your aura must make a Constitution saving throw, taking 2d8 radiant and 2d8 necrotic damage and becoming blinded till the end of their next turn on a failure, or half as much damage and not being blinded in a success.

While your Radiant Shield is active, the radius of its effect increases to 30 feet, and you deal both the radiant and the necrotic damage when hit with an attack.

Once you use this action, you can’t use it again until you finish a long rest, unless you spend 5 sorcery points to use it again.

  • Nebula - While wearing this magical armor, you are considered to be proficienct with it even if you lack proficiency with heavy armor, and you are resistant to psychic damage.     • Regeneration - you regain 5 hit points at the start of each of your turns.
    • Power - each of your spells gains a 2d8 bonus to one damage roll.
    • Mana - When you cast a spell of 3rd level or lower, roll a d6. If the result is greater than the level of the spell, you do not expend a spell slot.
  • Stardust - While wearing this magical armor, you are considered to be proficient with it even if you lack proficiency with heavy armor, and you are resistant to cold damage. Creatures you summon through class features or spells gain a +3 bonus to attack and damage rolls. The armor has three charges, and regains all charges daily at dawn. When you summon a creature throigh a class feature or spell, you can expend one charge to summon one additional creature. This creature lasts only half as long, or for one hour in the case of indefinite durations.

Homebrew / Items

Magic Toggle

Magic Toggle

Casting Time: 1 minute (ritual)

Range: 30 feet

Components: V, S, M (a pinch of iron and cobalt powder worth at least 10 gp, which the spell consumes)

Duration: Until Dispelled

You implant a small repeatable magical mechanical force within a tiny object within range. When you do so, choose two rotational states relative to it's current rotation for the item to switch between. When the spell causes the item to switch between the two rotational states, it does so with the least required movement and can be designated to take anywhere from 1 second to 10 minutes. Finally, determine the circumstance that will trigger the spell to rotate the object.

When the circumstance occurs, the object rotates to the next or previous state (the second state when triggered for the first time). If an outside force or object would prevent the object from rotating, it stops harmlessly and that particular trigger is ignored. When you cast this spell, you can have the spell end after it returns to its original position, or it can remain and repeat its rotation whenever the trigger occurs.

The triggering circumstance can be as general or as detailed as you like, though it must be based on visual or audible conditions that occur within 30 feet of the object. For example, you could instruct a lock to automatically reset its rotation when the door is closed.

Mask of the Wild Beasts

Mask of the Wild Beasts

Wondrous Item, varies

Attunement

Requires Attunement

Description

These dark ceramic and gold masks are fashioned after animals that are sacred in certain cultures. Each mask's appearance and properties are based on the sacred beast it represents. While attuned to a mask, you can end your attunement to it and attune to a different one over the course of 1 minute, instead of over the course of one or more short rests.

Crocodile (Common).

While wearing a crocodile mask, you gain a swimming speed of 30 feet and can hold your breath for up to 10 minutes at a time.

Lion (Uncommon). While wearing a lion mask, you have advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on smell. In addition, your nails extend into claws, turning your unarmed strikes with your hands into magic weapons that deal slashing damage with a damage die of 1d6.

Hawk (Rare). While wearing a hawk mask, you have advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on sight, and attacking at long range doesn't impose disadvantage on your ranged attack rolls. In addition, you can cast the feather fall spell at will, targeting only yourself.

Mule (Very Rare). While wearing a mule mask, your Strength score increases by 2, to a maximum of 20, you count as one size larger when determining your carrying capacity and the weight you can push, drag, or lift, and you have advantage on Strength and Dexterity ability checks and saving throws against being knocked prone. In addition, when you hit a Large or smaller creature with a melee weapon attack, you can use a bonus action to force that creature to make a DC 16 Strength or Dexterity saving throw (its choice). On a failed save, the creature is knocked prone.

Jackal (Legendary). While wearing a jackal mask, you have advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks and immunity to necrotic damage.

In addition, you can use an action to fire a beam of deathly green magic from your forehead at a creature you can see within 60 feet of you. The creature must make a DC 17 Constitution saving throw, taking 7d8 + 30 necrotic damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. Once this property of the mask has been used, it can't be used again until the next dusk.

A humanoid killed by this necrotic damage rises at the start of your next turn as a mummy under your control. The mummy acts on its own initiative count. On your turn, you can mentally command the mummy if it is within 120 feet of you and you aren't incapacitated (no action required). You decide what action the mummy takes and where it moves during its next turn, or you can issue it a general command, such as to attack your enemies or guard a location.

The mummy remains until you dismiss it as a bonus action, until it's reduced to 0 hit points, or until you are no longer attuned to any mask of the sacred beast, causing it to turn to dust. You can only create and control one mummy at a time in this way.

Morelock

Morelock

Prerequisites

  • Level 20 Cycle: You must have completed 20 levels of Warlock (PHB-2024) with no multiclassing.

The WarlockTable

Class Features

PL 21: Proficiencies

When you take this prestige class, choose two additional skills from the Warlock skill list. You gain proficiency in both.

PL 21: Ascended Pact Magic

Your amount of available pact slots increases per the Morelock Table.

PL 22: Improved Magical Cunning

You can now Expend an action, bonus action and all your movement to use Magical cunning.

PL 23: Patron

Your eldritch mastery has grown so strong you can now have 2 different patrons without conflict, You may choose the same warlock patron, or you may choose a new one. At PL 23, PL 26, PL 31 and PL37, you gain more features from your warlock patron.

PL 24: Ability Score Improvement

At PL 24, 28, 32, 36, and 39, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or two ability scores by 1. As normal, you cannot increase a score above 20 (unless another feature allows it). You may select a Feat instead of an ASI.

PL 25: Journeyman Pact Magic

Your Pact Slots increase in power. All of your available Warlock Pact Slots are now 6th level. You do not learn any new 6th-level spells to cast with these slots; they can only be used to upcast the Warlock spells you know of 5th level or lower, or to cast the specific 6th-level Warlock spells you have already learned through your Mystic Arcanum feature.

PL 29: Ascendant Contact Patron

Your connection to your patron transcends the boundaries of the planes. When you use your Warlock Contact Patron feature to cast Contact Other Plane, the casting time is reduced to 1 Action, and you do not need to speak aloud to ask your questions.

Additionally, once per Long Rest, you can cast the Gate spell without expending a Pact Slot or requiring material components. When cast in this way, the portal can only open to the home domain of your Patron, allowing you to step into their realm.

PL31: Heightened Mystic Arcunam

Choose another level 6 Warlock spell as this arcanum.

You can cast your 6th level arcanum spell twice without expending a spell slot, and you must finish a Long Rest before you can cast it in this way again.

As shown in the Morelock Features table, you gain another Warlock spell of your choice that can be cast in this way when you reach Warlock levels 33 (level 7 spell), 35 (level 8 spell), and 37 (level 9 spell), these can be cast as arcanums twice per long rest. You regain all uses of your Mystic Arcanum when you finish a Long Rest.

Whenever you gain a Warlock level, you can replace one of your arcanum spells with another Warlock spell of the same level.

PL 35: Expert Pact Magic

Your soul acts as a massive conduit for your patron's magic. All of your Warlock Pact Slots are now 7th level. As before, you do not learn new 7th-level spells for these slots; they may only be used to upcast your known Warlock spells of 6th level or lower, or to cast the 7th-level Warlock spells you have learned through your Mystic Arcanum feature.

PL 40: Pact Magic Mastery

Your mind has expanded to withstand the cosmic weight of your patron's true power, allowing you to fracture your focus without breaking it. You can now concentrate on two Warlock spells simultaneously, provided both spells were cast using your Pact Slots.

Wielding this dual magic is a volatile and taxing endeavor. If you take damage while concentrating on two spells and are forced to make a Constitution saving throw to maintain Concentration, you must make the roll with Disadvantage. If you fail the saving throw, the magic violently unravels, and you lose Concentration on both spells simultaneously.

Resistance. When the familiar takes damage, you can take a Reaction to grant it Resistance against that damage.

Homebrew / Items

Night Reaver

Night Reaver

Description

You learn the art of siphoning life from dying enemies and combining it with negetive energy to imbue necromancy into your fighting style. Reavers often kill those who are closest to death, whose spiritual binds are thin enough to cut free and use. Features:

  • 3rd Level - Criticality
  • 9th Level - Rend
  • 13th Level - Ward of Mortality
  • 17th Level - Echo of Reaping

3rd Level - Criticality

Starting at 3rd level, creatures with less than half of their total hit points gain a Death Mark, granting you the following benefits:

  • You gain an additional way to use your sneak attack; you don’t need advantage on the attack roll to use your Sneak Attack against a marked creature, so long as you don’t have disadvantage on the attack roll.
  • Attack rolls against marked creatures crit on 19-20.
  • You have a bonus on attack rolls against marked creatures. This bonus equals half your proficiency bonus.

9th Level - Rend

Starting at 9th level, you gain the ability to rend those close to death.

When you hit a marked creature with your Sneak Attack, you can deal additional damage equal to your rogue level. Once you use this ability, you may not do so against until you complete a short or long rest. If you reduce a creature to zero hit points with this ability, you regain a use.

13th Level - Ward of Mortality

Starting at 13th level, you learn to collect and conserve the life force you steal from dying opponents, which materializes as a ward.

When you hit a marked creature with rend, roll your total sneak attack die. You gain temporary hit points equal to the total, unless you already have more.

17th Level - Echo of Reaping

Starting at 17th level, you learn to travel to and harness remnants of death.

When you hit a creature with rend, you may teleport to a corpse within 90 ft of you as a bonus action, and the next attack you make before the end of your next treats the target as being blood marked. In addition, through a one-minute ritual, you may travel to an area of mass death or a sight where you slew a creature within 2 miles, bringing a number of willing creatures equal to the number of creatures you have killed today (maximum of 10). Once you use this ability, you may not do so again until you complete a long rest.

Homebrew / Items

Nindo of the Iron Fist

Nindo of the Iron Fist

Description:

This philosophical path is dedicated to the total mastery of the body. Shinobi of the Iron Fist view complex Ninjutsu as secondary, focusing instead on internal chakra circulation to achieve unmatched physical speed, durability, and raw striking power. They seek to surpass biological limitations through sheer willpower and rigorous training, defining their power by control over their chosen Master Weapon.

Level 3 - Initiation

Nindo Jutsu.

At certain levels you learn jutsu from your Shinobi Nindo, you always know these Jutsu and they do not count against your total known jutsu.

Rank Jutsu Learn Level
D Lion Combo 3rd
C Shadow of the Dancing Leaf 5th
B Leaf Great Whirlwind 8th

Fighting Style Options: You must choose a Fighting Style suitable for a close-quarters brawler. Choose one from:

  • Unarmed Fighting
  • Dueling
  • Defense

Master Weapon Discipline: You designate one Master Weapon from the following options: Unarmed Strike, Club (Nunchaku), Dagger, Sickle, Shortsword, Scimitar, Kusarigama or Dart.

  • Master Property: You can use the master Property of your Master Weapon. If you choose unarmed strikes as your master weapon, it gains the Push master property.

Gate of Opening:

You gain access to the first stage of the legendary Eight Gates. As a Bonus Action, you can open the Gate of Opening for 1 minute (opening your gates costs no Chakra). While active, your movement speed increases by 10 feet, and your attacks with your Master Weapon deal an additional 1d4 Force damage. You can open your gates a number of times equal to your Constitution modifier (minimum of once), regaining all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest

Higher Gates:

As you unlock higher Jutsu Ranks, you can open deeper gates whenever you open your gates, gaining each gate’s benefit cumulatively.

  • Second Gate — Healing (C-Rank, 5th level): you have Advantage on Strength checks and Strength saving throws.
  • Third Gate — Life (B-Rank, 8th level): your gate Force damage increases to 1d6.
  • Fourth and Fifth Gates — Pain and Limit (A-Rank, 13th level): your gate speed bonus increases to 20 feet and your gate Force damage increases to 1d8 (4th Gate) or 1d10 (5th Gate).
  • Sixth Gate — Joy (S-Rank, 17th level): your Master Weapon attacks gain an additional 5 feet of reach.

When your gates close, you take 1d10 damage for each gate you opened beyond the first; this damage cannot be reduced or prevented.

Level 7 - Weight Drop

You master physical movement, making you a highly mobile and resilient skirmisher.

  • Iron Conditioning: You can take the Dash or Disengage action as a Bonus Action on your turn.
  • Weight Drop: Your jumping distances are tripled. Additionally, when you fall, you can use your Reaction to reduce any falling damage you take by an amount equal to five times your Shinobi level.

Level 15 - Morning Peacock

You have attained such mastery over rapid Taijutsu that your attacks move with explosive speed, allowing you to bypass typical action limits.

  • The Third Punch: When you take the Attack action on your turn, you can make three attacks instead of two.
  • Explosive Blows: When you hit a creature three times with your Master Weapon in a single turn, the target takes an extra 3d6 Fire damage from the explosive friction created by your speed.

Level 20 - Eight Gates Release: Gate of Death (Capstone)

You puncture the cardiac pressure point, unleashing the red vapor of your burning blood to gain power that rivals the gods, at the cost of your own life force.

Activation: As a Bonus Action, you can open the Eighth Gate. You enter the Gate of Death Mode for 1 minute, or until you are reduced to 0 Hit Points.

While this mode is active, you gain the following benefits:

  • God-Like Speed: When you take the Attack action on your turn, you can make five attacks instead of two.
  • Pressure Strikes: Your melee weapon attacks gain an additional 10 feet of reach, striking enemies with air pressure alone.
  • Overwhelming Power: On a hit, your melee weapon attacks deal an additional 2d10 Force damage.
  • Unrestrained Chakra: The Chakra cost for all Taijutsu and Bukijutsu you cast is halved (rounded down, minimum of 1).

The Cost:

  • Burning Life: You cannot regain Hit Points by any means while this mode is active.
  • Inevitable Decay: At the end of each of your turns, you take 35 Bludgeoning damage. This damage cannot be reduced or prevented in any way, and it bypasses all resistances and immunities (including Temporary Hit Points).

Ending the Technique: The mode ends automatically if you drop to 0 Hit Points. You can also choose to close the gate early as an Action. When the mode ends (either by dropping to 0 HP or closing it early), you immediately suffer 2 levels of Exhaustion.

Orb of Remembrance

Orb of Remembrance

Wondrous Item, uncommon

Description

This glassy orb is 3 inches in diameter, weighs 1/2 pound, and is wrapped in a golden wire cage. Strange, wispy smoke drifts around inside the orb, creating cloud-like shapes that are almost recognizable as real-life objects.

While holding the orb, you can use an action to speak its command word, priming the orb and causing the smoke inside to restlessly billow and swirl. While holding the primed orb, you can gently squeeze it (no action required) to cause it to record that moment in time around you. When you do, the glassy sphere becomes perfectly clear over the course of 1 minute and reveals an exact duplicate of the area around you in up to a 30-foot radius as a miniature, illusory diorama inside it. While holding the orb, the scene inside soundlessly replays the next 6 seconds following the diorama's capture.

An orb remains primed for 1 minute or until used to capture a diorama. Touching a primed orb of remembrance to one that already has a diorama creates a duplicate of the diorama in the primed orb. Speaking the command word again while shaking the orb causes the diorama inside to disappear into smoke, allowing it to be primed once more.

Powderkeg

Powderkeg

Description

Volatile and dangerous, Powderkegs typically make use of exceedingly dangerous chemicals or magic to act as the ultimate deterrent. Despite this, Bulwarks under this specialization tend to show great care for the power they wield.

Features:

  • 3rd Level - Powderkeg Training
  • 3rd Level - Volatile Ward
  • 7th Level - Combustion
  • 13th level - Explosive Ward
  • 18th Level - Fission

3rd Level - Powderkeg Training

When you select this specialization at 3rd level, you gain proficiency with firearms and alchemist supplies.

3rd Level - Volatile Ward

Additionally at 3rd level, you have the ability to work volatile compounds into your armor and defensive strategies. Whenever you use your fortitude feature, the triggering creature takes fire damage equal to your bulwark level.

7th Level - Combustion

Starting at 7th level, your knack for mixing potent reactions extends to aid you in combat. While you are holding alchemist supplies and take the attack action, you can replace one attack on each of your turns with a burst of chemical energy.

Target a creature within 15 feet of yourself. The target must succeed a Dexterity Saving Throw (DC 8 + your Strength Modifier + your Proficiency Bonus) or take 2d8 damage. This damage is acid, fire or poison (your choice).

13th level - Explosive Ward

When you reach 13th level, you learn to improve your Volatile Ward with even more explosive potential. When you use your Volatile Ward feature, you can choose to have each creature within 20 feet of you take the damage, instead of just the triggering creature. If you do so, the feature deals only half damage.

18th Level - Fission

Starting at 18th level, the explosive potential within you reaches its pinnacle. As an action, you can trigger a chain reaction within your armor to detonate out in a violent burst. You immediately take 20d6 fire damage and 20d6 bludgeoning damage, and each creature within 40 feet of you must succeed a dexterity saving throw (DC 8 + your Strength Modifier + you Proficiency Bonus) or take the same damage, taking half as much on a successful save. Objects that are not being worn or carried in the area also take this damage. After using this feature, you have immunity to all damage until the end of your next turn.

Once you use this feature, you must finish a long rest before you can do so again.
