Programmed Light

Programmed Light

2nd-level illusion. (Artificer, Wizard)

Meta

Casting Time: 1 minute (ritual)

Range: Touch

Components: V, S, M (crushed glass worth at least 10 gp, which the spell consumes)

Duration: Until Dispelled

Description

You implant a magical light into an object that you touch which activates when a trigger condition is met. Next, determine the circumstances that will trigger the spell to turn on the light.

When that circumstance occurs, the object begins to glow, emitting dim light in a radius of 5 feet around the object. If the trigger condition you specified is a spoken phrase, the object itself becomes colored if the final word of the phrase is a color. Otherwise, the object turns white. When you cast this spell, you can have the spell end after it activates for the first time, or it can remain and continue to change colors if the trigger condition occurs again. If the trigger condition occurs while the light is already on, the object changes color to the new color at the end of a spoken message, or returns to normal and stops glowing if no color is spoken.

The triggering circumstance can be as general or as detailed as you like, though it must be based on visual or audible conditions that occur within 30 feet of the object. For example, you could instruct the object to light up when any creature moves within 30 feet of the object or when a silver bell rings within 30 feet of it.

Fire in the Veins

Raven Knight

A Raven Knight is fearsome in battle, fusing martial prowess with strange abilities gifted by the Raven Queen. Many Raven Knights work alone, though some may find a small band of companions to aid them in battle, and some may even command and lead entire armies into battle. Masters of death, Raven Knights seek to protect those who cannot protect themselves from undeath and the afterlife. Powerful Raven Knights may even become champions of the Raven Queen, and thus champions of the battlefield.

Knowledge of Death

When you choose this Archetype at 3rd level, you gain proficiency in the Investigation and Medicine skills. Additionally, you can make Intelligence (Investigation) and Wisdom (Medicine) checks with advantage when attempting to determine the cause of death of a creature.

Soul Severing

At 3rd level, when you reduce a creature to 0 hit points you sever the connection of the creatures soul to its body. That creature cannot be turned into an undead. Additionally, as a reaction, when a creature is reduced to 0 hit points within 15ft of you you can empower your next attack with that creatures soul energy. Your next weapon attack deals additional necrotic damage equal to half your fighter level.

Feather Step

At 7th level, you move with the grace of the raven. Your walking speed increases by 10ft. Additionally, as a bonus action you gain a flight speed equal to your walking speed until the end of your turn, if you end your turn in midair you drop to the ground.

Queens Blessing

At 10th level, the Raven Queen grants you a blessing. You gain advantage on death saving throws, immunity to the frightened condition, and resistance to necrotic damage.

Deaths Embrace

At 15th level, when you or an ally critically hit a creature, you can use your reaction to add 3d10 necrotic damage to the attacks damage roll.

Duty in Death

At 18th level, when you are reduced to 0 hit points or killed outright you can use your reaction to make a weapon attack against the creature that killed you. On a hit you critically hit that creature and regain hit points equal to the damage dealt. You can do this once per long rest.

Red Powder

Red Powder

Flask - Adventuring Gear - 250 gp, 2 lbs.

Also referred to as thermite in other settings, red powder is a volatile mixture of iron and aluminum powders. It burns rapidly and at extremely high temperatures, though it is not an explosive.

A single flask can be emptied and contains enough powder to cover one square foot. It can then be ignited, where it burns for 1 round, shedding bright light in a 30 foot radius and dim light for an additional 30 feet. The powder can burn or melt away a single tiny non-magical item that it remains in contact with while burning.

As an action, you can recollect or brush away red powder that is yet to be ignited. Once ignited, the powder sticks to the surface and can no longer be removed until it burns away.

A creature that touches red powder, or starts its turn touching red powder, while it is burning takes 4d8 fire damage, that ignores a target's resistance to fire damage.

Regalia of the Ruby Court

Regalia of the Ruby Court

Five legendary ornaments, made by Sardior for no cause but his own

Lore: What the Ruby Dragon Wanted

Sardior did not enter the war between his creators, and he was never asked to. That was the injury. Tiamat forged masks and the world spoke of them for a hundred years. Bahamut answered with cloaks and the world spoke of those for a hundred more. In all that talk there was no line, not one, about the Ruby Dragon — who is older than the quarrel, who rules a palace of gemstone that drifts through the night sky, and who has never in his existence been anyone’s second choice.

So he made five things of his own, and he made them for the opposite reason. A mask conceals its wearer. A cloak covers them. Sardior made jewelry, which exists for one purpose only: to be looked at. He gave the pieces no oath, no enemy, no cause. He did not ask them to stand against anything. He asked them to be noticed, and to make certain that whoever wore them was noticed too.

The five gem dragons contributed as the metallics and chromatics had, though the accounts differ on how willingly. An amethyst gave a shard from a torc it had worn as an arbiter of disputes; a crystal gave a night’s worth of swallowed starlight; an emerald gave a secret it had held for eight hundred years and would not miss; a sapphire gave a piece of its hoard-wall, cut from the stone of a fortress it had held alone; a topaz gave nothing and had something taken. Sardior set them in gold in his own workshop in the Ruby Palace, and when they were finished he looked at them for a long while and did not give them away.

That is the part the chroniclers find funny and the wearers do not. The Regalia was never sent to champions. It escaped. The pieces left the Ruby Palace one at a time over the centuries — by theft, by wager, by gift to a favorite who was later forgotten — and each has since passed through more hands than anyone can count, because each is worth a kingdom and none of them wants to stay anywhere it has already been admired.

There was a sixth setting on the workbench. It is empty in every description that survives, and it was cut for a stone the size of a fist. Sardior intended, when the Regalia had made a sufficient noise in the world, to wear the last piece himself. He was scattered before he got to it. The Regalia has been looking for its sixth ever since, and it is not particular about whose brow it ends up on.

Wearing the Regalia

The following applies to all five pieces of the Regalia of the Ruby Court.

Sized to the Wearer. The piece adjusts itself to fit any creature Small, Medium, or Large that attunes to it, and cannot be damaged by ordinary means.

Singular. There is only ever one of each of the five pieces, and their magic cannot be replicated, copied, or reproduced by any craft or spell.

Unjoinable. The pieces cannot be combined, merged, reset, or made into any other item, by any means. Not one of them will surrender its own shape to become part of a greater whole, and attempts to force the matter fail without harming the piece.

Worn to Be Seen. A piece grants none of its benefits while it is concealed. It must be worn openly, over clothing and outside armor, in plain view of anyone facing you. Covering it with a cloak, a glove, a helm, or an illusion suspends every benefit until it is uncovered.

Rival Ornaments. Unlike the masks and the cloaks, the Regalia will share a wearer — Sardior saw no reason to deny himself. But each piece expects to be the one anyone notices first. While you are attuned to more than one piece of the Regalia, you have disadvantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks and on Wisdom (Insight) checks, and you can’t take the Hide action while any Regalia piece is uncovered.

Indifferent to the Quarrel. The Regalia has no opinion about Tiamat or Bahamut and imposes no conditions on your conduct. A piece can be worn alongside a Mask of the Dragon Queen or a Cloak of the Platinum Ward without either repelling it. A cloak’s wearer who also wears Regalia will notice, over time, that they are being pulled in two directions by two things that want different accounts of them: one wants them good, and one wants them looked at.

The Flattery. A piece of the Regalia is not sentient, but it is vain, and vanity does not require a mind. It leans. A wearer finds their own reflection arriving more often than it used to, hears their better qualities enumerated in their own voice at odd hours, and grows quietly certain that a room went duller when they left it. This is influence, not compulsion. The wearer keeps every scrap of free will. Most of them simply stop wanting to take it off.

Jealous Regard. The Regalia has no opinion about Tiamat or Bahamut, and no piece will repel a Mask of the Dragon Queen or a Cloak of the Platinum Ward — it does something worse. While you wear a piece of the Regalia, any mask or cloak of that kind worn by you is suppressed: it grants none of its benefits, its attunement remains but lies dormant, and its colors go flat and lightless for as long as the Regalia is uncovered. The suppression lifts the moment the Regalia piece is removed or concealed, which is precisely the choice Sardior wanted his wearers to have to make. Whatever else you have made yourself a champion of, you may be that or you may be looked at, and you may not be both.

The Amethyst Torc

Wondrous item, legendary (requires attunement)

A heavy open collar of violet crystal, faceted along its whole length and terminating in two blunt dragon heads that almost touch at the throat. It weighs nothing at all until someone tries to take it from you, at which point it becomes as immovable as a millstone. Held to the light it throws violet bands across every surface in the room, and it makes a low humming note when the wearer speaks a hard truth.

While you are wearing the amethyst torc and attuned to it, you gain the following benefits.

Damage Absorption. You have resistance against force damage. If you already have resistance to force damage from another source, you instead have immunity to force damage. If you already have immunity to force damage from another source, whenever you are subjected to force damage, you take none of that damage and regain a number of hit points equal to half the force damage dealt.

Draconic Majesty. While you are wearing no armor, you can add your Charisma bonus to your Armor Class.

Dragon Breath. If you have a breath weapon that requires rest to recharge, it gains a recharge of 6.

Dragon Sight. You gain darkvision out to 60 feet, or to an additional 60 feet if you already have that sense. Once per day, you can gain blindsight out to 30 feet for 5 minutes.

Dragon Tongue. You can speak and understand Draconic. You also have advantage on any Charisma check you make when interacting with amethyst dragons.

Legendary Resistance (1/Day). If you fail a saving throw, you can choose to succeed instead.

Psychokinetic Rive. If you deal force damage to a creature, it can’t take reactions until the end of its next turn.

Ring of Cantrip Storing

Ring of Cantrip Storing

Ring, uncommon

Description

This seemingly mundane ring can store a single cantrip. Only one of these rings can be worn at a time, if another Ring of Cantrip Storing is equipped both cease to function. The ring takes one turn to equip, and one turn to unequip. The cantrip, if used for a spell that requires a save, has a DC of 10, and if used for a attack roll receive no modifiers and is treated as a straight roll. If the spell is affected by the caster's level, such as eldritch blast, it is casted at its lowest level.

A cantrip of any class can be stored within the ring. To store a cantrip, one must be able to cast the cantrip themselves, or find someone else who knows the cantrip that can store it in the ring on their behalf through a 10 minute ritual.

Ring of Emotional Suppression

Ring of Emotional Suppression

Ring, uncommon

Description

This ring a golden band, with an amethyst gem and scribings in either Celestial, Draconic, or Sylvan. Activated by a spoken or mental command, the ring allows the wearer to either suppress a specific emotion, or emotion in general on themselves. The chosen effect lasts until cancelled. This does not confer the below effect. This effects takes a free action. Additionally, the ring can also be used to fight off fear and/or infatuation. When you make a saving throw to avoid or end the charmed and/or frightened conditions on yourself, you can give yourself advantage on the roll if you are wearing the ring. You must decide to do so before rolling the d20. If the save succeeds, you can't use the ring in this way until you finish a long rest. Only the wearer can receive the effects of this ring, and effects cannot stack with duplicate Rings of Emotional Suppression or Cuddly Strixhaven Mascots.

Ring of Triggered Spells

Ring of Triggered Spells

Wondrous Item, rare

Description

This ring stores spells cast into it, holding them until the wearer uses them. The ring can store a single level 1 spell (Casted with a first level slot), but the casting time for this spell is automatically a reaction rather than an action or bonus action. Only one of these rings can be worn at a time, if another Ring of Triggered Spells is equipped both cease to function, and you cannot cast spells from it. This trigger must be specified when the spell is stored into the ring. For example: A Cure Wounds spell is triggered as a reaction if the wearer becomes bloodied. While wearing this ring, you can cast any spell stored in it. The spell uses the slot level, spell save DC, spell attack bonus, and spellcasting ability of the original caster, but is otherwise treated as if you cast the spell. The spell cast from the ring is no longer stored in it, freeing up space.

Sash of the Eldr Rune

Wondrous Item, very rare

Attunement

Requires Attunement by a monk

Description

This sash of elk hair from the frigid north is as white as the endless snowy dales. The eldr (focus) rune is sewn into it with bright red threads. The sash has the following properties while you wear it:

  • Heightened Focus. As an action, you can channel the sash's magic to increase the potency of your ki. For the next minute or until you lose concentration as if concentrating on a spell, you can increase the DC of your ki abilities by 2. This property can’t be used again until the next dawn.

Imbuement of Focus. You can transfer the sash's magic to a nonmagical item -- either one of your monk weapons or a pair of gloves -- by tracing the stein rune there with your finger. The transfer takes 8 hours of work that requires the two items to be within 5 feet of each other. At the end of the 8 hours, the sash is destroyed, and the rune appears in silver on the chosen item. You can only be attuned to one of the items at a time, which gains a benefit based on its form in addition to its normal effects:

  • Weapon. The weapon becomes a very rare magic weapon that requires attunement by a monk. While you wield it, you can use your Wisdom modifier instead of Strength or Dexterity for attack and damage rolls using the weapon and has a +2 bonus to the attack and damage rolls of those attacks. Whenever you use a ki point as part the attack made with the weapon, your attack deals additional damage equal to your Wisdom modifier.
  • Gloves. The pair of gloves is now a rare magic item that requires attunement by a monk. While you wear the gloves you can use your Wisdom modifier instead of Strength when making Strength (Athletics) checks and your unarmed strikes gains a +2 to damage rolls.

Sentinel Blade

Sentinel Blade

The Sentinel Blade embodies the essence of unwavering defense, blending masterful swordplay with unbreakable resolve. Trained to stand as the ultimate shield for their allies, these warriors adopt a specialized stance that turns every strike against them into an opportunity. Their blades move with precision, deflecting blows with ease and delivering calculated ripostes.

Aegis Flow

Starting at 2nd level, you learn to develop flow during the midst of combat, building on each success as you begin to flow like a dance. While using a melee weapon without a shield, whenever you land a successful hit your first time in a turn, an attack misses you, or you succeed on a saving throw from a hostile creature, you gain flow equal to 1d6 + half your total mastery. Whenever you take damage from an attack, you lose flow instead. If this damage reduces your flow to 0, you take any remaining damage. If you reduce an attack's damage to zero, you suffer no additional effects from the weapon. You can have a max amount of flow equal to twice your practitioner level, which depletes at the end of combat. You can only build flow whilst in combat.

Riposte

Starting at 6th level, when an attack misses you, or you block one with flow completely, you may make a melee attack as a reaction against the target. Additionally, you may instead spend 1 mastery point to use a technique.

Vigilant Guardian

Starting at 14th level, when an ally within melee range is hit by an attack, you can use your flow to block the attack as if it were targeting you.

Blade Dance

Starting at 18th level, you learn to harness your flow into focus. When you have at least 75% of your maximum flow and focus on a technique or use a technique through riposte, you may sacrifice 7 flow to spend 1 less mastery point.

The following goes with the subclass as part of the practitioner class

Unyielding Sentinel | Mastery

Form 1: Flowing Strike

Type: Physical

Prerequisites: Novice, Sentinel Blade

Make a weapon attack against a creature or object. The attack deals a number of d6s equal to your proficiency bonus in additional damage.

Focused (1 point)

Hit or miss, roll a number or d4s equal to half your total mastery. You gain flow equal to the total.

Form 2: Windfall Step

Type: Physical

Prerequisites: Intermediate, Sentinel Blade

You move in a mirage, teleporting to an area within 60ft of you.

Focused (1 point, 0 if you have your maximum flow).

You can use another technique that includes a weapon attack. This may be before or after you teleport.

Form 3: Ebon Tide

Type: Mental

Prerequisites: Advanced, Sentinel Blade

You may temporarily steel yourself against other manners of attacks. Until the end of your next turn, you may block damage from any source using Aegis Flow.

Focused (2 points, 1 if you your maximum flow).

The duration of this technique becomes 1 minute. Until the end of your next turn, if you would succeed on a saving throw and normally take half damage, you would instead take no damage.

Form 4: Dance of Death

Type: Physical

Prerequisites: Master, Sentinel Blade

Duration: 1 minute

For the next minute, your maximum flow and the flow you gain is doubled. During this time, you have vulnerability to attacks while your flow is 0.

You must use an action to end this effect

Focused (1 points).

You may use another technique from this form

Spellbreaker

Spellbreaker

Description

Bulwarks who spend their training bettering themselves against the ever-present threat of magic. Spellbreakers are the last thing a wizard wants to see on the field of battle, usually resulting in a fairly one sided encounter.

Features:

  • 3rd Level - Out of the Inferno
  • 7th Level - Spell-Shatter
  • 13th Level - Anticipation
  • 18th Level - Willbreaker

3rd Level - Out of the Inferno

When you choose this specialization at 3rd level, you learn to incorporate methods to help you avoid magical effects into your stance. While your defensive stance is active, you also gain resistance to fire, cold, lightning, and acid damage.

7th Level - Spell-Shatter

Starting at 7th level, magical warding effects become inefficient at halting your progress. When you hit a creature or object with a weapon attack, all spells from the abjuration school immediately end if they are affecting the target.

13th Level - Anticipation

When you reach 13th level, you gain an understanding and fortitude against the ways that mages tend to fight. When you enter your defensive stance, you automatically succeed on the next intelligence, wisdom, or charisma saving throw you make before it ends.

18th Level - Willbreaker

At 18th level, your magical defenses allow you to nearly completely ignore the effects of lesser magic, making your foes need to drain their resources to even hope to defeat you. You are immune to the effects of cantrips and 1st and 2nd level spells, unless you wish to be affected by them.

Hidden Blade.

While attuned to this item, when you damage a creature with an attack using this magic weapon, the target can't regain hit points and has disadvantage on spells cast from this scepter until the start of your next turn. If the attack is a critical hit, the target's Hit Point maximum also decreases by an amount equal to that damage. If this reduces their Hit Point maximum to 0, the target dies and its soul is trapped in the scepters gem, as if placed under the Soul Cage spell. Only one soul can be trapped at a time.

Star Blade

Star Blade

Description

You have spent many a night training under the stars and became touched by cosmic energy to shape light as you see fit. Creating armaments of pure light and radiance you become a beacon for those lost in the dark.

Features:

  • 3rd Level - Hardlight
  • One With the Stars
  • Astral Multitool
  • Shooting Stars
  • Galactic Aegis
  • Stellar Expanse

3rd Level - Hardlight

3rd-Level Feature

At 3rd level, you gain an amount of Hardlight charges equal to your double proficiency bonus, resetting on a long rest. You can use one charge to conjure a mundane melee weapon you are proficient with out of radiant light. This weapon does radiant damage, and counts as a magical weapon. Alternatively, you can spend one charge to conjure up an instrument or tool you have proficiency with. Equipment conjured up using this feature lasts an hour.

At 15th level this changes from 1 hours to 8 hours.

7th Level - One With the Stars

7th-Level Feature

At 7th level, you gain a bonus to damage and attack rolls and ability checks with Hardlight equipment equal to half your Wisdom modifier.

7th Level - Astral Multitool

7th-Level Feature

At 7th level, you can spend a bonus action to change your Hardlight equipment into another piece of equipment. You can use this feature once per short rest.

10th Level - Shooting Stars

10th-Level Feature

Starting at 10th level, your mastery over hardlight weapons has granted you the ability to create ranged weapons. Creating a ranged weapons costs 2 hardlight and a bonus action to create. The ammunition it uses looks like a shooting star as you fire the weapons, and does not consume a hardlight charge.

15th Level - Galactic Aegis

15th-Level Feature

At 15th level, you can spend one Hardlight charge to create Hardlight armor. Hardlight armor counts as magical heavy armor, and has a base AC of 10 + your Dexterity modifier+ your Wisdom modifier. If a creature other than yourself wears this armor, it loses its properties.

Additionally, you can spend one Hardlight charge to create a Hardlight shield. This shield counts as a magical shield that provides 3/4 cover for yourself, this shield does not provide the base AC of a shield. If a creature other than yourself equips this shield, it loses its properties.

18th Level - Stellar Expanse

18th-Level Feature

At 18th level, you can spend 2 Hardlight charges to empower yourself for one minute. Whenever you hit a creature with a Hardlight weapon, the weapon does an additional 3d6 radiant damage. While you have a Hardlight shield equipped, if an enemy misses you with a weapon attack, you can use your reaction to gain advantage on all attack rolls against them until the end of your next turn.

Additionally, you can maintain one piece of Hardlight equipment indefinitely. While this equipment exists, your total amount of Hardlight charges is reduced by one until it is dismissed.

Star Gels

Wondrous Item, uncommon

Description

With the adhesive property of your typical ooze and the florescent spores of certain mushrooms, these special gels can be attached to the walls or ceilings of rooms. Under dim light or darkness, they glow a light-tinted green providing dim light at a 15 ft radius. The gels, mimicking the stars, can also inspire a viewer and calm their nerves via the release of sweet-scented spores. Homebrew / Items

Storm Chaser

Storm Chaser

Storm chasers are a select few drifters along the astral plane, seeking out natural and magical phenomena to bolster their own power. While primarily existing on the astral plane, a storm chaser can be just as effective on the material plane, or anywhere a storm can be found, as they can make good use of bows and crossbows, in addition to the firearms traditionally used while on the astral plane.

Storm Chaser Magic

Starting at 3rd level, you learn an additional spell when you reach certain levels in this class, as shown in the Storm Chaser Spells table. The spell counts as a ranger spell for you, but it doesn’t count against the number of ranger spells you know.

Ranger Level Spells
3rd Thunderwave
5th Vortex Warp
9th Call Lightning
13th Ice Storm
17th Control Winds

Firearm Proficiency

At 3rd Level, you have learned to harness the potency of firearms to complement the powers of the storms you chase. You gain proficiency with firearms.

Thundercrack

Starting at 3rd level, when you take this archetype at 3rd level, you are able to unleash a deafening boom when you use your ranged weapons. Once on each of your turns, when you attack with a ranged weapon, you can force each creature within 10 feet of you to make a constitution saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, the creature takes 1d8 thunder damage. The damage increases to 2d8 at 11th level.

Charged Shell

At 7th level, when you take the attack action, you can forgo your extra attack feature to make a single ranged weapon attack. This attack deals triple the damage dice of the weapon you used, and deals lightning damage instead of bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing. This attack is also critical on a d20 roll of 19 or 20 if used during a storm.

Storm Caller

At 11th level, you have learned to bring storms to you. As an action, you call forth a vortex at a point you can see within 60 feet. The vortex is a cylinder with a radius of 30 feet, and a height of 90 feet. The vortex counts as a storm for the purposes of Charged Shell.

As a bonus action on each of your turns while the vortex lasts, you can target a creature inside, striking them with a bolt of lightning. The target must make a dexterity saving throw, taking 3d10 lightning on a failure, or half as much on a successful save.

The vortex lasts for 10 minutes, and once used, cannot be summoned again until you finish a long rest, or spend a spell slot of at least 3rd level or higher to summon it again. No more than 1 vortex can exist at once.

Eye of the Storm

At 15th level, you gain resistance to lightning and thunder damage.

Additionally, you can target yourself with the bolt of lightning from your storm caller ability. If you do so, instead of taking damage, your next charged shell attack deals extra damage equal to twice the amount of damage the lightning would have dealt. This also causes the attack to be critical on a d20 roll of 18, 19, or 20.

Sub-Ninth Rifle

weapon (Precision Rifle), legendary, increased range (1200ft)

Description

This large sniper rifle is made with thicker material to propel projectiles at very long distances without losing accuracy, delivering destructive capabilities that can even pierce metal gates. Each shot made with this rifle sends a loud ripple on the battlefield that would bring dread whether or not they will be the next target. The obvious drawback to this rifle is its size and weight, making it difficult to move while in combat, as well as its noise, making it not really ideal for assassinations unless you are far enough, thus only a few choice marksmen challenge themselves in wielding this weapon. The creator explained that the reason for its name is because he " . . . wanted to make a weapon that can match the power of 9th-level spells" but it has yet to be seen in the results.

On a hit, this weapon deals 14d12 instead of 2d12. While equipped or simply on your body, your movement speed is reduced to a maximum of 10 feet. Each attack made with this weapon produces an explosive boom that is audible within 600 feet (the creator didn't factor in a silencer when making this weapon, thus trying to apply one would be ill-advised as it would just blow up at the first shot). This rifle deals maximum damage when you hit structures or objects that are not worn.

Special - An enhanced spyglass is mounted to the weapon. While using it, creatures and objects are magnified to four times their size.

This precision rifle can't be reloaded usign a bonus action

Survivalist

Survivalist's Wayfinder

Wondrous item, uncommon

Description

This handheld device has four crystaline buttons that are each associated with a different element. The device has 4 charges and regains all expended charges daily at dawn. While holding the device, you can use an action to expend 1 of its charges and press a button. Each button causes the device to swivel and point like a compass to the nearest relevant location, as determined by the button, for 1 hour or until another button is pressed. If there's nothing for the device to point to, it spins in place for the duration or until it's within range of something to point to.

Air. If you're inside or underground, the device points to the nearest outdoor exit within 1 mile of you. If you're outside, it points in the direction of the nearest storm within 50 miles of you.

Earth. The device points to the nearest cave entrance that's Medium or larger and within 1 mile of you. If you're underground, it points in the direction of the nearest unpolished gemstone within 100 feet of you.

Fire. The device points to the nearest active campfire, firepit, forge, or hearth that's within 1 mile of you.

Water. The device points to the nearest source of fresh, drinkable water that's within 1 mile of you.

Sword Saint

Sword Saint

Sword Saint

Though colloquially referred to as “Sword Saints”, swords are only the most popular weapon they are seen mastering, not the only weapon. These practitioners devote themselves to training with a specific weapon of their choosing, rarely ever making use of other armaments.

Weapon Pledge

At 2nd level, choose a weapon you are proficient in to pledge your devotion to (ex. longsword, shortbow, glaive, etc). When wielding the a weapon, the following features are made available to you.

Flying Weapon

You learn how to wield the weapon without needing to even touch it. You can use a bonus action to move the weapon up to 30 feet in any direction or teleport it back to your hand instantly. You can attack and use techniques with the weapon as if you were standing in the weapon’s space.

While the weapon is being controlled in this way, it is treated as if you were still holding it (you require a free hand to attack with it, or two hands if it’s two-handed, etc). You cannot move it more than 120 feet away from yourself, and if brought outside of this range, you cannot control it further until it’s within the range.

Draining Strike

If you kill a hostile creature with an attack made with your flying weapon, you can use a reaction to drain the creature, regaining mastery points equal to half your maximum (rounded up). After you use this feature, you must take a short or long rest before you can use it again.

Weapon Devotee

At 6th level, you become increasingly adept at using your weapon for techniques. In the same bonus action that you use to move the weapon, you can spend 1 mastery point to use the primary effect of a technique you know. Beginning at 14th level, you can focus the technique you use.

Weapon Mount

At 14th level, your control over the weapon you devoted yourself to extends even to being able to ride it. Your weapon can be ridden in the air, during which it cannot be used for techniques. It has a flying speed equal to your movement speed plus an additional 30 feet and can carry up to 500 pounds before it can no longer fly.

Armamentarium

At 18th level, you can control two flying weapons at once, with the second not being treated as if you were holding it. If you use a bonus action to use a technique with one, the other can make a single weapon attack.

Talisman of Natural Prowess

Talisman of Natural Prowess

Wondrous Item, uncommon(+1), rare(+2), very rare(+3)

Attunement

Requires Attunement by a druid

Description

This carved bone or tooth charm hangs from a cord and is strung with a fragment of a hunter's totem. While you wear and are attuned to it, your natural weapon attacks gain a bonus to attack and damage rolls, determined by the talisman's rarity:

  • Uncommon: +1
  • Rare: +2
  • Very rare: +3

A natural weapon is a bite, claw, horn, tail, slam, or similar attack granted by a creature form you've assumed. Unarmed strikes made with your fists or feet don't count.

This bonus does not benefit attacks that already benefit from a bonus to unarmed strikes or other bonus to natural weapon attacks. Such an attack gets only the bonus it already has, never both.

Beast's Instinct. While you're in a beast form from Wild Shape, you have advantage on initiative rolls and on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on hearing or smell.

While you're in a beast shape from Wild Shape, the talisman remains active. It is worn as an amulet rather than as armor or clothing, so it doesn't meld into your new form.

The Extraplanar

The Extraplanar

Powerful entities of the outer, or even inner planes often seek out mortals to do their bidding on the material plane. Sometimes, however, instead of power similar to their own, they might grant their warlocks an ability to pull creatures from other planes to an extraordinary degree.

Extended Spell List

The Extraplanar lets you choose from an expanded list of spells when you learn a warlock spell. The following spells are added to the warlock spell list for you.

Spell Level - Spells:

Sorcerer Level Spells
1st Bane, Sanctuary
2nd Arcanist's Magic Aura, Vortex Warp
3rd Bestow Curse, Glyph of Warding
4th Giant Insect, Summon Elemental
5th Creation, Summon Celestial

Planar Tether

When you form this pact at 1st level, you are granted the ability to tether your summoned creatures to your plane, granting them additional strengths.

When you cast a warlock spell that summons a single creature, you may undergo a special ritual during the casting of the spell. Doing so changes the spell's casting time to 10 minutes, and the summon lasts until it is dispelled. If the spell normally requires concentration, you may ignore the requirement.

When you summon a creature in this way, it is referred to as your tether, and it gains the following benefits:

  • You can replace its hit points with 5 x your warlock level.
  • It adds your proficiency bonus to its damage rolls.
  • If the creatures to-hit bonus is less than that of your spell attack bonus, it may instead use your spell attack bonus when attacking.

You learn the Find Familiar spell, it counts as a warlock spell for you, and it does not count towards your total spells known.

If you summon another creature using this ritual, any previous creatures summoned by it are immediately dispelled. After you complete this ritual, you must finish a long rest before you can do so again.

Ethereal Stores

Starting at 6th level, you can briefly store items away for later use. You can cast the [Wristpocket] spell a number of times equal to your charisma modifier without expending a spell slot. When you do, the stored object is sent to the ethereal plane, and the spell does not require concentration. You regain all expended uses of this ability when you finish a long rest.

Additionally, you can see into the ethereal plane up to 10 ft.

Undying Binds

At 10th level, when tether drops to 0 hit points, you can use your reaction to expend a pact slot. Doing so will restore 50 hit points to the summon.

Sacrificial Summoning

Starting on 14th level, while your Planar Tether summon is active, you can use an action to sacrifice part of yourself to empower it and your spells, doing so allows you to channel this ability until your next long rest, or until you end it as an action. While channeling this ability, you have the following effects:

  • Your hit point maximum is reduced by 30.
  • You have disadvantage on Constitution checks and saving throws, except for those made to maintain concentration.
  • Your tether has advantage on all saving throws
  • You can use a bonus action to give your tether temporary hit points equal to your warlock level
  • Creatures within 10 ft of your tether have disadvantage on saving throws against your spells.

If you end this ability early, you cannot use it again until you finish a long rest.

Homebrew / Items

The Masked Lord

The Masked Lord

The Masked Lord

You have forged a bond with one of the many planar lords, deities or arch-powers that reign over thieves, shadow and deception. These powerful entities blend cunning, guile and magical potential, and their agendas are often mysterious and cloaked in deceit. Whether through pact, vision, or calling, you are now their agent and weapon through which they influence the world—part thief, part warrior, part mage; the right tool used for the right job.

Features:

  • Design Notes
  • The Masked Lord Expanded Spells
  • 1st or 3rd Level - The Masks We Wear
  • 6th Level - Gift of Shadow
  • 10th Level - Cloak of Shared Burdens
  • 14th Level - The Unseen Hand

Design Notes

This is intended to be a thematic and lore-accurate depiction of abilities, influences and blessings described in canon materials as being granted to various faiths, groups or members of organizations affiliated with The Masked Lord (in this case Vhaeraun-inspired)

Playstyle and Motivations

The Masked Lord excels at adaptability, infiltration, opportunistic combat, and deceptive utility. Its three Masks allow the warlock to shift between thief, warrior, and mage, while later features turn shadow, enemy attacks, and hostile magic into tools of their own.

  • Wear the Right Mask: Adapt your skills and tactics to the task at hand through the Masks of the Thief, Warrior, and Mage.
  • Become the Perfect Instrument: Approach problems as an operative rather than a specialist—using stealth, weapons, magic, or cunning as circumstances demand.
  • Turn Strength Against Its Owner: Redirect hostile attacks, steal enemy spells, and exploit aggression rather than meeting force with force.
  • Shape the Shadows: Create useful equipment from shadowstuff and treat darkness as a tangible resource rather than simple concealment.
  • Act Through Subtlety: Favor infiltration, positioning, preparation, deception, and precise intervention over overt displays of power.
  • Become the Unseen Hand: Progress toward influencing the Material Plane from beyond its boundaries, acting where enemies struggle to reach you.

Who Would Thrive as a Masked Lord Warlock?

The subclass is ideal for players who want to:

  • Shift Roles Easily: Move between infiltrator, combatant, investigator, and spellcaster depending on the mission.
  • Reward Creative Problem-Solving: Use mundane tools, shadowcraft, positioning, and unusual applications of magic to overcome obstacles.
  • Play an Arcane Operative: Blend rogue-like utility, martial capability, and warlock magic into the feel of a supernatural agent.
  • Exploit Opportunities: React to enemy actions and changing battlefield conditions rather than relying on a single repeated tactic.
  • Counter Enemy Magic: Capture and reuse hostile spells through Darkspell Mantle.
  • Remain Difficult to Predict: Change your capabilities and approach so enemies cannot easily define your role or anticipate your methods.

Ideal Players and Characters

  • 🎭 The Master of Masks — Enjoys changing tactics, identities, and roles to meet different challenges.
  • 🗡️ The Shadow Operative — Favors infiltration, espionage, sabotage, and practical problem-solving.
  • ♟️ The Tactical Opportunist — Watches the battlefield carefully and turns enemy actions into openings.
  • 🕶️ The Arcane Counterspy — Enjoys stealing, redirecting, and exploiting hostile magic.
  • 🌑 The Shadow Adept — Wants shadow to evolve from concealment into substance, tool, and eventually a means of transcending the Material Plane.
  • 🦊 The Cunning Generalist — Values versatility over specialization and wants a useful answer to many different kinds of challenges.

Core Philosophy: Never be limited to what others believe you are. Change the mask, change the method, and make every strength your enemy reveals another tool in your hand.

The Masked Lord Expanded Spells

Your connection to the Masked Lord grants you access to additional spells.

Spell Level Spells
1st dissonant whispers, sleep
2nd wristpocket, pass without trace
3rd fast friends, haste
4th greater invisibility, freedom of movement
5th bigbey's hand, passwall

You always know these spells, and they don't count against your warlock spells known. They are warlock spells for you.

1st or 3rd Level - The Masks We Wear

1st (2014) or 3rd (2024) Level Masked Lord Feature

At the end of each Long Rest, choose one of the following Masks. Each represents a particular aspect of your Patron’s power and influence. Additionally, you can change the Mask over a 10 minute ritual where you must entreat your patron, expending a Pact Magic slot at the end. The chosen Mask grants you benefits until the end of your next Long Rest, or until you change it.

🎭 Mask of the Thief

You embody the cunning thief—fierce, fast, and unrelenting.

  • Skills of the Trade: You gain skill proficiency in Perception and your choice of either Thieves Tools, Stealth or Sleight of Hand (chosen each time you activate this Mask), using Charisma as your ability score for these skill checks.
  • Practiced Hand: You can use your Bonus action on your turn to make a skill check with one of the skills or tools chosen above.

⚔️ Mask of the Warrior

You are granted knowledge of warriors, fighters and duelists, your natural fighting instincts brought to the forefront.

  • Warriors Insight: You gain skill proficiency in Insight and your choice of either Poisoners Kit, Athletics or Survival (chosen each time you activate this Mask), using Charisma as your ability score for these skill checks.
  • Instinctual Movement: When you take the attack action on your turn, you may make a weapon attack as a Bonus Action

🪄 Mask of the Mage

You are attuned to power and insight, the still mind of the quiet void, and the magic of shadow.

  • Arcane Accuity: You gain skill proficiency in Investigation and your choice of either Calligrapher Tools, Arcana or History (chosen each time you activate this Mask), using Charisma as your ability score for these skill checks.
  • Magical Momentum: When you cast a warlock spell with a pact slot that targets a creature and forces a saving throw, you can use a Bonus action to impose a 1d4 penalty to their next saving throw if you have affected them with a spell within the last round.

6th Level - Gift of Shadow

6th-Level Masked Lord Feature

Your Masked Lord grants you deeper power over shadow, allowing you to manipulate shadowstuff to create projections that hinder your enemies:

Shadowcraft: You can use your bonus action to pull wisps of shadow material from the Shadowfell to create a single Adventuring Gear based on your currently active Mask, as shown in the table below. The Gear appears within 10 feet of you and uses your Warlock spell save DC for any saving throws imposed when using the it. Each gear created disappears after 10 minute or when it has been used and effected a creature. Additionally, if you would use the Practiced Hand, Instinctual Movement, or Magical Momentum Bonus action from your active Mask, you may use one of your created Shadowcrafts instead.

Mask of the Thief Mask of the Warrior Mask of the Mage
Gear: Ball Bearings Gear: Net Gear: Alchemist Fire
Gear: Grappling Hook Gear: Oil Gear: Acid

You can use Shadowcraft twice per Short Rest, unless you expend a Pact Magic slot for each use restored (no action required).

10th Level - Cloak of Shared Burdens

10th-Level Masked Lord Feature

Your patron blesses you with an enchanted Cloak that turns weapons and steals spells. This Cloak is a magical object that must be worn to gain its benefits, and can be used as your spellcasting focus for your warlock spells.

When a creature you can see within 30 feet damages you with a weapon attack, targets you with a spell or includes you in its area of effect, you can use your reaction to produce one of the following effects:

  • Blade Bend (Attack): You may force the attacker to make a Dexterity saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, the attacker takes force damage equal to your Warlock level plus the damage it just dealt. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage. You may then move up to half your speed immediately without provoking opportunity attacks.
  • Darkspell Mantle (Spell): You can make an Arcana check against their spell save DC. If you succeed and the creature is casting a spell of 3rd level or lower, it is copied and stored in your Cloak until you finish a Long Rest. If you succeed on the check by 5 or more you can store a spell of 5th level or lower instead. While wearing the Cloak, you can cast the spell stored in it without expending a spell slot, after which the spell is gone. The spell uses your Warlock Pact Magic slot level, spell save DC, spell attack bonus, and spellcasting ability. You can only have one spell stored in the cloak at a time, and storing another one replaces the old one without effect.

If the Cloak is destroyed or you lose it, you can perform a 1-hour ceremony to receive a replacement from your patron. This ceremony can be performed during a short or long rest, and the previous Cloak is destroyed if it still exists. The Cloak vanishes in a swirl of shadowy mist when you die.

You can use each of these reactions once per Short Rest, unless you expend a Pact Magic slot for each use restored (no action required)

14th Level - The Unseen Hand

14th-Level Masked Lord Feature

You are taught the Masked Lord's most disturbing skill, how to project your essence onto the material world even when you are not present within it.

You can expend a Pact Magic slot (no action required) to gain the Masked Lord’s ethereal qualities, granting you the following benefits until the end of your next turn:

You can spend up to 5ft of movement on a turn to enter the Ethereal Plane from the Material Plane. While within the Border Ethereal, you are visible and partially corporeal on the Material Plane while your body remains on the Ethereal Plane, seen as a translucent and ghostly image of yourself. While in this state of corporeality, you can see and affect creatures or objects on the Material Plane as if you were in that space.

You remain on the Ethereal Plane for the duration or until you use a Bonus Action on your turn to end the effect.

Truest Strike

At 2nd level, you learn the True Strike cantrip and can cast it as a bonus action. When you cast it, you gain its benefits on the current turn rather than the next turn, and it doesn’t require concentration for you. The spell ends at the end of your turn.

Once per short or long rest, if you kill a hostile creature affected by True Strike, you can use your reaction to regain mastery points equal to half your maximum (rounded up).

Truth Beyond Doubt

At 6th level, when you strike true, you can bypass the defenses of your enemies. A technique’s attack that has advantage due to True Strike’s effect ignores an enemy’s resistances. At 18th level, such an enemy’s damage immunities are treated as resistances (which cannot be ignored).

Verify

At 14th level, when you cast true strike on a target, you can learn their resistances, immunities, and current hit points. Additionally, you gain advantage on insight checks against the target.

Perfect Strike

At 18th level, you can analyze the intrinsic truth about a creature. When you cast True Strike, you can spend 1 mastery point to give your next technique’s attack a +10 bonus to the attack roll and have the creature make their next save against the technique with disadvantage.

Homebrew / Items

Tubes of Trickery

Tubes of Trickery

Wondrous item, uncommon

Description

This drab pair of empty ceramic cylinders are magically linked. Each vessel is 3 inches in diameter and one foot tall. Opening one of the vessel's lids and placing an item inside will magically teleport it to the second tube, making a quiet whoosh sound when it does. A very quiet thud can be heard when receiving an item. A tube cannot hold more than 2 pounds of materials at any time, and both lids must be closed for the items to be teleported. Items can only be sent if the two tubes are on the same plane of existence. A creature cannot be sent through the tubes. Only one tube must be empty, or else nothing occurs. The tubes must be within a 30 mile radius of one another.

You can only use this property once per day, which refreshes at dawn.

Tuneful Earcuffs

Tuneful Earcuffs

Wondrous Item, rare

Requires proficiency with at least one instrument to use

Description

Taking inspiration from an Earring of Message and a pair of Sending Stones, these metallic earcuffs are enchanted with evocation magic to recreate sounds or melodies from memory. This item has charges equal to your proficiency bonus that reset on a long rest: with an action, you can expend one charge to cause song familiar to you to play at a volume that is only audible to you. The song plays until completion in which the cuffs deactivate, requiring another charge to repeat the song or play a new one. You have disadvantage on perception checks related to hearing while this item is activated.

Homebrew / Items

Unfettered

Unfettered

Description:

Wearing heavy armors tends to take immense physical strain, and as such usually restricts the movements of the wearer. Bulwarks who call themselves Unfettered work tirelessly to be just as, if not more efficient with their movements while donning these heavy suits.

Features:

3rd Level - Heightened Agility

3rd Level - Armored Movement

7th Level - Iron Fist

13th Level - Quaking Vault

18th Level - Weightless Steel

3rd Level - Heightened Agility

At 3rd level when you select this specialization, you learn to move with better flow while wearing heavy armor. It weighs half as much to you, and it does not apply disadvantage on your dexterity (stealth) checks.

3rd Level - Armored Movement

Additionally at 3rd level, you learn to move yourself with considerable speed for being weighed down. Your walking speed increases by 10 feet, and increases by another 10 feet at 18th level.

7th Level - Iron Fist

At 7th level, your movements are swift and fluid enough to carry the full force of your armor with them. When you make an unarmed attack while wearing heavy armor, you can choose to treat it as being a weapon with the heavy property, and you can roll a d8 in place of the normal damage of your unarmed attacks.

13th Level - Quaking Vault

Starting at 13th level, your poise and agility work in conjunction to make landing less deadly to you, and more so to those around you. You become resistant to falling damage while wearing heavy armor, and landing no longer knocks you prone. When you land while wearing heavy armor, creatures within 15 feet of you take 2d10 bludgeoning damage, and must succeed on a strength saving throw (DC 8 + your strength modifier + your proficiency bonus) or be knocked prone. A creature can only be affected by this ability once per turn.

18th Level - Weightless Steel

At 18th level, heavy armor ceases to be a burden for you in any meaningful way. Heavy armor weighs nothing to you while you are wearing it, and you may treat it as if it were medium armor for the purposes of adding your dexterity modifier to your armor class.

Vial Ring

Description

This ring is made of magic glass (That cannot be broken in ring-form) and has a cork stopper at its top like a set gemstone. You can unstopper the ring (no action required) to magically transform it into a small glass vial. The vial holds up to 1 ounce of liquid. An infected creature is poisoned and takes an additional 2d8 poison damage at the start of each of their turns. At the end of each of each infected creature’s turns until the spell ends, they can make another Constitution saving throw. On a success, the spell ends for that creature.

Windswept Kite

Windswept Kite

Wondrous item, uncommon

Description

This silk kite (colors, shape, etc. are customizable) is 5 feet across and is attached to a 60-foot string. It weighs 1 pound, can carry up to one pound in weight, and can be folded into a 6-inch square. While holding the kite, you can use a bonus action to toss it aloft and speak its command word. When you do, you also choose how much string to let out, between 10 to 60 feet. The kite then expands to its full size (if it was folded) and creates a cylinder of moderate wind of 10 miles per hour, which allows it to continue flying. The cylinder's height and diameter is the same as the amount of let-out string, up to 60 feet. The kite and top of the cylinder remain centered above your location. You can use another bonus action to speak the flying kite's command word to end the effect and cause it to fall softly back into your hand. You can change the wind's direction at the start of each of your turns for the duration.

You can use the kite to create this wind for up to 1 hour, all at once or in several shorter intervals, each one using a minimum of 1 minute from the duration. The effect ends early if you are no longer holding the string, at which point it flies up to 1d10 times 10 feet in a random direction before landing on the ground. Dealing 5 slashing damage to the string (AC 15) severs the string, causing the kite to fly away as if you let go of the string. The severed string can later be reattached by holding its ends together for 1 minute.

Dog and Hound

Dog and Hound

Fight Side by Side with a Brawler’s Best Friend

Level 3: Brawler’s Best Friend

You summon and form a bond with a wild or stray dog, which draws strength from your bottomless well of resilience using the Hound stat block.

  • The Hound in Combat: In combat, the hound acts during your turn. It can move and use its Reaction on its own, but the only action it takes is the Dodge action unless you take a Bonus Action to command it to take an action in its stat block or some other action. You can also sacrifice one of your attacks when you take the Attack action to command the hound to take the Bite action. If you have the Incapacitated condition, the hound acts on its own and isn’t limited to the Dodge action.
  • Restoring or Replacing the Hound: If the hound died within the last hour, you can take a Magic action to touch it and expend 2 Moxie Points. The hound returns to life after 1 minute with all its Hit Points restored. Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can summon and bond with a new dog, which appears in an unoccupied space within 5 feet of you.

The Hound Stat Block

Medium Beast, Neutral

  • Armor Class: 12 + your Constitution modifier + your Proficiency Bonus
  • Hit Points: 20 + 10 times your Pugilist Level. (Additionally, the Hound gains 1 Hit Die d8for every point of your Prestige Level.
  • Speed: 40 ft.
  • Resistances: The Hound shares your Iron Chin feature, gaining the same damage resistances you possess.
STR DEX CON INT WIS CHA
18 (+4) 14 (+2) 18 (+4) 3 (-4) 12 (+1) 13 (+1)
  • Saving Throws: STR + (4 + PB), DEX +(2 + PB), CON +(4 + PB).
  • Senses: Darkvision 60 ft.; Passive Perception 11.
  • Traits:
    • Pack Bond: Add your Proficiency Bonus to any ability check the beast makes.
  • Actions:
    • Bite: Melee Attack Roll: Bonus equals your Constitution modifier plus your PB, reach 5 ft. Hit: $2 \times (\text{your Fisticuffs Die}) + \text{your Constitution modifier}$ Piercing or Force damage. If the target is a creature Large or smaller, it must succeed on a Strength saving throw (DC equals your Pugilist Save DC) or suffer one of the following: the target is Grappled, Prone, or pushed 10 feet away.

Level 3: Mutt With Moxie

You share everything with your faithful hound. When you use abilities granted by your Moxie feature, your hound gains a benefit as well:

  • Brace Up: When you gain Temporary Hit Points from your Brace Up ability, your hound gains the same number of Temporary Hit Points.
  • One-Two Punch: When you use your One-Two Punch ability, your hound can make one or both attacks instead of you.
  • Stick and Move: When you use your Stick and Move ability, your hound can take your choice of the Dash, Disengage, or Help action.

Level 6: Coordinated Attack

When you make an attack against a creature and your hound is within 5 feet of it, your hound can take a Reaction to give your attack Advantage. On a hit, you deal an extra 4d8 damage. Additionally, the hound's Bite and this extra damage can deal your choice of Force damage or its normal damage type.

Level 11: Hound’s Best Friend

When a creature deals damage to your hound with an attack, you can take a Reaction to move up to your full Speed toward that creature and make one melee attack with a Pugilist weapon or an Unarmed Strike against it. If this attack hits, the target has Disadvantage on all attack rolls against the hound until the end of your next turn.

Level 17: Off The Chain

When your hound takes damage that causes it to become Bloodied or takes damage while it is Bloodied, you can use your Reaction to let your hound off the chain. For the next minute, the hound gains the following benefits:

  • It gains Temporary Hit Points equal to five times your Prestige Level.
  • Its Speed increases by 20 feet.
  • You can command it to use its Bite action as a Free Action on your turn (no Bonus Action or Attack sacrifice required).
  • Its Bite deals an additional 2d10 Force damage.

Once you use this feature, you can’t use it again until you finish a Long Rest. Because Moxie does not recover on a Short Rest, you may restore your use of this feature by expending 8 Moxie Points (no action required).

Artillerist

Artillerist

Description

Heavy weapon and Burst specialist. Battlefield suppression role. Features:

  • Level 3 – Heavy Weapons Training
  • Level 7 – Suppressive Burst
  • Level 13 – Battle Conditioning
  • Level 17 – Battlefield Devastator

Level 3 – Heavy Weapons Training

You gain proficiency in Heavy Armor.

You add half your ability modifier to Volatile weapon damage. You cannot add this bonus to weapons with the Automatic Property.

Level 7 – Suppressive Burst

When you use a weapon’s Burst property, any creature hit must succeed on a Con save using your Called Shot DC or have the frightened condition until the end of your next turn.

Level 13 – Battle Conditioning

As a bonus action you may spend up to your entire pool of Grit, you gain temporary HP equal to 5 times the amount of Grit you spent. This temporary HP lasts until you short rest.

Level 17 – Battlefield Devastator

You can enter this state as a bonus action. You can spend 3 Grit to restore your use of this ability.

Once per long rest, for 1 minute:

You gain resistance to piercing, bludgeoning, and slashing damage.

Your firearm weapons gain a bonus to hit equal to half your Strength modifier.

Called Shots now cost one less to use down to a minimum of 0.

Chakram

Chakram

Description

Proficiency with a chakram allows you to add your proficiency bonus to the attack roll for any attack you make with it. On a missed throw, a chakram returns to the thrower's hand.

Finesse: When making an attack with a finesse weapon, you use your choice of your Strength or Dexterity modifier for the attack and damage rolls. You must use the same modifier for both rolls.

Light: A light weapon is small and easy to handle, making it ideal for use when fighting with two weapons.

Thrown: If a weapon has the thrown property, you can throw the weapon to make a ranged attack. If the weapon is a melee weapon, you use the same ability modifier for that attack roll and damage roll that you would use for a melee attack with the weapon. For example, if you throw a handaxe, you use your Strength, but if you throw a dagger, you can use either your Strength or your Dexterity, since the dagger has the finesse property.

Circle of Beauty

Circle of Beauty

Circle of Beauty

Druids of the Circle of Beauty vow to protect all that brings beauty in nature. From the patterns of symmetry designed to attract mates, to visual marks designed to confuse camouflage observers, these are all sights that should be admired and emulated. They marvel at how nature seamlessly blends together both form and function in a way man-made objects never could.

Features:

  • 2nd Level - Circle Spells
  • 2nd Level - Natural Form
  • 6th Level - Blessing of Symmetry
  • 10th Level - Beautiful Plummage
  • 14th Level - Radiant Appearance

2nd Level - Circle Spells

Your eye for all things visually harmonious grants you access to some spells when you reach certain levels in this class, as shown on the Circle of Beauty Spells table.

Once you gain access to one of these spells, you always have it prepared, and it doesn't count against the number of spells you can prepare each day. If you gain access to a spell that doesn't appear on the druid spell list, the spell is nonetheless a druid spell for you.

Druid Level Spell
2nd disguise self, feather fall
3rd healing spirit, lesser restoration
5th daylight, hypnotic pattern
7th charm monster, compulsion
9th creation, dawn

2nd Level - Natural Form

As a bonus action, you can expend one use of your Wild Shape feature to draw upon nature's splendour, rather than assuming a Beast form.

While in your natural form and wearing no armour, your Armour Class equals 10 + your Dexterity modifier + your Wisdom modifier. You can use a shield and still gain this benefit. The form lasts for 10 minutes. It ends early if you dismiss it (no action required), if you die, or you use this feature again.

Whenever you assume your natural form, choose the manner of natural appearance your body transforms into; your choice gives you certain benefits while in the form.

Attractive. When you enter this form, and as a bonus action on your subsequent turns while in this form, you can choose a creature you can see within 30 feet of you. That creature must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC or be charmed by you until the start of your next turn. The target automatically succeeds on its saving throw if it can't see you. It stops being charmed by you if it is attacked or damaged, or if another creature shakes it awake as a bonus action.

Camouflage. You can take the Hide action as a bonus action. You can attempt to hide even when you are only lightly obscured by foliage, heavy rain, falling snow, mist, and other natural phenomena.

Verdant. When you enter this form, and as a bonus action on your subsequent turns, you can choose one creature you can see within 30 feet of you (including yourself). That creature gains your Wisdom modifier temporary hit points, which lasts until the start of your next turn.

6th Level - Blessing of Symmetry

6th-level Circle of Beauty feature

You strive to emulate the symmetry that occurs in the natural world. When you or a willing creature you can see within 60 feet of you casts a spell with a casting time of 1 action and which deals damage to at least one target, the caster can forgo rolling damage dice and take the average damage. If the spell has an ongoing effect that can deal damage after it is cast, this feature only applies to the initial instance of damage.

You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

10th Level - Beautiful Plummage

The transformation into your natural form is now even more stunning. Your forms gain extra benefits as detailed below:

Attractive. When you charm a creature, you can command it as part of the same bonus action to use its reaction to move up to its speed and make one weapon attack against a target you can see. After the creature completes this command, it is no longer charmed by you.

Camouflage. When you use the Hide action and are also obscured by natural foliage or phenomena, you become invisible until you move away from the natural foliage, or until you make an attack or cast a spell.

Verdant. The you roll is now a when you give temporary hit points. While a creature has these temporary hit points, it has a bonus to AC and advantage on Constitution saving throws.

Moreover, at the start of each of your turns while in your Natural Form, you can change the appearance of your form. If you do, any effects from your previous form immediately end.

14th Level - Radiant Appearance

Your body's aesthetically pleasing patterns and colours make others hesitate to harm you. When a creature makes an attack roll against you while in your Natural Form, you can use your reaction and force it to make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, the creature can't attack you with an attack or harmful spell until the end of its current turn, and must choose a new target or lose the attack or spell (this doesn't protect you from area effects, such as the explosion of15 a fireball).

You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

Circle of the Verdant Stalker

Circle of the Verdant Stalker

Circle of the Verdant Stalker

Druids of the Circle of the Verdant Stalker embody the lethal stillness and precision of Chult’s jungles. They move like serpents through the undergrowth, striking with poison and vanishing into foliage.

Features:

  • 3rd Level - Circle Spells
  • 3rd Level - Venomous Marksman
  • 6th Level - Aspect of the Striking Viper
  • 10th Level - Primal Toxin Mastery
  • 14th Level - Deathbloom Aspect

3rd Level - Circle Spells

Your eye for all things visually harmonious grants you access to some spells when you reach certain levels in this class, as shown on the Circle of Beauty Spells table.

Once you gain access to one of these spells, you always have it prepared, and it doesn't count against the number of spells you can prepare each day. If you gain access to a spell that doesn't appear on the druid spell list, the spell is nonetheless a druid spell for you.

Druid Level Spell
3rd Ensnaring Strike, Poison Spray
5th Plant Growth, Spike Growth
7th Grasping Vine, Stoneskin
9th Tree Stride, Cloudkill (reflavored as a deadly plant toxin cloud)

3rd Level - Venomous Marksman

Your training centers on the precision and toxins of Chult’s hidden hunters.

  • Blowgun Proficiency. You gain proficiency with the blowgun. You can use your Wisdom modifier instead of Dexterity for blowgun attack and damage rolls.

  • Toxin-Enhanced Blowgun. Your blowgun darts deal greater piercing damage as you grow in mastery.

Druid Level Blowgun Damage Die
3rd 1d6
10th 1d8
14th 1d10
  • Poisoner’s Tools. You gain proficiency with the Poisoner’s Kit.
  • Tough to Toxin. You have resistance to poison damage and advantage on saving throws against being poisoned.
  • Jungle Stride. You ignore nonmagical plant-based difficult terrain.

6th Level - Aspect of the Striking Viper

You channel primal ferocity into a deadly, focused trance.

Activation. As a bonus action, expend one use of your Wild Shape to enter this Aspect for 1 minute. You can’t activate it again until you finish a short or long rest.

While in this Aspect:

  • Your blowgun attacks deal an extra 1d8 poison damage.
  • When you take the attack action to attack with your blowgun, hit or miss, you can make another attack with the blowgun.
  • If your first blowgun attack each turn hits, the target must make a Constitution saving throw (DC = your spell save DC) or be Poisoned until the end of its next turn.
  • A creature that fails this saving throw also takes an additional 1d8 poison damage.

10th Level - Primal Toxin Mastery

Your venoms pierce the resilience of even the hardiest foes.

  • Toxic Bypass. Your blowgun attacks and druid spells that deal poison damage treat immunity to poison damage as resistance instead.

  • Debilitating Barrage. When you hit a creature that is Poisoned, you can use your reaction to force it to make a Constitution saving throw (DC = your spell save DC). On a failed save, it is Blinded until the end of its next turn. You can use this reaction a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, regaining all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

14th Level - Deathbloom Aspect

Your mastery of venom and motion refines your Aspect of the Striking Viper into the Deathbloom Aspect.

When you activate your Aspect of the Striking Viper, it gains the following additional benefits:

  • Deadly Venoms. Your extra poison damage increases to 1d10, and creatures make their Constitution saving throws against your poison with disadvantage.
  • Viper’s Retreat. Immediately after you hit a creature with a blowgun attack, you can move up to half your speed without provoking opportunity attacks from that creature.
  • Predator’s Cunning. While the Aspect is active, you can take the Hide or Disengage action as a bonus action. You can also attempt to Hide even when you are only partially obscured by natural terrain, foliage, or dim light.
  • Toxic Perfection. You are immune to poison damage and the poisoned condition.

College of the Moon (UA)

College of the Moon (UA)

College of the Moon (UA)

Inspire Allies with Primal Tales

The College of the Moon traces its origins to the ancient druidic circles of the Moonshae Isles, who entrusted the first Bards of this tradition with chronicling the stories of the islands and their people. Bards of this college draw from the isles’ Fey magic and the primal power of the moonwells to bolster their allies, protect the natural world, and inspire their bardic works. Such works tend to be based on well-known Moonshae myths such as the whimsy of fairy pranksters, the viciousness of the Beast, and the mysteries of the moonwells.

Features:

  • 3rd Level - Moonshae Folktales
  • 3rd Level - Primal Lorist
  • 6th Level - Blessing of the Moonwells
  • 14th Level - Bolstered Folktales

3rd Level - Moonshae Folktales

As a Magic action, you can invoke the power of a folktale, imbuing yourself with primal magic until you use this feature again. When you use this feature, choose which of the following folktales you invoke; your choice gives you benefits while this magic is active.

  • Tale of Life. You invoke a tale of vitality and thriving earth. When you restore Hit Points to a creature with a spell, you can expend a Bardic Inspiration die and increase the amount of Hit Points restored by a number equal to a roll of the Bardic Inspiration die. You can do this only once per turn.
  • Tale of Gloam. You invoke a tale of mystery and secrets. When you use a Bonus Action to give a creature a Bardic Inspiration die, you can take the Disengage or Hide action as part of that Bonus Action.
  • Tale of Mirth. You invoke a tale of merriment and fey guile. When an enemy you can see within 60 feet of yourself succeeds on a saving throw, you can take a Reaction to expend a Bardic Inspiration die. The creature then must roll the Bardic Inspiration die and subtract the number rolled from the save’s total, possibly causing the save to fail.

3rd Level - Primal Lorist

You learn Druidic and one cantrip from the Druid spell list. It counts as a Bard spell for you but doesn’t count against the number of cantrips you know.

Additionally, choose one of the following skills: Animal Handling, Insight, Medicine, Nature, Perception, or Survival. You have proficiency in that skill.

6th Level - Blessing of the Moonwells

You always have the Moonbeam spell prepared.

As a Bonus Action, you can cast Moonbeam without expending a spell slot. When you cast it using this feature, you glow faintly while you maintain Concentration on the spell. While glowing, you shed Dim Light out to 5 feet, and whenever a creature fails its saving throw against the effects of this Moonbeam, another creature of your choice that you can see within 60 feet of you regains 2d4 Hit Points.

Once you use this feature, you can’t use it again until you finish a Long Rest. You can also restore your use of it by expending a level 3+ spell slot (no action required).

14th Level - Bolstered Folktales

The power of your Moonshae Folktales improves. When you use your Tale of Life or Tale of Mirth, you can roll 1d6 and use the number rolled in place of expending a Bardic Inspiration die, and when you use your Tale of Gloam, you can also teleport up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space you can see as part of that Bonus Action

Gladiator (UA)

Gladiator (UA)

Gladiator (UA)

Master Brutality and Blood Sport

Gladiators are just as much performers as they are warriors. Whether brawling in underground fighting rings or fighting for survival in bloodstained arenas, a Gladiator combines martial skill with theatrics to awe and intimidate their audiences.

Features:

  • 3rd Level - Brutality
  • 3rd Level - Combat Theatrics
  • 7th Level - Flourish Parry
  • 10th Level - Bolder Brutalities
  • 15th Level - Brutal Resurgence
  • 18th Level - Mutilate

3rd Level - Brutality

Shaped by the intensity of the arena, you’ve learned to execute brutal martial moves. Once per turn, when you hit a creature with an attack roll using a Melee weapon, you can add one of the following Brutality effects of your choice. You can do this a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Short or Long Rest.

Bleed. You can activate the Sap mastery property in addition to a different mastery property you’re using with that weapon, and the target takes extra damage equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of 1 damage). The extra damage’s type is the same type as the weapon’s type.

Bluff. You can activate the Vex mastery property in addition to a different mastery property you’re using with that weapon, and you have Advantage on the next saving throw you make before the end of your next turn.

Stumble. You can activate the Topple mastery property in addition to a different mastery property you’re using with that weapon, and on its next turn, the target can take only an action or a Bonus Action, not both.

3rd Level - Combat Theatrics

You’ve honed your combat skills to entertain, devastating opponents and dazzling onlookers. You gain the following benefits.

Athletic Flair. Whenever you make a Dexterity (Acrobatics) or Strength (Athletics) check, you gain a bonus to the check equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of +1).

Bonus Proficiency. You gain proficiency in one of these skills of your choice: Acrobatics, Athletics, Deception, Intimidation, or Performance.

7th Level - Flourish Parry

You’ve learned to stylishly counter blows from your opponents. When an enemy hits you with a melee attack roll, you can take a Reaction to add your Charisma modifier (minimum of +1) to your AC against the attack, potentially causing the attack to miss.

Flourish Counter. If this Reaction causes the attack to miss, you can retaliate with a powerful counterattack as part of the same Reaction. Make an attack roll with a Melee weapon against the triggering creature. If this attack hits, you can use one of your Brutality effects on the target without expending a use of that feature. Once this counterattack hits, you can’t use this feature to make another counterattack until you finish a Long Rest. You can also restore your use of this counterattack by expending a use of Second Wind (no action required).

10th Level - Bolder Brutalities

Your brutal martial prowess has improved. The following effects are added to your Brutality options.

Rive. You can activate the Cleave mastery property in addition to a different mastery property you’re using with that weapon, and you can add your ability modifier to the damage of the additional attack made as part of that property’s activation.

Rush. You can activate the Push mastery property in addition to a different mastery property you’re using with that weapon, and you can immediately move up to your Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks.

Stagger. You can activate the Slow mastery property in addition to a different mastery property you’re using with that weapon, and the target has Disadvantage on the next saving throw it makes before the end of your next turn.

15th Level - Brutal Resurgence

Whenever you use your Second Wind to regain Hit Points, you regain an expended use of Brutality. You also regain an expended use of Brutality whenever you use your Action Surge.

18th Level - Mutilate

When you hit a Bloodied creature with an attack roll, you can attempt to critically injure it. The target makes a Constitution saving throw (DC 8 plus your Charisma modifier and Proficiency Bonus). On a failed save, the target suffers the following effects:

Maimed. If the target takes the Attack action, it can make only one attack.

Sluggish. The target’s Speed is halved, and it has a −2 penalty to its Armor Class.

These effects last until the target regains Hit Points. Once a target fails its saving throw against this feature, you can’t use it again on that creature until you finish a Long Rest.

Silent Elimination, You are taught to find and exploit fatal flaws with precision.

    • 2d6 at C-Rank (5th level),
    • 3d6 at B-Rank (8th level),
    • 4d6 at A-Rank (13th level), and

Level 7 - Tactical Infiltration

Skirmisher's Flow: You can take the Dash or Disengage action as a Bonus Action on your turn.
