  • Vanishing Strike: When you deal Silent Elimination damage to a creature, you can immediately attempt to Hide as part of that attack (no action required), provided you have any cover or obscurement (such as your Hidden Mist).
  • Silent Blow: When you hit a creature you are hidden from, that creature cannot take Reactions until the start of its next turn.

Level 15 - Lethal Toxins

You master the application of chakra-infused poisons to ensure your blows are debilitating and fatal.

Preparation: As a Bonus Action, you can spend 3 Chakra to coat one weapon with a neurotoxin for 1 minute. While the coating lasts, once per turn when you hit a creature with that weapon, the creature takes an extra 3d6 Poison damage and must make a Constitution saving throw (vs. Jutsu DC) or be Poisoned for 1 minute.

Toxic Expertise: Your Silent Elimination damage and your toxin damage from this Nindo ignore Resistance to Poison damage.

Level 20 - Apex Neurotoxin

You achieve ultimate mastery over toxins, delivering a single, decisive blow that paralyzes the nervous system, securing the kill.

Activation: When you hit a creature with a melee attack, you can spend 5 Chakra to apply the Apex Neurotoxin (no action required). The creature takes an extra 8d8 Poison damage and must succeed on a Constitution saving throw (vs. Jutsu DC) or be Paralysed for up to 1 minute. The target can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. This damage ignores Resistance to Poison damage and treats Immunity to Poison damage as Resistance.

Path of the Brawler

Path of the Brawler

A Subclass of Barbarian that focus on unarmed fighting

Features:

  • 3rd Level - Unarmed Combatant
  • 3rd Level - Brawler's Prowess
  • 6th Level - Reactive Fighting
  • 6th Level - Packin' Heat
  • 10th Level - Fearsome Critical

3rd Level - Unarmed Combatant

At level 3, your strength and general martial prowess increase the damage that you do with your bare fists. When you make an unarmed strike, your damage becomes 1d4 + your STR modifier. The damage dice increase with each level in this subclass, to become 1d6 at level 6, 1d8 at level 10 and finally 1d10 at level 14.

3rd Level - Brawler's Prowess

At level 3, While Raging, you gain new options to use as bonus actions, as long as you are not wielding any weapons or a shield.

  • Block: While raging, you can use your bonus action to raise your arms in a defensive stance. This gives you an AC boost of +2 until the start of your next turn. At level 10, this AC boost becomes +3
  • Jab: While raging, you can use your bonus action to make an unarmed strike against a target.

6th Level - Reactive Fighting

At level 6, while you are raging, when a creature attacks you and they are within 5 feet of you, you can make an unarmed strike against that creature as a reaction.

6th Level - Packin' Heat

At level 6, your unarmed strikes can even inflict damage on the toughest of foes, your unarmed strikes become magical for the purpose of overcoming non-magical resistance and immunity.

10th Level - Fearsome Critical

At level 10, when you score a Critical hit on a Target with your unarmed strike, you can apply brutal critical to your unarmed strike. Additionally when you score a critical hit on a target, they must save a Constitution saving throw against your save DC (8 + proficiency + strength bonus) or be frightened by you until the end of their next turn.

14th Level - Brawler's Focus

At level 14, while you are raging and you have only one creature within 20 feet of you, that creature has your undivided attention. You are in the "zone". You can make attacks against them with adv, and any wisdom saves they force you to make, are made with adv. While in the zone, if they try to leave your melee range, your Attack of Opportunity has the ability to stop them in their tracks, reducing their move speed to zero if they fail a strength save against your save DC (8+prof+strength bonus)

Path of Unlight

Path of Unlight

Path of Unlight

Unleash your inner light as blazing fury

Barbarians infused with the power of Unlight embrace uncontrollable magic in exchange for incredible physical prowess. The Unlight burning inside them illuminates the darkness while burning and blinding the barbarian's enemies.

Most barbarians on this path were first exposed to Unlight in the Underdark, sometimes referred to as the Underlight. The magic of Unlight is contagious and spreads in unpredictable ways. It infects people only briefly exposed to it and occasionally manifests in individuals who have never been to the Underdark.

Features:

  • Unlight Manifestation
  • 3rd Level - Radiant Rage
  • 6th Level - Unlight Revelation
  • 10th Level - Infectious Unlight
  • 10th Level - Harbinger of Unlight
  • 14th Level - Brilliant Rage

Unlight Manifestation

Barbarians on the Path of Unlight manifest the radiant energy of Unlight when they rage, but this energy can take many forms. You can roll on or choose a result from the Unlight Manifestation table to inspire the form your Radiant Rage takes.

1d6 Your Unlight Manifests As…
1 White light blazing from your eyes and mouth.
2 Complex arcane symbols of light etched onto your body.
3 A cyclone of bright light that whirls around you.
4 Cracks in your flesh that reveal burning light within.
5 A ghostly form made of light that hovers above you.
6 Pale fire that dances on the tip of your weapon.

3rd Level - Radiant Rage

The Unlight coursing through you fuels your Rage. While your Rage is active, you shed Bright Light in a 15-foot radius. Additionally, if a creature damages or hits you with an attack roll while within your area of Bright Light, the creature takes Radiant damage equal to twice your Rage Damage bonus.

6th Level - Unlight Revelation

You have proficiency in the Perception skill, if you lack it. You also gain Expertise in that skill.

While your rage is active, you have Blindsight with a range equal to that of the Bright Light provided by your Radiant Rage.

10th Level - Infectious Unlight

Damage you deal with Brutal Strike can be Radiant or the usual type (your choice). The following effect is now among your Brutal Strike options.

Radiant Infection. The target becomes infected with Unlight for 1 minute. While infected, it sheds Bright Light in a 10-foot radius and gains no benefit from being hidden or invisible. Additionally, at the start of each of its turns roll a 1d12; it takes that much in Radiant damage and also takes a penalty on the first attack roll and Constitution saving throw it makes before the start of your next turn equal to the amount rolled. The target can use an Action to purge the Infection from their system, ending the effect on a success.

10th Level - Harbinger of Unlight

You have Resistance to Radiant damage.

14th Level - Brilliant Rage

The aura of your Unlight is bolstered. While your Rage is active, you shed Bright Light in a 30-foot radius.

As a Bonus Action, you unleash your blinding radiance. When you do, each creature of your choice within 30 feet of you makes a Constitution saving throw (DC 8 plus your Strength modifier and Proficiency Bonus).

On a failed save, roll a number of d12's equal to your Rage Damage bonus. The target takes that much in Radiant damage and half as much radiant damage again at the start of their turn. Additionally they can see no further than 5ft in any direction until the end of their next turn. On a successful save they take half as much initial damage and no damage at the start of their turn, and suffer no effect to their vision.

You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Strength modifier, resetting on a Long Rest or if you expend a use of your Rage (no action required) to restore one use of it.

Piss and Vinegar

Level 3: Bad Attitude

Level 3: Salty Salute

As a Bonus Action, you can provoke a creature within 60 feet that can see or hear you. The target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw against your Pugilist Save DC.

  • On a Failure: The target takes Psychic damage equal to two rolls of your Fisticuffs die + your Constitution modifier.
  • Aggro Lock: Until the start of your next turn, the target has Disadvantage on any attack roll that doesn't include you as a target. If the target attempts to cast a spell that doesn't include you as a target, it must first succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or the spell fails and the action is wasted.

Level 6: Dirty Tricks

You have mastered the art of fighting unfair. You gain a Trick Pool equal to your Strength modifier (minimum of 1). You regain all uses of this pool on a Long Rest. You can spend a use of this pool (no action required) to apply one of the following Dirty Tricks when you hit with a Pugilist weapon or Unarmed Strike.

Once your pool is empty, you can continue to use these tricks by expending 2 Moxie Points per use.

  • Heelstomper: The creature must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or be Restrained (not just 0 speed) until the end of your next turn as you pin them down or crush a foot.
  • Low Blow: The creature must succeed on a Strength saving throw or be Stunned until the start of your next turn.
  • Pocket Sand: As a Bonus Action, you toss detritus. A creature within 15 feet must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or be Blinded for 1 minute. The creature can repeat the save at the end of its turns.

Level 11: Mean Old Cuss

Your insults are so vile they physically manifest as psychic pressure. As a Bonus Action, you can target a number of creatures up to your Prestige Level within 30 feet.

  • Effect: Each target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or take Psychic damage equal to three rolls of your Fisticuffs die + your CON modifier and be Frightened of you until the start of your next turn. While Frightened this way, a creature's speed is 0.
  • Usage: You can use this once per Long Rest for free, or expend 4 Moxie Points to use it again.

Level 17: Dirtier Tricks

Your "Dirty Tricks" now bypass certain resistances. When you use a Dirty Trick, the target has Disadvantage on the saving throw. Furthermore, you gain these elite maneuvers:

  • Rabbit Punch: When you hit, you strike a nerve cluster. The target must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or have its Damage Resistances and Immunities suppressed for 1 minute. The creature can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns.
  • Sucker Punch: When you hit a creature that has Disadvantage on the attack roll or is affected by one of your Dirty Tricks, you can spend 3 Moxie to turn the hit into a Devastating Critical. Roll the damage dice four times. The target must then succeed on a Strength saving throw or be knocked back 30 feet and fall Prone.

Sorrow Knight

Sorrow Knight

Sorrow Knight

Sorrow knights suffuse their opponents with grief and misery from the gloomy plane called the Shadowfell. These fighters harness their past despair to forge a connection with others and protect themselves. A sorrow knight’s intense loss - whether the loss of love, faith, or something equally profound - is the weapon they wield against their foes and their motivator to ensure that no one experiences that same pain.

Features:

  • Embracing the Gloom
  • 3rd Level - Despairing Strikes
  • 3rd Level - Solemn Gaze
  • 7th Level - Dreaded Appearance
  • 10th Level - Unsettled Strikes
  • 15th Level - Grim Constitution
  • 18th Level - Grieving Mantle

Embracing the Gloom

Sorrow knights deploy the gloom and sadness inherent to the Shadowfell, whether or not they have ever been to that grim place.

Roll on or choose a result from the Shadowfell Connection table to inspire the event that forged your connection to the Shadowfell.

Shadowfell Connection

1d6 The Despair of the Shadowfell Claimed You After…
1 You arrived too late to save your home from monsters that destroyed it.
2 You realized a good-aligned god never intends to answer your prayers.
3 You were not strong enough to save the love of your life from their untimely death.
4 A shadow crossing opened beneath your bed as a child.
5 You understood your parents were never returning to save you.
6 You fell into an open grave.

3rd Level - Despairing Strikes

Each sorrow knight bears an emotional wound like a deep scar, through which they channel despair against their enemies. This misery is fueled by special dice called Despairing Strike Dice.

The Despairing Strike Dice table shows the die size and number of these dice you have when you reach certain Fighter levels. A Despairing Strike Die is expended when you use it. You regain all expended Despairing Strike Dice when you finish a Short or Long Rest.

Despairing Strike Dice

Fighter Level Dice Size Number
3 D8 3
10 D10 4
15 D12 5

When you hit a creature with an attack roll using a weapon, you can expend a Despairing Strike Die and roll that die. You deal additional Psychic damage equal to the roll and can also add one of the following effects. You can’t expend more than one die per attack.

If a Despairing Strike effect requires a saving throw, the DC equals 8 plus your Wisdom modifier and Proficiency Bonus.

Abandoned. The target must succeed on an Intelligence saving throw or have the Deafened condition until the end of your next turn. While Deafened, the target regards all creatures it can see as enemies until the end of your next turn.

Dread. The target has Disadvantage on the next saving throw it makes before the start of your next turn.

3rd Level - Solemn Gaze

You can see through the darkness around you and recognize the darkness in others. You gain the following benefits.

Darkvision. You gain Darkvision with a range of 60 feet. If you already have Darkvision, its range increases by 60 feet.

Empathetic Inquiry. As a Magic action, you can attempt to search the mind of a creature you can see within 30 feet. The target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw (DC equals 8 plus your Wisdom modifier and Proficiency Bonus) or you learn an emotion that looms large in its mind, such as a worry, love, or hate. If the target can see you, it knows you have read its emotions. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of once). You regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

7th Level - Dreaded Appearance

When you use Tactical Shift, you can teleport to an unoccupied space you can see within 30 feet of yourself instead of moving.

Immediately after you reappear, you can briefly take on the appearance of creatures’ fears, visible only to those creatures. Each creature of your choice within a 10-foot Emanation originating from you makes a Wisdom saving throw (DC equals 8 plus your Wisdom modifier and your Proficiency Bonus). On a failed save, a target takes Psychic damage equal to a roll of your Despairing Strike die and has the Frightened condition until the end of your next turn. On a successful save, it takes half damage only.

Once you take on this appearance, you can’t do so again until you finish a Short or Long Rest.

10th Level - Unsettled Strikes

You further channel the pathos of the Shadowfell through your fighting abilities. The following effects are now among your Despairing Strike options.

Apathetic. The target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or have the Incapacitated condition until the start of your next turn. While Incapacitated in this way, the target can give only one-word responses when spoken to.

Lost. The target makes a Charisma saving throw. On a failed save, the target has the Blinded condition, and its Speed is reduced to 0 until the end of its next turn. On a successful save, the target’s Speed is halved until the end of its next turn.

Weary. The target must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or gain 1 Exhaustion level. This effect can’t increase the target’s Exhaustion level above 2. Exhaustion levels gained from this effect are removed at the end of your next turn.

15th Level - Grim Constitution

You have Resistance to Necrotic and Psychic damage.

In addition, when you are subjected to an effect that reduces your Hit Point maximum, you can make a DC 15 Constitution saving throw. If you succeed, your Hit Point maximum isn’t decreased. Each time you make this Constitution saving throw after the first, the DC increases by 5. When you finish a Short or Long Rest, the DC resets to 15.

18th Level - Grieving Mantle

When you use your Action Surge, you attune yourself to the Shadowfell for 1 minute or until you have the Incapacitated condition. For the duration, you gain the following benefits.

Shade Form. When you are hit by an attack roll, you can take a Reaction to become insubstantial for a moment and reduce the attack’s total damage against you by three rolls of your despairing strike die plus half your fighter level

Unwavering Resolve. You have Immunity to the Charmed and Frightened conditions. If you’re Charmed or Frightened when you activate your Grieving Mantle, the condition ends on you.

Squared Circle

Squared Circle

Drop and Lock Your Foes

Level 3: Groundwork

You have mastered the fundamentals of wrestling and submission. You gain the following benefits:

  • Compression Lock: Your grip is bone-crushing. When you start your turn with one or more creatures Grappled by you, you can deal Bludgeoning damage to each of those creatures (no action required). The damage equals one roll of your Fisticuffs Die + your Strength modifier.
  • Inescapable: When a creature makes a saving throw or ability check to escape your Grapple or resist your Shove, you can expend 1 Moxie Point to give that roll Disadvantage.
  • Stop and Drop: Your strikes lead naturally into takedowns. When you hit a creature with an Unarmed Strike, even if you use a mastery property, you can use the shove option against that target as part of the same attack, if instead you do the grapple option from heavy hitter you make the check with advantage.

Level 3: Muscle Mass

You have conditioned your body for maximum leverage. You gain proficiency in the Athletics skill. If you already have proficiency, you gain Expertise in it. Additionally, you can use your Strength modifier instead of Dexterity when determining your Armor class..

Level 6: Meat Shield

You know how to put an enemy between yourself and danger. While you have a creature Grappled, you gain Half Cover (+2 to AC and Dexterity saving throws) against attacks and effects made by creatures you aren't Grappling.

  • Redirect Strike: When a creature you aren't Grappling misses you with a melee or ranged attack roll, you can take a Reaction to force that creature to make a new attack roll against a creature you are currently Grappling. You can do this a number of times equal to your Strength modifier per Long Rest. You may expend 2 Moxie Points to use this feature again if you have no uses remaining.

Level 11: Heavyweight

Your technique allows you to manhandle even the largest foes.

  • Size Mastery: You count as two sizes larger for the purpose of Grappling or Shoving.
  • Relentless Drag: You no longer spend extra movement to move a creature Grappled by you, regardless of its size.
  • Iron Grip: Creatures have Disadvantage on any attack rolls they make against you while they are Grappled by you.

Level 17: Clean Finish

You have mastered the art of the "Lights Out" submission. When a creature ends its turn Grappled by you, you can take a Reaction to force it to make a Constitution saving throw against your Pugilist Save DC.

  • Effect: On a failure, the creature gains the Incapacitated condition until the end of its next turn.
  • The Finisher: If the creature is already Bloodied and fails this saving throw while already Incapacitated (such as from a previous turn's Clean Finish), its Hit Points are immediately reduced to 0 as you snap a vital joint or choke them into unconsciousness.

Once you successfully reduce a creature to 0 Hit Points using this feature, you cannot do so again until you finish a Long Rest. However, you may still use the Reaction to attempt to apply the Incapacitated condition.

Street Saint

Street Saint

Devote Yourself to Prayer and Pummeling

Level 3: Channel Divinity

You can channel divine energy directly from the Outer Planes to fuel magical effects. You start with two such effects: Fists of Faith and Grace of the Gods. When you use your Channel Divinity, you choose which effect to create.

Moxie Integration: Because Moxie is your primary long-term resource, you can use your Channel Divinity once per Long Rest for free. You can use it again by expending 3 Moxie Points (no action required).

  • Fists of Faith: As a Bonus Action, you imbue your fists with righteous fury. For the next minute, your Unarmed Strikes deal an extra 1d8 Radiant damage. This damage increases to 2d8 if the target is a Fiend or Undead.
  • Grace of the Gods: As a Bonus Action, you beseech the gods for grace. For the next minute, you have Resistance to Necrotic and Radiant damage, and whenever you make a saving throw, you can roll 1d6 and add the number rolled to the total.

Level 3: Lay On Hands

Your blessed touch can heal wounds. You have a pool of healing power that replenishes when you finish a Long Rest. With that pool, you can restore a total number of Hit Points equal to five times your Prestige Level.

  • Action: As a Bonus Action, you can touch a creature (including yourself) and restore a number of Hit Points up to the maximum amount remaining in your pool.
  • Purify: You can expend 5 Hit Points from the pool to remove the Blinded, Deafened, Paralyzed, or Poisoned condition from the creature.

Level 6: Ravaged But Resolute

When you use your Bloodied But Unbowed core class feature, you can choose to fully replenish your Lay On Hands healing pool. Once you use this feature, you cannot do so again until you finish a Long Rest.

Level 11: Aura of Resilience

When you use your Dig Deep core class feature, you radiate a protective, unseeable aura in a 20-foot Emanation originating from you for the next 10 minutes. The aura is inactive while you have the Incapacitated condition.

  • Effect: You and your allies within the aura gain Resistance to Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage (including magical sources).
  • Prestige Bonus: Allies in the aura also add your Constitution modifier to their AC.

Once you use this feature, you must finish a Long Rest before you can use it again, unless you expend 6 Moxie Points to use it again.

Level 17: Hallowed Hands

Your strikes carry the weight of divine judgment. Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with an Unarmed Strike or Pugilist weapon, you can expend points from your Lay On Hands pool to deal extra Radiant damage.

  • Damage: The damage equals the number of points expended.
  • Holy Smite: If the target is a Fiend or Undead, the damage is doubled.
  • Maximum: You can expend a maximum number of points per hit equal to your Prestige Level.

The Aegis

The Aegis

Psi Warrior. The mind as a wall others stand behind.

At PL 25 you choose a Doctrine; PL 29 and 33 branch within it; PL 37 gives your Doctrine's capstone.

Order Disciplines

Your Order grants these two disciplines at PL 21. They don't count against the number of disciplines you know, and no other Order can learn them.

Force Anchor

○ Focus. Difficult terrain doesn't slow you, and your Speed can't be reduced.

● Tether (3 psi) — Bonus Action. Anchor one creature within 30 ft. Until the end of your next turn it can't willingly move more than 15 ft from where it stands.

●● Ground the Line (8 psi) — Bonus Action. For 1 minute, allies within 15 ft of you can't be knocked Prone or moved against their will. No concentration.

Warding Field

○ Focus. Allies within 10 ft add your Psionic Ability modifier to Constitution saves made to maintain Concentration.

●●● Immutable Line (13 psi) — Magic action. Draw a 30-ft line you can see. For 1 minute, a creature can't cross it without succeeding on a Strength save, and one that fails takes 8d10 Force damage and its movement ends. No concentration.

PL 21: Guardian Field

+4 Psionic Energy Dice, and you regain your Proficiency Bonus in them on a Short Rest. Your Protective Field improves: its range becomes 60 ft, it reduces damage by the roll plus your Prestige Level rather than your Intelligence modifier, and using it on yourself doesn't expend the die.

PL 25: Choose a Doctrine (+2 dice)

Doctrine of the Shield

Protection. Allies within 10 ft of you have half cover, and your Guardian Field can be used at a range of 60 ft.

Doctrine of the Hammer

Force offense. Your Psionic Strike no longer expends a Psionic Energy Die, and you can use it twice on each of your turns rather than once.

Doctrine of the Anchor

Endurance. You can't be knocked Prone or moved against your will, and you have Advantage on saves against being Grappled, Restrained, or Paralyzed.

PL 29: Choose a Technique (+2 dice)

Shield

  • Interpose. When an ally within 30 ft is hit by an attack, you can use your Reaction to swap places with them; the attack hits you instead.
  • Wide Guard. When you use Guardian Field, it reduces damage to a second creature within 30 ft by the same amount.

Hammer

  • Repulsion. When you're hit by an attack, use your Reaction: the attacker makes a Strength save, taking 6d10 Force damage and being pushed 30 ft on a failure, half on a success.
  • Telekinetic Volley. As a Bonus Action, hurl debris at two creatures within 60 ft. Each makes a Dexterity save, taking 4d10 Force damage on a failure, half on a success.

Anchor

  • Gravity Well. Enemy movement within 15 ft of you costs double, and enemies that start their turn there take Force damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus.
  • Rooted Mind. You can't be teleported against your will, banished, or moved to another plane, and you have Resistance to Force damage.

PL 33: Choose a Mastery (+2 dice)

Shield

  • Kinetic Barrier. At the start of each combat, you and each ally within 30 ft gain Temporary Hit Points equal to your Prestige Level.
  • Bound Fate. Choose an ally on a Long Rest. While within 60 ft of you, they add your Psionic Ability modifier to all saving throws, and you can use Guardian Field on them without expending a die.

Hammer

  • Shattering Force. Your Force damage ignores Resistance and treats Immunity as Resistance. On a Critical Hit, the target is also knocked Prone.
  • Siege Mind. Once per turn when you deal Force damage, add one roll of your Manifestation Die, and the damage destroys any nonmagical object or structure it strikes.

Anchor

  • Fortress Self. If you haven't moved since the start of your turn, you have Resistance to all damage until the start of your next turn.
  • Unbreakable. When you're reduced to 0 Hit Points, you drop to 1 instead. Usable a number of times per Long Rest equal to your Proficiency Bonus.

PL 37: Doctrine Capstone (+2 dice)

Shield — Absolute Aegis. Once per Long Rest as a Bonus Action, for 1 minute: when an ally within 30 ft is targeted by an attack, you can use your Reaction to become the target instead, and you have Resistance to all damage taken this way.

Hammer — Fist of the Unseen. Once per Long Rest as a Bonus Action, for 1 minute you can make a telekinetic slam as a Bonus Action on each of your turns: one creature within 60 ft makes a Strength save, taking 8d10 Force damage and being knocked Prone on a failure, half on a success.

Anchor — Immovable Object. Once per Long Rest as a Bonus Action, for 1 minute you are immune to Critical Hits, have Resistance to all damage, and cannot be moved, Incapacitated, Stunned, or Paralyzed by any effect.

Control. You can control two creatures at once with Dominate Impulse, and dominated creatures act on your initiative.

PL 33: Choose a Mastery

Whisper

Dread

Alien

Alien — Apotheosis of the Outside. Once per Long Rest as a Bonus Action, for 1 minute your creature type becomes Aberration, you gain a flying speed of 60 ft and Resistance to all damage, and each enemy starting its turn within 30 ft makes an Intelligence save or takes 6d10 Psychic damage.

The Metallic Sovereign

The Metallic Sovereign

The Metallic Sovereign

Warlock Subclass (2024 Ruleset)

Your patron is a Metallic Dragon—a creature of ancient nobility, elemental might, and boundless memory. Unlike the terrifying tyrants that demand souls, your patron seeks a Steward: a mortal agent capable of walking where dragons cannot, mediating conflicts, and standing as a bulwark against the encroachment of Tiamat.

Possible Patrons of Faerûn:

* The King of Justice (Gold): You serve Protanther, the ancient King of Justice who dwells in the Galena Mountains. Your pact is one of strict law and punishing the wicked.

* The Silver Cloud (Silver): You serve Otaaryliakkarnos, the Silver Dragon who often walks Mulmaster in human guise. Your pact focuses on compassion and protecting the "small folk."

* The Coastal Warden (Bronze): You serve Nymmurh, the Bronze ancient of the Alambur Sea. Your pact is martial; you are a soldier against the aberrations of the deep.

* The Whispering Sand (Brass): You serve Ileuthra, the great information broker of the Anauroch Desert. Your pact compels you to gather intelligence and talk before you strike.

Features:

  • 3rd Level - Sovereign Spells
  • 3rd Level - Metallic Lineage
  • 3rd Level - Scales of the Steward
  • 3rd Level - Draconic Rebuke
  • 6th Level - Guardian’s Wing
  • 10th Level - Bastion of the Elements
  • 14th Level - Awe of the Wyrm

3rd Level - Sovereign Spells

The following spells are added to your Warlock spell list.

| Level | Spells |

| 3 | Aid, Chromatic Orb, Command, Dragon's Breath |

| 5 | Ashardalon’s Stride, Rime’s Binding Ice |

| 7 | Leomund’s Secret Chest, Raulothim’s Psychic Lance |

| 9 | Legend Lore, Summon Draconic Spirit |

3rd Level - Metallic Lineage

When you select this subclass, you must choose the type of dragon you serve. This choice determines the damage type for your subclass features.

| Dragon Type | Damage Type |

| Gold / Brass | Fire |

| Silver | Cold |

| Bronze | Lightning |

| Copper | Acid |

You learn to speak, read, and write Draconic. Additionally, you gain Proficiency in the History or Persuasion skill. Whenever you make a Charisma check to interact with dragons, you add double your Proficiency Bonus to the check.

3rd Level - Scales of the Steward

Your skin hardens with a shimmering, metallic sheen, acting as natural armor to prepare you for the front lines.

  • Natural Armor: While you are not wearing armor, your Armor Class equals 14 + your Dexterity modifier.
  • Shield Training: You gain proficiency with Shields. You can use a shield and still gain the benefit of your Natural Armor.

3rd Level - Draconic Rebuke

Your armor hums with the elemental fury of your patron, punishing those who dare to strike you. When a creature within 5 feet of you hits you with an attack, you can force that creature to make a Dexterity saving throw against your Spell Save DC. On a failed save, the creature takes damage equal to 1d8 + your Charisma modifier. The damage type is determined by your Metallic Lineage.

You can use this feature 3 times per long rest, regaining a single use when finished a short rest

The damage increases by 1d8 and the amount of uses increases by 1 when you reach Warlock levels 6 (2d8, 4 uses), 10 (3d8, 5 uses), and 14 (4d8, 6 uses).

6th Level - Guardian’s Wing

You can manifest the protective instinct of your patron. When a creature other than you, you can see within 10 feet of you is hit by an attack, you can use your Reaction to manifest a spectral, hardened dragon wing to shield them.

The damage of that attack is reduced by 1d10 + your Warlock Level.

10th Level - Bastion of the Elements

Your physical form has been tempered by the elemental fury of your patron, turning you into an immovable object.

  • Elemental Resilience: You gain Resistance to the damage type associated with your Metallic Lineage.
  • Unshakable: You are Immune to the Frightened condition. You have Advantage on saving throws and ability checks to avoid being knocked Prone or moved against your will.
  • Mental Sustenance: Whenever you succeed on a saving throw, you gain Temporary Hit Points equal to your Warlock Level.

14th Level - Awe of the Wyrm

As a Magic Action, you force any number of creatures within 30 feet that can see or hear you to make a Wisdom (Insight) check contested by your choice of Charisma (Intimidation) or Charisma (Performance).

If you win the contest, the target suffers a condition for 1 minute:

  • Intimidation: The target is Frightened of you.
  • Performance: The target is Charmed by you.

While affected, the target cannot take Reactions. The target can make a Wisdom saving throw against your Spell Save DC at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. A creature that wins the contest or succeeds on the saving throw is immune to this ability for 24 hours.

You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Charisma Modifier (minimum of once), regaining all uses on a Long Rest.

The Ursine Form

The Ursine Form

Mass over speed. Heavy shoulders, a hide that has stopped pretending to be skin, a frame that treats being hit as an administrative matter. Ursine in proportion, broadly speaking.

Baseline — Immovable Mass

  • Great Frame: You have advantage on Strength checks and Strength saving throws, and your carrying capacity doubles. While in Hybrid Shape, your Size increases to Large if you were Medium.
  • Thick Hide: You have resistance to Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage from nonmagical attacks, and you cannot be moved against your will or knocked Prone by any effect that doesn't first reduce you below half your Hit Point maximum.

Signature — Break the Blow (1 Primal Point)

  • Absorb: As a Reaction when you or a creature within 10 feet of you takes damage, reduce that damage by your Martial Arts die + your Wisdom modifier + half your Prestige Level.
  • Feed On It: You gain Temporary Hit Points equal to the amount reduced.

PL 25 — Ursine Branches

Choose one: The Wall, The Mountain, or The Maul.

The Wall

Opener — Sheltering Bulk: Allies within 10 feet of you gain half cover and have advantage on saving throws against being moved, knocked Prone, or Frightened. You are immune to the Frightened condition.

PL 30 — choose one:

  • Step In: When you use Break the Blow to protect an ally, you first move up to half your Speed to a space adjacent to them as part of the same Reaction, and the damage you reduce is dealt to you instead of them — after the reduction applies.
  • Bulwark Aura: The radius of Sheltering Bulk increases to 20 feet, and allies within it add your Wisdom modifier to their AC against Opportunity Attacks.

PL 35 — choose one:

  • Nothing Passes: Enemies treat every space within 10 feet of you as Difficult Terrain, and cannot end their movement in a space adjacent to an ally you can see.
  • Warding Growth: When you cast a spell of level 1 or higher, choose a number of allies within 30 feet up to your Wisdom modifier; each gains half cover and your Thick Hide resistance until the start of your next turn.

PL 40 — Capstone: The Line Holds: Break the Blow costs no Primal Point, has no limit on uses per round, and can protect any ally within 30 feet. While you are conscious, no ally within 10 feet can be reduced below 1 Hit Point by a single attack.

The Mountain

Opener — Deep Reserves: Whenever you would drop to 0 Hit Points, you can spend 3 Primal Points to instead drop to Hit Points equal to five times your Prestige Level, and end one condition affecting you. Once per Short or Long Rest.

PL 30 — choose one:

  • Unmoving: You are immune to being moved, knocked Prone, Grappled, or Restrained by any effect whatsoever.
  • Slow to Wound: Any single instance of damage is reduced by your Prestige Level before anything else applies.

PL 35 — choose one:

  • Rooted Casting: You have advantage on Constitution saving throws made to maintain Concentration, your Concentration cannot be broken by being moved or knocked Prone, and you automatically succeed on saves against Exhaustion.
  • Bottomless: Deep Reserves recharges on a Short Rest, and its cost is reduced to 1 Primal Point.

PL 40 — Capstone: Standing Stone: While above half your Hit Point maximum you have resistance to all damage except Force. While below it, you have advantage on every attack roll, and cannot be reduced to 0 Hit Points by anything short of a critical hit.

The Maul

Opener — Retaliation: Once per turn, when you hit a creature with a melee attack, if that creature has damaged you since the end of your last turn, you can make one additional melee attack against it as part of the same action. If you are using Flurry of Blows, this attack does not count against its number of strikes.

PL 30 — choose one:

  • Crushing Grip: When you hit a creature with a melee attack you can Grapple it as part of the attack, and Grappled creatures take your Martial Arts die at the start of each of their turns.
  • Sweep: When you hit a creature, you can force a Strength saving throw against your save DC; on a failure it is pushed 15 feet and knocked Prone.

PL 35 — choose one:

  • Punish: Your Retaliation attack deals additional damage equal to the damage you last reduced with Break the Blow.
  • Spellbreaker: When you hit a creature that is Concentrating on a spell, it has disadvantage on the saving throw to maintain it, and you can spend 2 Primal Points to impose automatic failure instead.

PL 40 — Capstone: Everything Breaks: Retaliation triggers once per turn against every creature that has damaged you, rather than only one. Your melee attacks score critical hits against Grappled or Prone creatures on a roll of 19–20.

Tower Shield

Tower Shield

Armor(Shield)

50 gp, 20lbs - AC +0

Also known as a Scutum, the tower shield is a large piece of curved metal or wood, or a composite of both. It is the size of it's user, too big and it is unwieldy if not impossible to use, and too small it becomes ineffective.

The shield confers no AC bonus to it's user by default. Instead it grants a damage threshold to you and creatures that you are providing cover for, so long as they are the same size or smaller than the shield. The damage threshold equals your strength modifier, plus your proficiency bonus when wielded with one hand, or twice your strength modifier plus your proficiency bonus when wielded with two. The damage threshold increases for each allied tower shield wielder within 5 feet, adding up to two of their proficiency bonuses to the damage threshold.

A creature with a strength score less than 13 has their speed lowered by 10 feet while wielding a tower shield.

This shield cannot be used as a base for an animated shield.

  • 14th Level - Embrace of Oblivion

3rd Level - Umbral Lord Spells

The magic of your patron ensures you always have certain spells ready; when you reach a Warlock level specified in the Umbral Lord Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

Umbral Lord Spells

  • 3rd: Dissonant Whispers, Phantasmal Force, Calm Emotions, Cause Fear
  • 5th: Summon Shadowspawn, Fear
  • 7th: Shadow of Moil, Phantasmal Killer
  • 9th: Dream, Modify Memory

These spells reflect the patron’s nature—magic that distorts perception, suppresses emotion, and turns sorrow into power.

3rd Level - Echoes of the Forgotten

3rd-Level Umbral Lord Feature

Your presence carries the emotional residue of the Shadowfell—haunting, weighty, and impossible to shake. Even the fiercest mind stumbles under the echo of forgotten regrets.

You gain proficiency in Insight or Intimidation (your choice).

Additionally, when you damage a creature with a Warlock spell or cantrip, you can mark it with Lingering Regret until the end of your next turn. The next time the creature makes an attack roll or ability check, it subtracts your Charisma modifier (minimum 1) from the roll, as if gripped by an emotion it cannot name.

You can affect a number of creatures this way equal to your Warlock level divided by 3 (rounded up), regaining all uses when you finish a long rest.

6th Level - Gravity of Sorrow

6th-Level Umbral Lord Feature

Despair halts even the strongest charge. You call forth a field of emotional gravity—a stillness that seeps into flesh and will alike.

As a bonus action, you designate a point within 60 feet. That point becomes the center of a 15-foot radius zone of heavy emotional drag until the start of your next turn.

Each creature of your choice that starts its turn in the area or enters it for the first time on a turn must succeed on a Strength saving throw against your spell save DC or have its speed reduced to 0 until the end of that turn. On a failed save, the creature also cannot Dash until the end of its next turn, as if the very act of movement had become too much to bear.

You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, regaining all uses when you finish a long rest.

10th Level - Despair-Wrought Form

10th-Level Umbral Lord Feature

Your patron reshapes you into an embodiment of psychic weight. You don’t lash out with fire or blade—you unravel resolve, layer by layer.

You gain resistance to necrotic and psychic damage.

As an action, you can manifest a mantle of oppressive sorrow for 1 minute. While active:

  • You emit a 20-foot radius aura of emotional gravity.
  • Each enemy that starts its turn in the aura must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or become frightened until the start of its next turn.
  • If a creature fails this saving throw a second time in a row, it becomes incapacitated until the start of its next turn, lost in overwhelming emotion.
  • If a creature fails the save on three consecutive turns, it becomes Paralyzed until it succeeds on the Wisdom saving throw or is outside the aura of oppressive sorrow.
  • The oppresive sorrow overrides any fear you are feeling, while the aura is active you are immune to frightened condition. You can use this feature once per long rest, or by expending a pact magic spell slot.

14th Level - Embrace of Oblivion

14th-Level Umbral Lord Feature

You carry the end in your wake. When a soul slips away nearby, you seize its unraveling and cast it like a shadow across the battlefield.

When a creature you can see within 60 feet drops to 0 hit points, you can use your reaction to claim its fading essence. Choose a number of creatures equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum 1) within 30 feet of the dying creature. Each must make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC.

  • On a failed save, a creature takes 5d10 psychic damage and is frightened until the end of its next turn.
  • On a successful save, the creature takes half damage and is not frightened.

While frightened in this way, a creature loses all temporary hit points, cannot gain temporary hit points, and cannot benefit from healing.

If a creature is already frightened by any means, it must use its action on its next turn to Dash away from you. If it cannot move, it instead takes an additional 5d10 psychic damage, writhing in place under the pressure of oblivion.

You can use this reaction up to a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier per long rest.

You are not a torch in the darkness. You are the hush after the flame goes out.

Homebrew / Other

Uphondo Lwebutho

Uphondo Lwebutho

Uphondo Lwebutho

"Horn of the Regiment." Uphondo is the horn — the same word used for the horn of an ox, and for the two wings of warriors that run wide and close behind an enemy while the chest holds them in place. Ibutho is the regiment: an age-set, everyone who came of age in the same season, trained together and sent into the field together. Together the name means something closer to one of the horns than a warrior who has a horn — you are not a soldier who belongs to a regiment, you are a piece of it, and the piece that moves. Plural, the tradition is called the izimpondo zebutho, the regiment's horns.

They do not wear armor. They wear a shield taller than a man and a spear shorter than an arm, and they arrive a day before anyone expects them. A regiment fights as one body: the chest holds the enemy in place, the horns run wide and close behind them, and the loins sit with their backs turned, waiting to be spent. A single warrior of this tradition carries the whole doctrine in their bones — hook the shield, open the ribs, stab once, call out.

In the Realms

Faerûn's closest parallel is the Shaar — the enormous savanna sweeping east from the Lake of Steam to the Eastern Shaar, where grassland nations rise and fall on the strength of their regiments rather than their walls. Shaaran warriors live and die by mobility across open ground, and a discipline built on encirclement, forced marches, and the shield line belongs there more naturally than anywhere in the North.

South and west, the tradition shades into other things. On the Chultan Peninsula, the same drill contracts to jungle warfare — shorter sightlines, ambush instead of encirclement, the horns closing through undergrowth. Further south still, across the Great Sea, lies Katashaka, the continent almost nothing in the North has mapped; regiments trained in this style occasionally arrive from there with no interest in explaining themselves.

A warrior of this tradition on the Sword Coast is almost always far from home; a veteran of a Shaaran ibutho who marched north with a caravan, or a Chultan raised to the shield in Port Nyanzaru and hired out of it.

Features:

  • 3rd Level - Ukuzivocavoca Kwebutho (Regimental Drill)
  • 3rd Level - Izimpondo ZeNyathi (Horns of the Buffalo)
  • 7th Level - Bamba Isihlangu (Hook the Shield)
  • 7th Level - Uhambo Olude (Barefoot March)
  • 10th Level - Bamba bese uhlasela (Chest and Loins)
  • 15th Level - USUTHU! (Frightful Warcry)
  • 18th Level - NGADLA! (Cry of Victory)

3rd Level - Ukuzivocavoca Kwebutho (Regimental Drill)

Unarmored Defense. While you aren't wearing armor, your AC equals the higher of 12 + your Strength modifier, or 10 + your Dexterity modifier + your Strength modifier. You can use a Shield.

You lose this benefit while a magic item is setting or increasing your Strength or Dexterity; a permanent increase you have already consumed, such as a Manual of Gainful Exercise, is your own.

Spear and Shield. While wielding a Shield and a Spear or Javelin, that weapon deals 1d8 in one hand and its thrown ranges are doubled.

3rd Level - Izimpondo ZeNyathi (Horns of the Buffalo)

Once per turn when you hit with a melee weapon, you can mark the target Encircled until the end of your next turn. Only one creature at a time; marking a new one ends the old.

An Encircled creature has its Speed reduced by 10 feet and can't Disengage. Once on each of your turns, when you or an ally hits it while you are both within 5 feet of it, that attack deals extra damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus.

7th Level - Bamba Isihlangu (Hook the Shield)

Once on each of your turns when you hit an Encircled creature, you can hook its guard aside (no action required). It makes a Strength save (DC 8 + your Proficiency Bonus + your Strength modifier). On a failure, until the start of your next turn it gains no benefit from a Shield or Cover, and the next attack against it has Advantage.

7th Level - Uhambo Olude (Barefoot March)

You and up to five companions can travel at a Fast pace without the penalty to passive Perception, and can force march extra hours equal to your Constitution modifier (minimum 1) without saving against Exhaustion. You have Advantage on saves against Exhaustion from heat, thirst, or marching.

10th Level - Bamba bese uhlasela (Chest and Loins)

Hold the Chest. Enemies leaving your reach treat that space as Difficult Terrain.

Send the Loins. As a Bonus Action, choose up to two allies within 30 feet who can see or hear you. Each can use their Reaction to move up to half their Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks, ending closer to your Encircled creature if able. Uses equal to your Proficiency Bonus, regained on a Short or Long Rest.

15th Level - USUTHU! (Frightful Warcry)

As a Bonus Action, each enemy within 30 feet that can see or hear you makes a Wisdom save (DC 8 + your Proficiency Bonus + your Strength modifier) or is Frightened of you for 1 minute, the creature can make the save again at the end of each of their turns. Your Encircled creature saves with Disadvantage. Until the start of your next turn, the first attack each ally makes against your Encircled creature has Advantage. Once per Short or Long Rest.

18th Level - NGADLA! (Cry of Victory)

Your Encircled damage rider no longer needs an ally — it applies whenever you are within 5 feet of the target — and it triggers on every hit rather than once per turn.

When you reduce a creature to 0 Hit Points with a melee attack, you can make one additional attack against a different creature: a melee attack within reach, or a thrown Spear or Javelin within normal range, drawing the weapon as part of the attack. You can move half your Speed first without provoking Opportunity Attacks, and the attack applies Encircled on a hit. Uses equal to your Proficiency Bonus, regained on a Long Rest.

Warrior of the Drawn String

Warrior of the Drawn String

Warrior of the Drawn String

The bow is an extension of the body. The draw is a breath, the release a strike, and the arrow is simply the fist arriving late.

Throughout this subclass, bow means a Shortbow or Longbow.

Features:

  • 3rd Level - Way of the Bow
  • 6th Level - Unerring Archer
  • 11th Level - Perfected Arts
  • 17th Level - Heart-Seeker

3rd Level - Way of the Bow

You gain proficiency with Longbows, and bows count as Monk weapons for you. You can also use the Mastery property of any bow you wield.

Arrow Arts. After you attack with a bow on your turn, you can spend Focus Points as a Bonus Action to loose one special arrow:

  • Focused Shot (1 point). Make one bow attack with Advantage. On a hit, add one roll of your Martial Arts die to the damage.
  • Split Shot (1 point). Make two bow attacks with Disadvantage against two creatures within 30 feet of each other.
  • Volley (2 points). Choose a Line 120 feet long and 5 feet wide originating from you, or a 15-foot-radius Sphere centered within 60 feet. Each creature in the area makes a Dexterity saving throw, taking Piercing damage equal to three rolls of your Martial Arts die on a failed save or half as much on a successful one.

6th Level - Unerring Archer

  • You don't have Disadvantage on ranged attack rolls because a hostile creature is within 5 feet of you.
  • Focused Quiver. You can conjure an arrow as part of any bow attack or Arrow Art, so you never need ammunition. Conjured arrows deal Force damage instead of Piercing.

11th Level - Perfected Arts

  • Focused Shot adds two rolls of your Martial Arts die, and the target has Disadvantage on its next saving throw before the start of your next turn.
  • Split Shot makes three attacks instead of two.
  • Volley deals four rolls of your Martial Arts die, and you can choose a number of creatures equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum 1) to be unaffected.

17th Level - Heart-Seeker

  • Inescapable Arrow. As an Action, spend 4 Focus Points to hit one creature you can see within your bow's long range — no attack roll is made. It makes a Constitution saving throw, taking 10d12 Piercing damage on a failed save or half as much on a successful one. A creature reduced to 0 Hit Points by this damage dies.

Way of the Sun Soul

Way of the Sun Soul

Way of the Sun Soul

Monk Subclass — D&D 5e (2014) (HB) Homebrew Revision

Sun Soul monks channel their ki into searing light and solar flame, empowering their strikes, projecting radiant energy, and eventually embodying the brilliance of the sun.

Features:

  • 3rd Level - Radiant Sun Soul
  • 6th Level - Blinding Radiance
  • 11th Level - Solar Ascension
  • 17th Level - Radiance Incarnate

3rd Level - Radiant Sun Soul

Radiant Sun Bolt

Whenever you make an unarmed strike as part of your Attack action, Martial Arts, or Flurry of Blows, you can replace that attack with a Radiant Sun Bolt.

Make a ranged spell attack using Dexterity as your spellcasting ability against a creature within 60 feet. You are proficient with this attack. On a hit, the target takes radiant damage equal to your Martial Arts die + your Dexterity modifier.

Searing Strike

Your unarmed strikes can deal radiant damage instead of their normal damage type.

Solar Radiance

You can cause your body to shed bright light in a 10-foot emanation and dim light for an additional 10 feet. You can activate or suppress this light at will (no action required).

6th Level - Blinding Radiance

Blinding Flare

After you hit a creature with a radiant unarmed strike or Radiant Sun Bolt, you can use your bonus action and spend 1 ki point to force it to make a Constitution saving throw against your ki save DC.

On a failure, the creature is blinded until the end of your next turn. On a success, it is unaffected.

11th Level - Solar Ascension

Solar Flight

When you use Step of the Wind, you gain a flying speed equal to your walking speed and can hover until the end of your current turn.

Searing Sunburst

As an action, you create an explosion of radiant energy centered on a point you can see within 120 feet.

Creatures of your choice within a 20-foot-radius sphere must make a Constitution saving throw against your ki save DC.

On a failed save, a creature takes radiant damage equal to four Martial Arts dice, is pushed up to 15 feet away from the center, and suffers Solar Burn.

On a successful save, it takes half as much radiant damage and suffers no additional effects.

Solar Burn. The target takes 1d6 fire damage at the start of each of its turns for up to 3 rounds. It can use a bonus action to extinguish the flames. Multiple applications refresh the duration instead of stacking.

You can use Searing Sunburst once without spending ki, regaining that use when you finish a long rest. Additional uses cost 3 ki points each.

17th Level - Radiance Incarnate

As a bonus action, you can spend 5 ki points to embody the full brilliance of the sun for 1 minute. The transformation ends early if you’re incapacitated or choose to end it (no action required).

While transformed, you gain the following benefits:

Solar Flight. You gain a flying speed equal to your walking speed and can hover.

Blazing Soul. Once on each of your turns when you hit with an unarmed strike or Radiant Sun Bolt, you deal additional radiant damage equal to two Martial Arts dice.

Sun Shield. When a creature within 10 feet of you hits you with an attack, you can use your reaction to deal radiant damage equal to two Martial Arts dice.

Eyes of the Sun. You have advantage on saving throws against effects that would impose the blinded condition.

Wrath of the Sun. Once during the transformation, you can use your action to unleash a wave of solar energy. Creatures of your choice within 30 feet must make a Dexterity saving throw against your ki save DC.

On a failed save, a creature takes radiant damage equal to five Martial Arts dice and falls prone. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage and isn’t knocked prone.

Amonkhet Naga

Amonkhet Naga

Ability Score Increase

Your Constitution score increases by 2, and your Intelligence score increases by 1.

Age

Like humans, naga reach adulthood in their late teens. They show no signs of aging beyond that point except for growing larger, so in theory, a naga could live well over a century.

Alignment

Most naga are either neutral or neutral evil in alignment.

Size

Naga stand about 5 feet tall when upright, but the total length of their bodies, head to tail, ranges from 10 to as much as 20 feet. Your size is Medium.

Speed

Your base walking speed is 30 feet.

Speed Burst

Using your tail as a propellant you can give yourself a speed boost. Immediately after you move at least 10 feet in a straight line, you can propel yourself 15 feet in the same direction without provoking opportunity attacks. You can use this a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

Natural Weapons

Your fanged maw and constricting serpentine body are natural weapons, which you can use to make unarmed strikes. If you hit with your bite, you deal piercing damage equal to 1d4 + your Strength modifier, and your target must make a Constitution saving throw (DC 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Constitution modifier). On a failed save, the target takes 1d4 poison damage.

If you hit with your constrict attack, you deal bludgeoning damage equal to 1d6 + your Strength modifier, and if the target is one size larger or smaller than the naga, the target is grappled (escape DC 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Strength modifier). Until this grapple ends, the target is restrained, and you can’t constrict another target.

Poison Immunity

You are immune to poison damage and can’t be poisoned.

Poison Affinity

You gain proficiency with the poisoner’s kit.

Languages

You can speak, read, and write Common and Naga.

Homebrew / Races

Avariel

Avariel

Ability Score Increase

Your Dexterity score increases by 2.

Your Wisdom score increases by 1.

Age

Although elves reach physical maturity at about the same age as humans, the elven understanding of adulthood goes beyond physical growth to encompass worldly experience. An elf typically claims adulthood and an adult name around the age of 100 and can live to be 750 years old.

Size

Avariel typically range from under four and a half to over five and a half feet tall and have slender builds with hollow bones. Your size is Medium.

Speed

Your base walking speed is 30 feet.

Flight

Thanks to your wings, you have a flying speed equal to your walking speed. You can’t use this flying speed if you’re wearing medium or heavy armor.

Darkvision

Accustomed to twilit mountains and the night sky, you have superior vision in dark and dim conditions. You can see in dim light within 60 feet of you as if it were bright light, and in darkness as if it were dim light. You can’t discern color in darkness, only shades of gray.

Keen Senses

You have proficiency in the Perception skill.

Fey Ancestry

You have advantage on saving throws against being charmed, and magic can’t put you to sleep.

Trance

Elves don’t need to sleep. Instead, they meditate deeply, remaining semiconscious, for 4 hours a day. (The Common word for such meditation is “trance.”) While meditating, you can dream after a fashion; such dreams are actually mental exercises that have become reflexive through years of practice. After resting in this way, you gain the same benefit that a human does from 8 hours of sleep.

Languages

You can speak, read, and write Elvish and one other language of your choice, typically Common, also known as Thorasta. Avariel typically speak the Skaevrym variant of Thorasta which is derived from North Eeastern Faerun near Sossel, the region nearest their settlement atop Mount Sundabar. Elvish is fluid, with subtle intonations and intricate grammar, which some Avariel speak with a more relaxed and breathy intonation akin to Auran, and the language is sometimes mixed with their own unique form of sign language based around aerial movement. Involving things such as flaps, stalls, and wind dips. It was a less subtle sign language than those of non-flying races, having been developed primarily for communication during flight.

Increase your Consititution score by 1, to a maximum of 20

Homebrew / Races

Faerie Elf

Faerie Elf

Physical Description

Faerie elves are roughly the same height as gnomes but weigh roughly 25 to 60 lbs. Faeries tend to have more vibrant eye colors of shimmering greens, blues, and reds. They have a pair of transparent wings that allow them to fly. Other than that they look like most wood elves.

History

Although not many people have seen these crossbreeds, the faerie elf is a mixture of a elf and a fey. They tend to keep their societies and culture hidden from public view. Faerie elves are known to have many conflicts within their society, from what little has been observed. They tend to have very different views of other races and cultures.

Society

Faerie elves tend to keep to themselves and tend to hide from other outside sources, mainly due to the harsh discrimination and prejudice their ancestors have experienced. They are buried deep within forests and caves and have a strong sense of family. They tend to have a hard time developing new relations with others, especially if they're neither fey, elf, or faerie. The ones who do leave the villages tend to be brave adventurers determined to prove the old ways are over.

Elf Subrace

Ability Score Increase

Your Charisma score increases by 1.

Size

Unlike most elves Faerie elves range from 3 to over 4 foot tall but have slender builds and weigh very little. Your size is Small.

Speed

Your base walking speed is 20 feet and your flying speed is 30 feet.

Fairy Wings

You have a pair of light, transparent wings that grant you a fly speed of 30-feet, allowing you a certain degree of flight. However, these wings can only fly up to a height of 10 feet, any higher and they fail until you are 10 feet above the ground again. This flight speed cannot negate damage inflicted from falling a height of 20 feet or more, only halve it. You lose your flying speed until you complete a short or long rest if they are directly exposed to water.

Tranquil Magic

The typical faerie focuses more on their mind rather than their strength. You know one cantrip of your choice from the cleric spell list. Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for it.

Homebrew / Races

Half Gnoll

Half Gnoll

Be it from the merging of peaceful clans, or a more unwelcome coupling of savage gnolls and their victims, some cases of Half-Gnolls can appear.

Half-Gnoll's heritages are human and gnoll, as different as night and day. The result of this often portrays itself as instinctual and common sense confusion: with two separate parts fighting on what the proper choice is. The only thing all can agree on is the strong sense of being part of a group, be it a village or a hunting pack. Whether they attempt to do so with humans or gnolls, they often face an uphill battle.

Half-Gnolls still have a craving for chaos and killing that their Gnoll blood possesses, but it is mostly easier to control, and can often be quelled with hunting and the occasional consuming of any blood and guts. If they end up killing or consuming an intelligent creature, however, there is still a high risk of them going on similar rampages.

Ability Score Increase

When determining your character’s ability scores, increase one score by 2 and increase a different score by 1, or increase three different scores by 1. Follow this rule regardless of the method you use to determine the scores, such as rolling or point buy. The “Quick Build” section for your character’s class offers suggestions on which scores to increase. You can follow those suggestions or ignore them, but you can’t raise any of your scores above 20.

Age

Half-Gnolls usually mature by the age of ten, and they often die of various reasons by the age of 35, but there are cases where they live up to the age of 75 without a real sign of old age, before seeming to lose all their strength immediately and falling into an eternal slumber.

Size

Half Gnolls are lean, lanky and tower over humans, often found in the range between 6 and 7 feet tall. Your size is Medium.

Speed

Your base walking speed is 35 feet

Darkvision

Thanks to your gnoll blood,  you can see in 60ft of darkness as if in bright light, and the rest in dim light. You can't discern colour in the dark, only black and white.

Septic Bite

Your jaws are a natural weapon, and your mouth is a breeding ground for disease. If you hit with this bite attack, you deal 1d4 + STR piercing damage plus an additional 1d4 poison damage.

Keen Smell

You gain advantage on any Wisdom (Perception) or Intelligence (Investigation) checks that involve smell.

Rampage

When you reduce a creature to 0 hit points with a melee attack on your turn, you may use a bonus action to move up to half your speed and make a bite attack

Languages

You can speak, read and write Common, Gnoll.

Gnoll is an abrasive language, communicating in growls, barks and broken Abyssal. Beings that can speak Gnoll can understand general concepts and few keywords in Abyssal.

It has no script of its own, often using Infernal script.

Age.

A typical kitsune lives to 600 to 1000. It gains an additional century for every tail it grows, to a maximum of 9 tails.

Alignment.

As kitsune are natural tricksters, they tend towards gentler forms of chaos.

Creature Type.

You are a fey.

Size.

A kitsune is usually between 4'5inch and 5'10inch. Your size is Medium.

Speed.

Your base walking speed is 35 feet.

Darkvision.

You can see in dim light within 60 feet of you as if it were bright light, and in darkness as if it were dim light. You can't discern color in darkness, only shades of gray.

Keen Senses.

Much like the foxes they resemble, kitsunes have heightened senses. You are proficient in the Perception skill.

Fey Ancestry.

Your fey lineage gives you advantage on saving throws against being charmed. Magic cannot put you to sleep.

Human form.

You can appear as a human indefinitely using a very simple illusion magic. However, on a (DC 10 + proficiency bonus + Charisma Modifier) Investigation check, a person looking directly at you can tell that you are not what you appear. You always appear to be the same human when you cast this spell. While in human form you have -1 to all dice rolls.

Fox Tails.

You have one tail when you are born and every 3 levels you gain another tail; lvl3 = 2, lvl6 = 3, etc. A kitsune's tails are a symbol of growth and realization for themselves and reflects how powerful they are. To your DM's discretion, A kitsune can also grow tail's for pivotal moments in its life or personal growth.

Fox Fire.

So long as your tails are not severed, you can cast certain spells. You know the dancing lights cantrip. At 3rd level you gain the ability to cast faerie fire once per long rest. Charisma is your casting ability for these spells.

Languages.

You can read and write both Common and Sylvan.

Class Features

PL 21: Proficiencies

When you take this prestige class, choose two additional skills from the Monk skill list. You gain proficiency in both.

PL 21: Ascendant Martial Arts

Your training has transcended mortal limits. Your Martial Arts die is now 1d12.

PL 22: Uncanny Metabolism (Prestige)

You can now use your Uncanny Metabolism feature twice per Long Rest, the second time you use it you only recover half of your total focus points. Additionally, when you use it, you regain a number of Hit Points equal to four times your Prestige Level.

PL 23: Perfect Deflection

You can now use your Deflect Attacks feature against melee, ranged, and energy-based attack rolls. When you do so, you can roll an additional Martial arts die and add the result to the damage reduction. The Deflection damage is increased to 4 martial arts die rolls

PL 23: Expanded Monk Tradition

Your talents expand, You may choose the same Monk tradition, or you may choose a new one to reflect the different studies and focus learned from another tradition. At PL 23, PL 26, PL 31 and PL37, you gain more features from your Monk tradition.

PL 24: Ability Score Improvement

At PL 24, 28, 32, 36, and 39, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or two ability scores by 1. As normal, you cannot increase a score above 20 (unless another feature allows it). You may select a Feat instead of an ASI.

PL 25: Relentless Pressure

When a creature successfully saves against your stunning strike feature, their speed is reduced to 0 until the start of your next turn and they are considered to be dazed for the same duration, your next attack against that creature will have advantage.

Additionally, once per turn when you attack a creature that is already dazed from one of your stunning strike attempts, you can attempt another stunning strike. The target makes the save with disadvantage.

PL 26: Martial Minimum

Your strikes are consistently devastating. When you roll a Martial Arts die, you treat any roll lower than a 2 as a 2. This minimum increases to 3 at PL 32, and 4 at PL 38.

PL 27: Monk Avoidance

At 27th level, your monk’s training and mental fortitude allows you to resist assaults on the mind. When you are subjected to an effect that allows you to make a Intelligence or Wisdom saving throw to take only half damage, you instead take no damage if you succeed on the saving throw, and only half damage if you fail.

PL 29: Ascendant Step of the Wind

When you use your Step of the Wind feature, you gain a flying speed equal to your walking speed until the end of your current turn. Additionally your movement speed increases by 20 feet.

PL 30: Focused Impact

Any time you roll a Martial Arts die (for damage or features), you can expend 1 Focus Point to roll an additional Martial Arts die and add the result to the first roll.

PL33: Resist Energy

Whenever you fail a saving throw that deals damage, you can use your perfect deflection ability to reduce the damage. You cannot however deflect the damage back if you reduce the damage to 0.

PL 34: Disciplined Thriver

Your mental and physical discipline grants you expertise in your defenses. Choose two saving throws in which you are proficient:

  • One Major Save (Dexterity, Constitution, or Wisdom).
  • One Minor Save (Strength, Intelligence, or Charisma). You add your Proficiency Bonus twice to those saving throws instead of once.

PL 35: Fluid Reflexes

You gain an additional Reaction on every round of combat. This reaction can only be used for Monk class features (such as Deflect Attacks or Slow Fall).

PL 38: Superior Focus

The cost of your superior defense or empty body is now 3 Focus Points, and you are invisible for the duration.

Additionally, your heightened senses give you blindsight to 30 feet.

PL 40: Peak Perfection

Your body and soul reach their ultimate form. You gain 6 ability points to distribute between your Dexterity and Wisdom scores as you choose. You can increase the ability scores to a maximum of 30 with this feature.

Phoenix

Phoenix

Ignite

At 1st level, you gain the ability to start fires with a touch. As an action, you can magically ignite a flammable object you touch with your hand—an object such as a torch, a piece of tinder, or the hem of drapes.

Mantle of Flame

Starting at 1st level, you can unleash the phoenix fire that blazes within you. As a bonus action, you magically wreathe yourself in swirling fire, as your eyes glow like hot coals. For 1 minute, you gain the following benefits:

  • You shed bright light in a 30-foot radius and dim light for an additional 30 feet.
  • Any creature takes fire damage equal to your Charisma modifier if it hits you with a melee attack from within 5 feet of you or if it touches you.
  • Whenever you roll fire damage on your turn, the roll gains a bonus to equal to your Charisma modifier.

Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest.

Phoenix Spark

Starting at 6th level, the fiery energy within you grows restless and vengeful. In the face of defeat, it surges outward to preserve you in a fiery roar. If you are reduced to 0 hit points, you can use your reaction to draw on the spark of the phoenix. You are instead reduced to 1 hit point, and each creature within 10 feet of you takes fire damage equal to half your sorcerer level + your Charisma modifier. If you use this feature while under the effects of your Mantle of Flame, this feature instead deals fire damage equal to your sorcerer level + double your Charisma modifier, and your Mantle of Flame immediately ends. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest.

Nourishing Fire

Starting at 14th level, your fire spells soothe and restore you. When you expend a spell slot to cast a spell that includes a fire damage roll, you regain hit points equal to the slot's level + your Charisma modifier.

Form of the Phoenix

At 18th level, you finally master the spark of fire that dances within you. While under the effect of your Mantle of Flame feature, you gain additional benefits:

  • You have a flying speed of 40 feet and can hover.
  • You have resistance to Poison & Fire
  • If you use your Phoenix Spark, that feature deals an extra 20 fire damage to each creature.

Homebrew / Races

The Mystic

The Mystic

Psionic Prestige Class

Every psi-adept eventually finds the same wall. The soulknife learns to sharpen thought into a blade but never learns what else thought can be. The psi warrior learns to shove the world with their mind but never learns to unmake it. The wall is not a limit of power — it is a limit of vocabulary. The Mystic is what happens when a mortal stops using the gift as a tool and begins speaking the language it was cut from.

Prerequisites

Level 20 Cycle. You must have completed a full 20-level paragon cycle satisfying the Purity Rule.

The Purity Rule. That cycle must have consisted entirely of levels from one of the following, with no multiclassing:

  • Rogue (Soulknife)
  • Fighter (Psi Warrior)
  • Sorcerer (Aberrant Mind)
  • Warlock (Great Old One Patron)

Hit Die: 1d8 per Mystic level

Your entry path determines your Order. You do not choose it.

Entry Order
Soulknife The Whetstone
Psi Warrior The Aegis
Aberrant Mind The Aberrant Bloom
Great Old One The Hollow Crown

Design Principle

This class is additive. You already have a combat loop that works — Sneak Attack, Flurry of Blows, Extra Attack, Metamagic, Eldritch Blast. The Mystic does not replace it and should never compete with it for your Action.

Almost every discipline is a Bonus Action, a Reaction, or a rider on something you were already doing. The handful that cost a full Magic action are Ascendant-band effects meant for the turn you decide to end an encounter.

Your Manifestation Dice are a separate pool from any psionic resource you already had. The two never convert. Your Order deepens the old pool across five growth points; the class runs the new one.
