PL 21 Core Features: Prestige Scaling, Proficiencies, Psionic Ability, Psionics, Manifestation, Psychic Focus, Separate Pools.

The Bands column shows the highest band you can activate. It includes every band below it.

PL 21: Manifestation

At the start of each of your turns, you can expend any number of your Manifestation Dice, rolling them all at once. The total is your Manifested Psi for the round.

That psi is available until the start of your next turn, including during other creatures' turns. Any left over is lost.

Generating psi costs no action. Expending dice is one decision, made once per round, before you know what the round holds.

You regain half your expended Manifestation Dice (rounded up) on a Short Rest, and all of them on a Long Rest.

Manifesting outside combat

When you aren't in initiative, there are no turns to key off. You can expend Manifestation Dice at any time with no action; the resulting psi lasts 1 minute or until spent, whichever comes first. Any effect you pay for runs its full written duration regardless.

Rolling a die vs expending one

Two phrases appear throughout this class and they mean different things:

  • "A roll of your Manifestation Die" refers only to the size of the die on the table — d8, d10, or d12. You roll one and use the number. Nothing is expended. Your pool is untouched.
  • "Expend a die" means the die leaves your pool and must be recovered on a rest.

So a feature that adds a roll of your Manifestation Die to damage costs you nothing and works every round forever. A feature that says expend is spending a resource. The same distinction applies to Psionic Energy Dice.

The three bands

Band Cost Typical action Dice to cover it Unlocks
Reflex 2–4 psi Rider, Reaction, Bonus Action one die covers two PL 21
Committed 6–9 psi Bonus Action or Reaction one die PL 23
Ascendant 11–14 psi Magic action two dice PL 33

There is no per-activation cap to track. If you can afford it and the band is unlocked, you can use it.

Psi is the only thing you spend. A psychic focus costs nothing and runs continuously, so a turn where you expend no dice still has psionics in it — just passive ones.

The trophy rule

Any feature that rewards you for reducing a creature to 0 Hit Points triggers only on creatures of Challenge Rating 1 or higher that you did not summon, create, or command. This covers Relentless, Feed, Siphon, Warped Blade, and anything like them. Minions are not a resource farm.

The one-spell rule

No feature of this class ever lets you concentrate on, or maintain, more than one spell at a time. Disciplines can stack with each other and with a spell where a feature allows it, but a second spell always ends the first. This holds regardless of Fractured Concentration, Psionic Mastery, or any combination of them.

What a turn actually looks like

A PL 26 Whetstone Soulknife. 8d10 Manifestation Dice.

Start of turn. She expends one die, rolls a 6. 6 psi for the round. Action. Attack action with Psychic Blades, as normal. Sneak Attack, as normal. On the hit she folds in Mindspike's Lance — 3 psi, no action — for an extra 3d8 and an Intelligence save. 3 left. Bonus Action. Cunning Action to Disengage, exactly as she always did. Someone else's turn. The wizard gets targeted. She spends her Reaction on Intellect Fortress's Ward, 3 psi. 0 left. Start of her next turn. The 3 evaporates. She decides again.

PL 21: Prestige Scaling

Any feature referring to your level uses your Prestige Level (PL) = 20 + your Mystic level.

Discipline save DC = 8 + Proficiency Bonus + Psionic Ability modifier. Discipline attack modifier = Proficiency Bonus + Psionic Ability modifier.

PL 21: Proficiencies

Choose two additional skills from Arcana, History, Insight, Investigation, Medicine, Nature, Perception, and Religion.

PL 21: Psionic Ability

Choose Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma. That ability powers every feature of this class. The choice is permanent, alterable only by retraining, and does not change the ability used by your entry subclass.

Soulknives may instead choose Dexterity — see The Whetstone.

PL 21: Psionics

You know the number of disciplines shown on the table, chosen from the Shared Disciplines list. Your Order grants two Order Disciplines that don't count against this number and that no other Order can learn. On each level in this class you can swap one discipline for another.

PL 21: Psychic Focus

As a Bonus Action, choose one discipline you know. You gain that discipline's ○ Focus benefit, which lasts until you are Incapacitated or until you use a Bonus Action to focus on a different discipline.

Focus costs nothing. It is not Concentration — it can't be broken by damage, and it doesn't interfere with a spell or discipline you are concentrating on.

Focus and manifestation are independent. Focusing on a discipline does not let you activate its options for free, and activating a discipline's options does not require you to be focused on it. You can be focused on Iron Skin for the AC while spending all your psi on Mindspike, and you can activate any option of any discipline you know regardless of what you are focused on.

In practice you set a focus once at the start of a fight and leave it. Switching costs a Bonus Action, so mid-combat changes should be a deliberate call — dropping the Stealth focus to pick up +1 AC when the fighting starts, for instance.

PL 21: Separate Pools

Manifestation Dice are their own resource. They are not Psionic Energy Dice, Focus Points, Sorcery Points, or spell slots, and never convert into each other in either direction. Your entry subclass's resource continues to work exactly as written, on its own recovery schedule — and your Order deepens it at each of its five growth points.

PL 22: Mystical Recovery

Once per Short or Long Rest, as a Bonus Action, you can expend any number of Manifestation Dice and regain Hit Points equal to the total rolled, rather than gaining psi from them.

This is the mirror of Consumptive Power: that feature turns blood into thought, this one turns thought into blood. Neither can pay for the other — Mystical Recovery spends dice, not psi, so psi gained from Consumptive Power can never be converted back into Hit Points.

PL 22: Ascendant Telepathy

You can speak telepathically to any creature you can see within 1 mile, and to any creature you've previously touched or linked with on the same plane. Language is unnecessary, though the creature must understand at least one language or be telepathic. You can maintain links with up to your Psionic Ability modifier in willing creatures, letting them speak to each other through you.

PL 23: Strength of Mind

After each Long Rest, choose two ability scores. You gain saving throw proficiency in them until your next Long Rest. If you are already proficient in a chosen ability, add half your Proficiency Bonus again to those saves instead.

PL 24: Ability Score Improvement

At PL 24, 28, 32, 36, and 39. Increase one score by 2 or two by 1, max 20 unless stated otherwise, or take a Feat.

PL 24: Potent Psionics

Once on each of your turns when you hit with a weapon or Unarmed Strike, or when you deal damage with a spell or discipline, deal an extra 2d8 Psychic damage, rising to 3d8 at PL 35.

PL 26: Die Minimum

When you roll a Manifestation Die, treat any result below 2 as a 2. This rises to 3 at PL 33 and 4 at PL 38.

PL 26: Consumptive Power

At any point during your turn, you can spend up to twice your Proficiency Bonus in Hit Points to gain an equal amount of Manifested Psi. No action required. Your current and maximum Hit Points are both reduced by that amount; the reduction to your maximum can't be lessened and lasts until a Long Rest.

Usable a number of times per Long Rest equal to your Proficiency Bonus. This is your correction when you underestimated the round.

PL 27: Unbound Focus

You can maintain the psychic focus of two disciplines at once, gaining both benefits. Setting a focus while two are active replaces one of your choice. It still costs one Bonus Action to change either.

PL 30: Overchannel

Once per turn when you activate a discipline, choose one:

  • Amplify. The damage dice of that manifestation are maximized.
  • Widen. Double the area or range of that manifestation, or add one target within its range.
  • Entrench. Double the duration of that manifestation.

Overchannel only ever affects the discipline you are activating. It does not touch weapon damage, Sneak Attack, Martial Arts dice, spell dice, Psionic Energy Dice, or any other damage in the same attack or turn — only the dice printed in the manifestation itself.

You take Psychic damage equal to the psi spent, which can't be reduced or prevented, and have Disadvantage on Constitution saves for concentration until the end of your next turn. Overchannel can't be applied to Ascendant-band options.

PL 31: Fractured Concentration

Concentrate on two disciplines at once, provided both were paid with Manifested Psi. You can't concentrate on a spell while doing so — see the one-spell rule. On a Constitution save to maintain, roll once with Disadvantage; failure loses both.

PL 34: Psionic Mastery

Once per Long Rest, at the start of your turn, you can gain Manifested Psi equal to your Mystic level — not your Prestige Level — without expending any dice. At PL 34 that is 14 psi, rising to 20 at PL 40. Until the start of your next turn, you can concentrate on any number of disciplines paid for with that psi simultaneously; concentrating on anything else ends them all.

PL 38: Psionic Body

  • Resistance to Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing; immunity to Psychic damage.
  • You no longer age; immune to disease, Poison damage, and the Poisoned condition.
  • No need to eat, drink, or breathe.
  • If you would die, roll a d20. On a 10+ you discorporate instead, vanishing with your gear at 0 Hit Points and reappearing at a place of your choice 1d3 days later on that plane, with the benefits of a Long Rest.

PL 40: Transcendent Mind

  • Inexhaustible. Once per Short or Long Rest, at the start of your turn, if you have no unspent Manifestation Dice, regain a number equal to half your Proficiency Bonus, rounded up.
  • Perfect Manifestation. Once per Long Rest, when you expend Manifestation Dice at the start of your turn, treat every one of them as its maximum. This applies only to Manifestation Dice rolled for psi — not to damage dice, Psionic Energy Dice, or any other roll.
  • Untouchable Will. Immune to the Charmed and Frightened conditions, to thought-reading and lie detection, and to possession or memory alteration.
  • Mastery Redoubled. You gain a second use of Psionic Mastery.

Shared Disciplines

Each discipline has one ○ Focus benefit and several paid options. The Focus applies only while you are focused on that discipline (see PL 21: Psychic Focus); the paid options can be used any time, focused or not. Saves are against your Discipline save DC. Action cost is listed on every option.

Rider means no action at all — you fold it into an attack or spell you were already making.

Mark Band Cost
○ Focus Free. Always on while focused.
● Reflex 2–4 psi
●● Committed 6–9 psi
●●● Ascendant 11–14 psi

When a creature attacks you, roll a d4; on a 2+ a duplicate is struck instead and destroyed. No concentration.

●●● Divergent Turn (14 psi) — Magic action. Take an additional turn immediately after this one. You gain no Manifested Psi at the start of that turn, and once-per-turn features you already used are not refreshed. You can't use this option again until you finish a Long Rest.

Unmake (Ascendant)

●●● Erasure (12 psi) — Magic action. One creature or object within 60 ft. A creature makes a Constitution save, taking 14d10 Force damage on a failure, half on a success. A creature killed by this leaves nothing and returns only via True Resurrection or Wish. A nonmagical object of Large size or smaller is destroyed outright.

●●● Unwrite (13 psi) — Magic action. End one magical effect of 8th level or lower within 60 ft, permanently. A magic item property ends until repaired, 1 week has passed.

Mystic Orders

Every Order has five growth points — PL 21, 25, 29, 33, and 37. Each carries a feature and a deepening of the pool you arrived with. PL 21 also grants your two Order Disciplines, detailed on each Order's page.

Growth rates. Your entry bump is proportional to your original pool: a third for Psionic Energy Dice, which are a subclass resource of twelve, and a quarter for Focus and Sorcery Points, which are full class resources of twenty. Every growth point after that adds a flat amount.

Pool PL 21 25 29 33 37 Total
Psionic Energy Dice +4 +2 +2 +2 +2 12 → 24
Sorcery Points +5 +2 +2 +2 +2 20 → 33
Pact Magic slots +1 — +1 — +1 4 → 7

Psionic Energy Dice and Sorcery Points also gain Short Rest recovery at PL 21, equal to your Proficiency Bonus. Focus Points and Pact slots already refresh on a Short Rest.

Your Order is fixed by your entry path, not chosen:

  • The Whetstone
  • The Aegis
  • The Aberrant Bloom
  • The Hollow Crown

Homebrew / Spells

Arcane Guardian

Arcane Guardian

Arcane Guardian

A sorcerer of selfless nature and protective pursuit, your magic manifests itself through your desire to support others, bringing you safety and security in the process. Imbuing allies with the same magic that suffuses themselves, these sorcerers augment their strengths, covering their weaknesses, and upon reaching mastery, become catalyst for the inevitable success of everyone under their influence.

Often called Arcane Guardians these sorcerers take a backseat to the events of life, letting others shine while they lift them higher, watching and protecting them. Many a hero was made by the hands of an Arcane Guardian.

Features:

  • 1st Level - Guardian Magic
  • 1st Level - Loving Protection
  • 6th Level - Gifting Inner Strength
  • 14th Level - Altruistic Splinter
  • 18th Level - Arcane Enlightenment

1st Level - Guardian Magic

You learn additional spells when you reach certain levels in this class, as shown on the Guardian table. Each of these spells counts as a sorcerer spell for you, but it doesn't count against the number of sorcerer spells you know.

Whenever you gain a sorcerer level, you can replace one spell you gained from this feature with another spell of the same level. The new spell must be an abjuration or a transmutation spell from the sorcerer, warlock, or wizard spell list.

Arcane Guardian Spells

  • 1st: bless, protection from evil and good
  • 3rd: aid, pass without trace
  • 5th: aura of vitality, protection from energy
  • 7th: aura of life, aura of purity
  • 9th: mass cure wounds, skill empowerment

1st Level - Loving Protection

Starting at 1st level, your selfless nature begins to show in your spellcasting. Whenever an ally within 30 feet of you fits the casting requirements for a spell with a casting time of 1 Reaction, you can spend an amount of sorcery points equal to the spell level to cast the spell and give the effects to them. You can do this an amount of times equal to your Charisma modifier, resetting when you finish a long rest.

6th Level - Gifting Inner Strength

Starting at 6th level, you harness the ability to spread your talents to your allies. Once per turn, as a bonus action, you can strengthen an ally's next spell or attack with a Metamagic option you have access to, spending sorcery points as you would to use the options normally. These options last for a minute. The viable Metamagic options are as listed:

Quickened Assault

When your target casts a spell that has a casting time of 1 action, they can choose to change the casting time to 1 bonus action for this casting.

Alternatively, they can make one melee or ranged weapon attack as a bonus action.

Subtle Assault

When the target casts a spell, they can choose to cast it without any somatic or verbal components.

Alternatively, they can give themself advantage on one melee or ranged weapon attack roll.

Empowered Assault

When the target rolls damage for a spell or weapon attack, they can reroll a number of the damage dice up to your Charisma modifier (minimum of one). They must use the new rolls.

Heightened Assault

When the target casts a spell that forces a creature to make a saving throw to resist its effects, they can give one target of the spell disadvantage on its first saving throw made against the spell.

Alternatively, if they make a melee or ranged weapon attack and hit, they can add your Charisma modifier to one of the damage rolls (minimum of one).

14th Level - Altruistic Splinter

Starting at 14th level, you learn to manipulate the bounds of your sorcery. Whenever you cast a spell that has a range of Self, you can spend an amount of sorcery points equal to twice the spell's level to change the range to Touch as long as the target is a willing creature. The spell level limit of this feature is half your Charisma modifier.  You can do this an amount of times equal to half your proficiency bonus, resetting when you finish a long rest.

18th Level - Arcane Enlightenment

Starting at 18th level, you gain the ability to funnel your strength into your allies. As an action on your turn, you can boost your allies' power until the end of your next turn. Every creature of your choice that is currently under the effects of a concentration spell cast by you receives the following additional effects:

  • Their speed is increased by 30 feet.
  • Every melee and ranged weapon attack roll they make is made with advantage. This advantage ignores any disadvantage also being applied to the target.
  • Any attacks the target makes that hit receive a damage bonus equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of one).
  • The target gains a bonus to AC equal to half your Charisma modifier (minimum of one).

This feature can be used a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, resetting on a long rest. Simulacrums are unable to use this feature.

Ethical Planar Binding

Ethical Planar Binding

5th-level abjuration. (Bard, Druid, Cleric, Wizard, Arcana Domain)

Meta

Casting Time: 1 hour

Range: 60 feet

Components: V, S, M (a jewel worth at least 1,000 gp, which the spell consumes)

Duration: 24 hours

Description

With this spell, you attempt to bind a celestial, an elemental, a fey, or a fiend to the Prime Material Plane for the Duration. The creature must be within range for the entire casting of the spell. At the completion of the casting, the target must make a Charisma saving throw. On a failed save, the creature is persuaded to stay on this plane for the duration. If the creature was summoned or created by another spell, that spell's duration is extended to match the duration of this spell.

A bound creature is friendly to you and follows your instructions to the best of its ability. You might command the creature to accompany you on an adventure, to guard a location, or to deliver a message. The creature obeys the letter of your instructions. If the creature carries out your instructions completely before the spell ends, it travels to you to report this fact if you are on the same plane of existence. If you are on a different plane of existence, it returns to the place where you bound it and remains there until the spell ends.

Ethical Caveat: The binding is a mutual agreement. Should the celestial, elemental. fey, or fiend feel that its binder is acting contrary to its original alignment, or forcing the creature to act in ways that it would not normally wish to do, the summoned creature may make a new CHA save with advantage to immediately teleport back to its own plane of existence. It may do this every round and will not take other actions beyond this save and protecting itself.

At Higher Levels

When you cast this spell using a spell slot of a higher level, the duration increases to 10 days with a 6th-level slot, to 30 days with a 7th- level slot, to 180 days with an 8th-level slot, and to a year and a day with a 9th-level spell slot.

Form Undead

Meta

Range: Touch

Duration: Instantaneous

Description

This spell must be cast within ten minutes after dusk. You must press the idol used for the material component of this spell to the corpse of a creature with a challenge rating of 10 or lower and hold it there for the duration of the casting of this spell. The corpse must be intact for the duration of this spell’s casting— a destroyed corpse causes this spell to fail.

The corpse reanimates, returning to life and using the statblock of the creature it belonged to, with the following changes:

  • its creature type becomes undead
  • its hit point maximum is halved
  • if it has class levels, it loses all of them
  • it loses any legendary actions and legendary resistances
  • It is unable to cast spells
  • it gains immunity to necrotic damage

As a bonus action on each of your turns, you can mentally command any creature you animated with this spell if the creature is within 120 feet of you (if you control multiple creatures, you can command any or all of them at the same time, issuing the same command to each one). You decide what action the creature will take and where it will move during its next turn, or you can issue a general command, such as to guard a particular chamber or corridor. If you issue no commands, the creature only defends itself against hostile creatures. Once given an order, the creature continues to follow it until its task is complete.

An undead raised by this spell is under your control for 24 hours, after which it makes a charisma saving throw. On a failure, you regain control of it for another 24 hours, whereupon it makes the save again. Each time it fails this saving throw, it gains a cumulative +2 bonus to the Charisma save.

On a success, it is hostile to all creatures (including yourself) and is under no compulsion to follow any orders you give it. It has disadvantage on attack rolls, ability checks, and saving throws it makes against you (except for the saving throws it makes to break free from your control).

Homebrew / Spells

Gnarly Druid

Gnarly Druid

Description

You were told nature has no true masters. You intend to prove that wrong.

Prerequisites: 5.5e (2024) Druid 20

Proficiencies

When you take this prestige class, choose two more skills from the Druid skill proficiencies. You are proficient in both of those skills.

Ascendant Spellcasting

Additionally when you take this prestige class, you gain a new set of spell slots to fuel your spells. You gain spell slots as per the Druid table based on your prestige level minus 20. When you prepare spells for the day, you may now prepare a number of spells equal to your prestige level + your Wisdom modifier.

You learn one Druid cantrip of your choice, and one additional Druid cantrip at 24th and 30th level.

Transcendent Wild Shape

21st level. Your connection to the primal has outgrown mortal limits. You gain one additional use of Wild Shape.

Your known forms increase by 2, and the maximum Challenge Rating for your forms increases by 1 (added to whatever maximum you already have from your class and subclass features). In addition, you may now learn Elemental stat blocks (in place of Beasts) up to CR 1 as known forms, representing your growing kinship with the raw substance of the world.

Expanded Druid Circle

22nd level. Your practice of the old ways deepens and broadens. You may choose the same Druid Circle you already belong to, or you may choose a new one to reflect the different truths nature has revealed to you.

Your choice grants you additional features at 22nd level, and again at 26th and 34th level.

Primal Resilience

23rd level. Nature itself shields you from harm. You gain resistance to poison damage and immunity to the Poisoned condition. While you are Wild Shaped, you also have advantage on saving throws against being charmed or frightened.

Ability Score Improvement

24th, 28th, 32nd, 36th, and 39th level. You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two of your ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature. You may select a feat instead of an Ability Score Improvement.

Greater Beast Spells

25th level. Your magic no longer cares what shape you wear. While using Wild Shape, you can cast any Druid spell you have prepared, including spells with a Material component that has a cost or is consumed, provided you have access to the required component or a Druidic Focus that can be worn or held in your current form (at your DM's discretion for unusual anatomies).

Elemental Ascendancy

27th level. Your command of the elements grows so complete that you no longer have to choose a single expression of it. You now have both options granted by Elemental Fury and Improved Elemental Fury, improved as follows.

Potent Spellcasting. Once on each of your turns when you deal damage with a Druid spell of 1st level or higher, you can add your Wisdom modifier to that damage.

Primal Strike. The extra damage of your Primal Strike increases to 3d8.

Master of Beasts

29th level. Your mastery of shapechanging reaches new heights. Your known forms increase by 2, and the maximum Challenge Rating for your forms increases by 2 (added to whatever maximum you already have from your class, subclass, and other features). Forms you adopt may now be Huge.

Apex Form

30th level. You can, as a Bonus Action, expend two uses of Wild Shape to instead take the form of a Primal Avatar: a towering, elemental-infused shape of your own design (DM's discretion on appearance) using the stat block of any Beast, Elemental, or Monstrosity with a Challenge Rating up to your Proficiency Bonus + 4 (CR 10 for most characters). While in this form, you retain the benefits of Greater Beast Spells and Elemental Ascendancy, and you gain temporary hit points equal to five times your prestige level. This form lasts for up to 10 minutes, until you drop to 0 hit points, or until you revert to your normal form as a Bonus Action.

You can use this feature once, and regain the ability to do so when you finish a Long Rest. If you've already used it, you can expend a spell slot of 8th level to use it again.

Evergreen Wild Shape Mastery

33rd level. You regain all expended uses of Wild Shape whenever you finish a Short Rest, in addition to your normal recovery.

Timeless Guardian

38th level. You have walked with nature long enough that its patience has become your own. You age at one-tenth the normal rate, have advantage on death saving throws, and gain resistance to necrotic damage.

World Tree

40th level. You have become a living conduit for nature's oldest and mightiest power. As a Bonus Action, you can cause a verdant grove to bloom across the ground in a 30-foot radius centered on you. The grove lasts for 1 minute, until you dismiss it (no action required), or until you use this feature again. While it persists:

  • The area is difficult terrain for enemies of your choice, but not for you or any creatures you choose.
  • At the start of each of your turns, you and up to five creatures you choose within the grove regain hit points equal to your Wisdom modifier + your Prestige level. Alternatively, you can instead deal that same amount of poison damage to a number of enemies of your choice within the grove (no save).
  • Ranged attacks made against a creature within the grove by an attacker outside it have disadvantage.

As a Bonus Action on later turns, while you are standing on natural terrain, you can teleport through the natural world to another point of natural terrain within 60 feet of your current position. If you aren't standing on natural terrain, you can instead teleport to any point within the grove. Either way, the grove's area then shifts to remain centered on you.

You can use this feature once, and regain the ability to do so when you finish a Long Rest.

At higher levels you conjure more daggers and make additional attacks: two daggers at 5th level, three at 11th level and four at 17th level. You can direct the daggers at the same target or at different ones, and you make a separate attack roll for each.

Magic Toggle

Magic Toggle

Casting Time: 1 minute (ritual)

Range: 30 feet

Components: V, S, M (a pinch of iron and cobalt powder worth at least 10 gp, which the spell consumes)

Duration: Until Dispelled

You implant a small repeatable magical mechanical force within a tiny object within range. When you do so, choose two rotational states relative to it's current rotation for the item to switch between. When the spell causes the item to switch between the two rotational states, it does so with the least required movement and can be designated to take anywhere from 1 second to 10 minutes. Finally, determine the circumstance that will trigger the spell to rotate the object.

When the circumstance occurs, the object rotates to the next or previous state (the second state when triggered for the first time). If an outside force or object would prevent the object from rotating, it stops harmlessly and that particular trigger is ignored. When you cast this spell, you can have the spell end after it returns to its original position, or it can remain and repeat its rotation whenever the trigger occurs.

The triggering circumstance can be as general or as detailed as you like, though it must be based on visual or audible conditions that occur within 30 feet of the object. For example, you could instruct a lock to automatically reset its rotation when the door is closed.

Homebrew / Spells

Memory Thief Sorcery (2024 Sorcerer)

Memory Thief Sorcery (2024 Sorcerer)

Memory Thief Sorcery (2024 Sorcerer)

The Memory Thief is a sorcerer touched by the silent weight of unspoken thoughts, lost truths, and stolen moments. Whether chosen by a god of shadows and secrets or born with the uncanny ability to pierce the veil of another’s mind, these sorcerers draw power not from raw elements—but from memory, emotion, and identity itself.

Every spell is an intrusion, every glance a chance to unravel another’s story. They are masters of mental trespass and psychic influence, collecting knowledge the way others collect coins. Some act as spies for hidden powers like Vhaeraun, gods of forbidden knowledge, or remnants of psionic empires. Others awaken to their abilities after surviving moments of profound trauma or divine contact—left able to steal what others cannot even remember.

"Thoughts and Emotions are the truest form of currency. I never pay full price." - Memory Thief

Playstyle and Motivations

The Memory Thief excels at subtle control, emotional manipulation, and deep utility in both narrative and combat play. With features that allow you to read and manipulate the thoughts and motivations of others, this subclass rewards strategic roleplay, creative problem-solving, and players who love to know more than they should.

  • Reclaim the Past: Seeking to recover a stolen or fragmented identity by stitching together memories from others.
  • Weaponize Secrets: Collecting powerful memories from kings, archmages, or ancient evils to manipulate the tides of history or blackmail enemies into silence.
  • Protect the Mindscape: Standing as a psychic guardian or counter-spy, exposing hidden corruption or breaking mind control through counter-manipulation.

Who Would Thrive as a Memory Thief?

The Memory Thief is perfect for players who want to:

  • Influence Story Through Subtlety: Gain leverage by collecting key memories, discovering hidden motives, or creating complex emotional bonds with NPCs.
  • Play with Identity and Perception: Use your magic to assume false roles, mimic memories, or veil your soul against detection.
  • Master Battlefield Presence Without Direct Violence: Weaken enemies emotionally, disrupt their thoughts, and track them across time and space.

Ideal Players and Characters

🧠 The Intrigue Manipulator

Players who thrive in espionage-heavy or social-intrigue campaigns, especially those who enjoy steering conversations with secrets and subtle leverage.

🕯 The Shadowed Seer

Players who love mysteries and clues, piecing together narrative threads from the minds of others, treating every memory like a breadcrumb on a hidden trail.

🎭 The Identity Shifter

Players who want to play with masks, personas, and the line between truth and falsehood—taking on aspects of others through their memories, voices, and fears.

Features:

  • 3rd Level - Umbral Spike
  • 6th Level - Thought Scribe
  • 14th Level - Hollow Mask
  • 18th Level - Dark One's Trespass

3rd Level - Umbral Spike

Once per turn when damaging a creature with a spell or attack, you can deal an additional 2d6 psychic damage and mark them. While the creature is marked, you know their direction and distance while they are within 90 ft of you, lasting up to 1 hour. You can spend sorcery points to extend the duration by an additional hour per sorcery point spent.

The extra damage increases at 6th (3d6) level, 14th (4d6) level, and 18th (5d6) level.

You can use this a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier, regaining all uses on a Long Rest, or by expending a spell slot for each use restored (no action required).

6th Level - Thought Scribe

When you cast a spell of 1st level or higher that forces a creature to make a saving throw, you can extract a thought strand (as with the Encode Thoughts cantrip) on a failure. Once you use this feature on a creature, you cannot use this feature on that target again until you complete a short or long rest.

The thought strand contains one memory of a significant event within the past 24 hours. Significant events typically involve powerful emotions, such as battles and betrayals, marriages and murders, births and funerals, or meetings with important friends or leaders. However, they might also include more mundane events that are nevertheless important to that creature.

In addition, while holding the thought strand, you can communicate telepathically with the target while they are on the same plane of existence as you. You can choose if they are able to respond or not.

14th Level - Hollow Mask

As a bonus action, you can spend 1 or more sorcery points to magically transform your essence for 10 minutes. For each sorcery point you spend, you can gain one of the following benefits of your choice, the effects of which last until the transformation ends:

  • You can see through solid objects to a range of 30 feet, and can see any invisible creatures to a range of 60 feet. Within that range you have advantage on checks made to find hidden creatures, traps, or secret doors for the duration of the transformation.
  • You cannot be detected or targeted by any divination magic, or perceived through magical scrying sensors unless you wish to be. If you choose to be affected, you can present false information to the divination magic or scrying sensor for the duration of the transformation.
  • You can choose a creature type other than your actual creature type. Spells and other magical effects treat you as if you were a creature of the chosen type. After the transformation expires, ongoing and future spells and magical effects treat you as your original creature type.
  • You have advantage on saving throws against effects which would cause you to be charmed, frightened, or possessed. If you succeed against such an effect, you have advantage on Charisma checks made against that source for the duration of the transformation.

18th Level - Dark One's Trespass

As an Action, you can force a target you can see within 60ft of you to make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC or be charmed or frightened (your choice) and you are able to detect the creatures surface thoughts and emotional state for up to 8 hours (those foremost in its mind, reflecting its current emotions and what it is actively thinking about). You can spend sorcery points to extend the duration by an additional hour per sorcery point spent. Alternatively, if you are holding a thought strand created by your Thought Scribe feature, you can target that creature as long as they are on the same plane of existence.

While charmed or frightened in this way, it undertakes to perform any services or activities you ask of it to the best of its ability. You can set the creature new tasks when a previous task is completed, or if you decide to end its current task. If the service or activity might cause harm to the creature, or if it conflicts with the creature's desires, the creature can make another Wisdom saving throw to try to end the effect. This save is made with advantage if you or your companions are fighting the creature. If the activity would result in certain death for the creature, the effect ends. During that time you can use a Bonus Action to see and hear through that creatures senses until the end of your next turn. You are blinded and deafened while this persists.

Once you use this Action, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest, unless you spend 7 sorcery points to use it again.

Phantom Ship Charm

Phantom Ship Charm

Wondrous item, very rare

Description

This small rusted anchor charm is bound to a cursed, lost ship: The Specter’s Breath. This ship and its crew were lost to the Ethereal Plane centuries ago, cursed to remain there and wander aimlessly until called back by an ancient relic charm. This small charm acts as the ship's tether to the Material Plane.

As an action, you can call out to the ship while holding the charm aloft. If you're within 30 feet of a body of water on the Material Plane, a full-sized anchor appears on the ground in an unoccupied space within 5 feet of the water. A wispy, gray chain appears on the anchor that extends into nothingness. After 1 minute, the Specter’s Breath emerges from the Ethereal Plane, pulled by the anchor's chain, and coming to rest in the water nearby. The ship is a longship 70 feet long and 20 feet wide. It's piloted by thirty-four crewmembers and five officers, all of whom are long-dead, ghostly remains of their former selves. They are formless and harmless, but are nevertheless visible and friendly to you and your companions. They can interact with the rigging, sails, and other equipment on the ship, but nothing else while they remain on the Material Plane. While the ship remains, it moves at a speed of 10 miles per hour, or half as much when there isn't any wind. Only you can command it and its crew while the charm is on your person.

The ship may be commanded for up to 10 days, after which you cannot summon it again until a further 10 days have passed.  Every day at dawn the ship and its crew begin to gradually fade over 10 minutes before they are returned to the Ethereal Plane. They may be resummoned the following dusk. The ship returns early if you speak the command phrase "Until the night calls once more," or if the ship takes enough damage that it would be destroyed. Anything not summoned with the ship is dropped into the water below the ship when it disappears.

Spirit Ejection

Description

You attempt to forcefully tear the spirit of a creature from its body, leaving it momentarily defenseless. Choose one humanoid creature within range (creatures under the effects of a spell, feature or magic item that wards them against Undead or possession cannot have their spirit ejected by this spell). The target must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failure, their spirit is ejected from their body and manifests as a spectral form within 10 feet of them. The target’s body becomes incapacitated, and has disadvantage on saving throws against effects that would possess them. The spirit resembles their mortal form in almost every way, replicating game statistics but not their possessions. Any damage or other effects that apply to your spirit or physical body affects the other. In addition, the spirit is incorporeal, resistant to all damage except psychic or radiant, and it must choose whether it gets a move, an action, or a bonus action on a turn; it gets only one of the three. The spirit is tethered to the body and cannot move more than 60 feet away from it.

At the start of each of the target’s turns, they can attempt a Wisdom saving throw to end the effect early. If they succeed, their spirit returns to their body, and they regain control at the start of their next turn.

If the body is reduced to 0 hit points while the spirit is still ejected, the creature dies instantly. If killed in this way, its spirit detaches from its corpse as a Specter under your control, the statistics of which are in the Monster Manual.

You can mentally command the Specter or any creature you made with this spell if the creature is within 60 feet of you (if you control multiple creatures, you can command any or all of them at the same time, issuing the same command to each one), and in combat the Specter shares your initiative count, but it takes its turn immediately after yours.

The Specter remains in your service for up to 10 days, at which point it vanishes to the afterlife. While the Specter is in your service, its soul is trapped and cannot be revived. A Remove Curse, Dispel Evil and Good, or Wish spell ends this spells effect.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 6th or 7th level or higher, the target has disadvantage on its initial saving throw. At 8th or 9th level, the target instead rises as a Poltergeist if killed.

You flood magic into your legs, allowing you to bound high into the air from a standstill. Your jump distance increases by 10 feet until the start of your next turn, and you can make a running high jump or a running long jump without a running start.

Task

Task

transmutation cantrip. (Bard (Legacy), Sorcerer (Legacy), Warlock (Legacy), Wizard (Legacy), Bard, Sorcerer, Warlock, Wizard)

Meta

  • Casting Time: 1 action
  • Range: 15 feet
  • Components: S
  • Duration: 1 hour

Description

With a flick of your wrist, you magically start the process of completing a small and simple task, such as flipping a book page, buttering bread, or heating a cup of tea, without any physical interaction. The task can't include anything that is intended to inflict a harmful effect on a creature and must be something you'd normally be able to accomplish without the use of magic. If the task would take longer than the duration (such as folding laundry, etc.), the task only progresses as far as it would within the hour. The spell fails if the target of the task has total cover from you.

If you cast this spell multiple times, you can have up to three tasks active at a time, and you can dismiss one of them as a bonus action.

Tenser

Tenser's Unbound Transformation

7th-level transmutation. (Wizard, Sorcerer, Warlock, College of Swords, College of Valor)

Meta

Casting Time: 1 action

Range: Self

Components: V, S, M (a few hairs from a bull)

Duration: Concentration, up to 10 minutes

Description

You endow yourself with endurance and martial prowess fueled by magic. Until the spell ends, you can't cast spells of 6th level or higher, and you gain two of the following benefits:

  • You gain 50 temporary hit points. If any of these remain when the spell ends, they are lost.
  • You have advantage on attack rolls that you make with simple and martial weapons.
  • When you hit a target with a weapon attack, that target takes an extra 2d12 force damage.
  • You have proficiency with shields, simple weapons, and martial weapons.
  • You have proficiency in Strength and Constitution saving throws.
  • You can attack twice, instead of once, when you take the Attack action on your - turn. You ignore this benefit if you already have a feature, like Extra Attack, that gives you extra attacks.

Immediately after the spell ends, you must succeed on a DC 15 Constitution saving throw or suffer one level of exhaustion.

At Higher Levels

When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 8th level or higher, you can choose an additional effect for every level above 7th.

The Aberrant Bloom

The Aberrant Bloom

Aberrant Mind. The thought and the spell were never separate things.

At PL 25 you choose a Weave; PL 29 and 33 branch within it; PL 37 gives your Weave's capstone.

Order Disciplines

Your Order grants these two disciplines at PL 21. They don't count against the number of disciplines you know, and no other Order can learn them.

Spell Graft

○ Focus. Your cantrips deal one additional damage die on a hit.

● Lance (3 psi) — Rider. Once per turn when you hit a creature or damage it with a spell, it makes an Intelligence save, taking 3d8 Psychic damage on a failure, half on a success.

●●● Grafted Casting (11 psi) — Magic action. Cast a spell of level 4 or lower that you know without expending a spell slot. If you choose, it deals Psychic damage instead of its normal type.

Writhing Form

○ Focus. You have a climbing speed equal to your walking speed and 5 ft of additional reach.

● Unspool (3 psi) — Bonus Action. Until the end of your next turn your reach increases by 15 ft, and you can Grapple at that range.

●● Wrong Anatomy (8 psi) — Bonus Action. For 1 minute you're immune to Critical Hits and have Resistance to Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage. No concentration.

PL 21: Woven Casting

+5 Sorcery Points, and you regain your Proficiency Bonus in them on a Short Rest. Once on each of your turns, when you cast a spell of level 1 or higher, you can activate one Reflex-band option as part of that same action.

PL 25: Choose a Weave (+2 Sorcery Points)

The Woven Mind

Fusion. When you cast a spell that targets a single creature, a Reflex-band option you activate this turn can target that creature without spending psi.

The Warped Word

Shaping. Every sorcerer spell you know of level 5 or lower counts as a Psionic Spell for the purpose of Psionic Sorcery. You can cast such a spell by spending Sorcery Points equal to its level, with no verbal, somatic, or material components — including materials that would be consumed, which the psionic casting supplies from nothing.

The Hungering Mind

Sustain. Once per turn when you damage a creature with a spell, regain Hit Points equal to twice the spell's level.

PL 29: Choose a Technique (+2 Sorcery Points)

Woven Mind

  • Resonant Weave. When you cast a spell of level 1 or higher, the first discipline you activate before the end of that turn costs 2 less psi, to a minimum of 0.
  • Dual Weave. Once per turn you can cast a cantrip as part of activating a discipline.

Warped Word

  • Reshape. When you cast a spell, you can change its damage type to Psychic or Force.
  • Displaced Casting. Your spells can originate from any point you can see within 60 ft. You must have a clear path to that point, and the spell's own range is measured from there.

Hungering Mind

  • Feed. When a creature dies within 60 ft of you, regain 2 Sorcery Points. Once per turn.
  • Siphon. When you reduce a creature to 0 Hit Points with a spell or discipline, gain Temporary Hit Points equal to your Prestige Level.

PL 33: Choose a Mastery (+2 Sorcery Points)

Woven Mind

  • Aberrant Reach. The range of your spells and disciplines increases by 30 ft and they ignore half and three-quarters cover.
  • Twin Manifestation. Once per turn, a Committed-band option you activate can target a second creature within range at no additional cost.

Warped Word

  • Unanswerable. Your spells and disciplines can't be counterspelled, dispelled, or detected as magic, and creatures have Disadvantage on the first saving throw they make against a spell of yours each combat.
  • Free Shaping. Once per turn you can apply one Metamagic option without spending Sorcery Points. You can't apply Quickened Spell or Twinned Spell this way.

Hungering Mind

  • Bloom. Enemies starting their turn within 10 ft take Psychic damage equal to your Psionic Ability modifier, and you regain that many Hit Points.
  • Consume Magic. When you end or counter a magical effect you did not create, regain Sorcery Points equal to its level.

PL 37: Weave Capstone (+2 Sorcery Points)

Woven Mind — Apotheosis of Mind. Once per Long Rest as a Bonus Action, for 1 minute: you can cast one spell of level 5 or lower as a Bonus Action on each of your turns, and your spells and disciplines ignore Resistance to Psychic and Force damage.

Warped Word — The Unwritten Word. Once per Long Rest as a Bonus Action, for 1 minute the shape of a spell stops constraining you. For the duration:

  • Every spell you cast can reshape its area into any form covering no more spaces than the original, and change its damage type to Psychic or Force.
  • The range of your spells increases by 60 ft.
  • The first time each turn a creature fails a saving throw against one of your spells, it takes additional Psychic damage equal to your Prestige Level.

This changes a spell's shape, not its rules. It never alters which ability a saving throw uses, a spell's level, or its casting time.

Hungering Mind — Devourer. Once per Long Rest as a Bonus Action, for 1 minute all damage you deal heals you for half the amount, and each enemy that fails a saving throw against you gives you 2 Sorcery Points.

The Bird of Prey Form

The Bird of Prey Form

Hollowed bone and spread pinion. A frame stripped of everything that isn't lift, ending in feet built to close on something and not open again. Bird of prey in shape, if not in species.

Baseline — Wind-Gripped

  • Open Sky: You gain a Fly Speed equal to half your Speed. While in Hybrid Shape, it becomes equal to your full Speed and you can hover.
  • Far Sight: You have advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks relying on sight and on Initiative rolls, and you can see clearly up to 1 mile with no penalty for distance.

Signature — Stoop (2 Primal Points)

  • Dive: As part of your Attack action, drop up to 60 feet in a straight line and make a melee attack. On a hit, add three Martial Arts dice of damage.
  • Carry Off: The target must succeed on a Strength saving throw against your save DC or be carried with you up to 20 feet in any direction and knocked Prone when released.

PL 25 — Bird of Prey Branches

Choose one: The Stooping Death, The Stormwing, or The Sky Sovereign.

The Stooping Death

Opener — Sky's Advantage: You don't provoke Opportunity Attacks while flying, and any creature that is Prone, falling, or has no Fly Speed grants you advantage on attack rolls while you are airborne.

PL 30 — choose one:

  • Terminal Velocity: Stoop adds one additional Martial Arts die for every 20 feet you dove, to a maximum of six total.
  • Wingover: After a Stoop, you can immediately fly up to half your Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks.

PL 35 — choose one:

  • Broken on Impact: A creature hit by Stoop has its Speed reduced to 0 until the end of its next turn and cannot take Reactions during that time.
  • Falling Star: When you end a Stoop, you can cast a spell with a casting time of an action as a Bonus Action. Once per Short or Long Rest.

PL 40 — Capstone: The Falling Sky: Stoop costs 1 Primal Point, can be used as a Bonus Action, and your Fly Speed doubles. Any creature you drop from any height takes falling damage as if it had fallen twice the actual distance.

The Stormwing

Opener — Cyclone: As an Action, spend 2 Primal Points to raise a 30-foot-radius storm around you for 1 minute. It is Difficult Terrain for creatures without a Fly Speed, ranged attacks through it have disadvantage, and creatures entering or starting their turn in it make a Strength saving throw against your save DC or are pushed 15 feet and knocked Prone.

PL 30 — choose one:

  • Eye of the Storm: You and allies you choose are unaffected by your Cyclone and can fly at half Speed within it.
  • Howling Winds: Creatures in your Cyclone are Deafened and cannot cast spells with Verbal components.

PL 35 — choose one:

  • Gathering Front: Cyclone's radius becomes 60 feet, and it moves with you.
  • Storm's Conduit: While your Cyclone is active, spells you cast that deal Lightning or Thunder damage add your Wisdom modifier to their damage, and their range doubles within the storm.

PL 40 — Capstone: Weather Front: Cyclone costs nothing, lasts until you dismiss it, and requires no Action to raise. Once per round you can direct a stroke of lightning at any creature within it, dealing four Martial Arts dice of Lightning damage.

The Sky Sovereign

Opener — Talon Grip: When you hit a Large or smaller creature with a melee attack, spend 1 Primal Point to Grapple it as part of the attack. It moves with you when you fly, has disadvantage on attacks against anyone but you, and takes your Martial Arts die at the start of each of its turns.

PL 30 — choose one:

  • Iron Grip: You can Grapple Huge creatures. A creature you Grapple has disadvantage on checks to escape, and takes two Martial Arts dice instead of one at the start of each of its turns.
  • Two Talons: You can maintain Talon Grip on two creatures at once.

PL 35 — choose one:

  • Drop: Releasing a Grappled creature while airborne deals falling damage and forces a Constitution save against your save DC or the creature is Stunned until the end of its next turn.
  • Weightless Casting: You can cast spells with Somatic components while Grappling a creature, and creatures you Grapple have disadvantage on saving throws against your spells.

PL 40 — Capstone: Nothing Below Is Safe: Talon Grip costs nothing and can seize a creature of any size. While you hold a creature aloft, it cannot be targeted by its allies' spells or abilities, and you can carry it at full Fly Speed without penalty.

The Canine Form

The Canine Form

Long-limbed and deep-chested. Digitigrade legs, a jaw built for closing distance and refusing to let go. Canine in silhouette, whatever the details.

Baseline — Tireless Gait

  • Relentless Stride: Your Speed increases by 15 feet and you ignore Difficult Terrain. The first time you move at least 20 feet toward a creature on your turn, your next melee attack against it before the end of that turn deals additional damage equal to your Martial Arts die.
  • Hunter's Nose: You gain Blindsight out to 30 feet via scent, you have advantage on Constitution saving throws made to avoid Exhaustion, and you can track a creature you've smelled within the last 24 hours with advantage.

Signature — Run Down (1 Primal Point)

  • Give Chase: As a Reaction when a creature within 60 feet of you moves, takes the Disengage action, or is reduced to half its Hit Points or fewer, you move up to your Speed toward it without provoking Opportunity Attacks.
  • Snap: If you end that movement within reach of the triggering creature, you can make one melee attack against it.

PL 25 — Canine Branches

Choose one: The Pack Leader, The Relentless, or The Tracker.

The Pack Leader

Opener — Shared Instinct: Allies within 30 feet of you add your Wisdom modifier to Initiative rolls. When you use Run Down, one willing ally within 30 feet may also move up to half their Speed as part of your Reaction.

PL 30 — choose one:

  • Drive the Quarry: Allies scoring attacks against a creature you moved toward this turn score critical hits on a roll of 19–20.
  • Herd: When an ally hits a creature within your reach, you can move that creature up to 10 feet to a space you choose.

PL 35 — choose one:

PL 40 — Capstone: Alpha: Allies within 30 feet gain your Tireless Gait Speed bonus and ignore Difficult Terrain. Run Down no longer costs a Primal Point and can be used twice per round. When you or an ally within 30 feet hits a creature you moved toward this turn, that attack deals additional damage equal to your Martial Arts die.

The Relentless

Opener — Hamstring: When you hit a creature with a melee attack, you can reduce its Speed by 15 feet until the start of your next turn. If its Speed reaches 0 this way, it falls Prone.

PL 30 — choose one:

  • Worry the Wound: A creature whose Speed you reduced this turn has disadvantage on the first attack roll it makes before the start of your next turn.
  • Long Wind: You can take the Dash action twice per turn, and you ignore the first 30 feet of any forced movement imposed on you.

PL 35 — choose one:

  • Closing Jaws: Your first melee attack each turn against a creature whose Speed is 0, that is Prone, or that you moved at least 20 feet toward deals additional damage equal to two Martial Arts dice.
  • Hounding Magic: When a creature fails a saving throw against a spell you cast, its Speed becomes 0 until the end of its next turn and it cannot teleport during that time.

PL 40 — Capstone: Nowhere to Go: No creature can take the Dash or Disengage action within 30 feet of you without first succeeding on a Wisdom saving throw against your save DC; on a failure, the action is wasted. Any creature whose Speed you have reduced to 0 takes damage equal to two Martial Arts dice at the start of each of its turns while it remains within 30 feet of you.

The Tracker

Opener — Deep Scent: Your scent Blindsight extends to 60 feet, and you know the exact direction and distance to any creature you have scented within the last 24 hours.

PL 30 — choose one:

  • Never Lost: You always know the way back to any place you have been, and you cannot be magically deceived about direction, distance, or location.
  • Run It Down: As a Bonus Action, name a creature you have scented within 60 feet. Until the end of your next turn you know its location, ignore any cover it has, and your attacks against it cannot miss due to concealment, invisibility, or illusion.

PL 35 — choose one:

  • Quarry's Curse: Once per turn, when you cast a spell targeting a creature you have scented, you can force it to reroll one successful saving throw against that spell, using the new result.
  • Cut Off: When a creature you have scented attempts to teleport or planeshift, you can spend 2 Primal Points to force a Charisma saving throw against your save DC; on a failure, the effect fails and is wasted.

PL 40 — Capstone: The Hunt Ends Where I Say: Your scent Blindsight extends to 120 feet and pierces invisibility, illusion, and shapechange. A creature you have scented cannot hide from you by any means, has disadvantage on saving throws against your spells and features, and takes additional damage equal to two Martial Arts dice the first time you hit it each turn.

The Feline Form

The Feline Form

Coiled and silent. Retractable claws, a spine that stores tension like a drawn bow, eyes that resolve detail in near-total dark. Feline in build, though not necessarily in kind.

  • Soundless: You have a Climb Speed equal to your Speed and can move across ceilings and vertical surfaces without a check. PL 25 — Feline Branches

Choose one: The Ambusher, The Shadow, or The Ripper.

The Ambusher

Opener — Patient Blood: You have advantage on attack rolls against any creature that hasn't taken a turn yet this combat, and against any creature that can't see you.

PL 30 — choose one:

  • Nowhere and Everywhere: While Invisible, your Speed doubles and you leave no tracks, scent, or trace of passage.

Homebrew / Spells

The Whetstone

The Whetstone

Soulknife. Thought sharpened until it cuts.

The Whetstone branches. At PL 25 you choose an Edge; at PL 29 and 33 you choose within it; at PL 37 your Edge gives its capstone. Each choice is permanent.

PL 21: Edged Thought

You alone may choose Dexterity as your Psionic Ability. A Soulknife's power was never seated in the intellect; it lives in the hand and the reflex.

Order Disciplines

Your Order grants these two disciplines at PL 21. They don't count against the number of disciplines you know, and no other Order can learn them.

Edge of Thought

○ Focus. Your Psychic Blades don't vanish at the end of your turn, and you can manifest them again with no action.

● Whetted (3 psi) — Rider. Once per turn when you hit with a blade, the target's Armor Class drops by 1 until the end of your next turn, stacking to 3.

●● Blade Chorus (7 psi) — Bonus Action. Make one blade attack against each of up to three creatures within 5 ft of you.

Killing Silence

○ Focus. You have Advantage on Initiative, and a creature you damage can't speak, shout, or cast spells with verbal components until the end of your next turn.

● Unseen Edge (4 psi) — Bonus Action. Until the end of your turn, your blade attacks against creatures that can't see you deal an extra 2d12 damage.

●●● The Quiet Between (12 psi) — Magic action. One creature within 30 ft makes a Constitution save. On a failure it takes 12d12 Psychic damage and is Stunned until the end of your next turn. If this reduces it to 0 Hit Points, it falls without a sound and no other creature notices for 1 minute.

PL 21: Ascendant Blades

+4 Psionic Energy Dice, and you regain your Proficiency Bonus in them on a Short Rest. Your Psychic Blades deal 1d12 Psychic damage, rising to 2d6 at PL 33, and gain the Light property.

PL 25: Choose an Edge (+2 dice)

The Thrown Edge

Range. Your Psychic Blades' thrown range becomes 120/240 ft, and you can originate a thrown blade from any point within 30 ft of you.

The Close Edge

Melee. Your blades gain the Nick property. When you hit with a blade in melee, you gain +1 AC until the start of your next turn, stacking up to +3.

Nick and Psychic Blades. Your Soulknife's Bonus Action blade attack and the Light property's extra attack are the same attack, not two separate ones. Nick lets you make that attack as part of your Attack action instead of as a Bonus Action, once per turn. It does not grant an extra attack — what it buys you is your Bonus Action back, which on this class is the scarcest thing you have. It still uses the smaller blade die.

The Quiet Edge

Strategy. When you deal Sneak Attack damage with your Psychic Blade, you can also deal Sneak Attack damage with the blade you use as a Bonus Action on the same turn. The Bonus Action blade uses half as many Sneak Attack dice, rounded down.

Note. The Close Edge and the Quiet Edge don't combine — they're different branches, and you choose one at PL 25. A Quiet Edge Soulknife keeps the standard Bonus Action blade attack and gets a second helping of Sneak Attack from it; a Close Edge Soulknife gets Nick and can fold that attack into the Attack action, but has no second Sneak Attack to apply to it.

PL 29: Choose a Technique (+2 dice)

If you took the Thrown Edge

  • Splitting Throw. When a thrown blade hits, it ricochets to a second creature within 30 ft of the first; make a separate attack roll against it.
  • Down the Blade. You have no Disadvantage on thrown blade attacks at long range, and you deal an extra 1d12 damage to creatures at least 60 ft away.

If you took the Close Edge

  • Whirl. When you take the Attack action, you can make one additional blade attack against a different creature within 5 ft of you.
  • Riposte. When a creature within 5 ft misses you with an attack, you can use your Reaction to make one blade attack against it.

If you took the Quiet Edge

  • Mark the Opening. As a Bonus Action, mark a creature within 60 ft. Until the end of your next turn, attacks against it by you or your allies have Advantage.
  • Vanishing Act. Immediately after you deal Sneak Attack damage, you can teleport up to 30 ft and become Invisible until the end of your turn.

PL 33: Choose a Mastery (+2 dice)

Thrown Edge

  • Storm of Edges. As a Magic action, throw a blade at each of up to your Proficiency Bonus in creatures you can see within 120 ft.
  • Piercing Line. As a Magic action, hurl a blade in a 60-ft line. Each creature makes a Dexterity save, taking 8d12 Psychic damage on a failure, half on a success.

Close Edge

  • Rending Thought. Once per turn, when you hit a creature that has already taken damage from you this turn, add one roll of your Manifestation Die to the damage.
  • Bladelock. When you hit a creature with a melee blade, it makes a Strength save or is Restrained by psychic edges until the end of your next turn.

Quiet Edge

  • Sever. Once per turn when you hit with a blade, expend a Psionic Energy Die: the target makes a Constitution save or takes maximum damage from the attack and can regain no Hit Points for 1 minute.
  • Read the Room. At the start of combat, you know the Armor Class and current Hit Points of every creature you can see, and you have Advantage on attacks against any creature that has not yet acted.

PL 37: Edge Capstone (+2 dice)

Thrown Edge — Blade Beyond Distance. Twice per turn you can attack with your Psychic Blades against any creature you can see within 120 ft, ignoring cover and any AC bonus from cover or shields.

Close Edge — Unmaking Cut. Once per turn when you hit a creature in melee, it makes a Constitution save. On a failure it takes an extra 6d12 Psychic damage and its Armor Class is reduced by 2 until the end of the encounter, stacking.

Quiet Edge — The Perfect Kill. Once per Long Rest, when you hit a creature that is unaware of you or that you have Advantage against, the attack is a Critical Hit and you roll maximum Sneak Attack damage.

Thought Forms

Thought Forms

7th-level transmutation. (Cleric, Druid, Sorcerer, Wizard)

Meta

Casting Time: 1 action

Range: Self (30 ft. sphere)

Components: V, S, M ((a gemstone worth at least 5,000gp, which the spell consumes))

Duration: Concentration, up to 1 minute

Description

Through carefully crafted thought projections and the transmutation of mental energies, you create a field of potentiality around you, exceeding your normal limitations. When you cast this spell you create 6 Thought Forms. You can consume these Thought Forms in a number of ways, granting additional benefits depending on your choice:

  • When you or a friendly creature within 30 feet of you misses with an attack, you can consume any number of Thought Form. They gain a +2 bonus to the attack roll equal to the number of Thought Forms consumed, potentially turning the miss into a hit.
  • Once per turn, when you or a friendly creature within 30 feet of you take the Attack action, you can consume 2 Thought Forms to allow them to make an additional attack as part of that same action.
  • When you or a friendly creature within 30 feet of you take damage from an attack, you can consume any number of Thought Forms as a reaction, granting them 10 temporary hit points for each Thought Form consumed. These temporary hit points last until the start of your next turn.
  • When you or a friendly creature within 30 feet of you fails a saving throw against a spell or magical effect, you can use your reaction to consume any number of your Thought Forms. They gain a +2 bonus to your saving throw for each Thought Form consumed, potentially turning the failure into a success.

As a bonus action on your turn, you can expend an unused spell slot to create a number of Thought Forms equal to the level of the spell slot expended, up to a maximum of 6.

Meta

You place a curse on a creature that you can see within range, forcing them to make a Wisdom saving throw or be cursed for the duration. While cursed, you are aware of the target's surface thoughts and emotional state, and can communicate telepathically with them.

Once on each of your turns when you hit the target with an attack or they fail a saving throw against a spell or magical effect originating from you, it deals an additional 5d6 psychic damage in addition to its other effects, and you become Vindicated, gaining advantage on the next attack roll, saving throw, or ability check (your choice) you make before the end of your next turn.

Once on each of the target's turns when they miss you with an attack or you succeed on a saving throw against a spell or magical effect originating from them, it takes 5d6 psychic damage and they become Discouraged, gaining disadvantage on the next attack roll, saving throw, or ability check (your choice) they make before the end of their next turn.

At Higher Levels

When casting this spell with a spell slot of 8th level or higher, you can target one additional creature for each spell slot level above 7th.

Transdimensional Expansion

Transdimensional Expansion

8th-level conjuration. (College of Creation, Sorcerer, Wizard)

Meta

Casting Time: 1 hour

Range: 100 feet

Components: V, S, M (1,000 gp worth of Residuum or any Arcane Dust/Powder)

Duration: 24 hours

Description

You magically expand the dimensions of an existing container, room, or otherwise fully enclosed space beyond its physical limits. Select an existing physical space (no larger than 125 sq ft.) with at most one single point of entry such as a lid, door, window or flap, (no larger than 10 sq ft), and with a solid border (no transparent walls, windows, etc.). As a part of this spell, the caster must inscribe runes around the opening and the borders of the space to maintain its external structure. The interior dimensions of that space expand by up to 5 feet in any direction that you choose as the spell takes effect, warping to accommodate any items or creatures inside.

When the spell ends, the space returns to its normal size and any items or occupants unable to fit in the original space are softly ejected through the opening. Casting this spell in the same space every day for 30 days makes the effect permanent; further castings can be used to expand an existing Transdimensional Space beyond its size provided that it still has a single exterior border with no more than one point of entry.

True Awaken

True Awaken

Casting Time: 8 hours

Range: Touch

Components: V, S, M (clay and runes worth 2,000 gp, consumed)

Duration: Instantaneous

You awaken the mind of a creature, granting it sentience and self-awareness. Choose one non-hostile creature you touch.

You can have a number of creatures awakened by this spell equal to your spellcasting ability modifier (minimum of one). If casting this spell would exceed your limit, the creature awakened longest ago immediately loses all benefits of True Awaken.

Restrictions:

This spell automatically fails if the target is summoned or maintained by a concentration spell, is planar bound, has Legendary Resistance, or has an Intelligence score of 10 or higher.

Limitations:

This spell grants no combat benefits, proficiencies, spellcasting, or CR increases. It does not remove or alter magical control already affecting the creature, and it does not restore lost memories or identity.

Creation:

Spell is created by Momo's Character Daemos

Homebrew / Spells

Undead Warlock 2024

Undead Warlock 2024

Undead Warlock 2024

You've made a pact with a deathless being, a creature that defies the cycle and life and death, forsaking its mortal shell so it might eternally pursue its unfathomable ambitions. For such beings, time and morality are fleeting things, the concerns of those for whom grains of sand still rush through life's hourglass. Having once been mortal themselves, these ancient undead know firsthand the paths of ambition and the routes past the doors of death. They eagerly share this profane knowledge, along with other secrets, with those who work their will among the living. Beings of this type include the demilich Acererak, the vampire tyrant Kas the Bloody-Handed, the githyanki lich-queen Vlaakith, the dracolich Dragotha, the undead pharaoh Ankhtepot, and the elusive Darklord, Azalin Rex.

Features:

  • Expanded Spell List
  • 3rd Level - Form of Dread
  • 6th Level - Grave Touched
  • 10th Level - Necrotic Husk
  • Spirit Projection

Expanded Spell List

3rd-level Undead feature

When you reach a Warlock level specified in the Undead Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells available and it doesn't count towards your amount of warlock spells known.

3rd Level - Form of Dread

3rd-level Undead feature You manifest an aspect of your patron's dreadful power. As a bonus action, you transform for 1 minute. You gain the following benefits while transformed:

  • You gain temporary hit points equal to 1d10 + your warlock level.,
  • Once during each of your turns, when you hit a creature with an attack roll, you can force it to make a Wisdom saving throw, and if the saving throw fails, the target is frightened of you until the end of your next turn.,
  • You are immune to the frightened condition.,You can transform a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest. The appearance of your Form of Dread reflects some aspect of your patron. For example, your form could be a shroud of shadows forming the crown and robes of your lich patron, or your body might glow with glyphs from ancient funerary rites and be surrounded by desert winds, suggesting your mummy patron.

6th Level - Grave Touched

6th-level Undead feature Your patron's powers have a profound effect on your body and magic. You don't need to eat, drink, or breathe. In addition, once during each of your turns, when you hit a creature with an attack roll and roll damage against the creature, you can replace the damage type with necrotic damage. While you are using your Form of Dread, you can roll one additional damage die when determining the necrotic damage the target takes.

10th Level - Necrotic Husk

10th-level Undead feature

Your connection to undeath and necrotic energy now saturates your body. You have resistance to necrotic damage. If you are transformed using your Form of Dread, you instead become immune to necrotic damage. In addition, when you would be reduced to 0 hit points, you can use your reaction to retore your hit points to twice your warlock level instead and cause your body to erupt with deathly energy. Each creature of your choice that is within 30 feet of you takes necrotic damage equal to 2d10 + your warlock level. You then gain 1 level of exhaustion. Once you use this reaction, you can't do so again until you finish 1d4 long rests.

Spirit Projection

Your spirit can become untethered from your physical form. As an action, you can project your spirit from your body. The body you leave behind is unconscious and in a state of suspended animation. Your spirit resembles your mortal form in almost every way, replicating your game statistics but not your possessions. Any damage or other effects that apply to your spirit or physical body affects the other. Your spirit can remain outside your body for up to 1 hour. When your projection ends, your spirit returns to your body or your body magically teleports to your spirit's space (your choice). While projecting your spirit, you gain the following benefits:

  • Your spirit and body gain resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage.,
  • When you cast a spell of the conjuration or necromancy school, the spell doesn't require verbal or somatic components or material components that lack a gold cost.,
  • You have a flying speed equal to your walking speed and can hover. You can move through creatures and objects as if they were difficult terrain, but you take 1d10 force damage if you end your turn inside a creature or an object.,
  • While you are using your Form of Dread, once during each of your turns when you deal necrotic damage to a creature, you regain hit points equal to half the amount of necrotic damage dealt.,

Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a long rest or by expending a Pact slot.
