Homebrew / Subclasses

Augmenter

Augmenter

Augmenter

The Augmenter is a unique blend of artificer and psychic, merging technology with mental prowess. These specialists understand the psyche and wield their own bodies as tools for both combat and manipulation. Whether augmenting their limbs or delving into the minds of others, Augmenters are masters of self-enhancement

Features:

  • 3rd Level - Augmenter Spells
  • 3rd Level - Self Augmentation
  • 5th Level - Extra Attack
  • 9th Level - Mind Over Matter
  • 15th Level - Master Augmenter
  • Augmenter Infusions

3rd Level - Augmenter Spells

You always have certain spells prepared after you reach particular levels in this class, as shown in the Augmenter Spells table. These spells count as artificer spells for you, but they don’t count against the number of artificer spells you prepare.

Augmenter Spells reflect your understanding of the psyche and allows you to influence the mind of others.

Augmenter Spells

3rd Level - Command, Dissonant Whispers

5th Level - Tasha’s Mind Whip, Crown of Madness

9th Level - Antagonize, Fast Friends

13th Level - Raulothim’s Psychic Lance, Compulsion

17th Level - Synaptic Static, Modify Memory

3rd Level - Self Augmentation

Starting at 3rd level, you master the technique of augmenting your own body. Each of the following parts of your body can be infused using your artificer Infusions; Torso, Head, Legs. You also gain access to Augmenter Infusions, these infusions are known and does not count toward your total of known infusions. For the purposes of normal Infusions, the Torso is seen as Armor, head as a Helmet or any peripheral that is worn on the head, and legs are seen as boots.

You also learn how to augment your arms with special arm weapons. These can also be infused, and you can only have one arm enhancement active at a time. Whenever you finish a long rest you can swap arm enhancements.

Arm Enhancements

These Enhancements count as weapons and infusions can be applied to them. Each enhancement grants the artificer an applicable fighting Style based on the installed enhancement.

Mantis Blade

You gain retractable blade attachments on either of your arms

Properties: Finesse

Fighting Style: Dueling

Damage: 1d6 piercing

Special: The blade can be retracted or unsheathed as a bonus action, leaving the hand free to wield other items. When you score a critical hit with the mantis blade the target needs to make a constitution save against your Spell DC or start to bleed. When bleeding the target loses hp equal to your proficiency bonus at the start of each of its turn. It can make the save again at the end of each turn.

Monowire Attachment

These fine wires get pulled from your wrists and are wielded like a whip.

Properties: Finesse, Reach

Fighting Style: Two-Weapon Fighting

Damage: 1d4 slashing

Special: The wires count as two separate weapons for the purpose of two weapon fighting, but only require a single infusion. The wires use Intelligence for its attack and damage modifiers.

Gorilla Arms

Your Hands and forearms are augmented with heavier metals and mechanical support.

Properties: Heavy

Fighting Style: Unarmed Fighting

Damage: Unarmed Strike, Bludgeoning

Special: You make your attacks with the Gorilla Arms as unarmed strikes. You also have advantage on Strength( Athletics) checks to escape, attempt, maintain grapples.

Arm Launcher

You can load bolts or sling bullets into your arm and fire them as projectiles.

Properties: Ranged (40/80), Reload (6)

Fighting Style: Archery

Damage: 1d8 piercing (bolts), bludgeoning (sling bullets)

Special: The Launcher leaves your hands open while firing. On a hit, the launcher does 1d4 force damage to the target, all creatures within 5ft of the target must make Dexterity save against your spell save DC or take 1d4 force damage.

5th Level - Extra Attack

Beginning at 5th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

9th Level - Mind Over Matter

At 9th level, your deep understanding of the mind allows you to manipulate the physical world with your thoughts. You gain the following abilities:

  • Mental Shield: You gain resistance to psychic damage. Additionally, when you take psychic damage, you can use your reaction to reflect half of that damage back to the attacker.
  • Psychic Insight: You can use your action to read the surface thoughts of a creature you can see within 30 feet. This effect lasts for 1 minute, and the target must make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, you can also implant a simple suggestion (as per the Suggestion spell) into their mind. This ability can be used once per short rest.

15th Level - Master Augmenter

At 15th Level your ability to enhance your augmentations has reached unparalleled heights:

  • You can now add 2 infusions to any of your augmentations.
  • You are able to use master properties for your arm augmentations. Each arm augmentation has two possible properties. When you switch out your arm augmentation you can choose which master property to use.
    • Mantis Blades: Graze, Sap
    • Monowire: Nick, Slow
    • Gorilla Arms: Sap, Push
    • Arm Launcher: Push, Vex

Augmenter Infusions

Subdermal armor - 3rd Level, Torso

Prerequisite: 3rd Level Augmenter, Unarmored

Item: Torso Augmentation (requires Attunement)

Effect: Your skin is reinforced with a layer of protective material, making you more resilient to physical attacks. Subdermal Armor makes the wearer’s AC equal 10 + Constitution Modifier + Intelligence Modifier

Chameleon Skin - 3rd Level, Torso

Prerequisite: 3rd Level Augmenter

Item: Torso Augmentation (requires Attunement)

Effect: You can use an action to blend into your surroundings, gaining advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks for 1 hour. This ability can be used once per short or long rest.

Instant Disguise - 3rd Level, Torso

Prerequisite: 3rd Level Augmenter

Item: Torso Augmentation (requires Attunement)

Effect: A sophisticated system of micro-projectors and sensors enables you to alter your appearance at will. As a bonus action you can cast the Disguise self spell on yourself, without spending a spell slot. This ability can be used a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once) per long rest.

Enhanced Sight - 3rd Level, Head

Prerequisite: 3rd Level Augmenter

Item: Head Augmentation

Effect: You gain proficiency in the perception skill, and can use Intelligence instead of Wisdom for Passive perception and perception checks

Cat Eyes - 3rd Level, Head

Prerequisite: 3rd Level Augmenter

Item: Head Augmentation

Effect: You gain dark vision out to 60 feet, if you already have dark vision from another source, its range is extended by 60 feet.

Alluring Visage - 3rd Level, Head

Prerequisite: 3rd Level Augmenter

Item: Head Augmentation

Effect: The infusion highlights your positive features and filters your words, making you sound and look more alluring than you are. You can add your Intelligence modifier to any charisma(persuasion) check you make against a single target.

Fortified Ankles - 3rd Level, Leg

Prerequisite: 3rd Level Augmenter

Item: Leg Augmentation

Effect: You gain a +10 feet to your walking speed, and your high and long jump distances are doubled.

Lynx Paws - 3rd Level, Leg

Prerequisite: 3rd Level Augmenter

Item: Leg Augmentation

Effect: Your footfalls are dampened allowing for silent movement. You gain advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks. Damage taken from falling is halved.

Swift Step - 3rd Level, Leg

Prerequisite: 3rd Level Augmenter

Item: Leg Augmentation.

Effect: You can take the dodge action as a bonus action. This ability can be used a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once) per long rest.

Blood Pump - 6th Level, Special

Prerequisite: 6th Level Augmenter

Item: Special Augmentation (requires attunement)

Effect: After finishing a short rest you can load any magical potion into the pump. You can then as a reaction to taking damage, prior to taking damage or making an attack inject the potion to activate its effect. Once activated the potion is consumed.

Arcane Shielding - 6th Level, Special

Prerequisite: 6th Level Augmenter

Item: Special Augmentation (requires attunement)

Effect: When you are hit by a melee attack, you can use your reaction to cast Shield without expending a spell slot. This ability can be used a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once) per long rest.

Healing Nanobots - 6th Level, Special

Prerequisite: 6th Level Augmenter

Item: Special Augmentation (requires attunement)

Effect: As a bonus action, you can release nanobots that heal a creature you touch for 2d8 + your Intelligence modifier hit points. This ability can be used a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once) per long rest.

Psychic Blades - 10th Level, Arm

Prerequisite: 10th Level Augmenter

Item: Mantis Blade

Effect: When you hit a creature with the Mantis Blades, you can choose to deal an additional 2d6 psychic damage. This ability can be used a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once) per long rest.

Entangling Wires - 10th Level, Arm

Prerequisite: 10th Level Augmenter

Item: Monowire Attachment

Effect: When you hit a creature with the Monowire Attachment, you can choose to restrain the target. The target must make a Strength saving throw against your spell save DC or be restrained until the end of your next turn. This ability can be used a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once) per long rest.

Impact Fists - 10th Level, Arm

Prerequisite: 10th Level Augmenter

Item: Gorilla Arms

Effect: When you hit a creature with an unarmed strike, you can choose to knock the target prone. The target must make a Strength saving throw against your spell save DC or be knocked prone. This ability can be used a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once) per long rest.

Targeting Reticle - 10th Level, Arm

Prerequisite: 10th Level Augmenter

Item: Arm Launcher

Effect: You gain a +4 bonus to attack rolls with the Arm Launcher. Additionally, you can use your reaction to impose disadvantage on a ranged attack made against you.

Optical Camo - 14th Level, Torso

Prerequisite: 14th Level Augmenter

Item: Torso Augmentation (requires attunement)

Effect: Advanced optical technology allows you to blend into your surroundings, becoming nearly invisible. As a bonus action you become invisible until the end of your next turn, or until you take damage from any source. This ability can be used a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once) per long rest.

Reactive Coil - 14th Level, Head

Prerequisite: 14th Level Augmenter

Item: Head Augmentation (requires attunement)

Effect: When you are hit by a melee attack, you can use your reaction to deal 1d6 lightning damage to the attacker. This damage increases to 2d6 if the attacker is wearing metal armor.

Hydraulic Jumps - 14th Level, Leg

Prerequisite: 14th Level Augmenter

Item: Leg Augmentation (requires attunement)

Effect: You can use a bonus action to jump up to 30 feet in any direction. If you land within 5 feet of an enemy, you can make a melee attack as part of the same bonus action.

Homebrew / Subclasses

Avenger

Avenger

Avengers seek to right a wrong, stopping at nothing to correct a past sleight. They dole out their revenge with their own hands, using steel just as much as spirit to forward their goals.

Soul of Vengeance

At 3rd level, you gain proficiency with medium armor, shields, and martial weapons, and you can use weapons as your spiritual focus. When you activate your spirit tether, you gain an amount of temporary hit points equal to 1d6 + half your spiritualist level (rounded down).

Avenger Arts

Also at 3rd level, you gain access to new spirit arts that reflect your soul’s hunger for vengeance.

Duel of the Fates

As an action, you can spend 1 spirit point to initiate a spirit duel with your target. The target must make a Charisma saving throw or be blinded. While the target is blinded this way, you are also blinded, except you and your target can still see each other normally. As long as this blindness persists, your weapon attacks deal an additional 1d6 damage.

Spirit Shield

When you are attacked by your tethered target while you are holding a shield, you can use your reaction to spend 1 spirit point and force the target to make a Charisma saving throw. On a failure, the attack misses, and the next attack you make against the tethered target has advantage.

Phantom Pain

As an action, you can spend 2 spirit points to share your suffering with the tethered target. For the next minute, whenever you take damage, the target takes half as much necrotic damage.

Extra Attack

Beginning at 6th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn. Moreover, you can use a spirit art that uses an action in place of one of these attacks.

Avenging Link

At 13th level, your soul lashes out at any creature that would harm you or your allies. Whenever a creature you can see within range of your spirit tether damages you or an ally within 30 feet, you can use your reaction to immediately create a spirit tether. The creature must be one of the targets.

Master Avenger

At 18th level, you master the art of vengeance. You learn the following spirit art:

Soul Coating

You can use 5 spirit points as an action to empower your weapon. For the next minute, whenever you hit a tethered target with a weapon attack, the attack deals an additional 3d6 force damage. The first time you hit a tethered target after using this art, it must make a Charisma saving throw. On a failure, the target is rended by your spirit, and cannot restore hit points or gain temporary hit points as long as your spirit tether lasts.

Homebrew / Subclasses

Barrow Lord

Barrow Lord

Barrow Lord

Command a Retinue of the Restless Dead

Barrow Lords call upon the dead as readily as the living, commanding the risen as soldiers and sending them into battle without hesitation. The dead may be mindless, but the habits of service endure long after the flesh has failed.

Features:

  • 3rd Level - Dread Retinue
  • 3rd Level - Grave Tithe
  • 7th Level - Formations
  • 10th Level - Disposable Forces
  • 15th Level - Deathly Drills
  • 18th Level - Grasp of the Starved
  • Barrow Thrall

3rd Level - Dread Retinue

You can call the dead from the earth to serve you. Your retinue holds thralls equal to one-third your Fighter level (round down), each using the Brute or Archer stat block (your choice) and sharing your saving throw proficiencies. Your thralls are Friendly to you and your allies and obey your commands. A thrall sinks into the ground when it drops to 0 Hit Points or you die.

Summoning Your Retinue. As a Bonus Action, you can summon a thrall in an unoccupied space of earth, sand, loose stone, or grave soil within 30 feet of yourself. You can do so a number of times equal to one-third your Fighter level (round down), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest. Summoning a thrall from the corpse of a Small or Medium creature within range expends no use. You can dismiss any number of your thralls at any time (no action required). If a summon would exceed your retinue's maximum, choose one existing thrall to sink into the ground.

The Retinue in Combat. Your thralls act during your turn. Each can move and use its Reaction freely, but can take no action other than Dodge unless you take a Bonus Action to command your retinue, in which case each thrall can take any action. While you have the Incapacitated condition, your thralls act freely.

3rd Level - Grave Tithe

When you or a thrall in your retinue reduces a Hostile creature to 0 Hit Points, you can regain an expended use of Second Wind.

Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a Short or Long Rest.

7th Level - Formations

Whenever you use Second Wind, you can also choose a Formation and command your retinue. The Formation lasts until the start of your next turn. A thrall benefits from the Formation only while within 60 feet of you.

Phalanx: A thrall has a +2 bonus to AC while within 5 feet of at least one other thrall. Starting at 15th level, each creature also gains Temporary Hit Points equal to your Fighter Level.

Vanguard: Each thrall's Speed increases by 15 feet. Starting at 15th level, when you choose this Formation, you can also designate one creature within 60 feet of yourself; your thralls have Advantage on attack rolls against it.

Wedge: Your thralls deal an extra 1d4 Necrotic damage on a hit. This extra damage increases to 2d4 at 15th level.

10th Level - Disposable Forces

Once on each of your turns, when you take the Attack action, you can cause one thrall within 30 feet of yourself to sink into the earth. If you do, you can make one additional attack as part of that action, and that attack deals an extra 2d6 Necrotic damage.

15th Level - Deathly Drills

When you choose a Formation using Second Wind, your retinue also gain its passive benefit until you use another Formation.

Phalanx: Your thralls gain a +2 bonus to AC.

Vanguard: Your thralls' Speed increases by 10 feet.

Wedge: Your thralls deal an extra 1d4 Necrotic damage on a hit.

18th Level - Grasp of the Starved

As an Action, choose a point you can see within 60 feet of yourself. Your thralls sink into the earth, and you summon up to your retinue's maximum number of thralls into unoccupied spaces within 30 feet of that point, regardless of the surface. As they rise, grasping hands erupt: each creature of your choice within 30 feet of that point must make a Dexterity saving throw (DC 8 plus your Proficiency Bonus plus your Constitution modifier). On a failed save, a target takes 5d8 Necrotic damage and is Restrained until the end of its next turn. On a successful save, a target takes half as much damage and isn't Restrained.

Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a Long Rest.

Barrow Thrall

Medium Undead, Neutral

AC 15 (Brute only) or 12 (Archer only)
HP equal to your Fighter level + 10
Speed 25 ft.

STR DEX CON INT WIS CHA
14 14 13 5 7 7
+2 +2 +1 −3 −2 −2

Immunities Poison; Exhaustion, Poisoned
Senses Darkvision 60 ft., Passive Perception 8
Languages Understands languages you know but can't speak.
CR None (XP 0; PB equals your Proficiency Bonus)

Actions

Grave-Iron (Brute Only). Melee Attack Roll: your Constitution modifier plus your Proficiency Bonus, reach 5 ft. Hit: 2d4 Necrotic damage

Barrow Shot (Archer Only). Ranged Attack Roll: your Constitution modifier plus your Proficiency Bonus, range 60/240 ft. Hit: 1d6 Necrotic damage.

Reactions

Body Block (Brute Only). Trigger: A creature the thrall can see attacks a target other than itself within 5 feet of it. Response: The thrall takes the damage instead of the target.

Source: Barrow Lord by Mendax1

Homebrew / Subclasses

Blood Hunter Subclasses

Blood Hunter Subclasses

Order of the Symbiote

Those who enter the order of the symbiote are either a crazed or brave few. Taking in a new being into their own during an induction to hemocraft, they are able to tap into a special power granted by being now two halves of a greater whole. Whether the symbiote be embedded within their flesh, or coiling around their skin, as this new creature's host the Blood Hunters of this order boast an unmatched ability to tear down the biologies of those they may face.

Rite of the Blighted

When you join this order at 3rd level, you learn the rite of the blighted as part of your crimson rite features. When you activate the rite of the blighted, the extra damage dealt is poison damage. Additionally, hitting a creature with a weapon infused with this rite that is neither undead or a construct deals extra poison damage equal to your hemocraft modifier.

Symbiotic Awareness

A limited consciousness within your symbiote grants you an increased perception of your surroundings. You gain proficiency in the perception skill. Additionally, you may add your hemocraft modifier to your initiative rolls.

Infected Exposure

At 7th level you know the Blood Curse of Exposure, which does not count towards your total number of blood curses known, and its potential rises to great power in combination with your toxins. If you apply your Blood Curse of Exposure to a creature after dealing poison damage from your Rite of the Blighted, the curse will instead last for 1 minute. If you have amplified the curse, you take damage equal to a roll of your hemocraft die at the start of each of your turns in exchange for your symbiote sustaining the infection.

If you already know the Blood Curse of Exposure, you may learn a different blood curse of your choice that you qualify for.

Brand of Contagion

At 7th level, when you apply your Brand of Castigation to a creature while you have your Rite of the Blighted active, you may choose to inflict the target with a virulent infection. The target must succeed a constitution saving throw or experience one of the following effects, as determined by rolling your hemocraft die.

Hemocraft Die Roll Effect
1 The target becomes Poisoned for 1 minute, and can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, expelling the poison on a successful save.
2 A wave of weakness falls over the target. All attack rolls have advantage against the target until the start of its next turn.
3 Your opponent's blood mixes with your symbiote, allowing a temporary breach in their immune system. The next blood curse you apply to that target within 1 minute that requires a saving throw will take effect regardless of whether or not their saving throw is successful or not.
4 A mild paralytic compound infuses itself within the target, reducing all of its speeds by 10 ft for 1 minute. The target can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success.
5 The toxins of your weapon attack invade the target's mind, causing them to make concentration saves at disadvantage until the start of your next turn.
6 Your target has its physical attributes ravaged to some degree. The target suffers a penalty to all Strength, Dexterity, and Constitution Checks and Saving throws equal to your hemocraft die until the end of its next turn.
7 Your target's vision fogs temporarily, causing them to become Blinded until the end of its next turn.
8 Toxins invade your target's body entirely, causing their muscles to lock. The target is Paralyzed until the end of its next turn.
9 An increased spike in potency causes your rite to deliver vastly increased lethality. For one minute, your Rite of the Blighted deals extra damage equal to three rolls of your hemocraft die instead of one.
10 Toxins manage to tear into your target regardless of their biologies. The target loses all resistance and immunity to poison damage for 1 minute, gaining vulnerability instead. The target can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a successful save.

Effects listed under a higher number than you can roll with your hemocraft die remain inaccessible until a level in which you can.

Mutualistic Host

Starting at 11th level, your symbiote is able to grant you a further boon to your health. Whenever an effect would restore your hit points, you regain an additional amount of hit points equal to a roll of your hemocraft die.

Additionally, you learn the druidcraft cantrip. Your hemocraft ability is your spellcasting ability for this spell.

Walking Dead

At 15th Level, If you are reduced to 0 hit points, your symbiote may assume control over your basic motor functions for a limited time in order to protect you. During this time you experience the following:

  • Your speed is halved
  • You cannot use your extra attack feature
  • You cannot take reactions
  • You Still make Death Saving Throws at the start of each of your turns
  • You suffer the normal effects of taking damage while at 0 hit points

The symbiote can maintain its control for a number of rounds equal to your hemocraft modifier (minimum of one), until you die, or until you regain at least one hit point. Once you use this feature, you cannot do so again until you finish a long rest.

Blood Curse of Lethality

At 18th level, your symbiotic connection grants you the ability to entirely ravage a creature's health. You gain the Blood Curse of Lethality for your Blood Maledict feature. This doesn’t count against your number of blood curses known.

Blood Curse of Lethality - When you hit a creature with a weapon infused with your Rite of the Blighted, you may choose to apply this Blood Curse. The target must make a constitution saving throw. On a failed save, the target takes 8d8 poison damage and suffers a random effect of your Brand of Contagion. The target takes half as much damage on a successful save and suffers no other effects.

Amplify - Amplifying this curse will instead reduce the target's hit points to 1 should they fail the saving throw, and take the full 8d8 poison damage on a success.

Homebrew / Subclasses

Blood Knight

Blood Knight

Blood Knight

The blood knight is the title given to an eldritch knight who chooses to delve into the taboo discipline of hemomancy, or the magic of controlling blood and life force. These warriors thrive in the heart of battle where the blood flows thickest, using it to enhance their offensive and defensive capabilities.

Features:

  • 3rd Level - Combat Hemomancy
  • 7th Level - Sense Life
  • 10th Level - Blood-Fueled Overdrive
  • 15th Level - Hemomantic Precision
  • 18th Level - Bloody Tyrant

3rd Level - Combat Hemomancy

Starting at 3rd level when you choose this archetype, you gain access to a series of hemomantic abilities that allow you to use the blood of your enemies to your advantage.

When you damage a creature that has blood within 30 feet of you with a weapon attack, you gain a special die called a blood die, which is a D6.  You can have a number of these dice up to a maximum equal to your proficiency bonus. Creatures that do not have blood do not generate blood dice, and you do not gain blood dice from attacks that are modified by blood dice.

You can expend blood dice to perform a number of hemomantic abilities described at the end of this features description.

Each time a hemomantic ability asks you to expend your blood dice, you can choose how many you want to roll and gain a benefit based on what you rolled.

Hemomantic Abilities

Combat Regeneration. At the start of your turn, you can spend blood dice to gain temporary hit points. Roll the dice you spend, add them together, and gain temporary hit points equal to the total, replacing any temporary hit points you already have.

Crimson Strike. You can use the Attack action to make a special melee attack, a crimson strike. If you're able to make multiple attacks with the Attack action, this attack replaces one of them. You brandish the weapon used in the technique and make a melee attack with it against one creature within 15 feet of you. On a hit, the target takes magical piercing, bludgeoning, or slashing damage equal to the total of the blood dice you spent.

Blood Shell. When you are hit by an attack, you can use your reaction to spend blood dice. Roll the dice you spend, add them together, and increase your AC by the amount equal to the total rolled against that attack.

Blood Clotting. As a bonus action, you can spend blood dice to throw blood onto a surface at a range of 15 feet and have it stick in a 25 ft. square. Any creature that starts its turn in that area or that enters that area during its turn must make a Strength saving throw with a DC of 10 + the amount you roll on your blood dice (A maximum DC of 8 + proficiency bonus + Strength or Dexterity modifier). On a failed save, the creature's speed is reduced to zero until the start of their next turn.

7th Level - Sense Life

At 7th level, you gain advantage on wisdom (perception) checks to spot and track enemies that have blood in their veins. In addition, your ability to sense blood can be so precise that you have advantage wisdom (insight) checks to tell if someone is lying to you.

10th Level - Blood-Fueled Overdrive

At 10th level, when you use your indomitable feature, you can expend one blood die and add it to the roll.

15th Level - Hemomantic Precision

At 15th level, you have a very tight control over blood you spill. You can re-roll one blood die once whenever you roll them for a hemomantic ability.

18th Level - Bloody Tyrant

At 18th level, when you hit a creature with an attack and have the maximum number of blood dice, you can expend them all to force the creature to make a Constitution saving throw with a DC of 8 + proficiency bonus + Strength or Dexterity modifier. On a failed save, the creature is paralyzed for 1 minute. At the end of each of its turns, the paralyzed target must make a Constitution saving throw at the end of each of its turns. On a successful save, this paralyzing effect ends.

Homebrew / Subclasses

Blood Magic

Blood Magic

Description

Considered taboo by many societies and magic practitioners, the use of blood magic—also known as hemocraft—is a rare art that harnesses the latent powers of a creature’s vitality to fuel and amplify the caster’s own capabilities, while manipulating and weakening the bodies of enemies from the inside. Some of the more macabre mages seeking to empower their arcane pursuits turn to hemocraft as a means of bolstering their spells, giving their own life’s blood to reach new heights of frightening magical prowess.

The secrets of hemocraft and other forms of blood magic were once the sole purview of the mysterious Claret Orders. In recent years, however, these secrets have begun to spread beyond the order’s members and into the hands of less scrupulous mages. Blood magic has a bad reputation in Tal’Dorei, even though its powers can be used for much more than evil.

Features:

  • 2nd Level - Blood Channeling
  • 2nd Level - Sanguine Burst
  • 6th Level - Bond of Mutual Suffering
  • 10th Level - Glyph of Hemorrhaging
  • 14th Level - Thicker than Water

2nd Level - Blood Channeling

When you choose this arcane tradition at 2nd level, you are able to use your own depleted life essence to channel your magical abilities. Whenever your current hit points are below your hit point maximum, you can use your own body as an arcane focus.

In addition, when casting a wizard spell that requires a costly material component, you can forego the component by taking 1d10 necrotic damage per 50 gp of the cost of the component (minimum 1d10). This damage can’t be reduced in any way. If this damage reduces you to 0 hit points, the spell fails but the spell slot is not expended.

2nd Level - Sanguine Burst

Also at 2nd level, you learn how to weave your life force into a spell you cast, boosting its intensity at the cost of your vitality. Whenever you roll damage for a spell you’ve cast of 1st level or higher, you can choose to take necrotic damage equal to the spell’s level to reroll a number of the damage dice up to your Intelligence modifier (minimum one). This damage can’t be reduced in any way, and you must use the new rolls.

6th Level - Bond of Mutual Suffering

At 6th level, when a creature you can see hits you with an attack, you can use your reaction to bind your vitality to the attacker and force them to share your pain. The attacker takes damage equal to the damage you took.

This feature cannot be used against constructs or undead. You can use this feature once. You must finish a short or long rest before you can use it again.

At 14th level, you can use this feature twice between rests.

10th Level - Glyph of Hemorrhaging

Starting at 10th level, when you damage a creature with a spell, you can choose to curse that creature for 1 minute. While cursed in this way, whenever the creature is hit by an attack, it takes an extra 1d6 necrotic damage. At the end of each of the creature’s turns, it can make a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC, ending the curse on a success.

This feature cannot be used against creatures that are undead or constructs. Once you use this feature, you can’t use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

14th Level - Thicker than Water

Upon reaching 14th level, the blood that flows through your veins is empowered with arcane vigor that mends wounds and helps preserve your life. Whenever a spell or magical effect causes you to regain hit points, you regain an additional number of hit points equal to your proficiency bonus.

In addition, while you are concentrating on a spell, you have resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical attacks.

Homebrew / Subclasses

Bombardier

Bombardier

Bombardier

Where the Alchemist brings life, the Bombardier brings ruin. Bombardiers are masters of volatile reagents, crafting incendiary flasks, caustic vials, and toxic brews designed to engulf their foes in lingering devastation. On the battlefield, they are walking arsenals, hurling explosive concoctions that set the world ablaze.

Features:

  • 3rd Level - Tool Proficiency
  • 3rd Level - Bombardier Spells
  • 3rd Level - Experimental Bomb
  • 5th Level - Volatile Savant
  • 9th Level - Corrosive Concoctions
  • 9th Level - Rapid Alchemy
  • 15th Level - Master of Ruin

3rd Level - Tool Proficiency

When you adopt this specialization at 3rd level, you gain proficiency with alchemist’s supplies. If you already have this proficiency, you gain proficiency with another type of artisan’s tools of your choice.

3rd Level - Bombardier Spells

You always have certain spells prepared after you reach particular levels in this class, as shown in the Bombardier Spells table. These spells count as artificer spells for you and don’t count against the number of artificer spells you prepare.

Artificer Level | Spells

  • 3rd | grease, inflict wounds
  • 5th | web, Melf's acid arrow
  • 9th | gaseous form, stinking cloud
  • 13th | greater invisibility, vitriolic sphere
  • 17th | wall of force, immolation

3rd Level - Experimental Bomb

Starting at 3rd level, whenever you finish a long rest, you can magically produce an experimental bomb in an empty flask or vial you touch. Roll on the Experimental Bomb table to determine its effect, which is triggered when you throw it.

As an action, you or another creature can throw the bomb up to 30 feet, where it shatters and releases its effect. A creature in the bomb’s area must make a saving throw against your artificer spell save DC to avoid or reduce its effects.

You can create additional experimental bombs by expending a spell slot of 1st level or higher for each one. When you do so, you use your action to create the bomb and roll for its effect on the Experimental Bomb table.

Creating a bomb requires alchemist’s supplies on your person, and any bomb you create with this feature lasts until it is thrown or until the end of your next long rest.

Experimental Bomb Table

  1. Corrosive Acid. Deals 2d6 acid damage in a 5-foot radius (Dex save for half). On a failed save, the acid clings to creatures, dealing 1d6 acid damage at the start of each of their turns until a creature uses its action to scrape or wash it off.
  2. Incendiary Fire. Deals 2d6 fire damage in a 5-foot radius (Dex save for half). On a failed save, creatures are set ablaze, taking 1d6 fire damage at the start of each of their turns until they or an ally uses an action to douse the flames.
  3. Toxic Gas. Creates a 10-foot radius cloud of poisonous gas that lasts for 1 minute. (Con save or be poisoned until the start of your next turn; repeat the save at the end of each turn). A creature must make the save whenever it enters the gas or starts its turn in the gas.
  4. Cryo Flask. Deals 2d6 cold damage in a 5-foot radius (Dex save for half). On a failed save, a creature is hindered by ice formations for 1 minute, or until it or another creature within reach uses an action to break the ice.
  5. Shrapnel Bomb. Deals 2d6 piercing damage in a 10-foot radius (Dex save for half). On a failed save, the creature takes 1d6 slashing damage the first time on each turn it moves 1 foot or more without teleporting. An affected creature or ally can use its action to remove the shrapnel.
  6. Sonic Blast. Deals 2d8 thunder damage in a 10-foot radius (Str save for half). Creatures that fail the save are pushed 10 feet from the center of the blast and are deafened until the start of your next turn.

Scaling: The initial and persistent damage increase at higher levels:

  • 6th level: +1d6 (or +1d4/+1d8 for relevant bombs)
  • 11th level: +2d6
  • 16th level: +3d6

5th Level - Volatile Savant

At 5th level, you have mastered the art of combining spellwork and alchemical destruction into seamless attacks.

  • Whenever you cast an artificer spell or cantrip on your turn, you can throw one of your Experimental Bombs as a bonus action.

You can treat any alchemical item (such as alchemist’s fire, acid vial, or an experimental bomb) as a simple ranged weapon with a range of 30/90 feet, using your Dexterity or Strength modifier for attack rolls. Damage dealt by the throw is 1d4 slashing damage plus your Dexterity or Strength modifier, in addition to the damage or effect normally dealt by the item.

9th Level - Corrosive Concoctions

At 9th level, your concoctions weaken enemy defenses and allow you to control the battlefield:

  • Creatures that fail their saving throw against one of your bombs have disadvantage on saving throws against the next alchemical effect you deal to them (from your bombs or alchemical items such as acid vial or alchemist’s fire) before the end of your next turn.

9th Level - Rapid Alchemy

Also at 9th level, you are able to craft bombs with remarkable speed:

  • You can use a bonus action instead of an action to craft your Experimental Bombs.

15th Level - Master of Ruin

At 15th level, your expertise in destruction allows you to maximize the potency of your creations and have better control over what you use:

  • You gain resistance to fire, and acid damage.
  • When a creature takes persistent damage from one of your Experimental Bombs (acid or fire) or an alchemical item (alchemist’s fire, acid vial), you can use your reaction to make the creature take maximum damage instead of rolling. You can use this ability a number of times equal to half your Intelligence modifier (minimum of 1). All expended uses are restored when you finish a long rest.
Homebrew / Subclasses

Channel of Artistry

Channel of Artistry

Artistry Channeler

Description

The Channel of Artistry represents channelers who want to master controlling the flow of their arcane energy, manipulating their power with finesse and elegance. They weave through combat like dancers and cast spells with the delicacy of an accomplished maestro.

Features

  • 1st Level - Armaments of Artistry
  • 1st Level - Elemental Savant
  • 6th Level - Weaving Strike
  • 11th Level - Beautiful Virtuosity
  • 11th Level - Harmonized Strikes
  • 17th Level - Culmination of Artistry

1st Level - Armaments of Artistry

When you pick this channel at 1st level, you gain proficiency in shortswords, scimitars, and whips. You also gain proficiency in one type of artisan’s tools of your choice.

1st Level - Elemental Savant

Your use and control of elemental energy is beautiful to many, and distracting to your opponents. Starting at 1st level, when you hit a creature with an attack, you have resistance to the first attack they make against you until the beginning of your next turn. Additionally, you may imbue two weapons instead of one. The imbued damage types must be the same for both weapons.

6th Level - Weaving Strike

At 6th level, you can sculpt your elemental energy with your weapon, enhancing both your own movements and your energy’s potency. When you deal damage with your Elemental Imbuement, the next attack roll you make during this turn has advantage, and your movement doesn’t provoke opportunity attacks until the beginning of your next turn.

11th Level - Beautiful Virtuosity

At 11th level, the beauty of your movement and the flow of your energy is entrancing and inspiring to allies. When you deal damage with your Elemental Imbuement, you may choose a creature within 30 feet that can see you. That creature may add your Elemental Imbuement die to the next attack roll, saving throw, or ability check they make until the beginning of your next turn.

11th Level - Harmonized Strikes

At 11th level, if you hit with a weapon attack from your attack action and hit with a spell attack roll made with your Overchanneled Imbuement in one turn, you may take a second bonus action that turn.

17th Level - Culmination of Artistry

At 17th level, you’ve perfected your casting as a form of art. You may use your Flash Charge feature an unlimited amount of times per day. When you hit with an attack, you may use your Flash Charge feature as a reaction. When you do, the attack deals additional damage equal to two rolls of your new Elemental Imbuement die.

Homebrew / Subclasses

Channel of Containment

Channel of Containment

Description

Features:

  • 1st Level - Armaments of Containment
  • 6th Level - Brawl Binding
  • 11th Level - Elemental Fortitude
  • 11th Level - Extra Attack
  • 17th Level - Culmination of Containment

1st Level - Armaments of Containment

When you pick this channel at 1st level, you gain proficiency in improvised weapons. You also gain proficiency in heavy armor. Elemental Core You learn to confine your arcane energy within your body, empowering your unarmed attacks. You may choose to Imbue your body with elemental energy as opposed to a weapon. While imbued, you gain the following benefits:

  • Your unarmed strikes use your Elemental Imbuement dice for its damage type.
  • When you attack with an unarmed strike, you may use your Intelligence modifier, rather than your strength modifier, for attack and damage rolls.
  • You gain resistance to the damage type you chose for your Imbuement
  • You can use your body as a focus for your Channeler spells

6th Level - Brawl Binding

Beginning at 6th level, when you use the attack action to grapple a creature, the target takes damage equal to one roll of your Elemental Imbuement die if the grapple succeeds. Whenever you take the attack action against the creature on subsequent turns, if you are still grappling the creature, you may choose to deal this damage again. Additionally, if you succeed on grappling a creature, you can use your Overchanneled Imbuement as a bonus action. Creatures you grapple have disadvantage on saving throws against spells you cast.

11th Level - Elemental Fortitude

At 11th level, your contained energy provides a defensive ward that sits just under your skin, protecting you from harm. When you are subjected to an effect that has you roll a saving throw to take half damage, if the damage type is acid, cold, fire, lightning, or thunder, you instead take no damage if you succeed on the saving throw, and only half damage if you fail.

11th Level - Extra Attack

Beginning at 11th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the attack action on your turn.

17th Level - Culmination of Containment

Beginning at 17th level, your arcane energy binds perfectly to your flesh. You gain the following benefits while Imbued:

  • You gain immunity to the damage type you chose for your Imbuement
  • Your walking speed increases by 20 feet
  • You no longer need to hit with an Imbued weapon attack to cast Channeler spells as a bonus action.
  • When you cast a Channeler spell, add your Intelligence modifier to your unarmed strike damage and any Strength, Dexterity, or Constitution checks you make until the end of your next turn.
Homebrew / Subclasses

Channel of Devastation

Channel of Devastation

Devastation Channeler

Description

The Channel of Devastation represents channelers who prefer focusing their energy in short, powerful bursts, often leading to disastrous results. Those who choose this channel work tirelessly to keep their energy concealed and suppressed, until they can let it all out in a violent burst.

Features

  • 1st Level - Armaments of Devastation
  • 1st level - Accelerant
  • 6th Level - Devastating Presence
  • 11th Level - Devastating Strikes
  • 11th Level - Extra Attack
  • 17th Level - Culmination of Devastation

1st Level - Armaments of Devastation

When you pick this channel at 1st level, you gain proficiency in glaives, greataxes, greatswords, halberds, and pikes. You also gain proficiency in heavy armor and shields.

1st level - Accelerant

At 1st level, you’ve learned how to create an accelerant with your devastating energy, overcharging your attacks. When you hit with a melee weapon attack, you can force the target to roll a strength saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failure, the target is knocked prone and suffers an additional effect depending on your imbuement. You may use this feature a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier. When you take a short or long rest, you regain all expended uses.

Accelerant Effect
Damage Type Effect
Acid The target’s AC is reduced by 1 until the end of your next turn.
Fire The target takes additional fire damage equal to one roll of your Elemental Imbuement die.
Cold The target’s speed is reduced by half of their maximum until the end of your next turn.
Lightning You may force one other creature of your choice within 10 feet of the target to take lightning damage equal to two rolls of your Elemental Imbuement die.
Thunder The target is pushed back 15 feet.

6th Level - Devastating Presence

At 6th level, your mere presence is recognized as a threat, inciting opponents to focus their aggression on you. Each creature of your choice that starts its turn within 30 feet of you and can see you must roll a Wisdom saving throw against to your spell save DC. On a failure, the creature has disadvantage on attacks that don’t target you until the end of that creature’s turn. If a creature succeeds on this saving throw, they are immune to this effect for the next 24 hours.

11th Level - Devastating Strikes

Starting at 11th level, whenever you deal damage with your Elemental Imbuement or a channeler spell that shares a damage type with your chosen Elemental Imbuement, you ignore resistance to that damage type, and you may treat immunity to that damage type as resistance.

11th Level - Extra Attack

Beginning at 11th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the attack action on your turn.

17th Level - Culmination of Devastation

At 17th level, you’ve wrought elemental devastation everywhere you’d gone, and have found the perfect way to channel it. When you hit with a melee weapon attack, you can reroll that attack against any number of other targets within 30ft, hitting each target simultaneously. You may use this feature a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier. When you finish a long rest, you regain all expended uses.

Homebrew / Subclasses

Channel of Madness

Channel of Madness

Madness Channeler

Description

The channel of Madness represents a rare and often fanatical sect of channelers that believe in submitting control over their mind and actions to the powers within themselves, even to their own detriment

Features

  • 1st Level - Armaments of Madness
  • 1st Level - Medium For Madness
  • 6th Level - Braincharge
  • 11th Level - Mental Overchannel
  • 11th Level - Psychic Armaments
  • 17th Level - Culmination of Madness

1st Level - Armaments of Madness

When you pick this channel at 1st level, you gain proficiency in hand crossbows, heavy crossbows, and longbows.

1st Level - Medium For Madness

At 1st level, you may select two 1st level enchantment spells. You learn these spells and may cast each of them once per day without expending a spell slot. At 6th level, you may choose two 2nd level enchantment spells, two 3rd level enchantment spells at 11th level, and two 4th level enchantment spells at 17th level.

Additionally, you may pick psychic damage as the damage type for your Elemental Imbuement.

6th Level - Braincharge

At 6th level, you’re able to overload the minds of others, driving them further towards insanity. When a creature fails the first save from an enchantment spell you cast, they take extra psychic damage equal to your Elemental Imbuement die. Then, you may have one creature you can see within 30 feet of you gain advantage on the next Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma saving throw they make until the beginning of your next turn.

11th Level - Mental Overchannel

At 11th level, when you deal psychic damage to a creature, you may choose to deal maximum psychic damage rather than rolling. If you do, the target is stunned until the beginning of your next turn. You cannot use this feature again until you finish a long rest.

11th Level - Psychic Armaments

At 11th level, when you imbue a weapon with psychic damage, you can change that weapon’s base damage type to psychic for as long as it’s imbued. Add your Intelligence modifier (minimum of +1) to the damage of your weapon attacks imbued with psychic damage.

17th Level - Culmination of Madness

At 17th level, it’s hard to tell if you’re still sane or not; your internal energy has corroded your mind past the point of no return. You gain advantage on saving throws against enchantment spells. In addition, you gain immunity to psychic damage and immunity to effects that would charm or frighten you. Once per day, when you cast an enchantment spell, if it would target only one creature and no other creatures, you can instead make it target as many creatures as you can see within 60 feet of you.

Homebrew / Subclasses

Channel of Volatility

Channel of Volatility

Description

The Channel of Volatility is a controversial path to undertake, as though it is the easiest channel to ‘master’, it may prove most perilous to the channeler using it. Those who practice the channel of Volatility must exercise extreme caution, else they risk losing control of their magic to horrific consequence.

Features:

  • 1st Level - Armaments of Volatility
  • 1st Level - Volatile Charge
  • 6th Level - Volatile Surge
  • 11th Level - Risk and Reward
  • 11th Level - Extra Attack
  • 17th Level - Culmination of Volatility

1st Level - Armaments of Volatility

When you pick this channel at 1st level, you gain proficiency in flails, mauls, and warhammers. You also gain proficiency in heavy armor and shields.

1st Level - Volatile Charge

Your internal energy is difficult to predict and control, yet it assists you when you need it most. Starting at 1st level, whenever you hit with a weapon attack using your imbued weapon, note the result of the attack roll and your Imbuement die roll.

Odd. If the result of the attack roll is odd, you gain temporary hit points equal to the result of your Imbuement die, which disappears whenever you take a short or long rest.

Even. If the result of the attack roll is even, the attack deals extra damage equal to the result of your Imbuement die.

6th Level - Volatile Surge

The unpredictable effects of your magic have branched into even more peculiar effects. Starting at 6th level, when you cast a channeler spell, roll your Elemental Imbuement die and note the result. Consult the Volatile Surge table for additional effects.

Surge Effect
Result Effect
1 You take damage equal to one roll of your Elemental Imbuement die.
2 You add another roll of your Elemental Imbuement die to the spell’s damage.
3 Your AC increases by 1 until the start of your next turn.
4 You gain advantage on your next attack roll until the end of your next turn.
5 You gain additional temporary hit points equal to one roll of your Elemental Imbuement die.
6 You can make an additional weapon attack as part of the same bonus action.
7 You gain resistance to the next attack that hits you until the start of your next turn.
8 Reroll on this table twice, and the effects of both rolls occur. If you roll the same effect twice, the effect only applies once.

11th Level - Risk and Reward

At 11th level; your frequent interactions with fickle energies have allowed you to lean further into their volatility. You learn one additional Ante option, and gain an additional Ante charge.

11th Level - Extra Attack

Beginning at 11th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the attack action on your turn.

17th Level - Culmination of Volatility

At 17th level, your destructive magic is longing for escape from your mortal shell. Once per day, when you’re reduced to zero hit points, you may choose to release all of your internal energy in one burst. Each creature of your choice within 30 feet of you must roll a dexterity saving throw equal to your spell save DC. On a failed save, a target takes 15d10 damage and is stunned until the end of their next turn. On a successful save, the target takes half as much damage and isn’t stunned. The damage type is the same as your elemental Imbuement. In either case, the explosion kills you immediately, disintegrating all non-magical gear and equipment you’re carrying and wearing.

Homebrew / Subclasses

Chaos Domain

Chaos Domain

Chaos Domain

In the domain of chaos, where whims rule and order trembles, the chosen clerics of the Chaos Domain walk a path paved with unpredictability and capriciousness. Whether by the whispered machinations of trickster deities or the primal forces of wild gods, these clerics wield the very essence of chaos itself.

Features:

  • 1st Level - Chaos Domain Spells
  • 1st Level - Chaos Bonus Proficiencies
  • 2nd Level - Channel Divinity: Chaos Warp
  • 6th Level - Twisted Fate
  • 8th Level - Divine Strike: Chaos Domain
  • 17th Level - Empowered Warp

1st Level - Chaos Domain Spells

You gain domain spells at the cleric levels listed in the Chaos Domain Spells table. See the Divine Domain class feature for how domain spells work.

Cleric Level Spells
1st Chaos Bolt, Dissonant Whispers
3rd Mirror Image, Enlarge/Reduce
5th Haste, Slow
7th Confusion, Polymorph
9th Dominate Person, Modify Memory

1st Level - Chaos Bonus Proficiencies

When you choose this domain at 1st level, you gain proficiency with martial weapons.

2nd Level - Channel Divinity: Chaos Warp

Starting at 2nd level, you can use your Channel Divinity to warp probability around you, causing unpredictable effects. As an action, you present your holy symbol and a number of creatures equal to your wisdom modifier you can see within 30 feet of you. Those creature must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw against your cleric spell save DC or be affected by one of the following effects rolled randomly for each target:

1d4 Effect
1 The target takes 2d10 psychic damage.
2 The target is blinded until the end of its next turn.
3 The target is charmed by you until the end of its next turn.
4 The target is frightened until the end of its next turn.

6th Level - Twisted Fate

At 6th level, your connection to the chaos that drives your every action allows you to twist the threads of fate in the world around you. As a reaction when a creature within 30 feet of you excluding yourself fails a saving throw, or check or misses an attack roll, the triggering creature must reroll the d20 and use the higher roll.

You can then choose a different creature you can see within 30 feet range. The chosen creature has disadvantage on the next attack roll, ability check, or saving throw it makes within 1 minute.

You can use this reaction a number of times equal to your Wisdom Modifier (minimum of once) per long rest.

8th Level - Divine Strike: Chaos Domain

At 8th level, you gain the ability to infuse your weapon strikes with divine energy. Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can cause the attack to deal an extra 1d8 psychic damage to the target. When you reach 14th level, the extra damage increases to 2d8.

17th Level - Empowered Warp

At 17th level, when you use your Chaos Warp, rather than rolling 1d4, roll 2d4. Each target that fails the save is affected by both effects you rolled.

If both d4s land on the same number, the target makes the saving throw with disadvantage and the effect is enhanced as follows:

d4 Effect
1 The target takes 4d10 psychic damage and can't use reactions until the end of its next turn
2 The Target is blinded and subtracts 1d6 from any attack roll or saving throw it makes until the end of its next turn.
3 The target is under the effects of the confusion spell until the end of its next turn.
4 The target is under the effects of the slow spell until the end of its next turn.
Homebrew / Subclasses

Circle of Beauty

Circle of Beauty

Description

Druids of the Circle of Beauty vow to protect all that brings beauty in nature. From the patterns of symmetry designed to attract mates, to visual marks designed to confuse camouflage observers, these are all sights that should be admired and emulated. They marvel at how nature seamlessly blends together both form and function in a way man-made objects never could.

Features:

  • 2nd Level - Circle Spells
  • 2nd Level - Natural Form
  • 6th Level - Blessing of Symmetry
  • 10th Level - Beautiful Plummage
  • 14th Level - Radiant Appearance

2nd Level - Circle Spells

Your eye for all things visually harmonious grants you access to some spells when you reach certain levels in this class, as shown on the Circle of Beauty Spells table.

Once you gain access to one of these spells, you always have it prepared, and it doesn't count against the number of spells you can prepare each day. If you gain access to a spell that doesn't appear on the druid spell list, the spell is nonetheless a druid spell for you.

Druid Level Spell
2nd disguise self, feather fall
3rd healing spirit, lesser restoration
5th daylight, hypnotic pattern
7th charm monster, compulsion
9th creation, dawn

2nd Level - Natural Form

As a bonus action, you can expend one use of your Wild Shape feature to draw upon nature's splendour, rather than assuming a Beast form.

While in your natural form and wearing no armour, your Armour Class equals 10 + your Dexterity modifier + your Wisdom modifier. You can use a shield and still gain this benefit. The form lasts for 10 minutes. It ends early if you dismiss it (no action required), if you die, or you use this feature again.

Whenever you assume your natural form, choose the manner of natural appearance your body transforms into; your choice gives you certain benefits while in the form.

Attractive. When you enter this form, and as a bonus action on your subsequent turns while in this form, you can choose a creature you can see within 30 feet of you. That creature must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC or be charmed by you until the start of your next turn. The target automatically succeeds on its saving throw if it can't see you. It stops being charmed by you if it is attacked or damaged, or if another creature shakes it awake as a bonus action.

Camouflage. You can take the Hide action as a bonus action. You can attempt to hide even when you are only lightly obscured by foliage, heavy rain, falling snow, mist, and other natural phenomena.

Verdant. When you enter this form, and as a bonus action on your subsequent turns, you can choose one creature you can see within 30 feet of you (including yourself). That creature gains your Wisdom modifier temporary hit points, which lasts until the start of your next turn.

6th Level - Blessing of Symmetry

6th-level Circle of Beauty feature

You strive to emulate the symmetry that occurs in the natural world. When you or a willing creature you can see within 60 feet of you casts a spell with a casting time of 1 action and which deals damage to at least one target, the caster can forgo rolling damage dice and take the average damage. If the spell has an ongoing effect that can deal damage after it is cast, this feature only applies to the initial instance of damage.

You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

10th Level - Beautiful Plummage

The transformation into your natural form is now even more stunning. Your forms gain extra benefits as detailed below:

Attractive. When you charm a creature, you can command it as part of the same bonus action to use its reaction to move up to its speed and make one weapon attack against a target you can see. After the creature completes this command, it is no longer charmed by you.

Camouflage. When you use the Hide action and are also obscured by natural foliage or phenomena, you become invisible until you move away from the natural foliage, or until you make an attack or cast a spell.

Verdant. The you roll is now a when you give temporary hit points. While a creature has these temporary hit points, it has a bonus to AC and advantage on Constitution saving throws.

Moreover, at the start of each of your turns while in your Natural Form, you can change the appearance of your form. If you do, any effects from your previous form immediately end.

14th Level - Radiant Appearance

Your body's aesthetically pleasing patterns and colours make others hesitate to harm you. When a creature makes an attack roll against you while in your Natural Form, you can use your reaction and force it to make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, the creature can't attack you with an attack or harmful spell until the end of its current turn, and must choose a new target or lose the attack or spell (this doesn't protect you from area effects, such as the explosion of15 a fireball).

You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

Homebrew / Subclasses

Circle of Bravery

Circle of Bravery

5th-level abjuration. (Bard, Druid, Cleric, Paladin)

Meta

Casting Time: 1 action

Range: Self (30 ft. sphere)

Components: V, S

Duration: Concentration, up to 10 minutes

Description

You conjure a field of magical inspiration that bolsters the resolve of your allies. Any creature you choose while they are in this field will have resistance against psychic damage and gain advantage on saving throws against the frightened and charmed conditions. If their save fails, any additional saves against the same effect succeed automatically.

Homebrew / Subclasses

Circle of the Sky

Circle of the Sky

Circle of the Sky

Features:

  • 2nd Level - Circle Spells
  • Where the Wind Guides
  • Early Bird
  • 6th Level - Gale Force
  • 10th Level - Jetstream
  • 14th Level - The Sky's the Limit

2nd Level - Circle Spells

Your connection to the sky allows you to learn certain spells. At 2nd level, you learn the gust cantrip, and it does not count towards the number of druid cantrips you know. At 3rd, 5th, 7th, and 9th level you gain access to the spells listed for that level in the Circle of the Sky Spells table. Once you gain access to one of these spells, you always have it prepared, and it doesn’t count against the number of spells you can prepare each day. If you gain access to a spell that doesn’t appear on the druid spell list, the spell is nonetheless a druid spell for you.

Druid Level Spells
3rd Air Bubble, Skywrite
5th Fly, Lightning Bolt
7th Conjure Minor Elementals, Freedom of Movement
9th Control Winds, Steel Wind Strike

Where the Wind Guides

Your connection to the winds allows you to reliably control vehicles and other structures that rely on them. You gain proficiency in either water or air vehicles (your choice), and while you are aboard such a vehicle, you always have optimal wind for traveling to your intended destination.

Early Bird

When you use your wildshape feature, the beasts you transform into can have a flying speed.

6th Level - Gale Force

At 6th level, you gain the ability to harness windflow to greater effect. Any wind powered structure, such as a wind mill, works at twice it's normal rate while within 5 miles of you. Additionally, water or air vehicles that utilize sails move twice as fast while you are on board.

Additionally, whenever you roll lightning, thunder, or bludgeoning damage from a druid spell you cast, you add your wisdom modifier to the total damage.

10th Level - Jetstream

When you reach 10th level, you gain the ability to move with a supernatural flow. Your walking speed increases by 15 feet, as does any flying speed of creatures you transform into with your wildshape feature. Additionally, you are considered to always be under the effects of the Freedom of Movement spell.

14th Level - The Sky's the Limit

At 14th level, your connection to the skies has given you a shared connection with all life that calls it home. When you use your wildshape feature, you can transform into any Beast, Dragon, or Monstrosity of Challenge Rating 4 or lower, so long as it has a flying speed.

Homebrew / Subclasses

Circle of the Verdant Stalker

Circle of the Verdant Stalker

Description

Druids of the Circle of the Verdant Stalker embody the lethal stillness and precision of Chult’s jungles. They move like serpents through the undergrowth, striking with poison and vanishing into foliage.

Features:

  • 3rd Level - Circle Spells
  • 3rd Level - Venomous Marksman
  • 6th Level - Aspect of the Striking Viper
  • 10th Level - Primal Toxin Mastery
  • 14th Level - Deathbloom Aspect

3rd Level - Circle Spells

Your eye for all things visually harmonious grants you access to some spells when you reach certain levels in this class, as shown on the Circle of Beauty Spells table.

Once you gain access to one of these spells, you always have it prepared, and it doesn't count against the number of spells you can prepare each day. If you gain access to a spell that doesn't appear on the druid spell list, the spell is nonetheless a druid spell for you.

Druid Level Spell
3rd Ensnaring Strike, Poison Spray
5th Plant Growth, Spike Growth
7th Grasping Vine, Stoneskin
9th Tree Stride, Cloudkill (reflavored as a deadly plant toxin cloud)

3rd Level - Venomous Marksman

Your training centers on the precision and toxins of Chult’s hidden hunters.

  • Blowgun Proficiency. You gain proficiency with the blowgun. You can use your Wisdom modifier instead of Dexterity for blowgun attack and damage rolls.

  • Toxin-Enhanced Blowgun. Your blowgun darts deal greater piercing damage as you grow in mastery.

Druid Level Blowgun Damage Die
3rd 1d6
10th 1d8
14th 1d10
  • Poisoner’s Tools. You gain proficiency with the Poisoner’s Kit.
  • Tough to Toxin. You have resistance to poison damage and advantage on saving throws against being poisoned.
  • Jungle Stride. You ignore nonmagical plant-based difficult terrain.

6th Level - Aspect of the Striking Viper

You channel primal ferocity into a deadly, focused trance.

Activation. As a bonus action, expend one use of your Wild Shape to enter this Aspect for 1 minute. You can’t activate it again until you finish a short or long rest.

While in this Aspect:

  • Your blowgun attacks deal an extra 1d8 poison damage.
  • When you take the attack action to attack with your blowgun, hit or miss, you can make another attack with the blowgun.
  • If your first blowgun attack each turn hits, the target must make a Constitution saving throw (DC = your spell save DC) or be Poisoned until the end of its next turn.
  • A creature that fails this saving throw also takes an additional 1d8 poison damage.

10th Level - Primal Toxin Mastery

Your venoms pierce the resilience of even the hardiest foes.

  • Toxic Bypass. Your blowgun attacks and druid spells that deal poison damage treat immunity to poison damage as resistance instead.

  • Debilitating Barrage. When you hit a creature that is Poisoned, you can use your reaction to force it to make a Constitution saving throw (DC = your spell save DC). On a failed save, it is Blinded until the end of its next turn. You can use this reaction a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, regaining all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

14th Level - Deathbloom Aspect

Your mastery of venom and motion refines your Aspect of the Striking Viper into the Deathbloom Aspect.

When you activate your Aspect of the Striking Viper, it gains the following additional benefits:

  • Deadly Venoms. Your extra poison damage increases to 1d10, and creatures make their Constitution saving throws against your poison with disadvantage.
  • Viper’s Retreat. Immediately after you hit a creature with a blowgun attack, you can move up to half your speed without provoking opportunity attacks from that creature.
  • Predator’s Cunning. While the Aspect is active, you can take the Hide or Disengage action as a bonus action. You can also attempt to Hide even when you are only partially obscured by natural terrain, foliage, or dim light.
  • Toxic Perfection. You are immune to poison damage and the poisoned condition.
Homebrew / Subclasses

Circle of the Warden

Circle of the Warden

Circle of the Warden

There are many things that need to be protected, some worth protecting with your life. Druids of this circle protect the natural order of the wilderness with their lives, often picking a place and staking their claim there for a large portion of their lives. Though they protect the land, the spirits of nature see fit to protect them in turn, the mark of a true Warden.

Features:

  • 2nd Level - Improved Shillelagh
  • 2nd Level - Warden Form
  • 6th Level - Forestwalker
  • 6th Level - Extra Attack
  • 10th Level - Arboreal Fortitude
  • 14th Level - Protector’s Resolve

2nd Level - Improved Shillelagh

At 2nd level, you unlock the versatile potential within the Shillelagh cantrip. You learn the shillelagh cantrip. If you already know this cantrip, you may learn a different cantrip of your choice from the druid spell list. Whenever you roll initiative and are not surprised, you can choose to immediately cast shillelagh as a reaction.

Additionally, when you cast shillelagh, you can choose to change the damage type of the weapon to bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing damage for the duration of the spell. The form of the weapon changes to suit the damage type chosen.

2nd Level - Warden Form

At 2nd level, you can allow the spirits of nature to wreath your form in protective foliage to enhance your endurance and martial capability. As a bonus action, you can expend a use of Wild Shape to take on your warden form. Warden form lasts for 10 minutes. It ends early if you are incapacitated or until you dismiss it (as a free action). While in warden form, you gain the following benefits:

  • When you enter warden form, you gain temporary hit points equal to your wisdom modifier + double your druid level
  • Your AC is equal to 13 + your constitution modifier.
  • You are immune to all plant-based difficult terrain, as well as all difficult terrain created by Druid spells you cast.

6th Level - Forestwalker

At 6th level, you become a natural at navigating the rugged and tough terrain of forests. You gain the following benefits while in warden form:

  • You are resistant to damage from Druid spells you cast.
  • You gain a bonus to all strength checks and saves equal to your wisdom modifier while in warden form.

Additionally, you are now unaffected by plant-based difficult terrain when not in warden form.

6th Level - Extra Attack

At 6th level, when you take the attack action, you can make an additional weapon attack as part of the same action. You can replace up to one of these attacks with one of your druid cantrips.

10th Level - Arboreal Fortitude

At 10th level, the fortitude of your warden form grows to reflect a growth in your resolve. While in warden form, you gain a bonus to any constitution saving throw you make to maintain concentration on a spell. This bonus is equal to your wisdom modifier. If you begin your turn in warden form and do not have any temporary hit points, you gain temporary hit points equal to your wisdom modifier.

Additionally, you have adapted your warden form to be fluid and fierce. You gain the following additional benefits while in warden form:

  • Your walking speed increased by 10 feet.
  • Your melee weapon attacks deal an extra 1d8 force damage on a hit.

14th Level - Protector’s Resolve

At 14th level, your will is inseparable from that of the forest, and you learn to command nature as your blade. You always have the wrath of nature spell prepared, and it doesn't count against the total number of druid spells you have prepared. Additionally, as part of the same bonus action that you take to activate your warden form, you may cast this spell. If you cast wrath of nature in this way, it will not require concentration, and the area of effect remains centered on and moves with you throughout the duration of the spell. You may only cast this spell in this way once per long rest.

Homebrew / Subclasses

Cleric Prime

Cleric Prime

Description

Now THIS is some real fuckin’ divinity

Prerequisites: Cleric 20

Proficiencies

When you take this prestige class, choose two more skills from the Cleric skill proficiencies. You are proficient in both of those skills.

Ascendant Spellcasting

Additionally when you take this prestige class, you gain a new set of spell slots to fuel your spells. You gain spell slots as per the Cleric table based on your prestige level minus 20. When you prepare spells for the day, you may now prepare a number of spells equal to your prestige level + your wisdom modifier.

You learn one cleric cantrip of your choice, and one additional cleric cantrip at 24th and 30th level.

Expanded Divine Domain

When you select this prestige class, choose one domain related to your deity. You may choose the same divine domain, or you may choose a new one to reflect the different aspects of your deity. Your choice grants you domain spells and other features when you choose it at 21st level. It also grants you additional ways to use Channel Divinity at 22nd level, and additional benefits at 6th, 8th, and 17th levels.

Embraced Divinity

Connection to your deity has reached new heights at 22nd level. You gain one extra use of your channel divinity, and regain all expended uses of your channel divinity after you complete a short rest.

You gain an additional use of your channel divinity at 33rd level.

Ability Score Improvement

When you reach 24th level, and again at 28th, 32nd, 36th, and 39th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two of your ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can’t increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.

Font of Divinity

When you reach 25th level, your deity supplies you with overflowing power, ensuring you are always able to carry out your duties. Whenever you roll initiative and have no uses of your channel divinity, you regain one use.

Blessed Might

At 29th level your divine might is bolstered. If you have the Divine Strike feature, the extra damage increases by an amount equal to your wisdom modifier. If you have the Potent Spellcasting feature, the extra damage increases by 2d8.

Greater Divine Intervention

When you reach 30th level, your deity is more swayed to intervene in more personal matters. When you use Divine Intervention for the purposes of replicating a spell, you only need to complete one long rest before you can use the feature again.

2024 Clerics are no longer limited to spells of 5th level or lower, but are still limited to spells on the cleric spell list or their domain spells.

Purge Undead

At 34th level, nearly all of your divine abilities carry with them the ability to deter the undead. When you cast a cleric spell of 1st level or higher, or use any channel divinity option, you may choose to activate your turn undead feature without expending a use of your channel divinity.

Sanctuary

When you reach 38th level, you always have the demiplane and word of recall spells prepared. Both of these count as cleric spells for you and do not count towards your number of spells prepared. When you cast Word of Recall, you can designate warp to one of any number of previously designated locations, though they must still meet the spell’s requirements.

Master Divine Intervention

At 40th level, your deity will never leave you in your times of need. You will always regain your use of divine intervention when you finish a long rest, regardless of what you use it for.

2024 Clerics will no longer be stricken with the sickness from the wish spell if they use it to do anything other than replicating spells of 8th level or lower.
