Features:

  • 3rd Level - Spellcasting
  • 3rd Level - Vexing
  • 9th Level - Delicate Deception
  • 13th Level - Binding Words
  • 17th Level - Archfeys Guile

3rd Level - Spellcasting

When you reach 3rd level, you augment your martial prowess with the ability to cast spells.

Cantrips

You learn three cantrips: Vicious Mockery and two other cantrips of your choice from the warlock or bard spell list. You learn another warlock or bard cantrip of your choice at 10th level.

Spell Slots

The Fey Duelist Spellcasting table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your warlock or bard spells of 1st level and higher. To cast one of these spells, you must expend a slot of the spell's level or higher. You regain all expended spell slots when you finish a long rest.

For example, if you know the 1st-level spell Charm Person and have a 1st-level and a 2nd-level spell slot available, you can cast Charm Person using either slot.

Spells Known of 1st Level and Higher

You know three 1st-level warlock or bard spells of your choice, two of which you must choose from the enchantment and illusion spells on the warlock or bard spell list.

The Spells Known column of the Fey Duelist Spellcasting table shows when you learn more warlock or bard spells of 1st level or higher. Each of these spells must be an enchantment or illusion spell of your choice, and must be of a level for which you have spell slots. For instance, when you reach 7th level in this class, you can learn one new spell of 1st or 2nd level.

The spells you learn at 8th, 14th, and 20th level can come from any school of magic.

Whenever you gain a level in this class, you can replace one of the warlock or bard spells you know with another spell of your choice from the warlock or bard spell list. The new spell must be of a level for which you have spell slots, and it must be an enchantment or illusion spell, unless you're replacing the spell you gained at 3rd, 8th, 14th, or 20th level from any school of magic.

Spellcasting Ability

Charisma is your spellcasting ability for your warlock or bard spells, since you learn your spells through dedicated study and memorization. You use your Charisma whenever a spell refers to your spellcasting ability. In addition, you use your Charisma modifier when setting the saving throw DC for a warlock or bard spell you cast and when making an attack roll with one.

Spell save DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Charisma modifier

Spell attack modifier = your proficiency bonus + your Charisma modifier

3rd Level - Vexing

Start at 3rd level, when you cast Vicious Mockery, you can now cast it as a Bonus Action. Additionally, the first attack roll, ability check or saving throw you make against an affected creature before the end of your next turn is made with advantage.

9th Level - Delicate Deception

Starting at 9th level, you can weave Fey Magic into your movements and attacks, enhancing them. Once per turn, you can modify a rogue feature to add an additional effect, as listed below:

  • Fey Attack: Sneak Attack deals an additional 1d6 psychic damage. This additional damage is increased at 13th (2d6) level & 17th (3d6) level.

  • Elusive Action: Immediately before or after using Cunning Action, a 5ft cube surrounding you becomes Heavily Obscured to everyone except you until the start of your next turn.

  • Distant Dodge: Whenever you use Uncanny Dodge after being hit with an attack, you may teleport up to 10 feet to an unoccupied space you can see.

You can use this ability a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of once), and regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest. You can also regain uses by expending a spell slot for each use you want to restore (no action required).

13th Level - Binding Words

At 13th level, you can weave a magical enchantment into your words, undermining and binding those that hear it. As an action you can speak a word infused with fey magic to a creature within 30 feet that can hear you, forcing them to make a Wisdom saving throw (DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Charisma modifier). On a failed saving throw, fey magic binds it, and the only actions that it can take before the end of its next turn are the Attack (one weapon attack only), Dash, Disengage, or Hide action. If the target succeeds on its saving throw, it has no hint that you tried to bind it.

Any creature under the effect of Vicious Mockery cast via your Vexing feature automatically fails the saving throw for this feature.

Once you use this ability, you cannot use it again until you finish a short or long rest. You can also regain uses by expending a spell slot (3rd level) for each use you want to restore (no action required).

17th Level - Archfeys Guile

Starting at 17th level, as an action you can make a Charisma (Persuasion or Deception) check against a creature that you can see that isn’t incapacitated, contested by a Wisdom (Insight) check. If you succeed, for the next minute, any deception or suggestions you make towards that creature are suffused with fey magic, and that creature remembers the conversation in a way that favors your intent, even creating temporary artificial memories that support your statements. Any contradictory evidence to oppose your deception is disregarded and they will rationalize any memories or statements from friends as illogical or even possible attempts to deceive them. When presented with facts contradicting your deception, the target can repeat the Wisdom (Insight) check, ending the beguiling effects on a success.

This benefit lasts for 10 minutes or until you successfully use this feature against a different creature. The effects of your magic linger on the target for up to 1 hour after you’ve successfully used this feature, or until they have a Dispel Magic or Remove Curse cast upon them. If the target remained beguiled for the full duration, the affected memories and altered perceptions become permanent.

Homebrew / Subclasses

Fighter Subclasses

Fighter Subclasses

Blood Knight

The blood knight is the title given to an eldritch knight who chooses to delve into the taboo discipline of hemomancy, or the magic of controlling blood and life force. These warriors thrive in the heart of battle where the blood flows thickest, using it to enhance their offensive and defensive capabilities.

Combat Hemomancy

Starting at 3rd level when you choose this archetype, you gain access to a series of hemomantic abilities that allow you to use the blood of your enemies to your advantage.

When you damage a creature that has blood within 30 feet of you with a weapon attack, you gain a special die called a blood die, which is a D6.  You can have a number of these dice up to a maximum equal to your proficiency bonus. Creatures that do not have blood do not generate blood dice, and you do not gain blood dice from attacks that are modified by blood dice.

You can expend blood dice to perform a number of hemomantic abilities described at the end of this features description.

Each time a hemomantic ability asks you to expend your blood dice, you can choose how many you want to roll and gain a benefit based on what you rolled.

Hemomantic Abilities

Combat Regeneration. At the start of your turn, you can spend blood dice to gain temporary hit points. Roll the dice you spend, add them together, and gain temporary hit points equal to the total, replacing any temporary hit points you already have.

Crimson Strike. You can use the Attack action to make a special melee attack, a crimson strike. If you're able to make multiple attacks with the Attack action, this attack replaces one of them. You brandish the weapon used in the technique and make a melee attack with it against one creature within 15 feet of you. On a hit, the target takes magical piercing, bludgeoning, or slashing damage equal to the total of the blood dice you spent.

Blood Shell. When you are hit by an attack, you can use your reaction to spend blood dice. Roll the dice you spend, add them together, and increase your AC by the amount equal to the total rolled against that attack.

Blood Clotting. As a bonus action, you can spend blood dice to throw blood onto a surface at a range of 15 feet and have it stick in a 25 ft. square. Any creature that starts its turn in that area or that enters that area during its turn must make a Strength saving throw with a DC of 10 + the amount you roll on your blood dice (A maximum DC of 8 + proficiency bonus + Strength or Dexterity modifier). On a failed save, the creature's speed is reduced to zero until the start of their next turn.

Sense Life

At 7th level, you gain advantage on wisdom (perception) checks to spot and track enemies that have blood in their veins. In addition, your ability to sense blood can be so precise that you have advantage wisdom (insight) checks to tell if someone is lying to you.

Blood-Fueled Overdrive

At 10th level, when you use your indomitable feature, you can expend one blood die and add it to the roll.

Hemomantic Precision

At 15th level, you have a very tight control over blood you spill. You can re-roll one blood die once whenever you roll them for a hemomantic ability.

Bloody Tyrant

At 18th level, when you hit a creature with an attack and have the maximum number of blood dice, you can expend them all to force the creature to make a Constitution saving throw with a DC of 8 + proficiency bonus + Strength or Dexterity modifier. On a failed save, the creature is paralyzed for 1 minute. At the end of each of its turns, the paralyzed target must make a Constitution saving throw at the end of each of its turns. On a successful save, this paralyzing effect ends.

Daredevil

The Daredevil fighter thrives on style, versatility and unpredictably. Their use of different weapon types makes them dangerous to any foe and they gain more confidence the more stylish their fighting is.

Daredevil impulse

Starting at 3rd level, every time you make an attack of a type different from the previous attack in the current combat, you gain one Style point. You have a maximum amount of style points equal to your proficiency bonus. When you roll Initiative your Style points reset to 0.

Attack types are classified as: Melee weapon attack, Ranged weapon attack and thrown attacks.

Style Points can be used to power your Flairs.

Flairs:

  • Wide attack: If you hit with a melee attack, you may spend 2 Style points to deal melee damage equal to half your Fighter level to all foes within 5 feet of your target.
  • Laser Focus: Spend 2 Style Points to gain advantage on your next attack roll.
  • Range Extender: You can add 10 feet to any ranged or thrown weapon's normal range for every point spent
  • Rush: Gain 10 feet of movement speed for each Style Point spent until the end of your turn.
  • Burst (4th level and up): As a bonus action, Spend 3 Style points to make a weapon attack.

Hotswap

At 3rd level, whenever you make an attack roll with a weapon, you can sheathe it and draw another in the same action. You can only do this once per action.

Fight or Flight

From 7th level you have a choice between staying in action and fighting defensively or moving around or to continue as is.  As a bonus action you can choose to either fight or flee from combat.

  • Fight: As a Bonus action you can give yourself a Bonus to your AC equal to the amount of Style Points you spend. This bonus lasts until the end of your next turn or until you are incapacitated. While Fight is active you cannot gain more Style points.
  • Flight: You can spend 2 Style points to disengage, you can't be targeted by opportunity attacks. You gain an additional 10 feet of movement until the end of your turn for every additional Style Point spent.

Double Trouble

You can choose an additional Fighting Style.

Additionally, using the Disengage, Dodge or Dash actions also builds your Style chain. For example: If you use a dodge action and make an attack on your next turn or vice versa you also gain a Style Point

Wild Rush

Starting at 15th level, when an enemy within 30 feet of you gets incapacitated or restrained you can use 2 Style Points as an reaction to dash straight toward the enemy. You move 10 feet for every point spent (minimum 2 points) and can spend additional Style for added Rush movement. You can  sheath your current weapon and draw another as part of the dash and make a single attack against that target.

Inferno Trigger

From 18th level, once per short rest you can expend 6 Style points as an action to trigger your Inferno action.

Inferno action: Can attack 6 times, ignore the loading and ammunition properties if the weapon has it. Any Critical hit deals an additional 10 damage of the weapons damage type. These attacks don't provide any Style points

Deadeye

The embodiment of grit, luck, and a well-placed shot, fighters who choose this martial archetype strive to emulate paradigms of accuracy. Deadeyes generally prefer fighting from comfortable ranges, employing the use of crossbows, firearms, and even throwing knives if a situation calls for them.

Perfect Sixth

Once per attack action beginning at 3rd level, when you make a ranged weapon attack roll against a creature, you can add a d6 to the result. You can add the d6 before or after seeing the results of the attack roll, but before the effects are applied. If the result of the d6 is a 6, you severely injure your target. Roll on the severe injury table to see the effect of the injury.

Severe Injury Table
2d6 Severe Injury
2 Shock. The target is stunned until the end of its next turn.
3 Fracture. The target can only take either an action, bonus action, or move on its next turn.
4 Punctured Lung. The target gains one level of exhaustion for the next minute.
5 Crushed Throat. The target cannot speak, use verbal components, or use any features that involve its voice until the end of its next turn.
6 Crushed Grip. The target drops anything it is currently holding, including grappled creatures.
7 Whiplash. The attack deals one additional die of weapon damage.
8 Broken Leg. The target’s movement speed is halved until the end of its next turn.
9 Embedded Ammunition. Until the end of its next turn, for every 5 feet the target moves, it takes 1d6 slashing damage.
10 Tear. The target has disadvantage on melee attacks until the end of its next turn.
11 Blind. The target is blinded until the end of its next turn.
12 Dead Shot. The triggering hit becomes a critical hit.

Before you make a ranged weapon attack, you can take a -5 penalty to the attack roll. If you hit, you apply a severe injury immediately. You can only apply one severe injury with each attack action.

A creature cannot be affected by the same severe injury more than once at a time, and a creature can expend one use of legendary resistance to ignore a severe injury’s effect.

Line ‘em Up

At 7th level, you become a master at hitting successive targets. When you take the attack action on your turn, each time you target a different creature than any other you’ve targeted this turn, you gain a cumulative +1 bonus to the attack roll.

Gambit

At 10th level, when you roll initiative, you can gambit a d4, d6, d8, or d10. Roll the chosen die and subtract it from your initiative. Until the end of your next turn, every creature below you in initiative takes extra damage when hit with your ranged attack rolls equal to the chosen die.

Duelist’s Aim

At 15th level, when you use the attack action to make a ranged weapon attack and you hit at least three consecutive attacks, your third attack inflicts a severe injury.

High Noon

At 18th level, you are adept at ending multiple targets at once. As an action, choose any number of targets that you can see within a cone the size of your weapon’s short range, up to 60 feet. You may make one ranged weapon attack against each target you chose inflicting the Dead Shot severe injury with each of them. You may use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, regaining all uses on a long rest.

Raven Knight

A Raven Knight is fearsome in battle, fusing martial prowess with strange abilities gifted by the Raven Queen. Many Raven Knights work alone, though some may find a small band of companions to aid them in battle, and some may even command and lead entire armies into battle. Masters of death, Raven Knights seek to protect those who cannot protect themselves from undeath and the afterlife. Powerful Raven Knights may even become champions of the Raven Queen, and thus champions of the battlefield.

Knowledge of Death

When you choose this Archetype at 3rd level, you gain proficiency in the Investigation and Medicine skills. Additionally, you can make Intelligence (Investigation) and Wisdom (Medicine) checks with advantage when attempting to determine the cause of death of a creature.

Soul Severing

At 3rd level, when you reduce a creature to 0 hit points you sever the connection of the creatures soul to its body. That creature cannot be turned into an undead. Additionally, as a reaction, when a creature is reduced to 0 hit points within 15ft of you you can empower your next attack with that creatures soul energy. Your next weapon attack deals additional necrotic damage equal to half your fighter level.

Feather Step

At 7th level, you move with the grace of the raven. Your walking speed increases by 10ft. Additionally, as a bonus action you gain a flight speed equal to your walking speed until the end of your turn, if you end your turn in midair you drop to the ground.

Queens Blessing

At 10th level, the Raven Queen grants you a blessing. You gain advantage on death saving throws, immunity to the frightened condition, and resistance to necrotic damage.

Deaths Embrace

At 15th level, when you or an ally critically hit a creature, you can use your reaction to add 3d10 necrotic damage to the attacks damage roll.

Duty in Death

At 18th level, when you are reduced to 0 hit points or killed outright you can use your reaction to make a weapon attack against the creature that killed you. On a hit you critically hit that creature and regain hit points equal to the damage dealt. You can do this once per long rest.

Revised Arcane Archer

Arcane Archer Lore

At 3rd level, you learn magical theory or some of the secrets of nature -- typical for practitioners of this elven martial tradition. You choose to gain proficiency in either the Arcana or the Nature skill, and you choose to learn either the prestidigitation or the druidcraft cantrip.

Arcane Shot

At 3rd level, you learn to unleash special magical effects with some of your shots. When you gain this feature, you learn two Arcane Shot options of your choice (see Arcane Shot Options below).

Once per turn when you fire an arrow or bolt from any bow as part of the Attack action, you can apply one of your Arcane Shot options to that piece of ammunition. You decide to use the option when the ammunition hits a creature, unless the option doesn't involve an attack roll. You have a number of uses equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses of it when you finish a short or long rest.

You gain an additional Arcane Shot option of your choice when you reach certain levels in this class: 7th, 10th, 15th, and 18th level. Each option also improves when you become a 15th-level fighter.

Arcane Shot Options (Revised)

The Arcane Shot feature lets you choose options for it at certain levels. The options are presented here in alphabetical order. They are all magical effects, and each one is associated with one of the schools of magic.

If an option requires a saving throw, your Arcane Shot save DC equals 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Intelligence modifier.

Banishing Arrow

You use abjuration magic to try to temporarily banish your target to a harmless location in the Feywild. The creature hit by the arrow must also succeed on a Charisma saving throw or be banished for 1 minute, or until you release the magic as a free action. While banished in this way, its speed is 0, and it is incapacitated. The affected creature can make a Charisma saving throw at the end of their turn, ending the effect on a success. At the end of the duration, the target reappears in the space it vacated or in the nearest unoccupied space if that space is occupied.

After you reach 15th level in this class, a target also takes 4d6 force damage when the arrow hits it.

Beguiling Arrow

Your enchantment magic causes this arrow to temporarily beguile its target. The creature hit by the arrow takes an extra 2d6 psychic damage, and choose one of your allies within 30 feet of the target. The target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw, or it is charmed by the chosen ally for 1 minute or until you release the magic as a free action. The target or any creature that can reach it can use its action to remove the arrow with a successful Strength (Athletics) check against your Arcane Shot save DC, ending the effect on a success. Additionally, this effect ends early if the chosen ally attacks the charmed target, deals damage to it, or forces it to make a saving throw.

The psychic damage increases to 4d6 when you reach 15th level in this class.

Bursting Arrow

You imbue your arrow with force energy drawn from the school of evocation. The arrow detonates after your attack. Immediately after the arrow hits the creature, the target and all other creatures within 10 feet of it take 2d6 force damage each and succeed on a Strength saving throw against your Arcane Shot save DC, or be knocked prone.

The force damage increases to 4d6 when you reach 15th level in this class. (edited)

Enfeebling Arrow

You weave necromantic magic into your arrow. The creature hit by the arrow takes an extra 2d6 necrotic damage on hit, as well as at the start of each of their turns for 1 minute or until you release the magic as a free action. The target must also succeed on a Constitution saving throw, or the damage dealt by its weapon attacks is halved until the start of your next turn. The target or any creature that can reach it can use its action to remove the arrow with a successful Strength (Athletics) check against your Arcane Shot save DC, ending the effect on a success.

The necrotic damage increases to 4d6 when you reach 15th level in this class.

Grasping Arrow

When this arrow strikes its target, conjuration magic creates grasping, poisonous brambles, which wrap around the target. The creature hit by the arrow takes an extra 2d6 poison damage, its speed is reduced by 10 feet, and it takes 2d6 slashing damage the first time on each turn it moves 1 foot or more without teleporting. The target or any creature that can reach it can use its action to remove the brambles with a successful Strength (Athletics) check against your Arcane Shot save DC. The brambles last for 1 minute, until you use another option, or until you release the magic as a free action.

The poison damage and slashing damage both increase to 4d6 when you reach 15th level in this class.

Piercing Arrow

You use transmutation magic to give your arrow an ethereal quality. When you use this option, you don’t make an attack roll for the attack. Instead, the arrow fires forward in a line, which is 5 foot wide and 30 feet long, before disappearing. The arrow passes harmlessly through objects, ignoring cover. Each creature in that line must make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes damage as if it were hit by the arrow, plus an extra 2d6 piercing damage. On a successful save, a target takes half as much damage. This option lasts for 1 minute, until you use another option, or until you release the magic as a free action.

The piercing damage increases to 4d6 when you reach 15th level in this class.

Seeking Arrow

Using divination magic, you grant your arrow the ability to seek out your target, allowing the arrow to curve and twist its path in search of its prey. When you use this option, you don’t make an attack roll for the attack. Instead, choose one creature you have seen in the past minute. The arrow flies toward that creature, moving around corners if necessary and ignoring three-quarters cover and half cover. If the target is within the weapon’s range and there is a path large enough for the arrow to travel to the target, the target must make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, it takes damage as if it were hit by the arrow, plus an extra 2d6 force damage, and you learn the target’s current location and distance for 1 hour or until you release the magic as a free action. On a successful save, the target takes half as much damage, and you only learn the targets current location and distance for one round. The target or any creature that can reach it can use its action to remove the arrow with a successful Strength (Athletics) check against your Arcane Shot save DC, ending the effect on a success.

The force damage increases to 4d6 when you reach 15th level in this class. (edited)

Shadow Arrow

You weave illusion magic into your arrow, causing it to occlude your foe’s vision with shadows. The creature hit by the arrow takes an extra 2d6 psychic damage, and it must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or be unable to see anything farther than 5 feet away for 1 minute or until you release the magic as a free action. The target or any creature that can reach it can use its action to remove the arrow with a successful Strength (Athletics) check against your Arcane Shot save DC, ending the effect on a success.

The psychic damage increases to 4d6 when you reach 15th level in this class.

Magic Ammunition

At 7th level, you gain the ability to infuse ammunition with magic. Whenever you fire a nonmagical arrow from a bow, you can make it magical for the purpose of overcoming resistance and immunity to nonmagical attacks and damage. The magic fades from the ammunition immediately after it hits or misses its target.

Curving Shot

At 7th level, you learn how to direct an errant ammunition toward a new target. When you make an attack roll with a magic ammunition and miss, you can use a bonus action to reroll the attack roll against a different target within 60 feet of the original target.

Quick-draw Shot

Starting at 15th level, your magical archery makes your movements swift. Whenever you hit a target with an Arcane Shot you can use your bonus action to make another ranged weapon attack against the same target using the same weapon.

Eldritch Mastery

At 18th level, your mastery of blending magic with archery teaches you to infuse your arrows with even greater magic, as well as combining them for greater effect.

Once per attack action, you can infuse a single arrow with two different arcane shot options, excluding piercing shot, having the target be affected by and taking damage from both shots. However when doing this you expend two uses of your Arcane shot.

You have two uses of this ability, and you regain all expended uses of it when you finish a long rest.

Weapon Master

Deft Grip

Starting at 3rd level, after you make a weapon attack using the attack action you can use a free action to swap to another weapon.

When you attack with a weapon, you receive a bonus to the attack based on the list below, however you may only benefit from a single bonus once per turn, even if your attack misses; You can however receive an additional bonus if you attack with a different weapon that causes a different type of damage. Ranged weapons do not benefit from Deft Grip, nor do generic “Elemental Weapons” (which collectively count as a single weapon), consumable items that grant additional damage, or spells.

Deft Grip DC: 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Dexterity modifier

Damage Type Effect Bonus Damage
Bludgeoning The heavy blow causes both stone and steel to crumple. Additional 1d6 damage if AC ≥ 15 1d6 or 2d6 bludgeoning damage
Piercing A swift thrust gives you extra reach. +5ft attack range 1d6 piercing damage
Slashing A swift slice carves through lightly armored opponents with ease. Additional 1d6 damage if AC ≤ 15 1d6 or 2d6 slashing damage
Acid The acid begins to eat away at flesh and damage armor. Dexterity saving throw. Upon a failure, the creature’s AC is reduced by 1 until the end of your next turn. At level 10 the AC reduction is increased to 2, and at level 20 it is increased to 3. 1d6 acid damage
Cold Frost begins to coalesce around the creature’s body, restricting movement. Constitution saving throw. Upon a failure the creature’s speed is reduced by half until the end of your next turn. 1d6 cold damage
Fire Flames engulf the target. Dexterity saving throw. Upon a failure the creature is set ablaze and takes 1d6 fire damage at the end of their turn. The fame can be put out by a suitable liquid or by using an action to extinguish it. 1d6 fire damage
Force The weapon impacts with incredible force. Strength saving throw. Upon a failure the creature is knocked prone. 1d6 force damage
Lightning Lightning arcs to the flesh of another creature on impact. A random hostile creature within 10ft is chosen. That creature makes a dexterity saving throw. Upon a failure, they take the full damage of the attack. 1d6 lightning damage
Necrotic The necrotic energy tears apart facsimiles of life. Doubled damage against temporary hp and creatures not in their original form (wildshape, poly, true-poly, shapechange, etc). Any damage that goes over the temp HP or the HP of the transformed creature is not doubled when applied to their HP/base form. 1d6 necrotic damage
Poison Poison seeps into the wound. Constitution saving throw. Upon a failure the creature suffers from the poisoned condition. The creature can repeat the save at the end of each of their turns. 1d6 poison damage
Psychic Psychic damage racks the mind of the target. The creature has disadvantage on any concentration saving throws for the damage caused by this attack. 1d6 psychic damage
Radiant Radiant light bursts from the weapon. Constitution saving throw. Upon a failure the creature is blinded. The creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns. 1d6 radiant damage
Thunder A thundercrack roars forth from the weapon. Constitution saving throw. Upon a failure the creature is deafened. The creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns. 1d6 thunder damage

Flowing Stance

At 3rd level, when you successfully hit another creature with a weapon that benefits from the Deft Grip bonus you receive a +1 to hit and to damage for your next attack if your next attack will also benefit from the Deft Grip bonus. These bonuses stack then reset to zero at the end of your turn.

Rapid Strike

Starting at 7th level, you learn to trade accuracy for swift strikes. If you take the Attack action on your turn and have advantage on an attack roll against against one of the targets, you can forgo the advantage for that roll to make an additional weapon attack against that target, as part of the same action. You can do so no more than once per turn.

Shatter the Horde

Starting at 10th level you can expend a use of your Action Surge to cause your melee attacks to strike any number of creatures within 5 feet of you, with a separate attack roll for each target. This benefit lasts for a single turn. This does not prevent a second Action Surge from being used on the same turn.

Focused Strike

Starting at level 15 you can expend a use of your Action Surge to focus all of your ability into a singular strike. Instead of making multiple attacks, you make a single attack against a target, and if it hits that attack is essentially multiplied by however many attacks you have remaining, including bonuses for each attack from Deft Grip and Flowing Stance; Additionally, after you use this ability, you can make no more attacks on the same turn. This does not prevent a second Action Surge from being used on the same turn. This ability must be declared prior to knowing if the Focused Strike hits.

Omnipath

At level 18, attunement slots for weapons that require attunement can shared in a single slot however, you can not dual wield weapons that require attunement without using a second slot, you receive no benefit from the weapon when it is not in use (such as auras or other passive buffs), and you can use one of the weapons at a time.

Revised Purple Dragon Knight

Rallying Cry

When you choose this archetype at 3rd level, you learn how to inspire your allies to fight on past their injuries.

When you use your Second Wind feature, each creature of your choice within 15 feet of you regains hit points equal to your fighter level, provided that the creature can see or hear you.

Royal Envoy

A Purple Dragon knight serves as an envoy of the Cormyrean crown. Knights of high standing are expected to conduct themselves with grace.

At 7th level, you gain proficiency in the Persuasion skill. If you are already proficient in it, you gain proficiency in one of the following skills of your choice: Animal Handling, Insight, Intimidation, or Performance.

Your proficiency bonus is doubled for any ability check you make that uses Persuasion. You receive this benefit regardless of the skill proficiency you gain from this feature.

Inspiring Surge

Starting at 10th level, when you use your Action Surge feature, you can choose an amount of creatures equal to half your fighter level (rounded down) within 15 feet of you. Those creatures can make one melee or ranged weapon attack with their reaction, provided that they can see or hear you.

Starting at 18th level, the range of your inspiration increases to 30 feet.

Bulwark

Beginning at 15th level, you can extend the benefit of your Indomitable feature to your allies. When you decide to use Indomitable to reroll an Intelligence, a Wisdom, or a Charisma saving throw and you aren't incapacitated, you can choose an amount of creatures equal to half your proficiency bonus (rounded down) within 30 feet of you that also failed its saving throw against the same effect. If those creatures can see or hear you, they can reroll their saving throw and must use the new roll.

Loyalty to the Crown

Starting at 18th level, when you target an ally with any of your bannerette features, that ally gains advantage on the next attack roll, ability check, or saving throw it makes until the end of its next turn.

Jade Lord

Throughout the continent of kara-tur, one mineral stands above all else in terms of status. Where in the west you would display decadence with gold, in the east, the truest symbol of power is jade. Legends tell of warriors embellished with regality, often proud in status and seeped in regality. The Jade Lords of Shou Lung were legendary figures that displayed power and wealth in equal measure, fighting with both honor and flair.

Regal Countenance

Even at 3rd level, you carry yourself with grace and nobility. You gain proficiency in either Persuasion or Intimidation. If you already have both of those proficiencies, you can choose a different proficiency instead.

Jade Shards

At 3rd level, the gutteral flow of combat splinters jade around you. When you hit a creature with a weapon attack or a creature hits you with an attack, a jade shard splinters off of you and orbits you for the duration. You can only have a number of jade shards equal to half your fighter level (rounded up) at a time. When initiative ends, any remaining jade shards drop to the floor and disappear.

You can expend any number of these shards to take special actions called jade tricks. If the trick requires the target to make a saving throw, the DC is calculated as follows:

Jade Trick DC

= 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Strength or Dexterity modifier (your choice)

If you’re able to make multiple attacks with the Attack action, a trick replaces one of them. You can only use a trick once per attack action.

Jade Blade.

Make a melee attack with a melee weapon you are holding against a target within range. On a hit, the target suffers the weapon attack’s normal effects and takes a number of d6s in additional damage equal to the amount of shards spent.

Nephrite Burst.

Make a ranged or thrown weapon attack (your choice) against a target within 120 feet of you. The attack deals a number of d8s of piercing damage equal to the amount of shards spent.

Jadeite Blast.

Choose a point you can see within 60 feet of you. Creatures within 10 feet of that point must make a Dexterity saving throw or take a number of d10s in slashing damage equal to the jade shards spent.

Mystic Stone

At 7th level, the jade you create is fortified. Damage from jade tricks count as magical for the purposes of overcoming resistance and immunity to non-magical damage.

Jade Armor

At 10th level, you learn to pull in the jade shards orbiting you to use as armor. As a bonus action, you can expend any number of jade shards to create jade armor. While this armor is active, you have half cover, or 3/4ths cover if you spent five or more shards. This armor lasts for a number of rounds equal to the jade shards spent or until the end of initiative.

Verdant Generosity

At 15th level, you are able to protect allies with your jade armor as well. If any ally is attacked or is forced to roll a saving throw, you can use your reaction to expend any amount of jade shards and encase them in jade armor. This armor confers the same amount of cover as your jade armor feature, but only lasts until the end of that ally’s next turn.

Jade Emperor

At 18th level, you learn a new jade trick.

Jadestorm.

By expending any amount of jade shards, you can create a jadestorm around you in a 20 foot radius, designating any creatures you wish to be unaffected by it. The storm travels with you, with its area being lightly obscured. An affected creature that begins its turn within the jadestorm takes bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage equal to the shards expended. Additionally, their AC is reduced by half the expended amount (rounded down) until the start of their next turn or until they leave the jadestorm. The jadestorm lasts for the expended amount of rounds or until the end of initiative.

Death Knight

The archetypal death knight focuses on honing negative energies into their attacks and integrating necromancy into their fighting style. While death knights don’t have to be tragic and dark, the energies used often corrupts the user

Death Tokens

During combat, when you kill a hostile creature, you gain a number of death tokens equal to half the creature's proficiency bonus (rounded down), which can be used to fuel your death knight abilities. Once a creature grants a death token, it may not do so until you finish a long rest. You may have a maximum number of death tokens equal to 1 + half your fighter level, rounded down, which last until your next long rest.

Undead Soldier

Starting at 3rd level, you learn to reanimate undead in the midst of combat. As an action, you may expend 2 death tokens to infuse negative energy into a corpse or pile of bones that you can see to turn it into an undead soldier. The corpse becomes a zombie or skeleton which lasts until your next long rest, where it then turns into dust. Undead soldiers share initiative with each other, but roll initiative on their own. As a bonus action, you may give them commands. If no commands are given, they do their best to defend themselves and you. Your undead soldiers additionally count as you for the purpose of gaining death tokens.

You may have a total number of undead soldiers equal to half your proficiency bonus (rounded down).

Rebuke of the Damned

Starting at 3rd level, you can expend one death token as a reaction when you or an undead soldier within 30ft of you is hit by an attack. Roll a number of d4 dice equal to your proficiency bonus, and reduce the damage taken by the total rolled, dealing the total back to the attacker as necrotic damage.

Sink or Swim

Starting at 7th level, you learn various uses for your death tokens.

  • As a bonus action, you can use a death token and select an undead soldier within 30 feet of you. Then, spend and roll up to a number of hit dice equal to your proficiency bonus. The undead soldier regains hit points equal to the total of the dice rolled.
  • As an action, you can spend a number of death tokens and target a undead soldier or corpse within 30 feet of you. Every creature within 10 feet of the undead soldier or corpse must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw (DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Constitution modifier) or take 1d4 necrotic damage and 1d4 fire damage per death token expended.
  • Once per turn, you may expend a death token slay an undead soldier early, instantly turning it into dust. When doing so, you may make an additional attack before the end of your next turn when you take the attack action.

Cull the Horde

Starting at 10th level, you can use death tokens to empower you and your undead.

  • Your undead soldiers gain a bonus to attack rolls and saving throws equal to half the death tokens you currently carry, rounded down.
  • Attacks done by your undead soldiers count as magical for the purpose of overcoming defenses.
  • You may spend two death tokens when creating an undead soldier to grant the soldier proficiency in light, medium, and heavy armor, shields, and martial weapons.

Black Speech

Starting at 15th level, You learn to speak, read, and write Black Speech, which can be used to communicate with undead and can not be learned through traditional means. Most undead lack the intelligence to convey or understand sophisticated concepts, but a non-hostile undead could relay what it has seen or heard in the recent past. This ability doesn't grant you friendship with undead, though you can combine this ability with gifts to curry favor with them as you would with any nonplayer character.

Additionally, having access to this speech grants you resistance to necrotic damage.

Grave Warden

Starting at 18th levels, when using your undead soldier feature, you can expend 6 death tokens to create a sword wraith warrior instead. In addition, you can use death tokens to do the following:

  • Armor of Bones: You may spend a death token when creating an undead to create large spikes of bones which protrude out the created undead. When a creature attacks that undead with a melee attack, they take magical piercing damage equal to your constitution modifier.
  • Lament of the Lost: As a bonus action, you can spend a death token to reposition any of your undead soldiers within 30 feet of you. You determine the new arrangement of these soldiers, and may swap your location with one of them.
Homebrew / Subclasses

Fighter Supreme

Fighter Supreme

Description

Fighter 2, the long awaited sequel

Prerequisites: Fighter 20

Proficiencies

When you take this prestige class, choose two more skills from the Fighter skill proficiencies. You are proficient in both of those skills.

Weapons Specialist

At 21st level you learn to better use the weapons that have served you up until this point. Choose three weapons. Your proficiency bonus is doubled for any attack roll you make using any of those weapons.

Supernatural Stamina

When you reach 22nd level your pool of stamina grows further with you. When you use your second wind feature to restore hit points, you add your prestige level to the healing instead of your fighter level.

Additionally, you gain one additional use of your second wind. You gain a 6th use at 30th level.

Expanded Martial Archetype

At 23rd level, you choose an archetype that you strive to emulate in your combat styles and technique. You may choose the same archetype, or choose a new one to expand your technique. The archetype grants you features at 23rd level, and again at 27th, 30th, 35th, and 38th level.

Ability Score Improvement

When you reach 24th level, and again at 26th, 28th, 32nd, 34th, 36th, and 39th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two of your ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can’t increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.

Using the optional feats rule, you can forgo taking this feature to take a feat of your choice instead.

Advanced Martial Training

When you reach 25th level your previous fighting styles grow to fit your new strengths. Any fighting style you gained through the fighter class or fighter subclass is improved in the following ways:

Advanced Archery:

You have a +2 bonus to attack rolls with ranged weapons. Your ranged weapons also deal one additional damage die.

Advanced Defense:

While you are wearing armor, you gain a +2 bonus to AC and saving throws.

Advanced Dueling:

When you are wielding a melee weapon in one hand and no other weapons, you gain a +2 bonus to damage rolls with that weapon. Additionally, creatures you hit with that weapon have disadvantage to hit anyone other than you until the start of your next turn.

Advanced Great-Weapon Fighting:

When you roll a 1 or a 2 on a damage die for an attack roll you make with a melee weapon that you are wielding in two hands, you can reroll the damage die. You may reroll the damage die if the result is a 1 or a 2 as many times as you like. The weapon must have the two-handed or versatile property to gain this benefit.

Advanced Protection:

When a creature you can see attacks a target other than you that is within 5 feet of you, you can use your reaction to cause that attack roll to automatically miss.

Advanced Two-Weapon Fighting:

When you engage in two-weapon fighting, you can make one additional attack with the second weapon as part of the same bonus action, adding your ability modifier to both if it does not already.

Tactical Reposition

Additionally at 25th level, your ability to maneuver the battlefield improves greatly. You can use your second wind bonus action as a reaction when a creature you can see within 60 feet of you ends their turn, using tactical shift as part of the same reaction.

Tactical Paragon

When you reach 29th level, your tactical mastery applies to a wider array of techniques. When you replace a weapon mastery with that feature, you can choose from the cleave and topple properties, in addition to push, sap, and slow.

Extra Attack

You attack five times instead of four when you take the attack action on your turn when you reach 31st level.

Unshakable

At 33rd level, your ability to resist outside effects to further focus on the battle is unmatched. When you use your Indomitable feature, the bonus to the saving throw is your prestige level rather than your fighter level.

Lifted Restraints

When you reach 37th level, your normal physical limits are no longer of concern to you. You gain one additional use of action surge, and can use it up to two times on a turn.

Additionally, Tactical Master and Tactical Paragon add the weapon mastery property without replacing the original, allowing you to use both mastery properties at once.

Advanced Weapon Mastery

When you reach 40th level, your mastery over weapons and combat knows no bounds, and your abilities can reflect that in full. Choose one weapon property to master. Whenever you activate that weapon mastery on any weapon, you can choose to activate its advanced effect instead.

Advanced Cleave:

If you hit a creature with a melee attack roll using this weapon, you can make a melee attack roll against each other creature of your choice in a cone aimed directly at the original target. The length of the cone is your weapon’s reach. On a hit, the additional creature takes the weapon’s damage, but don’t add your ability modifier to that damage unless that modifier is negative. You can make this extra attack only once per turn.

Advanced Graze:

If your attack roll with this weapon misses a creature, you can deal damage to that creature equal to half the weapon’s damage.

Advanced Nick:

When you make the extra attack of the Light property, you can make it as part of the attack action instead of as a bonus action. You can make this extra attack only once per turn. However, if you use your second wind, action surge, or indomitable features, you can make one weapon attack with that weapon as part of the feature.

Advanced Push:

If you hit a creature with this weapon, you can push the creature up to 20 feet straight away from you, regardless of its size.

Advanced Sap:

If you hit a creature with this weapon, that creature has Disadvantage on all attack rolls before the start of your next turn.

Advanced Slow:

If you hit a creature with this weapon and deal damage to it, you can reduce its speed to 5 feet until the start of your next turn. If the creature’s speed is already 5 feet or less, its speed is instead reduced to 0.

Advanced Topple:

If you hit a creature with this weapon, you can knock the creature prone. The creature must make a constitution saving throw (DC 8 + the ability modifier used to make the attack roll and your proficiency bonus). On a failed save the creature takes 1d6 bludgeoning damage + 1d6 more for each size category above medium.

Advanced Vex:

If you hit a creature with this weapon and deal damage to the creature, you have advantage on the next attack roll against that creature before the end of your next turn. You can then designate up to three allies, who gain advantage on their next attack roll against that target until the end of your next turn.

Homebrew / Subclasses

Fortune

Fortune's Shadow

Fortune's Shadow

In the clandestine world of rogues, a select few find themselves touched by the enigmatic forces of fate. These shadowy figures, known as Fortune’s Shadows, navigate the perilous dance of danger with a unique connection to the threads that weave destiny. Embracing Fortune’s Shadow means walking a razor’s edge, where every calculated risk and precise strike is a step further into the weave of destiny. Those who witness a Fortune’s Shadow in action may question whether their abilities are a result of skill, luck, or a mysterious force guiding their every move. One thing is certain – in the world of shadows and secrets, the Fortune’s Shadow is a rogue unlike any other, their fate entwined with the very essence of chance.

Features:

  • 3rd Level - Fortune's Gambit
  • 9th Level - Fateful Escape
  • 13th Level - Greater Gambit
  • 17th Level - Uncanny Fate

3rd Level - Fortune's Gambit

At 3rd level, upon dealing sneak attack damage with an even number, you gain a Fate Point.

As a bonus action, you can expend a Fate Point to make a daring gambit. Roll a d6 to determine the effect of the Gambit.

d6 : Gambit : Effect:

  1. Fleeting Shadows: You become invisible until the start of your next turn, you lose invisibility whenever you attack, or force a saving throw.
  2. Lucky Strike: Your next attack gains advantage.
  3. Evasive Maneuver: The next attack against you must be made with disadvantage.
  4. Weave of Fate: You gain temporary hit points equal to your rogue level.
  5. Deft Diversion: You can move up to half your speed without provoking opportunity attacks.
  6. Fortune's Grace: Add your proficiency bonus to your AC until the start of your next turn.

When rolling initiative your Fate Points reset to 0. You can a flip a coin, on a head to you gain a Fate point.

9th Level - Fateful Escape

At level 9 when you are reduced to 0 hit points and not killed outright, you can expend a Fate Point to cheat death. Instead of falling unconscious, you remain conscious with 1 hit point, and can immediately use a reaction to move up to your speed, without provoking opportunity attacks. Additionally, you gain advantage on Dexterity ability checks and saving throws for 1 minute, representing the temporary escape from fate’s grasp. Once you use this feature, you can’t use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

13th Level - Greater Gambit

At 13th level your Gambit's are improved. when you roll for a Gambit, you instead use the Greater gambit table:

d6 : Gambit : Effect:

  1. Persistent Shadows: You become invisible until the end of your next turn.
  2. Foretold Strikes: You gain advantage on attacks until the end of your next turn.
  3. Evasive Expert: You impose disadvantage on all attacks against you until the start of your next turn..
  4. Architect of Fate: You gain temporary hit points and regain hit point equal to your rogue level
  5. Perfect Diversion: You can move up to your speed without provoking opportunity attacks.
  6. Fortune's Gift: Add your proficiency bonus to your AC until the start of your next turn. Reduce damage taken from attacks by the same amount.

When rolling initiative you can now flip 2 coins, gaining a Fate point for each coin that lands on a head.

17th Level - Uncanny Fate

At level 17, when you use your uncanny dodge feature to halve damage received, you can spend a Fate Point to roll a d6. On an even result, the attacker takes force damage equal to the damage you received. On an odd result, you don't take any damage from the attack.

Homebrew / Subclasses

Grave Conclave Ranger

Grave Conclave Ranger

Description

Grave Wardens are grim trackers who walk the line between life and death. They hunt those who would unnaturally subvert the mortal cycle—powerful undead, necromancers, and entities that cling to a profane existence. By drawing on the cold, final energy of the grave, they imbue their weapons with grim power and attune their senses to the echoes of mortality.

Features:

  • 3rd Level - Grave Warden Magic
  • 3rd level - Armament of the Grave
  • 3rd level - Grim Hunter
  • 7th Level - Armament's Vigil
  • 11th Level - Soul's Vigil
  • 15th Level - Veil Walker

3rd Level - Grave Warden Magic

You learn an additional spell when you reach certain levels in this class, as shown in the Grave Warden Spells table. The spell counts as a ranger spell for you, but it doesn't count against the number of ranger s1pells you know.

Grave Warden Spells

Ranger Level | Spell

  • 3rd | Inflict Wounds
  • 5th | Ray of Enfeeblement
  • 9th | Speak with Dead
  • 13th | Blight
  • 17th | Negative Energy Flood

3rd level - Armament of the Grave

You learn a ritual that channels grim power into one weapon. Over 1 hour, which can be done during a short or long rest, you can touch one weapon you are proficient with. This weapon becomes your Bound Armament and gains the following benefits:

  • The weapon counts as magical for the purpose of overcoming resistance and immunity to nonmagical attacks and damage.
  • The weapon can be used as a spellcasting focus for your ranger spells
  • Once on each of your turns, when you hit a creature with an attack using this weapon, the attack deals an extra 1d6 necrotic damage. This extra damage increases to 2d6 at 11th level.

You can perform this ritual again to bond with a different weapon, which ends the bond on the previous one.

3rd level - Grim Hunter

Your attunement to the echoes of death sharpens your senses. You gain proficiency in your choice of either the Insight or Investigation skill. Additionally, you have advantage on Wisdom (Survival) checks to track Undead and Fiends, and on Wisdom (Insight) checks to discern the motives of those creature types.

7th Level - Armament's Vigil

Your Bound Armament glows faintly, visible only to you, whenever one or more Undead are within 120 feet of you.

Additionally, as a bonus action, or as a reaction when this glow first activates, you can project a 15-foot radius aura of censure. The aura lasts for 1 minute. When an Undead of your choice starts its turn within the aura, it must make a Wisdom saving throw against your ranger spell save DC. On a failed save, it has disadvantage on all attack rolls until the start of its next turn.

You can use this aura a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (a minimum of one). You regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

11th Level - Soul's Vigil

Your constant exposure to the energies of undeath fortifies your mind and body. You gain the following benefits:

  • You have advantage on saving throws against being frightened or charmed.
  • You gain resistance to necrotic damage.
  • When a creature you can see within 30 feet of you drops to 0 hit points, you can use your reaction to gain temporary hit points equal to your Wisdom modifier + your Ranger level.

15th Level - Veil Walker

You can step through the veil between life and death. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

  • Grave Step. As a bonus action, you can expend one use of this feature to teleport up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space you can see. When you arrive, each creature within 5 feet of you (other than yourself) must make a Dexterity saving throw against your spell save DC. A creature takes *3d10* necrotic damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.
  • Ethereal Reprisal. As a reaction when you are hit by an attack, you can expend one use of this feature to teleport up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space you can see. If this movement takes you out of the attack's range, the attack misses. The creature that attacked you must then make a Dexterity saving throw against your spell save DC, taking *3d10* necrotic damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.
Homebrew / Subclasses

Greaser

Greaser

Greaser

Since the dawn of humanity, there has always been a frontier to conquer. Between the wastes of the east, the fires of the hells, and the vastness of the astral plane, there has always been those that dared to tread the road less traveled. Traversing each regional obstacle brings with it a unique solution— the hellfire engines of Avernus, the spelljammers of the astral sea, and the machinations inspired by the great inventor Kwalish, all formed to blaze a trail through every path they come across.

Through the use of arcane influence and artificing prowess, a new school of thought has arisen among artificers; why spend your days walking through the most hazardous conditions when you can drive, sail, or fly through them instead? Thus, under the influence of vehicles from all different planes, the most ingenious of traveling artificers got to work.

Features:

  • 3rd Level - Bonus Proficiency
  • 3rd Level - Greaser Spells
  • 3rd Level - Arcane Vehicle
  • 5th Level - Extra Attack
  • 9th Level - Enhanced Modifications
  • 15th Level - Overdrive

3rd Level - Bonus Proficiency

When you adopt this specialization at 3rd level, you gain proficiency with smith’s tools. If you already have this proficiency, you gain proficiency with one other type of artisan’s tools of your choice. In addition, you gain proficiency in land and water vehicles

3rd Level - Greaser Spells

Starting at 3rd level, you always have certain spells prepared after you reach particular levels in this class, as shown in the Greaser Spells table. These spells count as artificer spells for you, but they don’t count against the number of artificer spells you prepare.

Artificer Level Spells

3rd Level - Burning Hands, Fog Cloud

5th Level - Locate Object, Dust Devil

9th Level - Slow, Stinking Cloud

13th Level - Hallucinatory Terrain, Sickening Radiance

17th Level - Passwall, Rary's Telepathic Bond

3rd Level - Arcane Vehicle

By 3rd level, you’ve successfully managed to create your first vehicle for traversal. At the end of a long rest, you may create a vehicle by choosing one of each of the following vehicle mod options below. The vehicle is a large magical object that can be mounted as if it were a creature, after which it acts as a controlled mount. It shares its turn with you, and can only take the dash and disengage actions. It is immune to psychic damage and uses your saving throw bonuses when applicable.

If the mending spell is cast on it, it regains 2d6 hit points. If it has been destroyed within the last hour, you can use your smith’s tools as an action to repair it, provided you are within 5 feet of it and you expend a spell slot of 1st level or higher. The vehicle returns to working order after 1 minute with half of its hit points restored.

At the end of a long rest, you can create a new arcane vehicle if you have your smith’s tools with you. If you already have an arcane vehicle from this feature, the first one is immediately destroyed. The vehicle is also destroyed if you die.

Vehicle Mods

Each vehicle can only have one vehicle mod of each option listed below active at one time. At the end of a short rest, you can use your smith’s tools to replace one vehicle mod of your choosing with another eligible of the same category. If a vehicle mod has prerequisites, you must meet them to learn it. A level prerequisite refers to your level in this class.

Vehicle Frame

Frame Type | Level | Speed | Hit Points | AC

  • Trailblazer| N/A | 60ft.| 5 x artificer level | 13 + PB
  • Seafarer | 5th level | 10ft., swim 50ft. | 4 x artificer level"\t"| 12 + PB
  • Cloudstrider | 9th level | 0ft., fly 40ft. | 3 x artificer level | 11 + PB

Vehicle Archetype

Archetype | Prerequisite | Details

  • Assault | N/A | The vehicle’s maximum hit points increase by 2 x artificer level.
  • Transport | N/A | The vehicle can hold up to 500lbs of items in a 5ft. cube of space.
  • Transit | 5th level | The vehicle’s speed increases by 10ft.

Mounted Weapon

Weapon | Prerequisite | Details

  • Skewer | N/A | Melee. The skewer deals 1d6 piercing damage for every 10ft. of movement used immediately before the attack, up to 3d6 piercing damage.
  • Glob Launcher | N/A | Ranged (60/120). The glob launcher deals 1d10 bludgeoning damage. A creature hit by this weapon has its movement speed reduced by 10ft. until the end of its turn.
  • Gas Sprayer | 5th level |15ft. cone. Creatures in the area must make a Constitution save against your spell save DC or take 2d8 poison damage and be poisoned until the end of their next turn.
  • Bombard | 9th level | Ranged (30/60). The bombard deals 2d6 fire damage. When you hit with an attack, all creatures within 5ft. of the target must succeed on a Dexterity save or take 2d6 fire damage.
  • Sol Spear | 15th level | Ranged (40/80.) The sol spear does 1d8 radiant damage. The first creature hit by the spear each turn must succeed on a Constitution save or be blinded until the end of its next turn.

Weapons mounted on your vehicle are simple weapons you are proficient in that can only be used by yourself while you are mounted. If the weapon requires an attack roll, you can add your Intelligence modifier, instead of your Strength or Dexterity, to the attack and damage rolls. Use your spell save DC for any saving throw related to your weapon. These weapons can be infused.

Specialized Modification

Mod | Prerequisite | Details

  • Bladed Edge |N/A| Creatures you move within 5ft of take 5 slashing damage. A creature can only take this damage once per turn.
  • Seatbelts | N/A |You automatically succeed on any checks you make to remain mounted.
  • Improved Treading | 5th level | Your vehicle’s movement ignores difficult terrain.
  • Sealed Cockpit | 5th level | You ignore the effects of extreme heat and extreme cold while mounted on your vehicle, and have access to a constant supply of fresh air.
  • Overtuned Engine | 9th level | The vehicle’s speed increases by 20ft.
  • Grappling Hook | 9th level | You can use an action to launch a grappling hook attached to a chain up to 50ft. away.
  • Heavy Shielding | 9th level | You have half cover while riding your vehicle.
  • Self-Repair Module | 15th level | If your vehicle has lower than half of its maximum hit points, it regains 5 hit points at the start of each of your turns. |Drop Compartments|15th level|Adds six small compartments that can each release their contents (such as caltrops/ball bearings) on the ground within 5ft. of the vehicle as a bonus action.

5th Level - Extra Attack

Beginning at 5th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn. Additionally, attacks from your mounted weapons count as magical for the purposes of overcoming resistance and immunity to nonmagical attacks and damage.

9th Level - Enhanced Modifications

At 9th level, you’re able to fit more modifications on your vehicle. You may now have two specialized modifications and two mounted weapons active at once.

15th Level - Overdrive

At 15th level, you learn to overclock your vehicle to force it to perform past its peak temporarily. As a bonus action, you can send your vehicle into overdrive for one minute. Doing so doubles its movement speed, makes it immune to all damage, and allows you to make up to three attacks with your mounted weapon each turn. At the end of the minute, your vehicle is immediately destroyed. You must finish a long rest to use this feature again, unless you spend a spell slot of 5th level or higher to use it again.

Homebrew / Subclasses

Harbinger

Harbinger

Harbingers are foretellers of death and destruction, serving as a warning for disaster and ruin. Oftentimes, they take it upon themselves to cause the catastrophes themselves.

For Whom the Bell Tolls

At 3rd level, you learn the toll the dead and sacred flame cantrips, which counts as a spiritualist cantrip for you. When you cast a spiritualist cantrip, the DC is equal to your Art save DC.

Whenever you activate your spirit tether, the target has disadvantage on the saving throw against spiritualist cantrips you cast until the end of your turn.

Harbinger Arts

Also at 3rd level, you gain access to new spirit arts that reflect your penchant for bringing about tragedy.

Mark of Suffering

As an action, you can spend 1 spirit point to attempt to imbue your target with a Suffering mark. The target must make a Wisdom saving throw or be marked and take 2d6 necrotic damage.

Whenever you cast a spiritualist cantrip on the marked target, you may trigger this spirit art’s effect again without spending spirit points.

Mark of Ruination

As an action, you can spend 1 spirit point to attempt to imbue your target with a Ruination mark. The target must make an Intelligence saving throw or be marked and subtract 1d6 from each saving throw it makes against your harbinger arts or spiritualist cantrips until the end of its next turn.

Whenever you cast a spiritualist cantrip on the marked target, you may trigger this spirit art’s effect again without spending spirit points.

Mark of Tragedy

As an action, you can spend 1 spirit point to attempt to imbue your target with a Tragedy mark. The target must make a Charisma saving throw or take 1d6 psychic damage each time it attacks or casts a spell until the end of its next turn.

Whenever you cast a spiritualist cantrip on the marked target, you may trigger this spirit art’s effect again without spending spirit points.

Enervating Marks

At 6th level, whenever the target of your spiritualist cantrips has a Suffering, Ruination, and Tragedy mark, you can add an additional 2 damage dice to the cantrip’s damage roll.

The Ninth Bell Tolls True

At 13th level, you find new ways of inflicting woe upon foes. The damage from your Suffering and Tragedy marks increase by 2d6.

In addition, when a target fails its saving throw against one of your marks, you can consume the mark. The mark is removed from the target, and you regain 2d6 hit points.

Master Harbinger

At 18th level, you master your prowess at bestowing tribulation. You learn the following spirit art:

Mark of Calamity

As an action, you can spend 5 spirit points to imbue your target with a Calamity mark. The target must make a Constitution saving throw or be marked, taking 4d6 force damage and suffering one level of exhaustion.

Whenever you cast a spiritualist cantrip on the marked target, you may trigger this spirit art’s effect again without spending spirit points. This mark can count as a Suffering, Ruination, or Tragedy mark for the purposes of satisfying the requirements of your enervating marks feature, but only one of the three at a time.

Homebrew / Subclasses

House of Bishops

House of Bishops

Dabblers in true arcane magic, supplementing perfected cantrips with real spells.

The House of Bishops adopts warmages with arcane potential, expanding on essential magic principles with traditional spellcasting. Such warmages might easily be confused for wizards or sorcerers, for they don the same garb and wield many of the same spells, but the warmage focus on perfection still takes precedence over garnering a vast array of magic.

Spellcasting

When you choose this house at 3rd level, you gain the ability to cast spells more potent than cantrips.

Spell Slots. The Bishop Spellcasting table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your spells of 1st level and higher. To cast one of these spells you must expend a slot of the spell’s level or higher. You regain all expended spell slots when you finish a long rest.

Spells Known of 1st Level and Higher. You know three 1st-level wizard spells of your choice, two of which you must choose from the conjuration and evocation spells on the wizard spell list. The Spells Known column of the Bishop Spellcasting table shows when you learn more wizard spells of 1st level or higher. Each of these must be a conjuration or evocation spell of your choice, except for the spells you learn at 8th, 14th and 20th level, and must be of a level for which you have spell slots.

Whenever you gain a level in this class, you can replace one of the wizard spells you know with another spell of your choice from the wizard spell list. The new spell must be of a level for which you have spell slots, and it must be a conjuration or evocation spell unless you are replacing the spell you gained at 3rd, 8th, 14th or 20th level.

Spellcasting Ability. Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for these spells.
