Bishop Spellcasting — spell slots per spell level.

Arcane Study

At 3rd level, you gain proficiency in two of the following skills of your choice: Arcana, History, Investigation, Medicine or Religion.

Flourished Casting

Also at 3rd level, your battlefield craft carries over into your greater magic. When you deal damage to a creature with a warmage spell of 1st level or higher, you can apply a Flourish to that creature as though the spell were a cantrip. This still counts as your one Flourish for the turn.

Mystical Companion

At 7th level, you learn the find familiar spell and can cast it as a ritual. The spell doesn’t count against your number of spells known. When you cast the spell, you can choose one of the normal forms for your familiar or one of the following special forms: pseudodragon or sprite.

Siege Casting

At 10th level, your warmage spells deal double damage to objects and structures. Additionally, when you cast a warmage spell that requires you to make a ranged spell attack roll, the spell’s range is doubled.

Spell Sculpting

Starting at 15th level, when you cast a warmage spell of 1st level or higher that affects other creatures you can see, you can choose a number of them up to your Intelligence modifier. The chosen creatures automatically succeed on their saving throws against the spell, and they take no damage if they would normally take half damage on a successful save.

Arcane Dominance

At 18th level, you learn to feed your greater magic back into the fundamentals. As a bonus action, you can expend a spell slot of 2nd level or higher to regain one expended use of your Overcharge feature. Once you use this feature, you can’t use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

Homebrew / Subclasses

House of Fortune

House of Fortune

Gamblers with their fingers on the scales of fate.

The House of Fortune throws out the warmage convention of meticulous, deliberate spellcasting in favour of wild magic that presses the odds. Everything these warmages touch — their bursts of power, their weighted dice, their marked decks — can fail horribly, so it is auspicious that they usually keep their fingers on the scales of fate. They have mastered not only a repertoire of cantrips but techniques to manipulate fortune itself, allowing them to risk everything and, more often than not, come out on top.

Bonus Proficiencies

When you choose this house at 3rd level, your light fingers and unscrupulous tactics help you win the day. You gain proficiency in either the Deception or the Sleight of Hand skill (your choice), and with dice sets and playing card sets. Additionally, you can use your Intelligence modifier in place of Charisma when you make a Charisma (Deception) check.

Fate Dice

At 3rd level, you gain four Fate Dice, which are d6s. Whenever you make an attack roll, ability check, saving throw or damage roll, you can expend one Fate Die and add it to the roll. You can wait until after you make the roll before deciding to expend the die, but you must decide before the GM determines the roll’s outcome.

Once you expend a Fate Die, it passes to the GM, who can spend it to add it to a roll made by an NPC or a monster. Once the GM has spent a die, it passes back to you, and so on. When you finish a long rest, you regain all of your expended Fate Dice, whether or not the GM has used them.

Beginning at 7th level, you have six Fate Dice instead of four.

Roll of Fate

Also at 3rd level, you can expend two of your Fate Dice as an action and roll them, creating a chaotic surge of energy. Consult the Roll of Fate table for the effect. Where the table calls for a saving throw, the DC equals your spell save DC.

2d6 Effect
2–3 You gain temporary hit points equal to twice your warmage level, which last for 1 minute, and you regain one of the two Fate Dice you expended.
4–5 You teleport up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space you can see.
6–7 Each creature of your choice within 30 feet of you gains a +1 bonus to Armor Class and to saving throws until the start of your next turn.
8–9 One creature you can see within 60 feet of you takes 4d6 necrotic damage, and you regain hit points equal to half the damage dealt.
10–11 You become invisible until the end of your next turn, as per the invisibility spell.
12 You cast the lightning bolt spell, using your spell save DC, and you regain both of the Fate Dice you expended.

Loaded Dice

By 7th level, you can subtly cheat your dice. Once on each of your turns when you roll a d6, you can flip the die upside down. On a balanced d6 the top and bottom faces add up to 7, so the new result is 7 minus the old one.

Twisted Fate

Starting at 10th level, the winds of chance follow your rolls rather than the reverse. When you make an attack roll or an ability check with disadvantage on your turn, you can attempt to invert fate as a bonus action: expend a Fate Die and roll it. On a 5, you ignore disadvantage on the roll. On a 6, you have advantage on the roll instead.

Roll the Bones

Beginning at 15th level, you can channel the chaotic energy of your dice in an instant. As a reaction when you take damage from a creature you can see, you can expend two Fate Dice to make a Roll of Fate.

Steal Luck

Starting at 18th level, when you roll initiative, roll a d6. You steal that many Fate Dice back from the GM.

Homebrew / Subclasses

House of Kings

House of Kings

Leaders and commanders with a wide array of manoeuvres at their disposal.

Warmages who train in the House of Kings specialise in tactics and strategy, learning age-old manoeuvres that give them the edge in combat. Natural-born leaders, Kings work best with a cadre of supporters to perform their tactics and overwhelm the enemy. More than any other warmage, those of this house treat life and death as a game of strategy to be understood and conquered.

Bonus Proficiencies

When you choose this house at 3rd level, you gain proficiency with medium armor, as well as with battleaxes, lances, longswords, tridents and warhammers.

Battle Tactics

At 3rd level, you learn stratagems that are fuelled by special dice called battle dice.

Battle Dice.

You have two battle dice, which are d8s. A battle die is expended when you use it. You regain all of your expended battle dice when you finish a short or long rest. Your battle die changes and more battle dice become available as you gain levels in this class, as shown on the Battle Dice table.

Warmage Level Battle Dice
3rd 2d8
7th 3d8
13th 4d8
18th 4d10

Using Battle Dice.

Once on each of your turns, you can expend a battle die to perform a stratagem of your choice. Your stratagem options are detailed at the end of this house description.

Saving Throws.

When a stratagem calls for a saving throw to resist its effects, the saving throw DC equals your spell save DC.

Lead from the Front

Starting at 7th level, you and each friendly creature within 120 feet of you that can see you ignore nonmagical difficult terrain.

Rally the Line

Starting at 10th level, when a friendly creature you can see within 30 feet of you fails a saving throw against a spell, you can use your reaction to expend a battle die and add it to that saving throw, potentially turning the failure into a success.

Stratagem: Checkmate

At 15th level, you learn the Checkmate stratagem. When you hit a creature with a weapon or spell attack, you can use your bonus action and expend a battle die to direct one of your companions to strike. Choose a friendly creature who can see or hear you and is within reach of the creature you hit. That creature can immediately use its reaction to make one weapon attack or to cast a cantrip that requires an attack roll, adding the battle die to the attack’s damage roll.

Grandmaster

At 18th level, when you roll initiative, choose a number of friendly creatures up to your Intelligence modifier within 60 feet of you that can see or hear you. Each chosen creature gains a battle die; you don’t expend your own battle dice for this feature. Once within the next 10 minutes, a chosen creature can expend that battle die when it makes an attack roll, ability check, saving throw or damage roll, adding the die to the roll. The creature can wait until after it makes the roll before deciding to expend the die, but must decide before the GM determines the roll’s outcome. A creature can have only one battle die from this feature at a time.

Stratagems

The stratagems are presented in alphabetical order.

  • Blitz. As a bonus action when you hit a creature with an attack, you can expend one battle die to manoeuvre one of your comrades into a more advantageous position. Choose a friendly creature within 60 feet that can see or hear you. That creature can use its reaction to move up to half its speed without provoking opportunity attacks from the target of your attack.

  • Check. As a bonus action when you hit a creature with an attack, you can expend one battle die to force that creature to flee. The target must make a Charisma saving throw; a creature immune to being frightened automatically succeeds. On a failed save, the target must immediately use its reaction, if available, to move up to half its speed directly away from you.

  • Flash of Brilliance. When you make an Intelligence or Wisdom check, you can expend one battle die and add it to the check. You can use this stratagem after the roll but must decide before the GM says whether the check succeeds.

  • Gambit. When you hit a creature with an attack, you can expend one battle die to give your allies an opening. The next creature other than you to make an attack against that target adds the battle die to its attack roll.

  • Mystic Counsel. As a bonus action, you can expend one battle die to give counsel to a creature that can hear you within 30 feet of you. Once in the next minute, when that creature makes a saving throw against a spell, it can roll the battle die and add the result to the save.

  • Stalemate. As a bonus action when you hit a creature with an attack, you can expend one battle die to hold that creature in place. Until the end of its next turn, the target can’t willingly move unless it first takes the Disengage action.

Homebrew / Subclasses

House of Knights

House of Knights

Frontline combatants who forge their swords and armour out of raw force.

The House of Knights has a long and storied tradition of melding melee combat and swordplay with the warmage’s simple spellcasting. Unlike other warriors, however, Knights rarely carry swords or shields into battle, for they can forge both out of magical force at a moment’s notice.

Bonus Proficiencies

When you choose this house at 3rd level, you gain proficiency with medium armor and martial weapons.

Force Breastplate

At 3rd level, plates of magical force reinforce your armour. While you are wearing light armor or are under the effects of the mage armor spell, you can add your Intelligence modifier, instead of your Dexterity modifier, to your Armor Class. While you are wearing medium armor, you can do the same, but the bonus you add this way can’t exceed +3.

Mystical Weapon

Also at 3rd level, you learn the force weapon cantrip, which doesn’t count against your number of cantrips known. Additionally, you possess a weapon made entirely of magical force. Whenever you would draw a weapon, you can summon this weapon to your empty hand and shape it into any simple or martial weapon of your choice. It deals force damage on a hit instead of its normal damage type. Whenever the weapon leaves your hand, it vanishes into a pocket dimension until you summon it again.

Flurry of Blades

Beginning at 7th level, when you cast a cantrip that allows you to make multiple spell attacks, such as force weapon or magic daggers, you can use your bonus action to make one additional spell attack with that cantrip. You can do so only once on each of your turns.

Knight’s Ward

Starting at 10th level, you can forge a hardened magical barrier between you and your foes. As a bonus action, you gain temporary hit points equal to your warmage level plus your Intelligence modifier, which last for 1 minute. Once you use this feature, you can’t use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

Tactical Maneuver

At 15th level, once on each of your turns, you can use up to 30 feet of your movement to teleport to an unoccupied space you can see.

Field of Blades

Starting at 18th level, you can summon a whirlwind of mystical weapons for a flurry of strikes. As an action, you can make a melee spell attack against each creature of your choice that you can see within 15 feet of you, with a separate attack roll for each target. On a hit, a target takes 2d10 force damage. Warmage Edge can enhance the damage of only one of these attacks, and you can’t apply an Overcharge to this feature.

Homebrew / Subclasses

House of Light

House of Light

9th-level Conjuration (Cleric, Celestial Patron, Druid, Sage, Sorcerer)

Casting Time: 1 action

Range: Sight

Components: V, S, M (a diamond worth 5,000gp)

Duration: Concentration, 1 minute

A pillar of radiance rises from a point you can see, enclosing an area of up to a 360ft radius, and 1 mile high in bright light. When you cast this spell, creatures of your choice must make a Constitution saving throw or be blinded for 1 minute. They may repeat the saving throw at the end of their turn, ending the blindness on a success.

Each round that you maintain concentration produces an additional effect, in addition to the last:

  • Healing Waves (Round 2): Creatures and objects within the area regain hit points equal to your spellcasting modifier. Creatures of an alignment you choose receive no healing and instead take the same amount as radiant damage so long as they have no fewer than half their hit points total.
  • Community (Round 3): Up to 5 willing creatures within the area can each sacrifice a number of hit points up to half your level. These hit points are represented as a pool of temporary hit points that can be divided as you choose among any number of creatures that you can see within range. Creatures can only sacrifice hit points once over the duration of the spell.
  • Vitality (Round 4): Creatures and objects within the area gain your choice of either bludgeoning, piercing or slashing damage resistance until the start of your next turn. Creatures of an alignment you choose receive no resistances and instead lose resistances, if any, of the chosen damage types until the start of your next turn.
  • Guiding Light (Rounds 5): Creatures within the area gain a 1d4 bonus to ability checks and saving throws until the start of your next turn. Creatures of an alignment you choose instead receive a 1d4 penalty to ability checks and saving throws until the start of your next turn.
Homebrew / Subclasses

House of Pawns

House of Pawns

Versatile cantrip masters who can assume the tricks of any house.

By far the most prominent warmage house is that of the Pawns. Warmages who join this house learn to stretch their skill with cantrips to its limits. A Pawn can master any cantrip or trick known to the other houses, for they embody the adaptability to which all warmages aspire.

Promotion

When you choose this house at 3rd level, you gain the adaptability of the quintessential warmage. You learn one warmage trick of your choice, which doesn’t count against your number of warmage tricks known. Additionally, whenever you learn a warmage trick, you can choose one that has another Warmage House as a prerequisite, as long as you meet all of the trick’s other prerequisites.

Adaptive Arcanist

Also at 3rd level, you learn to emulate the spellcasting prowess of other warmages. When you finish a short or long rest, choose one warmage cantrip. You know that cantrip, and it doesn’t count against your number of cantrips known, until you choose a different one with this feature.

Pawn Storm

Beginning at 7th level, if you target a creature with a cantrip, that creature can’t make opportunity attacks against you for the rest of the turn, whether or not you deal damage with the cantrip.

Additional Arcane Fighting Style

Also at 7th level, you can choose a second option from the Arcane Fighting Style class feature. You can’t take the same Arcane Fighting Style option more than once.

Adaptive Flourish

Starting at 10th level, when you use your Cantrip Flourishes feature you can apply any Flourish, not only those you know. You still apply only one Flourish on each of your turns.

Opening Move

Starting at 15th level, you add your Intelligence modifier to your initiative rolls. Additionally, when you roll initiative and you aren’t surprised, you can move up to your speed.

Fundamental Mastery

Starting at 18th level, your command of the fundamentals is total. Once on each of your turns, you can apply a second Flourish to a warmage cantrip.

Homebrew / Subclasses

House of Rooks

House of Rooks

Arcane assassins, scouts and spies.

The clandestine members of the House of Rooks make adept spies, assassins and scouts, though they might just as easily pick up jobs run by rogues and brigands. In addition to their suite of cantrips, Rooks are light on their feet and know a few tricks for opening doors in utter silence.

Rook Strike

Starting when you choose this house at 3rd level, you can use a bonus action to gain advantage on the next attack roll you make on your turn. Alternatively, you can impose disadvantage on a saving throw a creature makes against a warmage spell you cast before the end of your turn.

Once you use this feature, you can’t use it again until you finish a short or long rest, or until you reduce a creature to 0 hit points with a warmage cantrip.

Rasp

Also at 3rd level, you gain proficiency in the Stealth skill. Additionally, you can cast the knock spell at will without expending a spell slot. When you cast the spell in this way, it has a casting time of 1 minute and its casting is completely silent.

Arcane Acrobat

At 7th level, you gain proficiency in the Acrobatics and Sleight of Hand skills, and you can add your Intelligence modifier to Dexterity (Stealth) checks you make. Additionally, when you fall and aren’t incapacitated, you can subtract up to 60 feet from the fall when calculating falling damage.

Fleeting Decoy

Beginning at 10th level, as a reaction when you take damage from a creature you can see, you raise a defensive illusion to protect yourself from further harm. The next attack roll made against you before the start of your next turn has disadvantage.

Elusive Step

By 15th level, you are extremely difficult to pin down. Your movement doesn’t provoke opportunity attacks, and you can move through the space of any creature as though it were difficult terrain.

Flash of Feathers

Starting at 18th level, you can cast the invisibility spell once, targeting only yourself, without expending a spell slot or spell components. While you are invisible in this way, your speed is doubled, and you can make one attack or cast one warmage cantrip without ending the spell. Once you use this feature to cast invisibility, you can’t do so again until you finish a short or long rest.

Homebrew / Subclasses

Inner Elemental Sorcery (2024 Sorcerer)

Inner Elemental Sorcery (2024 Sorcerer)

Description

Your soul is bound to the primal weave of the four great elements—Fire, Earth, Water, and Air. Each spell you cast leaves a lingering Strain, a trace of elemental magic you can mold into disruptive bursts or overwhelming force.

Inner Elemental Spell List

When you gain a level in this class, you can choose from this list in addition to the sorcerer list. These spells count as sorcerer spells for you and don’t count against the number of sorcerer spells you know.

Sorcerer Level | Spells

  • 3rd | Chromatic Orb, Earth Tremor, Thunderwave, Melf’s Acid Arrow
  • 5th | Fireball, Lightning Bolt
  • 7th | Ice Storm, Stone Shape
  • 9th | Cone of Cold, Wall of Stone

Level 3 — Elemental Strains

You gain access to Strains, elemental charges tied to the four primal elements.

Elements & Damage Types:

  • Fire — Fire damage
  • Earth — Bludgeoning or Force damage
  • Water — Cold or Acid damage
  • Air — Thunder or Lightning damage

Gaining Strains

  • Whenever you deal damage with a spell and spend a sorcery as part of the spell, you gain 1 Strain of the matching element.
  • You can only gain 1 Strain per spell, even if it affects multiple creatures.
  • Strains reset to 0 on a short or long rest or if you don’t use any Strains for 1 minute.

Maximum Strains per Type:

  • 3rd Level: 1
  • 6th Level: 2
  • 14th Level: 3
  • 18th Level: 4

Strain Surge

You may only expend Strains when you also spend at least 1 Sorcery Point on the spell, you use a bonus action to surge a spell. The Strain adds an extra effect to the spell:

  • Fire: Target ignites, taking 1d6 fire damage at the start of its next turn.
  • Earth: Target’s speed is reduced by 10 ft. until your next turn.
  • Water: Target has disadvantage on the next Strength or Dexterity saving throw it makes before your next turn.
  • Air: Target cannot take reactions until the start of your next turn.

You can apply only one Strain Surge per spell at this level.

You do not gain Strain when you Surge

Level 6 — Chromatic Layering

You can now expend up to 2 Strains on a single spell, applying both single-element Surge effects to the same target.

If you choose two different elements, the combined magic creates an additional combo effect from the table below. This effect applies in addition to the normal Surge effects of both elements.

Two-Element Combo Table

Elements (2 Strains) Combo Effect
Fire + Earth A violent explosion scatters debris; creatures within 5 ft. of the target (other than the target) take 1d6 bludgeoning damage and must succeed on a Strength save or be knocked prone.
Fire + Water Steam burst blinds the target; it must succeed on a Constitution save or be blinded until the start of your next turn.
Fire + Air Superheated wind scorches and shoves; target takes an extra 1d8 fire damage and is pushed 10 ft. away from you.
Earth + Water Slick mud grips the target’s feet; target’s speed is halved and it must succeed on a Dexterity save or fall prone.
Earth + Air Shrapnel-laden gust; target takes an extra 1d8 piercing damage and must make a Constitution saving throw, on a fail loses concentration if concentrating.
Water + Air Icy wind chills the target’s bones; target takes an extra 1d8 cold damage and has disadvantage on attack rolls until the start of your next turn.

Save DC: All saves use your Sorcerer Spell Save DC.

Extra Damage Scaling: Extra damage dice from combo effects increase to 2d8 at 14th level.

Level 14 — Elemental Mastery

You can now expend up to 3 Strains on a single spell to induce a Major Strain effect, when you do so replace its normal Surge with a Major effect, these effects can only target a single creature

Major Strain Effects:

  • Fire: Dexterity save or the Target is engulfed in flames, taking 3d6 fire damage at the start of its turns for 1 minute, the target can make a dexterity saving throw at the end of it's turn to stop the burning.
  • Earth: Strength save or Target is restrained as stone or force binds them, the target can make a strength saving throw at the end of it's turn to free itself from its binding.
  • Water: Wisdom save or a single target is slowed (as the Slow spell) for 1 minute, the target can make a wisdom saving throw at the end of it's turn to end the effect.
  • Air: Constitution saving throw or the target is pushed 20 ft. and stunned for 1 minute the target can make a wisdom saving throw at the end of it's turn to end the effect.

If the initial saving throw is successful the target still suffers the effect from single surge table

Strain Conversion: As a bonus action, when you have at least 1 Strain of three different elements, you can expend all three to regain 1 Sorcery Point.

Level 18 — Chromatic Ascendance

When you have 4 Strains stored, you can absorb them as an action, entering an Ascendant Form for 1 minute. You automatically enter your Innate Sorcery state without spending Sorcery Points. While in an Ascendant Form, you gain resistance to the relevant damage types and special powers as listed below.

Single-Element Forms (4 Strains of one element)

Inferno Sovereign (4 Fire Strains)

  • Fire damage you deal ignores resistance.
  • Flame Wreath: A creature that touches you or hits you with a melee attack while within 5 feet of you takes 1d10 fire damage.
  • Blazing Ingress: You can enter a hostile creature’s space and stop there. The first time you enter a creature’s space on a turn, that creature takes 1d10 fire damage.

Earth Titan (4 Earth Strains)

  • You gain temporary hit points equal to twice your sorcerer level.
  • You cannot be pushed, knocked prone, or restrained unless you wish it.
  • Seismic Crash (1/turn): When you deal damage, you can cause the ground to quake in a 10-ft radius around the target. Each creature of your choice in the area must make a Strength save or be knocked prone and take bludgeoning damage equal to your Charisma modifier + your proficiency bonus.

Tide Monarch (4 Water Strains)

  • You gain a swim speed equal to twice your walking speed and can breathe underwater.
  • Water Form. You can enter an enemy's space and stop there. You can move through a space as narrow as 1 inch without expending extra movement to do so.
  • Crushing Pressure (1/turn): As an action you can attempt to crush a creature in your space, it must make a Strength saving throw (DC = your spell save DC). On a failed save, the creature takes 4d8 + your Charisma modifier bludgeoning damage and, if it is Large or smaller, it becomes grappled (escape DC = your spell save DC). While grappled in this way, the creature is restrained, begins suffocating unless it can breathe water. A creature within 5 feet of you can use its action to pull a grappled creature free, succeeding on a Strength (Athletics) check against your spell save DC. You can only grapple one creature in this way

Tempest Emperor (4 Air Strains)

  • You gain a flying speed equal to your walking speed.
  • When you deal lightning or thunder damage, you deal an extra 1d8 of that damage type, you can roll an extra d8 of damage if you roll an 8. This damage can do a max of 5d8 damage.
  • Storm Burst (1/turn): When you deal damage, you can unleash a 10-ft radius shockwave centered on the target. Creatures of your choice in the area take lightning damage equal to your Charisma modifier + your proficiency bonus and can’t take reactions until the start of your next turn.

Prismatic Overlord (1 of each Strain)

Choose 4 damage types from the following list:

fire, bludgeoning, cold, acid, lightning, and thunder damage

  • You gain resistance to the chosen types
  • Your spells ignore resistance to any of these damage types.
  • When you deal damage of one of the chosen damage types, you deal an extra 1d6 for each of the other damages (your choice each time).
  • Prismatic Pulse (1/turn): The first time you damage a single creature each turn, you unleash a burst in a 15-ft radius around it. Each creature of your choice in the area, excluding the target,  takes damage equal to your Charisma modifiers of each of the four elemental types

Homebrew / Subclasses

Jade Lord

Jade Lord

Jade Lord

Throughout the continent of kara-tur, one mineral stands above all else in terms of status. Where in the west you would display decadence with gold, in the east, the truest symbol of power is jade. Legends tell of warriors embellished with regality, often proud in status and seeped in regality. The Jade Lords of Shou Lung were legendary figures that displayed power and wealth in equal measure, fighting with both honor and flair.

Features:

  • 3rd Level - Regal Countenance
  • 3rd Level - Jade Shards
  • 7th Level - Mystic Stone
  • 10th Level - Jade Armor
  • 15th Level - Verdant Generosity
  • 18th Level - Jade Emperor

3rd Level - Regal Countenance

Even at 3rd level, you carry yourself with grace and nobility. You gain proficiency in either Persuasion or Intimidation. If you already have both of those proficiencies, you can choose a different proficiency instead.

3rd Level - Jade Shards

At 3rd level, the gutteral flow of combat splinters jade around you. When you hit a creature with a weapon attack or a creature hits you with an attack, a jade shard splinters off of you and orbits you for the duration. You can only have a number of jade shards equal to half your fighter level (rounded up) at a time. When initiative ends, any remaining jade shards drop to the floor and disappear.

You can expend any number of these shards to take special actions called jade tricks. If the trick requires the target to make a saving throw, the DC is calculated as follows:

Jade Trick DC

= 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Strength or Dexterity modifier (your choice)

If you’re able to make multiple attacks with the Attack action, a trick replaces one of them. You can only use a trick once per attack action.

Jade Blade

Make a melee attack with a melee weapon you are holding against a target within range. On a hit, the target suffers the weapon attack’s normal effects and takes a number of d6s in additional damage equal to the amount of shards spent.

Nephrite Burst

Make a ranged or thrown weapon attack (your choice) against a target within 120 feet of you. The attack deals a number of d8s of piercing damage equal to the amount of shards spent.

Jadeite Blast

Choose a point you can see within 60 feet of you. Creatures within 10 feet of that point must make a Dexterity saving throw or take a number of d10s in slashing damage equal to the jade shards spent.

7th Level - Mystic Stone

At 7th level, the jade you create is fortified. Damage from jade tricks count as magical for the purposes of overcoming resistance and immunity to non-magical damage.

10th Level - Jade Armor

At 10th level, you learn to pull in the jade shards orbiting you to use as armor. As a bonus action, you can expend any number of jade shards to create jade armor. While this armor is active, you have half cover, or 3/4ths cover if you spent five or more shards. This armor lasts for a number of rounds equal to the jade shards spent or until the end of initiative.

15th Level - Verdant Generosity

At 15th level, you are able to protect allies with your jade armor as well. If any ally is attacked or is forced to roll a saving throw, you can use your reaction to expend any amount of jade shards and encase them in jade armor. This armor confers the same amount of cover as your jade armor feature, but only lasts until the end of that ally’s next turn.

18th Level - Jade Emperor

At 18th level, you learn a new jade trick.

Jadestorm

By expending any amount of jade shards, you can create a jadestorm around you in a 20 foot radius, designating any creatures you wish to be unaffected by it. The storm travels with you, with its area being lightly obscured. An affected creature that begins its turn within the jadestorm takes bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage equal to the shards expended. Additionally, their AC is reduced by half the expended amount (rounded down) until the start of their next turn or until they leave the jadestorm. The jadestorm lasts for the expended amount of rounds or until the end of initiative.

Homebrew / Subclasses

Juggernaut

Juggernaut

Description

While in many cases using heavier two-handed weapons would put the user at a disadvantage defensively, Juggernauts utilize this augment to their offensive capabilities to compliment their defenses with little tradeoff.

Features:

  • 3rd Level - Martial Training
  • 3rd Level - Defensive Battering
  • 5th Level - Crushing Force
  • 13th Level - Demolishing Stance
  • 18th Level - Raw Terror

3rd Level - Martial Training

When you select this specialization at 3rd level, you gain proficiency in martial weapons.

3rd Level - Defensive Battering

Additionally at 3rd level, you have the ability to use larger weapons to block and deflect incoming attacks. While you are wielding a weapon with two hands, you gain a +1 bonus to your armor class. If the weapon has a magical bonus to attack and damage rolls, you can apply that same bonus to your armor class while wielding it in two hands.

7th Level - Crushing Force

Starting at 7th level, the sheer force you deliver with your attacks is enough to shatter your foe’s defenses. When you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can reduce the effectiveness of their armor, if they are wearing any, reducing their armor class by 3. Shields, and armor created by spells or other magic are unaffected, and you cannot reduce a creature’s armor class below what it would be without armor. This reduction lasts until the end of the creature’s next turn.

13th Level - Demolishing Stance

When you reach 13th level, your martial capability reaches new heights in conjunction with your defenses. While your defensive Stance is active, you gain a bonus to damage rolls with weapons equal to the armor class bonus given to you by your stance.

18th Level - Raw Terror

At 18th level, your very presence strikes terror into your foes. When a creature succeeds on a saving throw against your dueling stance, that creature becomes frightened of you until the start of their next turn.

Homebrew / Subclasses

Leviathan

Leviathan's Vessel Sorcerous Origin

Description

Water is the element of change. The creatures of the deep survive because they can adapt to anything — shifting, flowing, enduring. They are never truly alone; the ocean itself is community, a vast and endless embrace where life persists against crushing darkness.

The Leviathan is this truth given form: the abyssal power of the ocean, both merciless and sheltering, both devourer and protector. Those who carry its mark become vessels of unfathomable power, embodying the adaptability, love, and crushing might of the deep. A Leviathan Vessel suffocates breath, bends water into chains, and calls forth the jaws of the abyss to devour all who defy them.

Features:

  • 1st Level — Body of Water
  • Leviathan Vessel Expanded Spells
  • 6th Level — Crushing Currents
  • 14th Level — Abyssal Chains
  • 18th Level — Leviathan Ascendant

Leviathan Vessel Expanded Spells

The Leviathan Vessel lets you choose from an expanded list of spells whenever you learn a sorcerer spell. The following spells are added to the sorcerer spell list for you.

Sorcerer Level    Spells

1st    create or destroy water, fog cloud

2nd    blur, misty step

3rd    tidal wave, wall of water

4th    watery sphere, greater invisibility

5th    maelstrom, cone of cold

7th*    control water, dimension door

9th*    tsunami, gate

*Spells above 5th level count as Signature Spells. DMs may gate access to these as high-tier content

1st Level — Body of Water

You are bound to the ocean’s depths.

  • You gain a swim speed equal to your walking speed and can breathe underwater.
  • Once per long rest, or by spending 2 sorcery points, you can slip your form into liquid for an instant. As a bonus action, you may move through a space as narrow as 1 inch wide without squeezing.

6th Level — Crushing Currents

You can choke the life from others with conjured water.

As an action, choose one creature within 30 feet that needs to breathe. Spend 2 sorcery points and force the target to make a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC.

  • On a failed save, water floods their throat, making them gag. They cannot speak or cast spells with verbal components until the start of your next turn. If the creature is already underwater, it instead takes 2d6 cold damage as the abyss crushes its lungs.
  • On a success, the creature resists the effect.
  • Creatures that do not need to breathe are immune.

14th Level — Abyssal Chains

The abyss answers your will with shackles of water.

  • As an action, choose up to 3 creatures within 30 feet. Each must succeed on a Strength saving throw or become restrained by spectral chains of water until the start of your next turn.
  • While restrained in this way, a creature is treated as if caught within crushing currents.

Ocean’s Reach. You can spend 1 sorcery point as a bonus action to conjure and shape water manifestations. You may:

  • Create a platform of hardened water (Large, lasts 1 minute, supports creatures). The platform can hover and move up to 20 feet per round in any direction while you remain within 60 feet of it. You may mentally command its movement as a bonus action.
  • Form a wall of water (10 ft high, 10 ft wide, 1 ft thick, lasts 1 minute).
  • Summon a tendril of water to push or pull one creature within 20 feet up to 10 feet (Strength save negates).

18th Level — Leviathan Ascendant

You call forth the jaws of the deep.

Maw of the Abyss. As an action, you may spend 3 sorcery points to manifest the Leviathan’s spectral jaws. Choose a 30-foot line, 20 feet wide, within 60 feet.

    •    Each enemy in the line must make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC.

    •    On a failed save, the creature takes 2d10 force + 1d10 cold damage and is restrained inside the jaws until the start of your next turn.

    •    On a success, the creature takes half damage and isn’t restrained.

    •    Lingering Rift. After the jaws vanish, the ground (or space) in the area becomes a zone of churning abyssal water until the start of your next turn. Enemies treat this area as difficult terrain.

Homebrew / Subclasses

Leviathan

Leviathan's Vessel Sorcerous Origin

Leviathan's Vessel Sorcerous Origin

Water is the element of change. The creatures of the deep survive because they can adapt to anything — shifting, flowing, enduring. They are never truly alone; the ocean itself is community, a vast and endless embrace where life persists against crushing darkness.

The Leviathan is this truth given form: the abyssal power of the ocean, both merciless and sheltering, both devourer and protector. Those who carry its mark become vessels of unfathomable power, embodying the adaptability, love, and crushing might of the deep. A Leviathan Vessel suffocates breath, bends water into chains, and calls forth the jaws of the abyss to devour all who defy them.

Features:

  • Leviathan Vessel Expanded Spells
  • 3rd Level - Hydrokinesis Incarnate
  • 3rd Level - Dominion of Water
  • 6th Level - Binding Currents
  • 6th Level - Sculpted Water
  • 10th Level - Reactive Tide
  • 10th Level - Claim the Battlefield
  • 14th Level - Siphoning Cyclone
  • 18th Level - Leviathan’s Maw

Leviathan Vessel Expanded Spells

The Leviathan Vessel lets you choose from an expanded list of spells whenever you learn a sorcerer spell. The following spells are added to the sorcerer spell list for you.

Sorcerer Level    Spells

3rd    create or destroy water, fog cloud, tidal wave, wall of water

5th    maelstrom, cone of cold

7th    control water, dimension door

9th    tsunami, gate

3rd Level - Hydrokinesis Incarnate

You gain a swimming speed equal to your walking speed. You can breathe air and water. You gain resistance to cold damage.

3rd Level - Dominion of Water

As an action, you activate a 10-foot aura of water for 1 minute. Enemies treat it as difficult terrain. The first time each turn an enemy enters or starts its turn there, it takes magical bludgeoning damage equal to your Charisma modifier. Uses equal to proficiency bonus per long rest.

6th Level - Binding Currents

When a creature within 30 feet moves or fails a save against your Sorcerer spell, you may use your reaction. On a failed Strength save, it is restrained and takes 1d6 magical cold damage. On a success, it takes half damage and speed becomes 0. The restraint ends at the end of its next turn or earlier if it uses an action to break free. You can do this a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus per long rest.

6th Level - Sculpted Water

As a bonus action, create one water construct (Platform, Arm, or Mirror) within 30 feet for 1 minute. One at a time. Uses equal to your charisma modifier per long rest or 1 sorcery point. Constructs have AC 13 + PB and HP 10 + five times Sorcerer level.

10th Level - Claim the Battlefield

Once per turn when you cast a Sorcerer spell of 1st level or higher, one creature affected or within Dominion takes magical piercing damage equal to your Sorcerer level.

10th Level - Reactive Tide

When you or an ally within 30 feet is hit by an attack, use your reaction and spend 1 sorcery point to reduce damage by 2d8 + CHA. If the attacker is within 30 feet, push it 10 feet or move an ally 5 feet without opportunity attacks.

14th Level - Siphoning Cyclone

You wrench moisture from flesh and air alike, drawing it inward in a crushing spiral.

As an action, each creature of your choice within 20 feet of you must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failure, a creature takes 4d10 magical necrotic damage and is knocked prone. On a success, a creature takes half damage and is not knocked prone.

You then distribute hit points equal to half the total damage dealt, dividing them as you choose among yourself and any allies you can see within 30 feet. You can use this feature by spending 4 sorcery points.

Creatures that do not rely on moisture to survive have advantage on the saving throw, at the DM’s discretion..

18th Level - Leviathan’s Maw

As a bonus action, choose a point within 60 feet. Creatures in a 30-foot radius make Strength saves. Failures take 6d10 magical bludgeoning damage, are restrained until the end of your next turn, and pulled 15 feet inward. Successes take half damage. The area is difficult terrain and blocks teleportation until the start of your next turn. Once per long rest, regainable by spending 5 sorcery points.

Light Weaver

Light Weaver

Light Weaver

Your powers are drawn from the spark of light kindled within you. In places of great darkness, there are those born with an affinity for light, and every shadow has a source. The magic within you represents cosmic balance, flickering from radiance to darkness moment to moment.

Features:

1st Level - Trick of the Light

1st Level - Flickering Aura

6th Level - Refraction Shield

14th Level - Aura Magnification

18th Level - Light Weaver

1st Level - Trick of the Light

Starting at 1st level, you have darkvision out to a range of 60 feet. If you already have darkvision, it increases its range by 60 feet.

You learn the Light and Sacred Flame cantrips. At 3rd-level you learn the Darkness and  Faerie Fire spells, which are sorcerer spells and do not count against your spells known. They can cast normally, or by expending 2 sorcery points.

1st Level - Flickering Aura

Starting at 1st level, you can magnify the properties of light around you. At the end of a  short or long rest, you can choose whether your magic is light-shifted or dark-shifted.

While light-shifted you can use an action to emit an aura in a 15-foot radius around you.  This area is bright light. While the aura persist, you can use a bonus action to expand or reduce its radius by 5 feet, to a maximum of 30 feet each or a minimum of 10 feet. While dark-shifted you gain the same ability, but you project an aura of nonmagical darkness. This effect lasts for 1 minute, or until you are incapacitated.

Once used, you cannot use this ability again until you finish a short or long rest

6th Level - Refraction Shield

At 6th level, you can manipulate the light around you for protection. As a bonus action, you can spend 2 sorcery points to magically create a shield of light or dark. The shield lasts for 1 minute, or until you are incapacitated.

While this shield is in place, whenever a creature within 10 feet of you hits you with an attack, this shield flashes with searing energy, and the attacker takes 2d6 radiant damage if you are light-shifted or 2d6 necrotic damage if you are dark-shifted.

14th Level - Aura Magnification

While your Flickering Aura is active, you can now expand it up to 10 feet as a bonus action, up to a maximum of 60 feet. While within the aura, a number of creatures equal to your Charisma modifier also gain the benefit of your Refraction Shield, but no more than once per turn.

Additionally, you and those creatures have advantage on Wisdom (Perception) skill checks made while light-shifted, or Dexterity (Stealth) checks made while dark-shifted. You can add your proficiency bonus when making these skill checks by expending a sorcery point.

18th Level - Light Weaver

Embodying both aspects of Light and Dark, you gain resistance to both radiant and necrotic damage. Additionally, as part of the action to activate your Flickering Aura, you can transform yourself and gain the following benefits for up to 1 minute:

Upon activation or as part of the bonus action to expand or reduce it's radius, you can switch to either light-shifted or dark-shifted. Each creature of your choice within your aura must make a Constitution saving throw, taking 2d8 radiant and 2d8 necrotic damage and becoming blinded till the end of their next turn on a failure, or half as much damage and not being blinded in a success.

While your Radiant Shield is active, the radius of its effect increases to 30 feet, and you deal both the radiant and the necrotic damage when hit with an attack.

Once you use this action, you can’t use it again until you finish a long rest, unless you spend 5 sorcery points to use it again.

Love Domain

Love Domain

Love Domain

Clerics of the Love Domain serve gods of love, passion, and beauty, such as Sune, drawing on the purifying and enchanting power of the sacred waters, the Evergold. They are focused on protective healing, social grace, and captivating presence.

Features:

  • Love Domain Spells
  • 1st Level - Bonus Proficiencies & Evergold Touch
  • 2nd Level - Channel Divinity: Purifying Cascade
  • 6th Level - Flow of Beauty
  • 8th Level - Potent Spellcasting
  • 17th Level - Aura of Ideal Radiance

Love Domain Spells

Cleric Level | Spells

1st | Charm Person, Ceremony

3rd | Aid, Calm Emotions

5th | Beacon of Hope, Hypnotic Pattern

7th | Compulsion, Aura of Life

9th | Commune, Mass Cure Wounds

1st Level - Bonus Proficiencies & Evergold Touch

When you choose this domain at 1st level, you gain proficiency in the Persuasion skill and the Performance skill.

= Evergold Touch =

Starting at 1st level, whenever you use a spell of 1st level or higher to restore hit points to a creature, that creature gains **temporary hit points equal to your Cleric level + your Charisma modifier** (minimum of 1). These temporary hit points last for 1 hour.

2nd Level - Channel Divinity: Purifying Cascade

You can use your Channel Divinity to instantly cleanse and refresh those around you.

As an action, you present your holy symbol and evoke a wave of purifying golden energy. Choose any number of creatures within 30 feet of you. Any target you choose that is **Charmed, Frightened, or Poisoned** immediately ends that condition. Additionally, any creature whose condition is removed **regains a number of hit points equal to 1d6 + your Wisdom modifier.**

6th Level - Flow of Beauty

Starting at 6th level, you are perpetually surrounded by a faint glamour. You are under the constant effect of the *Disguise Self* spell, but you can only choose to appear as yourself at your most ideal and radiant. This effect cannot be dispelled by normal means.

Moreover, when a creature you can see within 30 feet of you succeeds on a saving throw against the **Charmed** or **Frightened** condition, you can use your reaction to grant that creature **advantage** on its next attack roll made before the start of your next turn.

8th Level - Potent Spellcasting

Starting at 8th level, you add your Wisdom modifier to the damage you deal with any cleric cantrip.

17th Level - Aura of Ideal Radiance

At 17th level, the Evergold flows through you in a constant, palpable wave of grace, affecting all who draw near. You gain the following benefits:

Sanctuary of Beauty.

When a creature within 30 feet of you makes an attack roll or targets you with a harmful spell, it must first succeed on a Wisdom saving throw against your Cleric Spell Save DC. On a failed save, the creature must choose a new target or the attack or spell is wasted. On a successful save, the creature is immune to this effect until the start of its next turn.This effect functions only if you haven't made an attack roll or cast a spell that affects an enemy creature since the end of your last turn. If you break this condition, the effect automatically resumes at the start of your next turn.

Protective Aegis.

When a friendly creature within 30 feet of you takes damage, you can use your reaction to reduce the damage taken by an amount equal to your Cleric level + your Wisdom modifier. You can use this reaction a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus. You regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

Homebrew / Subclasses

Maximum Rogue

Maximum Rogue

Description

Sneaky Sneak, Stabby Stab

Prerequisites: Rogue 20

Proficiencies

When you take this prestige class, choose any four more skills. You are proficient in all of those skills.

Precision Expert

Additionally when you take this prestige class your Sneak Attack improves to reflect greater precision and accuracy. Your Sneak Attack damage increases to a number of d6s equal to half your prestige level rounded up.

Superior Expertise

At 21st level, choose two of your skill proficiencies, or one of your skill proficiencies and one of your tool proficiencies. Your proficiency bonus is doubled for any ability check that uses either of the chosen proficiencies. If the skill already benefits from your expertise ability, your proficiency bonus is tripled instead.

At 6th level, you can choose two more of your proficiencies (in skills or tools) to gain this benefit.

Cunning Flexibility

At 22nd level, you can grant yourself moments of heightened agility when you need it the most. You gain a special bonus action that can be used only to use your cunning action. You can use this bonus action twice between short or long rests, and only once on each of your turns.

Expanded Roguish Archetype

At 23rd level, you choose an archetype that you emulate in the exercise of your rogue abilities. You may choose the same archetype, or you may choose a new one to further your techniques. Your archetype choice grants you features at 23rd level, and then again at 29th, 33rd, and 37th level.

Ability Score Improvement

When you reach 24th level, and again at 28th, 30th, 32nd, 36th, and 39th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two of your ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can’t increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.

Using the optional feats rule, you can forgo taking this feature to take a feat of your choice instead.

Impossible Dodge

Starting at 25th level your ability to move out of the way of life ending blows extends to new heights. When you use your uncanny dodge feature, the total damage is further reduced by half your prestige level. Additionally, if you use your uncanny dodge feature on an attack, damage from that attack cannot reduce you to 0 hit points.

Steady Strike

Practice has honed your strikes by 25th level. When you apply multiple cunning strike options on your sneak attack, you only pay the die cost for the most expensive effect.

Avoidance

Beginning at 27th level, your ability to dodge effects is no longer limited to just your quick reflexes. When you are subjected to an effect that allows you to make a saving throw to take only half damage, you instead take no damage if you succeed on the saving throw, and only half if you fail.

You cannot use this ability if you are incapacitated.

Perfected Talent

At 31st level, your defining skills have truly been perfected to the point of never failing you. Whenever you make an ability check using any of the skills enhanced by your Expertise or Superior Expertise features, you can treat a d20 roll of 14 or lower as a 15.

Deadly Strikes

At 34th level, you’ve practiced further ways to use your sneak attack to its fullest extent. The following effects are now among your Cunning Strike options.

Bleed (Cost: 5d6) - The target suffers large hemorrhages. At the start of each of the creature’s turns, it takes slashing damage equal to half your sneak attack damage. The bleeding creature, or a creature within 5 feet of them, can use an action to make a medicine check (DC = your cunning strikes DC) ending the effect on a success.

Execute (Cost: 10d6) - If the damage from this attack leaves the target with 60 hit points or less, they die.

Unnatural Reflexes

When you reach 35th level, you are exceptionally difficult to pin down by any. Your proficiency bonus for dexterity saving throws, and your choice of intelligence, wisdom, or charisma saving throws, is doubled.

Legendary Cunning

At 38th level, your ability and flexibility when it comes to movement are unmatched. The bonus action granted by Cunning Flexibility no longer requires you to rest between uses.

Luck no Longer

When you reach 40th level, your consistency is no longer mere luck. Once per turn when you miss with an attack roll which you have advantage on, you may choose to hit instead.

Homebrew / Subclasses

Medium

Medium

Mediums are the bridge between life and death, often treading over the gap between the two. They call forth spirits of the past, using them for power and knowledge.

Seance

At 3rd level, you are able to tap into knowledge from spirits that you know of. You learn speak with dead and can cast it only as if it were a ritual spell. Rather than targeting a corpse, you can speak the name of a deceased individual who died within 1 mile. If their soul is able, they can choose to manifest in an empty space within 5 feet of you and answer your questions.

Once a soul is manifested in this way, you can’t manifest the same soul again for 24 hours.

Medium Arts

Also at 3rd level, you gain access to new spirit arts that reflect your capacity to channel souls.

Channel Warrior

As an action, you can spend 1 spirit point to channel the spirit of a warrior. The spirit manifests as a spectral fighter that is always 5 feet away from your target. Whenever you activate your spirit tether, you can have the warrior strike at the target in the same action. The target must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or take 2d6 force damage. If you use this spirit art again on the same target, you can channel another warrior, up to a maximum of 3 total. Each new warrior increases the force damage dealt to the target by an extra 2d6.

Channel Trickster

As an action, you can spend 1 spirit point to channel the spirit of a trickster. The spirit manifests in the form of an imp, fairy, or any other tricky creature that is always 5 feet away from your target. Whenever you activate your spirit tether, you can have the trickster distract at the target in the same action. The target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or have disadvantage on attack rolls and Perception checks until the end of its next turn.

Channel Guardian

As an action, you can spend 1 spirit point to channel the spirit of a guardian. The spirit manifests as an ancestor, patron, or angel that is always within 5 feet of you. Whenever you activate your spirit tether, the guardian bestows 1d6 temporary hit points to you. If you use this spirit art again, you can channel another guardian, up to a maximum of 3 total. Each new guardian increases the temporary hit points gained by an extra 1d6.

Eternal Spirit

At 6th level, your frequent interactions with other spirits has strengthened your own considerably. The range of your spirit tether increases to 300 feet. In addition, if

your tether breaks while you have at least one active spirit art, you regain one spirit point.

Claircognizance

At 13th level, by drawing upon the experiences of the dead, you become temporarily able to utilize their skills. If you make a skill check in any skill you’re not proficient in, you can spend a spirit point to add your proficiency bonus to the roll. You can use this feature after the roll is made, but only before you know the results.

Master Medium

At 18th level, you master your influence over the souls of others. You learn the following spirit art:

Possession

If your target is a creature, you can use an action and spend 5 spirit points to attempt to possess them temporarily. The target must succeed on a Charisma saving throw or be possessed by you for a minute. During this time, your soul is transferred into the target’s form, and your original body is left paralyzed. You now control the body but you don’t deprive the target of awareness. You use the possessed target’s statistics, but you retain your alignment, Wisdom, Intelligence, and Charisma. You don’t gain access to the target’s knowledge, class features, or proficiencies.

You may end the possession at any time, upon which you return to your body without harm. At the end of each of their turns, the target can repeat the Charisma save, ending the possession on a success. If the target dies while you possess it, your soul is returned to your body without harm. However, if your body dies while possessing the target, the possession ends and you die.

Homebrew / Subclasses

Memory Thief Sorcery (2024 Sorcerer)

Memory Thief Sorcery (2024 Sorcerer)

Description

The Memory Thief is a sorcerer touched by the silent weight of unspoken thoughts, lost truths, and stolen moments. Whether chosen by a god of shadows and secrets or born with the uncanny ability to pierce the veil of another’s mind, these sorcerers draw power not from raw elements—but from memory, emotion, and identity itself.

Every spell is an intrusion, every glance a chance to unravel another’s story. They are masters of mental trespass and psychic influence, collecting knowledge the way others collect coins. Some act as spies for hidden powers like Vhaeraun, gods of forbidden knowledge, or remnants of psionic empires. Others awaken to their abilities after surviving moments of profound trauma or divine contact—left able to steal what others cannot even remember.

"Thoughts and Emotions are the truest form of currency. I never pay full price." - Memory Thief

Playstyle and Motivations

The Memory Thief excels at subtle control, emotional manipulation, and deep utility in both narrative and combat play. With features that allow you to read and manipulate the thoughts and motivations of others, this subclass rewards strategic roleplay, creative problem-solving, and players who love to know more than they should.

  • Reclaim the Past: Seeking to recover a stolen or fragmented identity by stitching together memories from others.
  • Weaponize Secrets: Collecting powerful memories from kings, archmages, or ancient evils to manipulate the tides of history or blackmail enemies into silence.
  • Protect the Mindscape: Standing as a psychic guardian or counter-spy, exposing hidden corruption or breaking mind control through counter-manipulation.

Who Would Thrive as a Memory Thief?

The Memory Thief is perfect for players who want to:

  • Influence Story Through Subtlety: Gain leverage by collecting key memories, discovering hidden motives, or creating complex emotional bonds with NPCs.
  • Play with Identity and Perception: Use your magic to assume false roles, mimic memories, or veil your soul against detection.
  • Master Battlefield Presence Without Direct Violence: Weaken enemies emotionally, disrupt their thoughts, and track them across time and space.

Ideal Players and Characters

🧠 The Intrigue Manipulator

Players who thrive in espionage-heavy or social-intrigue campaigns, especially those who enjoy steering conversations with secrets and subtle leverage.

🕯 The Shadowed Seer

Players who love mysteries and clues, piecing together narrative threads from the minds of others, treating every memory like a breadcrumb on a hidden trail.

🎭 The Identity Shifter

Players who want to play with masks, personas, and the line between truth and falsehood—taking on aspects of others through their memories, voices, and fears.

Features:

  • 3rd Level - Umbral Spike
  • 6th Level - Thought Scribe
  • 14th Level - Hollow Mask
  • 18th Level - Dark One's Trespass

3rd Level - Umbral Spike

Once per turn when damaging a creature with a spell or attack, you can deal an additional 2d6 psychic damage and mark them. While the creature is marked, you know their direction and distance while they are within 90 ft of you, lasting up to 1 hour. You can spend sorcery points to extend the duration by an additional hour per sorcery point spent.

The extra damage increases at 6th (3d6) level, 14th (4d6) level, and 18th (5d6) level.

You can use this a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier, regaining all uses on a Long Rest, or by expending a spell slot for each use restored (no action required).

6th Level - Thought Scribe

When you cast a spell of 1st level or higher that forces a creature to make a saving throw, you can extract a thought strand (as with the Encode Thoughts cantrip) on a failure. Once you use this feature on a creature, you cannot use this feature on that target again until you complete a short or long rest.

The thought strand contains one memory of a significant event within the past 24 hours. Significant events typically involve powerful emotions, such as battles and betrayals, marriages and murders, births and funerals, or meetings with important friends or leaders. However, they might also include more mundane events that are nevertheless important to that creature.

In addition, while holding the thought strand, you can communicate telepathically with the target while they are on the same plane of existence as you. You can choose if they are able to respond or not.

14th Level - Hollow Mask

As a bonus action, you can spend 1 or more sorcery points to magically transform your essence for 10 minutes. For each sorcery point you spend, you can gain one of the following benefits of your choice, the effects of which last until the transformation ends:

  • You can see through solid objects to a range of 30 feet, and can see any invisible creatures to a range of 60 feet. Within that range you have advantage on checks made to find hidden creatures, traps, or secret doors for the duration of the transformation.
  • You cannot be detected or targeted by any divination magic, or perceived through magical scrying sensors unless you wish to be. If you choose to be affected, you can present false information to the divination magic or scrying sensor for the duration of the transformation.
  • You can choose a creature type other than your actual creature type. Spells and other magical effects treat you as if you were a creature of the chosen type. After the transformation expires, ongoing and future spells and magical effects treat you as your original creature type.
  • You have advantage on saving throws against effects which would cause you to be charmed, frightened, or possessed. If you succeed against such an effect, you have advantage on Charisma checks made against that source for the duration of the transformation.

18th Level - Dark One's Trespass

As an Action, you can force a target you can see within 60ft of you to make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC or be charmed or frightened (your choice) and you are able to detect the creatures surface thoughts and emotional state for up to 8 hours (those foremost in its mind, reflecting its current emotions and what it is actively thinking about). You can spend sorcery points to extend the duration by an additional hour per sorcery point spent. Alternatively, if you are holding a thought strand created by your Thought Scribe feature, you can target that creature as long as they are on the same plane of existence.

While charmed or frightened in this way, it undertakes to perform any services or activities you ask of it to the best of its ability. You can set the creature new tasks when a previous task is completed, or if you decide to end its current task. If the service or activity might cause harm to the creature, or if it conflicts with the creature's desires, the creature can make another Wisdom saving throw to try to end the effect. This save is made with advantage if you or your companions are fighting the creature. If the activity would result in certain death for the creature, the effect ends. During that time you can use a Bonus Action to see and hear through that creatures senses until the end of your next turn. You are blinded and deafened while this persists.

Once you use this Action, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest, unless you spend 7 sorcery points to use it again.
