Sages who follow this philosophy, often called “Blue Mages” due to the color of the robes many traditionally wear, embody the ever-flowing state of the world and others, taking that change into themselves and granting them the uncanny ability to adapt their very beings into something that can at times be completely unrecognizable.

Class features:

  • 2nd Level - Bonus Proficiencies
  • 2nd Level - Azure Lores
  • 6th Level - Flesh Writer
  • 10th Level - Shaper of Evolution
  • 14th Level - Hardened Study
  • 18th Level - Ever-Evolving

2nd Level - Bonus Proficiencies

When you select this study at 2nd level, you gain proficiency with longswords and scimitars, as well as the survival and nature skills. Your proficiency bonus is doubled for any check you make that uses either of those skills.

2nd Level - Azure Lore

Additionally at 2nd level, you begin to uncover the ability to fundamentally change yourself in order to accommodate your continually evolving magic, starting with the ability to take the abilities of the monsters you face, using them as your own.

When you are targeted by a creature’s ability that does not originate from a weapon attack, spell, legendary action, or lair action, you can attempt to tap into a deeper understanding of it, and combine it with yourself. If you do so, any attack roll that is part of the ability automatically hits you, and any saving throw is automatically failed. Immediately after the effects are resolved, you may make a wisdom saving throw (DC 8 + the creature’s proficiency bonus + the creature’s constitution modifier). On a success, you may add the ability to your collection of Azure Lore, unless the creature’s challenge rating is higher than your sage level. You may only learn one Azure Lore ability per individual creature.

Whenever you use your Meditation feature to replace a spell that you know, you may replace it with one of your Azure Lore abilities. You can cast the ability as a spell, expending a spell slot of a level determined by the challenge rating of the creature. You automatically have any cantrip-level ability you gain through this feature available when you learn it. Follow Link to view Table

Challenge Rating Spell Slot Level
< 1 Cantrip
1 - 3 1st
4 - 5 2nd
6 - 7 3rd
8 - 9 4th
10 - 11 5th
12 - 13 6th
14 - 15 7th
16 - 17 8th
18 - 20 9th

Casting the spell requires Somatic components, but not Verbal or Material, and has a casting time equal to the action it took the original creature. If the ability has a recharge condition, you must meet that condition before you are able to cast that Azure Lore ability again.

You may place mind shapes on your Azure Lore abilities as normal when you gain that feature at 3rd Level.

6th Level - Flesh Writer

When you reach 6th level, you unlock the ability to tap into the abilities of the fallen and dead creatures you encounter. You may spend ten minutes while in contact with the corpse of a creature to attempt to absorb one of the abilities that it had in life. After the ritual has been completed, make a wisdom saving throw (DC 12 + the creature’s proficiency bonus + the creature’s constitution modifier). On a success, you may choose a single special trait from the creature to add to yourself. On a success or failure, you cannot use that corpse again to gain abilities through this feature.

The added trait cannot be Legendary Resistance or Limited Magic Immunity.

Once you add a trait to yourself, it cannot be removed by any means short of giving up the knowledge of the trait, which you can do as an action. You can maintain a number of these traits equal to your wisdom modifier. If you try to assimilate more traits than your maximum would allow, you may choose to give up one of your current traits for the new one.

10th Level - Shaper of Evolution

At 10th level, your spells shift to better reflect the evolution that you yourself have undergone. When you cast any of your Azure Lore skills as Focused Spells, you may expend one spell slot level lower than you normally would need to (minimum of 1st level).

You also gain the following Mind Shape, which can be placed on your focused spells as normal:

Evolving: You can cast this spell as a reaction to a creature you can see within 60 feet of you ending their turn.

14th Level - Hardened Study

When you reach 14th level, you no longer need to completely lower your defenses in order to intertwine your understanding of the abilities of others. When you attempt to learn an Azure Lore ability, attack rolls no longer automatically hit you, and you no longer automatically fail saving throws.

18th Level - Ever-Evolving

Normal physical limits no longer apply to the abilities you learn from your Azure Lore feature when you reach 18th level. You are now able to copy natural weapons, and Legendary Actions that target you.

If you cast a creature’s Legendary Action as a spell, it takes an action to do so.

Homebrew / Subclasses

Philosophy of Fallacy

Philosophy of Fallacy

There are ways of thinking that are often called incorrect by many, exhibiting illogical methods, or even simply being incorrect. However, certain Sages can utilize these ways of thinking in shaping their magic into something truly bizarre.

Bandwagon

The spells you cast carry the capacity to trick the very weave itself into allowing extra magic to be cast. When you cast a focused spell by expending a spell slot of first level or higher, the next time you or a creature within 30 feet of you casts that same spell at the same level before the start of your next turn, they do so without expending a spell slot, so long as the spell is of 5th level or lower.

Straw Man

Your illogical reasoning extends far enough to prevent harm to you, though opening you to potentially greater damage.

Starting at 6th level, as a reaction when you take damage, you can teleport to an unoccupied space you can see within 30 feet of you, creating an illusory copy to take the damage instead. If you take damage from any source before the start of your next turn, you are vulnerable to that damage.

Shaper of Delusion

At 10th level, you can further shape your spells to your own fallacy. When a creature casts one of your focused spells that benefits from your [Bandwagon] feature, that creature gets advantage on the next attack roll, ability check, or saving throw they make within the next minute.

You also gain the following Mind Shape, which can be placed on your focused spells as normal:

Delusional

When you cast the spell, you can choose to have it not take effect until you cast your next spell.

Red Herring

You learn to use your thoughts to distract those around you at 14th level. When a creature within 60 feet of you makes an attack roll, ability check, or saving throw, you can use your reaction to impose disadvantage on the roll. If the creature fails their ability check, saving throw, or attack roll, it takes psychic damage equal to half your sage level. If it succeeds, you take the damage instead.

You can do so a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier, regaining all uses after you finish a long rest.

Anti-Logic

At 18th level, you gain the ability to turn other’s perceptions to better serve your spellcasting, and at a heavy detriment to them. As an action, you can force a creature within 60 feet of you to make a charisma saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, the creature will willingly fail any saving throw against your sage spells, and is no longer considered willing for beneficial effects from allies. This effect lasts for 1 minute.

Once you use this feature, you cannot do so again until you finish a long rest.

Homebrew / Subclasses

Philosophy of Finality

Philosophy of Finality

Those who undertake the Philosophy of Finality hold the understanding that all things must come to their eventual end. Inclusive of their foes, and themselves. A Sage who follows this study may work to bring, delay, or even stop the meddling with of such events. Regardless of how these Sage’s may work, they have a full understanding that it cannot, and will not last forever.

Last Cast

As your pool of magic runs out, you manage to extort additional power drawing from its end. When you cast a spell of 1st level or higher, and expend the last spell slot of a given level, you gain a bonus to one damage roll equal to 2d8.

Resolve to End

At 6th level, lasting harmful effects are far less effective against you, as your understanding forces them to end. When you are targeted by a harmful effect with a duration of one minute or longer, you can choose to end the effect at the end of your next turn (no action required). Once you do so, you cannot do so again until you complete a short or long rest.

Shaper of Denial

At 10th level, your spells reflect the absolute finality that shapes your spells. When a focused spell ends on a creature, you can choose to end all beneficial or detrimental effects currently affecting them.

You also gain the following Mind Shape, which can be placed on your focused spells as normal:

Denying

If the spell causes a creature to be reduced to 0 hit points, it does not consume a spell slot. Once your denying spell prevents a spell slot from being expended, it cannot do so again until you create a new denying spell.

Forced Stop

Your understanding of the end of all around you can allow you to bring it to the present instantly, empowering you in the process.

At 14th level, you learn the Dispel Magic spell if you don’t already know it. You cannot replace this spell through meditation, and it does not count towards the total number of spells you know.

When you successfully end a spell or effect with Dispel Magic, you can use your Last Cast feature on the next spell you cast of 1st level or higher, even if you have spell slots remaining of the level you cast.

Denial and Acceptance

At 18th level, the knowledge of your end fuels you to persist should you fall before your time. If you die to any source other than old age, you are returned to life 24 hours later with all of your hit points at the location you died, so long as your soul is able to. If your body was destroyed, a new one is created. Once you are restored to life by this feature, you cannot do so again until you finish a long rest.

Homebrew / Subclasses

Philosophy of Mysticism

Philosophy of Mysticism

There are those who take their connection to magic to a completely higher level, sometimes utilizing understanding through godly entities or beings of similar power. Sages who undertake the Philosophy of Mysticism may work closely with clerics, paladins, or even warlocks to further strengthen their connection to the divine.

Divine Initiate

When you take this philosophy at 2nd level, you gain a small spark connecting you to a divine entity, granting you enhanced magic. Choose two spells of 1st level from the Cleric or Warlock spell lists. Both spells need not be from the same list. These spells count as sage spells for you, and do not count towards your number of spells learned. If you choose to replace either of these spells through Meditation[1], you can learn a Cleric or Warlock spell of any level of which you have spell slots to cast in its place.

Medicinal Spells

Your spells carry with them the capacity to heal both yourself and your allies. At 6th level, when you cast a sage spell of 1st level or higher that targets either you or an ally, you can cause that creature to restore a number of hit points equal to your sage level. You can do so a number of times equal to your wisdom modifier, and regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

Shaper of Fanaticism

At 10th level, you can further shape your spells to more closely fit the divinity you follow. When you cast a focused spell from the cleric or warlock spell lists, you can choose to have the spell count as one level higher than the slot used to cast it. In doing so, you can cast no spells other than focused spells for the next minute.

You also gain the following Mind Shape[1], which can be placed on your focused spells as normal:

Fanatical

When a celestial, fiend, or undead fails a saving throw against the spell, or are hit with a spell attack roll, they take extra damage equal to half your sage level.

Enhanced Divinity

Your mental connections to divine magic have had a profound effect on both your mind and body at 14th level. When you make a charisma check, you can add your wisdom modifier to the total.

Additionally, angel or bat wings sprout from your back (your choice) giving you a flying speed of 30 ft. You also gain resistance to radiant damage (if you chose angel wings), or necrotic damage (if you chose bat wings).

Envoy of the Heavens

At 18th level, your spells carry with them the very essence of the divine entities you’ve spent your life connected with. You gain the following benefits.

  • You can replace the damage type of your focused spells with radiant or necrotic.
  • Celestials, Fiends and Undead have disadvantage on saving throws against your sage spells.
  • When you restore hit points of another creature with a sage spell, you regain hit points equal to half the amount you healed.
  1. ↑ 1.0 1.1 Sage
Homebrew / Subclasses

Philosophy of Patience

Philosophy of Patience

So it is said that with patience comes wisdom. That wisdom can come in the form of great magical power for those who take upon patience into their very being. A sage who has undertaken the philosophy of patience is never the first to start conflict, but is rarely the first to fall as a result of it.

Bonus Proficiencies

A sage of patience is always prepared should theirs outweigh that of others. As such, you gain proficiency in light armor, medium armor, and shields.

Delayed Potency

Starting at 2nd level, you gain the ability to enhance your longer lasting spells at the cost of a slower start. When you cast a spell that makes multiple damage rolls, or lasts for multiple rounds, the first damage roll, or damage rolls during the first round, have all damage dice treated as their lowest value. In return, the last damage roll, or damage rolls during the final round, have all damage dice treated as their highest amount.

Evasive Casting

Your spells open a window of clarity to you, allowing you to avoid harm for a short time immediately after casting them. Starting at 6th level, you can take the dodge action as a bonus action if you use your action to cast a sage spell of 1st level or higher.

Shaper of Composure

At 10th level, your spells further evolve to reflect your patience. When you cast a focused spell, you gain temporary hit-points equal to your sage level.

You also gain the following Mind Shape, which can be placed on your focused spells as normal:

Composed

Creatures cannot react to you casting this spell.

Consummate Concentration

While concentrating on spells, both your mind and body become far more rigid. Starting at 14th level, while you maintain concentration on a spell, you gain a +2 bonus to your armor class and saving throws. Your concentration also cannot be broken as a result of taking damage.

Paragon of Patience

At 18th level your patience opens opportunities to you that others could not even hope to achieve. When you roll initiative, you may choose to instead place yourself at initiative 0. If you do so, you may take a second turn immediately after your first turn in the first round of combat.

Homebrew / Subclasses

Phoenix

Phoenix

Phoenix

Features:

  • 1st Level - Ignite
  • 1st Level - Mantle of Flame
  • 6th Level - Phoenix Spark
  • 14th Level - Nourishing Fire
  • 18th Level - Form of the Phoenix

1st Level - Ignite

At 1st level, you gain the ability to start fires with a touch. As an action, you can magically ignite a flammable object you touch with your hand—an object such as a torch, a piece of tinder, or the hem of drapes.

1st Level - Mantle of Flame

Starting at 1st level, you can unleash the phoenix fire that blazes within you. As a bonus action, you magically wreathe yourself in swirling fire, as your eyes glow like hot coals. For 1 minute, you gain the following benefits:

  • You shed bright light in a 30-foot radius and dim light for an additional 30 feet.
  • Any creature takes fire damage equal to your Charisma modifier if it hits you with a melee attack from within 5 feet of you or if it touches you.
  • Whenever you roll fire damage on your turn, the roll gains a bonus to equal to your Charisma modifier.

Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest.

6th Level - Phoenix Spark

Starting at 6th level, the fiery energy within you grows restless and vengeful. In the face of defeat, it surges outward to preserve you in a fiery roar. If you are reduced to 0 hit points, you can use your reaction to draw on the spark of the phoenix. You are instead reduced to 1 hit point, and each creature within 10 feet of you takes fire damage equal to half your sorcerer level + your Charisma modifier. If you use this feature while under the effects of your Mantle of Flame, this feature instead deals fire damage equal to your sorcerer level + double your Charisma modifier, and your Mantle of Flame immediately ends. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest.

14th Level - Nourishing Fire

Starting at 14th level, your fire spells soothe and restore you. When you expend a spell slot to cast a spell that includes a fire damage roll, you regain hit points equal to the slot's level + your Charisma modifier.

18th Level - Form of the Phoenix

At 18th level, you finally master the spark of fire that dances within you. While under the effect of your Mantle of Flame feature, you gain additional benefits:

  • You have a flying speed of 40 feet and can hover.
  • You have resistance to Poison & Fire
  • If you use your Phoenix Spark, that feature deals an extra 20 fire damage to each creature.
Homebrew / Subclasses

Physicist

Physicist

Physicist

The world we know has many rules and laws that dictate how it functions. Some explain why the sky is blue, others dictate how things fall, some even to help understand the best trajectory for a bolt or bullet. Regardless of what it may be, a Physicist is a specialized artificer that takes study of these natural laws to even greater lengths than most, learning to exploit them to achieve things previously thought impossible. While they may shy away from a technological side of artifice, make no mistake that the work of physicists is invaluable to almost all fields.

Features:

  • 3rd Level - Analytic
  • 3rd Level - Physicist Spells
  • 3rd Level - Experimental Formulas
  • 5th Level - Kinetic Bombard
  • 9th Level - Advanced Formulas
  • 15th Level - Newtonian Defiance

3rd Level - Analytic

When you choose this specialization at 3rd level, you can add half your proficiency bonus (rounded down) to any Intelligence check you are not already proficient with.

3rd Level - Physicist Spells

You always have certain spells prepared after you reach particular levels in this class, as shown in the Physicist Spells table. These spells count as artificer spells for you, but they don’t count against the number of artificer spells you prepare.

Artificer Spell List

  • 3rd Level: Magnify Gravity, Magic Missile
  • 5th Level: Borrowed Knowledge, Immovable Object
  • 9th Level: Counterspell, Pulse Wave
  • 13th Level: Gravity Sinkhole, Fire Shield
  • 17th Level: Antilife Shell, Telekinesis

3rd Level - Experimental Formulas

Starting at 3rd level, you learn various formulas that can be used to alter or improve your performance. You have a number of experiment points equal to half your artificer level (rounded down) and regain all expended points when you finish a long rest. Alternatively, you can expend a spell slot as an action to regain experiment points equal to the slot's level.

You spend experiment points on different formulas, of which you learn three from the following list:

  • Alternate Angle: When you make an attack with a weapon that deals bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing damage, you can expend one experiment point to change the damage type to a different type from the same list. The attack also deals an extra 3 damage.
  • Thermodynamics: When you take fire or cold damage, you can use your reaction to expend one experiment point to deal half that damage of the opposite type to the creature that dealt the damage to you.
  • Conservation of Energy: When you deal force damage to a creature or object, you can expend one experiment point to deal extra damage equal to half your artificer level. Doing so reduces your speed to 0 until the end of your next turn.
  • Electron Shell: As an action, you can expend one to five experiment points to create a shell around you, which has 4 charges, plus one for every additional point spent. When you take damage, the damage is reduced by the amount of charges, and one is expended. All remaining charges dissipate after one hour.
  • Polarize: When you make an attack or cast a spell that deals damage, you can expend an experiment point to forgo rolling damage to deal the average damage.
  • Applied Science: When you make an ability check, you can expend an experiment point to predict the result before seeing it. If you are correct, you gain a +10 bonus to the roll. If you are within 1, you gain a +5 bonus instead.

5th Level - Kinetic Bombard

Starting at 5th level, you are able to harness the outgoing kinetic energy of attacks. Once per round, when you make a weapon or spell attack, you can increase the damage of the attack by 2d4, this damage is force damage.

The damage dealt by this ability increases to 3d4 at 9th level, and to 4d4 at 15th level.

9th Level - Advanced Formulas

A breakthrough has led to your creation of even further refined formulas. At 9th level you learn two of the following advanced formulas:

  • Genius Precision: When you or a creature you can see within 30 ft of you make an attack roll, you can expend one experiment point to apply your flash of genius to the attack roll.
  • Kinetic Battery: As a bonus action, you can expend one experiment point to begin storing kinetic energy. For every 10 feet you move, you add 1d6 to the total stored kinetic energy, up to 10d6. The next time you damage a creature or object, the target takes damage equal to your kinetic energy. The battery lasts for 1 minute, and if the battery expires before you deal damage, you take force damage equal to your kinetic energy.
  • Meltdown: As an action, you can expend 2 experiment points to deal acid damage to a creature you can see within 60 ft equal to twice the amount of hit dice it has. This formula does not effect targets resistant or immune to acid damage.
  • Super-Magnetism: If a spell or effect you create would move a creature on a failed saving throw, you can expend one experiment point to move the creature even if they succeed. You must use this formula before the creature makes the saving throw.

15th Level - Newtonian Defiance

At 15th level, the natural laws of the world begin to bend at your command. You can cast the following spells with the following changes:

  • Reverse Gravity: The spell has the normal effect, except that you can orient the area in any direction and creatures and objects fall toward the end of the area.
  • Arcane Gate: The portals created by this spell can be oriented in any direction you choose, but must be created flat against a solid surface large enough to hold it.
  • Telekinesis: You can manipulate up to three objects at once. If one of those objects is a weapon, you can attack with that weapon as if you were holding it.

You can cast each of these spells once in this way, and must finish a long rest to do so again.

Homebrew / Subclasses

Powderkeg

Powderkeg

Description

Volatile and dangerous, Powderkegs typically make use of exceedingly dangerous chemicals or magic to act as the ultimate deterrent. Despite this, Bulwarks under this specialization tend to show great care for the power they wield.

Features:

  • 3rd Level - Powderkeg Training
  • 3rd Level - Volatile Ward
  • 7th Level - Combustion
  • 13th level - Explosive Ward
  • 18th Level - Fission

3rd Level - Powderkeg Training

When you select this specialization at 3rd level, you gain proficiency with firearms and alchemist supplies.

3rd Level - Volatile Ward

Additionally at 3rd level, you have the ability to work volatile compounds into your armor and defensive strategies. Whenever you use your fortitude feature, the triggering creature takes fire damage equal to your bulwark level.

7th Level - Combustion

Starting at 7th level, your knack for mixing potent reactions extends to aid you in combat. While you are holding alchemist supplies and take the attack action, you can replace one attack on each of your turns with a burst of chemical energy.

Target a creature within 15 feet of yourself. The target must succeed a Dexterity Saving Throw (DC 8 + your Strength Modifier + your Proficiency Bonus) or take 2d8 damage. This damage is acid, fire or poison (your choice).

13th level - Explosive Ward

When you reach 13th level, you learn to improve your Volatile Ward with even more explosive potential. When you use your Volatile Ward feature, you can choose to have each creature within 20 feet of you take the damage, instead of just the triggering creature. If you do so, the feature deals only half damage.

18th Level - Fission

Starting at 18th level, the explosive potential within you reaches its pinnacle. As an action, you can trigger a chain reaction within your armor to detonate out in a violent burst. You immediately take 20d6 fire damage and 20d6 bludgeoning damage, and each creature within 40 feet of you must succeed a dexterity saving throw (DC 8 + your Strength Modifier + you Proficiency Bonus) or take the same damage, taking half as much on a successful save. Objects that are not being worn or carried in the area also take this damage. After using this feature, you have immunity to all damage until the end of your next turn.

Once you use this feature, you must finish a long rest before you can do so again.

Homebrew / Subclasses

Psi Tracker

Psi Tracker

Description

In the silent reaches of wild places and hidden thresholds of civilization, there lies a path few can follow: that of the mind-hunter. The Psi Tracker merges the instincts of the wilderness stalker with the latent power of psionics, becoming a tracker not just of footprints and scent, but of thoughts, memories, and the flicker of intent. What begins as simple survival becomes something far deeper: the Psi Tracker reads the currents of the mind, discerns the trail left by fears and desires, and strikes when prey least expects that the hunter knows their inner terrain.

Over long hunts and sustained engagements, the Psi Tracker thrives in drawn-out chases where others would rush to violence. They wear down foes by probing their psyche, disrupting their will, and shifting the battlefield of consciousness. In that way, they become the perfect predator for aberrant threats, whispering shadows of alien thought or intruding into minds as subtly as the wind rustles forest leaves. Their power comes not simply from blade or bow, but from the mind’s edge.

Potential playstyle & motivations for a Psi Tracker:

  • You prefer slow, methodical engagements rather than outright brawls—tracking, disrupting, then striking.
  • You are motivated by uncovering hidden minds, unraveling secrets, and turning that insight into advantage.
  • You wield psionic power as a tool of the hunt: buffing yourself, marking your quarry, and manipulating the mental battlefield before delivering the kill.

Who would thrive playing this subclass:

  • Players who enjoy a mix of exploration, investigation, and combat—not just shooting arrows but reading intentions.
  • Players drawn to subtle control-effects, debuffs, and layered tactics rather than pure damage output.
  • Players who like characters with a mysterious aura—someone attuned to mental shadows and the unseen.

Ideal character and players:

  • A ranger whose backstory involves studying strange psychic phenomena, or hunting aberrations that prey on minds.
  • A player comfortable juggling resources (psionic dice) and making choices about when to engage or wear down enemies.
  • A gamer who wants to emphasize role-play of perception, interrogation, and tracking as much as weapon attacks.

Features:

  • 3rd Level - Psionic Power
  • 3rd Level - Psychic Spells
  • 7th Level - Empathic Awareness
  • 11th Level - Cognitive Bypass
  • 15th level - Mental Dissonance

3rd Level - Psionic Power

Starting at 3rd level, you harbor a wellspring of psionic energy within yourself. This energy is represented by your Psionic Energy dice, which are each a d6. You have a number of these dice equal to twice your proficiency bonus, and they fuel various psionic powers you have, which are detailed below.

Some of your powers expend the Psionic Energy die they use, as specified in a power's description, and you can't use a power if it requires you to use a die when your dice are all expended. You regain all your expended Psionic Energy dice when you finish a long rest. In addition, as a bonus action, you can regain one expended Psionic Energy die, but you can't do so again until you finish a short or long rest.

When you reach certain levels in this class, the size of your Psionic Energy dice increases: at 5th level (d8), 11th level (d10), and 17th level (d12).

The powers below use your Psionic Energy dice.

Psychic Mark: Whenever you cast Hunters Mark, you can expend a Psionic Energy dice and modify it. When cast in this way, it requires no components and once per turn you can deal additional damage equal to one roll of your Psionic Energy Die when you hit with an attack.

Psionic Fortitude: When your nonpsionic training fails you, your psionic power can help: if you fail a saving throw with which you have proficiency, you can roll one Psionic Energy die, adding half the number rolled to the save, potentially turning failure into success. You expend the die only if the roll succeeds.

3rd Level - Psychic Spells

When you cast a spell from the Conjuration or Transmutation school, you can do so without Verbal or Somatic components.

7th Level - Empathic Awareness

Starting at 7th level, your psionics have deepened your awareness of the world around you. You can use your action to roll and expend one Psionic Energy die to open your mind to the emotional and mental resonance of your surroundings. For a number of hours equal to the number rolled, you can sense whether any of the following are present within 3 miles of you (or within 1 mile if you are underground), or have been present within a number of days equal to your Wisdom modifier:

  • Intense thoughts or emotions (fear, anger, grief, ecstasy, anxiety)
  • Presence of Intelligent minds (creatures with Intelligence 6 or higher)
  • Psionic or magical phenomena of significant power (DM’s discretion)

You learn the direction of each detected source within range, but not its exact distance or number.

Additionally, once per use of this feature, you can make a Wisdom (Survival) or Wisdom (Nature) check, with a DC equaling your spell save DC. On a success you learn the distance to one significant location or creature from one of the options above, regardless of distance. If you succeed the check by 5 or more, you learn the distance to a specific location or creature (DM’s discretion), provided you have seen or heard of them before.

Once you use this feature, you can’t do so again until you finish a short or long rest, unless you expend an additional Psionic Energy die to use it again.

11th Level - Cognitive Bypass

When you move, you can temporarily blur the distinction between your body and your psychic echo. When you use the Tireless feature, you can roll and expend up to two Psionic Energy dice and add the number rolled to the Temporary Hit Points gained.

Additionally, you become partially incorporeal granting the following benefits for up to 1 minute, or until you are incapacitated:

  • You can move through creatures and objects as if they were difficult terrain.
  • The first time you enter a creature's space on a turn, that creature takes force damage equal to one roll of your Psionic Energy dice. Additionally, if you end your turn inside a creature or object, you and that target both take the same amount again in force damage.
  • When you hit a creature you have passed through with a melee weapon attack, you do not provoke opportunity attacks for leaving their reach.

15th level - Mental Dissonance

Your mastery of psionics lets you unleash waves of psychic intention that collapses thought and will.

Psychic Feedback: Hostile creatures that start their turns within 30ft of you take take Psychic damage equal to your Wisdom modifier if you have attacked or dealt damage to them within the last turn.

Intellect Spike: Additionally, as an action you can target a number of creatures within 30 feet of you equal to half your Wisdom modifier. Creatures targeted in this way must make an Intelligence saving throw (DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Wisdom modifier), taking psychic damage equal to your Wisdom modifier plus two rolls of your Psionic Energy dice and is incapacitated for up to 1 minute. On a successful save they take half damage and their speed is instead halved until the end of their next turn.

At the start of each of their turns while incapacitated, the damage they take from Psychic Feedback is doubled. They can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of their turns, ending on a successful save.

Once you use this feature, you can’t use it again until you finish a short or long rest, unless you expend two Psionic Energy dice to use it again.

Homebrew / Subclasses

Pyromancy

Pyromancy

Pyromancy

Features:

  • 1st Level - Heart of Fire
  • 6th Level - Fire in the Veins
  • 14th Level - Pyromancer's Fury
  • 18th Level - Fiery Soul

1st Level - Heart of Fire

At 1st level, whenever you start casting a spell that deals fire damage, fiery magic erupts from you. This eruption causes creatures of your choice that you can see within 10 feet of you to take fire damage equal to half your sorcerer level (minimum of 1).

6th Level - Fire in the Veins

At 6th level, you gain resistance to fire damage. In addition, spells you cast and effects you create ignore resistance to fire damage.

14th Level - Pyromancer's Fury

Starting at 14th level, when you are hit by a melee attack, you can use your reaction to deal fire damage to the attacker. The damage equals your sorcerer level, and ignores resistance to fire damage.

18th Level - Fiery Soul

At 18th level, you gain immunity to fire damage. In addition, you ignore resistance to fire damage and treat immunity to fire damage as resistance to fire damage. When treating immunity as resistance, features or feats that allow you to ignore resistance do not do so.

Homebrew / Subclasses

Raven Knight

Raven Knight

Raven Knight

A Raven Knight is fearsome in battle, fusing martial prowess with strange abilities gifted by the Raven Queen. Many Raven Knights work alone, though some may find a small band of companions to aid them in battle, and some may even command and lead entire armies into battle. Masters of death, Raven Knights seek to protect those who cannot protect themselves from undeath and the afterlife. Powerful Raven Knights may even become champions of the Raven Queen, and thus champions of the battlefield.

Features:

  • 3rd Level - Knowledge of Death
  • 3rd Level - Soul Severing
  • 7th Level - Feather Step
  • 10th Level - Queens Blessing
  • 15th Level - Deaths Embrace
  • 18th Level - Duty in Death

3rd Level - Knowledge of Death

When you choose this Archetype at 3rd level, you gain proficiency in the Investigation and Medicine skills. Additionally, you can make Intelligence (Investigation) and Wisdom (Medicine) checks with advantage when attempting to determine the cause of death of a creature.

3rd Level - Soul Severing

At 3rd level, when you reduce a creature to 0 hit points you sever the connection of the creatures soul to its body. That creature cannot be turned into an undead. Additionally, as a reaction, when a creature is reduced to 0 hit points within 15ft of you you can empower your next attack with that creatures soul energy. Your next weapon attack deals additional necrotic damage equal to half your fighter level.

7th Level - Feather Step

At 7th level, you move with the grace of the raven. Your walking speed increases by 10ft. Additionally, as a bonus action you gain a flight speed equal to your walking speed until the end of your turn, if you end your turn in midair you drop to the ground.

10th Level - Queens Blessing

At 10th level, the Raven Queen grants you a blessing. You gain advantage on death saving throws, immunity to the frightened condition, and resistance to necrotic damage.

15th Level - Deaths Embrace

At 15th level, when you or an ally critically hit a creature, you can use your reaction to add 3d10 necrotic damage to the attacks damage roll.

18th Level - Duty in Death

At 18th level, when you are reduced to 0 hit points or killed outright you can use your reaction to make a weapon attack against the creature that killed you. On a hit you critically hit that creature and regain hit points equal to the damage dealt. You can do this once per long rest.

Homebrew / Subclasses

Revised Arcane Archer

Revised Arcane Archer

Revised Arcane Archer

Features:

  • 3rd Level - Arcane Archer Lore
  • 3rd Level - Arcane Shot
  • 7th Level - Magic Ammunition
  • 7th Level - Curving Shot
  • 15th Level - Quick-draw Shot
  • 18th Level - Eldritch Mastery

3rd Level - Arcane Archer Lore

At 3rd level, you learn magical theory or some of the secrets of nature -- typical for practitioners of this elven martial tradition. You choose to gain proficiency in either the Arcana or the Nature skill, and you choose to learn either the prestidigitation or the druidcraft cantrip.

3rd Level - Arcane Shot

At 3rd level, you learn to unleash special magical effects with some of your shots. When you gain this feature, you learn two Arcane Shot options of your choice (see Arcane Shot Options below).

Once per turn when you fire an arrow or bolt from any bow as part of the Attack action, you can apply one of your Arcane Shot options to that piece of ammunition. You decide to use the option when the ammunition hits a creature, unless the option doesn't involve an attack roll. You have a number of uses equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses of it when you finish a short or long rest.

You gain an additional Arcane Shot option of your choice when you reach certain levels in this class: 7th, 10th, 15th, and 18th level. Each option also improves when you become a 15th-level fighter.

Arcane Shot Options (Revised)

The Arcane Shot feature lets you choose options for it at certain levels. The options are presented here in alphabetical order. They are all magical effects, and each one is associated with one of the schools of magic.

If an option requires a saving throw, your Arcane Shot save DC equals 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Intelligence modifier.

Banishing Arrow

You use abjuration magic to try to temporarily banish your target to a harmless location in the Feywild. The creature hit by the arrow must also succeed on a Charisma saving throw or be banished for 1 minute, or until you release the magic as a free action. While banished in this way, its speed is 0, and it is incapacitated. The affected creature can make a Charisma saving throw at the end of their turn, ending the effect on a success. At the end of the duration, the target reappears in the space it vacated or in the nearest unoccupied space if that space is occupied.

After you reach 15th level in this class, a target also takes 4d6 force damage when the arrow hits it.

Beguiling Arrow

Your enchantment magic causes this arrow to temporarily beguile its target. The creature hit by the arrow takes an extra 2d6 psychic damage, and choose one of your allies within 30 feet of the target. The target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw, or it is charmed by the chosen ally for 1 minute or until you release the magic as a free action. The target or any creature that can reach it can use its action to remove the arrow with a successful Strength (Athletics) check against your Arcane Shot save DC, ending the effect on a success. Additionally, this effect ends early if the chosen ally attacks the charmed target, deals damage to it, or forces it to make a saving throw.

The psychic damage increases to 4d6 when you reach 15th level in this class.

Bursting Arrow

You imbue your arrow with force energy drawn from the school of evocation. The arrow detonates after your attack. Immediately after the arrow hits the creature, the target and all other creatures within 10 feet of it take 2d6 force damage each and succeed on a Strength saving throw against your Arcane Shot save DC, or be knocked prone.

The force damage increases to 4d6 when you reach 15th level in this class. (edited)

Enfeebling Arrow

You weave necromantic magic into your arrow. The creature hit by the arrow takes an extra 2d6 necrotic damage on hit, as well as at the start of each of their turns for 1 minute or until you release the magic as a free action. The target must also succeed on a Constitution saving throw, or the damage dealt by its weapon attacks is halved until the start of your next turn. The target or any creature that can reach it can use its action to remove the arrow with a successful Strength (Athletics) check against your Arcane Shot save DC, ending the effect on a success.

The necrotic damage increases to 4d6 when you reach 15th level in this class.

Grasping Arrow

When this arrow strikes its target, conjuration magic creates grasping, poisonous brambles, which wrap around the target. The creature hit by the arrow takes an extra 2d6 poison damage, its speed is reduced by 10 feet, and it takes 2d6 slashing damage the first time on each turn it moves 1 foot or more without teleporting. The target or any creature that can reach it can use its action to remove the brambles with a successful Strength (Athletics) check against your Arcane Shot save DC. The brambles last for 1 minute, until you use another option, or until you release the magic as a free action.

The poison damage and slashing damage both increase to 4d6 when you reach 15th level in this class.

Piercing Arrow

You use transmutation magic to give your arrow an ethereal quality. When you use this option, you don’t make an attack roll for the attack. Instead, the arrow fires forward in a line, which is 5 foot wide and 30 feet long, before disappearing. The arrow passes harmlessly through objects, ignoring cover. Each creature in that line must make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes damage as if it were hit by the arrow, plus an extra 2d6 piercing damage. On a successful save, a target takes half as much damage. This option lasts for 1 minute, until you use another option, or until you release the magic as a free action.

The piercing damage increases to 4d6 when you reach 15th level in this class.

Seeking Arrow

Using divination magic, you grant your arrow the ability to seek out your target, allowing the arrow to curve and twist its path in search of its prey. When you use this option, you don’t make an attack roll for the attack. Instead, choose one creature you have seen in the past minute. The arrow flies toward that creature, moving around corners if necessary and ignoring three-quarters cover and half cover. If the target is within the weapon’s range and there is a path large enough for the arrow to travel to the target, the target must make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, it takes damage as if it were hit by the arrow, plus an extra 2d6 force damage, and you learn the target’s current location and distance for 1 hour or until you release the magic as a free action. On a successful save, the target takes half as much damage, and you only learn the targets current location and distance for one round. The target or any creature that can reach it can use its action to remove the arrow with a successful Strength (Athletics) check against your Arcane Shot save DC, ending the effect on a success.

The force damage increases to 4d6 when you reach 15th level in this class. (edited)

Shadow Arrow

You weave illusion magic into your arrow, causing it to occlude your foe’s vision with shadows. The creature hit by the arrow takes an extra 2d6 psychic damage, and it must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or be unable to see anything farther than 5 feet away for 1 minute or until you release the magic as a free action. The target or any creature that can reach it can use its action to remove the arrow with a successful Strength (Athletics) check against your Arcane Shot save DC, ending the effect on a success.

The psychic damage increases to 4d6 when you reach 15th level in this class.

7th Level - Magic Ammunition

At 7th level, you gain the ability to infuse ammunition with magic. Whenever you fire a nonmagical arrow from a bow, you can make it magical for the purpose of overcoming resistance and immunity to nonmagical attacks and damage. The magic fades from the ammunition immediately after it hits or misses its target.

7th Level - Curving Shot

At 7th level, you learn how to direct an errant ammunition toward a new target. When you make an attack roll with a magic ammunition and miss, you can use a bonus action to reroll the attack roll against a different target within 60 feet of the original target.

15th Level - Quick-draw Shot

Starting at 15th level, your magical archery makes your movements swift. Whenever you hit a target with an Arcane Shot you can use your bonus action to make another ranged weapon attack against the same target using the same weapon.

18th Level - Eldritch Mastery

At 18th level, your mastery of blending magic with archery teaches you to infuse your arrows with even greater magic, as well as combining them for greater effect.

Once per attack action, you can infuse a single arrow with two different arcane shot options, excluding piercing shot, having the target be affected by and taking damage from both shots. However when doing this you expend two uses of your Arcane shot.

You have two uses of this ability, and you regain all expended uses of it when you finish a long rest.

Homebrew / Subclasses

Revised Path of the Storm Herald

Revised Path of the Storm Herald

Revised Path of the Storm Herald

All barbarians harbor a fury within. Their rage grants them superior strength, durability, and speed. Barbarians who follow the Path of the Storm Herald learn to transform that rage into a mantle of primal magic, which swirls around them. When in a fury, a barbarian of this path taps into the forces of nature to create powerful magical effects.

Storm heralds are typically elite champions who train alongside druids, rangers, and others sworn to protect nature. Other storm heralds hone their craft in lodges in regions wracked by storms, in the frozen reaches at the world’s end, or deep in the hottest deserts.

Features:

  • 3rd Level - Storm Aura
  • 6th Level - Storm Soul
  • 10th Level - Shielding Storm
  • 14th Level - Raging Storm

3rd Level - Storm Aura

Starting at 3rd level, you emanate a stormy, magical aura while you rage. The area within the aura is lightly obscured. The aura extends 10 feet from you in every direction, but not through total cover.

Your aura has an effect that activates when you enter your rage, and you can activate the effect again on each of your turns as a bonus action. Choose desert, sea, or tundra. Your aura’s effect depends on that chosen environment, as detailed below. You can change your environment choice whenever you rage.

If your aura’s effects require a saving throw, the DC equals 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Constitution modifier.

Desert. When this effect is activated, creatures of your choice in your aura take 1d6 fire damage. The damage increases when you reach certain levels in this class, increasing to 2d6 at 5th level, 3d6 at 11th level, 4d6 at 17th level.

Sea. When this effect is activated, you can choose one other creature you can see in your aura to strike with lightning. The target must make a Strength saving throw. On a failure, the target takes 1d6 lightning damage on a failed save and is knocked prone. On a success, it takes half as much damage and isn’t knocked prone. The damage increases when you reach certain levels in this class, increasing to 2d6 at 5th level, 3d6 at 11th level, and 4d6 at 17th level.

Tundra. When this effect is activated, creatures of your choice in your aura must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failure, the creature’s speed is reduced to 0 until the end of your next turn, and the creature can’t take reaction for the duration.

6th Level - Storm Soul

At 6th level, the storm grants you benefits while your aura is active. The benefits are based on the environment you chose for your Storm Aura.

Desert. You gain resistance to fire damage. You can use an action to scatter sand in the area within your aura. Creatures within the area must make a Dexterity saving throw or be blinded until the end of your next turn.

Sea. You gain resistance to lightning damage, and you can breathe underwater. You can use an action to create a whirlpool around a creature you can see within your aura. It must make a Strength saving throw or be restrained until the end of your next turn.

Tundra. You gain resistance to cold damage. You can use an action to to grant temporary hit points to creatures of your choice in your aura equal to your barbarian level, as icy armor encases them.

10th Level - Shielding Storm

At 10th level, you learn to use your mastery of the storm to protect others. Each creature of your choice has the damage resistance you gained from the Storm Soul feature while the creature is in your Storm Aura.

14th Level - Raging Storm

At 14th level, the power of the storm you channel grows mightier, lashing out at your foes. The effect is based on the environment you chose for your Storm Aura.

Desert. Immediately after a creature in your aura hits you with an attack, you can use your reaction to force that creature to make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, the creature catches fire; until someone takes an action to douse the fire, the creature takes fire damage equal to half your barbarian level at the end of each of its turns.

Sea. When you create a lighting strike with your Storm Aura or a whirlpool with your Storm Soul feature, you can target two creatures instead of one.

Tundra. The area in your aura is heavily obscured, except for yourself and creatures of your choice when you activate the aura.

Homebrew / Subclasses

Revised Purple Dragon Knight

Revised Purple Dragon Knight

Revised Purple Dragon Knight

Features:

  • 3rd Level - Rallying Cry
  • Royal Envoy
  • 10th Level - Inspiring Surge
  • 15th Level - Bulwark
  • 18th Level - Loyalty to the Crown

3rd Level - Rallying Cry

When you choose this archetype at 3rd level, you learn how to inspire your allies to fight on past their injuries.

When you use your Second Wind feature, each creature of your choice within 15 feet of you regains hit points equal to your fighter level, provided that the creature can see or hear you.

Royal Envoy

A Purple Dragon knight serves as an envoy of the Cormyrean crown. Knights of high standing are expected to conduct themselves with grace.

At 7th level, you gain proficiency in the Persuasion skill. If you are already proficient in it, you gain proficiency in one of the following skills of your choice: Animal Handling, Insight, Intimidation, or Performance.

Your proficiency bonus is doubled for any ability check you make that uses Persuasion. You receive this benefit regardless of the skill proficiency you gain from this feature.

10th Level - Inspiring Surge

Starting at 10th level, when you use your Action Surge feature, you can choose an amount of creatures equal to half your fighter level (rounded down) within 15 feet of you. Those creatures can make one melee or ranged weapon attack with their reaction, provided that they can see or hear you.

Starting at 18th level, the range of your inspiration increases to 30 feet.

15th Level - Bulwark

Beginning at 15th level, you can extend the benefit of your Indomitable feature to your allies. When you decide to use Indomitable to reroll an Intelligence, a Wisdom, or a Charisma saving throw and you aren't incapacitated, you can choose an amount of creatures equal to half your proficiency bonus (rounded down) within 30 feet of you that also failed its saving throw against the same effect. If those creatures can see or hear you, they can reroll their saving throw and must use the new roll.

18th Level - Loyalty to the Crown

Starting at 18th level, when you target an ally with any of your bannerette features, that ally gains advantage on the next attack roll, ability check, or saving throw it makes until the end of its next turn.

Homebrew / Subclasses

Rook

Rook

Description

Decisive tactics and thoughtful planning are both highly important factors in the game of chess, and as certain Bulwarks are aware, the same goes for the art of war. Rooks are master tacticians, able to turn the tide of battle in their favor from nearly any position.

Features:

  • 3rd Level - One Step Ahead
  • 7th Level - Recapture
  • 13th Level - Gambits
  • 18th Level - Checkmate

3rd Level - One Step Ahead

When you select this specialization at 3rd level, you learn to apply yourself on the battlefield in a similar way to the pieces of a chess board.

You gain a pool of material equal to thrice your bulwark level to spend on plays. If a play allows you to move as part of it, you do so without expending your own movement, but you cannot have a speed of 0.

You recover all expended material when you finish a long rest.

Below is the list of plays:

Advance: When you take the attack action, you may expend three material to move up to your speed. You may take this movement before or after you make your attacks.

Back Rank: When you enter your defensive stance you can expend 3 material to impose disadvantage on all ranged attacks against you for the duration.

En Passant: When you attack a creature within 5 feet of you, you may expend 2 material to move up to 10 feet to another point within 5 feet of that creature. This movement does not provoke opportunity attacks, and your next attack roll against it has advantage.

Pawn’s Fury: During the first round of combat, you may expend 3 material to take an additional action. That action can be used to take only the Attack (one attack only), Dash, Disengage, Hide, or Interact with an Object action.

Knight’s Leap: When you jump, you may expend 1 material to triple your jump distance. It does not cost you any additional movement to do so.

Bishop’s Grace: As an action, you may expend 2 material to cast both guidance and resistance on yourself. Neither spell requires your concentration.

7th Level - Recapture

Starting at 7th level, you learn to reclaim the potential of the foes you fell. When you kill a creature with at least 30 hit points, you recover 5 material.

13th Level - Gambits

When you reach 13th level, you gain the ability to perform greater plays with great risk, though the potential payout is just as grand.

You gain access to the following plays:

Castling: When you enter your defensive stance, you may spend 7 material to choose one willing creature within 30 feet of you to trade places with. This movement does not provoke opportunity attacks. If when initiative ends, that creature has not taken damage since the switch, you regain 7 material.

Discovered Attack: When a creature within 5 feet of you targets you with an attack, you may use your reaction to expend 10 material. In doing so, you may make a melee attack against that target. If the attack reduces the creature to 0 hit points, you regain 10 material.

Promote: When you roll initiative, you may spend 20 material. For the duration of that combat you make plays, but not gambits, without expending material.

Queen’s Majesty: As a bonus action, you may expend 25 material in order to move up to twice your speed. For one minute after taking this bonus action, the amount of material you gain from your recapture feature is doubled.

King’s Command: As an action, you may spend 20 material to cast the Command spell (DC 8 + your strength modifier + your proficiency bonus) on any number of creatures within range. You must use the same command on each target. If no target succeeds their saving throw, you regain 10 material.

Rook’s Defiance: When you use your Fortitude feature, you may spend up to 20 material and further reduce the damage by that amount. If you reduce the damage to 0, you regain half the material spent.

18th Level - Checkmate

At 18th level, you have mastered the art of bringing fights to a decisive finish. When you take the attack action while your stance is active, you may choose to end your stance early. If you do, the first creature you hit takes extra damage equal to your bulwark level and is knocked prone.

Homebrew / Subclasses

School of Beating your Ass

School of Beating your Ass

Description

Features:

  • 2nd Level - Arcane Might
  • 6th Level - Special Delivery
  • 10th Level - Extra Attack
  • 14th Level - The ol' One-Two

2nd Level - Arcane Might

When you take this tradition at 2nd level, you learn to better partake in unarmed combat. You can replace the damage of your unarmed strikes with a d4 instead of their normal damage, and is considered magical for the purposes of overcoming resistance and immunity to non-magical attacks. This damage increases to 1d6 at 6th level, to 1d8 at 10th level, and again to 1d10 at 14th level.

Additionally, your hit point maximum increases by 2, and again by one each time you gain a level in this class.

6th Level - Special Delivery

When you reach 6th level, your technique has been honed to cast your spells through your martial combat. Once per turn, when you make an unarmed strike, you can deliver a spell's effects to the target as if you had cast it on them, in addition to the effects of the unarmed strike. The spell must have a casting time of one action, and must either be able to target another creature or area. If the spell would target an area, the effect's point of origin must be the target. Otherwise, you may shape the spell as you choose within the restrictions of the area of effect.. If the spell requires a saving throw, the target must make the saving throw as usual. If the spell requires an attack roll, the spell hits if the unarmed strike hits.

You expend a spell slot to cast the spell as normal, and the spell must be of a level no greater than your proficiency bonus.

10th Level - Extra Attack

Beginning at 10th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

14th Level - The ol' One-Two

Your culmination of martial and arcane knowledge has combined to great effect, allowing you to use one to make targets more vulnerable to another. If you hit a target twice on the same turn with unarmed strikes, the target has disadvantage on saving throws from the next spell you cast before the end of your next turn.

Additionally, when you damage a creature with a spell, the next unarmed strike you make against them has advantage, and deals extra damage equal to your wizard level.

Homebrew / Subclasses

Scrapper

Scrapper

Scrapper

Sometimes seen as the oddball of the various Artificer specialists, the Scrapper is a master of what other Artificers discard as junk. Make no mistake though, these hoarder misfits exemplify everything an artificer is at their core - Innovative, curious, with a spark of insanity mixed in with genius. They take what others see as trash, and turn it into works of art.

Features:

  • 3rd Level - Tool of the Trade
  • 3rd Level - Scrapper Spells
  • 3rd Level - Another's Treasure
  • 5th Level - Extra Attack
  • 9th Level - Junkrat's Armor
  • 15th Level - Sage of Junk

3rd Level - Tool of the Trade

You have proficiency with improvised weapons. You also gain proficiency with smith's tools. If you already have this proficiency, you gain proficiency with one other type of artisan's tools of your choice.

3rd Level - Scrapper Spells

Starting at 3rd level, you always have certain spells prepared after you reach particular levels in this class, as shown in the Scrapper Spells table. These spells count as artificer spells for you, but they don’t count against the number of artificer spells you prepare.

3rd level - magic missile, shield

5th level - cloud of daggers, locate object

9th level - leomund's tiny hut, melf's minute meteors

13th level - dimension door, fire shield

17th level - passwall, steel wind strike

3rd Level - Another's Treasure

Beginning at 3rd level, you can take anything lying around - A table leg, a shard of glass, a cooking pot - and turn it into a deadly weapon of war. When you hold/make an improvised weapon, the DM will determine if it deals slashing, piercing, or bludgeoning damage, and if it is one-handed (base 1d4 damage) or two-handed (base 1d6 damage) based on its resemblance to real weapons. You can use a bonus action to use your smithing tools to roll on the Upgrade Table to apply a random upgrade to an improvised weapon you are holding. An upgraded improvised weapon count as magical for the purpose of overcoming resistance and immunity to nonmagical attacks and damage.

d6 - Effect

1 Heavy Smashers. You affix heavy weights to the weapon, adding a bonus 1d6 bludgeoning damage. When you damage a target with this weapon, roll 1d4. On a 4, you can knock the target away from you up to 10 feet.

2 Spiky Stabbers. You attach spiky things such as rusted nails, sharpened sticks, etc. to your weapon, adding a bonus 1d6 piercing damage. When you damage a target with this weapon, roll 1d4. On a 4, you reduce that target's AC by 2 until the end of its next turn.

3 Sharp Slicers. You add sharp metal scraps, broken glass, or other slicing edges to your weapon, adding a bonus 1d6 slashing damage. When you damage a target with this weapon, roll 1d4. On a 4, the target's speed is halved until the end of its next turn.

4 Burning Flames. You coat the weapon in flammable materials, and set it alight, adding a bonus 1d6 fire damage. When you damage a target with this weapon, roll 1d4. On a 4, you can ignite the target. A target on fire takes 1d10 fire damage at the start of its turn. The target can use an action to put the fire out.

5 Shocking Coils. You wrap your weapon with suspect electrical components and wires, adding a bonus 1d6 lightning damage. When you damage a target with this weapon, roll 1d4. On a 4, the target must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or be stunned until the end of its next turn.

6 Venomous Goo. You slather the weapon in dangerous chemicals and diseased meat, adding a bonus 1d6 poison damage. When you damage a target with this weapon, roll 1d4. On a 4, the target must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or become poisoned for 1 minute. The target can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

An upgraded improvised weapon can be used in a number of attacks equal to your Intelligence modifier plus your proficiency bonus(a minimum of twice) before they break and become unusable. You can apply only one upgrade on an improvised weapon and it is removed when you drop or stow the weapon. If you try to upgrade another improvised weapon, the old upgrade is immediately removed, and then the new upgrade applies. You can also consume a spell slot to apply an upgrade to an improvised weapon as a bonus action. If you do, you may choose the upgrade applied from the Upgrade Table.

You are able to apply your infusions to your upgraded improvised weapons.

5th Level - Extra Attack

Starting 5th level, you can attack twice, rather than once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

9th Level - Junkrat's Armor

At 9th level, you have found new uses for all the scrap you carry around for makeshift weapons. Now, you know how to enhance your armor with ad hoc ablative shielding.

After finishing a long rest and if you are wearing medium or heavy armor, your armor gains a bonus to Armor Class equal to your Intelligence modifier (a minimum bonus of +1). Whenever you take damage, roll 1d4. On a 4, pieces of this scrap-built extra armor break off, and your bonus decreases by 1 point until it returns to its normal base value.

15th Level - Sage of Junk

By 15th level, you have become a lethal force with any random object that fits your fancy:

  • Whenever you hold an improvised weapon, you can automatically apply a random upgrade from the Upgrade Table.
  • When you cast a spell of 1st level or higher, the next attack you make with an upgraded improvised weapon deals extra force damage equal to 1d10 times the level of the spell cast, to a maximum of 5d10.
  • You now gain the Junkrat's Armor bonus after a short or long rest, instead of only a long rest.
Homebrew / Subclasses

Sentinel Blade

Sentinel Blade

The Sentinel Blade embodies the essence of unwavering defense, blending masterful swordplay with unbreakable resolve. Trained to stand as the ultimate shield for their allies, these warriors adopt a specialized stance that turns every strike against them into an opportunity. Their blades move with precision, deflecting blows with ease and delivering calculated ripostes.

Aegis Flow

Starting at 2nd level, you learn to develop flow during the midst of combat, building on each success as you begin to flow like a dance. While using a melee weapon without a shield, whenever you land a successful hit your first time in a turn, an attack misses you, or you succeed on a saving throw from a hostile creature, you gain flow equal to 1d6 + half your total mastery. Whenever you take damage from an attack, you lose flow instead. If this damage reduces your flow to 0, you take any remaining damage. If you reduce an attack's damage to zero, you suffer no additional effects from the weapon. You can have a max amount of flow equal to twice your practitioner level, which depletes at the end of combat. You can only build flow whilst in combat.

Riposte

Starting at 6th level, when an attack misses you, or you block one with flow completely, you may make a melee attack as a reaction against the target. Additionally, you may instead spend 1 mastery point to use a technique.

Vigilant Guardian

Starting at 14th level, when an ally within melee range is hit by an attack, you can use your flow to block the attack as if it were targeting you.

Blade Dance

Starting at 18th level, you learn to harness your flow into focus. When you have at least 75% of your maximum flow and focus on a technique or use a technique through riposte, you may sacrifice 7 flow to spend 1 less mastery point.

The following goes with the subclass as part of the practitioner class

Unyielding Sentinel | Mastery

Form 1: Flowing Strike

Type: Physical

Prerequisites: Novice, Sentinel Blade

Make a weapon attack against a creature or object. The attack deals a number of d6s equal to your proficiency bonus in additional damage.

Focused (1 point)

Hit or miss, roll a number or d4s equal to half your total mastery. You gain flow equal to the total.

Form 2: Windfall Step

Type: Physical

Prerequisites: Intermediate, Sentinel Blade

You move in a mirage, teleporting to an area within 60ft of you.

Focused (1 point, 0 if you have your maximum flow).

You can use another technique that includes a weapon attack. This may be before or after you teleport.

Form 3: Ebon Tide

Type: Mental

Prerequisites: Advanced, Sentinel Blade

You may temporarily steel yourself against other manners of attacks. Until the end of your next turn, you may block damage from any source using Aegis Flow.

Focused (2 points, 1 if you your maximum flow).

The duration of this technique becomes 1 minute. Until the end of your next turn, if you would succeed on a saving throw and normally take half damage, you would instead take no damage.

Form 4: Dance of Death

Type: Physical

Prerequisites: Master, Sentinel Blade

Duration: 1 minute

For the next minute, your maximum flow and the flow you gain is doubled. During this time, you have vulnerability to attacks while your flow is 0.

You must use an action to end this effect

Focused (1 points).

You may use another technique from this form

Homebrew / Subclasses

Spellbreaker

Spellbreaker

Description

Bulwarks who spend their training bettering themselves against the ever-present threat of magic. Spellbreakers are the last thing a wizard wants to see on the field of battle, usually resulting in a fairly one sided encounter.

Features:

  • 3rd Level - Out of the Inferno
  • 7th Level - Spell-Shatter
  • 13th Level - Anticipation
  • 18th Level - Willbreaker

3rd Level - Out of the Inferno

When you choose this specialization at 3rd level, you learn to incorporate methods to help you avoid magical effects into your stance. While your defensive stance is active, you also gain resistance to fire, cold, lightning, and acid damage.

7th Level - Spell-Shatter

Starting at 7th level, magical warding effects become inefficient at halting your progress. When you hit a creature or object with a weapon attack, all spells from the abjuration school immediately end if they are affecting the target.

13th Level - Anticipation

When you reach 13th level, you gain an understanding and fortitude against the ways that mages tend to fight. When you enter your defensive stance, you automatically succeed on the next intelligence, wisdom, or charisma saving throw you make before it ends.

18th Level - Willbreaker

At 18th level, your magical defenses allow you to nearly completely ignore the effects of lesser magic, making your foes need to drain their resources to even hope to defeat you. You are immune to the effects of cantrips and 1st and 2nd level spells, unless you wish to be affected by them.

Homebrew / Subclasses

Star Blade

Star Blade

Star Blade

You have spent many a night training under the stars and became touched by cosmic energy to shape light as you see fit. Creating armaments of pure light and radiance you become a beacon for those lost in the dark.

Features:

  • 3rd Level - Hardlight
  • One With the Stars
  • Astral Multitool
  • Shooting Stars
  • Galactic Aegis
  • Stellar Expanse

3rd Level - Hardlight

3rd-Level Feature

At 3rd level, you gain an amount of Hardlight charges equal to your double proficiency bonus, resetting on a long rest. You can use one charge to conjure a mundane melee weapon you are proficient with out of radiant light. This weapon does radiant damage, and counts as a magical weapon. Alternatively, you can spend one charge to conjure up an instrument or tool you have proficiency with. Equipment conjured up using this feature lasts an hour.

At 15th level this changes from 1 hours to 8 hours.

7th Level - One With the Stars

7th-Level Feature

At 7th level, you gain a bonus to damage and attack rolls and ability checks with Hardlight equipment equal to half your Wisdom modifier.

7th Level - Astral Multitool

7th-Level Feature

At 7th level, you can spend a bonus action to change your Hardlight equipment into another piece of equipment. You can use this feature once per short rest.

10th Level - Shooting Stars

10th-Level Feature

Starting at 10th level, your mastery over hardlight weapons has granted you the ability to create ranged weapons. Creating a ranged weapons costs 2 hardlight and a bonus action to create. The ammunition it uses looks like a shooting star as you fire the weapons, and does not consume a hardlight charge.

15th Level - Galactic Aegis

15th-Level Feature

At 15th level, you can spend one Hardlight charge to create Hardlight armor. Hardlight armor counts as magical heavy armor, and has a base AC of 10 + your Dexterity modifier+ your Wisdom modifier. If a creature other than yourself wears this armor, it loses its properties.

Additionally, you can spend one Hardlight charge to create a Hardlight shield. This shield counts as a magical shield that provides 3/4 cover for yourself, this shield does not provide the base AC of a shield. If a creature other than yourself equips this shield, it loses its properties.

18th Level - Stellar Expanse

18th-Level Feature

At 18th level, you can spend 2 Hardlight charges as a bonus action to empower yourself for one minute. Whenever you hit a creature with a Hardlight weapon, the weapon does an additional 3d4 radiant damage. While you have a Hardlight shield equipped, if an enemy misses you with a weapon attack, you can use your reaction to gain advantage on all attack rolls against them until the end of your next turn.

Additionally, you can maintain one piece of Hardlight equipment indefinitely. While this equipment exists, your total amount of Hardlight charges is reduced by one until it is dismissed.

Homebrew / Subclasses

Storm Chaser

Storm Chaser

Storm chasers are a select few drifters along the astral plane, seeking out natural and magical phenomena to bolster their own power. While primarily existing on the astral plane, a storm chaser can be just as effective on the material plane, or anywhere a storm can be found, as they can make good use of bows and crossbows, in addition to the firearms traditionally used while on the astral plane.

Storm Chaser Magic

Starting at 3rd level, you learn an additional spell when you reach certain levels in this class, as shown in the Storm Chaser Spells table. The spell counts as a ranger spell for you, but it doesn’t count against the number of ranger spells you know.

Ranger Level Spells
3rd Thunderwave
5th Vortex Warp
9th Call Lightning
13th Ice Storm
17th Control Winds

Firearm Proficiency

At 3rd Level, you have learned to harness the potency of firearms to complement the powers of the storms you chase. You gain proficiency with firearms.

Thundercrack

Starting at 3rd level, when you take this archetype at 3rd level, you are able to unleash a deafening boom when you use your ranged weapons. Once on each of your turns, when you attack with a ranged weapon, you can force each creature within 10 feet of you to make a constitution saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, the creature takes 1d8 thunder damage. The damage increases to 2d8 at 11th level.

Charged Shell

At 7th level, when you take the attack action, you can forgo your extra attack feature to make a single ranged weapon attack. This attack deals triple the damage dice of the weapon you used, and deals lightning damage instead of bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing. This attack is also critical on a d20 roll of 19 or 20 if used during a storm.

Storm Caller

At 11th level, you have learned to bring storms to you. As an action, you call forth a vortex at a point you can see within 60 feet. The vortex is a cylinder with a radius of 30 feet, and a height of 90 feet. The vortex counts as a storm for the purposes of Charged Shell.

As a bonus action on each of your turns while the vortex lasts, you can target a creature inside, striking them with a bolt of lightning. The target must make a dexterity saving throw, taking 3d10 lightning on a failure, or half as much on a successful save.

The vortex lasts for 10 minutes, and once used, cannot be summoned again until you finish a long rest, or spend a spell slot of at least 3rd level or higher to summon it again. No more than 1 vortex can exist at once.

Eye of the Storm

At 15th level, you gain resistance to lightning and thunder damage.

Additionally, you can target yourself with the bolt of lightning from your storm caller ability. If you do so, instead of taking damage, your next charged shell attack deals extra damage equal to twice the amount of damage the lightning would have dealt. This also causes the attack to be critical on a d20 roll of 18, 19, or 20.

Homebrew / Subclasses

Super Wizard

Super Wizard

Description

We know you’re still a spellblade

Prerequisites: Wizard 20

Proficiencies

When you take this prestige class, choose two more skills from the Wizard skill proficiencies. You are proficient in both of those skills.

Ascendant Spellcasting

Additionally when you take this prestige class, you gain a new set of spell slots to fuel your spells. You gain spell slots as per the Wizard table based on your prestige level minus 20. When you prepare spells for the day, you may now prepare a number of spells equal to your prestige level + your intelligence modifier.

You learn two wizard cantrips of your choice, and one additional wizard cantrip at 24th and 30th level.

Mystical Recovery

At 21st level when you use your Arcane Recovery Feature, you instead use your prestige level when determining the amount of spell levels you can recover. Additionally, any unspent spell levels may be recovered on later short rests before the end of your next long rest.

Expanded Arcane Tradition

When you reach 22nd level, you choose an arcane tradition, shaping your practice of magic throughout a multitude of schools. You may choose the same tradition, or you may choose to expand to a new tradition to expand your capabilities.

Your choice grants you features at 22nd level, and again at 26th, 30th, and 34th level.

Legendary Signature Spells

At 23rd level, your repertoire of signature spells improves to encompass higher level spells. Choose one 4th and one 5th level spell in your spellbook to add to your signature spells. You always have these spells prepared, they don’t count towards the number of spells you have prepared, and you can cast them once each at their lowest level without expending a spell slot. When you do so, you can’t do so again until you finish a short or long rest.

If you want to cast either spell at a higher level, you must expend a spell slot as normal.

Ability Score Improvement

When you reach 24th level, and again at 28th, 32nd, 36th, and 39th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two of your ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can’t increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.

Elite Spell Mastery

At 25th level, your magic flows through you effortlessly, and is able to produce your most practiced spells at no drain to you. Choose one of your 3rd level signature spells. You are now able to cast that spell at its lowest level without expending a spell slot. You no longer need to finish a short or long rest to do so again.

At 29th level, the other 3rd level signature spell is granted the same benefit.

Revised Wizards instead gain +1 to the maximum spellforge modifications to all of their created spells at 29th level.

Legendary Spell Mastery

When you reach 33rd level, it is practically nothing for you to produce even the most potent of your signature spells. You are now able to cast your 4th level signature spell at its lowest level without expending a spell slot, and do not need to finish a short or long rest to do so again.

When you reach 37th level, your 5th level signature spell is granted the same benefit.

Scholar of the Ages

At 38th level, your vast collection of arcane knowledge is always an arm’s reach away, and can never again be taken from you.
