Should a spellbook of yours ever be lost or destroyed, you can use an action to return the book to your hands in perfect condition. If the book was destroyed, it is returned in its entirety.

Arcane Intellect

When you reach 40th level, your constant dealing with arcane knowledge has opened your mind to concepts that, prior to now, you could not even begin to conceive. Your Intelligence and Wisdom scores both increase by 4, to a maximum of 30.

Homebrew / Subclasses

Swindler

Swindler

Swindler

Cheaters go by many names; swindlers, con-artists, charlatans. Whatever they may call you, whoever you might be perceived as, you’ll always be the first to let the world know that the cards in your hand are there entirely legitimately— you couldn’t have stacked the deck, the dealer shuffled beforehand! You weren’t responsible for the incomprehensibly lucky die rolls, either— you were borrowing the dealer’s dice, after all. Oh, and the drinking game you outlasted the dwarf barbarian in? You couldn’t have watered your drink down, the dealer poured it out for you!

…What? You’re being accused of paying off the dealer? Poppycock.

Features:

  • 3rd Level - Swindler’s Luck
  • 9th Level - Loaded Dice
  • 13th Level - Sure Shot
  • 17th Level - Don of Con

3rd Level - Swindler’s Luck

At 3rd level, luck seems to appear whenever it benefits you, almost as if you’re cheating. Whenever you make a roll with advantage, you may meddle with the roll, forgoing that advantage, and roll normally. The next time you roll without advantage, you roll with advantage.

9th Level - Loaded Dice

At 9th level, you cheat  act with more finesse, giving you more control over your actions. Whenever you make a roll with advantage, you may forgo that advantage to create a loaded die. You may store a number of loaded dice equal to half your proficiency bonus, rounded down. These loaded dice disappear on a short or long rest.

Whenever you roll an attack roll, ability check, or saving throw, you may spend one of your loaded dice to give yourself advantage on that roll. You may only spend one loaded die per turn.

13th Level - Sure Shot

By 13th level, your “luck” is far too consistent to be inconspicuous. When you roll with advantage, you may forgo that advantage to add +3 to the roll’s total. If the roll succeeds, you gain one loaded die.

17th Level - Don of Con

At 17th level, it’s quite clear you’ve been cheating all this time, some way, somehow. On the bright side, you don’t have to hide it anymore— whenever you miss with an attack roll, you can spend 3 loaded dice to turn that miss into a hit. When you fail a saving throw, you can spend 2 loaded dice to succeed automatically. When you fail an ability check, you can spend 1 loaded die to make the result 20.

Homebrew / Subclasses

Sword Saint

Sword Saint

Sword Saint

Though colloquially referred to as “Sword Saints”, swords are only the most popular weapon they are seen mastering, not the only weapon. These practitioners devote themselves to training with a specific weapon of their choosing, rarely ever making use of other armaments.

Weapon Pledge

At 2nd level, choose a weapon you are proficient in to pledge your devotion to (ex. longsword, shortbow, glaive, etc). When wielding the a weapon, the following features are made available to you.

Flying Weapon

You learn how to wield the weapon without needing to even touch it. You can use a bonus action to move the weapon up to 30 feet in any direction or teleport it back to your hand instantly. You can attack and use techniques with the weapon as if you were standing in the weapon’s space.

While the weapon is being controlled in this way, it is treated as if you were still holding it (you require a free hand to attack with it, or two hands if it’s two-handed, etc). You cannot move it more than 120 feet away from yourself, and if brought outside of this range, you cannot control it further until it’s within the range.

Draining Strike

If you kill a hostile creature with an attack made with your flying weapon, you can use a reaction to drain the creature, regaining mastery points equal to half your maximum (rounded up). After you use this feature, you must take a short or long rest before you can use it again.

Weapon Devotee

At 6th level, you become increasingly adept at using your weapon for techniques. In the same bonus action that you use to move the weapon, you can spend 1 mastery point to use the primary effect of a technique you know. Beginning at 14th level, you can focus the technique you use.

Weapon Mount

At 14th level, your control over the weapon you devoted yourself to extends even to being able to ride it. Your weapon can be ridden in the air, during which it cannot be used for techniques. It has a flying speed equal to your movement speed plus an additional 30 feet and can carry up to 500 pounds before it can no longer fly.

Armamentarium

At 18th level, you can control two flying weapons at once, with the second not being treated as if you were holding it. If you use a bonus action to use a technique with one, the other can make a single weapon attack.

Homebrew / Subclasses

Templar

Templar

Description

The scourge of the unholy. Bulwarks who call themselves Templar are the bane of all undead, fiends, and those that follow evil practices. Being a Bulwark, this means that such forces are met with only the strongest protections whilst engaging a Templar.

Features:

  • 3rd Level - Protection from Evil
  • 3rd Level - Spellcasting
  • 7th Level - Sanctify
  • 13th Level - Divine Stance
  • 18th Level - Evil’s Bane

3rd Level - Protection from Evil

When you select this specialization at 3rd level, you gain a supernatural protection from the forces of evil. When an undead, fiend, or other evil aligned creature deals damage to you, the total damage is reduced by an amount equal to your proficiency bonus.

3rd Level - Spellcasting

Additionally when you select this specialization, you learn to merge divine magic with your defensive tactics.

Cantrips

You learn two cantrips of your choice from the cleric spell list. You learn an additional cleric cantrip of your choice at 10th level.

Spell Slots

The Templar Spellcasting table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your cleric spells of 1st level and higher. To cast one of these spells, you must expend a slot of the spell’s level or higher. You regain all expended spell slots when you finish a long rest.

For example, if you know the 1st-level spell cure wounds and have a 1st-level and a 2nd-level spell slot available, you can cast cure wounds using either slot.

Spells Known of 1st-Level and Higher

You know three 1st-level cleric spells of your choice.

The Spells Known column of the Templar Spellcasting table shows when you learn more cleric spells of 1st-level or higher. Each of these new spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots. For instance, when you reach 7th level in this class, you can learn one new spell of 1st or 2nd level.

Whenever you gain a level in this class, you can replace one of the cleric spells you know with another spell of your choice from the cleric spell list. The new spell must be of a level for which you have spell slots.

Spellcasting Ability

Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for your cleric spells. The power of your spells may come from a deity, or personal sense of conviction against the unholy.

Spell save DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Wisdom modifier

Spell attack modifier = your proficiency bonus + your Wisdom modifier

7th Level - Sanctify

When you reach 7th level, you gain the ability to absolve creatures of the evil they embody. When an undead, fiend, or other evil aligned creature damages you, you may use your reaction to expend a spell slot. Doing so places the creature under the effects of Turn Undead (even if the target is not undead) on a failed wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. While they are turned in this way, the creature does not run away, and instead falls prone where they are standing on their turn.

13th Level - Divine Stance

At 13th level your defensive stance now carries with it the capacity to share your magic with your allies. When you cast a cleric spell with a range of self, or a cleric spell that only affects you while your defensive stance is active, you can choose to have it also affect each ally within 20 feet of you. If a spell’s duration would last longer than your defensive stance, it ends on your allies when your defensive stance ends.

18th Level - Evil’s Bane

When you reach 18th level your presence alone is enough to force evil from their hiding places. Undead, fiends, and other evil aligned creatures automatically fail saving throws against your dueling stance.

Homebrew / Subclasses

The Extraplanar

The Extraplanar

The Extraplanar

Powerful entities of the outer, or even inner planes often seek out mortals to do their bidding on the material plane. Sometimes, however, instead of power similar to their own, they might grant their warlocks an ability to pull creatures from other planes to an extraordinary degree.

Features:

  • Extended Spell List
  • 1st Level - Planar Tether
  • 6th Level - Ethereal Stores
  • 10th Level - Undying Binds
  • 14th Level - Sacrificial Summoning

Extended Spell List

The Extraplanar lets you choose from an expanded list of spells when you learn a warlock spell. The following spells are added to the warlock spell list for you.

Spell Level - Spells:

Sorcerer Level Spells
1st Bane, Sanctuary
2nd Arcanist's Magic Aura, Vortex Warp
3rd Bestow Curse, Glyph of Warding
4th Giant Insect, Summon Elemental
5th Creation, Summon Celestial

1st Level - Planar Tether

When you form this pact at 1st level, you are granted the ability to tether your summoned creatures to your plane, granting them additional strengths.

When you cast a warlock spell that summons a single creature, you may undergo a special ritual during the casting of the spell. Doing so changes the spell's casting time to 10 minutes, and the summon lasts until it is dispelled. If the spell normally requires concentration, you may ignore the requirement.

When you summon a creature in this way, it is referred to as your tether, and it gains the following benefits:

  • You can replace its hit points with 5 x your warlock level.
  • It adds your proficiency bonus to its damage rolls.
  • If the creatures to-hit bonus is less than that of your spell attack bonus, it may instead use your spell attack bonus when attacking.

You learn the Find Familiar spell, it counts as a warlock spell for you, and it does not count towards your total spells known.

If you summon another creature using this ritual, any previous creatures summoned by it are immediately dispelled. After you complete this ritual, you must finish a long rest before you can do so again.

6th Level - Ethereal Stores

Starting at 6th level, you can briefly store items away for later use. You can cast the [Wristpocket] spell a number of times equal to your charisma modifier without expending a spell slot. When you do, the stored object is sent to the ethereal plane, and the spell does not require concentration. You regain all expended uses of this ability when you finish a long rest.

Additionally, you can see into the ethereal plane up to 10 ft.

10th Level - Undying Binds

At 10th level, when tether drops to 0 hit points, you can use your reaction to expend a pact slot. Doing so will restore 50 hit points to the summon.

14th Level - Sacrificial Summoning

Starting on 14th level, while your Planar Tether summon is active, you can use an action to sacrifice part of yourself to empower it and your spells, doing so allows you to channel this ability until your next long rest, or until you end it as an action. While channeling this ability, you have the following effects:

  • Your hit point maximum is reduced by 30.
  • You have disadvantage on Constitution checks and saving throws, except for those made to maintain concentration.
  • Your tether has advantage on all saving throws
  • You can use a bonus action to give your tether temporary hit points equal to your warlock level
  • Creatures within 10 ft of your tether have disadvantage on saving throws against your spells.

If you end this ability early, you cannot use it again until you finish a long rest.

Homebrew / Subclasses

The Undead lord

The Undead lord

Undead Lord

There is undeath in your blood. Where other sorcerers inherit fire or storm, you inherited the grave — and the authority that comes with it. The dead do not merely answer you; they kneel.

Features:

1st Level - There's Undeath in Your Blood

1st Level - Born to Rule

6th Level - A King, and His Legion

14th Level - Undead Lord

18th Level - All for One

1st Level - There's Undeath in Your Blood

Starting at 1st level, you gain access to all spells from the Necromancy school that create or manipulate undead. These count as sorcerer spells for you.

1st Level - Born to Rule

Starting at 1st level, as an action you can animate one humanoid corpse within 30 feet of you into a zombie, or one pile of bones into a skeleton.

All undead created with this feature exist under your control for 1 hour, at which point they revert to an inanimate corpse or pile of bones. They act at the end of your turn in initiative, following your telepathic or verbal commands to the best of their ability.

You may use this feature once per long rest, unless you spend a sorcery point to do so again.

6th Level - A King, and His Legion

At 6th level, you gain a new Metamagic option. This does not count against the number of Metamagic options you know.

When you cast a spell that creates undead, you may spend a number of sorcery points equal to the level of the spell to double the number of undead created by that spell, or the number of undead you may re-assert control of with the spell.

14th Level - Undead Lord

At 14th level, spells and effects that specify a creature's type as undead treat you as an undead.

You no longer require food, water, air, or sleep. To take a long rest, you must spend 4 hours in an inactive state in order to complete the rest.

As an action, you may veil yourself to undead. If they would otherwise be hostile, they treat you with indifference for 10 minutes, or until you take any harmful action towards them. Additionally, for this duration, undead have disadvantage on all attacks against you, and you have advantage on any saving throws they force you to make. You may take this action once per short or long rest.

18th Level - All for One

At 18th level, when you are reduced to 0 hit points, you may spend 2 sorcery points and reduce one undead under your control within 15 feet of you to ash. You teleport to where that undead was, and regain hit points equal to half your sorcerer level plus your Charisma modifier.

Homebrew / Subclasses

True Path

True Path

True Path

The True Path requires the constant repetition of martial forms until absolute perfection is achieved. With perfection comes “truth”, an aspect of life that such practitioners would consider their peak.

Truest Strike

At 2nd level, you learn the True Strike cantrip and can cast it as a bonus action. When you cast it, you gain its benefits on the current turn rather than the next turn, and it doesn’t require concentration for you. The spell ends at the end of your turn.

Once per short or long rest, if you kill a hostile creature affected by True Strike, you can use your reaction to regain mastery points equal to half your maximum (rounded up).

Truth Beyond Doubt

At 6th level, when you strike true, you can bypass the defenses of your enemies. A technique’s attack that has advantage due to True Strike’s effect ignores an enemy’s resistances. At 18th level, such an enemy’s damage immunities are treated as resistances (which cannot be ignored).

Verify

At 14th level, when you cast true strike on a target, you can learn their resistances, immunities, and current hit points. Additionally, you gain advantage on insight checks against the target.

Perfect Strike

At 18th level, you can analyze the intrinsic truth about a creature. When you cast True Strike, you can spend 1 mastery point to give your next technique’s attack a +10 bonus to the attack roll and have the creature make their next save against the technique with disadvantage.

Homebrew / Subclasses

Umbral Lord Patron

Umbral Lord Patron

Description

You have made your pact with a being of the Shadowfell—not a tyrant, not a monster, but a sovereign of sorrow. The Umbral Lord is a force of stillness and forgetting, a presence woven into the death of joy and the fading of names. It offers you no glory, only power—drawn from what others try not to remember.

Features:

  • 3rd Level - Umbral Lord Spells
  • 3rd Level - Echoes of the Forgotten
  • 6th Level - Gravity of Sorrow
  • 10th Level - Despair-Wrought Form
  • 14th Level - Embrace of Oblivion

3rd Level - Umbral Lord Spells

The magic of your patron ensures you always have certain spells ready; when you reach a Warlock level specified in the Umbral Lord Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

Umbral Lord Spells

  • 3rd: Dissonant Whispers, Phantasmal Force, Calm Emotions, Cause Fear
  • 5th: Summon Shadowspawn, Fear
  • 7th: Shadow of Moil, Phantasmal Killer
  • 9th: Dream, Modify Memory

These spells reflect the patron’s nature—magic that distorts perception, suppresses emotion, and turns sorrow into power.

3rd Level - Echoes of the Forgotten

3rd-Level Umbral Lord Feature

Your presence carries the emotional residue of the Shadowfell—haunting, weighty, and impossible to shake. Even the fiercest mind stumbles under the echo of forgotten regrets.

You gain proficiency in Insight or Intimidation (your choice).

Additionally, when you damage a creature with a Warlock spell or cantrip, you can mark it with Lingering Regret until the end of your next turn. The next time the creature makes an attack roll or ability check, it subtracts your Charisma modifier (minimum 1) from the roll, as if gripped by an emotion it cannot name.

You can affect a number of creatures this way equal to your Warlock level divided by 3 (rounded up), regaining all uses when you finish a long rest.

6th Level - Gravity of Sorrow

6th-Level Umbral Lord Feature

Despair halts even the strongest charge. You call forth a field of emotional gravity—a stillness that seeps into flesh and will alike.

As a bonus action, you designate a point within 60 feet. That point becomes the center of a 15-foot radius zone of heavy emotional drag until the start of your next turn.

Each creature of your choice that starts its turn in the area or enters it for the first time on a turn must succeed on a Strength saving throw against your spell save DC or have its speed reduced to 0 until the end of that turn. On a failed save, the creature also cannot Dash until the end of its next turn, as if the very act of movement had become too much to bear.

You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, regaining all uses when you finish a long rest.

10th Level - Despair-Wrought Form

10th-Level Umbral Lord Feature

Your patron reshapes you into an embodiment of psychic weight. You don’t lash out with fire or blade—you unravel resolve, layer by layer.

You gain resistance to necrotic and psychic damage.

As an action, you can manifest a mantle of oppressive sorrow for 1 minute. While active:

  • You emit a 20-foot radius aura of emotional gravity.
  • Each enemy that starts its turn in the aura must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or become frightened until the start of its next turn.
  • If a creature fails this saving throw a second time in a row, it becomes incapacitated until the start of its next turn, lost in overwhelming emotion.
  • If a creature fails the save on three consecutive turns, it becomes Paralyzed until it succeeds on the Wisdom saving throw or is outside the aura of oppressive sorrow. -The oppresive sorrow overrides any fear you are feeling, while the arua is active you are immune to frightened condition. You can use this feature once per long rest, or by expending a pact magic spell slot.

14th Level - Embrace of Oblivion

14th-Level Umbral Lord Feature

You carry the end in your wake. When a soul slips away nearby, you seize its unraveling and cast it like a shadow across the battlefield.

When a creature you can see within 60 feet drops to 0 hit points, you can use your reaction to claim its fading essence. Choose a number of creatures equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum 1) within 30 feet of the dying creature. Each must make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC.

  • On a failed save, a creature takes 5d10 psychic damage and is frightened until the end of its next turn.
  • On a successful save, the creature takes half damage and is not frightened.

While frightened in this way, a creature loses all temporary hit points, cannot gain temporary hit points, and cannot benefit from healing.

If a creature is already frightened by any means, it must use its action on its next turn to Dash away from you. If it cannot move, it instead takes an additional 5d10 psychic damage, writhing in place under the pressure of oblivion.

You can use this reaction up to a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier per long rest.

You are not a torch in the darkness. You are the hush after the flame goes out.

Homebrew / Subclasses

Undead Warlock 2024

Undead Warlock 2024

Description

You've made a pact with a deathless being, a creature that defies the cycle and life and death, forsaking its mortal shell so it might eternally pursue its unfathomable ambitions. For such beings, time and morality are fleeting things, the concerns of those for whom grains of sand still rush through life's hourglass. Having once been mortal themselves, these ancient undead know firsthand the paths of ambition and the routes past the doors of death. They eagerly share this profane knowledge, along with other secrets, with those who work their will among the living. Beings of this type include the demilich Acererak, the vampire tyrant Kas the Bloody-Handed, the githyanki lich-queen Vlaakith, the dracolich Dragotha, the undead pharaoh Ankhtepot, and the elusive Darklord, Azalin Rex.

Expanded Spell List

3rd-level Undead feature

When you reach a Warlock level specified in the Undead Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells available and it doesn't count towards your amount of warlock spells known.

Form of Dread

3rd-level Undead feature You manifest an aspect of your patron's dreadful power. As a bonus action, you transform for 1 minute. You gain the following benefits while transformed:

  • You gain temporary hit points equal to 1d10 + your warlock level.,
  • Once during each of your turns, when you hit a creature with an attack roll, you can force it to make a Wisdom saving throw, and if the saving throw fails, the target is frightened of you until the end of your next turn.,
  • You are immune to the frightened condition.,You can transform a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest. The appearance of your Form of Dread reflects some aspect of your patron. For example, your form could be a shroud of shadows forming the crown and robes of your lich patron, or your body might glow with glyphs from ancient funerary rites and be surrounded by desert winds, suggesting your mummy patron.

Grave Touched

6th-level Undead feature Your patron's powers have a profound effect on your body and magic. You don't need to eat, drink, or breathe. In addition, once during each of your turns, when you hit a creature with an attack roll and roll damage against the creature, you can replace the damage type with necrotic damage. While you are using your Form of Dread, you can roll one additional damage die when determining the necrotic damage the target takes.

Necrotic Husk

10th-level Undead feature

Your connection to undeath and necrotic energy now saturates your body. You have resistance to necrotic damage. If you are transformed using your Form of Dread, you instead become immune to necrotic damage. In addition, when you would be reduced to 0 hit points, you can use your reaction to retore your hit points to twice your warlock level instead and cause your body to erupt with deathly energy. Each creature of your choice that is within 30 feet of you takes necrotic damage equal to 2d10 + your warlock level. You then gain 1 level of exhaustion. Once you use this reaction, you can't do so again until you finish 1d4 long rests.

Spirit Projection

Your spirit can become untethered from your physical form. As an action, you can project your spirit from your body. The body you leave behind is unconscious and in a state of suspended animation. Your spirit resembles your mortal form in almost every way, replicating your game statistics but not your possessions. Any damage or other effects that apply to your spirit or physical body affects the other. Your spirit can remain outside your body for up to 1 hour. When your projection ends, your spirit returns to your body or your body magically teleports to your spirit's space (your choice). While projecting your spirit, you gain the following benefits:

  • Your spirit and body gain resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage.,
  • When you cast a spell of the conjuration or necromancy school, the spell doesn't require verbal or somatic components or material components that lack a gold cost.,
  • You have a flying speed equal to your walking speed and can hover. You can move through creatures and objects as if they were difficult terrain, but you take 1d10 force damage if you end your turn inside a creature or an object.,
  • While you are using your Form of Dread, once during each of your turns when you deal necrotic damage to a creature, you regain hit points equal to half the amount of necrotic damage dealt.,

Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a long rest or by expending a Pact slot.

Homebrew / Subclasses

Unfettered

Unfettered

Description:

Wearing heavy armors tends to take immense physical strain, and as such usually restricts the movements of the wearer. Bulwarks who call themselves Unfettered work tirelessly to be just as, if not more efficient with their movements while donning these heavy suits.

Features:

  • 3rd Level - Heightened Agility
  • 3rd Level - Iron Fist
  • 7th Level - Armored Movement
  • 13th Level - Quaking Vault
  • 18th Level - Weightless Steel

3rd Level - Iron Fist

When you select this specialization at 3rd level, your movements are swift and fluid enough to carry the full force of your armor with them. When you make an unarmed attack while wearing heavy armor, you can choose to treat it as being a weapon with the heavy property, and you can roll a d8 in place of the normal damage of your unarmed attacks.

3rd Level - Heightened Agility

Additionally at 3rd level, the strength built by wearing heavy armor extends to enhance your reflexes. Whenever you make an ability check or saving throw, you can replace your dexterity modifier with your strength modifier.

7th Level - Armored Movement

When you reach 7th level, you learn to move yourself with considerable speed for being weighed down. Your walking speed increases by 10 feet, and increases by another 10 feet at 18th level.

13th Level - Quaking Vault

Starting at 13th level, your poise and agility work in conjunction to make landing less deadly to you, and more so to those around you. You become resistant to falling damage while wearing heavy armor, and landing no longer knocks you prone. When you land while wearing heavy armor, creatures within 15 feet of you take 2d10 bludgeoning damage, and must succeed on a strength saving throw (DC 8 + your strength modifier + your proficiency bonus) or be knocked prone. A creature can only be affected by this ability once per turn.

18th Level - Weightless Steel

At 18th level, heavy armor ceases to be a burden for you in any meaningful way. Heavy armor weighs nothing to you while you are wearing it, and you can add half your strength modifier to your armor class while wearing it.

Homebrew / Subclasses

Warrior of the Unbound Mind

Warrior of the Unbound Mind

Warrior of the Unbound Mind

Monks who follow the Warrior of the Unbound Mind manifest fragments of their consciousness as psionic projections. These spectral clones serve as both weapons and tools, allowing the monk to fight across multiple positions at once, confuse enemies, and strike with thought alone.

Features:

  • 3rd Level - Psionic Projection
  • 6th Level - Mental Anchor
  • 11th Level - Unbound Multiplicity
  • 17th Level - Ascendant Mind

3rd Level - Psionic Projection

At 3rd Level you learn to manifest one psychic shadow that shares your mobility.

  • Summon Projection: As a Bonus Action summon one Projection (lasts 1 hour) in an unoccupied space within 30 ft, the projection is a Construct of Psionic energy.
    • Stats: AC equals your Focus Save DC. HP equals two Martial Arts dice + Wisdom Mod. It is vulnerable to force damage, but immune to all conditions.
    • Mobile Strike: Any unarmed strike you make can originate from your space or the Projection's space. Attacks originating from the Projection deal Psychic damage.
    • Projection Movement: The Projection shares your movement speed. You can move the Projection up to your speed, using your movement allowance. It must remain within 60 ft. of you.
  • Psionic Burst: When the Projection is destroyed, use a Reaction and 1 Focus Point. Creatures of your choice within 10 ft. make an Intelligence Save, taking 2 Martial Arts dice psychic damage on a failure, or half damage on a success.

6th Level - Mental Anchor

Your Projection can now bind foes with psychic energy.

  • Psionic Grapple: Once per turn, when a Projection hits a creature with an unarmed strike, you can forgo the damage to attempt a psionic grapple. The target must succeed on an Intelligence saving throw or be grappled by psionic force. The DC for the saving throw and any escape attempts equals your Focus Point DC.
  • The Projection immediately dissipates when the grapple succeeds, and cannot trigger Psionic Burst.

11th Level - Unbound Multiplicity

Your mind’s grasp over its projections expands, granting superior tactical options.

  • Dual Existence: You can maintain up to two Psionic Projections at the same time. You may use all features from either Projection.
  • Projection Tactics: When a creature is hit by your stunning strike and within 5 feet of both your projections, they have disadvantage on the saving throw to resist the stun

17th Level - Ascendant Mind

You gain the power to lock down multiple foes and achieve psychic dominance.

  • Unbound Grip: Your Psionic Grapple no longer requires you to forgo damage on the attack, and it can target a creature of any size.
  • Domination Burst: When a creature fails its save against your Psionic Burst, the psychic damage increases to 3 rolls of your martial arts die, and they have disadvantage on all wisdom, intelligence and charisma saving throws and checks until the end of their next turn.
  • Relentless Command: While a creature is grappled by your Psionic Grapple, you can spend 1 Focus Point as a bonus action to move that creature up to 30 ft. This movement uses up to 30 feet of your own movement allowance.
Homebrew / Subclasses

Way fo the Feral Fang

Way fo the Feral Fang

Way fo the Feral Fang

Monks who follow the Way of the Feral Fang tap into their primal instincts, channeling the savage power of beasts. They unleash their inner ferocity, embodying the untamed fury of nature itself.

Features:

  • 3rd Level - Feral Strikes
  • 3rd Level - Closer to Nature
  • 6th Level - Bestial Agility
  • 11th Level - Fury of the Beast
  • 17th Level - Primal Resilience

3rd Level - Feral Strikes

Starting at 3rd level, when you use your Flurry of Blows feature, you can replace one of the unarmed strikes with the primal savagery cantrip. The primal savagery cantrip uses wisdom as your spellcasting ability modifier for its attack rolls.

3rd Level - Closer to Nature

Starting at 3rd level, you can choose to learn the druidcraft or shillelagh cantrip, you use wisdom as your spellcasting ability modifier for this cantrip

6th Level - Bestial Agility

At 6th level, your connection to primal instincts enhances your speed and agility. You gain the following benefits:

  • You have advantage on saving throws against effects that would cause you to be restrained or paralyzed
  • If you use your Primal savagery cantrip granted by Feral Strikes in a turn you can use your reaction when an enemy makes an attack of opportunity against you to roll a Martial Art Die and add the result to your AC until the end of your turn.

11th Level - Fury of the Beast

At 11th level, your strikes become even more savage and relentless. When you hit a creature with your primal savagery cantrip granted by your Feral Strikes feature, you can add your wisdom modifier to the damage dealt, in addition, if you spend 1 ki point, the target must also make a Wisdom saving throw (DC 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Wisdom modifier) or be frightened of you until the end of your next turn.

17th Level - Primal Resilience

Starting at 17th level, your primal connection enhances your body’s resilience and ferocity. As a bonus action, you can spend 4 ki points to enter a primal state of feral resilience that last for 1 minute. You gain the following benefits when in this state:

  • You have advantage on saving throws against being charmed or frightened.
  • You add an additional Martial Art die to your unarmed strikes
  • You have advantage on all Strength and Dexterity saving throws, and you gain temporary hit points equal to your Monk level at the start of each of your turns. Once you use this feature, you can’t use it again until you finish a long rest.
Homebrew / Subclasses

Way of the Crimson Veil

Way of the Crimson Veil

Way of the Crimson Veil

The Way of the Crimson Veil is an ancient discipline, its roots tangled in the dark history of Toril. Legends trace the origin of these blood monks to the city of Yûlash, a fallen city located near the ruined kingdom of Cormanthor. In the twilight of the city’s prosperity, a small sect of monks sought knowledge in places best left undisturbed. They unearthed forbidden tomes from the deep catacombs beneath Yûlash, written in blood and sealed by ancient rites.

Features:

3rd Level - Crimson Transfusion

3rd Level - Sanguine Arts

6th Level - Bloodbound Pact

11th Level - Improved Sanguine Arts

17th Level - Sanguine Edict

3rd Level - Crimson Transfusion

Starting at 3rd level, you learn to harness the power of your blood to fuel your abilities. You may use Crimson Transfusion to substitute your life force in place of ki. When you would normally expend a ki point, you can instead expend a use of Crimson Transfusion. When you do so, you take necrotic damage equal to three rolls of your Martial Arts die for each ki point replaced. Necrotic damage dealt by this ability treats immunity as resistance. You may use this ability a number of times equal to your wisdom modifier, regaining all uses upon completing a short or long rest.

3rd Level - Sanguine Arts

Starting at 3rd level, you unlock blood magic techniques that tap into your life force. You take necrotic damage equal to two rolls of your martial arts die. Necrotic damage dealt by this ability treats immunity as resistance. You gain access to the following Sanguine Arts abilities, which allow you to manipulate the power of blood for various effects:

  • Fleshweaver’s Mantle: As a bonus action, you may spend up to 3 ki points to weave a ward through blood magic. For each ki point spent, you may roll three of your martial arts die and gain temporary hit points equal to the total.
  • Leeching Blows: When you use your flurry of blows, you may choose to expend 2 ki points. During this flurry, your attacks deal additional necrotic damage equal to two rolls of your martial arts die. You regain hit points equal to the total necrotic damage dealt by these attacks.

6th Level - Bloodbound Pact

Starting at 6th level, you bind yourself and another willing creature through spilled blood. You may spend 2 ki to initiate a one-minute ritual, after which both you and the creature take necrotic damage equal to three rolls of your Martial Arts die. Once the ritual is complete, until your next long rest, both of you are aware of each other’s total hit points, general emotional state, and any conditions the other is afflicted by, provided they are also aware of the condition. In addition, both you and the creature gain resistance to necrotic damage for the duration.

Only one such pact may be active at a time.

11th Level - Improved Sanguine Arts

Starting at 11th level, you learn how to harness more sanguine arts.

Hemal Torrent: When you spend a ki point or use crimson transfusion, you may imbue your unarmed strikes with blood magic. Until the end of your next turn, your unarmed strikes deal slashing or piercing damage instead of bludgeoning, and you can target enemies within 30 feet.

Crimson Mist: As a bonus action, when expending a ki point, or when using crimson transfusion, you can expend 1 ki point to prepare yourself for an incoming attack. Before the end of your next turn, when you are hit by an attack, you can use your reaction to transform into a crimson mist, avoiding the attack and reappearing in an unoccupied space within 15 feet of your original location. This movement does not provoke opportunity attacks.

17th Level - Sanguine Edict

Starting at 17th level, when you take necrotic damage, as a reaction, you can make a ranged attack against a creature within 30 feet of you. On a hit, the target takes necrotic damage equal to the necrotic damage you received, before any damage reductions. This attack uses your Wisdom modifier for both the attack and damage rolls, and counts as an unarmed strike for the purpose of bonuses.

Homebrew / Subclasses

Way of the Dragon Turtle

Way of the Dragon Turtle

Way of the Dragon Turtle

Curiously, the Way of the Dragon Turtle is a bit of a misnomer for the monks that follow this style. Their link to the legendary beasts is practically nonexistent, only dubbed this way by others for their fortitude and control over heat and steam. Monks that follow this martial style are rarely taught formally, though they may occasionally take on no more than a few students who wish to learn the style. Those who follow the Way of the Dragon Turtle are self-made and remarkable, often gaining an innate understanding of the ki flowing through and around them after overcoming intense hardship. Although this style may seem less refined than its contemporaries, the technical ability of these monks is fatal to underestimate. They pose as much of a threat to their own bodies by manipulating pressure and heat as they do to others, and they must always understand their limits above all else.

Features:

  • Ki-Scorched Body
  • Impact Combustion
  • 6th Level - Pneumatic Blitz
  • 11th Level - Body of Vapor
  • 17th Level - Pressurized Retribution

Ki-Scorched Body

Perseverance manifested in the form of raw ki has scorched and hardened your soul and body. When calculating your Monk unarmored defense, you may instead use 13 + your Constitution modifier.

Additionally, your body is altered by the unrefined, explosive ki you harness, often leaving a strange mark on your likeness. You determine its appearance, or generate it randomly by rolling on the Ki-Scorched Characteristic table.

d6 Ki-Scorched Characteristic
1 Your hands and feet are blackened, giving them the appearance of charcoal.
2 Steam often rises from your ears, mouth and body when you experience intense emotions.
3 The skin around your elbows and shoulders is cracked and ossified, peeling slightly upward like the scutes of a turtle.
4 You have a large scar or burn mark on your body, which becomes searing hot in a fight.
5 Still sources of waters nearby you tend to become restless, showing tiny ripples and tremors.
6 Your skin fluctuates between feeling extremely hot and cold to the touch.

Impact Combustion

Your rudimentary abilities in channeling ki allow you to compress and expel moisture and heat. As an action, you can cast fog cloud without providing material components. Once you cast fog cloud using this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a short or long rest, unless you spend 2 ki points to cast it again.

Additionally, you gain the ability to convert the heat and force from blows you take into powerful outbursts. As a bonus action, if you have taken damage between the end of your last turn and the start of your current turn, you may spend 1 ki point to enter the Combustion state until the end of your turn. While in the Combustion state, you gain the following benefits:

  • You make Strength-based attack rolls with advantage.
  • Your unarmed strikes deal additional fire damage on a hit equal to one roll of your Martial Arts die plus your Wisdom modifier.
  • You can make one additional unarmed strike as part of your Attack action.

6th Level - Pneumatic Blitz

At 6th level, you gain the ability to catalyze the heat and momentum you build by moving into a volatile enhancement. If you move at least 30 feet in a straight line on your turn, you may immediately spend 2 ki points to increase your walking speed by 30 feet until the end of your turn. If you continue the current movement for at least 60 feet in a straight line, you may choose to emit a blast of excess pressure around you. When you end this movement, each creature within a 10-foot radius of you must succeed on a Strength saving throw or take a number of d10s equal to your proficiency bonus in force damage and be knocked prone. If a creature passes this saving throw, it takes half damage and is not knocked prone.

11th Level - Body of Vapor

At 11th level, your control of ki becomes more refined, allowing you to manipulate the elements of your physical form. As an action, you can spend 4 ki points to cast gaseous form on yourself, without providing material components. While in this form, your movement speed is not restricted to 10 feet.

Additionally, you may exit this form at any time on your turn. When you exit this form, you may heal 5d8 hit points. Once you regain hit points using this ability, you can't do so again until you finish a short or long rest.

17th Level - Pressurized Retribution

At 17th level, your mastery over the convergence and direction of ki reaches explosive heights. As a reaction to taking damage from a source other than yourself, you may spend up to six ki points. For each ki point you spend as a part of this reaction, you mitigate 5 damage. This damage mitigation is applied before any resistances you have. You may also redirect the force from this mitigated damage, blasting out a 40-foot cone of crushing steam. Creatures in this area must pass a Constitution saving throw against your ki save DC or take 10 fire damage for each ki point you spent as part of this reaction, taking half damage if they pass. Being underwater does not grant resistance to this attack.

Additionally, you are no longer required to have taken damage to enter the Combustion state as a bonus action.

Homebrew / Subclasses

Way of the Ki Blade

Way of the Ki Blade

Way of the Ki Blade

Masters of a martial discipline intertwined with the ethereal energies of ki, the practitioners of the Way of the Ki Blade are formidable warriors who wield weapons forged from the very essence of their inner strength. These adept martial artists combine their physical prowess with the disciplined art of ki manipulation, creating a dance of blades that transcends the limits of the mundane.

Features:

  • 3rd Level - Ki-Forged Weapon
  • 6th Level - Disruptive Weapon
  • 6th Level - Ki-Bound Weapon
  • 11th Level - Ki-Enhanced Focus
  • 11th Level - Ki-Forged Flurry
  • 17th Level - Ki-Blade Ascendancy

3rd Level - Ki-Forged Weapon

At 3rd level, you can spend 1 ki point as a bonus action to manifest a ki-forged weapon, turning a melee monk weapon into a weapon of pure energy for 1 minute. This weapon deals force damage instead of its regular damage type and uses your Wisdom modifier for attack and damage rolls.

In addition, at level 5 the weapon gains a +1 bonus to its attack and damage rolls, unless it is a magic weapon that already has a bonus to those rolls, this bonus increases to +2 at level 11

6th Level - Disruptive Weapon

At 6th level, once per turn you can spend a ki-point to temporarily transform your ki-forged weapon into an ethereal weapon. The next melee attack you make with it before the end of your turn ignores the target’s armor, requiring no attack roll. Instead, the target makes a Dexterity saving throw against your Ki save DC. On a failed save, the creature takes damage as if hit by an attack from your ki-forged blade and it's inner balance and movement is disrupted by your ki, the target's speed is halved, and it can't use reactions. On its next turn, it can use either an action or a bonus action, not both. On a successful save, the  target takes half damage from the attack and isn't disrupted. The blade returns to normal immediately after the attack

6th Level - Ki-Bound Weapon

At 6th level, If your Ki-Forged blade has the thrown property you can make it return to your hand immediately after it is thrown by spending 1 ki point.

11th Level - Ki-Enhanced Focus

At 11th level, your focused ki protects you from mental intrusions and damage. Your thoughts can't be read by telepathy or other means unless you allow it, and you also have resistance to psychic damage.

11th Level - Ki-Forged Flurry

At 11th level, when you use your flurry of blows, you can attack with your ki-forged blade instead of unarmed strikes.

17th Level - Ki-Blade Ascendancy

At 17th level, your connection to the essence of ki reaches its pinnacle. You can now infuse your ki-forged weapon with extraordinary power. As an action, you can spend 4 ki points to enter the state of Ki-Blade Ascendancy, which lasts for 1 minute.

While in this state:

  • Your ki-forged weapon deals an additional 1d8 force damage on each hit, and you gain a number of temporary hit points equal to twice the force damage dealt by this feature.
  • Whenever you hit a stunned creature with your ki-forged weapon, you can spend an additional ki point to attempt to paralyze the target. The target must succeed on a Constitution saving throw against your Ki save DC or be paralyzed until the end of its next turn.
Homebrew / Subclasses

Way of the Mirror Soul

Way of the Mirror Soul

Way of the Mirror Soul

Features:

  • 3rd Level - Light Echo's
  • 6th Level - Fractal Vision
  • 11th Level - Mirror Stride
  • 17th Level - Soul of Reflection

3rd Level - Light Echo's

3rd-level Mirror Soul feature

Starting when you choose this tradition at 3rd level, you can create reflections that disorient your foes and bolster your defense. When you use your flurry of blows, you can spend 2 ki points to cast the mirror image spell, replacing one of the unarmed strikes. When casted this way, you only make one illusory duplicate, unless you spend one ki point for an additional duplicate (3 duplicates max). For each duplicate you create, you gain 5 temporary hit points.

6th Level - Fractal Vision

6th-level Mirror Soul feature

As an action you may magically project your consciousness into a reflective surface that you can see. Projecting allows you to see and hear, as well as project your voice as though you were in that reflections space. During this time, you are blinded and deafened. You can sustain this effect for up to 10 minutes, and you can end it at any time (requires no action).

While being used in this way, you can use an action to project to another reflective surface that you can see. While you are projecting into a reflection, your reflection is visible, and can be interacted with by others, such as speaking with them. If any reflective surface along this path is destroyed or disrupted (in the case of liquids), this effect ends.

11th Level - Mirror Stride

11th-level Mirror Soul feature

You gain the ability to magically enter a mirror or reflective surface within 5 feet of you and move from inside it to inside another mirror or reflective surface being effected by your Fractal Vision feature.

You must spend 1 ki point and use 5 feet of movement to enter a reflection. As part of the movement used to enter the reflection, you can either pass into one of those reflections or step out of the reflection you're in. You appear in a spot of your choice within 5 feet of the destination, using another 5 feet of movement. If you have no movement left, you appear within 5 feet of the reflection you entered.

You can use this ability once per round, and take 1d10 force damage if you end your turn inside a reflection.

17th Level - Soul of Reflection

17th-level Mirror Soul feature

Starting at 17th level, you empower your Mirror Images for both defense and offense. While your Mirror Images persist, you gain the following benefits:

You and your illusory duplicates gain a +1 to Armor Class and Saving Throws for each duplicate still active (up to a maximum of +3)

Your unarmed strikes and monk weapon attacks deal additional psychic damage equal to your Wisdom modifier. (edited)

Homebrew / Subclasses

Weapon Master

Weapon Master

Weapon Master

Features:

  • 3rd Level - Deft Grip
  • 3rd Level - Flowing Stance
  • 7th Level - Rapid Strike
  • 10th Level - Shatter the Horde
  • 15th Level - Focused Strike
  • 18th Level - Omnipath

3rd Level - Deft Grip

Starting at 3rd level, after you make a weapon attack using the attack action you can use a free action to swap to another weapon.

When you attack with a weapon, you receive a bonus to the attack based on the list below, however you may only benefit from a single bonus once per turn, even if your attack misses; You can however receive an additional bonus if you attack with a different weapon that causes a different type of damage. Ranged weapons do not benefit from Deft Grip, nor do generic “Elemental Weapons” (which collectively count as a single weapon), consumable items that grant additional damage, or spells.

Deft Grip DC: 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Dexterity modifier

Damage Type Effect Bonus Damage
Bludgeoning The heavy blow causes both stone and steel to crumple. Additional 1d6 damage if AC ≥ 15 1d6 or 2d6 bludgeoning damage
Piercing A swift thrust gives you extra reach. +5ft attack range 1d6 piercing damage
Slashing A swift slice carves through lightly armored opponents with ease. Additional 1d6 damage if AC ≤ 15 1d6 or 2d6 slashing damage
Acid The acid begins to eat away at flesh and damage armor. Dexterity saving throw. Upon a failure, the creature’s AC is reduced by 1 until the end of your next turn. At level 10 the AC reduction is increased to 2, and at level 20 it is increased to 3. 1d6 acid damage
Cold Frost begins to coalesce around the creature’s body, restricting movement. Constitution saving throw. Upon a failure the creature’s speed is reduced by half until the end of your next turn. 1d6 cold damage
Fire Flames engulf the target. Dexterity saving throw. Upon a failure the creature is set ablaze and takes 1d6 fire damage at the end of their turn. The fame can be put out by a suitable liquid or by using an action to extinguish it. 1d6 fire damage
Force The weapon impacts with incredible force. Strength saving throw. Upon a failure the creature is knocked prone. 1d6 force damage
Lightning Lightning arcs to the flesh of another creature on impact. A random hostile creature within 10ft is chosen. That creature makes a dexterity saving throw. Upon a failure, they take the full damage of the attack. 1d6 lightning damage
Necrotic The necrotic energy tears apart facsimiles of life. Doubled damage against temporary hp and creatures not in their original form (wildshape, poly, true-poly, shapechange, etc). Any damage that goes over the temp HP or the HP of the transformed creature is not doubled when applied to their HP/base form. 1d6 necrotic damage
Poison Poison seeps into the wound. Constitution saving throw. Upon a failure the creature suffers from the poisoned condition. The creature can repeat the save at the end of each of their turns. 1d6 poison damage
Psychic Psychic damage racks the mind of the target. The creature has disadvantage on any concentration saving throws for the damage caused by this attack. 1d6 psychic damage
Radiant Radiant light bursts from the weapon. Constitution saving throw. Upon a failure the creature is blinded. The creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns. 1d6 radiant damage
Thunder A thundercrack roars forth from the weapon. Constitution saving throw. Upon a failure the creature is deafened. The creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns. 1d6 thunder damage

3rd Level - Flowing Stance

At 3rd level, when you successfully hit another creature with a weapon that benefits from the Deft Grip bonus you receive a +1 to hit and to damage for your next attack if your next attack will also benefit from the Deft Grip bonus. These bonuses stack then reset to zero at the end of your turn.

7th Level - Rapid Strike

Starting at 7th level, you learn to trade accuracy for swift strikes. If you take the Attack action on your turn and have advantage on an attack roll against against one of the targets, you can forgo the advantage for that roll to make an additional weapon attack against that target, as part of the same action. You can do so no more than once per turn.

10th Level - Shatter the Horde

Starting at 10th level you can expend a use of your Action Surge to cause your melee attacks to strike any number of creatures within 5 feet of you, with a separate attack roll for each target. This benefit lasts for a single turn. This does not prevent a second Action Surge from being used on the same turn.

15th Level - Focused Strike

Starting at level 15 you can expend a use of your Action Surge to focus all of your ability into a singular strike. Instead of making multiple attacks, you make a single attack against a target, and if it hits that attack is essentially multiplied by however many attacks you have remaining, including bonuses for each attack from Deft Grip and Flowing Stance; Additionally, after you use this ability, you can make no more attacks on the same turn. This does not prevent a second Action Surge from being used on the same turn. This ability must be declared prior to knowing if the Focused Strike hits.

18th Level - Omnipath

At level 18, attunement slots for weapons that require attunement can shared in a single slot however, you can not dual wield weapons that require attunement without using a second slot, you receive no benefit from the weapon when it is not in use (such as auras or other passive buffs), and you can use one of the weapons at a time.

Lore

Elysium: Floating City in the Sky

Elysium: Floating City in the Sky

The Beginning

And so it came to pass that the evils of long-past would not rest idly by. Arising from the crater of Dockers Bay, the entity which had wrought its destruction upon the town arose once again, and headed toward the survivors' encampment. Hastily were plans made, and the evacuation of all that remained was underway.

With groups of adventurers splitting to achieve differing objectives, ultimately the entity was stalled in a climactic battle, and in its haste, rent its destructive energy prematurely.

Having successfully evacuated North of the Cloud Peaks into the Wood of Sharp Teeth, the survivors once again set camp. In the wake of the comet entity's second destructive event, several changes had been observed:

First, the light of the comet in the sky dimmed to a level in which it is only just barely visible in the night sky.

Second, unlike in the wake of the destruction of Dockers Bay, there seemed to have been very little residual energy in the second crater - Almost no Nightwalkers or shadow entities of any kind.

Lastly, as the comet's light dimmed, something appeared to break off of it, hurtling across the sky like a meteor before impacting the ground some distance to the East of the new encampment. The expelled mass from the comet turned out to be a device created in the ancient Nethereil Empire by the Magos of Xiandlier Enclave. The floating enclaves of Netheril, powered by Mythallars, ultimately fell when the Mythallars, not wholly unexpectedly, were destroyed in what became known as Karsus's Folly.

Within the unique device was the creator himself, Magos Esra. Finding himself a man out of time, he was met by several adventurers from the encampment who had come to investigate the meteor which had fallen from the sky. The Magos explained that his enclave had been destroyed by the elder-evil, the Star of Ice and Hate, Delban. His description of the entity which came to do its master's bidding was identical to that of the Comet Entity which had destroyed Dockers Bay, and had sought to destroy the encampment at the Cloud Peaks. Seeking the power of the Mythallars of Xiandlier, it also took interest in the Magos' experiment, and ripped it straight from the enclave's core as well, taking the Magos along with it.

Now, having learned of the fate of the Netheril Empire, and much of the history that had passed in the thousand years or so since his own time, Esra seeks to rebuild his device, improve upon it, and re-create an enclave like those of ancient Netheril. At the invitation of the adventurers who had come across him after crashing into the forest, he appeared above the encampment with the beginnings of a new enclave: a mass of land and earth approximately 800 x 800 ft. He suggested that if he were able to get more power to the crystal core which sustained its floating and traveling capability, that it might be expanded upon in the future.

To that end, he invited the people of the encampment knowing they, too, had suffered at the destructive hand of Delban, to come aboard the nascent enclave, and stay there. In exchange, he asked that they render their aid should the floating island come under attack, or for the occasional task that might be required to maintain its integrity. He added that all were welcome to stay on the island, so long as they also did not interfere with his work, nor the operations of the crystal entombed at the core of the island mass.

The Realm Wanders

The island, which Esra named Elysium (for the hubris of the Netherese would naturally lead one to name their island for a Celestial Plane), was designed specifically to travel. It would not do to have it remain stationery over the Cloud Peaks once the refugees of Docker's Bay had come to settle the floating landmass.

Waterdeep

Having developed on the island a bit, and established a permanent residence and facilities, the new residents of Elysium decided that the island should set sail for Waterdeep. After several days of travel, Elysium arrived just over the horizon, staying fifty miles outside the border of Waterdeep.

The city's denizens, quite suspicious and wary of the sudden appearance of a giant floating landmass, resorted to keeping scouts on patrol regularly. Never was Elysium left without the watching eyes of Waterdeep scouts. While the adventurers of Elysium were regarded with mistrust and suspicion in Waterdeep, they had not as yet been barred from entering or conducting business there. Tensions however were high, and the slightest provocation, perceived or not, may tilt relations into open hostility.

The Annexation of Elysium

For a time, Elysium and Waterdeep coexisted relatively peacefully, though never without tension. Helping Waterdeep with some of its contracts helped the Elysians gain rapport, but it wasn't long before those in power found another avenue of taxation in the rich adventurers of the floating island, and Ramiel's Crusade in the east becoming an increasing threat provided yet more (albeit convenient) reason for Waterdeep to annex Elysium.

The annexation began cordially, if not gladly. While the adventurers weren't happy to have to pay taxes -- some even going so far as to find every way possible to avoid doing so -- many did see the value in such a close alignment with the Lords' Alliance. But it wasn't long before even that thin connection began to break down.

Word soon spread among Waterdeep's nobility of the new ward and the rich adventurers inhabiting it. Not to be outdone by these overpaid mercenaries who merely played at being nobles, but who clearly didn't see value of the land under their very feet, rich Waterdhavians began purchasing it and moving in. With the influx of people came an influx of problems, culminating in the attempted murder of a noble in the middle of the Cloud Top Inn.

Elysium Regains Independence

As the island further developed and began to move again, relations with Waterdeep were strained and Gray Wardens were placed as a proxy for the city staff to alleviate tensions and allow the island to roam without inciting diplomatic incidents. However, this was but a band aid, and relations with Waterdeep were stretched to the breaking point, resulting in Waterdeep releasing Elysium and allow it to become its own independent island.

Negotiations were conducted among the land owners within the Cloud Top Inn about what should be done for the new government, and it was decided that an unusual form of government known as a democracy would be set up on the island. So Thorlas, Lord Commander of the Gray Wardens and Noble Lord of Waterdeep, acting as the city-state's representative, officialized the documents set up during the discussion and independence was declared, resulting in the withdrawal of the Warden peacekeepers and the passing of the torch to the new government.

A woman by the name of Phoenix was elected to Mayor, with a supporting council comprised of Kaynes, Jerry, Alina, Alkafyn, Jack, and Cabbage. However they were not the only ones involved in the city's independence. Bryan, Clark Aiwon, Ajani, Loops Silva, Pon, Anastasia, and Vapor, among a number of other land owners, were present as well and contributed to the discussion. Together, they began the long and arduous process of nurturing the fledgling government.

Map of Elysium

Lore

The Wandering Realm's world is based on the world of Faerûn, but as a living world, it has evolved over time.

Lore

Sigil

Sigil

Sigil Clarifications

Sigil, the City of Doors, is a fairly special place in the multiverse. It is the ultimate neutral ground where people of all planes and background can meet and coexist. It also comes with some special rules, courtesy of the Lady of Pain, the godlike ruler of the mind bending city.

Access to the city is granted via portals, which can be any threshold from a doorway to window or a simple clearing in a forest, and is accessed via a portal key which can be anything from a literal key to a simple thought or whistled tune as you pass the threshold. These portals are not static and can be open for centuries, seconds, or for a five uses. In other words, access is based DM/Lady of Pain discretion.

Teleportation within the city does not function. Need to get around using good old fashioned leg power and it would be prudent to hire a guide if you're not a native or very familiar with the occasional loops of Mc Escher esque architecture.

Creatures or people spotted in Sigil are not considered to be within their natural environment for the purposes of Shapechange, Poly, etc unless the creature is native/unique to the city or Outlands such as a Cranium Rat Squeaker or Sunfly.

Binding and summoning magics also do not function within the city. Can't exactly allow the celestials to go around binding the fiends walking about, and vice versa. This is a city of neutrality, where all are permitted so long as they behave.

Items or knowledge brought back from alternate universes, timelines, settings, don't transfer to our main setting.

Space is... weird... in the city. Buildings move seemingly on their own, space is simultaneously compact and infinite, travel between any two places seeming to take a indeterminate amount of time. One can walk for years to get down a city block or seconds to cross to the other side of the city. It is as difficult to traverse as the DM desires and the space for new construction is seemingly infinite.

Laws of the Lady

Worship of the Lady is prohibited.

No harm may come to any dabus.

There are to be no challenges to the Lady's ultimate rule or authority within Sigil.

Any action which harms the city of Sigil either directly or indirectly will be considered as a direct attack against the Lady herself, and punished appropriately.

No divine entity may enter Sigil.

There may be at no time more than 15 factions operating within Sigil. (Though this rule was put into place during the Great Upheaval, it is unknown if it is still amongst her laws, and the dabus have refused comment. Most haven't risked testing it.)

However, there are more laws, but are determined and enforced by internal factions of the city and are not ultimate rules laid down by the Lady of Pain, who has instantly flayed and killed even the most powerful of adventurers for so much as looking at her. Thankfully she isn't seen around much.

Lore

The Destruction of Docker

The Destruction of Docker's Bay

The End

It is often the case that fairy tales have a definitive beginning and end. The real world, however, seldom confines itself to such limitations. Our story, set as it is within the Forgotten Realms, thus begins at the end of another: The port-town of Dockers Bay, located along the Sword Coast just West of The Cloud Peaks, saw a curious collection of characters: from the typical humans making their way in the world, to the demigods that lived among them as adventurers.

Long had the city been protected by powerful magic, beyond even that of the adventurers who resided there. So, when cataclysm befell the land, it confounded beliefs and shattered the sense of safety that all had resided comfortably under. It had started quite simply: A comet in the skies above. Over time, the comet revealed an unnatural nature - mages felt pain in their heads, people and animals were prone to emotional outbursts, and magical energies became unpredictable. As time passed, these effects grew in gravity, and new, worse effects appeared. Shadow creatures crept around the area, stalking the night - and certain people and creatures started being targeted.

None of these events, however, hinted at what was to come. A group of some of the most powerful adventurers - not just in Dockers Bay, but indeed the world - set out to investigate the comet, determine its origin, and put a stop to its increasingly dangerous effects. What they found was nothing short of an incomprehensibly overwhelming presence, nearly killing them all simply by way of hearing its thoughts through one of them as a medium. As the intrepid heroes retreated back to safety, events only grew worse. The sun turned red, and a massive, imposing figure appeared, levitating in the skies above the bay's massive harbor.

And then it awoke. None who were present to witness it directly survived, but what happened in its wake was apparent for all to see: The massive magical crystal towers which had long protected the town exploded, their devastating eldritch energy wiping out most ordinary people in the area.

The town was engulfed in magical flames of purple and green, and the dark silhouette of the massive imposing figure stood silent and still in the sky above as devastation spread across the land. A few of the adventurers, at least, were quick to act: escaping by various methods of teleportation and fast-moving travel on foot. Most others were not so fortunate, and were consumed in the cataclysm.

Fleeing East, the surviving adventurers of Dockers Bay set up a makeshift camp settlement at the foot of The Cloud Peaks. With only their clothes and equipment on their backs, and very little in the way of food and supplies, they regrouped, with more survivors finding their way to the makeshift settlement. It was there that these fine adventurers rested - discussing plans regarding the founding of a new settlement; perhaps somewhere far away, or perhaps somewhere else along the coast.

Lore

The Destruction of Docker

The Destruction of Docker's Bay

The End

It is often the case that fairy tales have a definitive beginning and end. The real world, however, seldom confines itself to such limitations. Our story, set as it is within the Forgotten Realms, thus begins at the end of another: The port-town of Dockers Bay, located along the Sword Coast just West of The Cloud Peaks, saw a curious collection of characters: from the typical humans making their way in the world, to the demigods that lived among them as adventurers.

Long had the city been protected by powerful magic, beyond even that of the adventurers who resided there. So, when cataclysm befell the land, it confounded beliefs and shattered the sense of safety that all had resided comfortably under. It had started quite simply: A comet in the skies above. Over time, the comet revealed an unnatural nature - mages felt pain in their heads, people and animals were prone to emotional outbursts, and magical energies became unpredictable. As time passed, these effects grew in gravity, and new, worse effects appeared. Shadow creatures crept around the area, stalking the night - and certain people and creatures started being targeted.

None of these events, however, hinted at what was to come. A group of some of the most powerful adventurers - not just in Dockers Bay, but indeed the world - set out to investigate the comet, determine its origin, and put a stop to its increasingly dangerous effects. What they found was nothing short of an incomprehensibly overwhelming presence, nearly killing them all simply by way of hearing its thoughts through one of them as a medium. As the intrepid heroes retreated back to safety, events only grew worse. The sun turned red, and a massive, imposing figure appeared, levitating in the skies above the bay's massive harbor.

And then it awoke. None who were present to witness it directly survived, but what happened in its wake was apparent for all to see: The massive magical crystal towers which had long protected the town exploded, their devastating eldritch energy wiping out most ordinary people in the area.

The town was engulfed in magical flames of purple and green, and the dark silhouette of the massive imposing figure stood silent and still in the sky above as devastation spread across the land. A few of the adventurers, at least, were quick to act: escaping by various methods of teleportation and fast-moving travel on foot. Most others were not so fortunate, and were consumed in the cataclysm.

Fleeing East, the surviving adventurers of Dockers Bay set up a makeshift camp settlement at the foot of The Cloud Peaks. With only their clothes and equipment on their backs, and very little in the way of food and supplies, they regrouped, with more survivors finding their way to the makeshift settlement. It was there that these fine adventurers rested - discussing plans regarding the founding of a new settlement; perhaps somewhere far away, or perhaps somewhere else along the coast.

Srd

SRD Reference

SRD Reference

This section provides a navigational entry point for official D&D 5e Systems Reference Document (SRD 5.1) content, published under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License (CC-BY-4.0).

:::caution Data Quarantine Notice
SRD content is physically airgapped from The Wandering Realm's curated Homebrew data at the backend level. JSON files, registry outputs, and Avrae export payloads are never merged — SRD data lives exclusively under data/srd/ and avrae/srd/.

The Catalog page surfaces SRD content only when the "Include Official SRD Content" toggle is explicitly enabled by the user. It defaults to off to preserve the curated, server-approved Homebrew-only view.
:::

What is the SRD?

The Systems Reference Document 5.1 is a curated subset of the D&D 5e rules published by Wizards of the Coast under CC-BY-4.0. It includes:

  • 319 official spells — canonical spell descriptions, components, and damage data
  • 362 magic items — official item descriptions and rarity ratings
  • Automation ASTs — Avrae-compatible automation payloads generated by the Polarity Engine

Browsing SRD Content

SRD spells and items are browsable in the Content Catalog via the "Include Official SRD Content" toggle. Entries from the SRD are clearly marked with an [SRD] badge to distinguish them from approved Homebrew content.

Data Sources and Licensing

All SRD content is attributed to Systems Reference Document 5.1 © 2016 Wizards of the Coast LLC.

Airgap Architecture

data/srd/spells/          ← 319 normalised spell JSON files
data/srd/items/           ← 362 normalised magic item JSON files
data/srd/automations/     ← Avrae ASTs (spells + items)
data/srd/srd_catalog.json ← Consolidated frontend catalog index

avrae/srd/twr-srd-spells.json  ← Isolated Avrae spell payload
avrae/srd/twr-srd-items.json   ← Isolated Avrae item payload

None of the above paths are ever concatenated with the primary content_registry.json, twr-tome.json, or twr-items.json homebrew outputs.
